The FX background thread, the audio thread, Havok worker 3 and the Wwise event manager each use 16-80 ms per second; the rest are idle.

An engine thread is an object of a small class with 11 virtual methods: vf0 the destructor, vf1 the shared Start 0x529500, vf8 the thread's name, vf9 its start stub and vf10 its stack size (the AI thread, vt 0x22FF668: "AIThread", 0x1AEA674, 0x10000). Start(this, routine, arg) stores the routine at +0x18 , the argument at +0x20 and the name at +0x28 , creates the OS thread suspended on the stub (handle at +0x08 ), applies priority and affinity settings and resumes it. Every stub is a jump to the trampoline 0x797DD4, which names the OS thread and calls routine(arg) . Every engine thread's stack therefore ends at 0x797DD4.

The main loop is 0xC24DB0. Each iteration either does the frame's work under 0x2D47E0 or waits in 0x3807E8 - 0x380FAC - 0x38105C ( MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx ). The wait is for the render thread. 0x38105C takes the render command queue (0x272E8D8; see the render thread below) and calls 0x1CF430 with its state block ( +0x38 ). 0x1CF430 loops while the render thread is behind: while the value at +0x198 is below the value at +0x1A0 , or equal to it and the ring's read cursor +0xD0 is still below +0x188 . Each pass sets +0x1EC , signals the render thread's event ( +0x130 ) and waits on its own event ( +0x128 ) with MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx , so window messages are still dispatched while the main thread waits. When the stop byte +0x120 is set, it only pumps messages ( PeekMessageW ). The main thread can therefore run ahead of the renderer only as far as the queue allows.

Sampled during play (4,000 samples at 400 Hz, every walk unwound to the thread's root 0x8C3E5C): Share Frame What it is --- --- --- 83.6% 0x2D47E0 - 0x1F68D8 the frame's work 51.4% 0x1A864C CGameClientShell vf1, the per-frame client update 16.8% 0x6B31DC - 0x2FA064 - 0x2F94F0 the object update scheduler running each NPC's update ( NPC vf18; below) 14.9% 0x1F6928 - 0x1F6958 MainScene vf10, the scene tick (below) 12.0% 0x3807E8 waiting 6.1% 0x1F7304 the AI world tick (inside the scene tick) 5.4% 0x3365A4 MainScene vf1, render submission (the HUD's CUIMgr::Render inside it) 5.0% 0x6528B8 Havok physics ( TtPhysics ) 2.7% 0x1B0EE4 animation pose jobs drained on the main thread The children of CGameClientShell vf1 run in this order (775 frames, 601 with at least two children sampled): 0x300CFC (vt 0x22C0BB0::vf1), 0x1A83AC - vt 0x2301178::vf14 0x1A8490 - 0x187A38 (a per-frame client update that fans out to many systems, the animation clip trackers among them), 0x1776B30, 0x1609AC, 0x47C1D4, 0x51C40C, 0x427B74, then Havok memory upkeep 0x709FC8. When the game window loses focus the simulation pauses: the world clock stops, the per-character update disappears, the scene tick drops to 5.8% of samples and the main thread spends 64-68% of its time waiting, while the renderer keeps drawing the paused scene at full frame rate.

Game objects are updated by a per-object countdown, not by a character loop. 0x2D47E0 passes [base+0x26FF050] to 0x1F68D8, which skips the walk while the object server [base+0x26FF058] reports itself busy; otherwise it calls 0x6B31DC on the update manager U = [base+0x26FF050]+0x3E0 (vt 0x22C0050). 0x6B31DC first drains a deferred-delivery buffer at U+0x690 (0x4CA9F8). Each entry names a target object ( +0x20 ) and a 16-bit tag ( +0x28 ); 0x4CAD68 decodes the entry's recorded payload in chunks of up to 512 bytes and hands each chunk to the target's vtable slot 19. The buffer is then reset and time-stamped, and 0x6B31DC calls 0x2FA064 : - 0x2FA064 walks the object sets linked from U+0x18 (node at set+0x18 , next at node+0x08 ; 130 sets in a loaded region). For each set it takes the set's due list set+0xE8 and hands every object on it to 0x2FA10C. - 0x2FA10C subtracts the object's time-domain step [[obj+0x88]+0x14] from its countdown obj+0xD0 . If the countdown is still above zero the object goes back on the list; otherwise it tail-jumps to the object's vf18, its Update (vtable +0x90 ), which is why vf18 appears directly under 0x2FA064 in an unwound stack. - SetNextUpdate 0x59AB3C(object, delay) stores the delay in obj+0xD0 and links the object into its set's due list ( [obj+0x58]+0xE8 ). It has 119 callers and 36 tail calls, many of them other classes' Update methods. The NPC class is vt 0x1FB3640 (the engine's class descriptor [[obj+0x78]]+0 reads NPC on 98 of 98 objects; vt 0x1FB3AA8 is the same object's secondary vtable). Its Update 0x2F94F0 first re-arms itself with a delay of 1e-7 s (the constant at 0x202EA30), meaning "again next frame", then calls 0x2F9478, shared with the player's Update 0x6E92F8. That runs one of: vf121 for a dead body (the ragdoll and body-cleanup path), vf122 in a special client state, or vf119 0x2F79A4, the AI update . One object set holds every character in the spawn manager (101 of 101, 98 of 98, 124 of 124 and 163 of 163 in four reads), and every one is re-armed at 1e-7 every frame, at distances from 0 to 467 m. Nothing on the path reads a position or a distance: there is no distance-based update rate for NPCs . Pausing works through the time source: while the game is paused its step is 0.0 (102 of 102 characters), so no countdown reaches zero and no NPC Update runs. The time source [obj+0x88] is the state of one of the engine's scaled clocks: NPCs use the world clock and the player the player clock (see Engine core), which is also how slow motion reaches their updates. The other objects on due lists (spawn closets, look-at and quest triggers, scenario-override volumes, quests, birds, spiders, script timers) together take under 0.3% of the main thread. Cost in play (three runs of 15, 15 and 20 s at 400 Hz, 1,220-1,857 presented frames, each sample attributed to the object whose Update was on the stack): the scheduler takes 16.3-17.3% of the main thread and the NPC Update 1.52-1.89 ms per frame, 12-14 µs per NPC per frame . The cost does not fall with distance (beyond 200 m: 10.7-11.4 µs per NPC); it follows what the NPC is doing (idle 9.9 µs, following a route 12.7, attacking 26.4, recoiling 20.8). Inside vf119, in call order: Share of the NPC update Call What --- --- --- 26% vf113 - 0x11B230 target selection: combat-threat scoring 0x2FA99C (about 7%) and a scan of the 27 target-select pickers in the table [base+0x26FFCC0] (0x11BF60, 9-12%) 10-12% vf112 - 0x11AEB8 aim and look-at trackers 4.5-7% 0x2F5E6C movement and path following 33-38% 0x1919C8 the plan tree tick (see AI): selection 4-5%, running steps 29-33%, of which the Attack step's attack picking 0x4612D8 alone takes 5-12% 2% 0x2F5EB4 collision avoidance radius 3-4% 0x2FD960 the NPC's services, each on its own timer against the world time 4% 0x2F6420 (tail) context actions, perception target overrides, post-update state Morale, talk, awareness markers and the rest take under 3% each.

MainScene is a static singleton [base+0x26FFAB0] (vt 0x1F68920). Its vf10 0x1F6958 is the scene tick; it calls, in this order (each call with the object it runs on; scene = the MainScene object, GM = the GameManager [base+0x26FFAA8] ): 1. scene+0x778 AI pre-tick 0x1F73DC, then the AI world tick 0x1F7304 2. scene+0x788 0x1F7240 3. scene+0x798 : game mode 0x11FA58, projectiles that stick or fly 0x1F721C, weapon-mode item givers 0x1F6EC4, and 0x4C6050, the list of synchronized / attached characters (it clears each NPC's AI-suspend byte npc+0x2C21 ) 4. scene+0x7D8 render restart 0x4E1538 5. GM+0x6C68 the faction system's fort-assault composition 0x1E2BC4, then GM+0x6CC8 fort-assault setup 0x4F4BDC 6. GM+0x6D30 the online manager's update 0x1E3E78 (the enter-world checks; it reports ENTER WORLD HANG DETECTED ) 7. scene+0x7E8 bundle unloads and world UI 0x16D9CC, scene+0x868 the character bundle manager 0x4B4FFC, scene+0x7E0 presentation bundles 0x5211DC 8. the collision global 0x2FD3B8, scene+0x7A8 slow motion 0x5CF55C, scene+0x7B0 dynamic object groups 0x5AC9AC, scene+0x7D0 resurrection and ambient areas 0x6978C8 9. GM+0x6D28 world items, gifts and the seeing stones 0x6EBE70, GM+0x6C60 the quest system 0x4A859C, GM+0x6D98 weather 0x43C574 10. world reset 0x1789F0C, then GM+0x6D90 0x179F64 (it walks a vector of objects and calls 0x179F98 on each one whose byte +0x252 is set) 11. GM+0x6D08 the script system 0x6D19B4 The tick makes 52 calls in all, with QueryPerformanceCounter timing around the AI world. The AI world tick 0x1F7304 runs on W = scene+0x778 and updates these modules: Module Slot Update --- --- --- battle-node capture W+0x88 0x6546E8 smart objects W+0x10 0x6B5258 AI core W+0x18 0x6EE15C NPC summon and dismiss W+0x08 0x1234EC fight circles W+0x28 0x6DE538 transient alarms W+0x38 0x607838 AI core W+0x40 / +0x48 0x48C7E0 / 0x6870FC find-player W+0x70 0x404EEC the buddy / follower system W+0xB0 0x3608C8 AI core W+0xB8 0x6D5394 the spawn-scenario module W+0xA8 0x378404 AI core W+0x90 / +0x98 0x72ABE4 / 0x1F5C94 The AI world also holds the spawn manager ( W+0x30 ) and the alarm system ( W+0x38 ); see AI.

The render thread is a static object at 0x267E338 (thread class vt 0x1FFD4D0: vf8 name 0x7F9AE0, vf9 stub 0x7F9AF0). Its routine 0x1C8F158 runs a one-time initialization 0x1C8ECB8 (it registers the world-mesh, world-client, texture-animation and CPU-texture resource types and the fog overlay material), signals that it is ready, then loops while (0x1C8EDE0(queue)) {} : it is a command processor.

The queue lives at 0x272E8D8; its state block at +0x38 holds: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x08 ring begin +0x18 ring end (a 2 MB ring) +0xD0 read cursor +0xD8 write cursor +0x120 non-zero stops the loop +0x128, +0x130 counters A command is a bound call {+0x00 thunk, +0x08 object, +0x10 method, +0x18 arguments} . The executor 0x188E08 calls the qword at the read cursor with rdx = &cursor ; the thunk advances the cursor by its own fixed size ( mov r8,[rdx]; lea rax,[r8+N]; mov [rdx],rax , 35 sizes in use) and tail-calls method(object, arguments) ; the executor then aligns the cursor to 8 bytes. The ring can therefore be walked exactly from its start to the write cursor. A frame is 360-371 commands from 44 distinct methods. Across two snapshots (24,944 commands / 68 frames and 18,169 / 49 frames) every frame issued its 22-23 once-per-frame commands in the same order: 1. setup 0x485420; 2. 0x258720 (28 per frame); 3. 0x177D7C (53 per frame, shader-constant uploads); 4. three calls on the surface-overlay renderable (vt 0x1FFECD8: 0x70C0E0, 0x7146A0, 0x72FDE0), the rain and fire overlay pass; 5. 0x5E9448 (53); 6. a once-per-frame block with the terrain 0x484844; 7. a long interleave of per-view work on objects of vt 0x1DAADB8; 8. the weather material overrides 0x1B7A40 / 0x1B7A94; 9. the scene command (below); 10. light-volume instancing 0x6C74A8 ( DrawIcosahedronInstancesIndirect ); 11. the 13 tiled-lighting tile updates (0x1791CC BufferTileIndices with 0x247108); 12. texture bindings 0x33651C; 13. exposure 0x1E8150 ( Lith.ExposureAdjustSpeed , Lith.BlowOutWeight ); 14. frame timing 0x6D5908; 15. Present 0x38052C; 16. Bink video 0x3322BC, which walks the live-video list 0x267E400; 17. 0x4C32E8, a call into the engine interface's render service; 18. high-resolution texture streaming 0x3807E4.

t: Where the render thread's time goes
x: Sampled during play (4,000 samples at 500 Hz; every stack unwound to the thread trampoline): 0x797DD4 trampoline - 0x1C8F158 render routine - 0x188DB0 - 0x188E08 executor (99.8%) 0x1EE210 scene command 79-85% 0x6EC61C - 0x116B694 - 0x1EAA54 (k fSampleScale) - 0x1EABC4 0x1EAF30 (animation-side work), 0x255CF8, 0x1EB038 first, in this order 0x33BCB8 scene passes 69-78% 0x33CD60 main pass list 56-67% 0x255920, 0x185410 G-buffer prelude (target set 7) 0x66E93C - 0x1EE4F8 - 0x387858 mesh pass A: the G-buffer 24-42% 0x33783C GPU particles 2-4.5% 0x1F02E8 - 0x1EE3E4 / 0x25619C mesh pass B: the shadow atlas 10-20% 0x384640 light accumulation (point-light compute 0x4D951C runs here) 3-4% 0x1021250 vegetation displacement and grouped GPU particles 3-4.5% 0x33740C post-processing (motion blur, depth of field, blur, vignette) 0x339D6C color-grading LUT 0x1EDE58 object-color compute 6-7% 0x38052C Present 7-10% The order inside 0x33CD60 comes from consecutive samples (taken 1.4 ms apart): when two consecutive samples sit in different children, the first child ran before the second. Over 8,370 samples, every such move went one way only: From To Moves The other way --- --- --- --- 0x255920 mesh pass A 380 0 0x185410 A 136 0 A the GPU particles 193 0 the GPU particles mesh pass B 89 0 A B 685 0 B the light accumulation 0x384640 214 0 the light accumulation the next frame's 0x255920 18 The frame is therefore: G-buffer prelude, G-buffer (A), GPU particles, shadows (B), lighting. Which targets each pass draws into is in Rendering. In 0x33BCB8 , 0x33CD60 runs first, 0x1021250 next and 0x1EDE58 last (a forward pass writing scene color and motion). In 0x1EABC4 , the three small children run before 0x33BCB8 in all 303 frames where two were sampled. The tree is the same whether the world is playing or paused. What identifies each branch: the GPU particle branch references StandardGPUParticle.Compute , StandardGPUParticle ParticleBuffer0/1 and CustomGPUParticle DrawIndirect / ParticleSource / ParticleDest ; the vegetation branch VegetationPatch InstanceBuffer DisplaceInstances and GroupedGPUParticle Source / DestDrawIndirect ; the post-processing branch tNeighborVelocityBuffer , tMaxVelocityBuffer , k fNearDOFParams , k fFarDOFParams , k fBoxBlurParams and k fVignetteParams . Both mesh passes draw through the same indexed-draw path (input assembly 0x17F1B0, DrawIndexed 0x17F5A4, the indirect mesh draw 0x17DC48).

0x38052C calls 0x38057C with the engine's static D3D block at 0x272D1C0 as this : Offset in the block Meaning --- --- +0x00 the device ( ID3D11Device1 ) +0x28 the immediate context as ID3D11DeviceContext1 , the handle the engine draws through ( [base+0x272D1E8] ) +0x88 the IDXGISwapChain +0xA8 presented-frame counter ( [base+0x272D268] ) +0xE0 flags (bit 0x800: tearing allowed) +0x7D0 the display refresh rate +0xA80 set when the window is occluded It flushes the context ( ID3D11DeviceContext::Flush , vtable slot 111), then calls IDXGISwapChain::Present (slot 8). The sync interval is 0 unless the caller asks for vertical sync, in which case it is the refresh rate divided by the frame-rate cap [base+0x2A371A4] , clamped to 1-4; the flags add DXGI PRESENT ALLOW TEARING when the swap chain supports it. DXGI STATUS OCCLUDED sets the occluded byte, device-removed and device-reset errors go to the error reporter 0x1C8AD0C, and every successful present increments the counter at +0xA8 . The byte [base+0x267E006] enables presenting. On a 240 Hz display the counter advanced 86 times per second.

- What kinds of payload the deferred-delivery buffer at U+0x690 carries, and who records them. - Whether a longer countdown written into obj+0xD0 after an NPC's Update would thin out distant NPCs safely: it depends on whether the skipped systems use the frame step or elapsed time.

t: Resource streaming, bundles and the file system

x: Every asset path is resolved through one priority vector on the file system object, a static at 0x2A54600 (a function-local static returned by 0x3DDD34). Entry 0 is consulted first. Offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 SRWLOCK (resolvers take it shared, mounting takes it exclusive) +0x68 / +0x70 the mount vector: 16-byte entries {u32 kind, Source } +0x78 u32 capacity +0x80 a hash - path table {u32 hash, char path} ; +0xC0 its generation +0xE0 the archive-scan bound: the index of the last archive entry + 1 Kind 0 is an archive tree ( CArchiveTree , vt 0x22C21B8); kind 1 a directory source ( DirectorySource , vt 0x22C21C8, with its directory string at +0x10 ). A directory source answers with GetFileAttributesW(directory + path) ; a hit stops the archive search, and the loader opens the loose file itself (0x529BF8 - GetLooseFilePath 0x52A2F8). The retail game already mounts its Game\ folder as the last entry; that is how the cinematic .vib movies ship as loose files. Mount(fs, Source out, path, unused, index) is 0xC28560. A folder becomes a directory source. A file that exists (0x52A42C) becomes an archive tree, opened by 0x11AE014, which keeps the path as given at archive+0x50 . A path that names nothing is skipped without a message. An archive's first file, archivepatchloosefiles.txt , is its path index: Mount merges it into the hash - path table at fs+0x80 (lookup 0x3DDAD8, merge 0x1182428) and recomputes the scan bound. An index past the end of the vector mounts at the top (0xC28818). There is no unmount method. Mount has three callers: - The command line. The file-system setup 0x119717C (called from the shell initialization 0x117CF30) first mounts every -arch <path argument at index 0, before it reads the config list. - The config list. The same setup then mounts the list's lines through 0x1197418 - 0x11972C8, each in front of the nearest earlier line's archive (the index comes from 0xC34960). The first line, ..\Game , therefore ends last, and every later line stacks above the one before it: this is the list's "file search order is from the bottom up". - Downloaded content. At run time the file system's "mount at the top" method (vt 0x22BF9C8 vf2, the object at [base+0x26FF048] ) is called by 0x1848A50 for the archives the online service downloads into the player's profile folder. In one running game the vector held 89 entries (capacity 96): 74 archives from the config list, with the 14 lines that name missing files skipped; the six downloaded packs at the top; and ..\Game\ last. A mount affects only the next load of a path. A resource the game already holds, or keeps cached without references, is handed back as it is (see Reloading below), and a fast travel does not re-read it. Every open walks the vector from the top (the resource open stage 0x3DD648 - 0x3DD8FC - 0x3DD9F8). An archive answers from memory, through a binary search of its folder table (0x3DDAB8). A directory source first checks its extension filter (0x3DDC18, a list of hashes of the text after the last dot, which is empty unless set, and Mount leaves it empty) and then tries a real file open (0x3DDCBC builds the path, 0xC3C1B0 opens it).

Paths and names are hashed with StringHash 0x423E70: h = h 919 + LUT[c] over the bytes, with the 256-byte table at 0x1DB50D0 (it folds case, so the hash is case-insensitive). The same hash names GameDB records, fields, animation clips, bones and world objects throughout the engine.

Every resource the engine knows is a node in a hash table owned by the resource system [base+0x2A86758] : 0x800 buckets of 0x18 bytes, bucket = hash & 0x7FF , list head at +0x08 . A node is resource + 0x10 ( +0x08 next, +0x10 hash). Resource offset Meaning --- --- +0x08 the loaded data (null = not resident) +0x28 char path +0x30 reference count +0x34 u16 claim count: how many loaded bundle contents name the resource +0x36 u16 flags: bit 0 a load finished; 0x10 a standalone request is pending; 0x08 a reload; 0x20 a re-request with stream detail +0x38 u32 byte size (the engine's own accounting) +0x52 type (27 bundle, 48 effect .fxp , 20 material .mat , ...) +0x60 busy while a load is in progress 0x17DE40 is the engine's "loaded" test. A resource whose count reaches zero is not freed: 0x1BEAAC unlinks it from an unused list ( +0x10 ) and keeps it for reuse. "Released" therefore does not mean "gone"; residency is decided by the data pointer.

[base+0x2A86750] holds the I/O core ( core , the bundle owner + 0x30; the owner, vt 0x22C0FF8, is built by 0x119E5D4 and its stages by 0x1183E8C). Three stages run on three threads, each thread receiving its own stage as its argument: Stage Address Thread (routine) --- --- --- open core+0x20 ResourceOpenThread (0x11AECC8, loop 0x1153AA4) load core+0xF8 ResourceLoaderThread (0x11AEE50, loop 0x1153A00) parse core+0x1F0 ResourceParserThread (0x11AEF58, loop 0x1153560) The open and load stages each hold two queues of 0x38 bytes at +0x00 and +0x38 , the thread object at +0x70 , a CRITICAL SECTION at +0xA0 , a work event at +0xC8 and a stop event at +0xD0 . A queue is a double-buffered vector of 16-byte {object, control block} handles: Queue offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 / +0x08 / +0x10 input vector: begin, end, u32 capacity (10,240) +0x18 / +0x20 / +0x28 output vector: begin, end, capacity +0x30 u32 high-water mark (the largest count ever reached) +0x34 u32 current count The consumer swaps the two vectors when the output is empty and reverses the run, so service is first-in first-out, and the stage runner always takes the first non-empty queue: queue 0 drains before queue 1 is touched. The parse stage has a request vector at +0x00 , a second work vector at +0x18 (capacity 128, consumed by 0x3DC654), its thread object at +0x30 , locks at +0x60 and +0x88 , and events at +0xB0 / +0xB8 . Bytes [base+0x262B520 / 521 / 522] switch the open, load and parse threads on; when one is 0 that stage's work runs inline in the caller. All three are on in the shipped game.

A request ( SResourceLoadRequest , the name in its destructor 0x3DD77C) is allocated together with its reference count (a make shared layout) and has no vtable: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 the opened file (vf0 closes it); null until the open stage has run +0x08 u8 canceled: every stage skips a canceled request +0x10 the resource being loaded (its path at +0x28 ) +0x18 streaming detail (set by 0x3DD548 from the texture streamer) +0x20 u32 queue index +0x28 the resource data being built ( +0x18 u32 state; 3 = finalized) +0x30 a bundle, for a bundle content load (the .embb path at bundle +0x70 ) +0x38 / +0x40 the bundle load's output slot and argument

1. Submit 0x3DDDEC queues the request on the open stage (or straight on the load stage when the open thread is off). Producers include the texture streamer 0x3DD45C and the bundle content job 0x3DB5E4. 2. Open 0x3DD588: picks the path (resource +0x28 , or the bundle's .embb ) and waits on a semaphore at core+0x7B8 that bounds how many files are open at once (0x1184864 creates it with an initial and maximum count of 32, the u32 at 0x262AAA0). It then opens the file through the file system and passes the request to the load stage. 3. Load 0x2D3444: a resource is read into new resource data (0x3DCFDC, 0x3DCF80) and passed to the parse stage (0x3DD248); a bundle content request goes to the bundle loader 0x3DBE50 with the path table below. 4. Parse 0x3DD2A8: releases the semaphore slot (0x3DD424), parses the data (0x3DD3C4) and hands it to its resource type (0x3DD310). Texture tiers wait. The texture streamer puts any request whose path contains tex0 or texuhd (the higher-resolution texture tiers) in queue 1 and everything else in queue 0. Because the runners drain queue 0 first, base textures, meshes and bundle content always open before the high-resolution tiers. In a long play period the open queues' high-water marks reached 1,812 (queue 0) and 1,567 (queue 1) against 33 and 32 for the load queues: the backlog builds in front of the file open.

The load stage carries the engine's global name table at +0xD8 ( core+0x1D0 ): a vector of {u32 hash, u32 0, char path} sorted by hash, 30,639 rows in a loaded region. Every sampled key (503 of 503) equals the hash of its path, and every row is in order. It names every kind of streamed file ( .fxp , .tex , .bnk , .bndl , .anix , .vol.inst , presentation bundles in every language). The load stage passes it to the bundle content loader. It is a row-for-row copy of the file system's hash - path table ( fs+0x80 ), which Mount builds from the path index file each archive may carry (0x1182428 merges every index into it, sorted); see Archives and file formats.

A bundle is a manifest ( .bndl ) plus a container of its contents ( .embb ); see Archives and file formats. The bundle registry belongs to the owner (vt 0x22C0FF8): vtable slot 24 0x3DC538 gets a bundle forcing the .bndl extension, slot 25 0x119F1E8 takes a raw path, and the registry at owner+0x718 keeps 0x18-byte rows {u64 hash, CResourceBundle , u64} (get-or-create 0x1B5DC0). CResourceBundle (vt 0x1E6E678, 0x178 bytes): Offset / slot Meaning --- --- vf0 / vf1 AddRef 0x3DEDA0 / Release 0x3DEA38 vf2 / vf3 Prefetch 0x3DECC8 / Discard 0x3DEAEC vf6 memory accounting 0x6E001C: {loaded, total, bytes}, cached at +0x60..+0x6C once complete +0x08 char path +0x14 reference count +0x18 the loaded content (a vector of resource handles; null = not resident) +0x20 the manifest resource (its data is null when the .bndl does not exist) +0x28 u16 prefetch count +0x2A u8 generation, incremented by every load and every discard +0x70 char[0x104] the paired .embb path The reference contract. A registry row holds no reference. Prefetch (0 - 1) references the manifest, requests it and, once its data is present, queues the .embb content load as a job on the bundle system (0x3DB574 - 0x3DB5E4). Discard is the exact reverse and asserts it is never the final reference. Release at zero unregisters and destroys the bundle (0x1B5C9C), detouring to 0x10DD00A if the prefetch count is still non-zero. A holder therefore keeps a handle and a prefetch, and lets go by discarding first and releasing second. A missing path is benign: the registry keeps an entry whose manifest has no data (ten such rows exist in a normal game). Loading a region's layer bundle does not place it in the world: its resources become resident, but world contexts and placed objects are unchanged. In a loaded region the registry holds about 544 bundles, and every character bundle the region uses is already resident.

t: How a bundle's content becomes resources
x: Manifests are sorted lists. Every shipped manifest lists its entries sorted by the P919 hash of the path as an unsigned number, then by the path compared case-insensitively. This holds for 806 of 806 loaded manifests (62,270 entries), and every stored hash equals the P919 of its path. The parsed manifest is reached as bundle +0x20 (the manifest resource) - +0x08 - [+0] - +0x10 , a block whose +0x0C is the bundle path's hash, +0x18 / +0x20 the entry list {u32 hash, pad, char path} and +0x28 / +0x30 the size list. The content loader is set algebra over sorted lists. 0x3DBE50 - 0x3DC04C runs std::set intersection (0x3E0218) and std::set difference (0x3DC388, 0x3DC3E0) over the container's sections, the manifest and the load stage's path table, with the comparator 0x11B5AD4 (hash, then stricmp ). The content's first vector ( content+0x00 / +0x08 , resources made by 0x3E0628) is B = (sections and manifest) minus the path table: what the container itself supplies. The second ( content+0x20 / +0x28 , 0x3E03B8) is A = the manifest minus B: entries that come from elsewhere. Of 877 loaded bundles, 398 hold such entries, shipped ones among them, so the second vector is not a "still loading" list. A path in the path table is therefore never taken from the container: a file at that path in any mounted archive replaces the bundle's copy. The first claim decides. Each A entry goes through 0x3E00FC, which adds a reference and a claim ( +0x34 ); on the first claim only, it also sets flag 0x10 and requests the resource as a file of its own (0x2D40A4). Container bytes reach resources through 0x11B5D14, a single forward pass over the .embb sections in file order against the first vector ( stricmp on the resource path, with the progress kept in content+0x18 ). 0x1CD4A3C loads a section only when the claim count goes from 0 to 1, or when its type is in a force mask: it clears flag bit 0, raises +0x60 and calls the type's loader. Every later claimant is skipped, so whichever bundle claims a resource first decides its data for as long as anyone holds it. A manifest out of order breaks the set operations: its entries fall into A, each is requested as a file, and those that are not files of their own load empty and stay empty until every claim on them is dropped. Shader trees are loose files that bundles list. A shader tree ( .fxo , tag SRHR ) ships as a loose archive entry. Of the 183,631 shipped manifests, 1,433 list at least one (9,381 rows in all), and the bundle's container usually carries a copy as a section as well. Because the tree is a file of its own, it falls into A and is requested standalone, and the container's copy is skipped. A material only registers the trees it names: unless a loaded bundle lists a tree, or the tree is loaded at start-up, it stays registered with no data and the material draws nothing. Gear needs two bundles. An armor piece's geometry lives in <piece g.bndl ( .mesh , .skel , .anix ) and its material and textures in a set-wide <set <slot m.bndl named by the design record ( Inventory/ArmorData field DynamicBundle ). The engine loads both through a gear load request (vt 0x1DB4F78, constructor 0x400AB8) that is created only for an equipped item (give path 0x355474 - 0x61B868 - 0x4B4C7C, item equip 0x40136C - 0x401680, re-skin 0x645890). A piece placed into an appearance without an item gets no request: its mesh is in memory but its .mat is a registered resource with no data. The save loader 0x1C112F8 restores non-item pieces ( smc nonequipment record list - 0x1162D40) without a request as well. A bundle that is resident only because another character's item requested it is released when that item goes away. The gear budget. These requests go through NemesisBundleMgr ( [GameManager+0x6C88] , named by its console commands NemesisBundleMgr.PrintMemory and PrintDynamicBundleData ). Its initializer 0x1B42728, run once from the database setup, sets the budget +0x00 to Faction/Global.NemsisBundleMemoryLimit x 10 (320 x 10 = 3,200) and builds one object (vt 0x1FF6B90, constructor 0x1C52B10) for each of the 1,484 DynamicResource/BundleDefinition records, kept in a table at +0x08 of 16-byte {record, object} entries. An object's cost +0x3C starts as an estimate, its bundle type's Bundles/Types.MaxMemoryPC (10 for Flair 1MB , 20 for Flair 2MB , 30 for Flair 3MB , the names being the console figures). When the load finishes, 0x3FFA24 replaces it once (latch +0x58 ) with the real size, bytes / 2^20, sets state +0x48 to 2 and tells the requesters. The estimates are generous: resident Flair 1MB bundles held a median of 0.40 MB (124 bundles, largest 1.12) and Flair 2MB a median of 0.018 MB (20). In one loaded Lithlad 157 bundles were resident at a total cost of 66.3 of the 3,200, so the budget was far from limiting. Each object's priority +0x38 is rebuilt from its requesters by 0x3FFB10. Each request carries five bytes at +0x50 : bytes 0, 1, 2 and 4 are flags, merged by OR, and byte 3 is a number, merged by maximum (0x3FFD44). The score is the highest DynamicBundleLoadPriority among the requesters plus that number, +1,000 for byte 0 (when the bundle has a handle), +10,000 for byte 1, +500 for byte 2 and +1,000 for byte 4. It is then scaled by the requester count: x1.25 at exactly 4, x1.5 at 6 or 7, x1.75 above 8, and unchanged at 5 and 8. Recomputed from the live requesters, this formula gives the value in +0x38 for 157 of 157 resident bundles (requester counts 1 to 49). The constructor 0x400AB8 copies the five bytes from a struct its caller passes. On the equip and re-skin paths, 0x400084 fills that struct: Byte Value --- --- 0 always 1 1 set when the owner reference has a +0x40 2 set when the owning character has +0x2700 , the follower byte +0x23B8 or +0x2C04 set (0x366B88) 3 the member's Player Interaction Score at that moment (0x595364, row 2 column 2 of the score object FM+0x150 , the dword at +0x38 ) 4 from 0x77F804 The score byte is a snapshot: on 34 requests of this kind held by spawned captains it was at or below the current score every time, and equal on 16. Requests made on the give path (0x4B4C7C) instead take their bytes from a struct at +0xF8 of the 25-slot item table, and those carry byte 0 clear. Each frame 0x614438 re-evaluates the requests when they have changed ( +0x50 ): it sorts them by +0x38 , highest first, and adds up their costs. Requests within the budget are loaded (0x614CB0), and the rest go on a local list. For each of those, 0x1B427E4 walks the armor's and then the weapon's OutOfMemoryBackups and takes the first backup whose bundles are all resident already. (In 0x1B424BC, for each bundle with an object, 0x614D3C requires a handle, its counters +0x4C and +0x50 equal, and the state +0x48 equal to 2.) The backup goes to the request's owner (0x1C11CD8, 0x1C11CFC). So a piece over the budget is replaced by something already in memory, and nothing new is loaded for it. The budget applies to this gear path only. Bundles/Policies carries budgets of its own ( Character Nemesis 1,600 on PC), which this manager does not read. Effects only load through bundles. An effect reference (for example an attack's AOEFX path) never loads anything; the effect system finds resident effects by name, and only a bundle (or start-up) makes one resident. A malformed effect stalls the loader. Every .fxp ends with a u32: the count of the database's (u32, u32) pair table ( db+0x68 ; 0 in 968 of 968 shipped effects). A file without it makes the database body reader 0x4B9B50 read 4 bytes past the end of the file (0x4B9C60); on the raw asynchronous stream (vt 0x1E71010) that read does not return, and every later load waits behind it until the game restarts. A missing file, by contrast, is harmless. The effect database's categories are sorted by the hash of their path (371 of 371), and the loader binary-searches them (0x115B4D4).

The engine's hot reload. ResourceMgr::Reload 0x119F4BC(owner, path), slot 7 of the I/O owner vt 0x22C0FF8 (owner = [base+0x2A86750] - 0x30 ), reloads one resource while the game runs. It works in four steps: 1. the filter 0x119EB60 refuses .gamedb , and refuses .anix and .objres according to two engine switch bytes (0x262B50A, 0x262B509); 2. the lookup 0x17AE1C refuses a resource that has no references; 3. 0x1188A00 clears every registered bundle's loaded counters; 4. CResource::Reload 0x3E0AE0 takes the lock, sets flag 8 and queues the resource through 0x2D40A4. Nothing in the executable calls it. It has two siblings: slot 6 (0x5D5A000 - 0xC2A880) reloads by path prefix, and slot 8 (0x119F528 - 0x119DA54 - 0x11B5F74) reloads by resource-type mask, bundle by bundle, asking for each bundle's content again. The per-frame processor 0x2D3E10 (its queue served by 0x2D35E8) acts on a queued resource by its state: State Action --- --- claim count +0x34 is 0 releases the data and does not ask again: a reload of an unclaimed resource is an unload flag 0x20 releases, asks again with the stream detail at +0x40 flag 0x08 releases, asks again by path with no stream detail: the reload flag 0x10 and no data asks by path (a bundle's A entry) always, at the end clears 0x08, 0x10 and 0x20 ( and 0xFFC7 at 0x2D4001) The parser thread runs the type's parse (0x3DD3C4); for a texture, the texture type's vf4 0x5018A4 creates the Direct3D texture. The finish, 0x3E0BD4, must run on the render thread ("Finalize can only be called on the Render Thread!", 0x4C2610). Reloading a 5.6 MB texture this way took about 14 ms from empty to whole: the resource received a new data object and a new ID3D11Texture2D , while its references and flags stayed unchanged. A changed file mounted under the texture's path reached the screen with that reload, without any travel.

CharacterBundleMgr ( CharacterBundleMgr.cpp ) is MainScene+0x868 ( [base+0x26FFAB0]+0x868 ). It decides which creature models are in memory. Offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 / +0x08 entries and their count (146 = the Server/NPCBundle records); an entry is 0x30 bytes: +0x00 the NPCBundle record, +0x08/+0x10 a vector of CResourceBundle (the same objects as the registry's: an entry holds references to its bundles), +0x28 requested +0x18 / +0x20 / +0x28 the load / unload queue {record, u8 unload} +0x30 the current WorldInfo record +0x38 the always-loaded set ( Nemesis , Playerskin Talion ) +0x50 / +0x68 / +0x80 the world set, the override set, the player's build set ( Playerskin DarkTalion at rest) +0x98 / +0xA0 two override list slots +0xA8 the provider ( StructuresWorldInfoBundleData primary record) +0xB0 dirty byte IsBundleLoaded 0x1665B4 asks 0x166630(entry + 8). That answers 0 while the requested byte is clear; otherwise it answers the state (vf5) of the first bundle whose state is neither 3 nor 4, or 3 when there is no such bundle. The entry counts as loaded when the answer is 3 or 4, so a bundle that failed (4) counts as loaded and one still streaming (1 or 2) does not. The update 0x4B4FFC runs when the dirty byte is set. The world set is the provider's list; the override set is the first override list (or the default list) with the records of the always, world and build sets removed (0xE9F280 swap-removes them), so no record is owned twice. The reconcile 0xE9F360 requests what is new and queues what dropped out for unloading, then the update drains the queue, firing loaded / unloaded events through the global script agent ( GM+0x6CF0 ). A request is a flag per entry, not a count: RequestBundleLoad 0x4B6204 turns a queued unload of the record back into a load, else starts the entry loading (0x4B6300) and queues {record, 0} , or fires the loaded event at once; RequestBundleUnload 0x19EB87C turns a queued load into an unload, else queues {record, 1} . The drain unloads an entry by dropping every bundle handle it holds (0x2EE10C, clearing the requested byte) and polls a load (0x4B52A8) until it is loaded. One unload therefore takes the entry's bundles whoever asked for them; only a separate handle on the .bndl outlives it. The build set is kept by the player's model change (vf136 0x19BF404): the old model's Character/Models.Bundle is taken out of the set and unloaded and the new one requested and put in, one in and one out at every change; the player's build gate reads the set (0x19EAD34). RequestBundleLoad has four callers: the spawn gate 0x16652C, the reconcile, the player's model change and the wrapper 0x19EB83C. 0x19EAC44 (called once, from 0x178701C) is the teardown: every entry unloaded, the four sets and the queue cleared. A list's length is its field descriptor's element count (read by 0xE9EA30): every Server/NPCBundle/Lists record has two fields (the bundle array, hash 0x7AB8B862, and an empty second array). World Island Day holds six bundles (Goblin, Spider, Warg Base, Fellbeast, Troll Base, Troll Poison) and World MinasIthil Day nine. A region keeps its whole creature set loaded for the visit; there is no per-encounter picker. A region change resets everything: every set and every loaded creature bundle is cleared, including loads requested on demand, and the region's sets are rebuilt (skins first, then the world set, about 3 seconds to resident). Loads requested directly with RequestBundleLoad persist within a region, because no set owns them. The spawn gate 0x16652C (template - model - NPCBundle - IsBundleLoaded 0x1665B4) requests a missing bundle only when the region's WorldInfo.IsTestWorld is set (0x5B85B4); retail regions have it clear, so a spawn whose bundle is not loaded is rejected ( [AI SPAWNAMBIENT REJECT] ... doesn't have character bundle loaded ). The descriptor 0x166878 reads only the template and the spawn manager ( SM+0x78 the per-template override table, +0x80 its count, +0x88 the AI/Templates category); the model and bundle are plain field reads (0x16680C, 0x166680). A null bundle allows the spawn: 94 of 177 templates have none (every orc and olog class, tamed wargs, the fellbeast), because their data is always resident. The chain from a spawn channel to its bundle is plain data: AITypes.Entries[] - StructuresAISpawnAmbientTypeEntry.AITemplate - AI/Templates.CharacterModel - Character/Models.Bundle . Scripts and the console reach the manager through System:LoadOverrideNPCBundleList(list, slot) / LoadDefaultNPCBundleList and the console commands CharacterBundleMgr.Dump , LoadOverrideBundle and LoadDefaultBundleList (command table at 0x2674408); quests unload their overrides when they end.

The engine's own byte count understates the real cost of a single bundle and overstates a burst. Nazgul base (36.0 MB by the engine's count) added 120 MB of committed memory and 120 MB of video memory, while 129 bundles requested at once (622 - 4,337 MB by the engine's count) added only 571 MB of video memory and 665 MB of commit, because they share resources. Bundle loads do not consume the scarce low (below 4 GB) address space. A fast travel releases everything a region loaded; nothing accumulates across regions. WorldInfo.MaxBundleSizePC (1096 on PC, 548 on consoles) is checked only when content is packed; no run-time code reads it.

- What the give path's flags struct at +0xF8 of the 25-slot item table holds. Its requests carry byte 0 clear and byte 3 values up to 41, and they are held at +0x108 of an object that is not a slot item, so the check that settled the equip path does not reach them. - The meaning of the resource-data states other than 3 (finalized), and what the parse stage's second work vector carries. - Why the global path table's second field is 0 while the per-bundle name arrays carry 1. - Which other code submits I/O requests: only two callers of the submit function exist, so the resource system may queue some loads elsewhere. - Whether an archive mounted after a world has loaded reaches a bundle that loads later: the load stage's copy of the path table follows the file system's generation counter ( fs+0xC0 ), but no such load has been traced. - Whether the reload works for resource types other than textures; only a texture has been reloaded and seen.

The game ships its data as 76 .arch06 archives in the install root plus a small loose Game\ folder; every asset path the engine opens is resolved through those archives in a fixed search order. These are the Steam build's files; the GOG build ships 71 of them and the Microsoft Store package 66, with the config list in UWP64\ (see Game builds). This chapter gives the archive layout, compression, the search order and the rules that pick one copy of a file, then the container and payload formats inside, each checked against the shipped files.

What Count Notes --- --- --- .arch06 archives 76 (113.5 GB on disk, 180.7 GB unpacked) 488,752 file records, 16,302 folder records Game\ folder 822 loose files, about 20 GB 741 .vib movies, 77 Wwise .pck packages, 2 .vid , 2 .cfg x64\default.archcfg 1 the archive config list (below) x64\oo2core 5 win64.dll 1 the Oodle decoder the executable imports The archives fall into families: Family Archives Files --- --- --- UI, characters, creatures UI Assets , CoreCharacter , Monsters 4,541 / 78 / 378 Presentations (scenes, dialogue) Presentations + 8 language archives ( en fr it de esla eses ptbr ja ) 39,096 + 39,098 each Regions BlackGates , BaradDur , Island , MinasIthil , MtnPass , snowMtn , Volcano , each with a Lighting twin 24 - 3,073 per region, 2 - 60 per lighting archive Benchmark level Benchmark 4,577 Numbered patches Patch 00 - Patch 13 , each with an LC twin 8 - 5,869 DLC patches Patch DLC1 - Patch DLC5 , each with an LC twin 1,216 - 21,489 Sound banks soundbundles 3,762 Engine data Global (shaders, materials), HotChunk (GameDB, strings) 244 / 48 High-resolution textures HighMip ; uhdmip , uhdmip DLC1 - DLC4 9,691; 6,572 + 3,091 DLC markers Blade , Lithlad 1 each Three archives are empty ( Patch 00 LC , Patch 12 , Patch 12 LC : a 65-byte header and one empty root folder). Blade.arch06 and Lithlad.arch06 each hold one file, dlc\blade.txt / dlc\lithlad.txt , whose eight bytes read Unlocked ; neither is in the config list and neither is mounted in a running game. HotChunk.arch06 holds the GameDB and the string tables: entry 0 is its path index (2,136 bytes, below), entry 1 database\game\game.gamedb (56,759,100 bytes), entries 2-29 the 14 language folders' string.strdb and string uwp.strdb , entry 30 globalbundles\globaldatabase.bndl and entries 31-47 the 17 globalbundles\globalresources <lang .bndl bundles.

t: The archive config list and the search order
x: At start-up 0x119717C mounts any archive named with -arch on the command line, then reads the config list: 0x1196FE0 takes default.archcfg (string at 0x22C0B20) unless -archcfg (0x22C0B08) names another file. The list is text, one path per line, ; starting a comment; it opens with the Game directory lines and states "file search order is from the bottom up". Every line goes through Mount 0xC28560 (see Resource streaming for the file system object and its mount vector). A directory becomes a directory source, an existing file an archive source ( CArchiveTree , vt 0x22C21B8), and a line that names nothing is skipped: the shipped list names five archives that do not ship ( Great Hall , Great Hall Lighting , TextureArrayPatch , HighMipA , uhdmipA ) and, for each high-resolution archive, a second spelling without ..\ that resolves to nothing in the Steam layout. The three empty archives are mounted like any other. The live order. Read from a running game, the mount vector is the list reversed, so the bottom line is consulted first: Search position Sources --- --- first archives the online service downloaded into the player's profile folder then uhdmip DLC4 , DLC3 , DLC2 , DLC1 , uhdmip , HighMip then HotChunk , Global then Patch 13 LC , Patch 13 , Patch 12 LC , Patch 12 , Patch DLC5 LC , Patch DLC5 , Patch 11 LC ... Patch 09 , Patch DLC4 LC , Patch DLC4 , Patch 08 LC ... Patch 07 , Patch DLC3 LC , Patch DLC3 , soundbundles , Patch 06 LC , Patch 06 , Patch DLC2 LC , Patch DLC2 , Patch 05 LC , Patch 05 , Patch DLC1 LC , Patch DLC1 , Patch 04 LC ... Patch 00 then Benchmark , then each region archive above its Lighting twin ( Volcano ... BlackGates ) then the eight language presentation archives, Presentations , Monsters , CoreCharacter , UI Assets last the ..\Game\ directory The DLC patches are interleaved with the numbered ones, so no "DLC above numbered above base" rule holds; HotChunk and Global sit above every patch, and the high-resolution texture archives above those. The resolver 0x3DD958 walks the sources from index 0 up to the archive-scan bound [fs+0xE0] and returns the first archive that holds the path. A path that ships in several archives (26,122 of the 431,226 distinct paths, up to 37 copies) is therefore served from the highest one: the engine's byte count for the loaded English string table is 7,797,636, which fits HotChunk's 7,797,584-byte string.strdb and none of the patch copies (7,110,464 and 7,143,600).

All 76 archives are LTAR version 4, little-endian. The engine's reader is 0x11AE284: it checks LTAR and version 4, reads the rest of the header (0x11AE20C), the name pool, the file records and the folder records (0x11AE154), then copies the archive's own path to archive+0x50 . Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- 0x00 char[4] LTAR 0x04 u32 version, 4 0x08 u32 name pool size 0x0C u32 folder count 0x10 u32 file count 0x14, 0x18, 0x1C u32 x 3 flags, each read as a boolean into archive+0x28..+0x2A (1, 0, 0 in all 76) 0x20 16 bytes copied to archive+0x18 (zero in all 76) 0x30 the name pool: NUL-terminated strings, offset 0 is an empty string 0x30 + pool size 30 bytes x file count file records then 16 bytes x folder count folder records then 6 bytes x file count zeros in every archive; the reader does not read them then file data File record (30 bytes): Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- +0x00 u32 name: offset of the file's leaf name in the pool +0x04 u64 data offset from the start of the archive +0x0C u64 stored size +0x14 u64 size +0x1C u8 reader kind, kept by the reader in the top byte of the stored-size word (1 on all 488,752 records) +0x1D u8 0 = plain bytes, otherwise chunked; kept in the top byte of the size word (9 on all records) The two bytes trail every record, the last one included. To open an entry (0x3DDAB8 - 0x11AE510), the engine reads it as a plain byte range (0x11DC110) when the byte at +0x1D is 0. Otherwise +0x1C selects the reader: 1 the chunked stream (0x11DC4B8), and 0 a streaming source with its own 512 KB buffer (0x11DCC64; VirtualAlloc of 0x80000 bytes, "Failed to allocate memory for source resource"). Underneath, 0xC37B50 reads from memory when the whole archive is resident ( archive+0x30 ) and otherwise opens the archive file again by its path ( archive+0x50 , through 0xC3C1B0: CreateFileW for reading, read sharing only, overlapped; stream class vt 0x1E70EA8). The two entry streams differ in one property that callers test. The plain byte range (vt 0x1E70F00) can seek, while the chunked stream (vt 0x1E70F88) cannot: its slot 3 answers no, and its seek only sets an error flag. A shipped entry is always chunked (kind 1, flag 9 on every record), so a loader that needs to seek, such as the GameDB loader looking for a patch database, can do so only for a plain entry or a loose file (see GameDB). Folder record (16 bytes): {u32 name, u32 first child, u32 next sibling, u32 file count} , with 0xFFFFFFFF for "none". The name is the folder's full path ( database\string\enus ), the root folder (record 0) has an empty name, and the reader turns the two links into pointers to 0x30-byte folder objects. Files belong to folders in record order: folder 0 owns the first file count records, the next folder the following ones, and so on, so a file's path is folder + "\" + leaf . Across all 76 archives, 16,226 of 16,226 non-root folders extend their parent's path and the counts add up to the file count. Lookup. 0x3DDAD8 splits a path at its last \ or / , finds the folder by binary search over the folder records (0x3DDB90, case-insensitive), then binary-searches that folder's leaf names with stricmp and returns the file record. Both tables are kept sorted for this. The leaf names inside every folder are in case-insensitive order (16,299 of 16,299 folders). The folder records are in case-insensitive order of their full paths, compared as if each ended in a backslash (76 of 76 archives); plain order differs in 7 archives, and only where one folder name is a prefix of another, such as bundles\dlc and bundles\dlc4 .

t: Names: what is a file fact and what is a reader trap
x: - A record's name offset points at its own leaf, relative to 0x30. Read that way, with folders taken from the folder table, every typed entry's content matches its extension: 482,736 of 482,736 entries of 16 typed extensions ( .bndl , .embb , .tex , .mesh , .anix , .bnk ...), and each of the 39 extensions in the install maps to one format (catalog below). No per-archive naming rule is needed. - The pool is not a list of entries in order. It also holds the folder paths, and it stores each leaf string once: 56,018 records share a leaf string with another record ( string.strdb in 14 language folders), while full paths are unique within each archive (0 duplicates). A reader that takes "the string after the previous name", or resolves offsets against a wrong base (0x18 instead of 0x30), names a neighboring file: on the same records those rules give a name whose extension contradicts the content for 396,483 and 388,454 records. The result looks plausible because a neighbor's name is still a real path. - A path names a file only within one archive; the same path in another archive is another copy, chosen by the search order above.

File data is a chain of chunks, each {u32 stored length, u32 length, bytes} , with every chunk header 4-byte aligned relative to the start of the entry and a record's stored size equal to the chain's length rounded up to 4 (19,993 of 19,993 sampled entries, up to 400 per archive). The chunk reader 0x11DC664: 1. reads the two lengths and asserts "Encountered a corrupted compressed chunk header." when either exceeds 0x10000, so a chunk holds at most 64 KB; 2. copies the bytes when the stored length is at least the length (a stored chunk); 3. otherwise checks that OodleLZDecoder MemorySizeNeeded(8 = Kraken, length) fits its 0x20800-byte work buffer and calls OodleLZ Decompress (fuzz-safe) from oo2core 5 win64.dll , asserting "Decompression failure." unless exactly length bytes come out; 4. skips to the next 4-byte boundary. In the sample, 638,807 chunks were packed and 31,098 stored. The first chunk of every one of the 488,752 entries decodes with the shipped DLL. Over the whole install the stored data is 62.8% of its unpacked size. Two compressors. A packed chunk starts with an Oodle block header whose second byte names the compressor. The shipped DLL's own OodleLZ GetChunkCompressor (which this build exports with two arguments: the buffer and an int for the independent flag) and OodleLZ Compress agree on the mapping: 8C 06 is Kraken and 8C 02 is LZB16 . Of 543,319 packed chunks in 15,519 entries (up to 300 evenly spaced entries in each of the 76 archives), 541,955 are Kraken and 1,364 LZB16, and the header names the compressor on every one. The split is by size: every LZB16 chunk unpacks to 257 - 2,044 bytes, every Kraken chunk to 2,050 bytes or more (98.4% of them to the full 0x10000). LZB16 therefore appears only as an entry's last chunk (316) or only chunk (1,048), never as its first or a middle one, and in every file type whose length leaves a short tail ( .bndl , .embb , .texuhd , .mat , .scripts and so on). The reader passes every chunk to OodleLZ Decompress , which dispatches on the header, so a rebuilt chunk may use any compressor the DLL decodes.

A root file, archivepatchloosefiles.txt , is record 0 in 37 archives ( Patch 01 - Patch 11 , Patch 13 and Patch DLC1 - Patch DLC5 with their LC twins, Global , HotChunk , soundbundles ): u32 1 u32 string bytes strings (NUL-terminated full paths) u32 count count x {u32 hash, u32 string offset} The rows are sorted by hash and every hash is StringHash of its path (73,038 of 73,038). The index lists an archive's loose files: every loose .anix , .bnk , .objres , .scripts , .mesh , .skel in those archives, and a .bndl exactly when its container is not in the same archive (34,920 of 34,926; 10,849 of 10,883 manifests that sit beside their container are left out); no .embb is ever listed. It also names 495 paths that its archive does not hold. When Mount adds an archive it looks the file up (0x3DDAD8) and passes it to 0x1182428, which checks the leading 1, keeps the string block, builds {u32 hash, char path} rows and merges them, sorted, into the file system's hash - path table at fs+0x80 under the lock at fs+0x98 , incrementing the generation at fs+0xC0 . In a running game that table holds 30,639 rows: exactly the 30,637 distinct hashes of the 37 shipped indexes, plus two rows from a directory mounted at run time. The load stage's name table ( core+0x1D0 , see Resource streaming) is a row-for-row copy of it (same 30,639 hashes, same string pointers). Archives without an index (regions, UI, presentations, high-resolution textures) are mounted and searched like the others. Hashing. StringHash 0x423E70 computes h = h 919 + LUT[c] with the table at 0x1DB50D0. The table folds case but not separators: \ is 42 and / is 52, so a path hashes as written with backslashes. Other values: . 55, - 39, 38, space 37, a - z 1-26, 0 - 9 27-36.

t: Bundles: the BNDL manifest and the EMBB container
x: A bundle is a manifest ( .bndl , magic BNDL ) naming its members, usually paired with a container ( .embb , magic EMBB ) of the same path stem holding their bytes. The bundle loader 0x3DBE50 reads the container through 0x11B5E68 (it checks EMBB and version 5); the manifest's loader 0x504C70, a slot of the manifest resource handler, checks BNDL and version 6. How bundles are requested, referenced and released is in Resource streaming.

Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- 0x00 char[4] EMBB 0x04 u32 version, 5 0x08 u32 path table size 0x0C u32 member count n 0x10 path table: n NUL-terminated paths, each padded with NULs to 4 bytes; the size ends exactly at the last padded path 0x10 + size u32 x n offset of each path, relative to 0x10 then n x {u32 size, payload} members in path order; each payload begins with its own 4-character tag There is no padding in the section chain: a payload is followed at once by the next size word, and payload starts are spread evenly over all 16 residues mod 16 (643 - 1,008 sections each, 12,031 sections). All 190,407 containers are version 5 and all pass the header rules (offsets 4-aligned and chained by padded length, size exact, padding all NUL); 2,441 are empty, the largest holds 11,178 members, 428,440 members in all. Walking the chain of 780 containers (up to 30 per archive, each at most 64 MB) ends exactly at the end of the file in 780 of 780, with no zero-size or overrunning section. A member's size word alone locates the next member, so a payload whose size word disagrees with its length makes the loader read the next size from inside the payload.

Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- 0x00 char[4] BNDL 0x04 u32 version, 6 0x08 u32 path table size 0x0C u32 path table size + the type string's length with its NUL, rounded up to 4 0x10 u32 member count n 0x14 u32 x n member sizes then path table, same rules as the container's then Bundles/Types:<Name , NUL-terminated, padded to 4 then u32 x n path offsets All 225,338 manifests are version 6 and parse to their last byte; the 0x0C rule holds on 225,338 (a constant +28 would be right on only 217,350). The type string names a record of the GameDB category Bundles/Types ; 130 distinct strings are used, led by Presentation (208,584), WorldQuest (4,111), Sound 1 (1,656), FlairWorld (1,312) and Flair 1MB (982); 11 manifests have no members and an empty type.

t: How a manifest and its container relate
x: Every container has a manifest with the same path stem in its own archive (190,407 of 190,407). In 186,478 of those pairs the manifest mirrors the container exactly: identical path-table bytes and offsets, and sizes that predict the container's length, 16 + path table size + 4n + sum(4 + size[i]) = container size In the other 3,929 pairs the manifest declares members the container does not hold: the Desert region's worlds\retail\desert\desert.bndl lists 3,805 members while desert.embb (1.43 GB, in Patch DLC4 ) holds 3,763 (the other 42 are 41 .cres prefab resources and one .record06 , none of them a loose entry). Taking the winning copy of each side by the search order (190,367 bundles): Relation Bundles --- --- same member list and sizes 184,506 same list, but the winning manifest re-declares some sizes 1,710 (2,844 of the changed sizes equal the winning loose copy of that member) manifest lists members the container lacks 3,770 other differences 381 Of the 13,695 paths that winning manifests list beyond their container, 8,521 ship as loose entries. Patches use this to update part of a bundle: 32,903 manifests ship in an archive above their container's best copy (27 below). Container-less bundles. 2,001 manifests have no container anywhere: sound bundles ( Sound 1 1,654, Sound 5 187 ...), the language string bundles ( StringDB , 73), GlobalDatabase (7), GlobalRenderingResources and a few others. Their 3,398 members resolve as loose entries (3,257) or container members (34); 3,016 of the 3,257 declared sizes equal the winning entry's size and 206 more equal another copy's. globalbundles\globaldatabase.bndl declares the one member database\game\game.gamedb .

- A path: the first archive in the search order that holds it. - A bundle: its manifest is opened by path like any file, so the winning manifest gives the member list. A member can be in the container, a loose entry of the same path, or both; when both exist, the measured case below shows the loose copy in use. - Standalone against embedded: 14,172 asset paths ship both as a loose entry and inside some container ( .bnk 3,658, .tex 1,804, .anix 1,612, .fxp 1,165, .mat 900, .scripts 835, .objres 680 ...). For the Desert main part, the live context-action data equals the standalone desert.objres of Patch DLC5 , not the section embedded in Patch DLC4 's desert.embb nor the older standalone copies of Patch 09 and Patch 10 ; the winning desert.bndl ( Patch DLC5 ) declares exactly that copy's size. The same holds for a layer's .scripts (see Scripting); a path can also ship as different loose and embedded clips (see Animation). - The GameDB: database\game\game.gamedb ships in nine archives ( HotChunk 56,759,100 bytes; Patch 01 - Patch 04 and their LC twins 58,084,930 - 58,099,992). HotChunk is above all of them, so a path lookup returns its copy (see GameDB). Distinct asset paths by where they ship (manifests and containers excluded): 238,588 only inside containers, 34,409 only loose (mostly texture tiers), 14,172 both.

Every file starts with a 4-character tag, and the extension decides it: across all 488,752 records each extension maps to one format ( .txt aside). Section tags inside containers follow the same table (12,031 of 12,031 walked sections), with one exception: a .tex section is TEXR or SLVT (9 of 3,181). Each format is loaded by a slot of its resource handler (vf3, .vid vf4) whose code checks the tag; the loader column gives the function holding that check and, where it differs, the handler's vtable.
