A texture file is a TEXR header followed by a standard DDS header and the pixel levels it carries. The loader 0x5030EC accepts TEXR version 8 and SLVT version 4 (a small header that wraps a TEXR ). Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- 0x00 char[4] TEXR 0x04 u32 version, 8 0x08 / 0x09 u8 log2 of the described width / height, rounded down (37,747 / 37,749 of 37,749) 0x0A u8 log2 of the depth (0 for 2D) 0x0B u8 mip count of the described texture (37,747 of 37,749) 0x0C u8 kind: 1 = 2D (37,749), 3 = volume (632) 0x0D u8 format class (table) 0x10 u16 name length 0x12 char[] name (no NUL) name end u8 3, u16 width, u16 height, u16 1, u8 mips, u8 1, u8 DXGI format the described texture (2D; a volume has u8 5, width, height, depth, mips, format) name end + 17, + 20 u8 x 2 the tier bytes (below), always equal name end + 19 u8 sRGB flag name end + 23 DDS header (with a DX10 extension when the format needs one), then the levels in this file Class DXGI format (files) --- --- 0 BC1 UNORM (7,938) 1 BC2 UNORM (142) 2 BC3 UNORM (17,296) 3 BC4 UNORM (86) 4 BC5 UNORM (7) 5 uncompressed: B8G8R8A8 UNORM (8,064), R16 UNORM (4,109), R11G11B10 FLOAT (5) 7 BC7 UNORM (88) 8 BC6H UF16 (14) The stored DXGI format is always the UNORM one; the sRGB flag marks color textures (set on 5,128 of 5,203 d diffuse maps, 1 of 4,712 n normal maps, 17 of 3,485 s maps, 95 of 2,511 m masks). Texture creation (0x1E71F0) maps each format to a typeless / UNORM / sRGB triplet from the table at 0x2777E20. Normal maps store X in green and Y in alpha (the shaders decode (G 2 - 1, A 2 - 1) ); s maps store reflectance in red, a mask in green and roughness in blue.

A texture can ship in up to three files with the same stem: File Archives Levels it carries, against the size its own header describes --- --- --- .tex bundles, regions, patches the whole chain from that size, or from half of it when the name field points at a .tex0 (2,697 files) .tex0 HighMip (9,037), Benchmark , patches 3 levels from half the size (7,879) or 4 levels from the size (3,752) .texuhd uhdmip , uhdmip DLC1 - DLC4 (8,752), Benchmark , patches exactly one level, the described size (10,297 of 10,297) The tiers of one texture do not always describe the same size: the .tex0 and .texuhd of a stem agree in 5,873 of 6,165 stems, a .tex and its .tex0 in 497 of 1,037, and the level ranges of neighboring tiers can overlap. The name field of a .tex0 or .texuhd names its own .tex (21,928 of 21,928); a .tex names its .tex0 (2,697) or itself (1,083); 12,673 world textures under worlds\ leave it empty. Only .tex and .texa files are bundle members (61,622 and 7,949 container members, no higher tier in any container or manifest); the higher tiers are loose entries streamed after base data (see Resource streaming). For the Ranger's starting sword the diffuse ships at 512 x 1024 ( .tex , 11 levels), 1024 x 2048 ( .tex0 , 3 levels) and 2048 x 4096 ( .texuhd , 1 level). Which tiers the engine asks for is written in the base file. Its two tier bytes after the name agree in all 17,821 shipped 2D container textures: Tier bytes Meaning Textures --- --- --- 0 this file holds the whole chain 6,795 1 one level less, plus a .tex0 3,008 2 one level less, plus a .tex0 and a .texuhd 8,018 The loader asks for a tier by the base file's own path with the extension swapped (0x3E0BD4), never by the name field. With tier bytes of 2 and no level skipped it asks for the .texuhd ; otherwise it asks for the .tex0 . The number of levels skipped is max(0, 2 - TextureQuality + (tiered ? 1 : 0) - bias) (0x5019F4), with the quality setting at [base+0x2A374A4] . The bytes at 0x08, 0x09 and 0x0B are a second copy of the described size, equal to the one after the name in 17,820 of 17,821 files, and they are what the texture object keeps ( +0x60 , written by 0x6A10C0; the object is created by 0x6A0C30). The GOG and Microsoft Store builds ship without the uhdmip archives, so they lack most .texuhd files (see Game builds). Texture arrays ( TEXA v1, 1,946 files: .texa , .texa0 , .texauhd ) carry a header, their own path and the source path of each slice, then a DX10 DDS whose array size is the slice count, slices stored one after another with full mip chains. In a measured area of Cirith Ungol they textured about 90% of the static world's triangles (see World).

Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- 0x00 char[4] MMSH 0x04 u32 version, 17 0x08 u32 bytes from 0x14 to the descriptor block 0x0C u32 descriptor block size 0x10 u32 4 + all buffer bytes 0x14 u32 0xEBAEC3FA 0x18 u32 object record count N1 0x1C u32 arena count N2 0x20 u32 x N1, i32 x N1 per object record: flags, and its arena (-1 = not drawn) then u32 x N2 three times per arena: vertex bytes, index bytes, palette bytes then descriptor block, starting with 0x1A1541BC then u32 0x95DBDB69 then the arenas' vertex, index and palette bytes All 711 loose meshes follow this exactly: the arena sizes add up to the rest of the file and every arena index is in range or -1. The descriptor block holds: - at +0x2C the cull distance (500 on 376 meshes, 400 on 153, 140 on 126), and at +0x30 a bounding sphere (center, radius); - one 48-byte record per arena, {u32 vertex bytes, u32 index bytes, u32 palette bytes, u32 group count, u16[16] LOD triangle ladder} , the ladder rising to the arena's triangle count (index bytes / 6: 16-bit indices), found for 4,377 of 4,377 arenas; - the object records again, as 16-byte {flags, object id, arena, material slot} entries, where an object's consecutive records are its LOD chain. The groups are listed in one table of 40-byte records inside the descriptor block, arena after arena: +0x00 vertex count, +0x04 first index, +0x08 index count, +0x10 palette length and +0x1C a vertex-format id whose stride is fixed per file ( +0x0C , +0x14 .. +0x1B and +0x20 .. +0x27 are not covered by the sums below). For every arena, the vertex counts times their format's stride add up to its vertex bytes, the index counts times 2 add up to its index bytes and the palette lengths add up to its palette bytes, and the index ranges follow on from 0. A search of the block for a table that closes in this way finds it in all 348 distinct loose meshes (the 711 loose entries without copies), with 2,124 arenas and 2,569 groups; 93 of the meshes have an arena drawn as more than one group. An arena is drawn as one or more groups that share its buffers; a group's vertices are two streams: - stream A, 16 bytes per vertex: half4 position with w = 1, ubyte4 weights summing to 255, ubyte4 indices into the group's palette; - stream B, the rest of the stride (60, 64, 68, 72 ... bytes in all): the UV area, then normal, tangent and binormal as float3 at stride - 40 , - 28 , - 16 , and a 4-byte color. UV0 is a float32 pair at +0 on stride 68 and +8 on stride 72; one LOD chain can mix strides. Weights are stored in BGRA order against RGBA indices: the weight of index slot k is byte (2, 1, 0, 3)[k] . A palette byte indexes the skeleton's name-table order, not its bind order. Shipped weapons and armor. The Numenorean sword ( player numenoreanswordt1.mesh ) has its grip at the origin, the blade along +Y, the width along Z and the thickness along X (bounds X +-4.35, Y -34.9 to 102.1, Z +-7.74 cm). It has 810 vertices and 1,320 triangles on one bone, Twitch , a stride of 64 and a cull distance of 140. Blades are about four times thicker than real ones (9.23 x 2.30 cm at y = 16). Tangents run along +dP/du and binormals along +dP/dv (median 0.996 and 0.997 over 16 weapon and armor meshes). Player weapons mostly ship one LOD (57 of 93) with 1:2 textures (81 of 93) and 1,500 - 2,348 LOD0 triangles; orc and olog weapons 1,334 - 1,996 LOD0 triangles with 1:1 textures (56 of 77). LOD chains follow two presets, 1 : 0.50 : 0.125 (a falchion: 2,000 / 1,000 / 250) and 1 : 0.7 : 0.4 : 0.2. Armor LOD0: helmets 1,661 - 2,857, chests 3,741 - 6,275, shoulder pairs 2,551 - 4,158 (both shoulders in one skinned mesh, vertex alpha 16 on the left and 64 on the right), legs 1,996 - 2,573.

0x00 'SKEL' 0x04 u32 x 16: [0] version 17, [1] header size 64, [2] string blob size, [3] string count (= [6] + [7]), [4] bone count, [5] bone bytes (= 37 x [4]), [6] .anix library count, [7] mesh-part count, [8] socket count, [9] bone count again, [15] extra animation track count 0x44 bounds: f32 radius, f32 min[3], f32 max[3] 0x60 mesh parts, each u32 LOD count + 14-byte LOD entries 0xDCDCFF00, string blob (offset 0 = empty string) bones, 37 bytes each, depth-first: {u32 name offset, u8 deform, f32 position[3], f32 rotation[4] (x, y, z, w), u32 child count} masks {u32 name, u32 bone count, u32, u8 value per bone}, sockets {u32 bone, u32 name, f32 rotation[4], f32 position[3], f32 scale} 0xDCDCFF01 string offsets (.anix libraries, then part names), 0xDCDCFF02 one flag per library, 0xDCDCFF03 one byte per bone 0xDCDCFF04 Havok cloth: u32 count, count string offsets, the cloth tagfiles 0xDCDCFF05 GPU cloth list: u32 count, count x {u32 0xBEEFFEED, u16 length + .cres path, f32 x5, u32, f32 x2, u32, f32} 0xDEADDEAD, 0xDCDCFF99 skeleton physics The loader (0x504420) reads the tail in that order. All 24,378 skeleton sections in the bundles carry the GPU cloth list, ending exactly on the two closing markers; 132 of them name a cloth file, 153 carry Havok cloth (see Cloth). All 973 loose skeletons satisfy the header identities and carry the five markers in order; their 73,958 bones all hold unit quaternions. The largest has 241 bones; the orc base rig ( orcs\base\orc base.skel ) has 100, the player's 128, a Gondorian's 95 and the olog's 89. Vertex palettes and the live pose arrays index bones in the skeleton's name-table order, not in the depth-first record order. Binds are in model space, in centimeters, Y up. Header word 15 counts extra animation tracks. Each has a name, a P919 type and default bytes, stored after the bone records, and the masks then carry a value for every bone and every extra track. Of the 4,589 distinct shipped skeletons, 8 have them (the head parameter rig with 235, a camera rig with 40, shields and a crossbow). Read this way, all 4,589 distinct skeletons, bundled and loose, are accounted for byte for byte.

0x00 'SKDB' u32 9 u32 header size 0x1C u32 key count u32 narrow-row count (0) u32 text units u32 narrow-text size (0) 0x1C key count x {u32 key hash, u32 text offset}, strictly ascending by hash then UTF-16LE text, NUL-terminated strings, exactly text units code units to the end of the file Every shipped table follows this (140 of 140: version, header size, strictly ascending keys, offsets in range, text ending at the file's end). There is one table per file and no per-language section: each language folder ships its own string.strdb and string uwp.strdb . The English table has 68,547 keys. A key is StringHash of the key name and an offset counts UTF-16 units: UI 1Sword Starting N (0xDCDB4713) reads "Urfael". Several keys can share one string. The engine looks a key up with a lower-bound search over the rows (0x472104 - 0x472134); its loaded table (vf1 0x1D23114) keeps the row count at +0x0C , the rows at +0x10 , the narrow rows at +0x18 and the UTF-16 text at +0x30 . Shadow of Mordor's string tables use the same format (10 languages of 32,643 keys).

Format Parsed --- --- LTAR archives / records 76 / 76 archives, 488,752 records, 16,302 folders; first chunk of every entry decoded names against content 482,736 / 482,736 typed entries path indexes 37 archives, 73,038 / 73,038 rows hash-exact BNDL 225,338 / 225,338 EMBB headers / chains 190,407 / 190,407 headers; 780 / 780 sampled chains exact (319 containers over 64 MB not walked) manifest mirrors container 186,478 / 190,407 (the rest list members the container lacks) TEXR 38,381 / 38,381 headers TEXA 1,946 / 1,946 version 1 MMSH 711 / 711 headers; 4,377 / 4,377 arena records SKEL 973 / 973 headers; 73,958 bones SKDB 140 / 140 CRES 827 / 827 distinct payloads (1,723 bundle sections, 232 loose entries) parsed to their last byte and re-emitted byte for byte SKEL tail (bundles) 24,378 / 24,378 skeleton sections: GPU cloth list exact

- What the record bytes 1 and 9 encode beyond selecting the chunked reader, and what the archive header flags at 0x14 / 0x18 / 0x1C switch: every shipped archive has the same values, so only the code that reads archive+0x28..+0x2A and the size words' top bytes can tell. - What the engine looks up in the hash - path table besides copying it to the load stage; the callers of the merged table at fs+0x80 are not traced. - Whether a loose member always replaces a container section, or only when its archive is above the container's: the measured Desert case has the loose copy higher. A bundle whose only loose member sits below its container would settle it. - Whether the engine reads more than one copy of database\game\game.gamedb ; the GameDB loader's use of the archives would settle it. - Whether anything outside the executable reads Blade.arch06 and Lithlad.arch06 . Inside it, nothing does: neither archive is in the config list or the live mount vector, no string in the executable names either archive or dlc\blade.txt / dlc\lithlad.txt , and the third caller of Mount , vt 0x22BF9C8 vf2 0x11ACD04, is a generic "mount this path and report success" method. - Whether the files of the folders the folder search cannot find are reached by another path (the merged hash table at fs+0x80 , or the next archive in search order). The search can miss folders: 0x3DDB90 binary-searches the archive's folder array ( +0x40 , 0x30-byte entries, count +0x48 ) with strnicmp , whose length its main caller 0x3DDAD8 passes as 0x105, and a mounted archive keeps its folders in the on-disk order (79 of 79 mounted archives compared, the seven below included). Replaying that search over every archive, 15 of 16,302 folders cannot be found, and every one of them is a name that is a prefix of a neighbor: bundles\dlc4 in Patch 09 , Patch 10 and Patch DLC4 ; in HighMip the prefab folders fort\stairsfortwallb and stairsfortwallc , wilderness\human\mdbuildingb , flair\mystic\mystwalllow , volcano\architecture\bridge\walkway and balrogpit\balrogpltfrm 05bot ; in uhdmip mystwalllow03 and balrogpltfrm 05bot2 ; in uhdmip DLC4 stairsfortwallb , mdbuildingb and mystwalllow ; and stairsfortwallb2 in Benchmark . The case that decides it: 11 of the 20 files in Patch DLC4 's bundles\dlc4 (the fourth story DLC's cinematic render bundles cin render d4can and cin render d4fin ) exist in no other archive, its LC twin included, so if those cinematics load, the engine reaches the files without this search.

t: GameDB: schema, records and field bindings

x: The game's data lives in one database, database\game\game.gamedb , stored in hotchunk.arch06 (56,759,100 bytes; see Archives and file formats). The running game's database is this copy: its 2,742 categories, 278,865 named (secondary) records and 415,767 inline (primary) records match the file one for one, with the same names in the same order. The same container, GADB version 17, also carries the behavior graphs ( .bvr , root type BlendDB ; see Animation) and the database inside every effect file (see Visual effects). Offset Type Meaning (value in the game database) --- --- --- 0x00 char[4] GADB 0x04 u32 version, 17 0x08 u32 size of the string block, root type name included (10,412,928) 0x0C u32 category count (2,742) 0x10 u32 secondary record count (278,865) 0x14 u32 primary record count (415,767) 0x18 u32 total cell count over all records (8,544,670) 0x1C u32 descriptor count (361,939) 0x20 u32 build tag (copied to the loaded database, +0x28 ; 0xD186F247 in the game database) 0x24 u32 in a patch database, the build tag of the base it was made for; 0 in a base database (copied to +0x2C ) 0x28 u32 44 0x2C u16 + chars the database path ( database\game\game.gamedb ) The string block follows. Its offset 0 is the root type name ( GameDatabase\0 ), and every offset in the file is measured from there: names, string values, and the binary values the file stores once and shares (float pairs, vectors, UTF-16 strings). Names are stored whole, never as the tail of a longer string: of the 181,736 distinct record-name offsets, 179,567 follow a NUL and the other 2,169 follow binary values of the block. Then come the field descriptors, 15 bytes each: Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- +0x00 u32 P919 hash of the field name (see Names and hashing below) +0x04 u32 the run's hashes in ascending order (entry k holds the k-th smallest) +0x08 u8 field index (declaration order) +0x09 u8 the run position of the descriptor that holds the k-th smallest hash +0x0A u8 type code +0x0B u16 element count +0x0D u16 link: the record's first cell for this field The value section starts with u32 0 and the category count. Each category is a 24-byte entry followed by its primaries, then its secondaries: Category entry Meaning --- --- u32 name (string offset): the path with / separators, AI/Templates u32 type name, dot-separated: AI.Template u32 source path ( \AI\Templates\gdb.category06 ; empty for inline-structure categories) u32 / u32 primary count / secondary count u32 sort key = P919 of the name Record field Primary Secondary --- --- --- name - u32 string offset cell count u16 u16 descriptor count u8 u8 first descriptor (index into the descriptor array) u32 u32 flag byte 0 (all 415,767) 8 (all 278,865) cells cell count x 4 bytes cell count x 4 bytes Categories are stored in ascending sort-key order, and all 2,742 sort keys equal P919 of the name. Inside a category the secondaries are stored in ascending P919 of their names (1,371 of 1,371 categories with two or more; no two names in one category share a hash). Both orders exist for the binary searches below. The file ends with a u32 count of a (u32, u32) pair table (the loaded database's +0x68 ); the game database's is 0, and the walk over the value section lands exactly on it. A file cell is 4 bytes: a word of Bools, a float, an integer, a string-block offset (string, enum name, wide string, float pair, vector) or an encoded RecordLink.

The loader 0x503694 (called from 0x74CF10) reads the 0x2C-byte header, refuses anything but GADB version 17 and sizes two allocations from the counts: an arena of categories x 0x58 + (descriptors + 2 x primaries) x 16 + secondaries x 0x28 + 0x88 bytes for the tables (30,491,600 for the game database), and an instance block of cells x 8 + 0x88 bytes for the values (68,357,496). Descriptors widen from 15 to 16 bytes. The record reader 0x4BA1F0 reads each 4-byte cell into an 8-byte cell. For every field of type 4 to 9 (strings, enums, wide strings, float pairs, vectors; the type test 0x4BA364 also accepts 12 to 16, which the game database does not use) it adds the string block's address to the cells, turning offsets into pointers into the block, which stays resident. A second pass, 0x4BAF6C, finishes two types: - StringEnum (5): the cell is replaced by StringHash of the string it points at. - RecordLink (10 and 11): the descriptor's type byte is rewritten to 10 ( and 0xCA; or 0x0A , flag bits kept), and each element is resolved. Category = value 20; a category past the table gives null. Index = value & 0xFFFFF: an index below the category's primary count selects that primary, a larger one the secondary index - primary count , anything beyond both gives null. In the running game the string, wide-string, float-pair and vector cells equal the block's address plus the file's offset (721,156 of 721,164 strings, 210 of 210, 166,606 of 166,606 and 50,734 of 50,734).

A static object of class vt 0x1FBD460 at 0x2A68350 (constructed by 0x1B06B6C) owns the game database: +0x18 the database object ( [base+0x2A68368] ), +0x20 the path database\game\game.gamedb . Its vf3 0x1B09BBC fills the category cache (below). Every category header points back to the database at +0x18 . Four patch archives, Patch 01 to Patch 04 and their LC twins, also ship a complete database\game\game.gamedb (58.08-58.10 MB against the HotChunk copy's 56.76 MB). Their headers name older builds: 2,435 to 2,438 categories against 2,742, and different build tags. The running game has 2,742 categories, so it loads the HotChunk copy and the older copies are shadowed by the archive search order, not merged. Of the 488,679 entries in the shipped archives, the only game databases are the nine copies above, and none is a patch database.

The loader can merge a second database into the game database as it loads: a patch, database\game\game.gamedb patch , which overrides records of the same name and appends new ones. No patch ships, and the shipped game never looks for one, because the loader asks for a patch only when the base database arrives through a stream that can seek. - Finding the patch. The GameDB resource class's load (vf3 0x17662B0, classes vt 0x22F34F8 and vt 0x22F5368) first asks the base stream whether it can seek (the stream's slot 3). A stream that cannot seek is read whole, and nothing else happens. Otherwise the loader reads the header and the database's own embedded path (header +0x2C ). It stops there when that path is empty (0x472C84), when it already ends in gamedb patch (0x1BEC90 compares the text after the last dot) or when the switch byte 0x266CD70 is 0 (it is 1 in the executable, and nothing writes it). Otherwise it swaps the extension (0x17AA78), asks the file system for database\game\game.gamedb patch and loads that through itself. Without the resource system, the loose-file route 0x1C3FF20 looks for <name [ <suffix ].gamedb patch beside a loose base (the format %s at 0x1FE1A80). - Which streams seek. An archive entry stored as Oodle chunks, as every shipped entry is (see Archives and file formats), opens as vt 0x1E70F88, whose slot 3 answers no. A raw entry opens as vt 0x1E70F00, which seeks: its vf4 0x11DC2D4 moves the inner file stream to start + position. The memory stream vt 0x1E6D228 and the loose-file stream vt 0x1E70EA8 seek as well. The merge therefore runs when the copy of game.gamedb that wins the search order is a raw entry or a loose file; the patch itself may be chunked, in which case it is read whole. - The build tag. A patch is kept only when its header word at +0x24 equals the base's build tag ( +0x20 ): 0x503694 compares the two, and 0x4BAD00 stores a database's two words at +0x28 / +0x2C . Shipped databases hold 0 at +0x24 (the running game database: +0x28 = 0xD186F247, +0x2C = 0), so a patch names the build it was made for, and one that names no build is dropped. - Room. For each base category, 0x4BA07C hashes the name ( StringHash , seed 0), finds the patch's category of that name (0x115B4D4) and sizes the record array for the base's and the patch's secondaries together (0x28 bytes each). A patch category without a base category of that name is skipped: a patch can grow categories, never add one. - Records. 0x4BAB60 takes each patch secondary in turn and binary-searches the base category for its name hash (0x278540). A match is overridden by the patch record (0x17675FC); a miss is appended after the category's last secondary, and the category's byte +0x30 is set to 1 (no longer sorted). - Links. Three passes (0x1766F08 - 0x1766E54 - 0x1766F70 / 0x1766FE4 - 0x1766BB0) go over every patch record, primaries included, and re-parent it to the base category of its name. A StringEnum string becomes its hash. A type-11 link ( category << 20 index ) is resolved inside the patch and re-typed 10, so a patch carries its own structure instances. A type-10 cell is an index into the patch's import table ( db+0x68 ), whose pairs name a category and a record by hash; it resolves to the base record of that name when there is one, else to the patch's own. The last pass re-points every link to the final record of its name. - The import table is the file's trailer: after the last category, a u32 count and that many (u32, u32) pairs, read into db+0x68 (0x4B9C52 - 0x4B9D37). Both shipped databases, this game's and Shadow of Mordor's, have a count of 0 and store their type-10 cells directly as category << 20 index (8,302 of 8,302 non-null cells sampled here, 7,276 of 7,276 in Mordor's): the by-name form exists for patches only. - Later tables see the new records. The start-up material-set cache, one entry per Model record by index, is built afterwards, in the subsystem initialization (0x1774278 - 0x1783DD0). In a running game, a patch that appended one Model record and one Model/SimpleModelPieces record raised those categories from 2,715 to 2,716 and from 1,727 to 1,728 records. Each new record's hash was the P919 of its name, both categories' +0x30 byte read 1, and the material-set cache's entry 2,715 held the new Model 's address. The new piece drew on a captain with the shipped meshes and textures its links named. Records that a save or an online upload refers to are stored by name. The reader 0x1BC159C - 0x1879468 - 0x187985C hashes the stored name and binary-searches one category; a name it does not find reads as null and is kept as such (the look reader 0x1C0546C writes the result straight into each appearance cell). A record that only a patch provides therefore loads as an empty value in a game started without that patch. The descriptor array ends exactly where the database object begins; the category array follows the object, and after it come each category's primaries and secondaries, in file order. Two rules place everything else, and both hold for the running game: - a record's descriptor run = descriptor array + 16 x first-descriptor index (686,399 of 686,401 records with fields); - a record's instance = instance block + 8 x (cells of all earlier records in file order) (694,628 of 694,632). Instances are therefore packed back to back: a record owns exactly cell count x 8 bytes, and reading past them reads the next record. In the running game the whole database lies below 4 GB, so the pointers in its cells have a zero high dword (166,606 of 166,606 float-pair cells).

FindDescriptor 0x25180C(record, &hash) (693 callers) uses them: with record flag 0x01 clear it calls FindDescriptorPermuted 0x251BD0, which binary-searches the +0x04 column and returns run + 16 x byte [entry+0x09] . Every record of a category declares the same fields in the same order (2,713 of 2,713 categories that hold records). What can differ per record is the element count of an array, and with it the links: 876 categories hold records with more than one layout ( Combat/Attack has 1,898 layouts over 16,976 records, Faction/Roles/Definitions 578 over 914). A cell is therefore found through the record's own run ( [rec+0x08] ), never through another record's. The links are part of the file: over 11,413,092 descriptor uses compared, the running game's descriptors equal the file's in hash, sorted column, field index, run position and type (11 read as 10) every time, in element count in all but 2 and in link in all but 1. The slot rule. Element i of a field is the 8-byte cell [rec+0x10] + (link + i) x 8 , for i below the element count; for any other i every getter returns the caller's default. A field with count 0 therefore has no value in that record, a scalar has count 1 whether it is set or not (a null RecordLink still has count 1), and an array of n elements occupies n consecutive cells. GetIntFast 0x278758 is the rule: movzx ecx, dl ; cached descriptor index shl rcx, 4 add rcx, [r10+8] ; descriptor = run + index 16 movzx eax, word [rcx+0Ch] ; element count cmp r8d, eax jae default movzx ecx, word [rcx+0Eh] ; link mov rax, [r10+10h] ; instance add ecx, r8d mov eax, [rax+rcx 8] ; cell link + element Bools are bits. A Bool's link is a bit index: the value is bit link & 31 of the 32-bit word in cell link 5 (GetBoolFast 0x274AE8; MakeFieldRef 0x2775C0 builds the same cell pointer and bit). In the 13,612 distinct loaded runs every Bool has count 1, and read this way none of them shares a cell with a non-Bool field of its run (52,003 of the 60,879 would if the link were a cell number). Up to 32 Bools share one word, so a Bool is changed as a single bit. Live cell i is file cell i. Comparing every cell of every record with the file: integers equal in 640,915 of 641,086 cells, floats in 900,372 of 900,436, Bools in 2,943,742 of 2,943,938 (the same bit rule applies to the file's 4-byte cells) and string values in 721,086 of 721,164.

The file stores each distinct string, float pair and vector once, and every cell that holds that value points at the same bytes; loading keeps the sharing. The 166,606 float-pair cells point at 3,071 distinct pairs: (0, 0) is shared by 72,774 cells across the database, (1, 1) by 17,492, (100, 200) by 13,591, (0.25, 0.25) by 13,257 and (0, 200) by 10,743. The 50,734 vector cells point at 2,596 distinct vectors, one all-zero vector serving 25,616 cells. Writing the floats behind such a pointer changes every field that shares them; storing a different pointer in one cell changes that field alone.

In the file a link is (category ordinal << 20) index , where the ordinal is the category's position in the hash-sorted table (the loaded header's +0x2C ) and the index counts the category's primaries first, then its secondaries. 0xFFFFFFFF is null; 0 is a real link (category 0, primary 0). In memory the cell holds the target's header address. In the running game 5,204,006 link cells hold 3,471,923 nulls (0xFFFFFFFF in the file, every one), 1,316,316 pointers to secondaries and 415,767 to primaries, and none point anywhere else. Every link to a primary targets a Structures category and every link to a secondary targets another category, so once both file types read 10, the target category tells which side a link addresses. Of the 1,732,083 non-null cells, 1,732,055 hold exactly the record the file's link names. Links carry no type. GetLinkCellFast 0x30E7B4 returns the cell as it is; GetLinkCellByName 0x68BB08 checks only that the field is a RecordLink ( type & 0x3F == 10 ) and that the element exists. Which category a field should point into is recorded only in its registration (a public <Type annotation, Inventory.Item for an item link). The code that follows a link treats the target as the declared type, so a link to a record of another category is read with the wrong layout.

A record with flag 0x10 is not addressed by the slot rule: its instance is a native structure laid out by its type's slots (SlotOffset 0x251C24, size step 0x251CAC), the by-name getters divert to the reflected path (GetLinkCellByName - ReadLinkReflected 0x16CE2E8 - ReadReflectedField 0x5DA158) and MakeFieldRef hands such records to 0x60B5FC. Every record of the loaded behavior graphs carries 0x1A (see Animation); no record of the game database sets the bit.

The slot is reached through the type entry: 0x166858 tests [[0x266CB70]+0x78] = 2 (slot 1's state), 0x166868 reads [[0x266CB70]+0x88] (its index), 0x1822494 returns [0x266CB70]+0x68 (its hash). The fast path applies the cached index to any record of the type, which is sound because the field order is fixed per category. Every type has a fast and a by-name getter (callers are distinct functions): Type Fast By name Native-structure path --- --- --- --- Bool GetBoolFast 0x274AE8 (1,634) 0x1157114 (1,850) - Float GetFloatFast 0x30E6B4 (1,517) GetFloatByName 0x115B43C (1,539) 0x5DA0FC Int GetIntFast 0x278758 (1,010) 0x1169594 (1,015) 0x176CE98 String GetStringFast 0x1CB3B0 (1,165) 0x115A54C (1,184); by hash 0x1152454 (537) 0x16CE290 float pair GetFloatRangeFast 0x311320 (354) not traced - RecordLink GetLinkCellFast 0x30E7B4 (5,215); copy 0x30E7A4 (537) 0x115AE24 / 0x68BB08 0x16CE2E8 Writers and array walkers use field references: MakeFieldRef 0x2775C0(out, record, descriptor) (2,085 callers) builds {+0x00 record, +0x08 cell pointer, +0x18 u16 type, +0x1A u16 count, +0x1C u8 Bool bit, +0x20 hash} ; MakeFieldRefByName 0x1957C4 adds FindDescriptor. FieldIterBegin 0x465A78 adds an index ( +0x28 ) and the count ( +0x2C ), and FieldIterAtEnd 0x2774A8 compares them.

t: Who reads a field, and when
x: Static analysis of the slots names the code that reads each field: 39,960 functions touch the slot of a GameDB field, and 13,425 call a one-field accessor. Following the value out of every read classifies 12,789 fields: Use Fields A changed cell takes effect --- --- --- used where read (compared, computed with, passed on) 8,685 the next time the reader runs copied into an object or a global 2,275 when the copying code runs again both 695 partly at once, partly at the next copy stored into an unresolved container 144 not determined returned only / unclassified 112 / 878 not determined A copied pointer value (a float pair, a vector, a RecordLink) stays live for the values behind it: changing the pair's floats is seen through the copy, while pointing the cell elsewhere is seen only after the next copy. When a copy is refreshed depends on what runs the copier: - Movement values. 0x187F94C(movement object, movement record) copies three Client/PlayerMovement fields into the player's movement object [player+0x2F88] : BaseSpeedMultiplier to +0x550 (the character's own +0x550 is unrelated and reads 0), FallMinHeight to +0x558 , and PlayerYawInterpolateTime (an integer, converted to float and scaled) to +0x554 . It keeps the record at +0x548 ; given the record it already holds, it returns without copying. 0x187F71C passes the record named PlayerMovement , found by name in the cached Client/PlayerMovement category. A change to that record's cells is therefore not seen by this consumer until a different movement record is applied and the original is applied again. - Per-event copies refresh at every event: StructuresCombatAttackData.AOE and AOEOnStart are copied by 0x2DED44, which runs under every attack start, so a change applies to the next attack. - Start-up and load compilers do not refresh on their own: the targeting cache 0x1C0B634 and the attack cache (see Combat), the material-set cache 0x1B6190C (see Characters), item prompt links (see Items) and the AudioHooks cache, which the audio thread compiles at load (see Audio and video).

t: Changing values in a running game
x: - A cell is plain memory: the getters read it on every call, with no lock, checksum or cache in between (the fast getters above are the whole read path). Whether a change is seen is decided by the readers' copies above. - Only the cells a record's own run claims belong to it: a field with count 0 has no cell, and an element written past a field's count lands in another field of the same record, or past the instance in the next record. - A Bool shares its word with up to 31 others; a whole-cell write changes all of them. - A StringEnum cell takes P919 of the enum name; a String, wide-string, float-pair or vector cell takes a pointer, and the bytes it points at are shared by every cell with the same value. A String list is stored inline, one pointer per element at consecutive cells; the strings are shared, the record instances are not, so pointing one record's cell at other text changes that record alone, while writing the text changes every record that names it. A string pointer need not be 8-aligned: strings in the block start at 4-byte boundaries. - A record's identity is its category, not its address. The engine's "Bad record index" assert (the string at 0x1F68DB0, used at 535 sites in 432 functions) compares the record's category [rec+0x18] with the expected one at 534 of those sites; the remaining site (0x10F903E) is a range test. Lookups by index then go through RecordIndexOf 0x1898E8, which is plain pointer arithmetic with no check. A copy of a record made elsewhere in memory therefore passes the assert and yields a meaningless index. At 477 sites the code that follows checks the index's range and compares keys, so the lookup misses and returns 0; at 10 it checks the range only; at 45 no check follows within 28 instructions. - A part drawn from a Model record that is not in the start-up material-set cache faults. The cache (0x1B6190C, [GameManager+0x6DD0]+0x18 , one 0x20-byte entry per Model record, by record index) is built once. Building a part queries it through 0x1BDA60 - 0x104338 - 0x1041C4 - 0x104258, which misses and returns 0 for a record outside the table; the caller 0x104234 then reads through that null pointer on the main thread. - Some per-character state is sized from a record only once. A character's state-effect manager [char+0x2B78] sizes its effect slots to the count of Character/StateEffects.CharacterFXPredicates when it is built (0x435F38 - 0x435E6C, "CCharacterStateEffectMgr can only be initialized once."), which happens when the character's identity is set. Its per-frame update 0x16AC90, however, takes slot i for the list's current i-th entry, with no bound. If the list is made longer while such characters exist, the update reads past the end of their slot vector (0x114ED48), or, where the memory there holds 0, stores a new effect past it (0x16B27B). - A RecordLink cell accepts any record: neither the getters nor the cell know the declared target, so nothing stops a link to a record of the wrong category, and its consumer reads that record with the declared type's layout.

- Apart from the AudioHooks records, which the audio thread compiles at load, which categories are read off the main thread (render, audio, input polling, animation jobs), so that a change can race its reader? Camera, interface world-UI, audio control values, input profiles, native wildlife, AI sensors and the weather and lighting structures are the candidates; sampling the field readers per thread, or tracing their callers to the thread routines, would settle it. - Do loads rebuild record instances from the file? A changed cell can return to the file's value after a loading screen, yet changed cells can also survive a region change; whether a load re-reads the instance block, and on which path, is not traced. - Whether anything re-sorts a category whose +0x30 byte a patch append has set; appended names that hash above the category's largest keep the order either way. - Which container sets record flag 0x01 (runs sorted by their own hashes): no game-database record sets it, and the byte scan that settled flag 0x08 finds 352 tests of some object's byte +0x01 against 1, which it cannot tell apart from record tests. - The meaning of the database's +0x58 / +0x60 and the type entry's +0x38 flags. (The build tag at +0x28 is checked only against a patch database's +0x2C , above.) - What the loader's rebasing test for types 12 to 16 is for. No shipped container uses them: the 314 GameDB containers in the archives (the game databases and every behavior graph) use only types 1-11 and 68, and the 1,310 world parts' property databases only types 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8.

t: World: regions, layers, placements and world objects
x: A region's world is a set of world parts , each streamed in as a section and turned into a world context full of placed objects. This chapter describes the parts on disk, the streamer that loads them, the objects they create and the world data that the rest of the engine queries.

The game has eight regions. Each has one main part ( worlds\retail\<folder \<folder , the only part with terrain) and a set of layers under worlds\retail\<folder \sectionsandlayers\ : story and side content, fortress pieces, lighting and its per-Overlord variants. In all, 1,303 layers ship (each identified by the paths its own container lists, never by its archive entry name): Folder Region Layers --- --- --- volcano Gorgoroth 243 snowmtn Seregost 239 island Nurnen 228 mtnpass Cirith Ungol 228 desert Lithlad 221 minasithil Minas Ithil 138 blackgates the Black Gate 4 baraddur Barad-dur 2 Seven regions have a region archive and a lighting archive ( <folder .arch06 , <folder lighting.arch06 ), and the patch archives add and replace parts. Lithlad has neither: its main part and all 221 of its layers are in the patch archives (the containers in Patch DLC4 , with standalone .objres and .scripts copies in later patches). A world part is an EMBB container (see Archives and file formats). Every layer carries its own prefab ( .inst ), and 1,302 of 1,303 layers carry the same eight further parts, named after the layer: .objres (the object registry below), .terrain , .hkai (navigation mesh), .wldclnt (static placements), .veggrid , .scripts (its script; see Scripting), .uis and .uiwd ; then the prefabs, meshes, materials, textures and effects it uses (176 layers also carry a world mesh, .wldmsh ). A layer's .terrain is an empty 12-byte section; only main parts carry terrain. Across all 1,311 parts (1,303 layers and 8 main parts) the object registries place 1,247,824 objects of 156 classes . The most common: AINodeMenacePlace 113,874, AINavMeshObstacle 67,714, SpecialFX 67,460, DynamicObjectGroupState 67,361, ScriptRelay 56,290, StaticLightOctreeBias 54,700, FireVolume 50,718, AISpawnerAmbientNormal 49,769, LightCube 47,771, Group 43,956, VolumeController 35,992. Patched registries win. The engine does not load the registry embedded in a part when a patch archive ships a standalone .objres for that part (2,753 standalone registries ship). Lithlad's main registry in a running game is the copy in Patch DLC5 (161,821 context-action lines), not the one embedded in the Patch DLC4 container (161,828) or the copies in Patch 09 / Patch 10 (161,836). Layer scripts follow the same rule (see Scripting).

t: How a region's world is assembled

x: WorldBundleMgr ( GameSystems\Core\WorldBundleMgr.cpp ) is [GM+0x6D90] . It keeps a registry vector of world bundle groups at +0x00 / +0x08 (145 groups in Lithlad, each pointing back to the manager at +0x240 ). The scene tick walks the groups (see Threads and the frame) and services only those whose want-load byte +0x252 is set. A group (0x258 bytes, constructor 0x1D297EC) is the head of a circular list of entries: +0x00 the first entry, +0x08 the last, closing back on the group in both directions. +0x251 set disables the duplicate check, +0x252 is the want-load gate. An entry (0x168 bytes, vt 0x1DB6558) is one requested section: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x34 u32 id = StringHash(path) (127 of 127) +0x38 list links {next, prev} +0x48 the CResourceBundle of the section (vt 0x1E6E678, path equal to the entry's: 127 of 127) +0x50 the part's object-registry request (set on 126 of 127) +0x58 the bundle load request +0x63 the path, inline ( ...\<part .bndl ) AddSection 0x4B41CC(group, path, &id) calls 0x4B420C, which rejects an empty path, appends .bndl , returns the existing entry when the path is already requested in that group (0x4B1FE4) and otherwise links a new entry at the front of the list. RemoveSection 0x4B1BCC(group, id) releases every entry with that id (0x4B5C34). The entry exists as soon as it is requested, long before its content has streamed. Requests are de-duplicated per group only, so the same section requested through two groups is loaded twice. A plain bundle load (see Resource streaming) makes a part's resources resident without placing anything; a section requested through a group is what creates its world context and objects.

MainScene ( [base+0x26FFAB0] ) owns eight group slots. In Lithlad during play they held: Slot Gates Sections --- --- --- +0x720 none (the null group) +0x728 flag +0x250 set worlds\retail\desert\desert.bndl , the main part +0x730 flag set empty +0x738 worlds\retail\shared\wraith\lightingwraith.bndl and prefabs\ui\worlduimenuws.bndl +0x740 want-load 0 the quest group: sectionsandlayers\fortassault\fortassault.bndl +0x748 flag set the fortress: drakecollision , fortwallgameplay , fortwallprops , and sectionsandlayers\dynamicfort\ keeplarge , flairoutlawkeepl , flairoutlawworld , gatessimple , pourtrapsfire , fort wd +0x750 duplicate check off empty +0x758 flag set empty The lighting layer is requested by the weather manager in its own group ( [[GM+0x6D98]+0x20] ): the current weather pattern's Section field names it (see Rendering, "Weather"). In Lithlad the pattern was DS OL Outlaw Clear , whose Section is worlds\retail\desert\sectionsandlayers\ol outlaw.bndl , and that group held exactly that section. The ol layers are per-Overlord variants: Lithlad ships nine ( ol dark , ol feral , ol machine , ol marauder , ol mystic , ol outlaw , ol slaughter , ol terror , ol warmonger ) beside its plain night01..03 layers; Nurnen, Cirith Ungol and Seregost nine each (Nurnen's and Cirith Ungol's include a shared ol share01 ); Gorgoroth 27, each also in bd and bduc forms. Lithlad's ol outlaw holds what a lighting layer holds (1,104 SpecialFX , 959 LightCube , 612 Sound , 175 WorldModel ... and an AtmosphereVolume ), much like its night03 (1,492 SpecialFX , 959 LightCube , 612 Sound , 32 AtmosphereVolume s). Of the 68 groups with entries, 63 hold only the menus' 3D scenes. They are 86 sections under prefabs\ui\mordormap\ (the world map's region pieces such as minasmorgul.bndl , and each fortress's keep and gate pieces by tribe, fortworldsections\keeps\blackguard\bgrdflairped05.bndl ), 12 under prefabs\ui\store\ , 6 battle-report scenes and 8 region-faction scenes ( wuim ws.bndl ). In all, 127 sections were loaded, 13 of them from worlds\ . Conditional sections. At load MainScene+0x760 .. +0x768 receives 16-byte pairs {section record, u32 id} copied from the region's WorldInfo.ConditionalWorldSections . The evaluator 0x1DFAC8 (called from 0x1DF500) reads each section's StructuresWorldInfoConditionalSection.GameDataVariable : true with id 0 requests the section through [MainScene+0x758] (0x4B41CC); false with a nonzero id releases it (0x4B1BCC). Lithlad has none; Minas Ithil during the Shadow Wars has 12 (its pre-fall sections released, the post-fall ones loaded). Region travel. The script call System:LoadWorld(DBWorldInfo.<world ) on the main thread starts a region load within 0.1-0.2 s ( LoadWorldCustom , which no shipped script uses, shares its implementation 0x1780824). The current region record [[GM+0x6C68]+0x1B0] changes at the start of the load, before the destination's objects exist.

The objects of a streamed part live in a world context (vt 0x1DB5D58). The object update manager's object sets (see Threads and the frame) are these contexts: 129 of 129 sets in Lithlad carry that vtable, and every placed object points back to its own at +0x58 (105,946 of 105,946). A context's object-name table is [ctx+0x68] : 0x800 buckets of 0x18 bytes, bucket = hash & 0x7FF , list head at +0x08 ; the node is embedded in the object at +0x28 ( +0x08 next, +0x10 hash, +0x18 name). Of the 129 contexts, 20 had a table, holding 105,946 objects; the largest is the main part's. Matching each table against the shipped registries by object name: Part Objects in the file In the live table Same name Same rotation Position within 1 cm --- --- --- --- --- --- Lithlad main 95,205 90,863 90,546 90,510 70,240 fortwallprops 679 635 635 635 635 ol outlaw 5,545 5,545 5,545 5,455 5,398 Of the main part's names, 4,659 are not in the live table, among them every StartupCommand ( .SC ) and some MapCanvas objects ( .MCNV H ); 317 names exist only live ( Avian0 .. Avian11 , CTP D 103.CTP ...). The position differences are AI placements moved vertically : 20,211 of the 20,306 moved objects in the main part are AI nodes, ambient spawners and combat teleport points. In every one of those classes the median horizontal change is 0.0 cm, while the median vertical change is -47 to -285 cm ( AINodeMenacePlace 6,802 of 6,869 moved, median -181 cm; AISpawnerAmbientNormal 4,343 of 4,920, -150 cm; AINodeRetreat 432 of 432, -285 cm; CombatTeleportPoint 751 of 849, -47 cm). The other 95 moved objects belong to other classes.

A part's .objres is an OBJR chunk registry: 'OBJR' u32 13 u32 hash u32 block count block count x { u32 name hash u32 size payload } The chain ends exactly at the end of the section in 1,310 of 1,310 parts. Parts with context-action data carry 14 blocks (724 parts), the others 12 (no CAWR / CADB). Each block hash is StringHash of the name its handler registers with the resource manager ; the names sit together in the image at 0x1E6B4E8-0x1E6B6B0, 14 of 14: Tag Hash Engine name Handler (vf3) Content --- --- --- --- --- KEYF 0x9B011056 ObjRes.Keyframer vt 0x23017A0, 0x4BB804 key-framed motion paths SFXS 0xBE10C375 ObjRes.SpecialFx vt 0x2301300, 0x4BB9E4 static effect placements SWFX 0x71F34310 ObjRes.WeatherFx vt 0x2301468, 0x7C692C weather-gated effect points ONLS 0xACECAC8A ObjRes.ObjNameList vt 0x2301808, 0x4BBB80 group member lists NLFE 0x9F53FC59 ObjRes.NativeLife vt 0x22F3A08, 0x7C34B0 ambient-life emitters PFDG 0x22A69B09 ObjRes.PrefabDebug vt 0x22F3B78, 0x4B8554 the prefab tree for the debug viewer (none) 0xC3685E5B ObjRes.Clutter vt 0x22F3890, 0x4B680C instanced clutter meshes with geometry SCRB 0xD69D2456 ObjRes.ScriptBind vt 0x230EF30, 0x4B6B58 which script function runs for which object and event VOLM 0x8A27BAE6 ObjRes.VolumeDB loader 0x7B83B8 convex volume brushes (see Rendering) CAWR 0xA7ED4C13 ObjRes.ContextLineDB vt 0x2301110, 0x4B6368 context-line owner index CADB 0x8B7E18E7 cntx vt 0x1FF6B98, 0x501478 context-action lines GADB 0x29F76277 ObjRes.ObjProps the object property database (none) 0xB9E81CF3 ObjRes.WorldPhysics which prefab each dynamic object draws, and collision shapes OBJL 0xAE72B7E7 ObjRes.ObjList vt 0x22C0338, 0x502B8C the object list Across the 1,310 registries the blocks total 736 MB: ObjRes.WorldPhysics 416 MB, CADB 123 MB, OBJL 84 MB, VOLM 40 MB, GADB 23 MB, PFDG 18 MB, ONLS 14 MB, Clutter 11 MB, SCRB 3.1 MB, NLFE 2.2 MB; the rest are under 0.4 MB. Atmosphere volumes and their VOLM brushes are described in Rendering; the context-action blocks and SWFX have their own sections below.

'OBJL' u32 5 u32 sets u32 N u32 class bytes u32 name bytes u32 group bytes 0x1C class names, object names, group names (NUL-terminated string tables) then per set: u32 set hash u32 count count x 50-byte record (unaligned) Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- +0x00 u32 class name (offset into the class table) +0x04 u32 object name (offset into the name table) +0x08 u16 the prefab instance that placed the object (offset into the group table; 0xFFFF = none) +0x0A u32 index of the object's record in the property database +0x0E f32[3] position, world space (cm) +0x1A f32[4] rotation quaternion (x, y, z, w) +0x2A u32 0 +0x2E u32 the authoring id of the object's template (see below; not kept at load) The table ends exactly at the block end and every offset lands on a string start in 1,310 of 1,310 registries (re-read on five layers and Lithlad's main part, 104,489 objects; the 9,284 layer objects all have unit quaternions). The loader (vt 0x22C0338 vf3, 0x502B8C) expands each 50-byte record into an 0x50-byte run-time record: +0x08 the name, +0x10 the group offset, +0x14 StringHash(name) , +0x18 the property record index, +0x1C the position, +0x28 the quaternion, +0x38 the word at file +0x2A , +0x40 the class name. It builds, per object set, a table of {name hash, u16 index} pairs used to find an object by name. It reads the id at file +0x2E into a local and discards it: nothing at run time keys on it. The id is the authoring identifier of the object's template. Every copy of an object placed through the same prefab carries the same id (one AINodeMenacePlace prefab node: 9,275 copies over 74 parts share 0x2651E0E7; one hanging-light trigger: 8,749 copies over 109 parts). Objects authored directly in a part have their own: over the whole game, 1,247,824 objects carry 167,063 distinct ids, 151,160 of them used by a single object. The id never equals the hash of the object's name (0 of 1,247,824) and stays within one class (two exceptions: 0 on every WorldInitializer and WorldCollision object, and one pair of unrelated objects, as expected from chance collisions among 167,063 random 32-bit values). Most lists hold one set, the world set (hash 0x3BDE767D). Object names carry their prefab instance and their role: Barre 46.DOGS Fire , MesaE 08.VC NoHang , HideS 138.FP , pGCarags.spwCaptain . In all ten parts read, the list opens with a WorldInitializer object and then WorldCollision objects at the origin: PhysicsBSP (and LargeAIIgnore in some layers); Lithlad's main part has four ( PhysicsBSP , PlayerBlocker , CameraBlocker , LargeAIIgnore ).

ObjRes.ObjProps is a complete GameDB database (version 17) whose root type is ObjectPropertyDB , with the category ObjectDB and records named ObjectRec (see GameDB). An object's OBJL record index selects its record, and every property the object reads at creation comes from it. Records are de-duplicated: objects with identical properties share one (Minas Ithil night01 : 3,160 objects, 1,886 records; Lithlad main: 95,205 objects, 21,430 records). In a running game an object keeps its record at +0x50 .

Both key objects by StringHash(object name) . - ONLS lists the members of every grouping object: 'ONLS' u32 1 u32 area bytes u32 index bytes ; the area holds groups {u32 n, n x {u16 length, name}} , the index {u32 hash(owner), u32 offset of its group} sorted by hash. Over 400 layers 6,360 of 6,360 owners are objects of the part ( Group 5,515, AINodeRoute 735, AINodeSearch 83, static-light probes) and 107,097 of 107,097 member names exist in OBJL. A prefab instance's children ( Barre 00.DOGS Alive , .VC , .NMO , .FX P ...) form one group. - SCRB says which function of the part's script runs for which object and event: 'SCRB' u32 1 u32 string bytes u32 bindings u32 objects , then the strings, bindings {u32 hash(event), u32 event name, u32 hash(script resource path), u32 function name} and an object index {u32 hash(object), u32 first binding, u32 count} sorted by hash. Over 400 layers 18,129 of 18,129 scripted objects are named ( ScriptRelay 8,906, ScriptObject 4,700, StartupCommand 2,795, QuestRelay 438, RemoteScript 365 ...), every script hash is the hash of the part's own worlds\retail\...\<layer .scripts path (5,844 of 5,844), and every bound name exists in that part's shipped script. Events include Script , Script1 , Start/Cleanup/Fail/CompleteQuestScript , PreActivateQuestScript , Departure/ArrivalScript , OnInitialize and OnEnterScript . A binding names either a function name = function(self, threadId, scriptId) ... end (4,938 of 6,312) or, for a ScriptObject 's Script , a script object name = hmake <Type meta { ... } (1,374).

The static placements (below) list only static prefabs. Everything the engine can burn, break, open or animate is an OBJL object, and its geometry and collision are found through this block: u32 n objects u32 n records n objects x u32 hash(object name) (unsorted) n objects x u16 record index records: {u32 1, u16 0, f32[6]} no path: world collision {u32 flag, u16 length, path, u32 key, f32 cull, f32 half[3], f32 centre[3]} a prefab (.inst) then the records' Havok shapes (tagfile TAG0, SDKV20160200, hknpCompoundShape) Lithlad's main part lists 18,943 objects over 585 records. In Cirith Ungol's main part 12,638 of 12,639 hashes are OBJL object names, all of geometry or physics classes ( FireProp 2,491 of 2,491, DynamicObjectGroupBrush 1,382 of 1,382, WorldModel 590 of 590, AINavMeshObstacle 6,397, the world-collision objects). A record's bounds are its prefab's decoded bounds (the orc furnace base: half-extents 18.1 x 8.9 x 22.1 m), and records are per (prefab, class), so a prop and its navigation obstacle use different records of the same prefab.

t: Motion paths, effects, ambient life and clutter
x: - KEYF ( CClientKeyframer ): 'KEYF' u32 1 u32 n u32 data bytes , n x {u32 id, u32 offset} ; an entry is {u32 5, u32 keys, u32 frames, u32 frame bytes} , keys {u32 hash(name), u32 frame} ( Open , Closed , Start , End ), frames of 40 bytes {f32 time (s), f32 offset[3], f32 quat[4], u32 0xFFFFFFFF, u32 tag} . The id is the KeyDataIndex property of a KeyFramer object (449 of 449 resolve). Of 1,310 blocks, 45 carry paths (431 paths; quaternions unit 4,848 of 4,848, times monotonic in 431 of 431); a gate leaf slides 400 cm over its 10 s TotalPathTime . - SFXS , static effects that are not objects (falling leaves, furnace smoke): header 1 off a off b n n2 0 0 , .fxp paths, at off a n x {f32 position[3], f32 cull range} , at off b n x {f32 quat[4], u32 .fxp path offset, u32 3, 0, 0} . The loader (vt 0x2301300 vf3, 0x4BB9E4) refuses a block unless (off b - off a) / 16 = n and n2 <= n , squares every cull range at load, and keeps n at +0x20 and n2 at +0x24 . n2 counts the distance-culled entries : the file puts every entry with a positive cull range first and the entries with range 0 after them. In all 60 non-empty blocks (5,737 entries) no entry before n2 has range 0 and none after it has a positive range; the game has exactly two range-0 entries, Minas Ithil's two distant waterfalls ( mi waterfallfar01 base and top , n 1,273, n2 1,271). - NLFE , ambient-life emitters: 'NLFE' 1 0x1C n group-name bytes name bytes groups ; the group names are NativeLife/Definition records ( con TourchLight , con MeatFlies ), then n group indices, n instance names ( light 05L.Moths ; prefixed by their prefab instance, not OBJL objects), n zeros and n positions. - Clutter ( CClutterMgr , ClientShellDLL\ClutterMgr.cpp ): instanced static meshes carried with their geometry. The header is u32 1 u32 string bytes u16 meshes u16 instances u16 elements u16 vertex buffers u32 buffer bytes ; then come the .mat strings, and per mesh {u32 material, u16 elements, u16 vertex buffers, u16 vertices, u16 indices, u16 users} with its vertex elements, 56-byte vertices {pos[3], normal[3], uv0[2], uv1[2], tangent[3], u32 color} and u16 triangle indices; then 40-byte instances {f32 pos[3], f32 quat[4], f32 scale, u16 left, u16 right, u16 mesh, u16 1} forming a binary tree with one root per block. The non-empty blocks number 51 (275 meshes, 9,630 instances); Lithlad's main part has 23 meshes and 1,657 instances. - PFDG , the prefab tree of the debug viewer (registered by CPrefabDebugViewer 0x1796274, which draws a cube CPrefabDebugViewer.Box scaled by each node's extent): 'PFDG' 1 n string bytes , n x {f32 center[3], f32 extent[3]} (the extent is signed: 21% have a negative component), n packed 21-byte nodes {u32 parent, u32 first child (0xFFFFFFFF none), u8 r, g, b, a, u32 path, u32 name, u8 flag} , strings. The shipped trees hold 381,195 nodes, every link valid. The viewer is created and its handler registered unconditionally at client start-up ( CGameClientShell::InitializeSubsystems 0x1772E1C), so the block is parsed on every load; the handler's finalize step (vf5 0x483F78) hands each tree, keyed by StringHash("<part .objres") , to the viewer (0x483FDC) and to nothing else. No other code names the resource type.

The whole section is read by one handler (vt 0x230A800 vf3 0x6B3510 - 0x6B3914, then 0x6B3664), in this order; the walk ends exactly at the section end in 1,310 of 1,310 parts: 0x00 'WDSC' u32 9 0x08 u32 CELLS u32 total boxes u32 INSTANCES u32 total groups u32 MESH ENTRIES u32 total materials u32 total polygons u32 total polygon vertices u32 STRING BYTES 0x2C strings: the part's .wldmsh, its materials, every prefab .inst it places MESH ENTRIES x {u32 n, u32 mesh path, u32 value, n x u32 material path} (1 when the part has its own world mesh) INSTANCES x 76 bytes (unaligned) CELLS x cell the trailing block The header's totals size one allocation for everything the cells hold (Lithlad: 1 cell, 16 boxes, 2 groups, 6 polygons with 24 vertices). An instance: Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- +0x00 f32[3] / f32[3] world bounds min / max +0x18 f32[3] pivot position (world, cm; the base center of the prefab) +0x24 f32[4] rotation quaternion (x, y, z, w) +0x34 f32 scale +0x38 u32 flags (only "non-zero" is kept) +0x3C u32 kind (two bits kept) +0x40 u32 the tag of the prefab LOD group to draw +0x44 f32 cull distance (cm) +0x48 u32 prefab path (offset from 0x2C) The reader 0x1CCB150 turns each into a 0x60-byte run-time record: Offset Holds --- --- +0x00 / +0x10 the bounds +0x38 the kind in bits 0-1, and "flags non-zero" in bit 2 +0x3C the squared cull distance (a default when the file value is not positive) +0x40 the pivot +0x4C the quaternion +0x5C the scale The file record's +0x40 word selects which LOD group of the prefab the instance draws. The reader passes StringHash(prefab path) and this tag to 0x58A928, which keeps, per prefab path, a small table of the tags placed with it (three inline, then blocks of 14) and returns the tag's index; the run-time record stores it at +0x3A . The tags are the ones the prefab's LOD records open with (see Prefabs below). In Lithlad and Minas Ithil, 18,937 of 18,937 instances whose prefab ships in the part's own container name one of their prefab's groups; 163 of them use a prefab with several groups, and 45 pick one other than the first. Composite prefabs use the same tag on their child records. Lithlad's 12,877 instances use 15 distinct tags, one per prefab for 241 of 242 prefabs. Lithlad's main part places 12,877 static instances of 242 prefabs (quaternions unit 12,877 of 12,877, scale 0.12-2.03, flags 1 on 12,789; cull distances mostly 60 m, 90 m, 350 m and 4 km). The kind is a property of the prefab (constant for 242 of 242): 0 on 11,659, 3 on 1,210 (cliff-base rocks, torches, fort stairs, doors, pickaxes) and 1 on 8 (a zipline). Layers place few or none (0 to 17 in five read). These are the static buildings, walls and rocks; prefabs that can change (destructible, animated, interactive) are objects instead. Cells (read by 0x6B3CD0). Each main part has one cell; 351 layers have one, 65 two, 2 more, and 884 none: u32 boxes u32 polygons u32 groups boxes x 32 bytes {f32 min[3], f32 max[3], u8, u8, u8, u8, u16, u16} polygons x {u8 n, n x f32[3]} (four vertices in every main part) groups x {u32 key, u32 n, n x u32 instance index} For each group the engine builds two lists of instance bounds, each entry the instance's bounds with its squared cull distance in the fourth component: one of every instance in the group, and one that leaves out the instances of kind 3. A cell's groups cover its instances: Lithlad's cell lists 12,714 instances under key 0 and 163 under 0xD7D4D586 (12,877 in all). The trailing block (read by 0x6B3664) opens with 13 words, four of which must be 0: A count first cell of a range 0 B count unknown 0 total s total hull references hull count unknown 0 total A-to-A references 0 (the loader keeps a pointer to the cells from "first cell" on, and the totals size its allocation); then: hulls x {f32, u32, u32 vertices, u32 n1, u32 n2, vertices x f32[3], n1 x u16, n2 x u16} A x {60 bytes, ending with u32 count c1, u32 count c2, i32 cell (-1 none), u8 count s; then s x 16 bytes, c1 x u32 hull references, c2 x u32 references to other A records} B x {u32 n, u32, f32, i32, i32, n x u32 references to A records} The engine computes each hull's bounds from its vertices. Every main part has one or two A records and one B record; Barad-dur and the Black Gate have no hulls, the others 86 to 207. Of the 1,302 layers, 1,217 carry only the empty 52-byte header, and 85 carry records.

A prefab's baked geometry; static world geometry is never .mesh (prefab .mesh files are the destructible and animated pieces). 'PRFB' u32 8 u32 hash ... with header words for draws [4] , materials [5] , child prefabs [6] and vertex formats [9] , then: - LOD records start at 0x38, 44 bytes each with -1.0 at +28 . They form groups, each opening with a per-group tag (0xD238B9DD on a keep wall, 0xD238B9DE on human buildings, 0x3249 on lanterns, and an extra leading group 0x159A on fortress pieces): a root {tag, -1, 0, 0, next = first unit, f32 cull distance} and units {tag, name hash, first draw, draw count, next unit (-1 = finest), f32 switch distance, f32, -1.0, 0, 0, distinct draws} . A placement names the tag of the group it draws (see Placements above). Per instance the engine walks coarse to fine and draws the first unit whose next is -1 or whose switch distance the camera is beyond (a keep wall switches at 320, 150 and 80 m and is culled at 7 km). A unit may draw nothing at its range; draws in no unit are depth-prepass and shadow casters. Header word [7] is not the unit count (88 of 431 chained prefabs disagree). - {u32 draws, u32 vertex bytes, u32 index bytes} , then per draw one vertex block ending at its vend (stream 0 then stream 1, stride-aligned), then u16 indices ( idx min .. idx max , rebased by idx min ). - The tail: vertex formats {u8 stream, u8 type, u8 usage, u8 index} (types 2 float3, 12 half4, 10 half2, 4 ubyte4; usages 0 position, 1 normal, 2 tangent, 3 binormal, 4 uv, 5 color), 52-byte draw records {0, n, n, index start, base, triangles, material, 0, 0, format, vend, f32, f32} , then the material paths. Positions are prefab-local with the pivot at the base center. A composite prefab ends with a block of placed child prefabs. A layer carries the prefabs it places as PRFB sections of its own container (Minas Ithil's sabotagecages 00 carries guard caragors.inst and three footprint-tracking prefabs).

t: World meshes, texture arrays, terrain and vegetation
x: - MESH version 5 ( .wldmsh ) is a part's own world-space mesh, laid out like the PRFB tables with the vertex buffer at 0x2C (header [3] draws, [4] formats, [9] vertex bytes, [10] index bytes); its materials index the part's WDSC list. Draws wider than 20 km are sky domes and vista cards (504 km in Minas Ithil's night01 , 960 km for Cirith Ungol's mt v01 ). - In Cirith Ungol about 90% of the world's triangles use texture-array materials ( .texa ), which blend array slices by a mask and a height map. - TERR version 9 ( <region .terrain ) , in main parts only (Barad-dur has none), is read by 0x7AC0F4. Per terrain it holds a root grid (4x4 or 8x8), the position (the center), a quaternion, the extent, the height range, a terrain shader parameter, the node count, a material and a global texture (a 32x32 flag map, one cell per depth-3 node). Then come the nodes, {u32 flags; unless flags & 0x20: f32 min, f32 max, u32 tile} , and tiles of three texture paths; the file ends exactly after them in every region. The shader parameter is 400, 500 in Lithlad and 1000 at the Black Gate: with Lithlad loaded, k vTerrainHullParams0.y and k vTerrainDomainParams1.w both hold 500, next to the height range 13,000 in k vTerrainDomainParams1.y . Each root is a quadtree stored in pre-order (flag bits 0-3 = children present, 0x40 root, 0x20 no data); every root's tile 0 is the region overview, deeper nodes own a 68x68 16-bit height tile and two 132x132 BGRA maps (four texture-array slice indices and their weights). World placement: U = (x - pos.x) / size + 0.5 , V = (z - pos.z) / size + 0.5 , y = pos.y + h range . The terrain shader disp terrain.fxo keeps the four heaviest of up to 24 slices per point; slice index 255 means no layer, which marks the holes (outside the play area, and pockets such as forts and caves). - VEGT ( .vegtile ) , vegetation, read by 0x503A0C: 'VEGT' u32 version (1-3) f32 center[3] f32 half[3] u32 species , then per species {u16 length, name, u32 n, n x 16-byte instance} . An instance is u16 qx, qy, qz (position = (center - half) + q step , step = max(half) 2 / 65535 ), u8 scale ( b / 127.5 ), a u8, four rotation bytes, a 3-byte bounding-sphere offset and u8 flags (bit 0 hidden). The rotation is decoded on the GPU ( vegetation sort nomotion.fxo ): cos yaw = 2 b0 / 255 - 1 , sin yaw = 2 b1 / 255 - 1 , a2 = b2 2pi / 255 - pi , a1 = b3 2pi / 255 - pi , world = s Rz(a2) Ry(yaw) Rx(a1) local + position . Species are Vegetation/Type records; 108 species and 1,291,234 instances ship, in tiles worlds\retail\<folder <n v.vegtile (inside the region folder for Gorgoroth and Seregost) and in layer tiles. A tile's file ends exactly after its last species.

Read on every object of the 20 named contexts in Lithlad (105,946 objects): Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- +0x00 ptr vtable: exactly one per class (142 classes, 142 vtables) +0x28 node the name-table node: +0x08 next, +0x10 hash ( StringHash(name) , 105,946 of 105,946), +0x18 name +0x40 char the registered name (equal to the node's, 105,946 of 105,946) +0x50 ptr the object's ObjectRec in its part's property database (a GameDB record on 105,383; null on 563) +0x58 ptr its world context (105,946 of 105,946) +0x60 node the update-list link (see Threads and the frame) +0x78 ptr its runtime class entry +0x80 ptr render component (set on 8,457) +0x88 ptr time source (see Engine core) +0x98 ptr physics body (pieces vector at body +0x08 .. +0x10 ) +0xAC f32[3] position (cm) +0xB8 f32[4] rotation quaternion (x, y, z, w): unit on 105,946 of 105,946 +0xC8 f32 scale +0xD0 f32 update countdown +0xD4, +0xD8 u32 copied from the create parameters +0x30 , +0x34 +0xDE u8 1 = the name was copied, 0 = it points into the part's string table +0xE2 u8 flags: bit 0 visible, 0x0C solid ( FireProp 0x0F on 4,077 of 4,129) Classes.
