t: Creating, binding, moving and removing objects
x: All of this runs on the main thread.

The object server [base+0x26FF058] (vt 0x22C0B28) is the world-object factory: Slot Function Role --- --- --- vf4 0x7AAB6C - 0x43DBC8 the time-sliced object-set streamer vf5 0x1F6EA0 "busy" (the update walk is skipped while it reports busy) vf8 0x43D630 CreateObject(params) : requires a class at params+0x40 , copies the parameters (0x43D680), calls the creator, then the new object's vf21 ( +0xA8 , post-create) vf14 0x502034 find an object by name in a context The creator 0x1CD454 (also called by the part loader 0x11B4EC0 for every object a part streams in) requires an object set at params+0x1A0 . It allocates the object through the class holder at params+0x40 and runs its ReadProps (vtable +0x60 , which pulls every property from the ObjectRec ). It then builds the transform from the parameters into +0xAC , registers the name, links the object into its context, builds its components (vtable +0x68 ) and activates it ( +0x80 , +0x70 , +0x48 ). A part's loader creates every object first and post-creates each afterwards. CObjectCreateParams (defaults 0x43DAA0): Offset Meaning (default) --- --- +0x01 flags, copied to the object's +0xE2 (0) +0x04 position (0, 0, 0) +0x10 scale (1.0) +0x14 rotation quaternion (0, 0, 0, 1) +0x30, +0x34 copied to the object's +0xD4 , +0xD8 (0, 0xFFFF) +0x40 the class holder (copied to +0x78 ) +0x168 inline name +0x188 name pointer (0 = use +0x168 ) +0x198 the ObjectRec (copied to +0x50 ) +0x1A0 the object set, that is the world context (copied to +0x58 )

The name registrar 0x4DBF08 either copies the name (and sets +0xDE to 1) or keeps a pointer into the part's strings ( +0xDE = 0). It then hashes the name into the node at +0x28 and calls the context's vf10 0x4DBF78, which picks the bucket ( hash & 0x7FF , 0x4DBF84) and appends the node at the tail (0x115ED3C, which asserts "Error: Adding a link that is already inside of a list" only when the node itself is already linked). Duplicate names are legal : nothing checks the name. The lookup 0x4DC078 compares the hash and then the name case-insensitively, walking from the tail, so the newest object of a name answers. Render and collision are bound by name. The component build (vtable +0x68 - 0x333430) asks the context's vf5 0x3334F0, which looks the registered name ( +0x40 ) up in the context's resource table ( ctx+0x98 ). An object created under a name its part does not list gets no render component and no physics; created under an existing object's name it receives that object's model and collision. Because the newest object answers a name, the members of a prefab created after the original members bind to each other during post-create.

A script's Create does not construct anything: the objects already exist in the part before any script runs, and scripts bind to them by name. The <Class .Create(scriptId, name, b3, relative) stubs of 117 of 125 script classes share 0x5013A8 - 0x501B64, which composes the name (a . prefix or relative prepends the prefab instance's name) and calls the object server's vf14 with the scriptId's own context; the lookup is not given the class. A missing name or a class mismatch returns Class.None ; ScriptObject.Create is a function of its own, 0x501CAC. A scriptId is {PrefabName, PropertyName, Instance} ; Instance is a weak handle (prefab instance at payload +0x48 ) that becomes null when the prefab's part streams out.

GameBase:CopyXForm(A, B) 0x1823B70 is SetPosition(A, B+0xAC) 0x1454EC followed by SetRotation(A, B+0xB8) 0xEF690. Render state and spatial structures follow the setters, and the call works across contexts. Collision follows ownership : the setter path 0x274C3C forwards to the physics body at +0x98 , so only pieces the object owns move. Of 3,491 FireProp s, 3,382 own no pieces (their collision is baked into the part's static PhysicsBSP ), so a moved bench or barrel stack keeps its old collision; DynamicObjectGroupBrush es (607 of 634) and cage brushes (vt 0x1FA3C00, 84 of 84) own theirs and stay solid where they go. A destructible prop is a prefab of sibling objects (brush, explosion, effects, nav obstacle, volume controller): moving one member leaves the others behind.

Objects live and die with their part's context. When the part streams again its objects are created again from the file, so a moved object is back at its authored transform and an object created into that context is gone. Nothing about placed objects is saved. A class's destructor is at +0x20 of its static descriptor.

Cages, nests, barrels, gates and traps are dynamic object groups : a DynamicObjectGroup object (the root) with DynamicObjectGroupBrush members (the breakable or interactive geometry), DynamicObjectGroupState members named after their states ( Barre 46.DOGS Fire , WaspN 03.DOGS Shoot ) and the prefab's effects. The brushes bind the group's composite prefab ( caragorcage , waspnest , ghulcloset : no draws of their own) and sit at fixed offsets from the root (35 of 35, 53 of 53 and 226 of 226 in those three); the drawn art is the prefab's children at the root's transform. The data is in four GameDB categories: Category Records Fields --- --- --- DynamicObjectGroup/Setup 103 States , VisibilityMaxDistance , Tags , ValidateStateTransitions , ValidateBrushDamage DynamicObjectGroup/StateTransition 101 StateToEnter , ActiveQuestList , IncludedParentStateTypeList , ExcludedParentStateTypeList , IncludedBrushDestroyedAttackCategory , ExcludedBrushDestroyedAttackCategory , ChildState , ChildrenInStateMin DynamicObjectGroup/StateType 77 none: bare state tags ( Alive , Destroyed , Hidden ...) DynamicObjectGroup/PlacementID 16 none: fortress slots ( GateBrow , WallTop , TowerFace , Keep ...) A transition is a guarded rule: the attack categories and parent states it accepts, and the state tag it enters. The state tags carry no data; what a state shows is the part's DynamicObjectGroupState objects for it and the scripts bound to them. At run time a group's current state is DOG+0x188 (the state object; its +0x180 is the StateType record), and DOG+0x190 holds its 32 state links. The group's post-create 0x4871190 collects the links but does not enter a state; a group streamed in with its part receives its initial state afterwards. DynamicObjectGroup:Script SetState is 0x5ADF0C(dog, StateType record): when the ready flag +0x22C is set the request is queued at +0x160 , otherwise it is applied at once (0x5AEABC). A brush's current state object is brush+0x148 ; while it is null, hits on the brush are routed nowhere. A brush's ReadProps does not fill the visibility flags (a FireProp 's does), so a brush created without them is invisible.

Light and sound objects read their colors and radii from their property records at creation and keep them in the object: Class vtable Live fields --- --- --- LightCube , LightSpot , LightDirectional , DecalLightDirectional 0x1FE1148, 0x1FE0998, 0x1FE0E98, 0x1FE0D40 +0x138 LightColor, +0x13C SpecularColor, +0x140 LightRadius, +0x144 IntensityScale Sound 0x1DBBE78 +0x130 OuterRadius In Lithlad the live values equal the decoded property records: LightColor, SpecularColor and IntensityScale 950 of 950, LightRadius 903 of 903, Sound OuterRadius 1,326 of 1,326 (each control read 0). Matching by name paired 2,810 lights; 45 sat more than 1 cm from their decoded position. Of those, 3 sit exactly where the patch .objres places them. The other 42 are lantern lights ( LightHangOrc l.LC Out01 , light NN.LC Out01 ) displaced 2-22 cm horizontally (vertical median 0.4 cm, none downward), and 16 of them moved between two reads a minute apart.

Where Talion can hang, pull up, vault, rail-run or leap from a mount is world data: context-action lines owned by VolumeController , WorldInitializer and StreamingStamp objects, built into a world grid on the ContextActionBuilderThread (see Threads and the frame) and queried by the movement behavior graphs. ContextActionDB ( ContextActionDB.cpp , initialized by 0x1B43A90, vt 0x23010A8) is [GM+0x6DA0] ; it registers the cntx resource type.

CADB (read by 0x7CB194 for the header and vt 0x1FF6B98::vf3 0x501478 for the body; exact in 724 of 724 parts, all version 3): 'CADB' u32 version u32 nA u32 nL u32 nP u32 nV u32 nO (0x1C bytes) nA x u32 action palette: hash of a Character/Models/ContextActions record nL x 0x34 line {f32 p0[3], f32 p1[3], f32 normal[3], u128 mask} mask bit i = palette action i nP x 0x10 plane {f32 normal[3], f32 d} nV x 0x20 volume {f32 min[3], f32 max[3], u32 first plane, u32 plane count} nO x 0x34 owner {u32 key, f32 min[3], f32 max[3], u32 first line, u32 line count, u32 list-1 first volume, u32 count, u32 list-2 first volume, u32 count} Across 724 parts: - 7,883 of 7,886 palette entries name one of the 124 Character/Models/ContextActions records (fields Group , DebugColor , AdditionalReferencedActions ), so a global mask fits in 128 bits; - 2,209,930 lines, every one owned exactly once and inside its owner's box; - 314,834 planes (all unit) and 50,668 volumes; - 32,104 owners, sorted, whose key is the hash of an OBJL object name (32,104 of 32,104: VolumeController 31,803, WorldInitializer 288, StreamingStamp 13). Lines are not level in general (1,551,979 slope), and 68,951 normals have a vertical component. The busiest actions by line count: Edge Hang 997,374, Edge Pullup 388,445, Edge NoHang 350,260, Block Movement 326,177, Block Movement RailRun 219,953, Edge Hang Dangle 216,272, Hurdle 94,327, Edge MountJumpTo 93,946, VaultOver Mount 91,633, Edge NoTrollJump 83,358, Rail Running 56,365. CAWR ( ObjRes.ContextLineDB ) is the owner index: 'CAWR' u32 1 u32 n n x {u32 key, u32 asset, u32 key} (exact in 724 of 724). key is the hash of the object name; the middle word is 0 on disk and is filled at load with the hash of the cntx resource that holds the owner (2,777 of 2,777 live).

A loaded cntx object is 0x80 bytes (0x7CD444): Offset Holds --- --- +0x08 a node in the database's list DB+0x68 (vf5 0x79A948 asserts "Duplicate asset being loaded.") +0x1C the asset's hash +0x20 the lines (stride 0x38: the mask at +0x00 , the vectors from +0x10 ) +0x30 the planes +0x40 the volumes +0x50 the owner keys +0x60 the owners vf4 0x41E564 rewrites every line mask from palette bits to global bits. The database's action table holds the count at DB+0x10 (124) and the entries at DB+0x18 : 0x28 bytes each, {u32 record hash, u128 own bit, u128 closure} , kept sorted ("Improperly sorted database records!"). Each action's closure is its own bit closed over its AdditionalReferencedActions to a fixed point, and a line stores the OR of its actions' closures. A query for one action therefore also finds every line whose action lists it. Live, for the four loaded parts with a shipped source, 163,048 of 163,048 lines equal the file in geometry and in the predicted global mask (the unconverted file mask equals the live one in only 806 of 161,821), as do 2,364 of 2,364 planes, 344 of 344 volumes and 2,091 of 2,091 owners.

Register 0x2B9E9C(DB, &handle, object, cut group) is called by three classes: VolumeController (vf21 0x2B9758), WorldInitializer (vf21 0x7A53B8) and StreamingStamp (vf16 0x1C2CF04). It resolves the object in two steps: CAWR (list DB+0x98 ) binary-searches the hash of the object's name (0x2BA01C), then the owner is found in the cntx object named by the middle word (list DB+0x68 ) by its key (0x2BB7B8). Live, 3,889 objects carried the VolumeController vtable, 3,748 of them named .VC ( .VC , .VC NoHang , .VC Pullup , .VC Side , .VC Alive , .VC Destroyed ) and the rest other markup names; 126 were WorldInitializer s and one a StreamingStamp ( SS 00 ). A registration row ( DB+0x50 , 0x38 bytes) is {u32 A, u32 B, ptr handle, u8 active +0x10, f32 pos[3] +0x14, f32 quat[4] +0x20, u32 cntx hash +0x30, u32 owner key +0x34} . A is a serial from DB+0x48 . B is the cut group : the hash of the object's ContextCuttingGroup property, one of the 11 field-less Character/Models/ContextActionCutGroup records ( PropKit , WallKit , WallFlair , GateKit , GateFlair , KeepWallFlair , KeepWallKit , TowerFlair , TowerKit , WildFlair , WildTower ); only VolumeController s pass one. VolumeController::SetEnabled 0x5B21A8 (a script function; the StartEnabled property seeds it) calls 0x2BA65C, which writes the row's active byte and sets DB+0x4C , the rebuild flag.

t: Building the grid: KILL and CUT volumes
x: QueueRebuild 0x2BB1C8 files each row by its transform (full rotation, translation only, identity). The build 0x2BA9F8 first instances every owner's two volume lists (planes transformed by 0x2BB01C, {A, B} copied, covered cells flagged), then inserts every line through 0x257C70: - List 1 = KILL. The engine calls these volumes MarkupKiller (4 to 64 cutting planes, asserted in 0x694AC4; the editor class is MarkupKillerBrush ). A line that touches an applicable kill volume is dropped whole. - List 2 = CUT. 0x2582F8 removes the part of a line inside an applicable cut volume; the outside pieces survive if they are at least 25 cm long (the constant 0x267A4D8, compared squared: grid +0x28 = 625). Uncut lines keep any length (20,199 live lines are under 25 cm). - Which volumes apply (0x258280): a volume applies to a line unless the line belongs to the volume's own owner (same A) or both have the same nonzero cut group. A line with A = 0 is never touched. A disabled owner's cut volumes are still built (125 of 1,051), but its own lines are hidden from queries. Measured in a running game (two reads with the world re-streamed between them; 186,023 and 184,993 lines): no line lies more than 1 cm inside a volume that applies to it, for 106 kill and 1,051 cut volumes. Control: the same volumes moved 300 cm along x would contain 31 kill and 1,890 cut lines.

[DB+0xB8] : Offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 / +0x0C f32 min[3] / max[3] +0x18 f32 inverse cell size[3] +0x24 u8 cell counts[3] +0x28 f32 minimum piece length squared (625) +0x30 the inner tables +0x38 u32 line count The cell target is 2000 x 8000 x 2000 cm (0x267A448 .. 0x267A450). Lithlad's grid spans 1,120 x 244 x 1,220 m in 56 x 4 x 61 = 13,664 cells of 2000 x 6105 x 2000 cm (the extent divided by the target, rounded up, on all three axes) and holds 184,993 lines. The inner tables are: - +0x10 cells (0x28 bytes: u32 index, u8 x, y, z, u8 has kill +7 , u8 has cut +8 , a run vector at +0x10 ); - +0x20 owner instances (0x20 bytes: u32 A, u8 active +4 , run vector +8 ); - +0x30 kill volumes; - +0x40 cut volumes (0x38 bytes: box, u32 plane count +0x18 , planes +0x20 , u32 A +0x28 , u32 B +0x2C , u8 cell range[6] +0x30 ); - +0x50 world planes (16 bytes {n[3], d} , inside when n . p - d <= 0 ). A world line is 0x40 bytes: u8 flags (bit 0 = owner active), u32 home cell bit 31 , u128 global mask +8 , f32 p0 +0x18 , p1 +0x24 , normal +0x30 .

ContextActionDB::Query 0xFEAFB0(DB, AABB box, u128 any, u128 all, u128 none, u128 not all, results ) locks DB+0x20 and runs 0xFEAE40 over every cell the box covers (0xFEB3B0) and every run in it (0xFEB070). It returns each active line once (de-duplicated by its home cell) for which mask & any != 0 , mask & all == all , mask & none == 0 and mask & not all != not all (a zero mask skips its test) and whose segment meets the box (slab test 0x5AA774). Results are {u32 n, n x 0x38 {u128 mask, p0, p1, normal}} , at most 256. Running the engine's own 0xFEAE40 in an emulator against live memory, on boxes around the player and on random lines with five or six mask sets, gave the same answer as this model in 96 of 96 and 80 of 80 queries. Returning inactive lines as well would have changed the answer in 18 of 19 and 9 of 9. The callers build the masks from the action table's own bits (0x41F954): any from a node's GameDBContextAction and GameDBContextAction OR , all from AND , none from NOT OR , not all from NOT AND . The seven callers of 0xFEAFB0 are behavior-graph nodes (see Animation): Predicate.DetectedEdge ( DetectEdgeData 0x1C6EF90: fields Direction , VerticalOffset , Radius , Height and the five action lists; box = position + (0, VerticalOffset, 0) +- (Radius, Height / 2, Radius); defaults -104, 100 and 10 cm), Predicate.FoundRailing / Modifier.FindRailing ( RailingData 0x1C700D4), Modifier.MoveWithBrush (vt 0x2303CD8::vf11 0x1C46DE0), Predicate.FoundContextActionBasic (0x41F39C), Character/Models.LockPhysicsContextActionRecords (0x41E70C - 0x41FBF0), 0x1C6FA58 (from 0x1BE703C, R Foot ) and 0x3ADC94.

ObjRes.WeatherFx places effects that play only under a given forecast. It is the empty 16-byte header in 1,300 of 1,310 parts; the ten others are seven region main parts (not Barad-dur), Minas Ithil's t1prefallprops and t1postfallprops , and Gorgoroth's fx environment (10 types, 51 points). 'SWFX' u32 1 u32 n types u32 n points n types x {u32 record hash, u32 first point, u32 END point} ranges tile [0, e0), [e0, e1) ... n points x f32 position[3] n points x f32 quat[4] The ranges tile the points in 10 of 10 blocks (79 of 79 types; quaternions unit 8,110 of 8,110). The type hashes are records of Weather/FX/Static (the category cached at 0x2700050; 32 records, 28 of 28 distinct hashes resolve): Ledge 1m / 3m / 5m / 10m / Corner , Curtain01 20m , Curtain02 40m , Curtain CeilingFill01 / 02 , Lightning Far0N , Lightning Near0N , Lightning VOL Far0N , Lightning VOL Near0N , Desert AtmoDust Lrg01 , ISLD Pollen 5m / 10m . A record has a BubbleRadius (cm: Ledge 1m 2,000, Curtain01 20m 15,000, Desert AtmoDust Lrg01 45,000, Lightning VOL Near 125,000, Lightning Far 300,000) and Data = StructuresWeather.StaticFXData { Predicate - StructuresWeather.StaticFXPredicate { Forecast - Weather/Predicates/Forecast/<RainLight RainMedium RainHeavy ... }, Effect ( fx\weather\rain\edgedrips\rainlight edgedrip01 1m.fxp , fx\weather\lightning\static lightning rainheavy far01.fxp )}: play this effect here, under that forecast, within the bubble radius. Lithlad's main part has six types and 1,646 points ( Ledge 1m 590, Ledge 3m 323, Ledge 5m 242, Ledge 10m 6, Ledge Corner 421, Desert AtmoDust Lrg01 64). The rain drips sit on the climbing ledges. In Lithlad the nearest live context-action line is within 25 cm of 538 of 590 Ledge 1m points (median 5.1 cm), 296 of 323 Ledge 3m , 233 of 242 Ledge 5m , 6 of 6 Ledge 10m and 310 of 421 Ledge Corner ; with every point moved 3 m sideways the counts fall to 34, 23, 15, 0 and 24. The dust points (64) lie a median 9.7 m from any line.

- World collision objects. Every part opens its object list with WorldCollision objects (vt 0x1DCD4A8; PhysicsBSP , and in a main part also PlayerBlocker , CameraBlocker , LargeAIIgnore ). Their records in ObjRes.WorldPhysics carry no prefab path; the block ends with the records' Havok shapes ( hknpCompoundShape in a TAG0 tagfile, SDK SDKV20160200 ; see Physics for the shape classes). A FireProp that owns no physics pieces is covered by its part's static PhysicsBSP collision instead. - Navigation. Every part carries one HKAI section, an HKAI header around a Havok tagfile holding hkaiNavMesh data (see Physics for the navigation-mesh layout). Placed objects carry more navigation data: AINavMeshObstacle (11,588 live in Lithlad), AINavMeshDynamicNavMeshPiece (the props' own navigation pieces, .dnmp ; 1,998 live) and DynamicOffMeshLink (2,986 live). - A prop's navigation obstacle and context-line controller are prefab siblings at one position , named with the prefab instance's prefix ( barre 02.VC , barre 02.NMO , barre 02.FV 00 ).

- What the 109 world contexts without a name table hold, and whether every loaded section maps to exactly one context: 127 loaded sections, 129 contexts and 126 live WorldInitializer objects (every part read opens with one) suggest it. - What the WDSC cell groups' keys and the trailing block's hulls and records are for. The handler's module also manages visibility layers : render commands set a layer's state, keyed by two words, and the module asserts "Setting visibility layer state on a visibility layer that does not exist" and "ReleaseVisibilityLayer must be paired with AddVisibilityLayer". Group keys such as 0xD7D4D586 / 0xD7D4D587 / 0xD7D4D58B differ only in their last character, as numbered layer names would; matching the keys against the layer state requests would settle it. What kind 3 excludes instances from (the second bounds list) is part of the same question. - Whether NativeLife emitter positions are world space: of 48 axis and sign choices the identity is by far the closest to the prefab's own objects (median 41 m), but no live emitter has been read. - What spawns a SWFX effect at run time: the block handler's vf5 0x6FEAF90 only queues the object on [GM+0x30] . Whether the rain-drip points are generated from the same ledge markup as the context-action lines, as their placement suggests. - Whether the lantern lights that sit 2-22 cm from their authored points follow an animated or simulated lamp socket (16 of 42 moved within a minute). - Which context-action nodes Talion's own behavior graph uses, and whether the other node types that carry the same action lists ( FoundContextAction , AlignToBrush , FoundContextActionEnd , FoundRailingCorner , CameraContextActionData , FindMoveAndPinIK ) reach the grid through the seven known callers. - Why the AI placements move vertically at load (class medians 0.5 to 2.9 m down, single objects up to 38 m down and 7 m up): a projection onto the navigation mesh or the ground would explain a move without a horizontal component. - Whether the context's resource table at ctx+0x98 , which the render and collision binding queries by name, is built from the part's ObjRes.WorldPhysics block. - What the TERR shader parameter does inside the terrain shaders (400 in most regions, 500 in Lithlad, 1000 at the Black Gate). The terrain domain shader computes its texture coordinate as world.xz / cb0[30].w ; if that register is k vTerrainDomainParams1 , the value is the world size of one texture repeat. Matching the register to the constant would settle it.

t: Scripting: HavokScript, world scripts and natives

x: The game's scripts run on HavokScript , Havok's fork of Lua 5.1 with typed structures ( hstructure declarations, hmake constructors) and light-userdata literals ( 0x572b96b9hi ); its standard library table is at 0x21DAEB0 and the source compiler ships in the executable. The main VM is [GM+0x6CE8] - a CScriptVM (vt 0x230EF00) whose +0x58 is the lua State : L+0x10 the global state ( +0x560 compiler settings, +0x588 the panic handler 0x1CFEEB4), L+0x48 / +0x50 the stack top and base; stack slots are 16 bytes {u32 tag, value} . - CreateVM 0x1CFE890 and SetupVM 0x1CFEBCC build a VM; RegisterAllScriptBindings 0x1C01778 registers every native, the per-type binder 0x1B9F69C registers the DB record types (see GameDB), and a helper 0x1D87644 registers into the main VM through the global script agent [GM+0x6CF0] . - LoadBuffer 0x55B920(L, compiler settings, ...) and Pcall 0x406344 run a chunk. - Natives do not validate their arguments, and engine asserts write to a null address, so a native called with an argument shape the shipped scripts never use can fault.

A script names a record as DB<Kind .Name ; the lookup ( WBDBRecordLookup ) takes the kind's live category and the name's hash and binary-searches the category (0x278540). The Lua names differ from the category paths: DBFX / DBFXSeq ( Client/ClientFXList / ClientFXSequence ), DBCombatBuff , DBMaterialState ( Combat/FX/MaterialController/States , 168 records), DBSlowMo (332), DBAlignments (52), DBBandType , DBCombatAppliedState , DBCharacterModels . A native's argument types are visible in its stub: each record argument is fetched as mov rdx, [rip+X]; call 0x407BAC , where [X] holds the live category of the expected kind (checked on 27 of 27 natives). Most DEBUG bindings are stripped (no implementation, or the empty stub 0x5009B0). Script calls into the engine fall in two groups: calls that set engine state or queue work (weather, material states, AI requests: AISpawnManager:SummonGrunts only queues a spawn request), and calls that dispatch to script listeners . System:ActivateRemoteScript , for example, is the script bus's Notify 0x605990, which calls the global script agent per listener and so belongs on the main thread.

The engine keeps a stack of the scripts it is running: depth u32 [base+0x2702540] , entries 0x277C1B0 + i 0x80 (at most 16; depth 0 is the static 0x2680000), entry +0x28 = the running script's name. 0x503EF8 returns the top entry's name. Only the engine pushes: the eventmap dispatcher 0x406538 (push 0x4066B8 - 0x5029D0 - 0x502A00 - 0x502A44, which always writes a name, "Invalid" at worst; pop 0x406744 - 0x115F8E0) and the resource loaders 0x4FD9C0, 0x4FEFA8 and 0x4A6088. A few natives require it: NPC::SetAlignment 0x7D2ED4 asserts "This function should only be called from script code" when the name is empty; the other direct users of the name are CPlayerObj::SetAISpectatorInvisible , the player's SetHidden (vf32, logging only), SetRetreatingEnabled 0x1BAE1F8, 0x1BA7C8C and 0x1D86F28. Such natives work only from inside an engine-dispatched script handler; LoadBuffer + Pcall push nothing.

Every world layer's script is one SCRI payload: "SCRI" u32 version (1) u8 flag u32 length body flag 1 = Lua source text, flag 0 = HavokScript bytecode ("\x1bLua" + header) It ships as a standalone <layer .scripts archive entry (the patch archives ship these, and the standalone copy wins) and / or as a SCRI section inside the layer's container. A layer's chunk ends with G.loadedresource = section <hash ; its entries are script threads function(self, threadId, scriptId) that may LithThreadSleep(threadId, seconds) . Objects named .SC are StartupCommand s whose <prefab SC Script <hash entry the engine starts as a thread. Script threads run on simulation time, so they wait while the game is paused or unfocused. Compiled layer scripts are cached for the whole process in the main VM's global reinstall (0x6A60EC: reinstall[id] unset - compile the buffer and set it; set - reuse it), so a layer's script is compiled once per process, the first time its region loads. Which object runs which script is world data: the layer's ScriptBind block maps objects and events to functions of the layer's own script (see World).

Payloads Distinct bodies Regions --- --- --- --- Lua source 3,829 2,562 snowmtn 791, island 767, volcano 752, mtnpass 747, minasithil 522, prefabs 226, benchmark 13, blackgates 5, baraddur 3, cinematics 2, shared 1 HavokScript bytecode 480 117 desert (all of it) The sources are the authored scripts, comments included. A layer's script object ( <layer SO Script <hash meta / inst ) declares its methods ( Init , Enable ...) and the instance fields it drives (dynamic object groups, relays, flags). Script SetState appears in 1,370 of the 2,562 scripts. The largest bytecode program, worlds\retail\desert\desert.scripts , has 2,227 functions, 184,681 instructions, 56,969 constants and 204 structure declarations, with no debug information. Function names carry a content hash, and prefab scripts compile into every region that uses them. Of the 1,939 distinct functions the desert's objects bind, 1,167 (60.2%) are defined by name in another region's source, and the same name means the same code: 616 of 617 compared functions match completely, while a random other function matches 33 of 617.

The interpreter. The main loop 0x1D88000 fetches a u32 instruction, takes op = insn 25 , refuses op 0x5B and jumps through a 92-entry table at 0x1D8B208. Two further interpreter functions start at 0x1D8B378 and 0x1D8E188, each with a 61-case dispatch of its own. The callers (0x6C8E38, 0x406C94) pick one by the mode word of the VM's global state [[L+0x10]+0x1C8] : 0 runs the main loop, 1 runs 0x1D8B378 and 2 runs 0x1D8E188. The word is written once, when the global state is built (0x1D0A294), from +0x80 of the VM-creation settings. The engine creates exactly one VM: CreateVM 0x1CFE890 is the only caller of both the settings initializer 0x1D0173C (which writes 0 there, names the state "Main State" and leaves the field untouched afterwards) and the state constructor 0x1D098C0. Modes 1 and 2 are therefore never selected in the shipped game, and the main VM runs in mode 0. The two other loops are generic builds of the same interpreter. They dispatch in two steps, through a 92-byte opcode-to-handler table (0x1D8E12C, 0x1D91308) and then a 61-entry handler table (0x1D8E038, 0x1D91214), and the two loops group the opcodes identically: - one handler serves the five call kinds ( CALL I , CALL C , CALL M , CALL , CALL I R1 ); - one serves the five tail calls, one the three GETTABLE forms and one the six SETTABLE forms; - each BK arithmetic or comparison opcode shares its plain twin's handler, as do EQ / EQ BK and CHECKTYPE D / GETSLOT D . The main loop's table has 74 distinct targets instead. Mode 2 also checks every fetch: the new instruction pointer must lie inside the function's code ( [proto+0x20] to + [proto+0x18] x 4 ) and be 4-byte aligned, otherwise it raises "VM Kernel error: invalid instruction pointer." (0x1D911D7). In all three loops the INTRINSIC opcodes (31-36) and DATA (76) return straight to the fetch, so no interpreter executes an intrinsic. An instruction's fields: Field Bits Meaning --- --- --- A 0-7 a register, or a flag for EQ / LT / LE / TEST C 8-16 RK: 256 and above = constant K[C - 256] B 17-24 bit 25 is set by the BK opcode of a pair (B is then a constant index) Bx 8-24 sBx Bx - 0xFFFF, relative to the next instruction DATA (op 76) is a word the VM skips; several opcodes own a fixed number of DATA words after them (inline caches, structure ids, SETLIST counts). NEWSTRUCT's DATA word holds the structure id. return f(x) compiles to TAILCALL followed by an unreachable RETURN A, 0 , and jumps are threaded (an inner else skip or a break lands directly on the enclosing construct's destination). The opcodes. The executable carries HavokScript's opcode-name table (records of 0x30 bytes from 0x26809C8, names HKS OPCODE , in opcode order; entry 92 is MAX ): Op Name Op Name Op Name Op Name --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- 0 GETFIELD 1 TEST 2 CALL I 3 CALL C 4 EQ 5 EQ BK 6 GETGLOBAL 7 MOVE 8 SELF 9 RETURN 10 GETTABLE S 11 GETTABLE N 12 GETTABLE 13 LOADBOOL 14 TFORLOOP 15 SETFIELD 16 SETTABLE S 17 SETTABLE S BK 18 SETTABLE N 19 SETTABLE N BK 20 SETTABLE 21 SETTABLE BK 22 TAILCALL I 23 TAILCALL C 24 TAILCALL M 25 LOADK 26 LOADNIL 27 SETGLOBAL 28 JMP 29 CALL M 30 CALL 31 INTRINSIC INDEX 32 INTRINSIC NEWINDEX 33 INTRINSIC SELF 34 INTRINSIC INDEX LITERAL 35 INTRINSIC NEWINDEX LITERAL 36 INTRINSIC SELF LITERAL 37 TAILCALL 38 GETUPVAL 39 SETUPVAL 40 ADD 41 ADD BK 42 SUB 43 SUB BK 44 MUL 45 MUL BK 46 DIV 47 DIV BK 48 MOD 49 MOD BK 50 POW 51 POW BK 52 NEWTABLE 53 UNM 54 NOT 55 LEN 56 LT 57 LT BK 58 LE 59 LE BK 60 CONCAT 61 TESTSET 62 FORPREP 63 FORLOOP 64 SETLIST 65 CLOSE 66 CLOSURE 67 VARARG 68 TAILCALL I R1 69 CALL I R1 70 SETUPVAL R1 71 TEST R1 72 NOT R1 73 GETFIELD R1 74 SETFIELD R1 75 NEWSTRUCT 76 DATA 77 SETSLOTN 78 SETSLOTI 79 SETSLOT 80 SETSLOTS 81 SETSLOTMT 82 CHECKTYPE 83 CHECKTYPES 84 GETSLOT 85 GETSLOTMT 86 SELFSLOT 87 SELFSLOTMT 88 GETFIELD MM 89 CHECKTYPE D 90 GETSLOT D 91 GETGLOBAL MEM In the main loop's table, opcodes 31-36, the INTRINSIC family, and 76 ( DATA ) point at the dispatch loop itself: the main interpreter treats them as no-ops. The shipped bytecode never uses the intrinsics (0 of 2,040,690 instructions in 18,994 functions). It uses 44 of the 92 opcodes. The 48 that never occur are 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, 18-21, 23, 24, 27, 29-39, 43, 48-51, 55, 61-63, 65, 67, 70, 77 and 79-90; among them are the plain GETGLOBAL , SETGLOBAL , CALL and GETUPVAL , the numeric for pair FORPREP / FORLOOP , and every slot and type-check opcode from 77 to 90 except SETSLOTI . The chunk format (the engine's loader: LoadHeader 0x1D1A234, LoadFunction 0x1D1AFDC ("code too deep" past depth 128), LoadConstants 0x1D1AB48, LoadDebug 0x1D1AD68, LoadStructures 0x1D1F048, LoadString 0x1D1B548, Align4 0x1D1A114 (to a multiple of 4 of the bytes read so far); the writer's DumpHeader is 0x1D06A14). Little endian; int 4 bytes, size t 8, instruction 4, lua Number 4 (float32). header "\x1bLua" 0x51 0x0E format 1 endian 4 int 8 size t 4 instruction 4 number 0 integral 3 build flags 0 referenced types int 13, then 13 x {int id, int length, "TNIL\0" ... "TSTRUCT\0"} function int upvalues int params u8 flags int max stack size t code count pad to 4 code int constant count, constants {u8 type: 0 nil, 1 u8 bool, 2 size t light userdata, 3 f32 number, 4 string} int has debug [debug] int child count, children debug int lines int locals int upvalue names int line defined int last line defined string source (null = the parent's) string name lines locals {string, start pc, end pc} upvalue names structs int 1, then {string name (null ends) size t id int int size t slot count slot count x {string name, size t, int, int, size t}} strings size t length (0 = null), then length bytes including the terminating NUL Checks on the shipped corpus: all 117 bytecode chunks reassemble byte for byte from a lossless listing; an operand-range check finds 0 violations over 2,040,690 instructions in 18,994 functions, while the same check with the A and B fields swapped finds 9,935 and with the opcode read one bit low 141,077. Decompiling the desert chunks back to Lua and comparing the 617 functions that also exist as source: 617 of 617 have the same calls and string literals.

t: The main thread's loop and the window pump
x: The main loop is 0xC25568: it calls the application object [base+0x26FEFD8] (vt 0x1FFE760) slot 33 ( +0x108 ) and slot 29 ( +0xE8 ), then pumps window messages ( PeekMessageW / DispatchMessageW at 0xC2589A) and runs a sleep limiter. The game window belongs to the main thread. The main thread's frame wait (slot 28 0x380FAC - 0x38105C - 0x1CF430) is back-pressure for space in the render command ring and pumps messages too (0x6EE5D0, dispatch 0x6EE670); both pumps share the re-entrancy byte 0x277DBB0. Posting to the render ring (0x381FCC posts {0x1EE088, context, function} ) uses an unlocked bump allocation, so only the main thread may post.

t: Rendering: the D3D11 layer, passes, shaders and lighting
x: The renderer is a deferred Direct3D 11 renderer that runs on its own thread as a command processor: the main thread records each frame into a command ring and the render thread replays it. How the ring works, the order of one frame's commands, where the render thread's time goes and how a frame is presented are in Threads and the frame ; this chapter covers what the renderer does with the GPU.

The engine keeps its Direct3D objects in one static block at 0x272D1C0, filled by the device setup function 0x1C8A068: Offset Address Meaning --- --- --- +0x00 0x272D1C0 ID3D11Device1 (138 code references) +0x08 / +0x10 / +0x18 ID3D11Device2 / 3 / 4 , queried only when the runtime supports 11.2 / 11.3 / 11.4 +0x20 0x272D1E0 a small engine object (vt 0x1FFC508) whose +0x08 is the next row +0x28 0x272D1E8 the immediate context as ID3D11DeviceContext1 , the handle the world renderer calls: 450 reads in 96 functions +0x30 / +0x38 the same context as ID3D11DeviceContext2 / 3 +0x50 0x272D210 ID3D11Multithread +0x58 0x272D218 IDXGIDevice2 +0x60 the adapter; +0x68 its IDXGIAdapter3 +0x70 the DXGI factory ( CreateDXGIFactory2 ) +0x78 the output +0x88 .. +0x98 the swap chain +0xA8 0x272D268 the presented-frame counter +0xB0 the feature level reached Device creation. 0x1C8A068 calls D3D11CreateDevice with no immediate-context output, the debug layer flag when the byte 0x2A37030 is set, D3D11 CREATE DEVICE DISABLE GPU TIMEOUT when 0x2A37034 is set and the WARP driver when 0x2A37032 is set. It tries feature levels one at a time, highest first, from a list chosen by the Direct3D runtime version (12.1 / 12.0 / 11.1 / 11.0 on a 12.1 runtime, down to 11.0 alone). It then queries the device for the interfaces above, fetches the context with GetImmediateContext1 / 2 / 3 (device slots 43, 50 and 61), sets the DXGI maximum frame latency to 3 (or to [base+0x267DFF4] when that is non-zero), and reads the threading and D3D11 OPTIONS to OPTIONS3 feature data into the block ( +0x180 , +0x1B8 , +0x1C8 , +0x1E8 ). On an AMD adapter it loads amd ags x64.dll , initializes the AGS driver extensions and reads the CrossFire GPU count; on an NVIDIA adapter it reads the SLI state; the count of alternate-frame GPUs is kept at +0x16F4 . No deferred context is created: in a running game +0x28 , +0x30 and +0x38 hold one object whose GetType returns 0 (immediate). Every world draw is therefore serialized on the render thread through that one context. Three engine objects keep their own copy of the device pointer (vt 0x22C5F50 +0xB0 , vt 0x230CBE0 +0xA8 , vt 0x230CBA0 +0x28 ); none keeps a copy of the context. The user interface does not use this path. Flash menus and the HUD draw through Scaleform GFx 's own renderer, Render::HAL (vt 0x2002498, 166 slots; 18 of them open a profiler scope named HAL::... : vf4 PushRenderTarget, vf11 BeginFrame, vf15 BeginScene, vf50 DrawProcessedPrimitive, vf55 PushBlendMode, vf58 PushFilters, vf74 beginDisplay ...). It holds its own context pointer at this+0x3B3C8 , and the 24 functions that read it make only UI-style calls (shaders, vertex and index buffers, blend and depth state, viewports, clears, DrawIndexedInstanced ).

Calls to the context through a register loaded from the handle appear in 76 functions. Shader-resource binding dominates (compute 27 call sites, vertex 26, pixel, domain, hull and geometry 25 each), then CopySubresourceRegion (12) and IASetIndexBuffer (11). The wrappers most of the renderer goes through: Function Does Callers --- --- --- 0x33C8C8 RSSetViewports 36 0x17DFA0 render targets and UAVs 19 0x388444 Dispatch 15 0x17C1FC bind shader resources on all six stages 11 0x389870 unbind 12 shader resources per stage 9 0x3870A4 input layout and vertex buffer 8 0x17C56C render targets and viewport 6 0x1E978C OMGetRenderTargets , clear render target and depth-stencil 5 0x17F1B0 / 0x17F5A4 input-assembler setup / DrawIndexed 0x246FC8 Draw 0x386D50 index buffer + DrawIndexed 0x17DB70 DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect 0x1CBE0F4 DispatchIndirect 0x1E83A0 samplers on five stages 0x1E8564 shaders on all stages 0x1E938C ClearState + ClearRenderTargetView 0x1CAA53C / 0x1CAB348 Map / Unmap 0x5EFE84 End (queries)

A pass entry point is a function that sets or clears render targets, dispatches compute work or draws indirectly through these wrappers: there are 55 . Grouped by the code module they sit in and the strings that module uses: Group Count Entry points --- --- --- render primitives and tessellation helpers 14 instanced and indirect draws with k fRenderObjectID / DrawIcosahedronInstancesIndirect (light volumes, render IDs) 10 0x388444, 0x1CBE0F4, 0x337E6C, 0x387DB8, 0x1CD2640, 0x1CD334C ... screen-space passes on tLastFrameMap + tSceneNormalMap 5 0x102ABF0, 0x102BCC0, 0x102CD90, 0x102DF00, 0x1030FE0 render-target clears and management 5 shared target and dispatch helpers (the module also holds the shadow-atlas settings) 5 targets 0x33B644 (runs inside the post-processing chain); dispatches 0x337964, 0x33DA28 and 0x337EB8 (the last two inside the GPU particles), 0x1CAA73C point lights ( CRenderNodeLightPoint::GetCBCachedData() ) 3 0x687424, 0x4D951C, 0x6FFD74 object-color compute ( k vObjectColor ) 3 0x1ED2F0, 0x1ED944, 0x1EDE58 GPU vegetation 2 0x101A9C0, 0x10199C0 UI ( uirender.cpp ) 1 0x2253D4

Passes do not bind targets one by one. They select a target set by number through 0x17C56C (state, clear color, clear mask, set id, ...): 0x17B9A4 turns the set id into up to five target ids and a viewport size, 0x17C940 turns each target id into its render-target object, and the function then clears what the mask asks for and calls OMSetRenderTargetsAndUnorderedAccessViews . The state object in use is [base+0x273C628] (vt 0x2002320; it exists only while a world is loaded). The slot holds the CURRENT pass's state: the renderer keeps about 35 state objects of this class in one pointer array and swaps the slot per pass, and the slot is cleared at the end of each frame, so code that reads it after the frame (at Present ) finds null. Of 200,000 reads taken from outside the render thread in one view, 147,359 found the main 4096 x 2160 state, 37,560 null, 7,171 a 3840 x 2025 state and the rest smaller passes. The struct at 0x273C620 holds +0x00 a counter (1 to 4), +0x08 the pointer and +0x10 the bound size (width height << 32); binds go through the struct's address (140 lea sites) and the only direct writers of the slot are resets (0x108EAB0, 0x8BC780). The state's fields: +0x0C / +0x10 the render size, +0xC20 the current set id (written only by 0x17C56C), +0xC28 the bound views (count at +0xC78 ), +0xC50 the depth view and +0xC60 the bound formats, which are also copied to the statics 0x273C208 (five formats) and 0x273C21C (the depth format). A render-target object holds its width at +0x00 , its height at +0x04 , its typeless and view formats at +0x08 / +0x0C , and buffers of 0x68 bytes from +0x50 (the view first), the current one selected by +0xB0 . Set Targets Use --- --- --- 1 the scene color lighting 2 depth only point-light work 3 / 4 scene color, (RGBA8,) motion the forward pass after the main list 7 the five deferred targets the G-buffer 13 depth only, a square three times +0x20 on each side the shadow atlas 27 a second depth buffer, one pixel per 16 x 16 screen tile point-light tiles 9 one target, 2048 x 2048 20, 21, 22 quarter-size targets post-processing 29, 30 half-size targets post-processing At a 4096 x 2160 render size the targets are: the G-buffer (below), two R16G16B16A16 FLOAT scene color targets that swap every frame (the current frame and the last one), a full-size R32 FLOAT target, a 256 x 135 R32G32 FLOAT target (one texel per 16 x 16 tile), and half- and quarter-size R8G8, R32 FLOAT, R16G16 FLOAT and R16G16B16A16 FLOAT chains. The main depth buffer is D32 FLOAT S8X24 UINT. RemapDeferredRenderTargets() 0x66E9C4 (named by its own assert) checks that set 7 is bound and rebinds a subset of its five targets by a bit mask, keeping the depth buffer.

Sampling the render thread (8,369 and 8,370 samples over 2 x 12 s, each one's call stack unwound and the bound-target statics read in the same instant) shows what each pass draws into and the order they run in. Inside the scene command, the main pass list 0x33CD60 runs, every frame, in this order (consecutive samples moved from each pass to the next one hundreds of times and never in the other direction): Order Pass Bound targets Share of render-thread samples (one Lithlad scene) --- --- --- --- 1 0x255920, then 0x185410 set 7 2 mesh pass A 0x66E93C: the G-buffer pass set 7 in 3,538 of 3,538 and 3,477 of 3,477 samples 41-42% 3 the GPU particles 0x33783C the five deferred targets 2% 4 mesh pass B 0x1F02E8: the shadow pass its main child 0x1EE3E4 draws with set 13 (depth only, D16) in 502 of 502 samples 10-11% 5 the light accumulation 0x384640 set 1, the scene color; its point-light compute 0x4D951C uses sets 2 and 27 4% Mesh pass A remaps the deferred targets to the first four before its draws, so its meshes write the four G-buffer targets; the passes that keep all five bound also write the motion target. Mesh pass B draws shadow casters into the shadow atlas (0x1EE3E4, the vegetation 0x1021250, 0x185410); the second writer of the shadow scale and move constants, 0x1CC8DA0, runs inside it with the atlas bound (8 of 8 and 7 of 7 samples), so it sets up one cascade at a time for the casters. One child of pass B, 0x1CC753C, draws with the scene color and the main depth buffer bound. After the main pass list come the vegetation displacement and grouped GPU particles (0x1021250), the post-processing chain (0x33740C: motion blur, depth of field, blur, vignette), the color-grading pass (0x339D6C) and, last, 0x1EDE58, which runs with the scene color and the motion target bound (sets 4 and 3): a forward pass that writes color and motion vectors. The user interface draws into an R8G8B8A8 target.

The renderer is deferred. The G-buffer is target set 7: four targets the G-buffer pixel shaders write, a fifth for motion vectors, and the main depth buffer (D32 FLOAT S8X24 UINT); all are the render size (4096 x 2160 in the measured game): Target Format Contents --- --- --- 0 R10G10B10A2 normals: bits 0-19 the bumped normal's offset, bits 20-31 the geometric normal 1 RGBA8 diffuse albedo (bytes 0-2) 2 RGBA8 specular: byte 0 roughness (the lighting uses r r ), byte 1 specular occlusion, byte 2 reflectance (above 0.667 = metal) 3 RGBA8 material: alpha bits 28-31 = the lighting class 4 R16G16 FLOAT screen-space motion Per-pixel render IDs. The renderer also keeps an object ID per pixel: the alpha byte of render target id 7 (state +0x910 , RGBA8), with a float copy in the alpha of target id 19 ( +0x500 , RGBA16F). Target id 2 ( +0x728 , R32) holds linear depth in centimeters. On the Army screen's stage the byte read 245 on the stage captains, 220 on enemies, 1 on the sky and 0 everywhere else: four values over 8,847,360 pixels. SetRenderID 0x1BF3AC(model, u8 id) stores the ID at model+0x40 and hands it to each piece: 0x1BF49C does so for the body [model+0x100] and the 23 appearance slots [model+0x108 + i 8] , and further setters cover the head and the children. Each piece's render instance (vf36 0x1BF4DC) queues a render command, so one piece can carry its own ID, which the render thread applies a frame later. The wraith-vision pass reads the IDs as colors through renderidcolorizer.tex . The lighting is a compute pass ( lighting\tiledlighting.fxo ) that reads the normal, specular and material targets as UAVs and branches on the class: 0 standard, 1 hair (a Marschner model), 2 subsurface / emissive . Its sun term is GGX; dielectrics use a fixed F0 of 0.04, and image-based light comes from split-sum probes sampled at mip 6 sqrt(roughness) . There is no screen-space reflection in the lighting. The work is tiled. Each frame the main thread issues 13 tile updates ( BufferTileIndices 0x1791CC with 0x247108) and one indirect draw of light volumes as icosahedra ( DrawIcosahedronInstancesIndirect , 0x6C74A8). The global shader constants (below) name the rest of the structure: - screen tiles, sorted into separate job queues by the kind of sun shadow they need ( k RwPCFShadowTiles , k RwPCFOneCSMShadowTiles , k RwNoSunShadowTiles , k RwPreLightbleedShadowTiles , k ScreenTileJobQueue , k ScreenTileWithCSMJobQueue , ClassifyJobCount ); - a light octree ( Octree Buffer , k OctLight vHalf , k OctLight vCharacterAdjust ); - per-type light index offsets ( k nPointLightIndexOffset , k nSpotLightIndexOffset , k nDirLightIndexOffset ); - a baked static light volume sampled by world position ( k mWorldToVolume , k vStaticLightVolume CellExtents / CellOffset / StencilHalf / StencilOffset / PivotContrast , k fStaticLightVolume Mip ), with BufferProbes ; - a sparse shadow tree ( SparseShadowTree , SSTCoarseLUT , SparseShadowTreeStartIndex / WriteIndex , k mViewToSSTree , k nTreeDepth , k nCoarseLevelRes / Offset , k fPeelingThreshold , k nSharedEmptyTileLocation , TreeStatsBuffer ). Sun shadows use four cascades , one per vector component of the shadow constants ( k vShadowScaleX/Y/Z , k vShadowMoveX/Y/Z , k vShadowSplitDistSquared , k vShadowSplitDistSelect , k vShadowFalloffParams , all written by 0x382484). In one live read the scales relative to the first cascade were 1, 0.335, 0.055 and 0.0066, and the squared split distances 864,076, 7,697,105, 287,907,008 and 12,008,197,120 cm^2: the cascades end at about 9.3 m, 27.7 m, 170 m and 1,096 m. The shadow maps live in one shadow atlas , a D16 UNORM depth target whose side is three times the target-state value +0x20 (12,288 x 12,288 in the measured game, where +0x20 held 4096), rendered by mesh pass B before the lighting. A second writer, 0x1CC8DA0, reuses the scale and move objects with another layout (about 2.5% of reads, one cascade's component set at a time); it runs inside the shadow pass while the atlas is bound. Spot and point lights project through k mSpotProjector LightTransform and k mCubeProjector LightTransform . The per-view constant buffer. Every G-buffer pixel shader and the lighting share constant buffer cb2 , the per-view buffer: cb2[4..6] are the camera-to-world rows (the lighting rebuilds a pixel's world position as dot(cb2[4..6], (view position, 1)) ). Column z of those rows is the camera's look axis and .w the camera position, so any material shader can read both. Material parameters ( .mat values) arrive in cb3 .

translucent\overlay\rainandfireoverlay.fxo is a full-screen pass that runs after the G-buffer and before the lighting. It reads and rewrites all four G-buffer targets as UAVs, so it changes every surface it covers: terrain, buildings, characters and gear. It rebuilds each pixel's world position from depth ( t0 ), reads the world normal ( t1 ; up is t1.y ), and owns: - wetness: the global wetness cb3[3].z lerps roughness toward the wet target cb3[4].x ; on level ground (up above 0.97) the bump is scaled to 15% before animated ripples are added; - an animated raindrop-impact mask from time-scrolled noise ( t4 ) that roughens, darkens and lowers reflectance where a drop lands, faded out beyond 75 m; - a roof-occlusion compare map ( t6 , matrices cb2[28..31] ) used by the rain branch within 75 m, so covered ground stays dry. The renderable behind it is the class vt 0x1FFECD8, which receives three render commands per frame (0x70C0E0, 0x7146A0, 0x72FDE0). Its parameters come from its material, rainandfireoverlay.mat , and from the weather (below). The pass belongs to the world view: menu scenes such as the army screen do not run it.

lighting\fogoverlay.fxo runs after lighting. It reads the lit scene and rewrites it as scene transmittance + inscatter (depth t0.x , the lit scene t3 , view-to-world cb2[4..6] ; its vertex shader builds the view ray from cb2[21] and the texture coordinate from cb2[22] ). Because fog is added after lighting, distant surfaces take the fog's color regardless of their albedo. The render thread registers the fog material ( fog overlay.mat ) during its own initialization.

Shaders ship as compiled .fxo files, addressed by tree path ( lighting\tiledlighting.fxo , solid\nemesis\gear lod0.fxo , translucent\overlay\rainandfireoverlay.fxo ...). A shader file holds variants: the orc gear shaders ( solid\nemesis\gear lod0 , lod1 , alphatest lod0 , alphatest lod1 ), which every orc shares, each carry three pixel-shader variants, skeletal, mesh type 4 (dithered fade: it discards where the dither value exceeds 1 - cb3[13].w ) and mesh type 5 (which blends reflectance toward four constant specular tints). Talion's gear uses its own trees ( talion armor , detail , armornocull , cloth , weapon , hair , ring ...); talion armor is one pixel shader whose output reflectance above 0.667 marks metal.

Every loaded shader tree, the renderer's own and every material's, hangs in one static hash table at 0x27AEC38 : 128 buckets of 0x18 bytes {first, last, self} (each bucket points at itself, so a bucket is recognizable), and the bucket is StringHash(tree path) & 127 . A node is: Offset Field --- --- +0x00 / +0x08 next / previous (the chain ends back at the bucket) +0x10 the tree path's hash (equal to the resource's +0x20 ) +0x30 the shader tree object in use +0x38, +0x50 the resource There is one node per material and draw state, not one per tree: Talion's armor shader had 33 nodes, his weapon 8, his cloth 8, his head 8. Walking one bucket finds every node of a shader. A material loaded later gets new nodes on the same tree. Tree names carry a content hash.

The engine's global shader parameters are 220 static objects of 0x50 bytes, laid out in runs in the image (the largest run is 28 objects from 0x2A3AD40): Offset Field --- --- +0x00 vtable: the value's class +0x08 flags; the high word is the value's size in bytes +0x10 the bind address, always self + 0x40 +0x18 the name ( k vObjectColor ) +0x20 u32 name hash, u32 index +0x28 / +0x30 previous / next sibling +0x40 the value the shaders receive Class Value size Objects Examples --- --- --- --- vt 0x2001AA8 8 (a buffer or view) 73 BufferTileIndices , SparseShadowTree , VegetationInstances0 vt 0x2001A98 16 (float4) 55 k vObjectColor , k vShadowScaleXY , k vToneMappingParams0 vt 0x2001AE8 12 (float3) 27 k vWorldSpaceEyePos , k vDirectional Dir vt 0x2001AB8 4 (uint) 18 k nCaptureMode , k nTreeDepth vt 0x2001AF8 48 (3x4 matrix) 12 k mObjectToWorld , k mWorldToVolume vt 0x2001A68 4 (float) 11 k fRenderObjectID , k fPaperWhite vt 0x2001AC8 64 (4x4 matrix) 7 k mObjectToClip , k mGFxTransform vt 0x2001A28 4 7 k numBufferEntries , k BufferOffset vt 0x2001A38 8 6 k HairLightFactor , k nPointLightIndexOffset vt 0x2001A18 16 2 k nLightIndex , k nClearMask vt 0x2001A48 12 1 k nCoarseLevelRes vt 0x2001A78 8 1 k nCoarseLevelOffset The names are a map of the renderer. Besides the lighting and shadow structures above, they cover: - object transforms with their previous-frame copies for motion vectors ( k mPrevObjectToClip , k mWorldToPrevWorld ); - temporal anti-aliasing ( k AAParams1/2 , k mPreviousMotionTransform , k PrevTexCoordScale ); - the six frustum planes; - tone mapping and HDR output ( k vToneMappingParams0/1 , k fPaperWhite , DynamicExposureBuffer ); - GPU cloth simulation ( k RwClothPosBuffer0..7 , k ClothConstraintsBuffer , k ClothBendSpringsBuffer , k ClothSpringGroupsBuffer , k ClothNodeDataBuffer , k ClothBoundingBuffer ; the solver and its constants are described in Cloth); - tessellated terrain ( k vTerrainHullParams0..2 , k vTerrainDomainParams0..3 : the hull and domain shader inputs); - GPU vegetation (instance buffers 0-7 with read-write twins, the per-LOD sort buffers k VegSortBufferLOD0..3 and DitherLOD , k VegInstanceCounters , override buffers and k WindFXBuffer ); - volumetric clouds (shadow, scatter, two noise layers, sun direction and color, dimensions and camera position); - GPU particles (emit rate, lifetime, inherited velocity, initial velocity and color ranges, grouped particles and a distance merge sort); - hair ( k HairParamsBuffer ), Bink video ( k vBinkUVScale ), and Scaleform's transforms and color vectors ( k mGFxTransform , k vGFxColorMulVector , k vGFxTexGen ). When values change. Sampling all 220 values 3,000 times in 5.5 s while the world was paused (the world clock did not advance and the camera-position constant held one value) and the renderer kept drawing (505 frames): 117 changed and 103 held. Many constants are therefore written per draw, per light or per pass, not per frame. k vObjectColor is refilled for each draw by 0x254B80 from the draw item's packed color at +0x4C (only when it differs from the previous draw's); the per-object matrices took hundreds of values; k vShadowScale and k vShadowMove each alternated between two values with the camera still. k vToneMappingParams0/1 and k fPaperWhite are rewritten every frame by the color-grading pass 0x339D6C from the frame's HDR settings. A value written into one of these objects from outside the render thread lasts only until the engine's next write, at most one draw.

A material's parameters can be changed at runtime through a material override handle (vt 0x1DC47B8; +0x18 u32 reference count). Its setters, all keyed by StringHash(name) with seed 0 (0x114CFB0): Slot Function Call --- --- --- vf3 0x3094FC SetParamFloat(this, hash, value) (asserts the reference count is non-zero) vf4 0x2E9944 - 0x2E994C SetParamFloatArray(this, count, {u32 hash, f32 value}[]) vf5 SetParamBool vf6 0x1CC2624 an array of another kind (through 0x11585A4) The setters copy their data and post it to the render command ring (0x1154B34 / 0x2E99E8 with 0x17906C), so they are main-thread calls. On the render thread 0x65482C calls 0x177D7C for each pair (0x177D7C is the constant-upload command that appears 53 times per frame); it writes the handle's record list [this+8] - {begin, end} , records packed as {u32 (5 << 28) (hash & 0x0FFFFFFF), u32 4, f32 value} . The list is the set of overrides currently applied. The weather owns one such handle for the surface overlay, [[GM+0x6D98]+0xC0] (its renderable at +0xB8 is the vt 0x1FFECD8 object above); the weather update 0x43C574 sets only k fWetness and k fRaininess through it. Weather patterns can name further material overrides ( nazgul wraithmode ambientoverlay.mat with k fIntensity 150 in the Minas Ithil Great Hall pattern); these reach the renderer as the render commands 0x1B7A40 / 0x1B7A94. Per-piece runtime material slots and the per-character material controller are in Characters .

The world's lighting look (exposure, bloom, fog and sky scattering, sun and moon light, shadows, wind, color grading) comes from AtmosphereVolume objects (vt 0x1FDEFB8) placed in world layers. Each volume names component objects in its own layer: Component vtable Main properties --- --- --- HDRSettingsComponent 0x1FCBEB8 ExposureAdj , Contrast , Saturation , BloomWeight , BloomThreshold , HDRMax , HDRGreyMin/Max , RelativeLightScaleWorld/FX , DynamicAmbientScalar , RadialBlur , each with a Use Override flag and an HDRTV twin for HDR displays FogSettingsComponent 0x1FCC318 SunColor , SkyColor (ARGB integers), SunIntensity , Rayleigh , Mie , SkyExtinction , LightWavelengths (atmospheric scattering) OutdoorLightComponent 0x1FCC0E8 DiffuseColor , SpecularColor (ARGB), Intensity : the sun or moon OutdoorShadowComponent 0x1FCC660 SkyShadowComponent 0x1FCC548 WindSettingsComponent 0x1FCC430 ColorGradingComponent 0x1FCC788 one property, 3DLUT , a texture path A component carries only the properties its author set; the rest fall back to engine defaults (the Minas Ithil HDR components set no SDR Contrast and mostly no Saturation ). Of the 147 property names, 130 were recovered as hashes of strings in the executable. A component stores no values. The values stay in the layer's property database: the component's +0x50 is its property record (field count, tag 0x0A, descriptor run at +0x08 , instance at +0x10 ; cells at instance + link 8 , booleans packed as bits), and the atmosphere system re-reads those cells every frame . Doubling ExposureAdj in the cells of the active HDR components moved k vToneMappingParams1.w from 0.104 to 6.656 on the next frame and multiplied k vSpecularColor by 64; restoring the cells restored both. Several records can share one instance, so the same cell can belong to more than one component. The volume registry is a static pool at 0x27293A0: 0x200 slots of 16 bytes {u64 0 used / 1 free, object} , a free-index ring at +0x2000 , head and count at 0x272BBA0 / 0x272BBA4 (initialized by 0x8BA7D4). A volume's components are weak references at +0x140 .. +0x148 (0x28 bytes each, the component at +0x20 ). +0x120 is the enabled byte, set through AtmosphereController::SetEnabled 0x1A3428(this, bool); its initial value is the property StartEnabled (default true, 0x1BF1848). Enabling and disabling blend over time on the game clock, so a paused game shows no change. Scope. A volume's own properties decide where it applies: WeatherContext "Wraith" marks Wraith World and cinematic overrides ( WraithAtmo at priority 42, PresentationWraithAtmo , Cinema Atmo , NazgulWraithAtmo ); Timer "UI" marks menu scenes ( AV Pause , AV Hier , AV Map , AV Market ); everything else is world. One Minas Ithil sample held 23 world, 24 menu and 8 Wraith volumes.

Volumes are spatial. Their shapes are convex brushes stored in the layer's object data, in a VOLM block (block id 0x8A27BAE6), in world space: header +0x18 instance count, +0x24 brush count, +0x28 name entries + 1, +0x34 face count, +0x38 face-vertex count, +0x3C plane count planes {nx, ny, nz, d} from 0x44 (a point is inside when n . p = d for every plane) then face counts, vertices type {StringHash("AtmosphereBrush") 0xD1A57B78, u32, char[64]} (absent when the block is empty) brushes 0x28 bytes {AABB, first plane, plane count, first face, first face vertex} instances 0x30 bytes {brush, 3 x u32, inverse translation, rotation quaternion, scale} names {P919 hash of the volume's name, count, first instance} A volume registers its brushes under StringHash(its name) when it activates (vf16 0x1C30068). Live, 48 of 50 registered brushes matched the file plane for plane, and 65 of 65 contained their own bounding-sphere center. Every frame the player view update 0x51C43C passes the active camera's position (camera vf6 0x1A6E3C on [CGameClientShell+0x898] ) to 0x2B1290 with the container [player+0x3340] . It runs a point query over every enabled brush; then, for each system state (HDR vt 0x1F673C8, Fog vt 0x1F67388, OutdoorLight vt 0x1F6E230, OutdoorShadow vt 0x1F6E260, ColorGrading vt 0x22F4BD0, Wind vt 0x22F4C00, SkyShadow vt 0x22F4C30, ScreenEffect vt 0x22F30C8, Rain vt 0x22F4D40), 0x2B164C picks the hit volume with the highest Priority that owns that system's component. Priority is read live each frame (0x2B182C, default 0), and on a tie the current winner stays. The winner (at state+0x28 ) blends in over its TransitionTime (for HDR, state = lerp(state, value, w) in 0x2B2CF0). The top volume's WeatherContext goes to the weather manager (0x7DC5C4 / 0x7DC4A0). The look therefore follows the camera, not the player: in one live check the query point was 3.8 m behind and 2.4 m above Talion.

The post-processing pass 0x339D6C binds two color-grading 3D LUTs ( tColorGrade3DLUT1/2 ) only while a ColorGradingComponent is active. Its view settings hold the two LUT textures at +0x290 / +0x298 , the enabled byte at +0x288 , the blend k fLUTBlend at +0x2A0 and the remaps k fLUT1Remap / k fLUT2Remap at +0x2A4 / +0x2A8 . LUTs are 8x8x8 RGBA8 volume textures; the default is Client/Shared.ColorGradingDefault = fx\common\colorgrading\baselinelut8x8.tex . The stage is rarely active: in the Minas Ithil main world four layers and one other object carry a ColorGradingComponent. An engine texture object holds its dimensions at +0x50 , the ID3D11Resource at +0x90 and its shader-resource views at +0x98 / +0xA0 .

The weather manager is W = [GM+0x6D98] : Offset Field --- --- +0x20 its world bundle group (the sections it loads) +0xA0 its section ids +0xC0 the surface-overlay material override handle +0x1C8 the pending pattern +0x1D1 apply now +0x1D8 the pattern being loaded +0x1E8 the current pattern +0x418 the forecast +0x421 a swap in progress A weather pattern is a lighting Section (a world layer loaded as a bundle) plus an effects Bundle , WeatherTypes and FXContexts . Each region's lighting is one layer, chosen by the current pattern's Section : Minas Ithil has day01 , night01 , morgul and gh night01 (the Great Hall at night). The update 0x43C574 - 0x1B4CFE8 releases every section the new pattern does not name and requests the ones it does in W+0x20 . Requests are de-duplicated per bundle group only (0x4B1FE4), so the same layer loaded through another group is a second copy. A pattern whose Section is empty names no lighting layer at all: switching to one releases the region's lighting and the scene renders black. From script: ChangeForecast is SetForecast 0x1DBBE4 plus the apply flag; ChangeWeatherPattern(p) (stub 0x1B7B734) sets the pending pattern and clears the forecast. A forecast record lists a pattern with options such as UsePrexisting , AllowTransitions and ResetTOD . The Minas Ithil finale ( finale mi.lua ) shows the pieces together: it hides the keep, calls ChangeForecast(MI GH Night) (pattern MI GreatHall Night , whose section is gh night01 ), and later ChangeForecast(None) . Falling rain, snow and ash are not part of the pattern's lighting. They are the climate's GlobalCameraFX : on each region load 0x1B4B34C (from vt 0x1F68920 vf4) creates one WeatherCameraFXController per entry through the object server (the manager's controller vector at +0x00 / +0x08 , entries of 0x28 bytes). A controller reads its record's FXData live (the record at controller +0x128 ). A fast travel within the same region does not rebuild them. Falling snow is gated only by the pattern's weather types and the NotWraith context. The sky is in its textures. The night sky domes' shader ( emissive radialblur noz constlerp ) only interpolates its patch slot, so a night sky's look, stars and all, comes from its panorama textures, night0X e.tex . These are BC6H HDR images of 8192 x 2048 with a single mip level, mapped onto each dome through its own mesh's texture coordinates. Water composes the view behind it as behind x clarity ^ thickness + fog color x light x saturate(sqrt(t) / clarity.w) + reflection . Its "interval" parameters are divisors, and the distant water's domain shader divides by the displacement amplitude.

- How the atlas is divided: whether the four cascades and the light shadows have fixed tiles of the 12,288 square, and how the sparse shadow tree and the screen-tile shadow classes divide the work. Reading the viewports the shadow pass sets per cascade would settle the first part. - What 0x1CC753C, the child of the shadow pass that draws with the scene color bound, renders before the lighting (emissive or sky geometry are candidates). - What the "center lit" set is ( k nCenterLitCount , k nCenterLitID , CenterLitBuffer ; the ID changed 83 times in a paused sample).

t: Visual effects: ClientFX data and runtime
x: Every visual effect - sparks, fire, blood, auras, light flares, screen effects, camera shakes and effect sounds - is a ClientFX effect: an .fxp file holding a small GameDB database of nodes, played by an effect manager as instances.

CGameClientShell [base+0x26FFA98] +0xA98 Simulation +0xAA0 RealTime +0xAA8 PlayerTime +0xAB0 CompanionTime +0xAB8 WorldUI (unique ptr - manager wrapper, 0x18358 bytes, vt 0x22F3178; global list [base+0x26C6A98]) +-- +0x28 inner manager (vt 0x1F67400, 0x18330 bytes) +0xB8 vector of 0x28-byte entries -- entry +0x18 -- effect instance (vt 0x1DAB360, pool 0x2A3E9A8) +0x230 FxResource (0x60) - keys - node types +0x220 KeyData block - one object per node +0x128 background work list -- FXBackgroundThread GameManager +0x6DB0 = the FX thread object (routine 0x116B11C) GameManager +0x6DB8 = the FX performance / budget manager (ClientFxPerfMgr.cpp)

An .fxp starts with LTFX and version 8, followed by a GameDB database ( FxGlobalProps and one record per node). The magic occurs exactly once in the executable, in the loader 0x48FBB90. The loader reads 8 bytes from a stream, checks LTFX and version 8 and allocates the 0x60-byte FxResource ; it then reads the database from the stream (0x74CF10) into FxResource+0x48 , or fails with "Failed to load the database out of a stream." The loader is vf3 and the processor vf4 0x3E4540 of the effect resource handler (vt 0x2312410); path resolution happens upstream, so the loader only sees a stream. The file ends with a u32: the count of the database's (u32, u32) pair table ( db+0x68 ), 0 in all 968 shipped effects checked. A file without it makes the body reader 0x4B9B50 read 4 bytes past the end (0x4B9C60), which stalls the resource loader (see Resource streaming). The database's categories are sorted by the hash of their path, and the loader binary-searches them (0x115B4D4). Running the engine's own load and processing on every shipped effect in an emulator, 968 of 968 read to their last byte and 949 are accepted; the 19 others are placeholders with an empty key list, which the processor refuses by design. Most effects ship as LTFX sections inside .embb bundles rather than as loose files: a sweep of 190,407 bundle containers found 30,531 effect instances.

t: The node types and their properties
x: The registry is a static array of 36 pointers at 0x21DB460 (ParticleSystem first, VolumetricCloud last) to 36 separate 0x50-byte type entries in the data section (0x2681DD0 - 0x26829F0): Offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 the name "ClientFX.<Type " +0x08 the type hash (u32, filled at start-up) +0x10 / +0x18 create / destroy a pooled run-time object (16 types; per-type pools at 0x277CA08 + 0x10 i, the tracer's at 0x2A3EA10) +0x20 / +0x28 create / delete the node's KEY object (bump-allocated from the resource's buffer) +0x30 destroy the key in place +0x38 / +0x40 measure / construct the node's per-instance KeyData object (20 types) Two families. The 20 keydata types keep one object per node inside each instance's KeyData block: ParticleSystem, GPUParticleSystem, StandardGPUParticleSystem, AnimatedModel, AnimatedPhysicsModel, AnimatedSkeleton, Beam, GPUCloth, MaterialController, Model, ParentedModel, PhysicsModel, PhysicsImpulseRadial, PolyTrail, DynaLight, DecalLight, Sprite, FlareSprite, LensFlare and VolumetricCloud. The 16 pooled types use run-time objects from per-type pools (base class vt 0x1DAA9D0): Sound, CameraShake, Create, CreateRay, Lightning, Tracer, DebrisSystem, Overlay, Rumble, Volumetric, SceneRender, ImpactDecal, Wind, VegetationDisp, PolyString and PolyCurve. Key objects derive from vt 0x1DB46A8 (sprites vt 0x1DCB558, GPU nodes vt 0x1DB46C8); KeyData objects from vt 0x1DAB2F0 (12 slots; vf6, vf7, vf8 and vf10 are the per-type overrides). GPUCloth is a Model node with twelve simulation properties of its own; it loads <model .GPUCloth.cres and hands its model to the engine's GPU cloth solver (KeyData vt 0x200A4A0, 0x80 bytes). Its key layout, the cloth file and the solver are in Cloth.
