Counted over all resident effects: 9,100 ParticleSystem keys, 3,746 MaterialController, 1,874 StandardGPUParticleSystem, 1,246 Sound and 1,235 Model. The property schema is built at start-up, into the uninitialized data section, by per-type initializers. Each initializer clears its type's property array ( memset , size = count x 0x48), then makes one registration call per property, PropRegister(slot, "Name", type code, &default, annotation, 1, sub, accessor) , where the type code is the database's own field type (2 float, 5 string enum with an annotation such as type=EImpulseFilter , and so on). The descriptor table at 0x263F800 has a stride of 0x40: +0x00 the property array, +0x08 the count, +0x10 the short name, +0x20 "ClientFX.<Type " , +0x28 the parent and +0x38 flags. It lists 50 classes with 2,228 properties (2,227 named): the 36 node types plus their shared bases - BaseFX (15 properties, the common header of every visual node), BaseSpriteFX (41), BaseCreateFX (38), LightningComponent (6), FlareComponent (4), DebrisType (8), OcclusionQueryFX (19), ReferenceFX (2), FxGlobalProps (5) and five curve classes ( CurveFloat , Int , Vector , Color , File ). Per-type counts include the inherited ones. A node record carries only a subset of its type's properties, so the engine binds fields by hash, not by position. Shipped effects use 33 of the 36 node types. AnimatedPhysicsModel, Tracer and VolumetricCloud have full property schemas (76, 37 and 39 properties) but appear in no shipped effect.

CGameClientShell::InitializeSubsystems 0x1772E1C creates five managers, one per time domain ("Could not init SimulationClientFXMgr!", RealTime, PlayerTime, CompanionTime, WorldUI): factories 0x176DC70 (Simulation, a 1 MB arena) and 0x176DBF4 (the others, 512 KB); wrapper constructor 0x1779A64, inner constructor 0x1779B20, initialization 0x177BB44(manager, time source, flag). Three more managers exist outside the client shell (updated from 0x224430, vt 0x1FFAFF0 vf18 0x1C815B4, 0x179AF98 and the UI.Portrait path 0x335E9C); eight in all are in the global list. The wrapper (vt 0x22F3178): +0x08 its link in the global list [base+0x26C6A98] , +0x18 a {vt 0x1DAA870, time source} pair, +0x28 the inner manager. Its vf1 0x482DE0 and vf2 0x482EB4 receive resource events: the wrapper is a resource listener, so an effect resource that unloads removes its instances from every manager (0x482EC0 - 0x177C824 under the manager's lock). The inner manager (vt 0x1F67400, 32 slots): Offset Holds --- --- +0x08 the FX thread object +0x11 threaded: queue work to the FX thread, otherwise run it inline +0xB8 the instance vector +0x108 work pending +0x110 / +0x128 work lists ( +0x128 = background) +0x148 the time-source pair +0x178 arena bytes +0x19C / +0x1A0 cost per key (128 / 64) +0x1A4 the budget left this frame +0x1B0 the per-frame arena +0x18268 .. +0x18320 six deferred queues +0x18328 the work-done event vf2 0x3E9E30 is CreateClientFX . In an open-world scene the Simulation manager held 541-569 instances, RealTime 2, PlayerTime 1-2, CompanionTime 0 and WorldUI 4; with the world map open WorldUI rose to 85 (the map's forest-fire and smoke effects run in the WorldUI domain, as do the army screen's effects).

Enumerate through the manager, not the heap. The vector at inner+0xB8 holds 0x28-byte entries whose +0x18 is the instance: 587 of 587 and 663 of 663 entries in two snapshots carried the instance vtable. A heap scan counts more objects with that vtable (927), because freed slots of the instance pool keep it. The entry : +0x00 byte, +0x01 a distance flag, +0x02 admitted by the budget, +0x04 the cull position (3 floats, cm), +0x10 / +0x14 squared radii, +0x18 the instance, +0x20 the parent instance. The instance loop writes +0x01 (0x24E1EC) as the inverse of "inside the radius at +0x10 , or culling off" whenever 0x24E678 finds it changed; it does not tell whether the effect draws (it reads 0 both with nothing drawn and with the effect's model drawn). Child effects live in the parent's own vector ( +0x18 ), not in the manager's; 0x1BAD70 picks the container and stores it at instance +0x260 with the index at +0x25C . The instance (vt 0x1DAB360, second vtable vt 0x1DAB350 at +0x08 ; constructor 0x1BB368, destructor 0x1BB79C): Offset Meaning --- --- +0x18 vector of child-effect entries +0x40 an intrusive list head +0x58 flag word +0x5C the transform, copied from the create structure +0xB8 the KeyData container and the instance clock: +0xB8 flag word (4 active, 1 looping, tested by 0x24EBB8), +0xBC previous time, +0xC0 time, +0xC4 length, +0xC8 previous loop count, +0xCC loop count +0xD0 the owning inner manager +0x150 / +0x1A8 handles (vt 0x1DABE28) to the parent object +0x180 / +0x188 create structure +0x20 / the socket index +0x220 the KeyData block (one 64-byte-aligned allocation: +0x00 raw, +0x08 size, then the node objects) +0x228 the resource hash +0x230 the FxResource The most common effects in a desert scene: torch caps (89 instances), collectible arrows (76), attached flies (69), forge fires (51), nest idles (43), night torches (34), dust (26), thermal vents (20). The FxResource is built once per loaded effect by the processor 0x3E4540: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 length in seconds ( ResourceLenMS / 1000) +0x04 MaxUpdateDistance +0x08 / +0x10 the key slot array / count (a slot is 0x18: +0x00 type entry, +0x08 key object, +0x10 KeyName) +0x18 / +0x20 / +0x28 the fx\...\x.fxp name, its hash, the short name +0x38 / +0x40 the aligned buffer holding slots and key objects / its size +0x45 PauseWhenNotVisible +0x48 the effect's database - freed after processing (0x3E4765) For each key, 0x3E477C finds the node type by the record's type hash (FindFxType 0x3E451C searches the 36 entries), builds the key object in the buffer through the entry's +0x20 , lets the key's vf1 parse the record, and destroys it through +0x30 on failure. An effect resource is resource type 48: handle+0x52 = 0x30 and [[handle+8]+8] is the FxResource (0x1BBBD4).

1. Main thread. CGameClientShell vf1 0x1A864C (after the performance manager's 0x69909C) calls 0x1AA1F8 for the five managers in slot order; it takes dt from the manager's time source (0 when paused) and calls ClientFXMgr::Update 0x1AAAFC. 2. Update finishes last frame's work first when +0x108 is set (0x1A9F20, 0x1AC584, 0x1AA000). It then drains the deferred queues, resets the frame arena, reserves the work list at twice the instance count, sets the budget to a quarter of the arena and runs the instance loop 0x24E040. Finally it queues itself to the FX thread (or runs 0x1AC638 inline) and sets +0x108 . 3. The instance loop 0x24E040 computes visibility from the squared camera distance against the entry's radii; charges the budget (keys x 128 the first time, keys x 64 for an admitted instance; over budget goes to 0x177BFE8); advances KeyData timing (0x24F2F0); and pushes the container to the background list ( +0x128 ) or the two others. 4. Dispatch. CGameClientShell vf2 0x1F6928 (and vf3 0x177473C) - 0x1F6258( [GM+0x6DB0] ) swaps the front and back manager vectors and signals the thread. 5. The FX background thread (routine 0x116B11C) waits on its work event, then for each queued manager runs 0x1AC638: under the manager's lock, every work item goes to 0x188CA4(KeyData container, 1, ...) - the per-node update of the instance's KeyData block - then it signals the manager's done event and its own. The FX thread object (vt 0x22F3120, name "FXBackgroundThread"): +0x08 handle, +0x18 routine, +0x20 argument (itself), +0x5C the owner thread (the main thread), +0x90 / +0x98 front / back manager vectors, +0xA0 dispatched, +0xA1 quit, +0xA8 work event, +0xB0 done event. Creation, culling, budgets, timing and the instance list belong to the main thread; the KeyData update of queued instances runs on the FX thread.

StartEffectSequenceOnCharacter 0x19B7850 - 0x19E16CC( , target, sequence, manager wrapper) - a pooled sequence player (vt 0x1DB7540, +0x10 = the manager wrapper) - its phases create their effects through 0x10EA78 (below) - 0x1BB950(wrapper, link, cs) the general entry: 72 functions, 87 call sites - 0x1BB980(inner, link, cs, 1) = manager vf2: resource check (type 0x30), distance refusal - 0x1BD0D0 enable byte 0x266D499, performance manager allocate from the pool - constructor 0x1BB368 - container 0x1BAD70 - fields from the create structure 0x1AA5EC - KeyData 0x1BC8A0 + add 0x1BB2E8 - register 0x1BB5E0 The fourth argument of 0x19E16CC chooses the manager, and with it the time domain the effect runs in. The create structure: +0x00 the resource handle, +0x08 flags (bit 0 = no distance refusal), +0x10 / +0x18 / +0x20 three kinds of parent (the manager's vf24 - vf28 build the attachment from whichever is set), +0x28 socket, +0x30 / +0x38 transform, +0x98 KeyData overrides, +0xB8 a parent-instance link. Other callers include ranged-weapon hit effects (0x158308), projectile models (0x10F52C), the player class, the combat area attack (0x4EA0A4) and melee surface impacts (0x15AF18 builds one from Surfaces/Impacts.PlayerMeleeImpactFX ). Attach points. Effects name an attach point by socket or by bone, in two spellings: across 95 distinct attach points L Hand (538 uses) and LeftHand (369), R Hand (93) and RightHand (114) all occur. One skeleton can carry both kinds: the player's 128-bone base rig has the bones L Hand , R Hand , L Foot , R Toe and Upper Torso , and sockets such as Torso , Head , LeftHand , RightHand , LeftFoot , RightFoot , Pelvis , SocketHead , SocketAttach and Socket Ring . The player's own burn effect attaches to R Toe , L Foot , Upper Torso and Arrow R Bicep , the last a socket that is no bone. Sockets are a table of their own beside the bones, so a bone list cannot validate attach names. A key's UpdatePos mode is SocketAttach (a socket or a bone name), NodeAttach (a bone name) or Follow (the character's frame). The base key loader (vt 0x1DB46A8 vf1 0x3E2D90) gives NodeAttach and SocketAttach the same flags, bits 3 and 5 of the key's u16 at +0x80 ; Follow sets bit 3, the Pos modes add bit 0 and the WSOffset modes bit 8. The loader keeps the name as a string at key +0x18 . The string null means unattached.

A Client/ClientFXSequence plays in three phases on a pooled sequence player (vt 0x1DB7540, pool 0x2A34E88, allocated by 0x7A8760, constructor 0x4EDF7C): Offset Meaning --- --- +0x08 / +0x0C / +0x10 state / pending state / timer +0x20 / +0x28 / +0x30 the Enter / Loop / Exit effect handles +0xD0 the sequence record +0xD8 / +0xE0 / +0xE8 per-instance Enter / Loop / Exit paths, cleared by the constructor on every allocation Its vf2(state, kind) dispatches the kinds CanEnter (0), CanExit (1), OnEnter (2), Update (3) and OnExit (4): State OnEnter Update OnExit --- --- --- --- 0 Enter vf6 0x15A19C: creates the Enter effect ( +0x20 ) unless its path is empty vf7 0x159FB4: the Enter handle null or done - state 1 vf8 stops +0x20 1 Loop vf9 0x15A4E4: creates the looping effect ( +0x28 ) vf10 0x15A0A8: the Loop handle null or done - state 2 vf11 stops +0x28 2 Exit vf12 0x15A988: stops +0x28 , creates the Exit effect ( +0x30 ), or with none - state -1 vf13: done - state -1 vf14 Each phase's path accessor (0x15A328, 0x15A55C, 0x15AA2C) runs at the moment the phase is entered. It reads the player's own path field first, then the record's <phase FXLookupTable , then its EnterFX / LoopFX / ExitFX cell; an empty path creates nothing. 0x19E16CC enters state 0 inside the call (vf1 at 0x19E17C4), so the Enter phase is running when it returns and the Loop phase is entered on a later update. The active sequences are keyed by (target, sequence). Of the 1,727 sequence records, 76 carry no effect in any phase. A looping effect whose length is not above 0.0 ( [0x202E584] ) fails an engine assert in ClientFXMgr::Update (0x24F2F0 - 0x10B1546); all 4,139 resident effects in one scene had a length above 0 (the shortest 0.020 s).

t: Keys, the instance clock and the MaterialController
x: A key's window is in seconds. The resource builder 0x3E477C clamps each key's StartTime / EndTime to [0, the effect's length] and stores them through 0x3E4A2C: key +0x08 start, +0x0C end, +0x10 the effect's length; a window of 0 or less removes the key. When the window covers the whole effect it sets bit 1 of the key's u16 flags at +0x80 (0x3E4A50), which the particle system's KeyData constructor 0x1BCE3C reads, with the instance's looping bit, to keep emitting across a loop instead of starting over. The instance clock is 0x24F2F0, which the instance loop calls with the instance's +0xBC . Each frame the previous time takes the current time, and the time advances by the step. A looping instance that has passed its length adds floor(time / length) to its loop count and wraps the time into [0, length]; a non-looping instance whose previous time has passed its length is finished (0x1A9CF8). Curves are shared by value inside one loaded effect. A float curve is a u32 count followed by (f32 t, f32 v) pairs, t being the key's life fraction, and identical curves are stored once: one flat 0.5 curve served five parameters of one effect (a material slot and four particle parameters). A change to a curve's values changes every parameter that points at it. The MaterialController (key vt 0x1DCC0A0) holds 8 float slots at +0xA8 , 0x20 bytes each: {char name, u32 P919("k f" + name) at +0x08, curve at +0x10} . Per-frame masks select what is updated: +0xA1 covers the float slots, +0xA2 a second scalar bank at +0x1A8 , +0xA4 a bank at +0x3A8 interpolated as four floats, and +0xA5 a bank at +0x4A8 interpolated as byte colors (0x267060). Its KeyData (0x699A20, 0xA0 bytes: +0x10 the instance's clock container, +0x18 the key) registers three update callbacks: 0x747958, 0x747960 and 0x677390. The last, through 0x24A664, computes t = (time - start) / (end - start), clamped to [0, 1]. It activates the key when its window is entered (0x2E94EC) and deactivates it on exit (vf29); in between it calls 0x249988, which evaluates the curves of the slots whose mask bit is set and pushes (hash, value) pairs to the material through the manager's vf4. The parser (vf1 0x70850C) sets a slot's bit only when its curve's keys differ (0x186104). A constant slot therefore reaches the material once, at activation, and a later change to its curve is never pushed. With the bit set and a changed curve, the update pushes the new values every frame. What draws. The resident effects in one scene decode to known node types without exception (4,140 of 4,140), and 837 of them draw nothing on screen: 502 are sound, camera shake or spawn effects, 137 screen overlays, 123 lights only and 75 MaterialControllers only. A ParentedModel with UseParentModel and an empty Model draws the character's own model, so it shows only through a material swap; the player's burn is such a swap (16 translucent slots to one material) plus 15 child effects at his sockets. Fades are per node type ( FadeInStartDist / FadeEndDist on sprites, SystemFadeInStart / SystemFadeOutEnd on the newer GPU particles); 912 drawing nodes fade out 2 to 4.5 m from the camera. InclusiveContexts gates (day or night, wraith, blood by race, orc rarity, kill camera and similar) sit on 1,873 nodes.

ClientFX.AnimatedModel draws a skinned model with its own skeleton playing its own clip, attached to a character. It has 71 properties: ClientFX.Model 's plus AnimName , AnimLength ( EAnimLength ), CustomAnimLength , LoopAnim and MovementEncoding . Across the 30,531 effect sections in the shipped archives, 191 distinct effects use a model with a skeleton: 282 AnimatedModel nodes (72 looping), 36 GPUCloth nodes (see Cloth), one AnimatedSkeleton and no AnimatedPhysicsModel. Their users include Sauron's fair form (110), the Nazgul's trail-node rigs (81: effect-only skeletons whose animated bones carry trail emitters), Celebrimbor's ghost, the wraith bow and glaive on a hand socket, the bola, the orc snare and the warg chains. - The clips a model can play are the .anix libraries its own skeleton lists (the skeleton's header, with the names in its DCDCFF01 string block); the mesh is found by the skeleton file's path stem. The fell-beast's head skeleton lists only fellbeast head.anix ; its effect body fellbeast fxlod.skel (144 bones) lists fb behavior.anix , fb sotp.anix and fellbeast base.anix . - Material slots are the skeleton's part cells: SolidMaterial0 / 1 and TranslucentMaterial0 / 1 are cell 0 (the nearest level of detail) and cell 1 (the far ones). - A child effect attaches by name , normally to the parent model's own bones (the Nazgul's trail rig moves its child trails on its animated bones). A name that the character's own pieces also carry can resolve on the character instead: a child anchored on the parent model's L Eye / R Eye drew at the player's eyes, names his hood, hair and head skeletons carry (9 of the 255 player skeletons; his base rig has neither).

- ParticleSystem simulates on the CPU. GPUParticleSystem is the "CustomGPUParticle" path and StandardGPUParticleSystem the newer GPU path; in the desert the GPU nodes outnumber the CPU ones (976 + 103 against 562). - Each manager's constructor loads the GPU particle materials (0x1D2E440: StandardGPUParticle SimEmit.mat , SimEmit Weather.mat , Sort.mat , ClearIndirectBuf.mat , TextureCopyTo2DArray.mat ) and the grouped particle data (0x1D2F1A0, Client/GroupedGPUParticleFX : one record, Fire , 16,384 particles per group). - GPU particles are emitted and simulated by compute shaders and drawn with indirect draws from GPU-written argument buffers: vt 0x1DBC638 vf4 0x1B572C ( CustomGPUParticle.Compute , ParticleSource , ParticleDest , DrawIndirect ), warm-up 0x1D2DB08, sort 0x587AE0; vt 0x2009DA8 vf4 0x1F18D0 - 0x103A960 ( StandardGPUParticle ParticleBuffer0 / 1 ); the curves texture array 0x1B722C; grouped particles vt 0x1DBC718 vf4 and vt 0x23125F0 vf4 0x1EFF0C. They run inside the render thread's scene passes (see Threads and the frame: the GPU particle branch 0x33783C), not as separate commands from the main thread.

- Per manager: the budget is a quarter of the arena each frame (Simulation 262,144); each instance costs keys x 128 on admission and keys x 64 afterwards. The console variable ClientFXMgr.FXInstanceBudget (0x266D4A0) feeds the two costs. - Per effect group ( Client/ClientFXBudget , 7 records: MaxSimultaneousFX / MaxNewFX): OnFire 30 / 10, Blinded 25 / 10, BloodDecals 30 / 4, Poisoned 30 / 10, Footsteps 100 / 10, Easterling SmokeScreen 2 / 2, OnFire Balefire 30 / 10, with a budget-exceeded behavior and pooling rules. They are copied once at start-up: 0x177BCE0 (from 0x1783DD0; skipped while the byte at 0x266D4F8 is set) builds one budget object per record - 0x177A3B4 copies MaxSimultaneousFX to +0x0C , MaxNewFX to +0x10 , the exceeded behavior and the pooling rules (radius, capacity) - and registers every path in the record's FXList by its StringHash . An effect is therefore assigned to its group by the hash of its file path, and an edit to the records after start-up is not seen. - Distance: MaxUpdateDistance ; creation is refused beyond the cull radius; visibility is decided per frame. - Particle limits are node properties (MaxParticleCapacity, MaxParticleLifeSpan, MaxParticleMethod, MaxParticleVelocity), not a global pool.

Wwise's threads carry no engine name: AK::EventManager (created by 0x1310C10; the audio render thread), AK::BankManager (vt 0x22D65D8 vf1 0x1312008), AK::IOThread (0x132E474, streaming) and AK Suspended (0x1309C78). GameAudioMgrThread is an engine thread (routine 0x181F638). Bink runs five threads inside bink2w64.dll , started by BinkStartAsyncThread from the render-side initialization 0x1CB60C0 (via 0x1CD21A0, which also calls BinkSetMemory ); Bink's own audio output is set up there too ( BinkSetSoundSystem2 + BinkOpenXAudio2 , 0x1CD22AC), and 0x1CB6194 stops the threads and frees Bink's globals. GameAudioMgrThread is started by 0x178C98C when byte [base+0x266D9D9] is set. Its routine registers with an engine service, then runs a job loop (0x6AB618) until its stop flag is set. Its first job (0x181F704 - 0x181ED58) builds the AudioHooks compiled cache (below). VideoClipRequestThread does nothing on PC. The engine interface builds its service once (0x117D315: 0x118 bytes, vt 0x22C0DD0, stored at +0xB50 ), and the thread (routine 0x11C7488, loop 0x11C7274) waits on an event, takes the request at +0x100 and dispatches its op code (request +0x08 : 0-6 and 8-12) through a table of 13 function pointers that the constructor 0x119A5CC fills. All 13 are the same stub, mov eax, 5; ret . The handler stores that result at request +0x358 (2 while running), and a non-zero result finishes the request with state 3 (request +0x0C ), so every request ends at once with result 5. The vtable is referenced only by the constructor and the destructor, so no class replaces the table.

The sound manager (vt 0x1E6D5F8, 47 methods) tests its enabled byte at +0x09 at the start of nearly every method. A sound object (vt 0x1DC35E8, pool stride 0x48) is one Wwise game object: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x08 position, 3 floats in cm (FLT MAX until the first position message) +0x14 orientation (front vector) +0x20 the u32 game-object id ( AkGameObjectID , zero-extended; -1 = none) +0x28 its emitter (emitter +0x00 = the same id, emitter +0x08 = this object) +0x30 events playing on it +0x39 registered Sound objects are created on demand by 0x6861A4 when an emitter has none, up to 725 in all ( cmp eax, 0x2D5 at 0x6861C2), and initialized by 0x686230, which registers the id with Wwise (messages 0xB and 0xE) and sends the position (0x3AE0BC). PostEvent refuses a 51st event on one object (0x3ADC5B); the end-of-event callback counts the events down. The emitter is the engine-side structure: +0x00 u32 id, +0x08 sound object, +0x10 position, +0x1C orientation, +0x28 registered, +0x29 enabled, +0x2B has a position, +0x34 last playing id, +0x38 last event id, +0x3C time, +0x60 name, +0x90 / +0xC8 / +0x100 the last event names (set by 0x3AD6A8). In an open-world scene the vector held 52 and then 121 sound objects a few minutes apart. The back-link check (emitter +0x08 equals the object and emitter +0x00 its id) passed on 121 of 121, the ids were unique, 94 objects were positioned and 44 had an event playing. Two sat exactly at the player's position: the player's emitters.

Wwise is linked statically: its code lies mostly in 0x12E0000-0x1340000, its file layer in 0xC35060-0xC3BC90 and the engine's integration in 0x11A2000-0x11DC000. The executable exports AK::GetWwiseXAudio2Interface ; xaudio2 9.dll is loaded at run time, not imported. Banks are BKHD version 118 (six of six sampled, init.bnk included). The executable exports 286 named symbols, 263 of them Wwise's (the AK::SoundEngine , Query , MemoryMgr , StreamMgr , DynamicSequence , MotionEngine , MusicEngine and Monitor APIs with their full C++ signatures, and Wwise's globals); the rest are Scaleform system and matrix functions and two memory pool ids. On disk. Banks live inside the archives: 6,974 loose sound\...\ .bnk entries plus 1,459 BKHD sections inside snd .embb bundles, 8,433 banks with 2,723 distinct names and 12,747 distinct event ids. Language banks are in sound\<language \ . Streamed media and voice are loose Wwise packages under game\sound\ : eight Streaming .pck files (about 1.16 GB) and, per language, External .pck and vo .pck . The file layer formats sound\%s\%u.bnk / .wem / .pck and sound\%u.wem / .pck (0x11D2550): files by id, with a language folder. The bank's object hierarchy ( HIRC , bank version 118): each object is a u8 type, a u32 size and a u32 id; an event (type 4) is a u32 action count and the action ids; an action (type 3) is a u16 action type (0x0403 Play) and a u32 target. A node's parameters are a u8 effect override, a u8 effect count n, a u8 bypass and 7 bytes per effect, one more byte in this version, then the u32 output bus and the u32 parent; containers are reached through their children's parent fields across every bank. A sound's source is a u32 plug-in, a u8 stream type, the u32 media id, the u32 in-memory size and a u8 of bits (a source plug-in, plugin & 0xF == 2 , adds a u32 size and its data). The node types in use are 2, 5, 6, 7 and 9. Read this way every parent of every node resolves (49,636 of 49,636 across the 8,433 banks; without the version's extra byte, 2), and 39,263 of 40,710 sound sources find their media (35,139 of 35,984 embedded, 248 of 248 streamed, 3,876 of 4,478 prefetched). The packages hold 5,111 streamed media ids. Streaming bank data ( Sound/ ): Sound/StreamingSoundBanks (1,958 records: EventPrefixes, EventSubStrings, GlobalStateEvents, SoundEventPlaybackStrategy such as PlayWhenLoaded, SoundBundleToLoad naming sound\bundles\snd .bndl , Priority, StopEventsBeforeUnloading, AlwaysInUse, WaitSecondsBeforeUnloading, SoundBankGroup), StreamingSoundBankGroups (13), StreamingSoundBankSubLists (19), StreamingSoundBankList (1, GlobalMemoryBudgetMB), StreamingGlobalAssetLists (4), StreamingGlobalStateEvents (11) and DlcSuppressLists (2). An event whose name matches a record's prefix loads that record's sound bundle, a bare .bndl manifest that names the .bnk with no container behind it. The bank gate. 0x3AD888(context, emitter, name, flags) runs before every post, and a false result means the event is not posted (0x3AD7AC returns 0). Until the bank system is ready ( context+0x121 clear) it queues the event at context+0xC0 and returns false. Then it hashes the name and binary-searches a sorted table ( context+0x90 , 8-byte entries). An event that is not in the table, or whose entry has no bank (u16 +0x04 = 0xFFFF), plays at once. Otherwise, for the entry's bank (built by 0x1D2B658: +0x50 SoundEventPlaybackStrategy , +0x60 Priority , +0x94 WaitSecondsBeforeUnloading in ms, +0x98 AlwaysInUse ): 1. a bank with byte +0x9C set refuses the event; 2. the bank's last-use time +0xAC is stamped; 3. a bank not yet requested ( +0x9D clear) refuses the event when its size would pass the context's limit and its priority is below context+0x1C ; otherwise it is marked requested and joins the load list context+0xA8 . The limit +0x10 is GlobalMemoryBudgetMB in bytes and +0x14 GlobalMemoryCloseToBudgetMB (62,914,560 and 52,428,800 live, exactly 60 and 50 MiB); +0x18 is the amount in use (48.0 MiB in one loaded Lithlad, with 4,596 events in the table); 4. the emitter's id joins the bank's list +0xE0 ; 5. a bank that belongs to an exclusive slot ( +0x88 , byte +0x99 ) replaces the slot's previous bank in the map at context+0x48 , which is released; 6. a loaded bank ( +0x9B ) plays the event now; 7. otherwise the event waits on the bank only when its strategy is PlayWhenLoaded (1) and fewer than 20 events are waiting ( +0xB0 ). Under DoNotPlay (2) the event is dropped and only the load goes ahead. DoNotPlay is set on 76 of the 1,958 records, PlayWhenLoaded on 1,882. Loading. A bank is an engine resource. The bank loader (vt 0x22C3850 vf4 0x54FEA4) gets the file's bytes, builds a 0x18-byte handle and calls the sound manager's vf32 0x54FF78, which parks banks under the bank lock until init.bnk has loaded. The handle holds +0x00 the bank id, +0x04 the size, +0x08 the data, +0x10 a "not init.bnk" flag and +0x11 a "not a Metadata bank" flag. 0xC378A0 loads one bank. The size must be at least 0x14, and the bank's language id ( BKHD+0x10 ) must be 0 or the current language, so banks of another language are refused. Then 0x12F1A00 copies the bank into a Wwise pool, or 0x550088 loads it in place. The live bank list. The bank manager [base+0x26FF9B0] keeps a hash table at +0x90 (buckets, u32 count of buckets, capacity, item count); entries point at bank slots (vt 0x1DBAA38: +0x10 u32 bank id, +0x18 data, +0x20 next in the chain, +0x38 u64 size). In an open-world scene 83 banks (210 MB) were loaded, all identified by id; the largest were global ui (26.7 MB), wraith (25.9), cbt insta chordkills (13.2), wld glb (13.0), mus global (12.4), char troll glb (10.8) and cbt player (10.5). Only 51 of the 83 data pointers still pointed at the bank: the source buffer of a copy-loaded bank is freed, so +0x18 is not reliable. Two more tables exist at +0x78 (12,289 buckets, 8,775 items) and +0xA8 (29 buckets, 4 items).

AudioHooks data (keys, hooks, conditions, game conditions, dialogue events) decides which line a character says. It is compiled into the audio cache at load by 0x1872B88 on the audio thread (builders 0x1871D7C, 0x1871C44 and 0x1872800); a change to the GameDB records afterwards has no effect. Fields read live instead: the dialogue-event priorities (0x66BCA0 / 0x66BD18), DialogCooldowns.Duration , Faction/Events/Events.KeepPriority , catalyst RandomChance and Presentation/Cooldowns.Duration . - Condition types are a 146-value string enumeration (registrar 0x83BC8C; CharacterEvent = 95, CharacterEventCount = 96), evaluated by the switch 0x189EC0 (case table 0x18B944). The CharacterEvent matcher 0x74EC88 compares an event's age (now minus the event time) with the condition's minimum and maximum. - AddKey 0x18E560 runs every hook of a key, without stopping at the first match. CanPlay 0x66BC00 lets a new line take over a talking character only if its PriorityInterrupt is strictly greater than the current line's PriorityContinue ; between equal priorities the first line wins. - A CharacterModel game condition (type 121) compiles to one bit (the payload's u16 at +0x62 ), tested against the speaker's audio-character bit set at +0x188 (0x18A8BA - 0x18BBD8). There are 124 such conditions; the player's audio character is [GameAudioManager+0xA5138] . - Audio characters (vt 0x1F797A8; a pool inside the audio manager at +0x38 , stride 0x4F8) keep a copy of their captain's event history at +0x248 , taken when the character spawns. - CCharacter.AddAudioHookKey 0x2D9B1C(character, key) fires a key on a character directly; keys without conditions (such as the per-line keys of scripted scenes) play whenever they are fired. The graph's size: 18,510 keys (4,635 post a Wwise event directly, 12,428 go through dialogue, 569 chain to further keys), 29,616 hooks and 29,709 actions ( SoundEventName on 7,598, DialogEventList on 17,214, pointing into the 17,239 AudioHooks/DialogEvents records). A following key and a switch to set are inline structures: StructuresAudioHookNextKey {AudioHookKey, DelaySeconds} (set on 590) and StructuresAudioHookSetSwitch {SwitchName, SwitchValue} .

An animation clip's events reach the character through its anim-event handler, vf19 0x4CD070 of the character classes (read here on CPlayerObj , vt 0x1F96818). The handler hashes each command's verb (0x813BCC upper-cases the first character, and 0x569FF8 folds the rest as h = h 31 + upper(c) ) and hands the hash to each component in turn: the character itself at +0x2680 , its combat object at +0x26A8 , its visual at +0x2348 and the non-player part at +0x1AF0 . Each component compares the hash with constants. A name table at 0x1F96580 holds 16-byte rows {u32 hash, pad, char name} . AUDIO HOOK KEY (0x88C44F8C) is compared in six functions (0x4CDA66, 0x769598, 0x787ED2, 0x7A3FB8, 0x7BA2EC, 0x1A3B2AC), and FOOTSTEP L / R / KEY , BODY IMPACT , SURFACEIMPACT , GROUNDCHECK and AUDIO HOOK KEY UI / UI ALWAYS have their hashes in the code as well. There is no sound verb. The hashes of SND , SND GROUND , SND SCUFF , SND PIVOT , SND UI , DIALOG EVENT , DIALOG KEY , SOUNDEVENT , FOOTSTEP and FOOTSTEP FL / FR occur nowhere in the executable as compared values, whereas 144 of the 204 verbs that the orc clips write do; the other 60 are misspellings. A clip therefore posts a Wwise event only through an AudioHooks/Keys record ( audio hook key <key ) or through a footstep type, which is itself a key ( fts step , fts run , fts scuff , fts land , fts jump , fts walk , fts step l and others, whose events depend on the surface). The game's 77,040 clips (in 4,565 files) write audio hook key 121,048 times, naming 1,715 distinct keys. They write snd 326 times, in 216 clips of 48 files: older text carried over in boss, Nazgul and prototype files, which plays nothing. Some clips also name keys that the database does not contain ( fol cmn recoil , fol cmn pivot ); these are silent as well.

WBMovieMgr (vt 0x230B308, 5 methods, WBMovieMgr.cpp ). vf2 0x32F930 is Create(out, name, flags) . A .vid name goes to 0x33048C: a resource request of type 0x10 through the resource system, malloc(0x168) , the constructor 0x3306A0, then vf22 with the UHD setting [base+0x272EC80] . Any other name goes to 0x1CA0538, which accepts only .bk2 , .bik and .mp4 , and only while the byte [base+0x2A37714] is set; it is clear in the shipped game. vf3 0x1CA0608 and vf4 0x331170 call vf5(bool) and vf16(float) on every live video under the list lock. A video resource (vt 0x2005158) is 0x168 bytes. Its base class (vt 0x1DB1800, constructor 0x33092C) holds +0x08 a list node and +0x18 the reference count; the resource adds +0x20 the Bink player, +0x28 a lock, +0x50 a copy of the play state and +0x58 / +0x60 state. vf22 0x33058C queues it to the render ring, and 0x3305D0 links it into the global video list (head 0x267E400, node = resource + 8, lock 0x2A37718). vf23 0x529BF8 opens the file (Bink player vf6) and vf25 0x33232C is the per-frame update (decode via 0x33236C, then copy player +0x168 to +0x50 ). The render command 0x3322BC walks the list on the render thread every frame and calls vf25 on each video. The Bink player (vt 0x1DB1740, 0x3F0 bytes, constructor 0x330830) holds +0x08 the HBINK , +0xF8 the open state (0 open, 3 failed), +0x168 the play state (2 = failed to open) and +0x170 the file name. vf14 0x331D78 Open(name, flags) calls BinkOpenWithOptions with a custom file callback 0x7A9EA8 that reads through the engine's file layer (0x1CD2194). vf15 0x331358 pauses, vf7 0x331620 sets volume and speakers, vf11 0x332420 registers frame buffers. HBINK : +0x00 width, +0x04 height, +0x08 frames, +0x0C current frame. On the army screen one video was live ( interface\videos\kraken\traits\resistant beast.vib , 1024 x 512, 239 frames, looping); in the open world the list was empty and no Bink player existed. The console variable Video.UHD ( WBMovieMgr.cpp , handler 0x1CA04F8: 0 never, 1 always, 2 default) is stored in [base+0x272EC80] .

Interface/Movies holds 950 records with 29 fields: Movie (the path), AudioBundle, AdditionalAssetBundle, Loop, MenuBackgroundVideo, CanSkip, FullScreen, RenderGameInBackground, ScreenPosition, PauseGame, PauseAI, PauseMovieOnLastFrame, RenderBars, PlayCreditsOnFinish, fade-in and fade-out frames, SyncVideoToWwiseAudio, WwiseAudioKey, SkipSoundKey, GlobalBusKey, StopGlobalBusKey, CommandSet, Sounds, Events, OverlayVideos, OverlayMaterial and RequiredSubtitleEntries. Records name a .vid ; the engine opens the .vib beside it. A path is set on 939 records: 725 resolve to a shipped movie (711 distinct files) and 214 name movies that do not ship (cut skill-progression, attribute and trait clips). Flag counts: SyncVideoToWwiseAudio 947, PauseGame 943, CanSkip 919, Loop 740, FullScreen 210. Event lists live in Interface/Movies/Events/{PresentationEvents, BossInfoEvent, UIVideoElementEvents, HUDWidgetConfig, GameEvents} . The game ships 743 movie files under game\cinematics\videos (about 10 GB) and game\interface\videos (about 2 GB): 12.85 GB and 3.8 hours in all. Of these, 668 are Bink 2 ( KB2j 661, KB2i 7) and 71 Bink 1 ( BIKi ), all named .vib ; the header word at +0x04 is the file size minus 8 in 739 of 739. Resolutions: 1024 x 512 (479, the UI clips), 1920 x 1080 (125, the cinematics), 512 x 256 (76), 4 x 4 (56 placeholder clips of the third story DLC), 1280 x 720 (2) and 3840 x 2160 (1). Only interface\videos\intro.vib has an audio track: movie sound comes from Wwise. Who plays a movie. 0x32F3AC (it reads the Interface/Movies fields and the master volume and starts the interface's cinematic state) plays a movie record. Its callers include the presentation element start 0x5D20C4 (via 0x32F3A0), the console command UI.PlayVideo (handler 0x17C0ADC), a video render-target path 0x335CF4 and the skip prompt 0x17F0E48. The UI video player 0x17FC5C0 (callers include CacheLoadWorldVideo 0x1B76988) creates videos through WBMovieMgr vf2; Video.GotoFrame is handled by 0x17FE1C8.

t: Animation: clips, behavior graphs and the runtime

x: Animation is written by Monolith, not Havok. The executable carries run-time type information for exactly one Havok animation class, hkaSkeleton (kept for cloth deformation), and for no Havok Behavior class at all; the many hka and hkb names elsewhere in the file are Havok's serialization name table, which survives without the code. The engine's own animation sources are named in its strings: AnimNodeLink.cpp , ThreadAnimNodeLink.cpp , AnimationMgr.cpp , BehaviorData.cpp , CharacterBehaviorInterface.cpp , SimpleModel.cpp and FacialAnimationMgr.cpp .

header 'ANIX' 0x2C 0x30 file size track count track table offset block chunk offset block chunk size anim chunk offset anim chunk size 1 1 tracks run-length runs {channel hash, run length, node hashes}: rotation 0x27436396, position 0x00CE66FC, events 0x210C8F5A anim +0x00 directory offset (0x10), +0x04 clip count, +0x0C the EVENT DICTIONARY offset; chunk directory {u32 name hash, u32 relative offset}; records are not in directory order record name[0x30] +0x30 (flag << 16) (0x7C + 16 blocksets + 8 named) +0x34 blocksets +0x36 named +0x38 groups +0x3A tracks +0x3C root summary: start position, start rotation (x, y, z, w), end position, end rotation +0x74 u32 +0x78 duration (ms) +0x7C codecs (4 characters per group), group of each track (u8), remap (u16 per track), blockset table {offset, size, t0, t1}, named table {hash, offset}, the KeyString blob blockset u32 named count, u16 group offsets, u16 named offsets, align 4, u32 LITH 0x2B99DBC1 LITH {keys, n2, n3, times[keys], 0} Codec Content --- --- SQ03 constant rotations: 42-bit smallest-three, three per 16 bytes AQ03 animated rotations with their own key times (keys may skip frames where motion is smooth) SV01 / AV01 constant / animated vectors UATR position polylines: a u8 segment and a u8 weight per key, then a 4-aligned float3 palette UAQT / UAVT keyed rotations / vectors STRI event strings (offsets into the KeyString blob) The codec registry. Every codec's block evaluator is registered by its FourCC through one routine, 0x11B51BC, into one registry object at 0x2A55CF0. The routine takes the FourCC as an immediate in edx and the evaluator in r8, and it leaves r8 alone, so the shipped code registers SQ02 with SQ01's evaluator. The thread-safe accessor 0x261618 returns the registry, and the evaluator slots sit inside it (for example 0x2A55D18 SQ03 and 0x2A55D38 AQ03). Three tables fill it: Table Registers --- --- 0x11E1940, by CPU cpuid , then SSE4.1 ( bt ecx, 0x13 ), else SSE3 ( test cl, 1 ), else neither, each branch registering SQ01 / SQ02, SQ03, AQ02, AQ03 (SSE4.1: 0x11E0694, 0x2D21B0, 0x11DE4B0, 0x2D26E0; SSE3: 0x11E0D44, 0x11E13F4, 0x11DF098, 0x11DFC80; neither: 0x11E9520, 0x11E9578, 0x11E884C, 0x11E89FC); then, for every CPU, Q101 0x11E93D0, SV01 0x5D4114, AV01 0x5D3FC4, PQ03 0x11E916C 0x11DE35C, plain USVO 0x11DE2B8, UAVO 0x11DE114, USCO 0x11DE260, UACO 0x11DDE80, USFT 0x6A6B6C, UAFT 0x11DDF5C, CAF2 0x11DDCC4, CAF4 0x2D20A4, USBT 0x7B3C50, USIN and UASI 0x11DE28C, UABT 0x11DDDE8, UAIN 0x11DE034, UASC 0x7E33D0 0x11DDC00, tracks CATR 0x11DD618, CART 0x11DD3F8, UATR 0x183810, CSTR 0x11DD8C4, CSRT 0x11DD83C, USTR 0x11DDB38, STRI 0x11DD954 (it hashes the literal "KeyString" once), CACQ 0x11E8FDC, CRS3 0x11E9110, UAQT 0x33DF48, UAVT 0x183688 Any current CPU takes the SSE4.1 branch. A FourCC is an immediate, so it names each evaluator in any build of the executable (see Game builds: Steam, GOG and Microsoft Store). Event commands. A clip's event text is a list of commands separated by ; ( snd fol cmn attack windup; BPW; STARTFACING; AFACE Angry; ), stored under the KeyString hash 0xB9010BE0. The character's animation-event handler (vt 0x1F96818 vf19, 0x4CD070) hashes each command's verb: 0x813BCC upper-cases the first character, and 0x569FF8 folds the rest as h = h 31 + upper(c) (the keyword hash below). It hands the hash to each component ( +0x2680 , the combat object +0x26A8 , the visual component +0x2348 and, for an NPC, +0x1AF0 ), and each compares it against constants. The table at 0x1F96580 holds 16-byte rows {u32 hash, padding, char name} (the row at 0x1F96658 is AUDIO HOOK KEY , hash 0x88C44F8C). AUDIO HOOK KEY is compared in six functions (0x4CDA66, 0x769598, 0x787ED2, 0x7A3FB8, 0x7BA2EC, 0x1A3B2AC). FOOTSTEP L / R / KEY , BODY IMPACT , SURFACEIMPACT , GROUNDCHECK and AUDIO HOOK KEY UI / UI ALWAYS also have their hashes in code. The engine has no SND verb: the hashes of SND , SND GROUND , SND SCUFF , SND PIVOT , SND UI , DIALOG EVENT , DIALOG KEY , SOUNDEVENT , FOOTSTEP and FOOTSTEP FL / FR occur nowhere in the executable as compared constants, while 144 of the 204 verbs the orc clips write do (the 60 missing are misspellings). So a clip posts a sound only through an AudioHooks/Keys record ( audio hook key <key ) or a footstep type, itself a key ( fts step , fts run , fts scuff , fts land , fts jump ...). The 77,040 clips of the 4,565 shipped files write audio hook key 121,048 times (1,715 keys) and snd 326 times (216 clips in 48 files, among them Sauron's and the Nazgul prototype's): text carried over from older files, and silent. Some clips also name keys the shipped database lacks ( fol cmn recoil , fol cmn pivot ), which are silent too. The gameplay commands the orc clips use include APPLYDAMAGE , AD , BCOL / ECOL , BHITWIN , BCANWIN / ECANWIN , BTS / ETS , BPW / EPW , the facing commands ( STARTFACING , BEFACING ), ComplexAnim , STOP ALIGN and the face expressions AFACE / RFACE / CLFACE . - A record ends at the next record by position, the event dictionary or the end of the chunk, not at the directory's next entry. - Group and LITH offsets inside a blockset are u16, so a blockset holds at most 64 KB; long clips use several blocksets that share their boundary key, with absolute LITH times, an AQ03 block header of (start time, end time, keys) and one STRI group per blockset. - Unused SQ03 slots must hold a valid quaternion: zero bits decode to a negative value under the square root, and the vectorized SQ03 evaluator asserts. Shipped files never leave them zero. - The clip root is the character's position, about 1 m above the feet (the same reference as the live position at CCharacter+0xAC ). - One path can be several different files: pl sync chordkill front.anix ships as a 466,997-byte loose entry and as a 464,227-byte bundle section; the game uses whichever its region loaded.

resource table [base+0x2A86758] + (hash(path) & 0x7FF) 0x18; resource +0x08 = a 0x28-byte entry {+0x00 handle vt 0x1DB4508, +0x08 the anim object, +0x18 3, +0x24 index} anim object vt 0x1E6F528 (constructor 0x57E4F4, 0x88 bytes); +0x30 the data object, cached +0x38 anim chunk and +0x68 block chunk (0x57E5A8) data object 0x28 bytes (loader 0x480AEC): +0x00 block chunk (16-aligned) +0x18 size, +0x08 anim chunk +0x1C size, +0x10 node / track pairs +0x20 count anim registry [base+0x26FEFF8] + 8 + (hash(path) & 0x3FF) 0x18, node = object + 0x10 The samplers (0x260740, 0x261360) re-read these pointers and the clip record on every sample, so a change to a clip's values in memory plays on the next frame. The track-to-bone binding is a vector per skeleton indexed by the file's track index and built at load, so a clip with a different track layout cannot replace a loaded one in place. A region change reloads the region's animation files. Events are pre-parsed. When an anim object attaches, 0x4B9E58 parses the file's event dictionary (the anim chunk's +0x0C : a path, clip names, every event string, then each clip's events) into per-clip objects in an arena. The anim object holds the arena at +0x40 (its size at +0x48 ) and, at +0x50 .. +0x58 , a vector of {u32 hash(clip), object } . A clip object holds +0x10 frames, +0x14 count, +0x18 duration (ms), +0x20 a u32 frame per event ( +0x28 count), +0x30 the events as (string index << 24) ms with 0xFF meaning no text ( +0x38 count), and +0x40 the strings ( +0x48 count). Playback reads these tables, never the STRI tracks. Which characters can play a clip. A character plays a clip by name from its skeleton family's clip table (0x302540): [[[[char+0x110]+0x1C0]+0x50]+0xB0] (vt 0x1E6F3F8). A table takes clips only from files its member list names ( +0x78 / +0x80 , 0x38-byte entries: +0x20 the path, +0x28 the anim object while loaded); the orc list names 3,363 paths and the olog's 2,268. A file at a path the list does not name registers nowhere, even in a listed folder; a listed path that ships in no archive (2,107 of the orc list's) is an unused slot. Loading a bundle registers its clips, unloading unregisters them. The orc, Gondorian and Easterling families share many entries (one anim object for orc deathtaunts.anix in all three); the olog's list is separate. Six tables served 47 spawned characters in one scene. Armor shoulder-pad helper bones ( L/R SPadX ) are keyed at half of the arm's swing (correlation 0.99 to 1.00 on five sprint clips), so they follow the arm by design data, not by a constraint. The orc clips never key the ten twist helpers ( L/R ArmuX , Bicep , Forearm , Wrist , Thigh : 0 of 4,463 clips in 351 files), so the engine places those itself; every other orc bone is keyed somewhere, the fingers in 99% of clips ( L Index1 in 4,421). The weapon grip is a layer as well as baked into clips: orc awareness misc.anix ships Orc L Hand Weapon / Orc R Hand Weapon , and a fight plays the right one at run time (41 starts in 250 s of one fight).

The .skel file format is described in Archives and file formats. Its header word 15 counts extra animation tracks ( Track : a name, a P919 type and default bytes) stored after the bone records, and the masks then hold one value per bone and per track (of the 4,589 distinct shipped skeletons, 8 carry them: param head 235, camrig 40, shields, a crossbow). The name table's order is the runtime bone index, not the depth-first record order. The loaded skeleton. The resource table [base+0x2A86758] + (P919(path) & 0x7FF) 0x18 gives a resource whose +0x08 entry holds the Skeleton at [entry+0x08] (0xB8 bytes, loader 0x504420): +0x10 the bone set (0x98 bytes), +0xB0 the clip table (see Which characters can play a clip above). Bone set offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 the local binds, 32 bytes per bone (translation, w, rotation) +0x38 nodes, 0x40 bytes: byte 0 the parent (0xFF for the root), 1 the bone's index, 2 the first child's index, 3 the child count, 4 deform; +0x24 the local translation and rotation +0x40 the bone count +0x70 / +0x78 the names / their hashes +0x80 the inverse model-space binds, 28 bytes per bone +0x88 the same inverses, 32 bytes per bone (w = 1.0) The loader (0x4127F8 - 0x411110) inverts the file's model-space binds in place (0x341280, without normalizing the quaternions) and keeps the file's own values nowhere. A scan of 3,440 MB found no copy outside the skeleton arrays, and 1,486 of 1,491 resident skeletons (44,757 bones) equal their shipped files on every array. Because the inverse does not normalize, inverting it again scales the translation by q to the fourth power. The skinning palette. 0x183B90(out, bone set, N, pose) computes out[i] = pose[i] [boneset+0x88][i] , reading the stored inverses on every call; it is called from the per-model publish 0x251534 (from 0x187A38 and 0x3053AC). The model (vt 0x1F6F950) holds its own part at +0xC8 (vt 0x1DB7380: +0x1D8 the skeleton, +0x198 the buffer handle, the real buffer [[handle+0x10 + i 8]] , four slots) and a holder at +0x240 ( [holder+0x40] the pose node: +0x10 data, +0x1C count). Of 960 live palettes, 959 equal the formula (175 heads, 176 bases; another model's pose fails as a control). So a changed inverse bind shows at the next palette build: after one in a running game, 4 of 21 models drawn with that head already held the new palette while the game stood paused, and 17 did not yet. Who draws with which skeleton. Of 1,410 live parts, heads (175) and weapons and props draw by their own palette with no binding; pieces (544) and worn weapons (85) draw by the base rig's palette through a binding. A head's body bones ( pNull .. Head : 8 on Talion's player head01 g , 9 on orc heads) follow the rig. Talion's rig is player base (128 bones, 543 animation sets, 11 bindings); his head player head01 g has 241 bones and its own face set. Piece maps. A piece worn on a rig goes through one CModelSkeletonMap per (rig, piece) (vt 0x1DC7220, 0x2F0 bytes, constructor 0x702870, built by 0x6D5B30 - 0x6D5D68 - 0x199990), owned by [GameManager+0x40] (find-or-create 0x1CC280 over four sorted vectors). Besides the bone-number table at +0x38 (see Captain appearance, "Pieces on other skeletons"), it holds: Offset Holds --- --- +0x10 / +0x14 the rig's and the piece's hashes +0x30 its own parent +0x32 FORCE +0x50 roots +0x68 pairs {rig bone, piece bone, rig parent} +0x80 deltas (f32[3], the rig's local translation minus the piece's) +0x98 the count +0xA8 / +0xB0 the two skeletons +0x2C0 listeners A piece bone whose local translation lies 0.1 cm or more from the rig's (squared distance 0.01, the float at 0x202E820), and everything below it, is retargeted (table flag 0x1000); FORCE retargets every matched bone. That rule reproduces 217 of 217 live maps (1,116 pairs); 53 are forced (heads). A part (vt 0x1FE1A00: +0x48 its render object, +0x70 the piece skeleton, +0x80 the map) carries a 0x68-byte retarget block at [render+0x160] : +0x20 deltas, +0x38 the piece's inverse binds of the paired bones (w cleared), +0x50 pairs (91 of 91 equal the map's). A map is built once; a change of which bones retarget applies only when the game builds the map again. Followers are not binds: [own+0x150] holds one 32-byte row per rig bone a follower (a head, a hood) follows, and live 0 of 978 rows of orc base 's 163 followers equal a model bind, while two followers of the same six bones hold different values: per-character data. Rest copies and what the clips drive. Each (skeleton, .anix ) binding in the clip bank [base+0x26FF080] keeps a rest copy, built by 0x57EF20 from the local binds and the file's bind clip; the sampler 0x261360 copies it into the pose, then the clip's tracks overwrite the lanes they drive ( binding+0x18 : u16 byte offsets). The undriven lanes equal the skeleton's local bind: 100,222 of 100,222 on orc base (1,019 sets), 88,256 of 88,256 on player base (544), 12 of 12 on an orc head. An orc head's face set drives the rotation of 133 of its 134 bones and the position of 123; Talion's head 240 and 232 of 241; on orc base almost every rotation is driven but the position of 66 of 100 bones by no set, and player base 100 of 128. So on a head a changed bind shows as the opposite change of the mesh (the animation keeps the pose and the inverse changes), while on a body a changed bind position moves the joint. Rigs compared. The Olog rig shares the player rig's joint convention but not its rest pose: 77 shared bones (Olog 89, player 128), a child joint's direction in its bone's own frame differing by a median 0.0 degrees over 21 chains, Neck (34.4 degrees) and Spine4 (26.2) differing by pure swing, a twist difference of median 6.4 and at most 15.6 degrees, and 1.58 times the height. Talion's locomotion clip pl movaction.anix keys 55 of the player's 128 bones and, played by bone name, drives 47 of the Olog's 89. Shadow of Mordor's orc skeletons ( SKEL v8) share the same space (see Comparison with Shadow of Mordor).

A .bvr is a GameDB database whose root type is BlendDB . Its categories are node types ( BlendState , StateTransition , Animation.SimpleAnimation , Predicate.And , Modifier. ...); its records are the graph's nodes, mostly named secondary records, with inline structures ( PotentialFrame , AnimPoint , ValueModifier , AnchorData , TrajectoryPoint ) as primaries. The player graph has 139,198 records in 270 categories: 46,400 structures, 22,229 state modifiers, 21,128 predicates, 15,704 transitions, 7,561 logic nodes, 6,454 camera modifiers, 3,750 states, 3,069 animations and more. Record Holds --- --- BehaviorSource the root: StartState, DefaultWeightset, ModifierTypes, PreviewModel, TrackingStates, reset-to-default states BlendState one animation state: AnimationLink (the animation tree), Links (outgoing transitions) with a normalized-time window each and a minimum character LOD; Modifiers; Rate, DefaultBlendTime, BlendInterpolationMethod, Looping, Mirrored, gravity and foot / hand IK, movement / rotation / collision scale, NativeState, AIPosture, Priority CameraBlendState a camera state: CameraModifiers and a predicate StateTransition an edge: target node, predicate, blend time, window, sync, mirroring, interpolation The 29 graphs hold 10,702 blend states and 73,448 transition links. The four player graphs (player elf, el2, elt, bar) have about 2,050 states and 1,700 camera states each; the warg has 431, the troll 218 and the five orc class graphs 132-136. Smaller graphs serve the Easterlings, ologs, humans, the AI Talion, the fellbeast, Sauron's war form, the Nazgul, the Balrog, Gollum, goblins and spiders. Of the links, 73,017 resolve to a state and 431 have no target; none names a missing state. From the start state, 5,300 states are reachable by transitions; the rest are entered by code (grabs, riding, ladders, mount deaths: the states that synchronized attacks and presentations force). All 17,606 clip references of the states resolve to a clip in some .anix (the .skel animation-set paths the nodes name ship nowhere, so the join goes through the clips' own names). A BlendDB record is a native structure. Its header byte +0x01 is 0x1A (flag 0x10) on all 318,372 live records, so its fields sit at instance + SlotOffset(type, field) (SlotOffset 0x251C24, size step 0x251CAC) instead of the GameDB slot rule, and compiled code reads them as plain members. By-name getters divert such records to the reflected path (GetFloatByName 0x115B43C - 0x5DA0FC). BlendState live layout: Mirrored +0x68 , Priority +0x80 , DefaultBlendTime +0x88 , StartPct +0x98 , Rate +0xA8 , Gravity +0x110 , Looping +0x118 , Links +0x138 ( {pointer, count} ); editor-only fields take no bytes. Six fields read live equal the disk decode for 10,697 of 10,697 records. Only two "play as" tiers are authored into the player graph: the tags pool (371 records) holds PlayAs Spider and PlayAs Gollum , and Client/PlayerMovement has exactly five records (PlayerMovement, PlayerMovement Alt01, SpiderMovement, GollumMovement, DwarfMovement).

M = [[char+0x110]+0x1C0] is the character's model animation instance (vt 0x1DA9700; the model object is vt 0x1F6F950). M+0x08 is a vector of 0xA0-byte trackers, one per active clip ; M+0x50 the skeleton resource; M+0xC8 the pose-job descriptor and M+0xD8 its 20-byte blend entries (one per tracker); M+0x118 the time source; M+0x128 job submitted, +0x12A needs evaluation. Tracker offset Meaning --- --- +0x02 flags: bit 0 advanced by the engine clock, bit 1 loop, bit 3 cleared on wrap +0x04 u16 delay counter (0xFFFF = none) +0x08 the clip name's hash +0x0C current key index +0x10 rate (time += (dt + remainder) x rate) +0x14 weight +0x18 sub-millisecond remainder +0x1C playback position in ms +0x24 weight-set index (-1 = whole body) +0x44 key count +0x4C duration in ms (equal to the clip record's +0x78 in 100 of 100) Tracker 0 is always the clip base (the model's base pose). Clips layer per body part rather than cross-fade: a player at a fidget state carried base plus PL Base Idle B ( pl fidgets.anix ) and two pairs of fist idle clips, all at weight 1.0 with different weight sets. Most trackers have rate 0 and are not engine-advanced: the graph writes their time. In play, tracker time advanced at the world clock's rate (median 1.0 ms per world ms over 42,123 consecutive same-clip pairs; 731 loops or restarts).

Ragdolls are a death effect. Every character model carries a physics ragdoll, but the powered ragdoll, its brain and the joint tuning from the database are started only by the dead-body step 0x2F8460: the slot claim (0x65C214), the brain start (0x65C274) and the joint setup (0x64D4A4) each have that one caller. Knockdowns and other reactions of living characters are animations.

The NPC Update runs its dead-body branch, slot 121 (base implementation 0x175020), once the combat object's dead byte [char+0x26A8]+0x4A0 and the byte char+0x225E are set (see Threads and the frame); on the frame of death the AI update itself calls the step once. 0x2F8460(state = char+0x1AF0 , character): 1. Reads Combat/Category.RagdollReaction of the killing attack (0x65E990; 11 of 2,559 categories set one) and, when a ragdoll is pending, its InitalVelocityScale and ForceValue . 2. Claims a ring slot, then, when the character's model ( [char+0x2B30] ) names a Character/Models.RagdollConfig , applies that config's joints, enables the ragdoll and starts its brain; otherwise it starts the controller with no config and no brain. 3. Fires Combat/Buffs.DeathProjectiles , switches the character to RigidBody , plays the clip named by Character/Models/Global.RagdollDeathAnimation ( base ) on the model and posts the audio hook CharacterSwitchesToRagdoll . 4. On every later frame: runs the brain (0x30F6D4), then tests for rest. Counting from the state's time stamp and leaving out the brain's running time, a body is at rest after 15 s, or after 3 s once its speed falls below Character/Models/BodyCleanup.AtRestSpeed (15 cm/s without a record). A resting body that is not the player goes to the body cleanup 0x6C00A0 ( Lifetime , SinkDistance ); otherwise 0x145218 relaxes the hit reaction ( RelaxTime , start and end friction and tau factor). The thresholds are initialized data ( [base+0x26736A4] 15.0, [base+0x26736AC] 15.0, [base+0x26736B0] 3.0, enable bytes [base+0x26736A8] and [base+0x26736C0] ), each read only by this step. The two BodyCleanup records, Troll (15 models) and Fellbeast (2), set AtRestSpeed to 1,000,000, so those bodies rest at once; the other 264 models use the default. The per-character body settings are copied from Character/Models/Global when the character is created (0xFCFB4, from its slot 16), into char+0x1E50 : Offset Field Shipped --- --- --- +0x239 BodyRagdoll true +0x218 BodyDeathDirMinY 0.4 +0x238 BodyDeathForce true +0x21C BodyDeathForceScale 0.5 +0x234 BodyDirDeathForce true +0x220 BodyDirDeathForceScale 1.5 +0x228 BodyStickDist 400 +0x22C BodyStickTime 0.3 +0x230 BodyDeathScaleVelocity 1.0 +0x224 BodyDeathClampVelocityMax 800 A later edit of the record reaches only characters created afterwards. Offset from the character Content --- --- +0x110 - +0x1C8 the physics ragdoll (below) +0x1AF0 dead-body state: +0x00 phase (0 while alive), +0x308 the killing attack, +0x310 the BodyCleanup record, +0x320 a time stamp (f64), +0x350 - +0x35D flags +0x1AF8 the ragdoll controller +0x1E50 body settings (above) +0x2C17 u8, set on a corpse

[model+0x1C8] (26 of 26 characters read): Offset Content --- --- +0x00 pointer to the shared definition of the skeleton's ragdoll (one per body family) +0x30 the character +0x38 the model +0x78 , +0x88 per-body arrays (count at +0x80 , +0x90 ) +0x98 joint objects (count at +0xA0 ) Every ragdoll has one body more than joints: orcs, Olog-hai and cave trolls 20 bodies and 19 joints, humans and wargs 21 and 20. A joint object (vt 0x1DB4980) keeps the powered-angle limits of its pitch, yaw and roll axes in radians at +0x0C - +0x20 (slots 10-12 convert from degrees), mirror bytes from +0x24 (slots 13-15) and a motor-disabled byte at +0x28 (slot 8). The joint setup (entered at 0x64D4A4, which reaches its body 0x64D4B8(ragdoll, config) by a conditional tail jump) walks the config's Ragdoll/Constraints : joint [+0x98][Index] , motor disabled unless Powered , then each axis's ConstraintAxisData MinPoweredAngle / MaxPoweredAngle (default -180 / 180) and Mirror . On the 11 corpses read whose powered ragdoll started, 19 of 19 joints hold exactly the database limits; living characters hold unconfigured joints (±565.49, 180 × π). The database tuning therefore reaches the physics only at death. Ragdoll has two configs, Orc Base and OlogHai Base , each a brain and 19 joints (indexes 0-18, torso to feet). Character/Models.RagdollConfig names Orc Base on 113 models (humans included, whose 20th joint is never tuned), OlogHai Base on one and nothing on 167; models without a config, such as wargs, still take a ring slot but get no brain.

The engine runs at most eight powered ragdolls. [base+0x26FFB90] holds eight controller pointers and [base+0x26FFB88] a cursor. The claim releases the controller in the cursor's slot if there is one (0x65C528), stores the new controller, writes the slot index into controller+0x2EC and advances the cursor modulo 8. A released controller keeps +0x2EC at -1 and its joints keep their tuning. In one read 15 corpses lay in the world and two held slots.

The controller at char+0x1AF8 : Offset Content --- --- +0x08 the character +0x10 the brain ( Ragdoll/Brains ) +0x18 the config +0x20 , +0x28 the current and the prior behavior controller +0x48 eight 0x50-byte players +0x2C8 , +0x2CC , +0x2D0 height, speed, average body speed +0x2D4 - +0x2E8 time stationary, moving, on ground, in air, in the current behavior, in total +0x2EC ring slot, -1 for none The brain step 0x30F6D4 runs only while the controller holds a slot. It updates the samples and the timers (the brain's OnGround and Stationary float ranges decide which timers run), then walks Brain.BehaviorControllers in order and takes the first controller whose conditions all pass. The conditions cover float ranges (height, velocity, average body velocity, and the time on ground, in air, stationary, moving, in the current behavior and in total), spine upright, head severed, include and exclude hints, the current and prior controller, and the combat state. On a change it records the prior controller, resets the behavior timer, picks a BehaviorSet whose RequiredRagdollConfig is the controller's config, picks one of its behaviors and starts the behavior's Sequences . Orc Base lists ten controllers ( DieHeadSeveredController , DieController , FallingBraceImpactController , TuckAndRollController , FallForwardBraceController , WritheOnGroundController , PanicLostGroundController , the two leg-kicking controllers and FallbackController ); OlogHai Base three. A behavior ( Ragdoll/Behaviors , 18) sets strength and stiffness ranges, joint masks and scalar mappings; a sequence ( Ragdoll/Sequences , 16) plays timed target poses ( Clamp , PingPong ), and a target pose sets per-joint pitch, yaw and roll. In one read of eleven corpses with a brain, three ran DieHeadSeveredController , four DieController and four WritheOnGroundController (one entered from FallForwardBraceController ).

Two keyword tables name the ragdoll controls a clip can carry, each entry a 32-bit hash and the name: - at 0x1E658B0: RAGDOLL , DESTROY , RESUMERAGDOLL , DISALLOWRAGDOLL , ALLOWRAGDOLL , DELAYRAGDOLL , COLLISION CHECK NONE , COLLISION CHECK WORLD ONLY , COLLISION CHECK ALL , GROUNDCHECK , RAGDOLL STIFFNESS , NEVER RAGDOLL , FREEZERAGDOLL and BEHAVIOR HINT ; - at 0x1F9FC40, for sync actions: SYNCACTION ALLOWDEATH , SYNCACTION DELAYDEATH , RESUMERAGDOLL , ALLOWRAGDOLL , RAGDOLL , DELAYRAGDOLL and STOP ALIGN (this table has no terminator; its seven entries run into a string). The hash is the multiply-by-31 string hash over the upper-cased, sign-extended bytes: 0x569FF8(rest of the string, seed) computes seed 31 + c per character, recursively, and its callers seed it with the upper-cased first character, so a keyword matches in any case (17 of 17 table entries reproduce). The same hash has 18 callers, among them the slot-19 method of four classes. The keywords are not turned into flags when a clip loads: the dead-body step asks the clip at run time. 0x75BB34(character, attack) copies the RAGDOLL and RESUMERAGDOLL entries to the stack, and 0x2C5DD8(character, attack) uses the DESTROY entry. Both pass the key set to 0x4CAB0C, which walks the events of the clip the character is playing (when [[char+0x26A8]+0x114] is not -1) and compares each event name's hash with the keys; otherwise they pass it to 0x2C5E10, which checks the attack's own animation: the clip named by AnimationData.Name (looked up in the character's set by 0x4C8A0C) or, without one, the AnimationData.BehaviorNode , where each key is tested by name (0x1BDEA50). The dead-body step 0x2F8460 is the only caller of 0x75BB34 and one of two callers of 0x2C5DD8 (the other is 0x19B6D1C). It calls 0x75BB34 only while the state byte +0x35A is set, then clears that byte without testing the result. The DESTROY query gates the step's flags: while +0x353 is set and the killing attack shows no DESTROY , the step can enter phase 5 (after further checks, among them the attack's AttackPostData.SuppressDeathAnimGroundCheck ) and sets +0x356 when a second query, on the record 0x190E80 returns (a wrapper of the Combat/Attack.MultiHitRecords accessor), finds DESTROY ; in another branch, no DESTROY sets +0x35C and +0x35D . The other entries of both tables have no direct reader in the code (checked for four of them). In a sample of 40 clip files (302 clips, 4,192 events) the ragdoll events are DELAYRAGDOLL 23, RAGDOLL 22 (one with argument 0.25), ALLOWRAGDOLL 15 and RESUMERAGDOLL 14, spelled in any case. Combat/Sync records can start the source or the target with a delayed ragdoll ( StartWithDelayRagdollSource 1 of 1,507, StartWithDelayRagdollTarget 98).

- Which code reads the clip keywords that have no direct reader ( DISALLOWRAGDOLL , DELAYRAGDOLL , FREEZERAGDOLL , BEHAVIOR HINT and the sync-action table), and why the dead-body step calls the RAGDOLL query without testing its result. - Which Havok objects stand behind a joint object (it points to objects of vt 0x1DABE88 and vt 0x22C2EE0), and whether they own the live hkpRagdollConstraintData instances; the hknpRagdoll and hknpRagdollKeyFrameHierarchyUtility classes ship, with no use traced. - How the animated pose hands over to the ragdoll at the switch (only the base clip is replayed), and what the byte +0x46 of the physics ragdoll means (set on every corpse and on 7 of 11 living characters). - Which graph node writes the trackers' time, and where the transition in progress and its blend time are held (not in the character's state slots or the link). - What clears the state slots +0x1198 and +0x11A8 for a moment (43% of samples read null). - The role of the AnimationMgr's 256-object pool. - The hand-off from the pose output to skinning. - Which render-thread code consumes a part's retarget block ( [render+0x160] ), and whether a hood worn on the head rig draws by the head's palette (it has no model of its own). - How the hand-weapon layer blends over a clip's own finger keys: whether it overrides them (which would make the grip the clips bake redundant) or adds to them. - Which names AnimLink.PlayAnim accepts (state names, clip names or both). The request builder 0x41A1E0 takes two names: PlayAnim fills the first, which keeps only StringHash(name) at link+0x23C and sets link+0x262 ; the second form instead looks the name up as a record of the character's graph category [char+0x11C0] (0x7C6F20) and keeps the record at link+0x248 . The request is then posted to the animation side (0x1159E8C), whose use of the hash is not traced.

Physics is Havok Physics 2016.2 ( hk2016 2 0 r1 ) in its new pipeline: the hknp classes, which replaced the older hkp API. The build is a hybrid: rigid bodies are hknp , but ragdoll constraints are still the legacy hkpRagdollConstraintData and hkpLimitedHingeConstraintData . Havok AI ( hkai ) provides navigation meshes, avoidance and silhouettes, and Havok Cloth deforms cloth with hkaSkeleton ; Havok Animation and Behavior are not used (see Animation). HavokScript runs the game's scripts (see Scripting). A second cloth system, the engine's own GPU cloth, runs in a compute shader for orc and olog gear, banners, flags and others (see Cloth). Havok work runs on three HavokWorkerThread s (shared routine 0x11AFE58) and on the main thread's task queue: in play the main thread spends about 5% of its time in the physics step ( TtPhysics , 0x6528B8) and about 3% in the Havok task queue, where hkaiAvoidanceSolverTask shows up.

The world has exactly one construction path (its constructor 0x15464FC has one caller, 0x11B1504, whose only caller is 0x1187004), and the engine publishes its owner in a static slot: [base+0x2A86760] the physics owner (0x6860 bytes), published by 0x1186FB0 (1 write, 66 reads in 60 functions) [base+0x2A86768] u32 generation, incremented at each publish owner+0x20 - hknpWorld (allocated from the Havok heap, 0xAA0 bytes) The world is rebuilt on every world load.

hknpWorld (vt 0x22EEA90). Sub-objects, named by their own run-time type information: Offset Class --- --- +0x018 a pointer to itself +0x470 hknpMultithreadedSimulation +0x478 hknpDynamicSpaceSplitter +0x488 hknpHybridBroadPhase +0x6C8 hknpStreamContactSolver +0x6D0 hknpConstraintAtomSolver +0x9C0 gravity , an aligned hkVector4 (0, -9.81, 0, 0): Y is up, SI units +0x9D8 hknpMaterialLibrary (vt 0x22ED5C8; from the construction info, else a default made by 0x154AC7C) +0x9E0 hknpMotionPropertiesLibrary (vt 0x22ED290; 8 motion properties) +0x9E8 the body-quality library (0x620 bytes: 32 inline 0x30-byte hknpBodyQuality ) Arrays are Havok hkArray s ( {T data, u32 size, u32 capacity and flags} ). The body arrays at +0x040 , +0x050 , +0x0C8 and +0x0D8 / +0x0F8 hold 15,360 entries each: the body capacity is 15,360 , kept as parallel structure-of-arrays lanes. +0x0B8 is the active-body id list (254 of 15,364 in a combat scene); a body id packs index generation << 24 . +0x108 has capacity 1,024, matching the material palette. This gravity drives the rigid-body solver only. Characters move through the engine's character controller, which the behavior graph owns (see Animation).

Both libraries keep their entries in an hkArray at +0x30 . The material palette is one contiguous array of 1,024 hknpMaterial entries (vt 0x1DAC040, stride 0x80): Offset Type Field Default --- --- --- --- +0x32 hkHalf dynamic friction 0.5 +0x34 hkHalf static friction 0.5 +0x36 hkHalf restitution 0.0 +0x3C f32 - 0.05 +0x40 f32 max contact impulse (-1.0 = an untouched slot) -1.0 +0x44 f32 - 1.0 +0x48 f32 - 1.0 hkHalf is not IEEE half precision: it stores the top 16 bits of a float32 (decode with float from bits(h << 16) ). Only a handful of entries are configured - they carry a maximum contact impulse of FLT MAX instead of the sentinel - and the number grows during play as surfaces register on demand: 13 and then 18 configured entries were seen in one world about an hour apart. Entries 0-7 are nearly uniform (friction 0.5, restitution 0, with one bouncier entry at 0.199 and one at friction 0.547 / restitution 0.05), so a handful of shared materials surfaces the whole world.

t: What is live, and what ships unused
x: A census of the live heap in a desert scene (169 live Havok classes; controls passing): Class Live --- --- hknpConvexPolytopeShape 6,673 hknpBoxShape 5,680 hknpCapsuleShape 3,062 hknpCompressedMeshShape (static world collision) 798 hknpTriangleShape 528 hknpCompoundShape 372 hknpSphereShape 264 hknpShapeMassProperties 7,009 hknpMaterial 1,024 hknpBodyQuality 32 hkpRagdollConstraintData 1,857 hkpLimitedHingeConstraintData 420 hkaiNavMeshInstance 464 hkaiNavMeshClearanceCache 5,300 hkaiPointCloudSilhouetteGenerator 3,124 hknpWorld 1 The default modifier set ( hknpDefaultModifierSet ) instantiates the six per-contact modifiers: trigger, mass changer, restitution, soft contact, surface velocity and animated-shape surface velocity. Shipped in the executable with their vtables but never instantiated: the complete Havok vehicle suite ( hknpVehicleInstance with its engine, transmission, steering, suspension, brake, aerodynamics, velocity damper, tyre marks and ray-cast wheels), Havok's demo guns ( hknpBallGun , hknpGravityGun , hknpProjectileGun , hknpMountedBallGun , hknpFirstPersonGun , hknpFirstPersonCharacter ), the spring / unary / binary actions, and the linear and circular surface velocity objects.

Havok allocates its whole heap in one call (0x11870E4); its size is the u32 at 0x262AC80. The world, both libraries, the material palette and the motion array all live in that single region, which is the largest single allocation in the process (512 MB with a raised setting).

t: Tagfiles: navigation meshes and collision shapes
x: Havok data ships as tagfiles (root hkRootLevelContainer ) that carry their own type table, so every class layout is read from the file itself. Every carrier parses exactly: 923 standalone .hkai files (185 types), 1,176 HKAI sections inside bundles, and 5,148 physics files in world-object entries plus 4,808 inside bundles (196 types). - Navigation meshes: hkaiNavMesh version 16 (208 bytes): faces, edges and vertices in world space (cm). worlds\retail\mtnpass\mtnpass.hkai (37.5 MB) holds 713 navigation meshes, all structurally exact; its main mesh has 205,467 vertices, 273,917 edges and 49,774 faces (3-14 edges each); every edge's opposite is symmetric (227,694 of 227,694). The smaller meshes are the dynamic navigation pieces of props ( Resou 09.W.dnmp , Store 34.NMPtop ). - Collision shapes: roots are hknpCompoundShape s holding hknpCompressedMeshShape , hknpConvexPolytopeShape (boxes and capsules), hknpSphereShape , hknpHeightFieldShape and hknpConvexShape , in meters; an instance places a shape as p' = R (p scale) + t .

What a character, a projectile or a sound does when it meets geometry is decided by the surface it touched: one of the 78 Surfaces/Surfaces records (type Surface.Surface ). Field Records with it set Read by --- --- --- CanSeeThrough 21 0x274AA0 (0x272E48 tests it before CanShootThrough ) CanShootThrough 26 0x405CC8 (four call sites) CanPlayerRangedTargetThrough 23 0x739490, which also requires CanShootThrough CanDoFootsteps 55 footstep code FootPrintFX / FootPrintLifetime 0x10FBA8, 0x2DA0F8 (the feet: 0x2DA16C, FrontRightFoot ...); a list of StructuresSurfaceFootstepData WeaponFX 59 link one 0x15B0DC; Surfaces/WeaponFX (13: default , Wood , Stone , Metal , Dirt , Water ...) OcclusionFactor 0x405A64, through the audio occlusion query 0x383104 CollisionProperty 41 link one 0x1B6D1D8; Collisions/CollisionProperty CanWallClimb 7 0x1C71B44 (six call sites, 0x123E24 and 0x371708 among them) IsSlippery 14 0x652048, after a world query in 0x6518E4 CanWargJump 60 0x1BE5ABC, in the warg's navigation jump test ( FoundNavMesh JumpUp , 0x449F90) IsFireProp 12 0x405B28 CanSpiderCrawl 73 nothing CanMeleeThrough 10 nothing FXContextList a string of effect contexts ( stone ...) Every field but two has an accessor read by game code; CanSpiderCrawl and CanMeleeThrough are registered in the schema and filled in the data, but no code reads them. The sets are telling: - wall-climbing is allowed only on Air , AxeClimb , Can Scramble , PlayerBlocker Dust and the three No WallRunPlusSlip surfaces; - the 14 slippery surfaces are the No WallRun family, the player blockers, Perimeter , Wood Tree and Slippery ; - the 12 fire props are the wood and cloth surfaces; - warg jumps are refused on 18 surfaces, among them the five Drake collision surfaces, which are also the only five that refuse spider crawling. Surface ids. Collision data does not name a surface by index but by a 16-bit id folded from the P919 hash of its record name: id = (h + (h 16)) & 0xFFFF (78 of 78 surfaces, no two sharing an id). A table of 16-byte entries {u16 id, ..., +0x08 the record} between [base+0x277C9E0] and [base+0x277C9E8] (78 entries, in the category's record order) maps an id back to its record: 0x2748F8 compares the id with the "no surface" value at 0x2A868F8 (0) and searches the table. A query result carries a surface reference {u16 id, u8 valid} , resolved by 0x2748E4 (null when the valid byte is 0). A world object can also carry its own surface: the u16 at +0xCE (0x274B5C; 0x274B68 returns the u32 at +0xCC , whose high half it is). In one loaded world 107 of 105,842 placed objects set it (106 metal cage , one water shallow ); every other object holds 0, no surface. Impacts and collision properties. Surfaces/Impacts has 65 records, one per material and size ( Small , Medium , Large , Ambient , Explosion , with OlogHai variants, Fist , Nazgul Projectile ); Surfaces/SurfaceFXType names the eight impact kinds. Collisions/CollisionProperty has 52 records, of which the surfaces use nine ( Wood 16 times, Metal 6, water 5, Cloth 4, Stone 3, Footstep 2, Sand 2, Flesh 2, Orc head 1); the table also carries props of a contemporary setting that nothing in this game's surfaces refers to ( Office Chair , Keyboard , ComputerCase , Radio , Deli SignChains , CeilingTile , Duct , PropaneTank ...).

- What registers a new material slot during play. - The meaning of the unnamed floats of a material ( +0x3C , +0x44 , +0x48 ) and of the solver values near the gravity vector. - How collision geometry carries a surface per triangle or per shape: the query result's {u16 id, u8 valid} reference is filled from somewhere in the collision data. - What CanWallClimb permits, given that it is set on the No WallRunPlusSlip surfaces and clear on WallRun .

t: Cloth: GPU cloth and Havok Cloth
x: The game ships two cloth systems. The engine's own GPU cloth simulates orc and olog gear, a few player and Eltariel bodies and cloaks, an Easterling cape, banners, flags, warg drool and a weapon's cloth in a compute shader, from <stem .gpucloth.cres files; Havok Cloth, carried inside skeleton files, drives the player's capes. A piece uses one or the other: none of the 132 skeleton sections that name a GPU cloth also carries Havok cloth.

A .cres file is a container of GPU buffers. One reader loads every kind (0x72E4A8, slot 3 of vt 0x230A868; resource type 12): u32 'CRES' u32 version (1 - 5) version = 3: u32 tag u32 tag version the pair must be one of the table below string: u16 length + bytes read and dropped (at most 259) version = 4: u32 n + n bytes the resource's own blob version = 3: u32 buffer count (else 1) per buffer u32 count u32 stride u32 format then count x stride bytes In version 5 the format word is the StringHash of a format name, looked up in a table the reader builds at 0x27AF880: Float32 , UInt32 , SInt32 , UInt16x2 , UInt8 , UInt8x4 , UNorm8 , UNorm8x4 , FloatR11G11B10 , Float16x2 , UNorm16x4 , Float16x4 , Float32x2 , Float32x4 (typed buffers, ids 0 - 13) and Structured (a structured buffer of the given stride). A name outside the table refuses the file. Version 2 - 4 store the id directly; version 1 stores only a byte size of 32-bit words. The reader also accepts a CRES wrapped in an SLVT version 4 envelope. The loaded object is 0x48 bytes (constructor 0x72EC50): the blob at +0x00, the buffer pointers at +0x10, their byte sizes at +0x28. Tag Tag version Shipped Buffers Files --- --- --- --- --- GPUC 2 240 in bundles + 12 loose 6 (below) + blob <stem .gpucloth.cres , the cloth file PRTS 4 1,322 + 41 4 structured (strides 16, 12, 8, 16) + blob <model ps.cres , prefab fp.cres LOCT 1 122 + 115 1 UInt32 <map .lsomap.cres and .env.cres (loader 0x1CBD2D8) SSTR 1 39 + 63 1 UInt32 + blob world layers' .osc .cres , named by an SSTFile property (loader 0x1B50440) HAIR 3 1 loose 1 structured (stride 76) materials\0dev\engine\hairlookup array.cres Every shipped CRES is version 5 with exactly the tag version in the table, and its name string is empty.
