t: AI: planning, perception, spawning and group combat
x: Every NPC runs one update per frame that selects a target, aims, moves and ticks a tree of planner steps whose priority order decides its behavior. NPCs enter the world as requests queued on the spawn manager, made by ambient spawners, scripts and summons, and resolved from a spawn channel to a template, a model and a character type.

t: The AI world and the NPC
x: The AI world is the object at [[base+0x26FFAB0]+0x778] (the MainScene's AI slot; its members and the order in which the scene tick runs them are in Engine core and Threads and the frame). Of the 24 non-null qwords in its first 0xC8 bytes, only the object at +0x98 begins with an image vtable: it is the engine thread object of class vt 0x22FF668, the AIThread . An AI character is an NPC (vt 0x1FB3640; the class descriptor gives 0x3180 bytes). Its AI components hang off the character: Offset Component --- --- +0x2128 the AI/CharacterTypes record (the brain lookup reads it) +0x2410 the alignment ( Character/Alignments , see Characters) +0x2BF8 u32 index into the sighting matrix +0x2C21 byte that suspends the plan (set while a queued teleport is pending; see Quests, story and scenes) +0x2C70 the target tracker +0x2CE8 the planner (below) +0x2CF0 the perception component (its +0x00 points back at the NPC) +0x2CF8 movement and path following +0x2D00 the service set +0x2D08 morale +0x2D18 alertness (0x190F7C returns its current AI/Alertness/Level ) +0x2D20 talk +0x2D28 the target selector (the perceiver; its current focus at +0xF0 ) +0x2D38 the plan tree (below) +0x2E71 AI-alive byte, cleared when the AI dies The update. The object update scheduler runs every NPC's Update every frame; there is no distance-based rate (Threads and the frame has the scheduler and the cost of each part). Inside the AI update vt 0x1FB3640::vf119 (0x2F79A4) the order is fixed by the call sites: target selection (vf113 - 0x11B230), aim and look-at (vf112 - 0x11AEB8), movement (0x2F5E6C), the plan tree tick (0x1919C8), collision avoidance, the service set (0x2FD960), morale, talk, awareness markers and, last, context actions and perception target overrides (tail 0x2F6420). Per NPC per frame the plan tree takes about 35% of the update and target selection about 26%; an NPC in Attack costs about 2.7 times an idle one.

The planner [npc+0x2CE8] is a 0xFF8-byte object with no vtable. The NPC class builds it in 0x49B858: 0x49CB20 allocates 0xFF8 bytes and runs the constructor 0x45F354, which builds seven 0x58-byte sub-objects at +0x118 .. +0x328 . The character's destructor 0x49CEC0 tears down +0x2CE8 , +0x2CE0 and +0x2CD8 in reverse order. In all, 779 functions load the pointer, among them the script natives NPC::Search and NPC::CircleMidPoint and the character methods vf19, vf54, vf75 and vf111. The planner holds no step. The code around it reads these members: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x430 when non-null, the target-select scan is skipped +0x440 the NPC's bitset of allowed target-select pickers +0x500 float, reset to 1.0 when a step ends +0x697 byte, cleared when a step ends +0x7A4 when set, the AI update first calls 0x2AD844 on the alertness object +0x7D0 read by the Flee step's update +0x7F8 an intrusive list of observer hooks from many objects +0x810 the current target the running steps validate against +0x910 despawn requested ( NPC::DespawnOffscreen 0x1A8BC08) +0xA60 non-null while the NPC is infighting ( NPC::IsInfighting 0x1A8D1B8) +0xB18 / +0xB1C / +0xB20 presentation state (0x190FF0 ORs the three)

A step type is a GameDB category under AI/Planner/Steps/ ; its records carry the tuning (for example FleeAmbush.TraitsRequired and FleeAmbush.SearchDistance ) and a C++ class implements it. AI/Planner has 69 categories: Context , Steps (the base), Trees and 66 step types: Animate, AssembleAtNode, Attack, AttackPreview, Attract, BaitAttract, BeckonWithTalk, CaptureBattleNode, CheerExitCombatSpaceSource, CircleAlly, CircleTarget, CombatRecoil, CombatState, CombatTaunt, CombatWeaponChange, Cower, DespawnOffscreen, ElevateTransientAlarm, ExitCombatSpace, Fall, FindAlertnessSource, FindPreceivedOpponent, Flee, FleeAmbush, FollowLeader, FollowRoute, FollowWaitForBand, GiveUpOnPlayer, GoTo, GoToAndMount, GoToCircleAlly, GoToPreferredAttackPosition, GoToRallyPoint, Idle, Investigate, Investigating, LeadPlayer, LeaveObstacle, MenaceTask, Mounted, MoveTowardSpawner, NodeAnimate, Patrol, PerformSyncAction, PresentationIdle, Priority, ReactToAlertnessChange, ReactToAreaAlarmLevelChange, ReactToDeadBodyInvestigation, ReactToGlimpsed, ReactToKnownDeadBody, ReactToMoraleModifier, Retreat, RetreatIdle, RetreatToDistance, ReturnToBandLeader, ReturnToBattleNode, ReturnToConfinementNode, ReturnToPursuitConstraint, TauntOpponentNonAttackable, TraitCatalystReaction, UseAttackNode, UseFixedArcherNode, UseWorkNode, WargChaseTarget, WargCircleTarget. AI/Planner/Trees has 8 records: BasicEnemy , BasicEnemy Archer , Goblin , Idle , Prisoner , Spider , Troll and Warg . Every tree but Idle lists ForcedAttack first and then, in this order, PerformSyncAction , Fall , CombatRecoil , CombatState , Animate , Mounted , NodeAnimate and PresentationIdle before its own entries; BasicEnemy inserts Attack HighPriority right after ForcedAttack . Idle 's only step is Idle .

A step's GameDB record type selects its C++ class. The table combines classes read from live plan stacks (the vtable at step+0 against the category of the record at step+0x10 , which paired one to one in 12 of 12 cases) with classes named by the categories their own methods read: Step Class --- --- Attack vt 0x1FBD028 BaitAttract vt 0x1DCAE08 CheerExitCombatSpaceSource vt 0x1DC62B8 CircleTarget vt 0x1DC60E8 CombatRecoil vt 0x1DC6420 Cower vt 0x1FBCF08 DespawnOffscreen vt 0x1FBCE78 FindAlertnessSource vt 0x1FBCDE8 FindPreceivedOpponent vt 0x1FBCD58 Flee vt 0x1DC5010 FleeAmbush vt 0x1FBCCC8 FollowLeader vt 0x1DAA638 (in 121 of 121 trees' step lists) FollowRoute vt 0x1DB0C98 GiveUpOnPlayer vt 0x1DB0D38 GoToPreferredAttackPosition vt 0x1FBCB00 Idle vt 0x1DB57B0 Investigate vt 0x1DC4ED0 Investigating vt 0x1DB55F0 MenaceTask vt 0x1DC5F50 Mounted vt 0x1DC6BB0 Priority vt 0x1FBC5E8 ReactToAlertnessChange vt 0x1DB5720 ReactToAreaAlarmLevelChange vt 0x1DB5520 RetreatIdle vt 0x1FBC8C0 ReturnToBandLeader vt 0x1DC6540 UseFixedArcherNode vt 0x1DC4F80 UseWorkNode vt 0x1DC51E0 WargChaseTarget vt 0x1DCB0D8 Every step derives from vt 0x1FBD1D8; the steps that issue a move request (Flee, FleeAmbush, DespawnOffscreen) share the bases vt 0x1DAA7E8, vt 0x1DB5500 and vt 0x1DB1050. MenaceTask reads AI/SmartObjects fields, and the class vt 0x1FBAC38 that reads FollowLeader fields is not the step's class. A step object holds +0x08 the NPC, +0x10 its definition record ( AI/Planner/Steps/<Type ; the field accessors take it) and +0x19 a byte that vf1 reports. A Flee step is 0x5F0 bytes.

The interface is read from Flee (vt 0x1DC5010) and FleeAmbush (vt 0x1FBCCC8), and from the tree code that calls the slots: Slot Role --- --- vf0 scalar deleting destructor (Flee 0x72A3AC: destructor 0x72A3E0, then the sized delete 0x8C4370 with 0x5F0) vf1 writes 2 bytes: a class constant (Flee 1, FleeAmbush 0) and this+0x19 ; every step class's vf1 lies in 0x780680-0x780710 vf3 PREPARE(context), called on each candidate right before vf5 at selection vf4 RELEASE, after a rejected vf5 and after vf10 when the step leaves the stack vf5 EVALUATE(context, &out) at selection: 0 = take this step, non-zero = reject. Flee returns 2 when NPC::IsFleeing is false; FleeAmbush also needs the player's bodyguard and its record's TraitsRequired and SearchDistance vf7 called on the finished step during unwind; a non-null result is copied into the parent's context vf8 return true in both classes read (0x4E7DD0 / 0x7F7DE0) vf9 UPDATE(forced, context = tree+0x48 , &out), every tick: 0 = keep running, 1 or 2 = finished. Flee and FleeAmbush return 2 when [planner+0x810] no longer equals the target they stored ( this+0x5E0 / this+0x430 ) vf10 END(reason): 1 when the step finished with status 1, otherwise 2. Flee cancels its move request (0x44344C), stops fleeing (0x359988), clears planner+0x697 and sets planner+0x500 to 1.0 vf11 EVENT(message): 0x3F5B38 sends a message to every active step (from character vf19) vf12 / vf13 CHILD FINISHED, on the parent: vf13 when the child returned 1, vf12 when it returned 2; a non-zero return ends the parent too (0x3763A8) vf14 called on every active step by 0x3F566C (from 0x4428B0, which also reads AI/Count/Configuration.RunSimulation ) vf15 STILL VALID(context): 0x3F5AD0 (from character vf53) unwinds the stack from the first step answering false vf16 debug description ("Approaching", "<not active ") vf17 debug filter match (0x1B04B68, only while the byte 0x2A361F1 is set; filters at 0x2A361F8 / 0x2A36200) A step's preconditions are code in vf5 and vf9 and its tuning is its record, so whether an NPC flees is decided by NPC::IsFleeing and the record's gates, not by the Flee step's existence. The planner's debug output is compiled in but never switched on. The switch 0x2A361F1 is read by seven instructions (0x191030, vt 0x1DB55F0 vf5, vt 0x1FBC5E8 vf5 and vf6) and written by none. It lies in zero-initialized memory, so it stays 0 in a normal run. The two filters are string objects created at start-up (0xC16F0, 0xC1780) that the vf17 match 0x1B04B68 compares with an object's name.

The plan tree is built once, at character set-up, from the NPC's AI/CharacterTypes.PlanTree record (accessor 0x7279C0): vt 0x1FB3640::vf12 0x3FA718 - 0x45AFDC - 0x6FC774 - 0x6FC7B8 - ... - the step factory 0x45CEE8 (2,800 bytes). The factory reads the step record's category ( [record+0x18] ), compares it with a table of cached category pointers at 0x2A359D8 + n x 0x18 and jumps to that type's creator (Flee 0x6E71D8 - constructor 0x6E7288, FleeAmbush 0x6EB52C - 0x6EB5DC, Cower 0x1ADD54C - 0x1B02E84; each creator is called only from the factory). All 64 branches resolve to a category and a class vtable. The factory recurses (0x45CEE8 - 0x45C724 - 0x45CEB0 - 0x45CEE8), so composite steps build their children. 0x45AFDC stores the result at [npc+0x2D38] by move-assignment (0x75F2DC); the old tree is freed by 0x3EB630. The services are built from the type's AI/CharacterTypes.ServiceSet records by the loop 0x45B1B8, which calls 0x45B290 with [npc+0x2D00] and each record. If the character type has no PlanTree , the brain lookup returns null and the creator frees the new object (see Spawning below).

[npc+0x2D38] is a unique pointer to the plan tree: Offset Holds --- --- +0x00 the AI/Planner/Trees record +0x08 the NPC +0x10 the root step ( AttackPreview record ForcedAttack ) +0x18 / +0x20 the active stack , 0x18-byte entries {u8 ticks, u32 status @+4, u64 @+8, step @+0x10} , root first, the running leaf last +0x30 / +0x38 every top-level step, 0x10-byte pairs {step , u8 forced ok @+8, u8 presentation ok @+9} , in the order selection tries them +0x48 the context passed to step slots +0x50 / +0x51 / +0x52 replan request / presentation latch / reset request A live read of 115 NPCs found a tree on every one: BasicEnemy 92 (53 steps in the list), BasicEnemy Archer 20 (49 steps), Warg 2, Troll 1. A typical stack is Priority:Passive - FollowRoute:FollowRoute or a single Idle . The leaves in that read were Idle 57, FollowRoute 25, Attack 13, CircleTarget 5, CombatRecoil 4, Mounted 4, UseWorkNode (record UseMenaceNode ) 3, and one each of FindPreceivedOpponent, ReactToAlertnessChange, GoToPreferredAttackPosition and Flee. Child steps appear only on active stacks; the +0x30 list holds the top-level priority entries.

0x1919C8(tree, forced) is called by the AI update (vf119, forced = 0, skipped while 0x11548E0(npc) holds, that is, while npc+0x2C21 is set) and by 0x2FD850 (forced = 1, which checks the same byte). 0x2FD850 is reached from the batch 0xF41E30 right after Quest AI REPLAN Requesting replan... , so a replan that a quest requests ticks at once. 1. Reset. With +0x52 set, 0x3EB9C4 ends every active step (vf10) and clears the stack. 2. Presentation. The planner's presentation state (0x190FF0) is latched in +0x51 . On its rising edge 0x4E7E04 ("presentation started") unwinds the plan, so a scene pre-empts anything the NPC was doing. 3. Select 0x191030 runs when +0x50 is set and the character's vf113(1) is true, or when the stack is empty (through 0x3F65F4). It walks +0x30 in order, skips the running step and every pair not allowed now (0x191374: a forced tick needs byte +8 , a presentation byte +9 ), and calls vf3 then vf5; the first step whose vf5 returns 0 is pushed . List order is priority order. 4. Update 0x191ADC gives vf9 to each stack entry with ticks != 0 and status 0. A non-zero result either parks in the entry (when a deeper entry follows) or finishes the top step. 5. Unwind 0x376E28 / 0x3763A8 gives the finished step vf10(reason) and vf4 and pops it. Its parent gets vf13 or vf12 with the child's status and ends too when that call returns non-zero. The pair bytes and the list order are per-NPC heap state rebuilt with the tree, so a change to them lasts until the NPC's tree is rebuilt. A step's record is read by vf5 and vf9 each time they run. In play the tick takes 33-38% of the NPC update, 0.50-0.73 ms per frame for 121-159 NPCs, of which selection takes 4-5% and the running steps 29-33%. The heaviest running steps are Attack (its attack picking 0x4612D8 over the combat tree's nodes and pools, 7-15%), FollowLeader (3-9%, band movement 0xF498C0), CircleTarget and FollowRoute.

During a fight against the player (73.5 s of world time, 1,215 samples, up to 17 NPCs engaged, one fight circle), the NPCs whose leaf step was Attack numbered 0 in 65 of 122 timeline samples, 1 in 32 and 2 in 25, and never 3 or more. A typical snapshot had 10-12 in CircleTarget and 1-2 in Attack . The leaf transitions were CircleTarget - Attack 30, Attack - CircleTarget 25, GoToPreferredAttackPosition - CircleTarget 25, CircleTarget - CombatRecoil 19, CircleTarget - GoToPreferredAttackPosition 17 and CombatRecoil - CircleTarget 16. The CircleTarget / Attack alternation is the fight circle handing out attack turns; the circle itself is in Combat.

The first call in the AI update, vf113(5) - 0x11B230, picks the NPC's target: 1. Threat. The target selector [npc+0x2D28] (0x11BCC8 - 0x11C9AC) scores candidates in 0x2FA99C from AI/CombatThreat (43 records, one per kind, among them Infantry Orc , Archer Orc , Troll Cave , Balrog , Player and Nazgul ), using CombatThreatTargetWeight , DefaultInitialDetection , DefaultMax , DistanceInfluence , CombatThreatAttenuationRange , ally and opponent proximity influences and distances, CombatThreatInitialValues and CombatThreatThreshold , plus the fight circle's RingSettings.TargetWeightAdjustment . A character type names its picker in AI/CharacterTypes.CombatThreatPicker . 2. Target selects. A tail jump reaches the target tracker 0x11B258 ( [npc+0x2C70] ; "Target just changed", "Selecting %s against %s") - 0x11BE00 - 0x11BF60 , the scan of the target pickers. The pickers live in a table at [base+0x26FFCC0] , whose +0x00 holds the u32 count (27) and +0x10 an array of picker pointers (0x11C018 returns entry i). 0x11BF60 returns at once when planner+0x430 is set or the bitset planner+0x440 is empty. Otherwise it walks the table in order: it skips every picker whose key ( picker+0x08 ) is not in the NPC's bitset, returns the current one if it is reached, and otherwise calls the picker's vf3 and returns the first that passes. AI/TargetSelects has 27 records whose Class field names 22 classes, with four records sharing AlertnessSource and three sharing Disturbance . The 27 table objects have the same shape: 22 classes in the vtable range 0x22FF778 - 0x22FFD18, with vt 0x22FF778 four times and vt 0x22FF9B8 three times. Record Class Cost --- --- --- Mounted Mounted 0 Fleeing Fleeing 0.4 BuddyCommand BuddyCommand 0.9 BaitAttract , PresentationIdle same 1.0 AnimateTask , CombatScripted same 1.5 AlertnessSourceWhileSurprised AlertnessSource 1.9 CombatThreat CombatThreat 2.0 GoToAndMount GoToAndMount 3.0 OpponentNonAttackable OpponentNonAttackable 3.5 OpponentDamage Disturbance 3.9 OpponentPerceived OpponentPerceived 4.0 OpponentDisturbance Disturbance 5.0 ScriptedSearch ScriptedSearch 6.75 Disturbance Disturbance 7.0 CircleAlly , AlertnessSourceFromAlert , AlertnessSourceFromAlert Monster , AlertnessSourceWhileAlert CircleAlly / AlertnessSource 8.0 Talk Talk 8.5 LeadPlayer LeadPlayer 8.9 Ally , ExitCombatSpaceSource same 9.0 OpponentGlimpsed , KnownDeadBody same 10.0 WaitForBandMember WaitForBandMember 11.0 The other fields are Delay and ChainDelay (pool ranges), MaxChainDelayCount , UseSuperJumpAgainstPlayer , UsePursuitConstraint , Stimulus ( CombatThreat and CombatScripted list FactionThreatSound , AlertLookoutSound , AttackingTarget , BandMateThreatSound , AlertLookoutVisible ) and Validation (for example Surprised , Alert , LostPlayerFromAlert and OpponentDamage ). A character type chooses its set in AI/CharacterTypes.TargetSelectSet (for example Default or Default Monster ). An AI's target comes from this pass, not from its attacks: AttackData.Target is null on all 34 Balrog and AI-Talion attacks sampled. NPC::SetCombatScriptedTarget 0x1A8DC60 refuses a dead NPC and hands a script's target to the target selector [npc+0x2D28] (0x44C644) and then the planner.

AI/CharacterTypes (81 records, 62 fields) gathers everything above for one kind of AI. Troll Cave , for example, sets PlanTree Troll , TargetSelectSet Default Monster , Alignment Troll Cave , PlayerFollowerAlignment PlayerFollower Beast , BrandedAlignment / ActivatedBrandAlignment WraithInfight Beast , SensorSet Trolls , ServiceSet Troll , AlertnessProfile Troll , Perception CaveTroll , PerceptionTarget Trolls , CombatThreatPicker Troll Cave , CharacterVisibleStimulus TrollVisible , CharacterAudibleStimulus CharacterAudibleLoud , SenseUpdateRate 0.1, GiveUpOnPlayerData Troll , ActAsFactionMember False, CanRetreat False, plus movement (rotation times, stopping distances, WalkRunRange ), collision avoidance and mounted-collision shape fields.

AI/Perception/Types (240 records) is compiled once, at start-up, into a table of the AI system [base+0x26FFBF8] , with the rows at +0x300 and the u32 count at +0x308 (240, all AI/Perception/Types ). Each row is 0x58 bytes: Row offset Value (from the record) --- --- +0x00 the record +0x10 PerceiveRadius +0x14 RecognizeRadius +0x18 SurpriseRadius +0x1C PerceiveDelay +0x20 RecognizeDelay +0x34 cos( FOVHorizontal ) +0x38 sin( FOVVertical ) +0x3C NoFOVRadius +0x48 HearDistance +0x54 HearDelay The FOV fields are half-angles in degrees: Alertness Spider Drone 70 / 25 is stored as 0.342 / 0.423, and Biped AlertSuspicious TargetKnown Trolls 120 / 60 as -0.5 / 0.866. The radii and delays in the rows equal the records' values (3 records checked field by field). The table survives loading screens. Each AI then copies its own values. The perception refresh 0x499724 (component = [npc+0x2CF0] ) reads the current alertness level ( UseSneakingPerceptionDistanceFactor ), the faction row's PerceptionOverride , AI/Perception.DefaultPerceptionList , the weather modifier ( AI/Perception/PerceptionWeatherMod.WeatherModifier ), AdditionalSensorSet , SimulatedRecognizeEnemyDistance (stored at +0x1A8 ) and PerceptionOverrides , and fills the component's two perception copies ( +0xC8 , +0x118 ). It is the only caller of the AI/Perception/Duration slot helpers. Record edits are not seen. A write to AI/Perception/Types changes nothing in play (scaling every record by 0.5 left three AIs' copies unchanged): the radii, angles and delays an AI uses come from the start-up table through 0x499724.

A character type's SensorSet (13 records in AI/SensorSets ) composes observers and interpreters , with includes. BasicObservers holds BandMate, Audible, SuspectsTarget, NearBandLeader, MountedCharacter, RecognizeRange, FOV, CloseTarget, Obscured and SightRange, and BipedObservers adds Gathering and HiddenCharacter. Default (bipeds) interprets Attract, EnemyDelayedDisturbance, MoraleVictimAudible, FactionDisturbance, MoraleAudible, Distract, FactionDamaged, FactionThreat, EnemyDisturbance and BrandedDefendPlayer, and Monsters adds BaitAttract. Wargs , Trolls and Balrog add their own hidden-character observers. Characters emit stimuli named by their type ( CharacterVisibleStimulus , CharacterAudibleStimulus , CharacterSneakingAudibleStimulus , AssaultCharacterVisibleStimulus ). The player's emitters are built from AI/CharacterTypes by 0x440F80, whose only caller is the player's stimulus update 0x7AA29C (player vtable slot 59). Sight sits at player+0x2190 and sound at player+0x21B8 , each with the live emitter at +0x20 .

[base+0x26FFC48] (also the AI world's +0x50 ) is a 4.6 MB block of 256 perceiver blocks of 0x4808 bytes: +0x00 the owning character, then 256 facts of 0x48 bytes. The fact a perceiver holds about character c is at block + 8 + idx 0x48 , where idx = u32 c+0x2BF8 (below 256; the player is 0). In one read, 116 of the 256 blocks had an owner. Fact offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 the target +0x3C float +0x40 awareness; 4 = engaged, which raises threat ( BlockInitialThreatAgainstTarget ) +0x41 relationship, written once when the fact is created (0x222A44 <- 0x122340); 3 = hostile +0x42 byte NPC::CreateCharacterFact 0x1A8B9B4 - 0x6063E4 creates facts.

Forget 0x6C79D8( , character, filter) visits every perceiver block whose fact about character has relationship 3: 0x2E6EE4 makes the perceiver ( [owner+0x2D28] ) drop the character as its focus ( +0xF0 ; 0x2E6EB0 - 0x11C9AC), queues the player's combat object at [base+0x26FFB70]+0x1050 (0x442F84), and 0x2229C0 resets the fact (target 0, relationship 2). It wipes every hostile AI's knowledge of the character however it was gained, by sight, sound or a hit. Its callers are the player's stimulus update, Combat/Buffs.ClearNPCAwareness (0x452ED8), ClearAIDetectionBrush volumes (0x2B3B74) and the attack path 0x4CDE54. AI-spectator invisibility. CPlayerObj::SetAISpectatorInvisible (player, bool) 0x19BF378 writes the byte player+0x2F10 and runs the stimulus update 0x7AA29C. While the byte is set (or the spectator state 0x171A78 holds), the update releases both emitters (0x4410E0), runs the forget path and zeroes the player combat object's +0x596 ; otherwise it rebuilds the emitters from the character type. Since 0x440F80 has no other caller, nothing is emitted while the byte is set, regardless of the GameDB. The byte is written only by the setter and the constructor (0x19B8D8C, 0). Its engine users are SetHidden (player vf32 0x19BF91C, which also sets SetSpectatorInvisible at +0x3882 ), hiding places (0x1A001E0) and the script binding CPlayerObj.SetAISpectatorInvisible (0x1BA7D48, unused by the shipped scripts). The engine clears the byte after those uses, and a save load builds a fresh player object.

An NPC's alertness object ( [npc+0x2D18] ) moves between the 11 AI/Alertness/Level records: Inactive , ActiveBuddy , Surprised , Alert , BaseHighAlarm , AcquiringTarget , TargetDead , LostPlayer , Suspicious , BaseLowAlarm , Cower . A level sets BehaviorEditValue (Inactive 0, Suspicious 0.33, Surprised 0.67, Alert 1.0), UseSneakingPerceptionDistanceFactor (read by the perception refresh), CombatReady , PreserveCharacterFacts , DismissDisturbancesImmediately , map rendering and AllowRestrictedNodes . A character type's AlertnessProfile (16 records, among them Default , DefaultMonster , AlwaysAlert , Coward , Troll , Warg and FortAssault ) sets the default, simulated, inactive and exit-forced levels, the awareness icons and the ranges. The AI world's alarm system ( +0x38 ) is ticked by 0x607838 as the transient alarms. Area alarm levels are AI/SpawnAmbient/AlarmLevels : Empty , Low , High , HighWave2 and HighWave3 , with IsElevated true for the three high ones. On the NPC side there is an AreaAlarm service (every 0.5 s) and the steps ElevateTransientAlarm and ReactToAreaAlarmLevelChange .

t: Sides: alignments, the relation table and teams
x: The relation table. [base+0x2A868C0] points to a static object at 0x27977F0, which holds at +0x00 the u32 N, the number of Character/Alignments records (52), and at +0x08 a pointer to the N x N byte matrix. It is built once by 0x1C03908, entered only by a tail call from 0x1C03BD0 (which stores the pointer, the one write among its 34 references), whose one caller 0x1B07200 sits in the AI stimulus module. For each alignment record i the builder walks its Alignment rows, each a StructuresRelationship { Stance , turned into a byte by 0x1A98488; Others }, and writes matrix[i N + RecordIndexOf(other)] = stance only while the cell is still 0, so the first row that names a pair wins. Because the table is compiled, a later edit of an alignment record reaches nothing. On the diagonal, 27 sides are friendly to themselves, 5 neutral ( Grabbed , Orc Prisoner , Branded , Explosion DamageAll , Aligned DamageAll ), 4 hostile ( Troll Cave , Poison Barrel Infight , Trait Unstable Follower , Trait Unstable Sauron ) and 16 unset (0, read as 2 by the hit gate). The lookup 0x18BC88(table, row, column) returns the first non-zero cell over the two characters' slot ids (the asking side's ids outer), 2 when all are 0 and 0 when either has no side. The hit dispatcher's friendly-fire gate drops a hit when it returns 1 (see Combat, "Health and damage"). The same object holds, inline at +0x818 , a 256 x 256 byte cache of relations between live characters, indexed by their sighting slot char+0x2BF8 (in a live read, follower to enemy was 3 on 40 of 40 cells and follower to follower 1 on 380 of 380), and a 65,536-bit override set at +0x10818 . The cache follows a side change in the same step (a read every second showed the new values at once and the old ones again after a reset). 0x1C03BDC( , a, b) forces one cell to 3 and sets its override bit. Its one caller is the threat module 0x605D98 ( CCharacter::ApplyThreatRecord 0x19B3280, with a Combat/Threat record, a target and a float scale). Ready-made teams. The fight pits' Duelist A , B and C are friendly to themselves, hostile to the other two both ways and neutral to Spectator . Player , PlayerFollower and Orc FactionA read the Duelists as 0 or 2, and the Duelist rows name neither Talion nor any army. Trait Unstable Follower is hostile to itself, the three Duelists, Spectator , Orc FactionA , PlayerFollower and other sides, and friendly to Player . Poison Barrel Infight (the free-for-all of the poisoned grog) and Trait Unstable Sauron are hostile to Player . Every shipped five-side clique of mutually hostile, self-friendly sides contains Player or a follower side. A character's side: two stacks. An NPC (vt 0x1FB3640) keeps a requested stack at char+0x2EC0 and the effective one at char+0x23E0 , both laid out as 7 record pointers ( +0x00 .. +0x30 ) and 7 u32 record indices ( +0x38 .. +0x50 ). 0x18BF0C(stack, slot, record) writes both halves. Slot 6 holds the base side, slot 4 a script override, slot 3 the Unstable trait's side and slot 2 Hatred (both put there mid-fight by trait catalysts; the refresh's callers include the catalyst 0x40D3C4). Slot 0 is the engine's: the NPC update vf119 0x2F79A4 clears it (and may refill it from planner+0xA00 ) when 0x115471C and 0x1A8D1A0 pass. Lower slots sit above higher ones: in a pit fight a trait side in slot 3 above the pit's side in slot 4 turned a captain on his own team until the trait's side left. - NPC::SetAlignment 0x7D2ED4 consists of the script-context check (0x503EF8), a dead test, 0x18BF0C( npc+0x2EC0 , 4, record) and 0x440B24(npc, 0). NPC::ResetAlignment 0x7D722C does the same with null. Because of the script-context check, the call works only inside an engine-dispatched script handler (see Scripting). - The refresh 0x440B24(npc, force) has 18 call sites. Unforced, it skips while the current attack's StructuresCombatAIData.AllowAlignmentChange is false, so a request can wait in the requested stack until the next caller. Its source is npc+0x2EC0 , or for a ridden mount the rider's effective copy plus Combat/MountData.MountedAlignment in slot 0. 0x440F28 copies it into +0x23E0 , the notifiers 0x440F08, 0x440EE4 and 0x440CAC run, the planner's +0xA08 / +0xAF0 are cleared, and the same follows for the mount. A reset sent during an attack therefore lands in the requested stack only, and the effective one keeps the old side until a later refresh. - In a live read, 6 of 6 unridden NPCs held requested == effective, with the base side in slot 6, and 2 of 2 ridden beasts took their rider's side ( PlayerFollower Beast - PlayerFollower ). Two wild wargs carried Aligned AllFriendly in slot 4 outside any script fight, so slot 4 has other writers. - On Talion char+0x2EC0 is something else (the parked inventory while he plays as an orc; see Fight pits below), and his planner pointer is a self-pointing container head: the side setters are NPC-only. - Fall-through. An override row answers only for the sides it names: the Duelist rows name no Talion and no army, so an enemy captain on Duelist B still resolves Orc FactionA - Player = 3 against Talion, and a follower on a Duelist side resolves PlayerFollower - Orc FactionA = 3 against bystanders. Making two sides fight. Putting characters on hostile sides through slot 4 and refreshing does not start a fight by itself: friendly NPCs keep no sighting facts about each other, so there is nothing to act on. The pit script's sequence does start one: the side, a senses cycle and a scripted target. NPC::SetSenses 0x35D6D4(npc, bool) consists of a dead test, the byte +0x2DD5 and 0x35D6F8. That function combines +0x2DD5 .. +0x2DD7 into +0x2DD4 , flags the perceiver's entry idx 0x38 + 0xB in the table [base+0x26FFBE0] and, when switching off, runs 0x686B94 (the target dropped through [npc+0x2D18] , the stimulus list [npc+0x2CE0]+0xD8 and the perception block reset). NPC::SetCombatScriptedTarget 0x1A8DC60(npc, target, 0) consists of a dead test, the target's combat object 0x11B680, either a request 0xF41250(npc, owner, 2) or the selector 0x44C644( [npc+0x2D28] , combat object), and then the planner 0x1AA1714. It creates sighting facts along the targets at once (awareness 4, relationship 3), and NPC::ClearCombatScriptedTarget 0x1A8B640 undoes it. Three enemy grunts put on Duelist A (two) and Duelist B (one) this way fought each other within 6 s. CCharacter::SetMinHealthPct 0x19B7294 (not script-only) sets char+0x2500 = pct x the maximum health [combat+0x428] , a floor in health points (1.0 means no damage).

The service set [npc+0x2D00] is a list of 0x18-byte entries {service, f64 due time} ; 0x2FD960 runs a service's vf4 only when the world time passes its due time, so services are time-sliced while the rest of the update runs every frame. AI/Services (20 records) gives each its class and interval in seconds: Service Interval Simulated interval --- --- --- HeadTracking 0 - ManageCharacterFacts , Riding 0.1 - MonitorCharacter 0.25 - AreaAlarm , AlertnessManager , LeaderBrand , GiveUpOnPlayer 0.5 - AttackStructures 0.75 1.0 Gather , Patrol , MoveTowardSpawner , SpawnPersonnelWaves , Pulse , WargCloseQuarters 1.0 - VerifyTasks , FixedArcher 1.0 3.0 WargCanChaseTarget 1.5 - TraitTracker , TraitTrackerCloseRange 5.0 -

The spawn manager [base+0x26FFBE8] (also the AI world's +0x30 ) is null at the main menu. Engine core gives its role as the in-world test and its entry layout; the table gives the rest of the object: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x60 / +0x68 the character array: 0x40-byte entries, the character at +0x20 , the AI/SpawnAmbient/Removal record at +0x28 for ambient-owned characters +0x78 / +0x80 / +0x88 the per-template override table, its count and the AI/Templates category (see Resource streaming) +0x98 the request list : an intrusive list with a sentinel at +0x98 (empty = it points at itself) +0x168 / +0x170 / +0x178 / +0x17C a second roster of ambient characters : a vector (data, end, u32 capacity, owns-buffer byte) of 0x28-byte entries, a polymorphic object at +0x00 and the character at +0x20 +0x180 the ambient budget: a copy of the active AI/Count/Configuration.MaxAmbientAI (0x5C133C) +0x18C the cursor of a sliced pass over the container at +0x48 / +0x50 : 0x2735EC resumes from it and resets it to 0 once it passes the container's count +0x190 the number of ambient-owned characters (entries with a Removal record) +0x194 byte set by AISpawnManager:Enable (0x1B81FB4) +0x1D0 a block holding 200 AI slots of 0x148 bytes from +0x98 +0x1E0 the counter behind the names noname<N given to characters spawned without a name (0x3FA718 formats the name, then adds 1) The second roster's members stay in the ambient count +0x190 but are left out of the living-AI count: 0x1A93278 (used by ForceAISpots ) counts the living entries of the global AI list that it does not find there. RemoveAllAmbientAI (0x1A92D54) despawns the main array's characters first (character slot 26), then pops this roster from the back and despawns each entry's character the same way. 0x4A2D84 erases a given character's entry (called from character slot 17), and 0x4A2DC4 finds the character there and lowers +0x190 by one (called from character slot 128 and from 0x360988). A spawn (0x1A932F8, which logs Spawned AI %s from Spawner %s ) appends to the main array and raises +0x190 . The roster was empty (begin equal to end) in every one of 219 reads through a same-region fast travel and the 20 s after it. The first qword of its buffer then read vt 0x1DAAA20, a base vtable that 1,309 constructors and destructors write, which is what an element's destructor leaves behind. The same fast travel tore the ambient population down and rebuilt it: +0x190 fell to 0 and rose to 7 within 20 s of arrival, although the region did not change. When 0x5C133C copies MaxAmbientAI it also walks the 200 slots and opens the first MaxAmbientAI of them (slot byte +0xE8 cleared), closing the rest, so a budget above 200 opens no more slots. Dead characters leave the array (0 corpses among 107 entries with a fresh corpse at the player's feet), so its length counts the living. The AI list [base+0x2728ED0] .. [base+0x2728ED8] (begin, end) keeps dead AIs too (60 of 111 entries in one read). The manager is reallocated during travel. Its destructor 0x1A90C60 clears the global and deletes every queued request, so a fast travel discards pending spawns. The script interface AISpawnManager offers Enable 0x1B81FB4, Disable 0x1B819D4, RemoveAllAmbientAI 0x1BA2AB8, ForceAISpawnerSet 0x1B830A8, AddScenarioOverrideRecord 0x7B91DC, SummonGrunts 0x1BB138C and SummonNPCs 0x1BB1468. The same table (registered by 0x1B91DC8, twelve functions) also holds ForceAISpots 0x7B9264, CalcNumFactionMembersForHijackRecord 0x1B76B58, AddScenarioOverrideRecordPersistent 0xF77760, RemoveScenarioOverrideRecord 0x1BA317C and Debug ResetScenarioMgr 0x1B812F0. AISpawnerAmbientSet registers 44 functions (0x1B928EC: enable, restock, replenish, scenario, distance, predicate, removal and node-tag accessors, Create , Cast , Serialize ), and DifficultyMgr five (0x1B96668): SetScriptDifficultyRange 0x1BAE47C, LockAITemplate 0x1B8D93C, UnlockAITemplate 0x1BB2188, ClearLockedAITemplates 0x1B7C2D8 and GetSpawnLimit 0x1B89BD8.

Live census. In one loaded desert world, walking the world contexts' object tables found 5,002 AISpawnerAmbientNormal objects (vt 0x1DC5800), packed at a stride of 0x1D0 (4,556 of the neighbor gaps). Their channels ( +0x1C0 ) include Owner DifficultyMelee 915, Owner Infantry 779, Goblin Difficulty 480, Owner Warg 475, Owner DifficultyAny 378, Spider AI 286 and 233 Enemy . On 400 of them +0x158 held an AI/SpawnAmbient/Areas record (400), +0x160 an AI/SpawnAmbient/AlarmAreas record (387), +0x170 an AutoNodeTag (4), +0x178 / +0x190 the FortAssault/Side / StageList records (5) and +0x198 an Inventory/Transform (30). The placed spawners (see World for their placement and counts) are classes derived from AISpawnerAmbientBase (0x1C0 bytes): Class Size Constructor --- --- --- AISpawnerAmbientNormal 0x1C8 0x48CE4A0 AISpawnerAmbientLocation 0x1C8 0x1AC393C AISpawnerAmbientSocial 0x1C8 0x1AC1374 AISpawnerAmbientHijack 0x1C8 0x1AC3028 AISpawnerAmbientQuestPreset 0x1C8 0x1AC1CF4 AISpawnerAmbientRow 0x1D0 0x1AC195C AISpawnerAmbientQuestJobNormal 0x1D0 0x48CC5D0 AISpawnerAmbientQuestJob 0x1D8 0x6F1718 AISpawnerAmbientGangSimEvent 0x1E0 0x1AC4774 AISpawnerAmbientNemesis 0x1E8 0x6F008E0 AISpawnerAmbientSimEvent 0x1F0 0x6EFD590 AISpawnerAmbientBodyGuard 0x200 0x48CD3C0 AISpawnerAmbientGangMember 0x208 0x1AC50C8 Two set classes derive from GameBase instead: AISpawnerAmbientSet (0x300 bytes, constructor 0x1AB9C38) and AISpawnerVignetteSet (0x338, derived from the set). The set's script interface includes SetAIToSpawn (0x5EB1F8). AISpawnCloset (0x250 bytes, GameBase , constructor 0x1AB5E68) objects are updated by the object scheduler (80 on its due lists in a loaded region); three channels are named for closets ( Owner Closet Gang , Owner Closet GangSmall , Owner Closet GangNoArcher ) and AI/Constants.SpawnClosetIdle is Bip SpCloset Idle . ScenarioOverrideVolume objects (0x160 bytes, 16 on the due lists) also update there. When a spawner may spawn. The base check vt 0x1DC5988::vf38 0x16588C refuses, in this order, when: - there is no player object; - the flag +0x1B2 is set ("Waiting to snap to nav-mesh"); - the evaluations have not passed ( +0x1B1 clear; the message reports +0x1AF as "updating" and +0x1B8 as "checked"); - a spawn predicate fails (0x165B68, below); - the spawner is full. The count check uses signed bytes: MaxSpawn at +0x1AD (0 = no limit) and CurSpawned at +0x1AE , refusing when CurSpawned = MaxSpawn (the message's arguments fix which byte is which). AISpawnerAmbientNormal 's vf38 0x165844 runs that check first, then resolves its channel (0x114B1BC calls the channel resolver CreateEntityFromArchetype 0x1B3098 with the channel at +0x1C0 and the spawner's alarm area at +0x160 ) and runs the character-bundle gate 0x16652C (see Resource streaming). The resolver walks the channel's AI/SpawnAmbient/AITypes entries and keeps the templates of the best Priority (below 101). When the channel is DifficultyBased , the alarm area decides which table applies: 0x1B62F6C turns the area into its current alarm level (0x11FBC8: the live alarm state looked up through [base+0x26FFBF0] , otherwise the area's TransientAlarmSettings.RequiredDefaultAlarmLevel ) and takes the first table in [GM+0x6CC8]+0x18 whose AlarmLevelList.AlarmLevels contains that level (0x465CE8). A spawner in an alarmed area therefore spawns from a different difficulty table than the same spawner at rest. Every refusal is formatted for [AI SPAWNAMBIENT REJECT]: , but the logging function 0x19C83AC is empty in the shipped build. The predicate. 0x165B68 takes the given predicate or the spawner's own ( +0x168 , an AI/SpawnAmbient/Predicates record, of which 67 exist). With none, it passes. When the bytes +0x1A8 , +0x1A9 and +0x1AB are all set it computes the distance from the spawner ( +0xAC ) to the player and evaluates the predicate on it (0x165C4C); otherwise it passes both positions (0x166DF8). A predicate record has CanSpawnWithoutEntry , ProcessAllValidIntervals and Entries ( StructuresAISpawnAmbientPredicateEntry : Distance , RandomWeightRange , MustBeOffScreen , MustBeLineOfSight ). AmbShort , AmbLong and AmbDesert are three of the 67. The budget. 0x1A92F18 lets a request through when [SM+0x190] + requested <= [SM+0x180] . Past the budget, it passes only when the scenario's AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenarioSetup.ForceAISpots is set and the caller's flag is clear. Spawner sets are refused by 0x1AB9E0C for eleven reasons, each formatted for [AI SPAWNAMBIENTSET]: : not enough AI slots, the set cooldown, the quest-finish cooldown, the time of day, a global-variable predicate, the area's alarm level ( AI/SpawnAmbient/AlarmAreas ), a disabled scenario, a scenario already active, a disabled optional category, a category that may not spawn more AI, and no spawnable hijack for the type. Like the per-spawner refusals, these messages go to the empty logging function 0x19C83AC. Scenarios. AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenarioSetup (282 records) gives Priority , ScenarioType , RequiredAITypes , global and instance cooldowns, ForceNextScenario , ForceAISpots , MaxConcurrent , MaxConcurrentAI , MinDistance , ScenarioCategories , StartDisabled , IgnoreMaxConcurrent , AutoCooldownChance and AllowFailedSpawn . AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenario (53) gives Priority , FrequencyDecay , MaxConcurrent , MaxConcurrentAI , StartDisabled and ScenarioCategories . Removal rules are AI/SpawnAmbient/Removal (45 records, among them AmbShort R , AmbLong R , Offscreen , AwayFromPlayer , Never and Stronghold Removal50M ), and areas are AI/SpawnAmbient/Areas (180).

A spawn channel is an AI/SpawnAmbient/AITypes record (250; the scripts call the type DBAISpawnTemplate ). Its fields are DifficultyBased , PlayerWeightOnly , EnsureClassUnlocked , GruntBrandStatus , GruntActivateBrand , GruntPlayerFollowerStatus , InfightingRecord , Buff , Entries and four item lists given to grunts on the player's side or against it. A channel carries an allegiance, not a cast. Owner Infantry , Invader Infantry and Enemy Infantry resolve to the same template ( Orc Infantry , priority 0) and differ only in GruntPlayerFollowerStatus (2, 3 and 0), which partitions all 250 channels: Status Channels Family --- --- --- 0 129 enemies, wildlife and debug: every Enemy , Balrog , FellBeast , Nazgul Generic Solo , 22 of the 23 GangType 1 42 the player's side: 15 of the 17 Gondorian , DLC4 Easterling , DLC4 Torvin , Gollum , Spider AI Follower , Carnun Warg Friendly , 5 of the 6 Summon 2 24 the area's owner garrison: 23 Owner and AmbSpontaneousEvent 3 17 invaders: Invader 4 19 fort-assault defenders: 17 FortAssault Owner , Owner GraugapultRider , Owner Troll Graugapult 5 19 fort-assault attackers: 17 FortAssault Invader , Invader GraugapultRider , Invader Troll Graugapult Entries. In a live read, every channel carries an Entries array of StructuresAISpawnAmbientTypeEntry primaries {Priority, AITemplate} (250 of 250). The channel resolver 0x1B3098 reads EnsureClassUnlocked and PlayerWeightOnly , walks Entries (accessor 0x1B3DD0, priority 0x1B3D64, template 0x1B3CFC), collects the templates by priority, and takes a further path through the game manager for DifficultyBased channels. ResolveEntityArchetype 0x6FBEB8 finds a channel by name: it hashes the name and binary-searches the cached category [base+0x27022D0] ( +0x28 count, +0x38 the hash-sorted records), the same category the summon bindings use as the script type of their channel argument.

The chain is plain data: channel Entries[].AITemplate - AI/Templates (177 records; fields GlobalVarUnlock , CharacterModel , CombatProp , Alignment , DisplayInMenu , DefaultAISetMountData ) - Character/Models (281 records, 102 fields, among them CombatTree , SimpleModel , Skeleton and AIName ) - AIName = the AI/CharacterTypes record - its PlanTree . Of the 177 templates, 167 reach a character type with a PlanTree and 125 one with PlayerFollowerAlignment filled (Balrog, every troll and graug, drakes, the Carnan beasts, GP Bruz , GP Ranger , Baranor, Idril, Prototype Celebrimbor ). All 13 Nazgul templates (the Witch-king, Isildur and both forms of Sauron among them) have a brain but an empty PlayerFollowerAlignment . Talion , Dark Talion , Idril , Carnun and Shelob FairForm are presentation types whose tree is Idle . The model picker. Character/Models.CharacterModelPicker ( +0x208 of the record instance) names a Character/Models/ModelPicker . At creation 0x3FAE4C walks its Entries and returns the first CharacterModel whose GlobalVarPredicate passes, or the model itself. Only AI Talion carries a picker ( ModelPicker::Talion ), and its entries return the player's equipped skin. Every player skin's AIName is AI/CharacterTypes::Player , which has no PlanTree , so in the AI set-up (0x3FA718 - 0x45AFDC) the brain lookup 0x7279C0( [obj+0x2128] ) returns null and the creator 0x1CD454 frees the object (0x4DBD18). Nothing is logged and the summon that asked for it has already returned true. With the picker cell empty the model stays AI Talion (character type AI Talion , tree BasicEnemy ) and creation proceeds like any other.

QueueFmSpawn 0x1A91360(spawn manager, member, &transform , name, callback, int, byte) is the engine's "spawn this faction member here", the call the ambush system makes (0x1C7E434, log string "[FACTION AMBUSH]: ... Requesting to spawn faction member %s", which passes itself as the callback). It allocates a 0xB0-byte request (0x3DE238), runs the constructor and tail-jumps into the queue push, so its return value is the push's, not the request. The request runs later. Its Execute 0x1A927F8 takes the archetype from the member's own AI class (0x115F788), creates the body (0x1036D0), then the brain and configuration, and binds member and body (0x1AA20F4). Everything on that path allocates in the engine, so it belongs on the main thread. Request offset (constructor 0x1A90560) Meaning --- --- +0x00 vtable 0x1FB3F10 +0x08 its queue link {next, previous}, self-linked at construction +0x18 a weak reference to the member (vt 0x1DAB1C0; its target at +0x38 ), linked into the member's own list at FM+0x08 (0x597E84 - 0x597F00) +0x40 position, f32[3], cm (0x7FD96C) +0x4C rotation, a quaternion (x, y, z, w) (0x7FE6EC) +0x5C the name, copied ( strncpy s ) +0x80 the callback's weak link (0x1A9028C) +0xA8 / +0xAC the int and byte arguments The transform is seven floats, position then quaternion. CharacterTransform 0x180458(object, out) fills one from an object's +0xAC / +0xB8 through 0x182110. The queue is a circular intrusive list whose sentinel is the spawn manager's +0x98 : IntrusiveListPushFront 0x1161ED4(head, node) links request+0x08 right after the sentinel and asserts "Adding a link that is already inside of a list" when the node is not self-linked. A waiting request is found by walking [manager+0x98] back to the sentinel for vtable 0x1FB3F10 with [request+0x38] = the member. The ambient spawner skips a member whose body is already in the world ( FM+0x48 set, with flag bit 1).

Two script bindings queue spawn requests; neither creates anything itself. - AISpawnManager:SummonGrunts (summoner, channel, count, summon data): the stub 0x1BB138C calls 0x1A92FCC , which refuses a null summoner, channel or summon data and then, per unit, calls 0x572834(spawn manager, channel, summoner position, summoner, summon data, 0). That checks the summon data's Ambushes (0x572924: an ambush entry the faction system accepts takes the summon over unless its OnSuccessStillSummonNPC is set), allocates a 0x78-byte request (vt 0x1DBBBA0) and pushes it on the request list SM+0x98 . A live request held the summoner at +0x60 , the summon data at +0x68 and 0 at +0x70 . The request's processor is its vf1 0x606D68. - AISpawnManager:SummonNPCs (anchor, channel, count, summon data): the stub 0x1BB1468 calls 0x1A93064 , which snapshots the anchor's transform, allocates one 0x78-byte request per unit (0x1A90634; live requests carry vt 0x22FE510, processor 0x1A92A1C) and pushes it on the same list. It always returns 1. Its requests carry no summoner, so their characters keep the alignment of the channel's type: an AI Talion summoned this way is Orc FactionA , hostile. The main tick drains the list first in, first out, within about 2 ms of a call in play. While the world is paused nothing drains, and requests queued meanwhile all spawn at the transform they captured. Both processors resolve the channel (0x1B3098) and create through 0x1036D0 (world context, class 0x1FB3EC8, &position, template, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0). A summoned NPC is named SpawnReq... (for example SpawnReqGrunt80 ) and is already on the update scheduler's due list before it appears in the spawn manager's array. A summon made with the player as summoner and Summon Grunts comes out PlayerFollower ( npc+0x2410 ) with the follower byte npc+0x23B8 = 1, 0.3-2 m from the player about 3 s later. Summon data ( Combat/SummonData , 55 records; the scripts' DBAISummonData ) holds AIBandType , RemovalRecord , NavMarker , ScriptTags , AudioKey , MatchSummonerPlayerFollower , ItemsToGive , GruntTrait , RemoteScript , Alignment , UseSuperJump , AINodeTags , AINodeTagsAreMandatory , GoToAndMount , Ambushes , SpawnAtCombatTeleportPoint and EntranceSmartObject . Summon Grunts has the band HenchmenMob , the removal AmbLong R , the tag AmbSummonOrcTag , MatchSummonerPlayerFollower True and the remote script AmbSummonedOrcs . Summon Bait has the removal AmbShort R and the tags BaitSummonNPC and BaitNPC , and spawns at the AI Bait Generic combat teleport point. NPC summons ( Combat/NPCSummon , 107 records) are the trait- and ability-driven layer on top, with AISpawnType (a channel) or AISpawnTypePicker , Count , TeleportSettings , SummonData , SummonPlayerBodyguards , MakeGangMember and SpawnFactionMemberMount .

A captain's gang is a trait ( Faction/Traits/Definitions , see Captain traits). Quirk HasGang Normal Hunters , for example, sets GangLeader True, GangClassTypes - the channel GangType Hunters , GangSize 4, Catalyst Gang SummonOnSpawn , Item Item Quirk HasGang , and GangNPCSummon - Combat/NPCSummon::Gang Normal Hunters SpawnIn , which summons GangType Hunters with MakeGangMember True and summon data Summon Gang . The 23 GangType channels (among them Archers, Defenders, Warriors, Hunters, Savages, Ologs, Graugs, Caragors, Ghuls, Spiders, FellBeast, Easterling squads and summon groups) are ordinary spawn channels. Groups move as bands , defined by AI/BandTypes (66 records, among them Mob , HenchmenMob , Bodyguard , FollowLeader , SingleFile , TwoColumns , March , Skirmish 5Man , DiamondSurround , ChainGang , Wargs , FlyingV and GP Buddy ) with BandData , MovementData , NewLeaderOnRemoval , FollowDelay and NativePredicates . Summon data names a band ( Summon Grunts - HenchmenMob ). The band steps are FollowLeader , FollowWaitForBand and ReturnToBandLeader , with the target select WaitForBandMember . FollowLeader's update 0x48DB00 calls the band movement 0xF498C0. The AI world ticks the buddy and follower system at +0xB0 (0x3608C8), and buddies have their own target select ( BuddyCommand ) and alertness level ( ActiveBuddy ).

Story characters that guide Talion somewhere (Ratbag, Idril, Blade, Gollum, the Ranger, the third story DLC's Architect, Thrall and Flint, the fourth's Gondorians) run a lead behavior configured by one of the 16 AI/LeadPlayer records (distances in cm, times in seconds): Field DLC3 Architect Read by --- --- --- LeadRange (2,000, 4,000) 0x1AE7794 SlotRadius (200, 400) 0x1AE7794, 0x1AFD62C WaitWidth / WaitExtension 1,200 / 200 0x1AE7794 ReachRadius / ReachMovementSpeed 500 / Run 0x1AFD62C BeckonDelay / BeckonSmartObjectPicker (4, 6) / Bip Idle Looping the step's vf9 0x1AFD1E0; the picker also 0x1AFC7FC (from vf5) BeckonAudioInitialDelay / BeckonAudioRepeatDelay (2, 3) / (5, 8) AllowRepathing , RepathDelay true, 5 0x1AE70D4, 0x1AE7488 UnreachableRepathDelay 1 0xF40F00 ReferenceAgentHorizontalRange / VerticalRange 300 / 500 0x1AE7488 PauseConversation (-1, -1) 0x1AE70D4, 0x1AE7B5C MovementData LeadPlayer Architect (an AI/BandTypes/BandMovementData record) The script native NPC::LeadPlayer starts it (0x1AE70D4 reads AllowRepathing and PauseConversation ). Every NPC update ticks the guide's lead state (0x1AE7338, through 0x2F6150 on the NPC's +0x2D30 ): it recomputes the lead geometry (0x1AE7794: LeadRange , SlotRadius , WaitWidth , WaitExtension ), the reference agent and repath timer (0x1AE7488) and the conversation pause (0x1AE7B5C). The planner's LeadPlayer step (vt 0x1FBCA70) does the beckoning: its update vf9 0x1AFD1E0 waits BeckonDelay and then plays a smart object from BeckonSmartObjectPicker , and 0x1AFD62C tests arrival against ReachRadius .

The creature a captain rides comes from the trait Quirk HasMount : MountAITemplate - AI/Templates::Warg Tamed , FleeFindMount - AI/FindMount::FleeOnWarg (attack type Mount Warg , SearchRadius 2500, MountCharacterType Wargs , MountIsSummoned True), FleeSpawnMountChance 0.25 and FleeSummonMount - Combat/NPCSummon::Flee Mount Warg (channel Enemy Warg ). A rider's gang of beasts walking alongside is a separate gang trait. A template's DefaultAISetMountData names its ride ( Warg Tamed - AI SetMount Warg ). Combat/MountData (31 records, 24 fields) describes each ride. SetMount is 2 on the 24 SetMount / AI SetMount records and 3 on the 7 Dismount ones. The other fields include CombatBehaviorState (for example RidingWarg , RidingTroll , RidingOlog , RidingMedic and GrabbingAI ), AttachNode ( Saddle on 20 of the 24 mounting records; SocketAttach for carrying an ally and for the medic, attach for the meat shield, Null for the spider), behavior nodes for rider and mount, visibility, the attack types used when the mount or the attached target dies, MountedAlignment , and buff and item lists. The planner steps for it are GoToAndMount and Mounted .

AI/Count/Configuration (16 records) sets the budget: MaxAmbientAI , MaxHighPriority , MaxMedPriority , MaxLowPriority , MaxDeadBodies , RunSimulation , MaxSimulatedAnimations , PrioDefinition , PrioTokenDefinition and the LOD configurations. The active configuration is [base+0x2A63018] ( +0x28 of the static object at 0x2A62FF0 that 0x201DE8 initializes once). Free roam uses Default (as shipped: MaxAmbientAI 100, priorities 10 / 10 / 30, MaxDeadBodies 10). Quests switch configurations through 0x5C1294; across the others, MaxAmbientAI ranges over 10-200 and MaxDeadBodies over 10-60 (for example Assault 160 / 10, CarnanSideMissions 100 / 60 and DLC3 MoreBodies 100 / 55). The switch takes a configuration only if the validator 0x5C1638 passes: MaxAmbientAI + MaxDeadBodies <= 230 and MaxHighPriority + MaxMedPriority + MaxLowPriority + MaxDeadBodies <= 256 ; otherwise it silently keeps the old one. MaxAmbientAI reaches the spawn manager only through the copy 0x5C133C (re-run by the script command SetAICount and by quests), so a later edit of the record is not seen until that copy runs again. Corpses. On a death (0x49FE20) the cull 0x40538C reads the active configuration's MaxDeadBodies and walks the dead-body list (head [base+0x2672CB8] {+0 last, +8 first} , node at char+0x2298 , next at +8 ), removing every body past that index, off-screen ones first.

AI/Constants has one record, Constants , which sets PersonalBubbleDistance 50, ThreatUnseenTime 10 s, OnScreenCheckDelay 0.1 s, NodeClusterRadius 120, RetreatThreshold 3, RetreatCount -1, BrandedDefendPlayerMinimumRange 500, MinimumPlayerTargetedStimulusDuration 1.0, DamagedAtNodeAvoidanceTime 40-80, the unreachable-position delays (first 2.5-6, new 15-30, visible 1-2.5), BattleNodeMaxSelectionsPerFrame 255 and BattleNodeMaxChildSelectionsPerFrame 32, MaximumAllyGruntsInCombatSpace 10 and MaximumOpponentGruntsInCombatSpace 10 , DefaultCharacterModel Orc Infantry , NPCKnockBackAttack NPC Knock Back , DefaultIdle LoopingIdle , SpawnClosetIdle Bip SpCloset Idle , ObjectAlignmentName Player , the player- targeted stimuli PlayerBeingAttackedSound / PlayerBeingAttackedVisual , and the combat-circle directions. The grunt caps are read through 0x6DD4B0 (ally): an override in the quest system [[GM]+0x6C60]+0x588 (ally) or +0x58C (opponent) wins when it is 0 or more; otherwise the record is read (the integer read defaults to 3). Both overrides read -1 in free roam. Quest/Quests carries the same field (registered min=-1;max=10 ). Crowd AI. AI/Simulation (15 categories) is the cheap AI of army battles. Its 12 Configurations (for example OrcDefender , Spiders and FellBeast ) pick animation pools (idle, movement, off-mesh, activity, attack, recoil), CanTargetNonSimulated , potential riders and an attack budget AttackThrottling {AttackCapacity, AttackWeight} : Grunt 4 / 1 (four grunts on one target), Named 4 / 4 (one), Warg 8 / 4, Troll 20 / 20 and FellBeast 40 / 4. This is a second attacker limit, separate from the fight circle. The count configuration also carries RunSimulation (read by 0x4428B0) and MaxSimulatedAnimations .

Captain events that can be played or simulated (for example duels and pit fights) are sim events ( Faction/Events/SimEvent , 431 records, 41 fields, among them Type , Participants , WinChance , WinChanceJobSubject / WinChanceJobOpposition , SubjectWinsSimulate / OtherWinsSimulate , Results , life spans, RequiredCooldown and UniqueSimEventGroup ). 0x834F50 builds the engine's table of sim-event kind names (hashed, eight entries): 0 Automatic , 1 Story , 2 SimEventSingle , 3 SimEventDuel , 4 SimEventAugment , 5 FortAssault , 6 Conquest , 7 FortAssaultUnfinished . Sim-event records use per-record descriptor runs ( Arena has 56 cells, Gauntlet 51), so field offsets differ from record to record. Participants is an ordinary fixed-count RecordLink array: Arena 3 ( Arena 01 .. Arena 03 ), ArenaFollower 2, ArenaTest 3, Duel 5, Duel Origin 5, DuelG 2, Gauntlet 1 ( Gauntlet 02 ), Gauntlet2 1 ( Gauntlet Other Lvl 2 ), Gauntlet3 1 ( Gauntlet Other Lvl 3 ). Participants ( Faction/Events/SimEventParticipant , 572 records) carry JobRecord , JobGroup , Exclusive , CanBeBodyguard , Purposes , RewardList , ChanceToFill and the bodyguard builders. Win chance decides only a simulated outcome, when the player walks away from a fight; a watched fight is decided by the fight itself. Faction/Events/SimEventChance has 34 records, four of which compare as follows: Field Arena Duel Default 2orc arena Default 1orc general --- --- --- --- --- StartChance 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.6 CharacterLevelDeltaScalar 0.05 0.02 0.02 0 HenchmanDeltaScalar 0.15 0.15 0.15 0.15 SupporterDeltaScalar 0 0.15 0.15 0.15 TotalInteractionScoreDeltaScalar / Max 0.008 / 1.0 0.003 / 1.0 0.003 / 1.0 0.003 / 1.0 PlayerFollowerTotalISDeltaScalar / Max 0.0025 / 1.1 0.0025 / 1.1 0.0025 / 1.1 0.0025 / 1.1 TraitPairs 20 31 20 none The other fields are RPSPairs (empty on these four and on the two below) and ClampFinalChance (a pool range). SubjectAlwaysWins and SubjectAlwaysLoses differ only in StartChance (1.0 and 0.0; every scalar 0, both Max -1.0). Arena , ArenaFollower , ArenaTest and Gauntlet to Gauntlet3 link WinChance to Arena , Duel and Duel Origin link it to Duel , and DuelG to Default 1orc general . The chance is computed by 0x1BEDA40, the only reader of StartChance : StartChance , plus the level difference times CharacterLevelDeltaScalar , plus the henchman difference times HenchmanDeltaScalar , plus two further terms (0x1BEF460 and 0x1BEDD84), plus the subject's supporter term minus the other's ( SupporterDeltaScalar ), plus an interaction-score difference built from TotalInteractionScoreDeltaScalar , PlayerFollowerTotalISDeltaScalar and their Max caps. The sum is clamped to the ClampFinalChance range.

The pits in the Army menu are Quest/Quests records of type Quest/Types::Gauntlet ( IsGauntlet , ActivationType 1, CanReplay and XPAwardOnReplay True, ItemAwardOnReplay False): <MI MP IS DE VO SM Gauntlet , Gauntlet2 and Gauntlet3 (18) plus three PS Gauntlet records without a job set-up. Per tier, only the following differ: - the job chain JobSetupSimple - <R Gauntlet Lvl N - the job PS Other Cap Gauntlet <R [ Lvl N] - the champion's builder Faction/FactionMemberBuilder::Gauntlet <Region LvlN ; - the rewards (tier 1 SkillPoint , tier 2 PC Mirian Comb Arena2 <Region , 5,000 Mirian, tier 3 Gauntlet3 CitadelUnlock <Region , in Minas Ithil PS Raise Child1 UNLOCK ); - the Predicates (tier N needs <R Gauntlet Lvl {N-1} Complete and a living follower captain of the region army through Faction/CountFilters::IS Gauntlet ). Every pit quest owns its predicate primary (27 of 27 unshared). Completion is the global variable <R Gauntlet Lvl N , set by the fight script. The predicate Int PlayerMustOwnZone takes 0 for any region, 1 for a region the player owns and 2 for a region the player does not own (availability 0x1E00C4, see Quests, story and scenes). The three Minas Ithil pits ship 0, and the other fifteen 1. An empty PlayerMustOwnZoneFactions falls back to the current region's faction (0x1B5C820(FS, 1)), and MinPlayerFollowerFactionMembersInZone 1 refuses a region whose army has no living follower captain. Inactive quests are not re-checked on their own: the quest system re-runs every quest's predicates only when its timer cell QuestSystem+0xE8 (u32) is non-zero and older than the millisecond clock, then zeroes it. Online pits ( <R ArenaOnline ) are evaluated only in a region whose Overlord is the player's follower, unless the byte 0x2A36439 is set (0xEA5590; see Saves, the store and the network layer). The fight is the layer script. The prefab prefabs\gameplay\quests\powerstruggle\gauntlet.prefab06c is placed in <region /gauntlet 00/01/02 (its quest relay names the tier's quest) and, as arena.prefab06c , in <region /arena 00 , the Arena power struggle between two enemy captains. Its layer properties define spawner sets: C1 (job PS Subject , the player's follower), C1G (his gang, sized by his gang trait), C2 ( PS Other , the champion), C2G , and Door and Spectator ( StartEnabled , 30 spawns, alignment Spectator ). The sides are the alignments Duelist A (C1), Duelist B (C2) and Duelist C (hostile to both, neutral to spectators). - Timer. GameData.GauntletTimerValue (150 s) is read at fight start and counted by a script timer in 10 s ticks. Every tick on which ST:GetIntervalRemaining() is below GameData.GauntletTimeRemaining (120) gives both duelists Script Quest ArenaDamageScalar ( Arena DamageScalar : +0.15 damage per stack). A timeout is a draw: no global variable is set and the quest awards no items. The newer copy of the script also heals both captains on a timeout and floors them at 50%. - Outcome. When C2 is killed, the outcome is Gauntlet BlueOrc Win on the follower (forced level-up, reward list PS DuelWin CanChangeRole , LevelsToAdd 0), the objective PS Gauntlet Obj and the tier's global variable. A loss gives Gauntlet BlueOrc Lose on the follower (action 8: he dies, with the event's Resurrection record) and Gauntlet RedOrc Win on the champion ( LevelsToAdd 1, ClearBuilderInstance , action 2: the champion takes the loser's seat; see Faction-event actions below). In a measured loss, the champion took the dead follower's exact seat and gained one level. ForceLevelUp adds no level of its own. Walking away runs QR:SimulateSimEvent() with the Arena win chance. Dominating either captain ends the fight ( SubjectDominated / OtherDominated ). - Two copies of the script. The Minas Ithil gauntlet 00.scripts ships in Patch 05 (1,332 lines) and Patch 06 (1,443 lines), and both define the class gauntlet SO Script 5eae30cb . The newer copy adds AddLevels (a winning follower gains Gauntlet AddLevels 01 .. 20 by the level gap: 20 when he is 26 or more levels below the champion, 1 when he is 11 or more above), DLC IsFriendlyOnlineArena true during the fight, the timeout heal and PS Gauntlet PostFightSpawn when C2 lives. It also comments out the loss pair AddGauntletEnemy / GauntletEnemy EnterHierarchy in all three death branches. Both Lithlad copies ( Patch 09 , Patch DLC5 ) are the newer variant, and in a Lithlad fight DLC IsFriendlyOnlineArena read true during the fight and false after. - What the script does to each captain at spawn: senses off until the intro ends, Script Item Intro 2Target , the other's PS DuelistC1 / C2 , Script Item DoNotBleedOut , Script DisableSummons , Item BypassKillStealPrevention , Pass KillCam PIS Test IT , Arena DisableWallRecoils , Item Disable Retreat , the side, a confinement ( SetConfinement , C2's gang too, C1's gang not) and a visible nav marker. On death it fires PS Arena DisableCollision . SetAIToSpawn(1, n) fills the captain slot and (2, n) the gang slot sized by GetGangSize() . Gang members charge the enemy captain ( ApplyThreatRecord(Showdown Charge) , MonitorCharacter , SetCombatScriptedTarget ). MissionEnd decides only by aiCaptain1:IsAlive() . C2's death branches register C1DeathRelay (hash 0xA6106936), so C2DeathRelay never runs and the sim-event result reads SubjectDied when the champion died. A C1Victory (C1 back to his point, C2's gang removed, SetC2 re-enabled for a next opponent) has no caller in either copy, and the script never enables the spectator set the layer flags StartEnabled . - A fight as recorded in three Lithlad tier-3 fights: when the fighters appear, the script's Player:Hide(true) sets Talion's hidden byte +0x3882 and his AI-invisible byte +0x2F10 in the same tick. The sides go into slot 4 (see Sides above) one tick later, and the arena camera director takes its two combatants after the intro (20 s) and releases them at the result. In all three fights the losing captain was held at exactly 10.0 HP until a finishing scene, and trait catalysts pushed the Hatred, Victim and Unstable sides above the pit's sides mid-fight (see Sides above). The dead captain's member read the dead and shown-dead bits (2, 21), +0x2A8 the killer's character type, +0x2B0 the finishing sync attack, +0x2C0 the resurrection record and a cleared builder link at +0x350 . - Dormant hazards. The remote-script objects rsOil , rsCaragor , rsGhul , rsArrows , rsGas , rsRiot and rsGraug listen to the remote scripts PS Arena Oil through PS Arena Graug in all 29 gauntlet, arena and online-arena layers, but no shipped script fires them (only PS Arena DisableCollision is fired). Riot() is the only hazard with a working body (each spectator joins Duelist A, B or C at random). The arrow, oil and ghul hazards walk groups ( GArrows , GSpouts , GGhuls ) that none of the 20 pit layers sets, and the caragor, gas and graug hazards only print. The script's play-as branch ( QR:GetPlayerFactionMemberIndex() 0x1A50ED8 - 0x19F4D30, 1 or 2 when the player's play-as key [player+0x2708] matches the subject's or the other job's captain) makes the player captain 1 or 2, but MissionEnd decides the win on aiCaptain1:IsAlive() . The key ( +0x2710 the pool index, -1 for none) is set by CPlayerObj::SetPlayAsFactionMemberNPC (0x19BFA08 - 0x19BD070(player, member, 1), which applies the member's seed, personality, class model through Character/Models.PlayerVersion and appearance, and the items marked KeepItemWhenOrc ). It parks the player's real model at player+0x2ED8 , his appearance at +0x2EC8 and his inventory (the visual component) at +0x2EC0 . ClearPlayAsFactionMemberNPC (0x19BB794 - 0x19BB610, secondary vtable 0x1F969A0 slot 12) clears the key and restores all three.

The consequences of a pit's result are the faction events' Actions , a list of values. The handler 0x40C304 (log string "HandleFactionEventAction: Event = %s; Subject = %s; Other = %s", compiled out) resolves the subject and the other through 0x18DDCC, walks the list (accessor 0x40C8F4, element 0x40CB6C) and switches on each value: Value Effect --- --- 0, 2 MOVE: the subject takes the other's seat ("Loser (%s) Vacating their position %d, %d": unseat 0x61B274; "Winner (%s) moving into position %d, %d": 0x61E13C(FS, subject, row, column), the row index and column from the event's +0x56 / +0x57 ), only when that row is above the subject's 1, 7 the other dies: 0x5966C4(FS, other) with the event's Resurrection record (0x1BB9F84) 8 the subject dies, the same way 3, 4 the other becomes the subject's henchman ("%s Became Henchmen of %s", 0x1BB767C; 3 also checks the preset's CanEverBeHenchmen ) 5 0x1BC3F80(subject) 6 the subject clears his boss ("%s Cleared his Boss", 0x1BB8E30) 9 0x1BB9080(subject) and FS+0x1ED = 1 10 swap seats ("Other moving into position %s, %d") 11 / 12 the subject / the other leaves his seat (0x61B274) 14 the subject is seated in the other's place (0x61B274(other), then 0x61E13C) The pit's events carry these actions: Gauntlet BlueOrc Win none (plus ForceLevelUp and the reward list, one of PS DuelWin BrawlMaster , PitFighter and NothingHappens ), Gauntlet RedOrc Win 2 (plus ForceLevelUp , LevelsToAdd 1, ClearBuilderInstance ), Gauntlet BlueOrc Lose 8 ( LevelsToAdd 1), Gauntlet RedOrc Lose 8 ( LevelsToAdd 1, ClearBuilderInstance ) and AddGauntletEnemy none (a SimEventTagModList ). The script applies RedOrc Win with the champion as subject and the follower as other, and the Lose events go on the loser alone. Both recorded outcomes match: in one a champion died with Resurrection LowerBody , and in the other a follower died with Resurrection OrcSlash and the champion took his seat.

- On the map and compass, NavMarkerTypeQuest is Interface/NavMarkerTypes::Arena ( interface\textures\hud\questicons\new\kraken\powerstruggle.tex , 60 px, PrimaryIconOverride ArenaIcon , minimap questarrow.tex ). - The start card uses the WorldUIConfirmSequence QS Gauntlet Base WUIP ( bundles\animationcharacters\menu\queststart.bndl ; steps QS GauntletEnemy Setup , WalkOut , FadeUp , Idle PR ; alignment Job Other ; see The mission start screen) and the strings PS Gauntlet Name , PS Gauntlet1 Desc , PS Gauntlet Desc Short and PS Gauntlet Desc Comp MM . A plate's tints are therefore data. - The champion's job PS Other Cap Gauntlet <R sets AlwaysUseBuilderRecord True with its builder, AddHenchmen True and OtherJob PS Subject Cap Vs .
