- Faction/SimEvent/Gauntlet (4: Island , Island2 , Island3 , SnowMountain ) leads through GauntletTier ( Stages ) and GauntletTierStage ( SimEvent , Configuration ) to the Gauntlet sim events. These records are not what the playable pits run. - GauntletMgr saves its tiers (0x1A825EC): +0x48 an array of 0x10-byte entries {TierRecord, u32 NumCompletes} , +0x50 their count. Loading (0x1A824E4) zeroes every NumCompletes , reads the saved tiers back and sets the byte +0xB0 . - The pit spawn scenarios are the AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenario records ArenaCombatants , ArenaCombatantsKeep , ArenaEvent , ArenaEventActivator and ArenaEventActivatorKeep , and in SpawnScenarioSetup the beast and orc pairings (among them ArenaGraugVsGraug , ArenaCaragorsVsCaragors , ArenaOrcsVsOrcs , ArenaNamedVsOrcs , ArenaOlogVsOlogKeep , ArenaEventFight and ArenaEventRandom ). - The arena camera director is [[base+0x26FFA98]+0x8B8] , held by the client shell (the getter 0x2F6D1C asserts it is non-null; in a live game it is an object of vt 0x22F3E48). The script class ArenaCameraDirector ( Start 0x1BB0118) hands it the two combatants through 0x1D78EB4 - 0x179EE48. The finish 0x179CADC (also the console command Arena.Camera.Finish ) resolves them from handles at +0xB0 and +0xB8 through its tracker at +0x2A0 (0x179D410, 0x179D49C, each cast to a character), makes both the player's bodyguards, and reads the gauntlet stage from the quest at [+0x700]+0x258 ( Quest/Quests.GauntletStage ). The camera data is Arena/CameraDirector::Duel ACD (camera lists, picker, HUD state, ArenaRadius ). - Duel ACD is the only Arena/CameraDirector record. It has ArenaRadius 1350; StartCameraList 3, PrimaryCameraList 6, SecondaryCameraList 3 and TertiaryCameraList 1 entries (10 distinct Arena/CameraEntry records); and CameraPicker ArenaList , HUDState OrcArena and CommandSet ArenaCamera . Arena/CameraObject holds eight objects ( Center OBJ , Combatant1 OBJ , Combatant2 OBJ , Fallback OBJ , Stands1 OBJ .. Stands4 OBJ ). The director's set-up 0x179E3C8 looks up Combatant1 OBJ , Combatant2 OBJ and Center OBJ and reads ArenaRadius . Eight Mob/MobDefinition records ( Arena EnemyDef MD , Arena EnemyInf MD , Arena EnemyArmy MD , Arena EnemyOlog MD and the four Arena Friendly MD ) each hold one Members field. - Who won. 0x179EE48 calls the arena telemetry builder 0xF511E0. It counts a combatant as dead when bit 2 of its FactionMember+0x508 is set, or else when CCharacter::IsDead (0x190F1C) holds for the character at +0x48 of the same FactionMember, and reports Combatant 1 , Combatant 2 , Draw or Both Dead . The quest-complete screen 0xE69B60 tests bit 21 (0x200000) of +0x508 on both combatants: both set gives UI QuestComplete Resolution Gauntlet BothDead , one set gives UI QuestComplete Resolution Gauntlet Winner , and neither gives UI QuestComplete Resolution Gauntlet Timeout . The same function picks UI QuestComplete Resolution Showdown Dead from bit 21 and UI QuestComplete Resolution Showdown Recruit from bit 27. - AutoInfight is Monolith's stripped captain-against-captain harness. The script call Faction:DEBUG StartAutomatedInfighting (0x1B80A3C) reads its three arguments and returns 0, so its driver [FS+0x60] is never created. Behind it the faction system's update 0x1E2BC4 ticks 0x1A73F58( [FS+0x60] ): a fight object at +0x38 that is done is destroyed (0x1A85488) with a cooldown at +0x40 , and without one a new one is built (constructor 0x1A84FC0, vt 0x1FB2C40, 0xF0 bytes, two transforms). 0x1A85550 picks a random pair of the current army (0x1C1B91C) and turns the first's follower bit off and the second's on (0x7D52B0, a change that is saved). 0x1A857F8 then stages the fight: it clears the spawn manager's enable byte ( +0x194 ), removes every ambient AI and the dead bodies, queues the members at +0x38 and +0x60 of its object through 0x1A91360 under the names AutoInfightNPC1 and AutoInfightNPC2 (with itself as the callback, ids 1 and 2), and clears the bytes +0xB8 and +0xB9 . Its results were written through the file name template %sAutoInfight %s.txt . - The gauntlet menu's input actions are SimEventGauntlet MenuEnter 0x16A, SimEventGauntlet MenuExit 0x16B, SimEventGauntlet ActivateFirst 0x16C and SimEventGauntlet ActivateLast 0x16D. Arena CameraAdvance is 0x15A (the input-action table 0x3123CC stores the values explicitly; it has 0x179 entries). - Arena telemetry names the arena type (0x1B2A1F4: 0 Gauntlet , 1 Blood Duel , 2 Assassination , 3 Online Ranked , 4 Online Friendly ) and the event (0x1B2A1C0: 0 Started , 1 Hazard Triggered , 2 Completed ). - Infighting between two NPCs is held by the planner: NPC::IsInfighting 0x1A8D1B8 is !IsDead && [planner+0xA60] != 0 .

- Which copy of the Minas Ithil pit script runs, Patch 05 or Patch 06 (the Lithlad copies are the newer variant)? Is ST:GetIntervalRemaining() in its damage ramp the whole timer's remainder or the current 10 s tick's? - Why did followers put on hostile pit sides not fight in four attempts (with the senses cycle and scripted targets, as for the enemy grunts that did)? Either the target check 0x18BE04 ends in a leash test (the anchor 0x4474DC, radius +0x240 around +0xAC ) and follower grunts stay anchored to Talion, or followers may never attack followers. - Does a load rebuild the compiled relation matrix, and who applies Trait Unstable Follower besides the trait catalysts (no world script does)? - Are followers capped at Talion's level? Two winning followers stopped at 80 while enemy captains read 82 and 85 (flag bit 10 is "ignore the player-level cap"). - What do the step status values mean? Both step classes read return 2 for a failed precondition and for a lost target; watching a step that completes normally (a GoTo arriving) would show whether 1 means success. What does vf8 ( return true in both) answer? - What does forced change in a quest-requested replan beyond the pair byte +8 , and what do the 0xA8-byte entries of the batch 0xF41E30 hold? - Which systems set the suspend byte npc+0x2C21 besides the queued teleport? No stack entry parked a non-zero status in a 73.5 s fight capture, and the byte was never seen set in it; reading it during a mount, a synchronized kill and a dialogue would show the answer. - Which classes implement the 50 step types that have no class named from their own field reads? The factory map gives every one a vtable, but the table above lists only the ones read live or named. - Is the target-select table ordered by Cost ? Mapping each of the 27 objects ( picker+0x08 ) to its record would show it, and which pickers dominate the scan. - Which Enemy channels are replaced by Owner / Invader channels when a region loads? In one loaded desert, 233 of the 5,002 live ambient spawners (4.7%) still carried Enemy channels, so the replacement is not applied to all of them. - Why does a Balrog summoned onto the player's side follow but never fight? Its combat tree has no CombatCircleNodes , unlike the AI Talion's ( AI Talion CombatCircle ). Comparing the attack decision of an AI Talion against an orc with the Balrog's would locate the difference. - What puts a character into the spawn manager's second roster at +0x168 ? No function that loads the manager writes the vector or takes its address to append, so the append goes through another pointer to it. What are the values at +0x184 / +0x188 (40 and 8 in one reading, 30 and 8 in a later one, both in Lithlad)? No code in the offset index reads or writes them directly.

t: Combat: attacks, targeting, predicates and resources
x: Every combatant carries a combat object, and every attack is a record whose compiled predicates decide when it may run. This chapter follows an attack from those records through targeting, input and damage, then covers resources, weapon elements and slow motion, capture points, the fight circle, combat states and actions, area attacks, the player's execution companions, struggles and hit categories.

Every combatant has a combat object (vt 0x1F995E0) at CCharacter+0x26A8 (mirrored at +0x2978 ): Offset Meaning --- --- +0x28 / +0x48 the owner character (AI characters have vt 0x1FB3640) +0x38 the AI slot: the owner on an NPC, 0 on the player +0x40 the player slot: the player on his own combat object +0x50 the combat component (player only) +0x58 the combat tree ( Combat/Tree , for example AI Easterling Defender ), set by 0x4EECA4 +0x60 the character type ( Easterling Defender ) +0x68 the FX lookup key ( Client/FXLookup/Key ), copied from the tree's FXLookupKey by 0x4EECA4 (see Characters, the player and the camera) +0xA8 its own current target +0x2F0 the combat state machine (below) +0x2F8 the ammunition object (player only) +0x318 the stat table +0x338 / +0x340 the Might meter / the Wrath meter +0x3A0 the health listener +0x3F8 a pointer to the last-damage record (vt 0x1DAA9C0; empty until a hit) +0x428 / +0x42C / +0x430 maximum health, health, and their ratio +0x480 the tree's PreferredWeaponSlot +0x4A0 dead: CCharacter.IsDead (0x190F1C) tests this byte +0x5A0 the cooldown table +0x5F8 the computed maximum-health stat (value at +0x50 ) +0x68A the tree's CanGainThreatAgainst +0x691 a per-attack "this blow kills this target" state (below) CCharacter+0x2410 (mirror +0x2EF0 ) is the character's Character/Alignments record (one of 52, among them Player , PlayerFollower , BuddyFollower , Orc FactionA , Troll Cave and Warg Brown ), and +0x23B8 is its follower byte. Dead characters leave the spawn manager's array, so its count is a count of the living. Destructible props (for example Env Destroy FirePit ) are combat objects too and can be targeted. The player's combat component is [player+0x2FA0] ( comp+0x08 = the player). It holds FreeAim at +0x668 , the targeter container at +0x5C0 , the companion manager at +0xC68 , the active attack record at +0xF00 and a list of hostile types at +0xEF0 .

Combat/Attack has 16,976 records. An attack names its AnimationData (clip, playback rate as an enum pair read at attack start, sync, overrides), AttackData (target selector, area attack, teleport, translation scaling, item slot to draw, ranged overrides) and AttackPostData . The targeting cache [GM+0x6CD8] is compiled at world start: Offset Content --- --- +0x08 / +0x10 the Combat/Attack entries (16,976 x 0x58 bytes, in database order) +0x8058 the Combat/Target entries (0x1B8 each, built by 0x1B69838) +0x8088 the compiled Combat/Pool entries (0x48 per pool record index) An attack entry holds +0x00 the Combat/Attack record, +0x18 the damage formula and +0x40 .. +0x48 the compiled predicate pairs {evaluator, record} (0x10 each). The damage formula is a plain pointer to a Combat/Stat/Formula/Damage record ( DmgForm All Instakill in 1,681 entries, DmgForm ZERO in 1,563, DmgForm AI Melee in 809); it is null in the 8,879 attacks that ship no formula. A change to a predicate record's value is seen at the next test; linking an attack to a different predicate record takes effect only when the compiled pair changes too. A compiled pool entry ( [[GM+0x6CD8]+0x8088] + recordIndex 0x48 , data at +0x08 ) holds at +0x00 an attack-type restriction and its vector (0x3FC280), and at +0x20 a combat-state restriction and its vector (0x3FC254, tested against the current state [[0x2F5288(component)]+0x2F0]+0x58 ). They are compiled at load from the pool's original attacks.

Combat/AttackPredicates/ holds 124 predicate types with 9,311 records (one or two fields each; PredicateAttackTypeIncluded alone has 5,806). In all, 14,593 attacks carry predicates, compiled into 95,979 pairs. The 105 predicate types in use map one to one onto 105 evaluator functions , a contiguous library at 0xECF9E0 - 0xEE4FB0; the other 19 types are used by no attack. A lock range exists in three copies, and only the third gates acquisition: 1. the GameDB value Combat/Target.WeightData.DistanceRange (a pair in the shared float pool); 2. the compiled Combat/Target entry in the targeting cache (compiler 0x1C0B634), which holds +0x0C the maximum range, +0x14 the maximum range without input, +0x168 the maximum angle, +0x20 / +0x24 the screen width and height, and compiled boolean pairs {present, value} from +0x194 . +0x190 holds MaxDistance PlayerAlly x 100 (the field is authored in meters), and the byte +0x1B5 enables it; +0x195 is RequireLOS, +0x1A0 the outside-screen test (off for every player selector) and +0x1B0 / +0x1B1 RequireStraightPath; 3. the player's live targeters : the container at comp+0x5C0 keeps a pool at +0x18 / +0x20 of 0x80-byte targeters (vt 0x1DB1040; +0x28 the current target, +0x30 the Combat/Target record, +0x38 the range ; 114 in the player's pool) and lists at +0x48 / +0x50 (0x20-byte {key, begin, end, capacity} , 192 lists keyed by candidate character type). Every list is sorted by range, longest first, and acquisition (0x18D06C) returns at the first targeter whose range is below the candidate's distance. Keeping a target (0x18CDD4) checks +0x38 too. Membership in a list is the type filter. The candidate filter 0x18626C has 38 logged rejection reasons ( [COMBAT TARGET] ). A follower is rejected (0x366B88) when the ally byte is set and its distance exceeds the ally maximum. The scorer is 0x30B2D4. RequireStraightPath rejects any target without a straight walkable path (sword selectors set it, the bow does not), which excludes enemies below a rooftop. The compiled ally byte is set exactly when the authored maximum is above zero, so the data cannot express "reject allies at any distance".

Combat/Node = {Type, Predicate - a primary {Input, Chord}, Pools[] - Combat/Pool.Attacks[] , Links[], RequiredTransitionType, KBMNode}. 0x310C00(node, isGamepad) returns the node's keyboard and mouse variant (KBMNode, field 16; node slot array at 0x2650EE0), and its six callers resolve every node of a list through it. The player's tree ( Combat/Tree::Player Character ) has 146 roots (192 PC nodes in all). - Input records. The ActionID cell is the action id itself (Light 0xA247C387, Heavy ...388, Stun ...389, Dash ...38A; keyboard-only actions 0xE8C05C0x). InputType is 0 for press, 1 release, 2 held and 3 held for the previous node. GameChanger WraithDash HeldPrev (Light + mode 3) is a shipped hold-to-chain. - Holds. MinHeldDuration (0x6FEF14) passes on a released button only when the release time equals the current time, which never happens in practice. Every shipped hold therefore uses InputType 2 plus MinHeldDuration (for example Tackle Attempt , Riding KillMount ). An input entry is {u32 press, u32 release, u16 action} (0x19B488). - The input-driven node runner 0x30FD80 is reached only from the player tick (0x162560 <- 0x43B8F4); AI combat has no virtual controller. It picks an attack with PickAttack 0x275730, which runs PoolCheck 0x3FBA8C on each of the node's pools. The pool's predicate ( StructuresCombatPoolPredicate ) can require an item, typically a skill item, tested by 0x276E1C(inventory, list); a pool that fails is rejected before any attack predicate runs, and a null item skips the test. The pool rejection log 0x19C83AC is an empty ret in the shipped build. - AI attacks carry no target selector ( AttackData.Target is null): an AI's target comes from its perception and threat picker. Synchronized attacks. Combat/Sync.InitialAlignment decides who moves: 0 moves the attacker to the victim (EnableAlignment), and 1 with TeleportDuringInterpolation moves the victim to the attacker. Any synchronized kill therefore closes the distance itself. AttackData.Teleport - Combat/AttackTeleport (11 records) teleports at attack start without a sync. AttackData.AOE - Combat/AOE spawns an area attack (1,840 attacks set it). AttackData.AOEOnStart fires it at the start; otherwise only a clip event (such as PL WraithAOE ) fires it. The Shadow Strike kills already sever the head ( SeverActionTarget Head, SeverTargetOnKill ). A swapped animation changes what plays; the attack record keeps what it applies (its categories and actions). Aerial combat is ordinary data. The fell beast's death-from-above moves are combat nodes and pools like any other ( AI FellBeast DFA Shallow , Steep and Troll , each with Into , Attack and Out ). The player's gliding is a set of input predicates (for example Combat/Predicates/Input::DLC4 Gliding Start , Exit , DFA and Ranged ) and behavior-state lists ( PC Gliding , DLC4 Gliding , DLC4 GlidingRanged , Aerial Ranged , AerialRanged Active ), and aerial archery's animations are the player graph's PL AerialRanged nodes. The aerial bow mode PC Ranged Sniper Aerial is chosen only while the player's behavior states include falling, jumping, wall-jumping or gliding (see Characters, the player and the camera, for the ground predicate every ground shot carries).

The attack's target comes from 0x76A890(component, attack) in two lanes. When the attack's selector equals FreeAim's +0x88 (the draw mode's TargetOverride ), the target is FreeAim's ray-cast targeter [fa+0xB0] , which is what the reticle is on; otherwise it is the selector's live targeter in comp+0x5C0 , the lock. A targeted projectile never ray-casts: the shot (0x4CDE54 - 0x2E8994 - 0xFC15A0) and the projectile update (0x116E64 - 0x11734B) find the target alive (0x1A4F2F0) and apply the hit at its node (0x4EBED0), so walls do not stop a locked arrow. The reticle color is FreeAim's state byte fa+0x4CA , set by 0x1A0EE8 from the target in FreeAim's weak handle ( fa+0x30 ): 0 hidden, 1 nothing, 2 neutral, 3 hostile, 4 ally and 5 a world point. 0x114C588 passes it to the HUD crosshair. Each frame 0x379578 ray-casts. A character hit goes to 0xFA640 - 0xFA788(fa, player, combat object, hit), and anything else to 0xFA788(fa, player, 0, 0), which clears FreeAim's targeter through its vf1 (0x18D298). The draw-snap aim assist (0x19F9E0 - 0x19E73C, CP RangedAutoTarget ) does not steer the shot and expires after about 0.4 s.

Cooldowns are one latched end time. CheckCooldown 0x493320 returns [obj+0x10] - now , floored at 0. StartCooldown 0x1A78B34 evaluates MinTime and MaxTime through the stat-value evaluator 0x30F42C when the cooldown starts. It takes MinTime plus a random fraction of the difference (0x1B3C6C; MinTime alone when MaxTime is not larger), multiplies by 1000.0 (the float at 0x202E644) and stores now + milliseconds , so a duration change applies at the next use. The time source 0xF23310 reads one of four of the engine's clocks chosen by Combat/Cooldown.TimerType ( obj+0x14 ; 0 the unscaled clock 0x2702550, 1 the world 0x2702598, 2 the real-time clock 0x2702590, 3 the player 0x2702548; see Engine core). Every combat character owns a cooldown table at [combat+0x5A0] : +0x00 slots (stride 0x20: +0x00 key, +0x08 record, +0x18 the u32 end time, +0x1C the clock id), +0x08 count (356 = the whole Combat/Cooldown category), +0x10 the category. The start path 0xF13920 indexes it by record index. Of the 356 cooldown records, 342 use a raw value, 8 a formula (the summon wheel's mounts and followers, through MountCoolDown and FollowerCoolDown ) and 6 a variable. Might is a charge meter at combat+0x338 (vt 0x1DAA9C0: owner +0x20 , value +0x2D0 , maximum +0x3A8 = 200, two chunks of +0x348 = 100). Wrath is the same class at combat+0x340 . A hit's gain is not a Combat/ResourceGain record: IncrementHitCounter 0x2DC668 - AddCharge 0xFFA8C takes the amount from a table compiled into the meter at +0x28 / +0x30 . The player's table has 62 entries of 0x18 bytes, {Combat/Category, item list, stat value option} ; the first category match wins, and the last entry is the default. Combat/ResourceGain is the other path ( ApplyResourceChange 0x59CD94, used by executions and abilities). FillToMax 0x19D37B0(combat object) - SetValue 0x44FCD0 fills the meter. Its only caller is the buff system ( Combat/Buffs.FillChargeMeterOnRemoveBuff , 0x451EF0), and the path allocates from the engine heap, so it belongs on the main thread. Ammunition is the object at combat+0x2F8 (player only). It holds the owner at +0x20 , six slots of 0x90 at +0x28 for ammunition types 2-7 (slot 0 = arrows; AddResource 0x19D24F8) and, at +0x38C , the reference count of the Combat/Buffs.UnlimitedAmmo buff. A slot holds the maximum at +0x54 , the stat variables Int AmmoCount , Int AmmoCount1..6 and HasFullAmmo at +0x60 / +0x68 / +0x70 , the stored count at +0x88 and the HUD slot at +0x8C . The setter 0xEE9D40(slot, count, owner) clamps to the maximum, returns when the count equals the stored one, stores it, and updates the stat variables (0xEE9FC0), the quiver visual (0xEE9F20) and the HUD. The refills are 0xEE5BE0 (all) and 0xEE5CD0 (one type), both gated on GameModes.CanRefillAmmo , and 0xEE5CB0 (ungated). The ammunition tick 0x45144C refills every frame when the byte [base+0x2A34D6C] is set or the unlimited-ammo buff is active. That byte is the engine's own infinite-ammunition switch, written nowhere in the shipped code. Arrows are spent by Combat/ResourceGain records with a negative additive value ( SniperShot Spend , NormalShot Spend , ShadowStrike ToNav Spend -1, ShadowStep Spend -2, AllAmmo Spend -50).

The damage info passed with a hit holds +0x20 the attacker's combat object (0 when there is none), +0x28 the damage and +0x30 the attack or source. ApplyDamageInternal 0x2E4BE8(combat, info) reads [[info+0x20]+0x40] (the attacker's player slot) before Faction::TriggerAmbush (0x2E4E3A) and compares it with the target's mount (0x2E4C41). ApplyDamageInternal (163 instructions, read whole) works as follows. A dead target returns at once. A mounted target can pass the damage to the mount's combat object. ActionsOnAttackHit Target 0xF10D50 runs, and 0x2E4E80 copies the info into the last-damage record. Then: - A damage of at most 1e-4 in size ( [0x202E860] ) takes the zero branch: the owner's vf83 and 0x2E54BC, and nothing else (no state interrupt, no HUD push, no player branch). - For the player only, 0x778E88( [GM+0x6D18] , health + damage, damage, source) records it in a 10-slot ring of recent damage at +0x938 . - Health = min(health - damage, maximum). At 0 or below the kill 0x4A022C runs, health is set to 0 and +0x4A0 to 1, all in this one call on the main thread, with no can-die gate, so no later frame can undo it. Otherwise 0x2E54BC runs. - The ratio is stored and the listener called; then 0x1E51B0(combat, health, source, attacker) runs, then the AI (0x441228) or player (0xF364A0) reaction. - A second kill test follows for a living character whose byte char+0x23BD is set (0x11548B0). The health bar is pushed; nothing polls health. 0x1E51B0 updates the stat variables through 0x1E52D4 (the records at [[GM+0x6CD8]+0x8360] health and +0x8368 the ratio) and the health-triggered states 0x1E5F14 ( Combat/States/Auto.HealthRemainRange , Definitions.InterruptOnHit ), then calls 0x1E6018(char, health). On the player ( char+0x2700 ), that function keeps the last health and a running delta at [GM+0x6D18]+0xBE4 / +0xBEC and calls 0x188F098(health, maximum). That call takes hud = [[UIManager]+0x30]+0x48 and runs 0x4AACDC(hud, hud+0x318, health, maximum), and the LowHealth byte hud+0x1370 follows ratio <= 0.25 ( [0x202E9BC] ). The element's target value is at +0x1F4 and its maximum at +0x200 , and the change animates after Interface/ElementSetup.HUDResourceAnimationDelay (150 ms). The call checks [UIManager+0x30] but not the object under it. NPCs get a health nav marker instead. A write of the health value alone therefore leaves the bar where it was: read live once, health 722 of 722 stood beside a ratio of 0.5523 and a bar at 398.8 of 722. The engine's setters. AddHealth 0x37FEE0(combat, delta) refuses a dead target, clamps health + delta to [0, maximum], stores the ratio, calls the listener and pushes (0x1E51B0(combat, health, 0, 0)). Its callers include CCharacter::Heal 0x19B6584, the Health cheat 0x65ADCC (delta = maximum), SetResource 0x19D9C7C and AddResource 0x19D24F8. The maximum refresh 0x37EFCC(combat) stores a new maximum when the stat is dirty or differs from [[combat+0x5F8]+0x50] , clamps health down to it and pushes, so a raw write of the maximum is undone wherever it runs. Regeneration 0x44D1CC runs at most every 100 ms, not while dead or while the current state's AllowHealthRegen is false, and reads the stored ratio. The damage evaluator 0x3643E8 (794 instructions) applies a floor, TargetMinHealth , which is the highest of: - the formula's TargetMinHealthFinal plus 0x6C74D8 (an auto state's ClampHealth ); - Player.MinHealth , the float at 0x2A418D8, for the player only; - PlayerFollower.MinHealth (0x2A418DC) for followers, otherwise 0x2A418E0 for other NPCs; - the defense record's StructuresCombatStatValue.MinHealth ; - the character's own floor char+0x2500 (set by CCharacter::SetMinHealthPct 0x19B7294 as pct x maximum). The three globals sit in writable data, have one reader each and no writer, and read 0.0. The floor then works in health points: a floor above the current health makes the damage 0, and a hit that would cross it is cut to health - floor (0x364F49). With dl = 1 the evaluator returns the target's whole health as damage (0x3644BD); 0x2E3B6C, 0x6A4194 and 0x115401C pass 0. 0x6A4194 with r8b = 1 is a lethal-hit prediction (health - damage <= 0), which the floor also answers. After the floor the evaluator applies the bonus-damage (critical) scalar FormulaBonusDamageScalarOverride , the victim's current defense record ( [ctx+0x58] , StructuresCombatStatValue.DamageAmount - StructuresCombatModifier multiply / add) and two global multipliers. PlayerCanTakeDamageFromAllies governs the player as the victim of his allies. The same path reads developer bytes that no shipped code writes: [0x2674820] = 1 (0 makes the player take 0), [0x2A34D67] (the player's hits forced to 1,000,000, and also any attacker-less hit on a victim whose +0x2700 is 0) and [0x2A34D68] (non-player attackers do 0, and the hit continues). The hit dispatcher 0x2EE394 (16 call sites in 15 functions, 638 instructions) handles a hit before any damage: - The invulnerability test ( [[GM+0x6CA8]+0x30] , 0x115441C: the target or its rider is the player) sits at the top and leaves with 0, so the whole hit is discarded: no attack data, CanTakeDamage , evaluator, hit state (0x2EFD44, 0x2E3AAC), hit counter (0x2DC668), ApplyBuffListOnHit , hit effect (0xEAEDD0), damage over time or threat. - The friendly-fire gate sits at 0x2EE58B: when 0x2EF0E4(attacker side, target char+0x23E0 ) returns false, the hit is dropped whole. It is false only when 0x18BC88 returns 1. The attacker side is the attack's StructuresCombatAttackData.AlignmentOverride ( ...Branded when 0x1156B94 says the attacker is branded) when set, otherwise a copy of the attacker's own side. - After the evaluator, 0x2EE6F3 overwrites the damage with 1,000,000 ( [0x202E470] ) when its eighth argument is set or [0x2A34D67] is on with a player attacker. Of the 16 sites, 7 pass a literal 0, 8 a cleared register and 1 forwards; the one that can pass 1 is the melee hit test 0x2C658C ( ApplyDamageRange , "Hit - Distance ... Angle"), with r10b = 1 when the attacker's +0x691 is set and its +0xA8 is the target (0x2C6A53). 0x19D9C24 (one caller, 0x2C3D68) sets +0x691 only while +0xA8 and the current attack match its arguments, and StopAttack 0x2EA790 clears it. It is a transient per-attack state of synchronized kills. - The hit effect 0xEAEDD0 - 0x1CDE00 keeps the damage in the hit event ( +0x38 ; +0x00 position, +0x0C normal) and tests only its sign: a damage above 0 fires [[GM+0x6CD8]+0x8320 / +0x8328] , one below 0 fires +0x8330 / +0x8338 , and 0 fires nothing. Sides at the gate. A character's effective side is the 0x58-byte stack at char+0x23E0 (see AI, "Sides"). It holds its Character/Alignments record at +0x30 (0 = none, and the gate lets the hit through) and from +0x38 seven u32 slot ids, which are record indices in Character/Alignments . An id of N or more is skipped, not a terminator (0x18BCAD; Talion reads 0xFFFFFFFF six times, then 7). 0x18BC88(table, row, column) returns the first non-zero cell of the relation matrix over the two sides' id pairs (the row's ids outer), 2 when all are 0, and 0 when either side has no record. The values are 1 friendly, 2 neutral, 3 hostile . The matrix ships 1,802 zero cells, 278 friendly, 201 neutral and 423 hostile, and it is not symmetric. In a live game, 48 of 48 followers read Talion as 2 while Talion reads them as 1, and 7 of 7 enemies are 3 both ways. Followers' hits therefore never land on Talion, while Talion's land on followers. The sides that call Talion a friend are, as followers, PlayerFollower , PlayerFollower Beast , BuddyFollower , BuddyFollower Beast , WraithInfight , Branded and WraithInfight Beast (Talion reads them as 2), and also Aligned AllFriendly , GP PlayerBuddyAI and Despawn BuddyDismiss (1). The table object has 33 code readers, 15 of them through 0x18BC88. The attacker-less hit 0xEADE70(victim, ...) has no side test. It runs CanTakeDamage (0xEAE22F), the evaluator, the force at 0xEAE431 (victim +0x2700 = 0), the apply 0x42B290 and the kill 0x4A022C. It has six callers: the damage-over-time tick 0x2E7BA4 (whose source [dot+0x48] is null or the victim), the area tick 0x2E6BFC, the melee routine 0x2C642C (when the attacker's combat object is not resolved by 0x1A6CCE0), the projectile handler 0xFC15A0, 0xF43270 and 0x1BF8B30. CCharacter::Die calls ApplyDamageInternal directly with 100,000, past every floor. Damage formulas. Combat/Stat/Formula/Damage (353 records; 101 are the player's) is a node list. Each node ( StructuresCombatFormulaDamageNode ) has an optional VariablePredicate / DamagePredicate , an Operation ( Combat/Stat/Formula/FloatOperation ) and ReturnImmediateIfPassPredicates , and is evaluated per hit by 0x3643E8 with both sides' stat sheets ( VariableSource 0 the formula's own side, 1 the other, 0x2783D4). An operation (0x362C34) sums its ADD entries minus its SUB entries into A. It sums its MUL entries (they add up, 1.0 when there are none), divided by the summed DIV entries unless those are about 0, into M. OperationType 0 gives (value + A) x M, and 1 gives value x M + A. The largest shipped float constant is 9999 ( MultiplyBy9999 ). Nested formulas are cached per character, without an attacker. An entry with FormulaSource 1 calls 0x363DB0(the other side's sheet, formula, 0), which returns [entry+0x14] from sheet+0x48 (0x40-byte entries by record index, count sheet+0x50 ) and recomputes through 0x362688 only when the entry's dirty bytes ( +0x08 , +0x09 ) are set. A missing entry gives 0.0. A record edit therefore reads back but changes nothing until its entry is recomputed. Of the player's 101 formulas, 2 clamp their output, 88 reach five shared defender sub-formulas ( Equip BonusDef Beasts / Undead / Uruks DefScalar , Gem GreenRing DefScalar , Prestige MountDefScalar ), the most shared per-hit victim predicates reach 32 ( IsTarget Monster , IsCursedTarget , IsEnraged Target , IsPoisoned Target ), and the most shared operations are Oper DmgAll ZERO (68) and Oper DmgAll InstaKill (24). Characters carry a bool stat IsPlayerFollower .

t: Weapon elements, procs and slow motion
x: A captain's weapon element lives on the attack; the item only unlocks it. The trait Curse Weapon gives the items CursedWeapon , Item HasAnElementalWeaponFromTrait and Item HasACurseTrait . The hit is the category ApplyStatusEffect Curse WeaponKindRequired ( PredicateHasItem CursedWeapon , ApplyBuffListOnHit Curse NoBonusKind Weapon ), which the attacks themselves list. Of the 16,976 attacks, 1,234 carry the curse category, 1,328 fire, 1,370 poison and 1,225 all three. The freeze categories sit only on the player's attacks ( PC ApplyStatusEffect Freeze WeaponKindRequired 509, Dagger 170). An orc weapon's glow is a lookup on the weapon, keyed by a tag on the buff. Buff apply walks ClientFXAttachItemSlot twice: EquipmentFXType - 0x4F4834(vc, slot, type) (0x453658) and EquipmentFXSequence - 0x1BCE998(vc, slot, sequence) (0x4536C9). Inventory/EquippedWeaponData holds EquipmentFX / EquipmentFXActive lists of {FXType, FXSequence} pairs (914 pairs, all on orc weapons: 0 of 1,397 player weapon records has one, so on the player's weapons a tag draws nothing). Four tags exist: Poison 304, Cursed 301, Flaming 155, Bleeding 154. Bleeding is a cut element: Combat/Buffs::SavageWeapon has no holder, and Weapon Bloody is named only by 150 pairs. The player's blade looks come from the charged-weapon table ( Combat/FX/ChargeWeaponFX : PC WeaponBuff Fire / Freeze / Poison / Curse , PC FireSword01 , CurseSword , BL ChargedSword ) and the buffs' FX contexts. Frozen is an animation rate. PC Freeze FreezingWeapon is StateFlags Quick Stunned for 7-10 s with Combat/States/AnimRateController::Frozen taking the rate to 0.0 over 0.5-0.9 s. Nothing freezes the player. Procs run on a captain's own buff. There are 225 Combat/Buffs/Procs/Definitions (151 with player predicates). Buff Trait Lifesteal.Procs - ProcDef AI Lifesteal ( MustBeDispatchSource 1) heals the captain on a hit. Proc predicates are Quest/AutoObjectives of type 15 ( AI HitPlayer = SourceAttackHit + target type Player Character + SourceAttackCanIncrementHitCounter ). A proc's predicate can test the victim's stats ( StatPredicateTarget - Combat/Stat/Formula/VariablePredicate ), and procs carry TargetAppliedState . The 27 shipped Clear buffs share a Group with the buff they clear. A group is a replace rule: 0x36A35C refreshes the same buff and first removes another of its group. A buff's flags reach its holder (apply 0x452ED8, remove 0x451EF0) by three routes: NativePredicates strings go through 0x375044( [char+0x28]+0x120 , name, true); BoolStatVar goes through 0x1E4874( [combat+0x318] , variable, true), with the entry found by 0x1E4948 in the stat table's +0x90 {entries, u32 count, category} (0x18 bytes each, {record, u8 value at +0x08} , indexed by record index; "Bad record index" when the category differs); ClientFXSequence applies on any holder, and ClientFXSequencePlayer on the player only. A buff with LimitRawMoveMag of 0 or more stores it through the NPC planner [char+0x2CE8] , which on the player is a self-pointing container head, so on the player the store lands inside his own object, with no fault. Slow motion. Every slow-motion wrapper tail-jumps to the request 0x5D08B8( [base+0x2A86888] , slot, record or 0, flag), and the lowest slot runs. The slots are 4 0x5BB5E0, 5 0x19CFF60, 6 scripts ( System::SlowMoStart 0x626C98), 7 0x19CFD60, 8 0x19CFDE0, 9 0x19CFEE0, 10 the player's weapon modes 0x7A35D8, 11 presentation elements 0x5D09E0, 12 0x4359DC, 13 the buff clear 0x19CFCEC, 14 an attack's AISlowMo 0x7BEB48, 15 0x6EEFC4 and 16 0x19CFE60, so a weapon mode outranks a presentation. A scale is (1, N) , meaning N times slower, stored as a shared float-pool pair. A buff's SlowMo field only stops a slow motion (its accessor 0x451E14 has one caller, the remove path, which clears slot 13). A buff starts one through ForcedWeaponMode (holder [char+0x560] , 0x19D9B94) - the mode's SlowMo - a SlowMo record in slot 10 ( PC Buff GameChanger , DLC4 SlowMo OnBrutalStealth ; 7 buffs set the field), and the slow motion ends with the buff (read on 3 of 3 such buffs, in the same 50 ms sample). Of the 332 slow-motion records, 9 leave the world alone and slow only the player: DLC4 GC 1 SM 2x for 10 s, PlayerDeath SM 4x, Predeath Savior Ranged Paused SM 5x, Kill Sync Obituary Far SM 10x, Predeath LoseMinigame SM 11x, Predeath Savior Entrance SM 30x, Predeath Savior Ranged SM and Release SM 50x. Under DLC4 GC 1 SM the clocks read world 1.000 player 0.500 : the player's own motion follows his clock (see Characters, the player and the camera, for why his movement record's speed multiplier does not). The player's element buffs are Flame Weapon , Frost Weapon , Poison Weapon and Curse Weapon , in the melee slot. Flame Weapon lasts 10 s and is a chance bonus {C PC ApplyFire, +1.0} ; Frost Weapon is the same on C PC ApplyFreeze , with no FX type or context; and Curse Weapon adds the material state Curse .

The engine's [COMBAT WEAPONBUFFFX] system draws a buff's effect on an equipped weapon, driven by buff apply and remove through ClientFXAttachItemSlot - Combat/Predicates/InventorySlot.Slot . - The store [vc+0x4A8] is a 0xA0-byte block made on first use (0x4F4964), holding EquipmentFXType[10] and then ClientFXSequence[10] by equip slot (0 sword, 1 dagger, 2 bow). Every accessor asserts slot < 10. The type setter 0x4F4834(vc, slot, type) stores it (0x115F614) and re-dresses (0x4F49C0); the type clear 0x1BC9CB0 clears only while the slot still holds that type. The sequence setter 0x1BCE998 stores it in the block and at holder+0x1A8 and redraws nothing; 0x1BC9C40 clears it. The getters (0x4F48E4, 0x4F4904) have one caller, the holder build 0x40014C. A slot's holder is [vc+0x38 + slot 0x28] : each equip entry is a 0x28-byte reference at vc+0x18 + slot 0x28 (vt 0x1DB7630; +0x20 the target, the holder, 0 for an empty slot). - The re-dress 0x4F49C0(holder, type) caches the type at holder+0x1B0 and returns at once when it is unchanged or the parts vector holder+0x148 is empty. Otherwise each part [[holder+0x148][i]]+0x20 gets holder+0x1A8 when set, otherwise the weapon look's own pair for the type. 0x3FE1FC(look, type, part) takes the first EquipmentFXActive pair whose FXType matches and its FXSequence[part] only while part < count, otherwise 0 (0x3FE04C does the same on EquipmentFX ). A one-hand orc look's pairs therefore hold one sequence (part 0), a shipped two-weapon look holds each twice ( Orc 1HB MeatBoneClubX2 : Weapon Fire , Weapon Fire ), and a Defender's shield (part 1) never takes his spear's effect. A set sequence overrides the look's pairs, and a type change is what makes it show. The generic orc sequences in the base list are Bleeding - Weapon Bloody , Cursed - Weapon Cursed and Poison - Weapon Poison ; in the active list they are Cursed - Weapon Cursed Active , Flaming - Weapon Fire (Flaming lives in the active list only) and Poison - Weapon Poison Active . - The parts own their players. 0x3FE0F0(fx, sequence) stores fx+0x1C8 and, when the part has renderables ( fx+0x120 ), makes a player at fx+0x188 if there is none, binds it to fx+0x58 and starts the sequence ( EnterFXUseTarget ). Sequence 0 stops it (0x771BDC). 0x3FE2A0 does the same for fx+0x1D0 and the player fx+0x190 ; then 0x3FE488 runs each active player only while [fx+0x1E5] is set and [fx+0x1E4] is not (0x7B24B4). - The active window belongs to the animations. [fx+0x1E5] is written for every part of all 10 holders at once by 0x1BCEAE8(vc, bool) - 0x1BDF444(holder, bool), whose one caller is the model-string dispatcher 0x4CDE54 ( [COMBAT MODELSTRING] ): the clip event ENABLEWEAPONFX (hash 0x630F8E71) sets it and DISABLEWEAPONFX (0x715E0EB6) clears it. - Re-equip order. The holder build 0x40014C re-dresses the new holder before it copies the sequence to +0x1A8 , so a re-worn item shows nothing until the next type change. - Of the 11 buffs with weapon effects, only FX GondorWeapon set a sequence, and they name no slot. Of 1,727 Client/ClientFXSequence records, 74 are named for weapons, swords or blades. PC WeaponBuff Fire and StormbringerWeaponFX are played by nothing (0 holders, against 172 for Weapon Fire ), and their files ship in no container.

A fort or outpost capture point fills as follows, according to the code and the shipped records. - The tick runs 0x6546E8 - 0xF324F0 - 0x362304(manager, node, dt) once per node. The manager holds 256 character slots (0x28 bytes: +0x00 character, +0x10 node, +0x18 rate, +0x1C side, +0x1D present, +0x1F advancing), a node list at +0x2838 .. +0x2840 , the player's node at +0x2850 and his rate at +0x2858 . When +0x285E is set, the tick is skipped. Rates are summed per side into two pairs, presence and advance. The player counts for presence inside the shape at [node+0x240] and for advance inside the one at [node+0x270] , into which CaptureRadius is copied (0x4A62C4). - The node ( BattleNodeCapture , vt 0x1FB9E90) holds +0x580 the AI/BattleNodeCapture record, +0x590 the full amount, +0x594 the current amount, +0x598 a cap (used when 0 or more), +0x5AC the holder (0 defense, 1 offense, 2 neutral), +0x5AD the status and +0x5BC the active flag. SetCaptured 0x7B16A8 copies MaximumAmount into +0x594 , and ResetCapture 0x1ACE498 copies InitialAmount . - CaptureRatio is not a speed. 0x361B6C reads it every tick (default 1.5, [0x202E8F4] ), and 0x362068 uses it only to decide who holds the point. From holder 0, presence[1] ratio x presence[0] flips it to 1; holder 1 stays while presence[0] <= ratio x presence[1]; and from 2 the larger side takes it. - Speed is 0x361FC8. Holder 1 moves (advance[1] - advance[0]) x dt when OffenseCanAdvance is set and that value is positive; holder 0 moves (advance[0] - advance[1]) x -1 x dt when DefenseCanAdvance is set; and holder 2 does not move. Defenders inside the radius therefore subtract from the attackers' rate. 0x76B588 adds a rise and snaps at +0x590 (returning 4, otherwise 3); 0x361A34 applies a fall and stops at 0 (returning 0, otherwise 1). - The rate 0x3625C0(combat, side) takes the tree's AssaultCaptureRateOffense or ...Defense and evaluates it through the cached 0x363DB0 (above). Of 281 trees, 24 use the player's pair, 41 use Assault Capture Off Rate / Def Rate , and 1 uses DLC3 Assault Capture Off Rate Talion . Assault Player Capture Rate is 7, times 1.3 under DLC4 OutpostReward FasterCapture and times 2.0 under DLC4 CaptureFaster , unclamped. Defense Player Capture Rate adds 9999. Record MaximumAmount CaptureRadius --- --- --- Capture PlayerInvading 300 800 Capture PlayerDefending 400 800 DLC4 OutpostAssault 400 1125 All three have InitialAmount 0, CaptureRatio 1.0, OffenseCanAdvance true and DefenseCanAdvance false.

The fight circle decides which NPCs attack a target, how many at once and when. Data. The fight circle's data spans 27 categories under Combat/FightCircle/ and StructuresCombatCircle : - Circle (15, one per target kind, among them Player, Player Eltariel, AI Talion, Troll, Warg, FellBeast, Balrog, Cage and Barrel) holds ArcAngle, BucketRays (8 for the player), PreDeathAttackerLock (6 s for the player) and DefaultPlaybook[] . - PlayBook (41) - PlaySets[] - Plays[] . A Play has a SelectionWeight (a weighted pick; 0 = never), difficulty weights, a predicate, delays on hit / miss / counter / abort, global cooldowns and Stages[] - StageNodes (a small state machine with next-stage links) - Stage . - Stage (201) holds NumAttackersMin / NumAttackersMax (1-16), AttackType, MultiAttackerDelay and Role (distance, camera, off-screen and last-attacker weights, stat predicates). The (min, max) pairs are (1,1) 160, (1,5) 6, (1,3) 5, (8,8) 5, (5,5) 5, (2,2) 3, (1,4) 3, (4,4) 3, (16,16) 3, (1,16) 2, (1,6) 1 and (5,10) 1. - Other categories include Participant (59, per attacker kind, with fields such as RequireLOSToAttack, FarDistance and RunDistance), Setup (11), Rings (28 radius bands) and CirclePolicy (16). Against the player ( VS Player Default , 42 plays), melee is PC BaseMelee (weight 0.1), whose stage PC Melee Single has one attacker. PC DoubleMelee (two attackers) has weight 0.0, so two-orc melee plays never start. PC BaseMeleeAndRanged and PC BaseRange add PC Ranged Single (1-3 archers). The mass stages belong to the Nazgul (5 melee with a 1.2 s stagger, 5 or 4 ranged), the no-path case ( PC Ranged Multi 2-6, PC Melee NoPath 5-10), goblins (6, 1-16) and the fellbeast (5). The pre-death play is PC BasePredeath , with weight 100,000 and one attacker. Runtime. The fight-circle manager is the AI world's +0x28 ( MainScene+0x778 ); its +0x48 is an intrusive list of circles (the list node is the circle object, about 0x200 bytes). The tick runs the scene tick - AI world tick 0x1F7304 - 0x6DE538(manager) - 0x377528 (walk the circles) - 0x3775A4(circle, now) - 0x377744 (only while the byte 0x267358C is set) - 0x377830 - 0x3778D4 / 0x4259A0 - 0x425B60 - 0x425C3C. That function reads the stage's NumAttackersMin and Max on every stage start, computes count = min + rand(max - min) (0x426840), clamps it to the role's candidates (0x11D89C) and assigns attackers one by one with the stage's delay. The statics are 0x2673584 = 500 ms and 0x2673588 = 100 ms (the play re-evaluation interval). A circle holds +0x38 the target's combat object, +0x1A0 the current attacker's, +0x1E4 / +0x1E8 world-clock timestamps (the 100 ms and 500 ms checks) and +0x1F4 the number of participants. An NPC joins when its target changes (0x37CA3C "Target just changed." - 0x37CAA4 - 0x2C1004 - 0x2C0FCC - 0x2C0144 - 0x2C0280, the circle's playbook accessor 0x2C0C6C) and from planner steps. The planner's CircleTarget / CircleAlly steps are the NPCs waiting their turn (see AI).

Combat/Actions/ holds 60 action types with 938 records; the largest are InventoryItemAdd 245, AudioKey 187, InventoryItemRemove 145, NPCSummon 50, BuffRemove 34, CreateTrapAtSource 33, CombatMeterAdjustment 30, FactionEventAdd 30, ResourceGain 26 and AOERemove 18. 0x1A6E090 registers one handler per type through 0xF17060 as {category, handler} pairs; most handlers lie in 0xF12810 - 0xF16F60. The handlers by type: Type Handler Type Handler --- --- --- --- StartCooldown 0xF13920 CreateTrapAtSource 0x1A6ED34 CreateTrapAtTarget 0x1A6EE6C CombatMeterAdjustment 0x1A6EFB0 CombatMeterClearSource 0xF15E00 PauseStateTimer 0x1A6F02C SetBrand 0x1A6F080 SetPlayerFollower 0x1A6F0B8 SeverFactionMember 0x1A6F1F8 StartRangedDrawTimer 0x1A6F25C StartConeSequence 0xF169B0 SetVisible 0x1A6F1A4 TeleportToRangedTargetLocation 0x1A6F264 ConsumeDamageCounterCharge 0xF13820 ConsumeHitCounterCharge 0xF13870 NPCSummon 0xF15EE0 NPCDismiss 0xF15EC0 StopAISlowMo 0xF16DD0 ResetStruggleCount 0xF16840 ClearAllDOTBuffs 0xF137B0 DifficultyIncrementKillCount 0xF13A80 ClearGruntTrait 0xF137C0 InventoryItemAdd 0xF14220 InventoryItemRemove 0xF15C60 FactionEventAdd 0xF13BF0 FactionAmbushTrigger 0xF13BB0 ConditionalResourceGain 0xF137E0 AOERemove 0xF128C0 BehaviorStateAddTemporary 0xF13280 CreateNavMarkerAttack 0xF13A10 ResourceGain 0xF16930 AudioKey 0xF12960 BuffRemove 0xF13340 MeleeFX 0xF15DC0 DespawnNPC 0xF13A60 DespawnNPCOffscreen 0xF13A70 CancelAttackMount 0xF13750 CancelAttackRider 0xF13760 UIProgressMeterStart 0xF16F00 UIProgressMeterStop 0xF16F30 SheatheWeapon 0xF16980 QuestStartAmbient 0xF167C0 StateFlagRemove 0xF169E0 StateTagVolumeAttach 0xF16A00 StateTagVolumeClear 0xF16DA0 InventoryItemSlotVisible 0xF15CF0 AOECreate 0xF12810 AOEPickerCreate 0xF12870 ProfileStatIncrement 0xF16660 ModelString 0xF15E60 ChainCreate 0xF13770 ChainReturn 0xF13790 RemoveAttachedProjectiles 0xF167D0 AmmoResourceTypeActivate 0xF12930 CooldownReset 0xF138C0 WeaponAnimStart 0xF16F60 BuddyMarkTarget 0xF132F0 BuddyClearTarget 0xF132D0 InventoryItemDropLoot 0xF14FA0 InventoryItemConvertToResource 0xF14E20

Combat/States/ has 8 categories with 846 records: - Definitions (112 states, 30 fields) say what a state permits: InterruptOnHit, EnableCollisionCapsule, AICanSeeThrough, EnemyAICanTarget, CanPlayerTarget, AllowHealthRegen, AllowPlayerDetection, DisableSenses, AllowFleeing, ForceFall, DisableAllTraitCatalysts and ReplanOnRemove. They also hold fail and pre-death conditions, health adjustment and an attack on exit, a buff, a command set (the player's inputs while in it), a presentation event, a struggle pool, an animation rate controller and the transition graph (TransitionIntoFlags, RemainInStateFlags, included and excluded transitions). States include KnockDown, Stunned, Blinded, OnFire, Grabbed, Vulnerable, Raised, Cursed, RuneFeared, SmokeScreen, WraithPinned / SpiderPinned, Bip BleedOut, Player Death, the bosses' pre-death states, ambient states (Caged, Kneeling, Sitting, Mourning) and boss phases. - AppliedState (364) describes how a state is applied (base chance, chance formula, buff chance, duration and overrides, flags, a HUD prompt). - Flag has 113 records, and Setup (31) gives per character type the valid states, overrides and buff replacements. - Auto (36) holds the health-triggered states, with activation and remain ranges, filters and health clamps; the clamps include the boss phases (for example AI Balrog ClampHealth 50Pct / 75Pct , AI ArPharazon Phase2 35PctHealth / 65PctHealth and AI FellBeast HealthAdjust ). A state is applied through the chain CCharacter::ApplyCombatState 0x19B3230 - the combat object - 0x19D2834 - 0x105704(the state machine [combat+0x2F0] , state, 0, [combat+0xE0] ). The script binding ApplyCombatState 0x1B751F4 resolves its record through the cached-category slot 0x27008D0 ( Combat/States/AppliedState ).

Area attacks are data in Combat/AOE (627 records, with fields such as Tick, Timer, TickDelay, MaxAOELength, StartNode (a bone), Alignment, UseTargetLocation, UseRayCast, RecalcStartEachTick, CanHitSource and HitOncePerSpecialAttack) and Combat/AOE/Tick (752 records, 56 fields, among them Radius, Angle, dynamic radius, MaxAIToHit (-1 = unlimited), HitAllAI, CanHitMainWorld and attack overrides), plus Combat/AOE/Picker (33), ProjectileTarget (5) and ProjectileSpray (2). Area ticks apply damage through tick attacks whose compiled predicates decide who may be hit. Ragdolls span 14 categories, which hold the Havok active-ragdoll tuning. Ragdoll has two bodies (Orc Base, OlogHai Base), each with a brain and 19 joint constraints (38 Ragdoll/Constraints records). The other categories include Ragdoll/Behaviors (18: strength and stiffness ranges and masks, sequences), Sequences (16), TargetPoses (32), ConstraintTargetPose (112), BehaviorControllers (13), float ranges, masks and audio tables.

Combat/PlayerCompanion/ defines the spectral companions that execute for the player. Setup::Player links the groups Execution Lvl1/2/3 (Quantity 20, a combat prop with its own tree, 68 CB execution attacks, selector CB Duel Instakill ), which trigger while the parent attack carries an included category, on input or at a hit-counter value. The groups are compiled when the player's model is set (build 0x1881264, called from 0x183C0B8, which sits under the player's model and skin setters). Changing the records later has no effect until then. A compiled group (vt 0x1F7A188, stride 0x2B0) holds +0x18 the group record, +0x40 owner, +0xA0 / +0xA8 included categories, +0xB8 / +0xC0 excluded, +0xD0 companion type, +0xD8 prop, +0xF8 effect sequence, +0x104 auto-trigger hit count, +0x13D can evaluate input, +0x13E swallow input, +0x13F parent must have an active attack, +0x140 parent must reject input, +0x142 auto-pick on an enemy's counter window, +0x143 auto-trigger on the hit counter, and +0x120 / +0x128 required item / buff. The manager is [comp+0xC68] , with its groups at +0x58 / +0x60 . - At every player attack start, 0x2C3D68 - 0x4E8B54 - per group 0x4E9094 latches the group when the attack has an included category and no excluded one. - Input goes through 0x4E85D0: first a swallow pass over a separate vector ( mgr+0x70 , holding only Counter FromGTD ), then the player's own tree, then the normal pass 0x4E8B94 over the groups. A group must pass its gates: the swallow flag clear, can evaluate input, latched, the item-slot mask, the parent's input decision, the event id (small command ids such as 0x6B attack, 0x6C and 0x85), and its required buff and item. It then gets an instance (0x65A990: one per latch with a budget, otherwise up to Quantity), and EvalNodes 0x795E7C picks an attack ( PickAttack ) and a target (0x76A890 with the player's component), places the companion (0x18800FC) and starts it (0x1888918). - EvalNodes evaluates every attack with the player as the attacker, so attacker-side predicates (Focus, distance, direction) are measured from the player. - Two launches happen without input, both with mode 5 (no input match): 0x6D27D0 from the hit counter (every multiple of the group's auto count) and 0x76EE08(component, enemy combat object), raised when an enemy opens a counter window, with an explicit target. - The execution pools require the wraith-execution skill item ( CSP Chord InstaK Child1 - PS Execution Child1 WraithExecution SKILL ): without it every pool is rejected before any attack predicate runs.

A struggle is the player's input minigame inside a paired animation: the Last Chance ring before death, button mashes, holds, stick directions and aiming. Struggles run only for the player; the other participant only plays its half of the paired animation.

Category Records Role --- --- --- Combat/Struggle/Types 8 a counter family: reset rules, reset cooldown, presentation events, an optional stat mirror Combat/Struggle/Pools 49 a type and an ordered list of options Combat/Struggle/Options 131 predicates and a list of struggles Combat/Struggle/Struggle 132 one minigame: input kind, buttons, timings, ring sizes, widget, audio, camera Combat/StruggleRemaining 1 maps the Last Chance count to the remaining chances shown on the HUD (3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 0) The types are FF PC RMT Melee, BH3 Sequence, BIP TribeAtk Dark, BIP TribeAtk Warmo, Werewyrm Struggle, PreDeath, PreDeath Caragor and PC PinnedState ButtonMash. Only PreDeath mirrors its count into a stat ( Combat/Stat/Variable/Float.LastChanceCount ), and its reset cooldown of 1e10 seconds means the count never expires. InputType is ECombatStruggleInputType (table 0x2A4DD00, built by 0x8629AC); the shipped struggles use each kind as follows: Value Kind Struggles Data struct --- --- --- --- 0 QuickTime 1 QuickTimeData 1 Aim 13 AimData (cursor speed and ramps, target scale, sequence length 2-8 s) 2 PressCount 19 PressCountData (presses to win, branch on win, fail on a wrong button) 3 Hold 4 HoldData (required hold duration, prompt offset) 4 InputDirection 4 DirectionData (direction, a 70-degree range on the warg domination records) 5 Ring 91 RingData (motion, win, perfect and lose ring scales, fail time, slow motion, can get perfect) The results are ECombatStruggleResult Fail 0, Success 1 and Perfect 2 (0x862BDC). The widget position type is None 0, SourceNode 1 or TargetNode 2 (0x862B00). The buttons are the actions CombatStruggle01 to CombatStruggle10 , enabled by the command set Profile/CommandSets.CombatStruggle (127 of 132 struggles). The Last Chance ring is drawn with three materials ( lastchance red.mat for the moving ring, lastchance blue.mat for the win ring, lastchance white.mat for the perfect ring) whose alpha reference parameters Interface/UIMaterialOverride/Struggle.SharedStruggle names. Struggles start from Combat/Sync records (paired animations): 49 of 1,507 carry a StrugglePool , with StruggleWinSync (46), StrugglePerfectSync (30) and StruggleLoseSync (10) naming the paired animation that follows each outcome and PerfectStruggleRequiredItem (23, all PS Struggle Crit ) gating Perfect on a skill. Combat/States/Definitions also has a StrugglePool field, empty on all 112 shipped states. The shipped syncs reference 17 of the 49 pools.

The struggle state lives on the player's combat component ( [player+0x2FA0] , also the combat object's +0x50 ): Offset Meaning --- --- +0x08 the player +0xC70 the struggle started by a paired animation +0xC78 the struggle started by a combat state +0xE30 the per-type count table (entries of 0x18 bytes); +0xE38 the entry count +0xE68 the combat object +0xF5F / +0xF60 can lose a struggle / can lose an aim struggle ( CCharacter.DEMO SetPlayerCanLoseStruggle 0x19B397C, ...Aim 0x19B3998) The pool evaluator 0x1843E04 returns nothing unless the combat object has both +0x40 and +0x50 . On the player's combat object +0x40 is the player; on 11 of 11 non-player characters sampled live both are 0. For a paired animation the engine takes the participant whose combat object has +0x40 , or that participant's rider, so a mounted player struggles through the mount's paired animations.

0x1843E04(pool, combat object, target, option out) reads the type's count, walks the pool's options in order and returns the first whose predicates pass (0x18464E4: count range or count formula, buff, the player's items, the target's items, stat predicates, the target's health range). From the passing option it takes the struggle at index min(count, n - 1) (0x18458F4), so an option's list is a difficulty ladder indexed by how many struggles of that type have already happened, and its last entry repeats. Each count-table entry is {type record, u32 count, u32 expiry in ms, stat-variable link}. The live table holds one entry per type, in record order. Starting a struggle adds 1 (0x17B2858 - 0xCB03A0), sets the expiry to now + ResetCooldown x 1000 on the engine's millisecond clock ( [[0x2702598]+0x8]+0x18 ) and mirrors the count into the type's stat. Reading an expired count zeroes it (0xCAF140). Entering a state with a fail condition resets every type marked ResetCountOnDeath (0x6EF838). Success / Perfect / Fail apply ResetCountOnPerfect and ResetCountOnLose (0x74B130), and the combat action ResetStruggleCount 0xF16840 resets one type.

- From a paired animation, a struggle starts through 0xFB268 - 0x6EF978 - 0x6EF9DC. From a combat state, it starts through the state change 0x2C14C8 - 0x6EF838 - 0x6EF908 - 0x6F0000, which requires the state machine's +0x58 to equal the state being entered and the state's timer to be running (0x6F03CC takes the largest remaining time over the 0x20-byte timer entries at [state machine+0x00] , skipping paused ones). +0x58 of the state machine is therefore the current state. - 0x6EF9DC orders source and target by TargetStruggle , shows the option's HUD prompt, allows Perfect only if the player owns the sync's required item, and then builds one object per input kind. The objects are QuickTime 0x18421C0 (0x170 bytes, vt 0x1F76D28), Aim 0x1842120 (0x180, vt 0x1F76C80), PressCount 0x1842198 (0x178, vt 0x1F76C28), Hold 0x1842148 (0x1B8, vt 0x1F76CF0), InputDirection 0x1842170 (0x150, vt 0x1F76D60) and Ring 0x18421E8 (0x198, vt 0x1F76CB8), all on the base constructor 0x1842490 with seven virtual slots (0 destructor, 1 update, 2 finish with a result, 4 done, 5 kind-specific start). - The common start 0x1845C94 stores the player, source and target handles ( +0x08 / +0x30 / +0x58 , pointers at +0x28 / +0x50 / +0x78 ), the struggle record ( +0x80 ), the input window ( +0xF0 / +0xF4 ), the result ( +0xFC ), the type's four presentation events ( +0x100 to +0x118 ), Perfect allowed ( +0x138 ) and can lose ( +0x139 ). It then applies the command set, starts the camera presentation on the player's presentation component ( [player+0x2FC0] , 0x17A505C) and attaches the widget to the configured bone. The input window is animation data. 0x184340C reads the events BSW and ESW (0x227C894 / 0x227C898) from both participants' paired clips (0x1847248) and keeps the earliest start and the latest end; without them the struggle ends at once. The struggle's clock (0x18431E4) is the playback time of the source's paired clip (0x1143C0), so slow motion and animation rate stretch the window with the scene.

Every frame 0x162560 ticks both slots (0x6EFF54, 0x6EFF9C): update, then done, then the result 0x184531C. A Fail is reported as Success when the struggle's can-lose byte is 0 or the static byte 0x2671491 is 0 (it is 1 in the executable and live, and no code writes it). - After a paired animation, Fail plays StruggleLoseSync , Success StruggleWinSync and Perfect StrugglePerfectSync (falling back to the win sync). The matching audio key plays (Perfect falls back to Win), the next paired animation starts through 0x19D96B8, and then the script event CCharacter.OnCombatStruggleEnd (its P919 hash stored at 0x272911C by 0x42E6490) fires with won and perfect flags. - After a combat state, Success and Perfect clear the state (0x19D2834 with no state). - The common finish 0x1847188 plays the type's OnFail / OnSuccess / OnPerfect presentation event with the struggle's camera type. Button mash (PressCount). The phase byte +0x16E steps through waiting, window open at BSW , counting, timed out and done. The required button ( +0x168 ) is a weighted random pick over the struggle's input list (0x18451F4). Each right press increments +0x16D , and reaching +0x16C wins (0x1846B38). A wrong press fails when FailOnIncorrectInput is set, and passing ESW fails. Both counters are single bytes (the start stores NumPressesForWin with mov [obj+0x16C], al at 0x6B11216 and the input compares bytes at 0x1846B78), so the value is taken modulo 256: the "impossible" goblin mash with 999999 presses needs 63. Last Chance ring (Ring). The start (0x6B12660) moves the effective end of the window earlier by Interface/Shared.LastChanceInputLagBuffer (ms, +0xF8 ), evaluates the three ring scales against the player's stats and converts them to alpha references: perfect +0x170 = 0.025 x (1 - 0.2 x P / 50) + 0.0075, win +0x174 = 0.85 + 0.2 x (1 - 0.5 x W / 100) and moving ring +0x178 = 0.05 + 0.45 x (1 - M / 1500). It also stores +0x184 = 1 - Lose / 100, +0x188 FailTimeStart, +0x18C failure allowed (AllowFailure and 0x2671491) and +0x138 CanGetPerfect. The update 0x1848304 opens the window at BSW and starts the struggle's slow-motion record. At the shortened end it enters the failing phase when failure is allowed, and it resolves Fail at ESW . When failure is not allowed, 0x1847B20 instead saves the source's animation rate ( [combat object+0x260]+0xB0 ) and sets it to 0, so the paired animation, and with it the struggle clock, holds until the player presses; resolving (0x18473D8) restores it, ends the slow motion and plays the cursor effect.

What a hit does to its target and its attacker is a Combat/Category record. There are 2,559 of them, with 412 Combat/Category/Lists that group them for the category predicates (see the predicate table above). By name, 1,009 are the player's ( PC ), 755 the AI's ( AI ), 98 and 87 belong to the two story-DLC heroes ( PLBar , PLBoG ), and the rest cover the Wraith, dominations, resurrections, environment ignitions and kill cameras. Each record has 49 fields; the table gives how many of the 2,559 set each: Field Set on Typical values Read by --- --- --- --- ResurrectionSettings 1,013 Faction/Resurrection Resurrection PlayerArrow 245, PlayerSlash 130, Generic 124 0x77EDA8 (console ValidateResurrection , 0x77EBB8) Threat 803 Combat/Threat PC Ranged 393, PC Base 213, AI Base 155 0x644CA0 AppliedState 475 Combat/States/AppliedState (for example KD 100PCT ShortDur , PC AltFire Stun and PC Ranged Burn ) 0x2DE270 IncreaseStats 351 stat ids (18 on 229) HitFX 341 Combat/FX Hit Medium 86, Hit Large 36 0x666BE8 (0x6662A8) ExplicitHitFX / ExplicitCritHitFX / ExplicitBlockHitFX 296 / 194 / 191 Combat/FX/HitFX records HitFXOnBCOL 173 Hit BloodDecal 172 ApplyBuffListOnHit 152 Combat/Buffs/BuffLists ( PC KillStealPrevention 53, Poison BaleFire 15) 0x2EF724 (0x2EE394) PredicateHitCounterRange 117 HC High / HC Medium / HC Low ResourceGainOnStart / ResourceGainOnHit 112 / 82 Combat/ResourceGain lists 0x2DB030 (0x2DAC84) MoraleModifierTarget 68 AI/Morale/Modifiers (for example Player HOG and Player Wraith Flee ) 0x65E84C (0x2EE394) FireData 58 Fire/IgnitionTypes (for example FlameArrow and Explosion Freeze ) 0x4EB26C (0x4EA0A4, the area-effect code) ClearAllCombatState / ...OnStart 43 / 50 true ThreatInverted 34 threat reductions AppliedStateSelf 29 states applied to the attacker StateOverride 27 Combat/States/Definitions (for example WraithPinned L and WraithStunned ) 0x65387C PredicateHasItem 22 Inventory/Items (for example FlamingWeapon ) RagdollReaction 11 Combat/RagdollReaction (for example Bip Reaction Death Generic ) 0x65E990 (0x2F8460, the dead-body path) DamageData / DamageSelfData 8 / 9 Combat/Damage (for example KillSelf ) ExitNavMesh 6 Combat/ExitNavMesh ForceRecognitionWithThreat (2,151), ApplyStateOverrideAtStart (2,556), ClearAllCombatStateClearPrevious (2,546), ClearAllTargetCombatStateClearPrevious (2,556) and EnablePresentations (2,553) are set almost everywhere. Six fields are set on no record ( PredicateEnergyLevel , NonLocalScreenShakeFX , ClearCooldownTargetOnStart , AddItems , RemoveItems and AddItemsOnBrand ), although the code reads at least four of them (accessors 0x2DDFAC, 0x666C58, 0x2DEC50, 0x2CAB30): they are supported but never used.

- Do the player's buffs time out on his own clock? A 5 s buff lasted 9.6 - 9.7 s under a slow motion that halved his clock. - Does holder+0x1E5 mark a sheathed weapon? The charge player 0x44F5A8 picks FXSequenceSheathed when 0x1154918 reads it set, and it is a different object from the parts' +0x1E5 . Which clips send ENABLEWEAPONFX / DISABLEWEAPONFX ? - What do the other direct callers of ApplyDamageInternal do (0x19B39E4, 0x643058, 0x2E0520, 0x15B444, 0x106D04, 0x42B290)? How is fall damage applied, and what are the regeneration bands at +0x120 / +0x180 ? - What sets a cached formula entry's dirty bytes ( +0x08 / +0x09 )? Does a capture node's +0x590 always equal MaximumAmount , and does the engine set the IsPlayerFollower stat on live followers? - What does the combat state machine's +0x60 hold next to the current state at +0x58 ? - What do the fight circle's +0x188 / +0x190 pointers hold? - How is the Last Chance press judged? The open parts are the ring's input listener (vt 0x1F76BE0 slot 1 - 0x1846974) and where LastChanceRingForgivenessBuffer (read by 0x18434A8) enters the comparison. - What is the update logic of the Aim, Hold, InputDirection and QuickTime struggles? - Which records use the 32 pools that no shipped paired animation references (the BH3 sequence, warg and troll domination, the pinned-state mash and several boss pre-deaths): a later database layer, quest scripts, or the combat-state path? - What does 0x6A3BE4 contribute on a Fail? It plays the current attack's presentation event on the player's presentation component.

t: Items: inventory, gear, affixes, gems and skills

x: The player's inventory lives in the visual component: vc = [[base+0x2797808]+0x2348] (vt 0x1FD63F0; the same object the Skills screen uses, [UIManager+0xB0] ). The inventory proper is embedded at vc+0x3D8 ; 25 slot vectors sit at vc+0x4D0 + i 0x18 : Slot Content --- --- 0 Melee (sword) 1 MeleeAux (dagger) 2 Ranged (bow) 3 RangedAux 6 Utility 7 Tribe 9 MeleeOffHand 11 / 12 / 22 cloak, armor, ring (by their contents) The slot names are Combat/Predicates/InventorySlot . Index 0 of a slot vector is not the equipped item. The equipped items are named by the equip array vc+0x38 + slot 0x28 (14 of 14 equipped items read). For the weapon slots 0, 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7, the entry is a holder (vt 0x1DB1F68) whose +0x140 is the item. For the cloak (11), armor (12), Isildur's ring (13), hands (14), scabbards (16, 17), hair (19) and ring (22), the entry is the item itself. An item is equipped when the array names it and its equipped byte +0xA9 is 1; the byte alone can lag a change. - Owned counts : vc+0x740 / +0x748 , records {+0x00 item, +0x20 u32 count} (714 stacks on a finished save). Count 0x509074, consume 0x4F163C(vc, item, n), give 0x1BCE0C0(vc, item); the general give is 0x1C01E0(vc, item, n). vc+0x3D8+0xF0 is an append-only change log, not the counts. - Held test 0x24DF7C(vc, item): bit recordIndex(item) (0x1898E8) of the held bit set [vc+0x490] (0x24EB74); without a bit set it walks the stacks (0x36A17C). It has 102 callers (combat, quests, skills). The item instance (vt 0x1FDABF8): Offset Meaning --- --- +0x20 u32 id +0x24 u32 level +0x2C u32 slot / holder index (copied from the equipped-weapon data by 0x1BF3750 / 0x1BF3474 / 0x649790) +0x38 the Inventory/Items record +0x40 the Inventory/EquippedWeaponData record (a weapon's look) +0x48 the Inventory/ArmorData record (an armor's design) +0x60 socket objects (a per-item path no shipped item uses) +0x78 affix instances {+0x00 Affix/Definition, +0x08 f32 value, +0x0C f32 bonus from ModifyOtherAffix} +0x88 / +0x8C the ability list's capacity / owned byte +0xA8 / +0xA9 new / equipped +0xB0 nemesis origin +0xB8 the upgrade challenge (vt 0x1DC0F70; +0x78 progress / target, the card's "5 / 10") +0xC8 GUID The item destructor (0x1C7DB4 - 0x114D828) always frees the ability objects and frees the list's buffer only when the owned byte is set. Captain traits that carry items are items of the same class. Function Address --- --- AddItemToInventory(vc, record, quantity, prebuilt, duplicate, notify, &out, 0) / add a count 0x1C1224 / 0x1C01E0 item constructor / destructor; build (data, record, builder, level, rng) 0x1C7CCC / 0x1C7DB4; 0x11565A4 - 0x649790 add an ability (item, definition) ; re-roll; append 0xFB98A0; 0x64A9C8; 0x64A018 validated equip (vc, item) 0x1BCA298 re-skin (item, look, design, combat, equipped) ; the loot component's vf3 (armor 0x3FFDF8 - 0x4C5CC0, weapon 0x715D24 - 0x3FD228) 0x645890; 0x40000C add a buff (combat, buff, source, 0) / remove one (combat, buff) 0x36A35C / 0x6DEAC4 register / unregister a proc (from the affix apply 0xFE68F0) 0x7A2AF0 / 0x7A2900 an affix's Desc accessor 0x1913734 - GetStringFast 0x1CB3B0 apply / remove mod sets (combat, mods, 1) 0x69B8A0 / 0x69B6F4 attach / detach / read an item context (vt 0x1F65BE0) 0x1769EE8 / 0x176A1A0 / 0x2B287C add to / subtract from a chance (store, ChanceType, f32) 0x1A2B314 / 0x1A2B654 - Unique items. Items.MaxQuantity is 1 on 63 of the 340 records the player's gear uses; the engine refuses a second copy of such an item. - The nemesis origin ( +0xB0 ) names a legendary after the captain it came from: a 0x20-byte block (allocated by 0x1BF1D74 - 0x1C019F8) of +0x00 the Faction/Loot/NemesisGear record, +0x08 the Faction/Loot/NemesisGearDescription , +0x10 the captain's role ( Faction/Roles/Definitions ), +0x18 u32 the name hash (the P919 of an OrcNameGen1st NNN key) and +0x1C u32 the rarity hash. The display name 0xD062C0(item, buffer, flag) formats the design's ItemName (from the look at +0x40 , else the armor design at +0x48 ) with arguments from the origin; without an origin a legendary's key prints its placeholder ("Blood Sword ({1!ls})"). In one save 43 of 71 pieces carried an origin. - A look is read at equip. Writing an equipped armor's design ( +0x48 ) in place does not redraw it, and the item can then no longer be selected; with the item off, the same write takes effect when it is equipped again. The in-place re-skin 0x645890 is meant for an item that is its slot's only one. - Removing a buff removes one instance. 0x6DEAC4 takes the first instance of that record in the combat object's buff list [combat+0x1A0] (0x45050C), then compacts the list (0x36B7A0).

A weapon has no stats of its own: Inventory/WeaponData holds only sheath, effects and predicates. Every number on gear is an affix ( Inventory/Affix/Definition , 2,961 records). An affix's value is FloatIndex.IndexedValues[ItemLevel - 1] of its VariableMin table (10 of 10 checked live). A sword's "Melee Attack" is the affix 1Sword Base Prop <rarity or set - Float DmgMod M FLAT (level 80: Common 160, Epic 166, Legendary 169); the player's own Float DmgBase M BASE is 0, so the sword's roll is the whole flat input to the player's melee damage formula ( DmgForm Plyr Melee ). Equipping adds deltas. 0x40136C(item, apply, owner combat object) calls 0xFE68F0 per affix - 0x1A105D8(store, variable, +/- (value + bonus)). Unequipping subtracts the current values, so an affix value changed while the item is equipped leaves the stat table out of step. The engine's own upgrade (0xFBAAC0, at 0xFBB2EC: strip, level = min(owner level + 1, 80) , recompute) removes, changes and re-applies. The validated equip 0x1BCA298 (equipping another item, or nothing, in the slot) removes every delta the engine's equip paths applied, and equipping the changed item the same way applies them again. Loading a save rebuilds the stat and chance tables from the worn gear. The player's stat table is [[[player+0x26A8]+0x318]+0x60] + recordIndex 0x50 = {variable record, +0x08 f32 value} , 622 entries (the Combat/Stat/Variable/Float category; lookup 0x1E53B8). A level-indexed value table clamps an index past its end to its last entry (0x64AA40); the tables end at 91 to 94 entries. Card text. An ability's line on the item card is its affix's Desc key, formatted with the value ( {1!.0f} ); the token {M} draws the Mirian icon. The 809 abilities a player item can carry print only 525 distinct lines: 70 lines repeat over 354 records. In 58 of those 70 every copy writes the same stat, buff or proc, one copy per rarity and set (sword base damage at level 80: 159 common, 163 rare, 166 epic, 169 on every legendary set); in the other 12 the copies differ. Gem lines are worded by the socket ("Weapon: ...% increased damage" is melee damage on a sword gem, stealth damage on a dagger gem and ranged damage on a bow gem). One shipped line is wrong: 4Shield 2Common FollowerHPMod shows the sword's "{1} Melee Damage" text, while its only effect is VariableMod Mod FollowerMaxHP . The abilities include 34 set bonuses ( LegendarySet <Set Affix1 / Affix2 , at 2 and 4 pieces) and 299 NemesisAffix rewards. A save keeps identity, not numbers : id, level, the item, look and affix hashes, the GUID and the nemesis origin; computed values (such as 157.0 or 169.0) occur nowhere in the decrypted save. See Saves, the store and the network layer, for the inventory section's layout.

GemData.SocketAffixes gives one affix per socket type (red on a sword Float DmgMod M PCT 0.10 - 0.30, green life steal 0.04 - 0.20, white Mirian 0.05 - 0.15, blade critical damage 0.20 - 1.00). Sockets belong to slots, not items. Six live socket objects (vt 0x1FDAED0) sit at [vc+0x3D8+0x80] = {entries, 8} , each entry {GemSocketType, socket } ; a socket holds +0x18 the gem, +0x20 the type and +0x28 its affix vector. Constructor 0x1BFB8AC(memory, type, gem), SocketGem 0x1BFBCB8, apply 0x1BFBC50(socket, 0 / 1, owner, GemItemLevel) over the socket's affix vector.

The player's combat accepts a held item only if the Combat/Predicates/Item lists name it: PC Sword (73 items), PC SwordOrDagger , PC ActivateEquip (378), PC Sword Or GroundGlaive , PC SwordOrDaggerOrGroundGlaive and Trait ItemBreaker IgnoreSwordList . An item on none of these lists renders and equips, but no attack, combo or dodge starts with it. Items.WeaponType is null on every player sword and is not the gate for the player.

A skill row is an Inventory/ActiveItemGroup record (89): Entries[] - StructuresInventoryActiveItemGroupEntry {RequiredItem = the variant's unlock item (held = bought), ActiveItem[] = the SKILL / DUMMY items whose possession makes it active} . An unlock finds its row through Inventory/Items.ActiveItemGroup . These fields have exactly two readers: - The Skills screen's active test 0x1BCD6DC(inventory, unlock): unlock held - its row - the first entry with RequiredItem == unlock - its ActiveItem[0] held. The node state 0x18A1770: 3 active (drawn white), 2 owned, 1 available, 0 locked; the effect pickers 0x19453D0 and 0x19480D4 ask the same test. - The click swap 0x1BC8C94(vc, unlock) (wrapper 0x1BC8C6C(vc, Skills record)): entries with another RequiredItem lose their active items, entries with this one gain theirs (inventory events at GM+0x6D18 , types 8 and 7). Other callers: the loadout apply 0x1BCC1C4 (from the inventory re-init 0x4F0938), 0x17D9E4C and 0x1B56FA4. Which move a button runs. The node runner 0x30FD80 tries the current node's links, then the root list of the tree at comp+0xEF0 in order; each root is resolved to its keyboard variant, validated (0x310C5C: type, cancel condition, transition; 0x310F10: the input) and PickAttack 0x275730 runs; the first root that yields an attack wins. An attack's priority (attack cache entry +0x0C ) ranks attacks only inside one node. A skill variant whose moves sit in their own earlier root node therefore hides the later nodes on the same input: of 49 multi-variant rows, only Quick Throw does this (Rapid Throw, root 107, before the shared node, root 108). A multi-projectile volley is one data link : AttackData.Multishoot - Combat/Multishoot (one projectile per Entries wedge; FanOfKnives = 5), read at every shot by 0x2E8994 (0x6F6510; ProjectileCluster wins when set). HUD button prompts : Combat/PromptOverride/Setup - Override (one per button, CommandID ) - Prompts[] ; the evaluator 0x277650 reads the compiled entry: +0xE8 IncludedItem (any of, 0x276E1C), +0xF0 IncludedItemAll (all of, 0x6E42A4), +0xF8 ExcludedItem. The link is copied at load (0x1C0DAE8); the list is walked live. StructuresQuestPredicates.RequiredInventoryItemAll is the only other all-of item field.

An orc's weapons are items in its inventory ( FM+0x050 ): the held weapon at inventory+0x38 (item) and +0x40 (look), the thrown weapon through FM+0x060 . The weapon's type is the item's Inventory/Items.WeaponType ; the look ( EquippedWeaponData ) decides only the model. - The look's slot. EquippedWeaponData.ItemSlot is the inventory slot a look belongs to: 0 Melee (581 looks), 1 MeleeAux (407), 2 Ranged (697), 3 RangedAux (8: the olog arquebus, flamethrower and harpoon), 6 Utility (34: every Orc Misc prop, drawn in the hand), 7 Tribe (15: exactly the Orc Trb / Orc TrbVis looks), out of 1,763. The game always pairs items and looks of the same slot (813 of 813 orc weapons in one census). A tribe weapon is drawn only while a tribal attack draws slot 7. - Where it is drawn and where it rests. EquippedWeaponData.Model - StructuresInventoryItemModel ActiveNode / InactiveNode : every weapon a class holds is drawn in RightHand and rests in a sheath socket (spears Socket Sheath Spr , archer crossbows Sheath Archer , defenders Socket Sheath Def01 , berserkers Ber R sheath , infantry and ologs L sheath ). Throwables are LeftHand with no rest socket: they exist only during the throw. Sauron's and the Nazgul's hand weapons rest nowhere. - Classes. Combat/InventorySetup::Orc Spearman gives one weapon, Orc 1HR ThrowingSpear , in the ranged slot: the spear is both the throw and the melee weapon, so spearmen have an empty hand slot. Berserker dual wielding is in the look: looks with an X2 suffix draw a model in each hand. - Every orc weapon look resolves the same way ( EquippedWeaponData.Model - StructuresInventoryItemModel.Models - StructuresInventoryModel.ModelRecord - a Model ); see Characters for holders and how a drawn weapon is rebuilt.

A legendary gear effect is data wiring around an affix: Inventory/Affix/Definition .Buff - Combat/Buffs a held effect .Proc - Combat/Buffs/Procs/Definitions (223) an on-event effect .Chance - Combat/Buffs/ChanceTypes a bare tag (the key) .ChanceValue - Combat/Stat/Variable/FloatIndex "1" = 100% Combat/Buffs/Procs/Definitions: Chance, Predicate, ResourceGain, Buff, MustBeDispatchSource, MustBeDispatchTarget, AllowDuplicateProcs, TargetBuff, TargetAppliedState, RandomStatusEffect Predicate - Quest/AutoObjectives (the quest event vocabulary: PlayerHit Sword, PlayerKill AnyKill ...) TargetBuff - Combat/Buffs .OneTimeAOE / .LoopingAOE / .OneTimeAOE Player / .DeathAOE - Combat/AOE - .Tick - Combat/AOE/Tick (Radius, Angle, MaxAIToHit, Attack, AOEFX) Base Prop affixes are always on ( SetProp affixes need the set's pieces). Across the 752 area ticks the radius ranges from 0 to 1,000,000 (median 550; 20,000 is the shipped "whole arena" value). Combat/AOE.Alignment decides who is damaged ( DamageAll includes followers). How an area ticks. Combat/AOE.Tick is a list of 1 to 8 Combat/AOE/Tick records (1 on 344 of 627 areas, 2 on 132, up to 8 on 7), fired in order: the tick loop 0x4E9D28 keeps the next one's index at +0x18C and stops after the last. It fires when the area's tick timer ( +0x150 , {clock, u32 end in ms} ) has expired and re-arms it with TickDelay seconds (0x4EA90C: end = now + seconds x 1000); a timer without a clock counts as expired (0x4E9E98). The area's creation (0x15B994, "%s created AOE: %s") leaves the tick timer unarmed, so the first tick fires on the area's first update, and arms only the length timer +0x178 , with MaxAOELength when that is above its threshold.
