Timer is an integer (1 on 583 areas, 2 on 41, 3 on 2, 4 on 1), not a duration.

The affix apply 0xFE68F0 hands an affix's Proc to the register function 0x7A2AF0 on equip (0x7A2900 on unequip). Procs live in one global dispatcher, [base+0x26FFB70]+0xE8 : 30 vectors of 0x18 bytes, one per DispatchPredicate.Type of the proc's trigger (0xE96DE0; a type of 30 or more is not registered). An entry is 0x48 bytes (built by 0x7A2A40 / 0x7A2A78): Offset Meaning --- --- +0x20 the owner (the player's combat object) +0x28 the proc +0x30 the proc's Chance key, copied at equip +0x38 the proc's Predicate , copied at equip +0x40 a count: a duplicate raises it unless AllowDuplicateProcs is set +0x44 - +0x47 the dispatch source / target flags Registration is skipped while [owner+0x30] is set. A later change to a proc's Chance or Predicate is therefore not seen until the item is equipped again, whereas its action fields ( Buff , TargetBuff , TargetAppliedState , ResourceGain ) are read each time it fires (0x714948). Of the 223 shipped procs, 221 use a Predicate (215 of them from Quest/AutoObjectives , 6 from Combat/Buffs/Procs/Predicates ), 131 a ResourceGain , 60 a Buff , 37 a Chance , 26 a TargetBuff , 10 a RandomStatusEffect list and 8 a TargetAppliedState , such as OnFire MedDur . The resource a Combat/ResourceGain record restores is set by its ResourceType : 1 Focus, 2 elf-shot, 8 Might, 9 mount stamina and 10 Wrath, with no type meaning health. Nothing hands out 13 of the 223 procs, three of them complete ( ProcDef AoEFreeze Execute , ProcDef PoisonAoE BrutalStealthKill and ProcDef ConvertBeasts WhileMounted ). Combat/Buffs/ChanceTypes records have no fields. Every firing adds a buff instance. A proc's Buff lands on the player as a new instance each time the proc fires, and its ActionsOnApply runs again. A buff whose StatDuration is empty never expires, so such instances accumulate. Shipped buffs without a duration include AoEFreeze , AOE MoraleBomb Small and PLBar StunAoE OnLowHealth . ConsumeWholeChargeMeter is true on 1,125 of the 1,126 Combat/Buffs records: it is a default and says nothing about a particular buff. Summons. A buff summons through ActionsOnApply - Combat/Actions/NPCSummon , as DLC4 SummonSpider OnStealthKill does; otherwise the 50 summon actions are run by attacks ( ActionsOnAttackStart Source ). A summon action names a Combat/NPCSummon record {AISpawnType, Count, SummonData, DeferredCooldown} , and its SummonData decides the side and the lifetime. With Alignment set to BuddyFollower or BuddyFollower Beast , the summoned characters fight for the player; with MatchSummonerPlayerFollower , they take the summoner's side. A RemovalRecord ( AmbShort R , AmbLong R ) removes them; without one they stay. Of the 58 Combat/SummonData records, Hammerhand Summon Goblins summons 8 ghuls on the enemy side ( Orc FactionA ) with no removal. The game caps its own summoning buffs within the buff itself. DLC4 SummonGhul OnStealthKill and Spider last 1 s, summon on apply, and carry a one-time area ( PLBar Kill ExcessSummonedGhuls / Spiders ). The area's first tick marks up to 4 ghuls or 6 spiders ( MaxAIToHit ) and its second kills the rest; both ticks hit only allies that carry Buddy Summoned . A summon action's DeferredCooldown does not limit repeated firings.

The player's chance table is [[combat+0x320]+0x228] : entries of 0x10 bytes {record, f32} and a u32 count at +0x230 , indexed by Combat/Buffs/ChanceTypes record index and built on the first addition (flag store+0x240 ). A roll passes when the chance is greater than a uniform random number in [0, 1). The adder 0x1A2B314 builds the table when needed and adds; the subtracter 0x1A2B654 subtracts with no clamp and does not build the table, and its lookup asserts ("Bad record index") on a table not yet built or on a record of another category. A buff's chance modifier ( StructuresCombatBuffChanceMod {ChanceType, AdditiveReward} ) is added when the buff is applied (0x4543C0) and subtracted when it is removed (0x454ABC). Seven keys roll on the player's attacks with no ability at all: C PC ApplyFire (528 sword attacks, through PC ApplyStatusEffect Fire WeaponKindRequired ), C PC ApplyFreeze (529), C PC ApplyFireExecute (74), C Machine ExplodeOnGlaiveHit (40 held glaive swings), C HeadExp (14 flurry kills), C BrutalK 3xMorale (80) and C Blast HeadExp (80 chain attacks). The dagger and bow have their own: C PC ApplyFireDagger (158), C PC ApplyFreezeDagger (159), C PC ApplyFireHeadshot and C ApplyFreeze CriticalHitRanged (on 58 elemental-arrow attacks), and C Celebrimbor Headshot FreezeAoE (on 10 heavy headshots). Keys such as C BowCrit HeadExp , C PinOlogs , C MarkExecute HeadExp and C Terror Headshot HeadExplode sit on bow item data and reach no attack without an ability of their own. Of the 78 keys, 11 have no holder in the shipped data. Elements by weapon: Weapon Fire Frost Poison Curse --- --- --- --- --- Sword key C PC ApplyFire key C PC ApplyFreeze buff Poison Weapon buff Curse Weapon Dagger key C PC ApplyFireDagger key C PC ApplyFreezeDagger buff Equip 2Dagger L ApplyPoisonOnStealthHit buff Equip 2Dagger L ApplyCurseOnStealthHit Bow key C PC ApplyFireHeadshot key C ApplyFreeze CriticalHitRanged buff Equip 3Bow ApplyPoisonOnCriticalHit + stat C ApplyPoison Ranged buff Equip 3Bow ApplyCurseOnCriticalHit + stat C ApplyCurse Ranged The player's fire and frost categories carry no item gate (the orcs' gate on PredicateHasItem FlamingWeapon , CursedWeapon or PoisonedWeapon ). Flame Weapon is a chance bonus of +1.0 on C PC ApplyFire ( Frost Weapon the same on C PC ApplyFreeze ). The sword's own poisoned and cursed states hang off a category nothing holds, so poison and curse on the sword need the buff.

An affix's Buff and Proc are read only when its item is equipped or a gem is socketed. The field bindings list three readers, all on those paths: - 0x40136C (log tag [COMBAT BUFF] ), called from the equip paths 0x4010D8 and 0x1BF2ED8, which reads the affix through 0x1BFBC50 and also applies the item's ActiveBuffData , ActiveVariableMod , ActiveMaterialOverrides and AppearanceTagsOnEquip ; - the gem-socketing path 0x1BFBCB8; - 0x1C7FCD8, reached from the same equip path (0x4010D8 - 0x1C68B58 - 0x1C7FC04). A change to an affix's Buff or Proc record therefore takes effect at the next equip, not at the next event.

- What the integer Combat/AOE.Timer controls (1 to 4; its relation to the length of the Tick list varies: equal on 337 areas, smaller on 271, larger on 19), and whether an area whose TickDelay is longer than its MaxAOELength gets past its first tick. - What the four records of the inventory's last slot entries are on a finished save (ids one above the highest item). - What reads Float Temp ForUnimplemented , the only variable the weapon life-steal and Mirian gems write (21 cell references against the 20 abilities that write it). - Whether code reads Equip Has 1Sword FireWeapon by name: Flame Weapon 's flag feeds it, and no record names it.

t: The Nemesis system: factions, captains and the army
x: Every named orc, olog and story character is a FactionMember owned by the faction system, seated in an army's rows, and changed by faction events that the engine applies to it. The hierarchy, the promotions, the returns from death and the ambushes are data: rows, events and reward lists in the Faction/ categories of the GameDB, driven by a small set of engine functions. Traits, classes and personalities are covered in Captain traits, classes and personalities; story characters, betrayal scenes and region ownership in Quests, story and scenes; looks in Captain appearance; scars in Captain scars and the return from death; imported Shadow of Mordor captains in The Nemesis Forge; and the save format in Saves, the store and the network layer.

The faction system is FS = [GM+0x6C68] ( [[base+0x26FFAA8]+0x6C68] ; see Engine core). The scene tick calls 0x1E2BC4 on it every frame (see Threads and the frame), and through 0x1E2A58 that call also runs the ambush update 0x6DDBA8. Offset Meaning --- --- +0x30 the ambush manager (below) +0x68 the pools: one 0xC0-byte entry per Faction/Pool record +0x70 u32 the pool count (9) +0x80 / +0x88 army - pool : 16-byte entries {Faction/Definition record, its pool object} , count 38 (in a loaded campaign: 10 armies use the DLC3 pool, 9 QuestReplay, 8 MainGame, 6 InvasionGame, 2 DLC4, 1 each Player, Demo and QuestReplay Ratbag2) +0x98 the army contexts: a map {+0x00 entries, +0x08 u32 count (38), +0x10 the Faction/Definition category} +0xB0 / +0xB8 role use : 16-byte entries {Faction/Roles/Definitions record, u32 counter, f32 the role's WeightReductionPerUse} , count 914; the counter reached 740 in a late campaign whose turn counter read 712, so it is not the turn of last use +0xC8 / +0xD0 names in use : 32-byte entries {Faction/NameTable record, vector of u32 name ids (begin, end), u32 capacity, u32} , count 4 (Orc, Olog, Forthog, Easterling); in a loaded campaign 80 of the 80 Orc ids and 29 of the 30 Olog ids were held by current members +0xE0 the trait flag table (see Captain traits) +0xE8 u32 the trait flag table's count: 493, one 16-byte entry per Faction/Traits/Picker record +0xF8 / +0x100 32-byte entries {Faction/Traits/PickerLevelRemap record, vector of u32 pairs, u32 capacity, u32} , count 5 ( TraitLevelOffset 0 , -1 , -2 , +1 , +2 ): each record's remap table, decoded +0x128 / +0x130 scar use : 24-byte entries {Combat/Scar/Type record, the record again, f32 current weight, u32 times given} , count 24; the weight is the record's WeightPerUse list at the use count ( Curse , given 44 times: 0.0001, the last of 1000, 10, 1, 0.01, 0.0001) +0x1B0 the current region (a Regions/Region record) +0x1B8 the current region's army (a Faction/Definition record) +0x1F0 events queued while another is being processed; +0x208 is the busy flag +0x218 u16 the turn counter (below) +0x21C the world's running total of resurrections: incremented with the member's FM+0x500 at every cheat-death mark, and read when the odds table is chosen (see Cheat death and the return, below) Each of the per-record tables above opens with {entries, u32 count, u32 hash, the category} .

Members live in pools, one per game mode, not per region: the MainGame pool holds every captain of every region. A pool entry's first qword is its Faction/Pool record. The pool object starts at entry+8 (vt 0x1FD8310) and holds its member vector at +0x18 / +0x20 ; FM+0x174 is the member's index in that vector (500 of 500 members). The entries follow the Faction/Pool record order (9 of 9: Player, QuestReplay, QuestReplay Ratbag2, InvasionGame, Test, Demo, DLC3, DLC4, MainGame), so MainGame is entry 8. Entry+0xB0 repeats the record, and entry+0xB8 holds its MaxMembersToTrack (9 of 9). Pool MaxMembersToTrack Serialize NemesisCanComeFromThisPool --- --- --- --- Player 32 False False QuestReplay 50 True False QuestReplay Ratbag2 75 True False InvasionGame 250 True False Test 32 False False Demo 64 True False DLC3 450 True False DLC4 250 True False MainGame 500 True True The MainGame record also carries importance coefficients ( ImpC XPLevel 1.5, ImpC RowRank , ImpC Role , ImpC ISTotal 1.0). A new member comes from 0x1BD2E20 (reached through 0x1C23C10), which builds the object with 0x19ED468. When the pool is full, it recycles its least important member, but never one with a row ( +0x268 ), a preset ( +0x190 ), a current sim event ( +0x4F0 ), a unique builder instance ( +0x350 ) or flag bit 45. A late campaign's MainGame pool sits at its 500 cap. In one such save, the recyclable members were 201 dead former followers and 48 unassigned grunts, and no living follower.

An army is a Faction/Definition record. The game ships 38, and every one has a context in every game mode. The context map at FS+0x98 is indexed by the definition's record index: entry+0 is the record and the context is entry+8 (vt 0x1FDDF78, 0x290 bytes per entry). 0x18DE04(map, record) returns it and asserts "Bad record index" when the record belongs to another category. The faction system's initialization 0xF64CA0 runs at every load (through the save chunk vt 0x1F6F1C8, slots 12 and 13) and builds the army-to-pool table FS+0x80 from each army's Pool cell. Kind Armies Pool --- --- --- Campaign Faction MinasIthil , Faction MtnPass , Faction island , Faction volcano , Faction snowMtn , Faction desert Real MainGame Unused twin Faction desert (same row records as Faction desert Real , FillFactionOnInitialization False) MainGame Quest replays 10 Faction <region QuestReplay QuestReplay (QuestReplay Ratbag2 for RB2 ) Online invasions 6 InvasionFaction InvasionGame Blade of Galadriel 5 Faction <region DLC3 , 5 Real Faction <region DLC3 DLC3 Desolation of Mordor Faction desert DLC4 , Faction desert mercs DLC4 DLC4 Other Faction Demovolcano (Demo), Faction Player (Player, one 32-seat row player created ), Faction None A region's army is its Regions/Region.Faction : Region record Region Army --- --- --- MinasIthil Minas Ithil Faction MinasIthil MtnPass Cirith Ungol Faction MtnPass island Nurnen Faction island volcano Gorgoroth Faction volcano snowMtn Seregost Faction snowMtn desert Lithlad Faction desert Real Each region also names an InvasionFaction , and Gorgoroth a DEMOFaction ( Faction Demovolcano ). The region-to-army lookup 0x1E4418 first reads Regions/Region.GameModeFactionOverrides ( StructuresRegionGameModeFaction , keyed by the current game mode), then Region.Faction . The region desert mercs names no army in its Faction field. Its override maps it to the mercenary army in the Desolation of Mordor mode, so the lookup returns null for it in any other mode. Because twins share row records, a row name does not identify the live army: the live army is the one a seated member's FM+0x178 names. The definition decides how an army is built and run: Faction/Definition field Meaning --- --- Pool , RequiredSaveSlot the pool it draws from; the save slot ( Faction/SaveSlot : MainGame, DLC3, DLC4) it belongs to; army initialization skips the fill of an army whose slot is not the current one Rows its rows, in order (an array: 6 in five regions, 5 in Minas Ithil, 3 in the mercenary army) EventSetup its event switchboard (below) PresetMembers , QuestOnlyPresetMembers story characters built at army initialization, and those only quests build InitFactionOnCreate , FillFactionOnInitialization whether the army is initialized and filled MustHaveOverlordOnLoad , EmergencyOverlordBuilder the Overlord guarantee and the builder that provides one InitialMemberIntelLevel , InitialMemberDefaultFollower , InitialMemberIsMercenary flags given to filled members (the mercenary army: 30, True, True) InterrogationSetup , NameLockedCombatTree intel stages and the combat tree shown for an unknown member ( Orc Unknown ) AdvanceTODCurrentFaction , AdvanceTODStoryActive which armies process a turn (below) WorldUIFaction the Army-screen stage the army is drawn on (see User interface) PlayerBodyguardSummonDataSlot0-2 summon data for the player's bodyguards (filled only in Faction desert DLC4 ) HireCostOption , HireCostVariable the hiring price scalar

Context offset Meaning --- --- +0x08 / +0x18 / +0x20 the army's pool binding, a handle: a list node {next, previous} at +0x08 , its owner at +0x18 and the pool object the army draws from and registers members in at +0x20 , linked into the list headed at pool+8 (the faction system's initialization, 0xF661A3 - 0xF661E5) +0x30 the army's summary container: one summary per seat (see User interface) +0x90 / +0x98 the army's sim events +0xD8 an object used for a row's level (0x1C1BDA8) and to test the army's own presets (0x1C1C638) +0xF8 / +0x100 the runtime rows (below) +0x140 pending work, drained by 0x1C1C4E4 on a flushing turn +0x1E0 staggers the first three events' lifetimes +0x1ED, +0x218, +0x219 generate at the first tick; regenerate after an event ends +0x1EE, +0x1F0 dirty bytes set when a seat is vacated +0x21C the fill latch: the army fills once per initialization A full pool's eviction reads each army's Pool field (0xF67970), not the binding list; the only walker of that list found is the pool's base destructor 0x1BD20EC.

The Army screen draws an army on the world section its definition's WorldUIFaction names (see User interface for the screen itself). The menu world holds one stage object per region (vt 0x1FA4008, Hier.Map.Region , at the region's map position, on the active list 0x2675860). It requests its section only when it activates: slot 16 (0x1A34E78) reads the Region record ( [obj+0x188] ), maps it to an army (0x1E4418), takes that army's world section and requests it (0x4B420C) into the object's own group. The stage owner [base+0x26FFB60] (vt 0x1F97950) holds 38 slots of 0x50 bytes at +0x2B8 (count +0x2C0 ), one per army in army-table order, keyed by the Faction/Definition at +0x00 (38 of 38). StageFor 0x455EDC returns a slot's +0x48 , the spawned stage object (vt 0x1FA2FB8, its fort at +0x1E8 ), and +0x28 .. +0x48 is an object handle chained on the region object's +0x2A8 . Armies of one region share one stage object (21 of 38 slots filled in one campaign). Every slot is empty after a load until [owner+0x400] goes to 1, around the first visit to the Army screen. A region stage object that activates while its region maps no army requests nothing, so that army has no stage at all: its slot stays empty and the region object's +0x2A8 points to itself. The Mercenary screen opened on such an army never leaves its loading screen. The camp's own object ( Hier.Map.Region 13 DLC Mercs ) exists in the main campaign, but on a campaign load it activates before desert mercs maps to an army. Replaying the section request alone does not bring the stage up. Fort pieces. An army's stage fort comes from Faction/World/Faction.FortPicker - a Fort/Setup - Fort/Piece entries {FactionPredicate, HierarchyMenuPredicate, RequiredPredicateValue, Piece} . 0x62B600 builds the piece list from all seven entry lists, keeping an entry when 0x62BB18 finds its predicate equal to RequiredPredicateValue . Shipped data uses that test only on lighting (132 of 132 entries; Keep 0 of 135, Gate 0 of 726, Streamed 0 of 33). 0x2EC464 then diffs the list (pieces no longer listed go, new WorldUIFortPiece objects come) when [fort+0x271] is set (by 0x326168). A normal fort's Foundation piece has no section of its own, but the Desolation of Mordor camp's Foundation Desert Mercs brings its own ground ( prefabs\ui\mordormap\foundation desert mercs.bndl , UI ZoneMapFortFlair , 91 assets, 49.6 MB), which is why that camp shows on the map as a square of terrain.

An army's Rows are Faction/Rows records named <region Row <rank . The seat count of a row is its ColumnMax : Row Rank Seats in five regions Minas Ithil --- --- --- --- Row Overlord Overlord 1 1 Row Inner Warchief Warchief Inner 2 (no row) Row Outer Warchief Warchief Outer 4 5 Row Captain 0 Captain 4 4 Row Captain 1 Captain 8 8 Row Captain 2 Captain 7 7 total 26 25 The quest-replay, invasion and Blade of Galadriel armies of each region have the same rows (the DLC armies through their own DLC3 <region Row records), the Desolation of Mordor desert army the same 26 seats, and the mercenary army three captain rows DLC4 desert Row Mercs 0/1/2 of 5 seats with HireCost 6000, 3000 and 1500. The 38 definitions name 208 rows in all; the six campaign armies hold 155 seats. Ranks. Faction/RowRanks has four records: Rank IsOverlord IsWarchief ImportanceScore CanBePlayerBodyguard --- --- --- --- --- Overlord True False 0 False Warchief Inner False True 40 False Warchief Outer False True 40 False Captain False False 0 True Row records carry the rules of their seats: Faction/Rows field Meaning --- --- Rank , ColumnMax , ColumnLocks the rank, the seat count, per-column lock entries (two on the inner warchief rows) GlobalVarPredicate a campaign gate on the row (Overlord rows: OverlordsUnlocked in Nurnen and Cirith Ungol, IntroComplete in Minas Ithil, none in Gorgoroth) EnableHenchmen , HenchmenRows , HenchmenCount , HenchmenAddChance Overlord and warchief rows bring henchmen (bodyguards) from the region's three captain rows, add chance 0.35 ResurrectionEnabled whether a death in the row can be cheated InitialLevels , InitBuilderChance , InitBuilderRecords levels and builders used when the row is filled SimEventGenerationSetup , SimEventGeneration what missions members of the row generate (below) Locations , LocationsLowPriority , LocationsLastResort where members of the row are placed in the world (55 / 27 / 5 locations on a Nurnen captain row) RewardListOnEnterRow rewards applied on entering the row (every Overlord row: the Legendary upgrade lists, below; in Nurnen the warchief rows Default TerrorBodyguardDefeat and the captain rows Default BloodBrother ) RandomIntelWeight intel weight: 1.0 captains, 0.5 warchiefs, 0.25 the Overlord PerceptionOverride , DifficultySetupOverride , DeathStimulus the Overlord and warchief rows' perception ( Warlord ), difficulty and the stimulus their death sends HireCost the mercenary rows' price CanBeRevengeTarget , ClearExistingSimEventsOnEnterRow , RemoveBossOnEnter further row rules Runtime rows. The context's rows at ctx+0xF8 / +0x100 are 0x28 bytes, one per definition row: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 the Faction/Rows record +0x08 / +0x10 the seats: int32 per column, the occupant's pool index, -1 = empty +0x20 u32 seat count: the record's ColumnMax (208 of 208 live rows across the 38 armies, with the seats vector the same length) +0x24 u32 column lock bits (tested by 0x24EBB8) A member's own seat is FM+0x268 (the row record) plus FM+0x51B (the column; 0xFF = rowless). Several members share one row record because a row has several seats; each seat holds exactly one member. The save stores the row as its index in the army's Rows and the column as a byte. Moving members. - Seat is 0x61E13C(ctx, fm, row, column, flag), where flag 1 means a new member (the creator 0x1C1D378) and 0 a move (the sim outcome 0x40C304). It refuses a move into a warchief row whose side differs from the Overlord's when FM+0x4F8 is set (0x1E4C08 / 0x114E020). Before seating, it vacates the member, re-levels him for the row (0x1C1BDA8 - SetLevel 0x35188C) and checks that the column is below the seat count, unlocked and empty; it then writes the pool index into the seat, FM+0x51B and FM+0x268 (0x61B614). - Vacate 0x61B274(ctx, fm) writes -1 into every seat holding his index, sets FM+0x51B = 0xFF and FM+0x268 = 0, and sets the dirty bytes ctx+0x1EE / +0x1F0 . 0x61D354(fm, bool) marks a member as moving ( FM+0x51F ). - Swap , the engine's own at 0x40C767 (inside the event-processing code), marks both members, vacates B, unlinks B's pool node ( FM+0x18 ), seats A into B's seat and B into A's old one (both with flag 0), and unmarks them. - Transfer between armies is FactionSystem::TransferMember 0xF6AC90(FS, fm, {army, row, column}). It refuses unless both armies share a pool, and it refuses a move inside one army. It unlinks the member (0x1C25500), rewrites FM+0x178 (and +0x180 when empty) and fires the destination's EventSetup.TransferIntoFaction (every base army ships Transform HireMercToEmpty ). Any two MainGame armies share a pool. Dead captains keep their seats. In a late campaign the six regional armies held no empty seat and one to three dead captains each. The sim-event seat predicate 0xFDC350 treats an empty seat, or a dead member without flag bit 4, as free ("Passed: Dead") and refuses a dead member with bit 4 ("Failure: Resurrectable"), then checks the preset, spy (bit 28) and follower (bit 27) states, a blocking captor event and a duel. The jobs that take a dead or empty seat ( Quest/Jobs/Definition DeadOrEmptyPosition , WC , Overlord ) require MustHaveCanResurrect False. Of the 849 shipped jobs, 26 set that field, all to False. A captain who will return therefore keeps his seat. Filling. FillFaction 0x1C1E13C(ctx) is army initialization's fill. For each row and each column whose seat holds -1 and whose lock bit is clear, it creates one new member, either from the row's InitBuilderRecords by InitBuilderChance (0x1C1E280 - 0x1C1CFAC) or by the generic build 0x1C1D100. The generic build allocates the member (0x1C23C10 - pool 0x1BD2E20), builds him (0x1BC0084), registers him in the pool (0x61B5E8), levels him (0x1C1BDA8 - SetLevel), seats him (0x61E13C with flag 1), applies the definition's intel, follower and mercenary flags, and adds henchmen (0x7DEEE0). The builder path calls no SetLevel. The latch ctx+0x21C limits the fill to once per initialization (0x185FE0).

The FactionMember (vt 0x1FD5EA0) is 0x528 bytes . Both allocation sites ask for 0x528 bytes (0x19ED468: mov ecx,0x528 - allocator 0x3DE238 - constructor 0x1BB4C1C; 0xF99FF0 likewise) and the constructor's last store is +0x520 . Everything at +0x530 and above belongs to other allocations: the appearance object is a separate object at [FM+0x2D8] (it sat directly after the member for 0 of 206 row captains), and the traits live in vectors (see Captain traits). The constructor allocates that object itself, right after the member (see Captain appearance), so whether it sits at FM+0x530 depends on the heap's history: in two other running games it did for 55 of the first 60 seated captains and for 459 of 484 MainGame members. Fixed offsets past +0x528 therefore read whatever allocation follows the member. The appearance cells are reached only through [FM+0x2D8] . Valid member test. A member is valid when [FM+0x178] is a GameDB record (526 of 526 members pass, 0 of 53 other pointers do). FM+0x174 is not a validity flag: the MainGame and DLC pools both hold a member at index 0. Member keys. The engine refers to a member by the pair {faction record = FM+0x178, u32 pool index = FM+0x174} , not by pointer: faction events, ambush requests and the boss link all store keys.

The key names are those of the member document that the exporter 0x1BC5044 writes and the importer 0x1BC21B4 reads. The importer's callers are an online arena opponent (0x1BC04E4), a fort's member array (0x1BD3BD8) and the demo orc (0xF58270). The local save writes each member through 0x594788 and reads him back through 0x1BC0F2C, field by field without names. Flags go through the flag setter 0x1156740(fm, bit, value).
