0xFF = rowless +0x51C u8 set to 1 by a full trait rebuild +0x51F u8 the moving mark +0x520 u8 2 for a builder-built member, 3 for a story character The document form. Besides the binary save, a member is written and read as a key-named document tree: the writer 0x1BC45A8 (its callers include the console commands FactionMember.Save and FactionMember.Save.Pos and presentation code) and the reader 0x1BC159C (used by the member factory 0xF99FF0 and presentation code). The "document key" names in the table come from this pair, which also names +0x278 CharacterModel , +0x2D8 SMCStorage , +0x500 ResurrectionCount , +0x520 InitializationType and +0x180 InitialFaction (also read by a third reader, 0x1BC20B0). The last-death block is written by 0x1BC4FCC and read by 0x1BC1F50 with FM+0x298 as the base: +0x10 LastDeathCharacterType , +0x18 LastDeathAttack , +0x20 ExitNavMesh , +0x21 LastDeathPlayerKiller . Records in the binary save are stored by name hash: 0x594788 writes a record cell through 0x36E044, which takes [record+4] when [record+1] & 2 ( [record+4] is the P919 hash of the name on 8 of 8 faction records), and 0x1BC0F2C finds the record again by a binary search of its category (0x17A9528). After the seed, a member's entry holds the hashes of FM+0x178 and FM+0x180 (528 of 528 members; the 7 moved captains carry two different hashes). A record that is not the shipped one but keeps its header therefore saves as the shipped record, and a load puts the shipped record back. The role cells are saved the same way (0x594788 and 0x7C5158 - 0x36E044).

The name is a string id, FM+0x170 . 0x1BC6040(fm, id) stores it, looks up the localized UTF-16 string, converts it with WideCharToMultiByte on the system ANSI code page ( CodePage 0, Windows-1252 on a Western system) and copies at most 31 characters into the 32-byte buffer FM+0x498 ; an id of 0 clears the buffer. A builder-built orc gets his name id from the name table of his class map ( StructuresFactionClassDataMap.NameTable ; Faction/NameTable has Orc, Olog, Forthog and Easterling), so +0x498 is a derived copy and the id is what the save keeps. The title is read by 0x4721A8(fm): the role at [[FM+0x2E0]+0x10] when he has a mock member, else FM+0x318 , then the role's Title , a string key whose text is found by hashing its content (0x471F2C), so the key itself can live anywhere. Of 560 members, 79 carried a mock member, 3 of them with a role other than FM+0x318 . The army summary caches the title's hash at +0x114 (the refill 0x169168). Each of the 914 roles has 29 fields and its own instance. Of the 21 functions that name the role category, none reads a member's role, and the one by-record role table ( FS+0xB0 ) has two callers, neither passing a member's role. Scripts find members by role through Quest.GetFactionMemberOnRoleList .

FM+0x4B8 is stored 0-based; the game shows it plus one, and caps the shown level at 85. SetLevel 0x35188C ends in 0x353C44, which sets flag bits 30 and 31 when the level reaches two thresholds read from the army; crossing the second with no tribe assigns one (0x1BC6718, reason "XPLevel"). Seating re-levels a member for the row (0x1C1BDA8); a story character without a row starts at NoRowXPLevel - 1 .

t: What survives a rebuild, a load and an upload
x: - A rebuild. The console command Faction.RebuildSMC 0x1C5BDA8 rebuilds every member of the current region's army through RebuildDirect 0x1BC3AA8, which empties his items and gives them again from his identity (personality, role, tribe, class kit, army outfit; see Captain appearance). Anything that lived only in his appearance cells or in items his identity does not give (a scar from AddScar , a reward's items) is gone afterwards. The engine's own builds run the same steps only when a member is created. - A load. The binary save keeps his records by name hash, his items by record hash ( Item , WeaponData , ArmorData and the give source when below 11), his appearance slots 0-15 and palette, and only the pickers of his trait slots, which the load rolls again (see Captain traits). The load (0x1BC0F2C) does not re-dress him, so he shows his saved appearance cells until the first re-dress. - An upload. The exporter 0x1BC5044 writes 71 keys and the 35-key appearance document: identity by record hash, random seed , the level, the name id, every flag bit by name, the trait picker and marker lists and the inventory, plus texts for the server ( name , title , rarity and status strings). The importer 0x1BC21B4 reads 57 of them: the receiving game takes the name from name string id hash and the title from role record , re-adds the trait pickers through 0x7CD03C and rolls them itself (a slot holding an option other than its picker's roll does not travel), and always re-dresses him from his items. FM+0x180 , appearance slots 16-22, the design cells and the material overrides are not exported.

- From the seats. For each army context, each runtime row and each column, a seat value other than -1 is a pool index into the army's pool object ( ctx+0x20 ). This finds exactly the seated members, dead or alive, with their row and column. - From the pools. Walk every pool's member vector and keep the valid members ( [FM+0x178] is a record). A member with a row ( FM+0x268 , named <region Row <rank ) is a captain, warchief or Overlord; dead ones have flag bit 2. Story characters carry FM+0x190 and normally no row. Spawned members have FM+0x48 . Pools are by game mode, so the region of a member is his army ( FM+0x178 ) or his row's prefix, never his pool.

FM+0x508 is a u64 of flags. The getter 0x114B55C is a bare bt [fm+0x508], bit ; 0x114DFE8 tests bit 2 (dead). The loader's keys name most bits, and the FactionMember document writer 0x1BC45A8 (whose keys run from Identity , Flags and XPLevel to Inventory ) names more. It writes each boolean key from one getter call: IsResurrected bit 0, IsDead 2, KilledByPlayer 3, CanResurrect 4, PresentedToPlayer 5, IdentityPresented 7, HasEverSpawned 9, IgnorePlayerLevelRestriction 10, HasVow 12, SeveredHead 17, IsMockDead 21, CanInterrogateAbout 22, RevengeTarget 24, WasEverPreset 25, Builder CanNotSave 32, Builder DisableSimEvents 33, DisableTraitChanges 38, DisableRelationships 39, CanNotDropLoot 40, CanNotChangeXPLevel 41, CanNotApplyContract 42 and CalcXPLevelOnAssignToRow 44. PlayerFollower , Spy and Prisoner come from functions (0x114E020, 0x1149E50, 0x1BBCAEC) rather than a single bit. Three bits have no saved key. Bit 37 marks a temporary member: 0x1BBF928 sets it when the builder's byte +0x180 is set, and 0x1BC04E4 sets it on an online arena opponent ( online arena opponent , which also clears the follower bit). A quest's Cleanup OnEnter (0x7652BC) then calls 0x1B5E0B4, which checks the bit, confirms the member still sits at its pool index, nulls that slot and destroys the member. Bit 35 is set in one place, 0x61CED0, which assigns a member to a sim event: it copies bit 0 of the intel mask FM+0x510 at that moment. In one campaign, all 102 members with bit 35 held that mask bit, none of the 75 members without it had bit 35, and 350 members held the mask bit without it. Bit 16 is set by the un-death 0x630644 immediately before it clears the dead bit, and that function never clears it. Yet only 1 of the 86 members with a return on record ( FM+0x500 above 0) carried it, so it does not mark a returned member; the return count FM+0x500 does. Bit Name Meaning and writers --- --- --- 0 is resurrected set by the un-death 2 is dead SetDead 0x626E38 3 killed by player 4 can resurrect a return from death is pending (below) 5 is player presented the player has met him 7 is menu presented shown in the hierarchy; set after creation 9 HasEverSpawned 10 IgnorePlayerLevelRestriction ignore the player-level cap (setter 0xF88AA0) 12 has vow 14, 19, 34, 43 derived from his traits (see Captain traits) 38 DisableTraitChanges also derived from his traits 17 is severed decapitated; set by the sever-on-death handler 0x6DE30C 21 is mockdead the mock member is dead: the hierarchy shows him eliminated 22 can interrogate about 24 is revengetarget 25 was ever preset 27 is player follower setter 0x7D52B0 28 is spy 29 the player's bodyguard 30, 31 level thresholds (above) 32 Builder CanNotSave not written to the local save 33 Builder DisableSimEvents 39 DisableRelationships 40 CanNotDropLoot 41 cant change xp level / CanNotChangeXPLevel 42 CanNotApplyContract 44 CalcXPLevelOnAssignToRow 45 never recycled by a full pool 48-50 the player's bodyguard summon slot 0/1/2, read by the summon 0x1010790 51 mercenary (setter 0xF88AD0, getter 0xF86B90) The document writer 0x1BC45A8 and reader 0x1BC159C name more bits (getter 0x114B55C and setter 0x1156740 with the bit number next to each key): 9 HasEverSpawned (also set by 0x356370), 10 IgnorePlayerLevelRestriction , 32 Builder CanNotSave , 33 Builder DisableSimEvents , 36 Prisoner , 38 DisableTraitChanges , 39 DisableRelationships , 40 CanNotDropLoot , 41 CanNotChangeXPLevel , 42 CanNotApplyContract and 44 CalcXPLevelOnAssignToRow . FM+0x50C is not a separate field: it is the word's upper half (the constructor stores +0x508 as one qword; 40 of 40 seated captains agree). The engine's setters do more than the bit, so a direct write to the word skips their side effects: - SetDead 0x626E38(fm, dead) sets bit 2 and, when FM+0x398 names a campaign variable, sets that variable (0x59A1D8): a story character's death unlocks the next scene this way. Its un-death branch (0x627197) clears bits 2, 12 and 17 but not 21. - The follower setter 0x7D52B0(fm, bool) changes the member. The character's CCharacter::SetIsPlayerFollower 0x102F0C(char, bool) also sets the character's follower byte ( +0x23B8 ) and its combat stats before calling it. When the member's row sets Faction/Rows.TriggerQuestEvalOnSetPlayerFollower (as snowMtn Row Captain 0 does), the setter asks the quest system [GM+0x6C60] to re-evaluate (0x1B562F0, a jump to 0x7AF25C) and adds the army's sim-event picker ( Faction::AddFactionSimEventPicker 0x1B5E5D8, its only caller). The seat move 0x61E13C is the only other caller of 0x1B562F0. Region ownership is the Overlord's bit 27 (see Quests, story and scenes). - The intel setter 0x353EC4(fm, level, fireEvent, force) refuses a level that is not higher unless forced, clamps to the setup's DataStages , writes FM+0x51A and rebuilds the mask FM+0x510 (0x62136C). It notifies the player (0x7BE290, which reaches the global script agent [GM+0x6CF0] , so it belongs on the main thread), updates trait visibility on a body, fires the army's DataLevelChangeEvent when asked, and re-resolves his traits (UpdateTraits reason 6). - Bit 32's clear 0x18E218 is a bare btr with no event. The pool serializer 0x59460C writes every member unless 0x595890(fm) (= not bit 32) refuses him, and 0x595CA0 is the only other reader of bit 32. Members held by the online garrison carry it. Bit 32 is the engine's Builder CanNotSave (its string at 0x1BC19B4). It is set directly by the builder build 0x1BBF928, the document reader 0x1BC159C and the wrapper 0x1BC6004.

Everything that happens to a member is a Faction/Events/Events record (2,039 ship, each with the same 77 fields) applied by the engine: 1. System::CreateAndProcessFactionEvent 0x1B5B610(FS, event, subject, other) builds a 0x60-byte descriptor holding the subject's key, the other's key (index -1 when there is none), the event and the other's row index (0x1E4D90) and column, then calls 0x40C0AC(FS, descriptor). The script binding 0x1B7F210 resolves its handles in the current region's pool first. 2. 0x40C0AC processes the event synchronously; an event raised while another is in progress ( FS+0x208 ) is queued at FS+0x1F0 and drained afterwards (post-processing 0x1E2DA0). 3. 0x40C13C - 0x62E670, the dispatcher, picks and records the event's replay (the Army-screen flashback: 0x7421A0 - 0x741284, [SIMEVENT REPLAY] ), then the apply 0x630644 changes the member. The shipped events set these fields (counted over the 2,039 records): Field Events Effect --- --- --- LevelsToAdd 1,736 (1,711 of them 1) levels; LevelsToAddFollower (44) for followers RewardLists 558 reward lists to roll (below) ReplayType , Replay 420, 153 the replay shown for the event KeepPriority 153 how long the history keeps the event (below) SetMockMemberDead 142 (113 True) mark the mock member dead or alive ForceLevelUp 82 PickNewSimEvent , PickNewLocation 53, 14 re-plan the member UnlockName , UnlockTraits 47, 19 intel SetIsPrisoner , SetPlayerFollower , SetIsSpy 46, 35, 29 links to Combat/Predicates/Bool/True or False Ambush 32 queue an ambush ClearCopyFactionMemberData 24 drop the mock member Resurrect 18 un-death for a member with bit 4 ScarType 18 a scar ( Branded Slave 14, Shamed 3) EjectIfWarchief , EjectIfOverlord 12, 11 remove him from a warchief or Overlord seat CreateFactionMemberProfile 11 make a grunt or creature a named member ( ActiveKillPlayer grunt , ActiveKillNamedAI ) SetRevengeTarget , RevengeTargetType 4, 9 ToggleIsPlayerFollower 4 the four arena wins ChangePlayerBodyguard 1 BecomeBodyguard PlayerResurrect 1 Resurrected PlayerAbility RaiseDead CopyAndHideFactionMemberData 0 ActiveKillPlayer grunt , the event of a grunt killing the player, sets CreateFactionMemberProfile , UnlockName , SetRevengeTarget (type Kill), SetMockMemberPresented , KeepPriority 100 and the reward lists KillPlayer Rewards grunt and gruntSlaveBrand . The apply and following. The apply calls the follower setter only behind SetPlayerFollower (a link, 0x630CB8) and ToggleIsPlayerFollower (a bool, 0x630EF5); an event without them leaves an enemy an enemy. Rewards. For each reward list the engine draws count = 0x34F980(list) rewards with reward = 0x350500(fm, list) (eligibility 0x105AEC, weights 0x3505F4, a random pick; 0 = none) and applies each with ApplyReward 0x3511F4(fm, reward, other, 1) - 0x351AF8, which re-resolves every trait slot (see Captain traits). Called directly, ApplyReward skips eligibility.

Which event a game situation fires is per army: Faction/Definition.EventSetup names a Faction/Events/Setup record (seven ship: one per region and Faction Player Setup ). In Nurnen's setup: Setup field Event --- --- KilledByPlayerEvent ActiveKilledByPlayer KillPlayerEvent , KillPlayerAlreadyNamed , KillPlayerAssistEvent ActiveKillPlayer grunt , ActiveKillPlayer AlreadyNamed , ActiveKillPlayerAssist ResurrectedPresentationEvent Resurrected Presented EventSwapFactionPositionsPromotion / PromotionEmpty Transform SwapPromotionOccupied / Transform SwapPromotionEmpty EventSwapFactionPositionsDemotion / DemotionEmpty , Lateral / LateralEmpty the matching Transform Swap events EventSlotOverlord , EventSlotOverlord NoChange Transform SlotOverlord , NoChange OverlordEjectedEvent , WarchiefEjectedEvent OverlordEjected , WarchiefBrandedEjection SetPlayerFollowerEvent , ClearPlayerFollowerEvent ActivePlayerFollowerSet , ActivePlayerFollowerClear EventApplyIsPlayerFollower , EventRemoveIsPlayerFollower IsPlayerFollowerApply , IsPlayerFollowerRemove TransferIntoFaction , TransferOutOfFaction Transform HireMercToEmpty , TransferOutOfFaction DataLevelChangeEvent , GainInterrogationIntelEvent , InterrogatedEvent DatalLevelChanged , ActiveGainInterrogationIntel , ActiveInterrogated HierarchyPresentedEvent , HenchmenKilledEvent , BossKilledEvent , LoadMemberEvent HierarchyPresented , HenchmenKilled , BossKilled , LoadMember TimePassedEvent TimePassed (one level) FleeEvent , FleeRunStartEvent , DespawnWhileFleeingEvent ActiveFlee , FleeRunStart , ActiveDespawnWhileFleeing TimedSimEvents HalfEmpty , Resurrection , FillUpCompletely LongDelay , CompletelyEmpty PromoteEventSetup Faction/Events/PromotionEventSetup/Default ( HardMode and MinasIthil variants exist) A promotion, a demotion or a lateral move is therefore an event; the seat changes themselves go through the seat function with flag 0 (from the sim-event outcome 0x40C304) and the engine's swap.

The missions on the Army screen (power struggles, hunts, executions, fort assaults) are sim events , and they advance in turns, not in real time. - AdvanceTurn 0x1B5EE88(FS, unused, u8 flushPending) increments the turn FS+0x218 and, on a flush, runs 0x1C1C4E4 on every army (draining ctx+0x140 ). It then runs 0xFDEC20(ctx, save slot), turn processing and generation ( FactionSimEventGenerate 0x597A9C), for every army that passes 0x1B5B058. That test refuses an army with AdvanceTODCurrentFaction unless it is the current region's army ( FS+0x1B8 ), and otherwise requires the army's AdvanceTODStoryActive to match a state read through [GM+0x6D30] (0x114E008). The campaign armies ship with the first False and the second True. AdvanceTurn's callers are the quest post-active state 0x19F8C34, the world reset 0x1789F0C (the player's death), the single-hierarchy view 0x434CF0 (no flush) and 0x1B5ED08. The world clock stops while the Army screen is open. - Generation. For each member, his row's SimEventGenerationSetup lists entries that are tried in order (0x5924EC; each entry may require a follower, a non-follower or either). An entry's Faction/Events/SimEventGenerationType records (68 ship) are picked by weight (a reservoir pick 0x1B3B90 in 0x5926EC; a failure drops the type and retries) and 0x5935DC creates the event. A type's weight is Weights[min(active events of that type in the army, count - 1)] , or its WeightOverride 's entries when set (difficulty-scaled through SimEventGeneration constants); weight 0 is the cap. PowerStruggle Act2 lists 13 sim events (among them Chase, Duel, Execution2, GraugHeist, the raids and the trials) with Weights 10, 7, 4, 0 and the global-variable predicate Act2 . Candidate lists are capped at 64 (0x597E44). Members with a current event ( FM+0x4F0 ), dead members without bit 4 and members with bit 21 are skipped, and each member gets one event at most. - The event object (vt 0x1DBC8A8) holds the army at +0x40 , the Faction/Events/SimEvent at +0x48 (431 ship), its quest at +0x50 / +0x58 (a Quest/Quests record such as VO Chase 02 ), the generation type at +0x60 , a serial number at +0x94 and the turn it expires at +0x98 (created turn plus the type's lifespan). An army's events are at ctx+0x90 / +0x98 .

Each member can hold a cooldown table [FM+0x258] : a 0x18-byte object {entries, u32 count, category} of {record, u32 expiry turn} entries, the category being Faction/Events/SimEventCooldown ( [base+0x2701A18] ; two records, PowerStruggle CD and HuntingMission CD ). The gate 0x1BC0C2C(fm, SimEvent.RequiredCooldown ) passes when there is no table or the entry has expired, and refuses when the table exists but has no entry (the lookup 0x1BBC410 returns null). The setter 0x1BB7578 creates and sizes a table (0x1BBF840) only when none exists. The FactionMember loader creates the table when the save flags one (0x1BC0F2C) but never sizes it, and reads each saved entry into a temporary (0x1BC0EC4). After a load, every member that had a cooldown is refused power struggles and hunts permanently: in a late-campaign pool of 500, no table was sized and 60 living seated captains carried an empty one. An emulated generation pass on Minas Ithil's army, with every captain free and no events, refused 204 of 221 generation attempts. Within those attempts, every power-struggle and hunt candidate check (340 of 340) failed at this gate; the other refused attempts failed at their campaign gates.

Death and return run through the kill path and events: 1. Mark. The kill path 0x6DB95C (0x1BB9F84 for event kills) stores the death's Faction/Resurrection record at FM+0x2C0 and, when the row has ResurrectionEnabled , rolls the odds (0x6DBD4C: presets refused, row, predicate, odds table). On success, the evaluator 0x1BC5D44 adds the scar types his sever effects bring to the list at FM+0x358 and picks a fitting scar (0x1B5AA00(FS, [FM+0x370] , cause, [FM+0x500] ); with none, the result is "No Available Scars" and nothing changes). It then increments FS+0x21C and FM+0x500 , sets bit 4, stores the scar at FM+0x348 (unless it equals FM+0x370 ) and fires the record's DeathEvent through 0x40C0AC. Captain scars and the return from death describes how the scar is chosen. Without ResurrectionEnabled , the kill path resets the mock member (0x6DBCFC). 2. Queue. The death event ( WillResurrect <death , 23 of them, KeepPriority 30) carries reward lists that queue the ambush: CheatDeath Ambush for an enemy, CheatDeath Betrayal or CheatDeath FollowerStillLoyal for a follower. CheatDeath Ambush retries forever ( RetryMax -1, RetryDelay 0.25 minutes), never for an Overlord, and fires only in its own region. One such request reached 1,121 retries. The return is not a job: no shipped job requires MustHaveCanResurrect True. 3. Complete. Only the apply 0x630644 performs the un-death. When the member has bit 4 and the event has Resurrect , or the event has PlayerResurrect , it clears bits 4 and 6, sets 0 and 16, clears 2 and 17, and then runs 0xE7DF70(fm). Resurrected Presented (the ambush's success event) adds SetMockMemberDead False, ClearCopyFactionMemberData , PickNewSimEvent , one level plus a player-based level change, and EjectIfWarchief / EjectIfOverlord . Bit 4 has other readers: the seat predicate 0xFDC350, the cancel pass 0xF9BA70 (from 0xF665F0 and 0xFA0D30: a dead member with bit 4 that fails 0xFF3D30 loses bits 4, 0 and 16), the sever abort 0x6DE30C ("Aborting Resurrection, Faction member was severed after death", only while the corpse is in the world), SetDead, the writer 0x1BC5044 and the FactionMember document writer 0x1BC45A8 (whose keys include CanResurrect ). The data. Faction/Resurrection has 34 death types. Each names an OddsTable ( Faction/Resurrection/Tables : Base, Bleedout, BodyCleaved Uruk, Death from Fall, HeadRemoved Olog, over 14 Faction/Resurrection/Chance records), a ScarType , a SecondScarChance and SecondScarType , a DeathEvent and loot tags. The odds roll (0x6DC65C, called from 0x6DBD4C) walks the table's ChanceRecords and keeps a Faction/Resurrection/Chance record only when the world total FS+0x21C lies within its MinTotalResurrected to MaxTotalResurrected and the member's own count FM+0x500 within MinThisGuyResurrected to MaxThisGuyResurrected (0x6DC784; a negative bound is no bound). The shipped records use the world total as a campaign stage and the member's count as a repeat counter: Chance record World total Member's count --- --- --- Resurrection 1st , Resurrection 1st FallOnly 0 any Resurrection 2ndFew , Resurrection 2ndFew FallOnly 1 - 4 any Resurrection 3rdFew , Resurrection 3rdFew Bleedout 5 or more any Resurrection 1stFew OlogHeadRemoved / 2ndFew OlogHeadRemoved up to 2 / 3 or more any ResurrectSameGuy Again / Again2 / Again3 any 1 - 2 / 2 - 3 / 4 or more ResurrectSameGuy Again OlogHeadRemoved / Again2 OlogHeadRemoved any 1 - 2 / 2 or more Resurrection BodyCleave any any From the fifth return of a campaign on, the world total is above every upper bound (it read 375 in one late campaign), so only the records without one stay eligible: the 3rdFew pair, 2ndFew OlogHeadRemoved , Resurrection BodyCleave and the same-member records. Resurrection Torment has the table Base, the scar Curse , a second scar ( Sack Head or Metal Head ) at 0.5 and the event WillResurrect Torment . Resurrection HeadRemoved has no odds table and no death event: a decapitated orc never returns (the olog has its own table). The mock member. FM+0x2E0 is a 0x20-byte copy {appearance, inventory, role, flag} that the Army screen draws instead of the real member while it exists (0x75D2FC / 0x75D314 read it), and whose role the title read takes first (79 of 560 members carried one). Rewards with CopyAndHideFactionMemberData build it (22 of 1,239 rewards: role transforms, pinnacle scars), as does an event's SetMockMemberDead True. ClearCopyFactionMemberData , SetMockMemberDead False and the kill path without resurrection drop it. Bit 21 says the mock member is dead. Every death in a resurrection row keeps the copy, whether or not the member will return. Among living members, only a member who has returned but is not yet presented carries it, together with bit 21 ( SimResurrected sets Resurrect without touching the mock member). In one late save, all 11 seated dead members had bit 21 and 9 of them a copy; of 197 seated living members, one (returned, not yet presented) had a copy and bit 21. Raising the dead. Resurrected PlayerAbility RaiseDead , the only event with PlayerResurrect , performs the un-death on any member, scars him Resurrected PlayerAbility RaiseDead , adds a level, aborts his ambushes and rolls PlayerSkill Resurrected Captain : one of four rewards giving the tribe TribeDef Undead , the undead items, personality Damaged901 Undead pss Moaner , deranged markers, a permanent fire vulnerability, poison immunity and Unbreakable, after removing every fire and poison trait. It does not touch the follower bit.

FM+0x300 / +0x308 is the member's history: 16-byte entries {Faction/Events/Events record, u16 the turn} , in order (488 of 488). 0x631648 trims it whenever it exceeds 32 entries through 0x1BC3EB8, which erases the entry with the lowest KeepPriority , the oldest on a tie; the save writes 32 slots (0x594788). KeepPriority is read only by that eviction. The shipped priorities are 30 for the WillResurrect death events and Resurrected Presented , 10 for ActiveKilledByPlayer , 100 for ActiveKillPlayer grunt , and 50 for frequent events such as ActiveInitialPlayerThreat , ActiveKillNamedAI , FleeRunStart and every fear or hate trigger. A full history therefore drops its deaths before those events: 196 of 515 histories were at the cap, and 18 of 86 members who had cheated death had lost the record of it, all 18 at the cap. A spawned character's audio object receives a copy of the list (see Audio and video).

The ambush manager is [FS+0x30] . TriggerAmbush 0x6DDCB8(manager, definition, forced member) only queues a 0x40-byte request in the vector at +0x338 : Request offset Meaning --- --- +0x18 the region's army it was queued in +0x20 the Faction/Ambush/Definition +0x28 the forced ambusher's key ( {0, -1} = none) +0x38 u32 due time in milliseconds on the world clock +0x3C retries A second request for a queued definition is refused unless its forced member is dead (0x114DFE8), and one for the active definition is refused. The update 0x6DDBA8 runs only while no ambush is active ( [manager] holds the active one) and evaluates each due request with 0x6DD92C. A forced member already in the world is discarded. The gates are the global enable [base+0x267D598] , manager+0x368 (the running quest allows ambushes), +0x369 (the player is not in a FactionAmbushDisableBrush ) and the post-quest timer +0x36C , and a request whose army is not the current region's is retried (see Quests, story and scenes). 0x1C5E358 then runs the chance (0x1C5F0E8: AmbushChance , the global-variable predicate, the player's excluded attacks, tags and buffs, minimum followers, the Overlord-follower predicate), the ambusher pick 0x1C5D458 (the forced one unless he is spawned or fails the job, else a job pick 0x1B5AC8C; 16 definitions with NeverPickAmbusherWithJob or no job can only fire with a provided ambusher), the validation 0x1C5F070 (not spawned, rank not in ExcludedRowRanks ) and the result 0x1C5D624. A failed pass re-queues the request after RetryDelay minutes. A rowless member's rank is null, so an empty ExcludedRowRanks refuses every rowless ambusher. The active ambush object (vt 0x1FFACB0) keeps the ambusher at +0x38 , the definition at +0x90 , the completed flag at +0xA5 and the done flag at +0xA6 . Its slot 2, 0x1C7E1FC, only sets +0xA6 , after which the manager's tick drops the request and deletes the object.

FM+0x390 is a Faction/Traits/MarkerRarity record: OrcRarity Common , OrcRarity Epic , OrcRarity Legendary and a test record OrcRariry Unique (display name test string ). Each gives the hierarchy's selection effect ( Interface/ElementFXList/Rarity ), a priority (0, 1, 2) and a tint (Epic 0xFFED5132, Legendary 0xFF4509C4). Rarity is also a trait: Picker OrcRarity - the OrcRarity trait - the item Buff OrcRarity . A Legendary carries two epic traits ( ET ) and an ET CanRemove marker; an Epic carries one. A Training Order is an event. Contract LegendaryTraining adds one level and rolls the reward lists Contract LegendaryTraining CommonOrc , EpicOrc , Default EpicTraits PickRemovable and MarkerSwap . The events Upgrade OrcRarity ToEpic and ToLegendary are the other upgrades. The marker swap LT MarkerSwap is eligible only for a member who already has an epic trait ( IncludedTraitPicker PickerListRaw AllEpicTraits ), so applying it directly through ApplyReward makes a Legendary with no epic traits. Rolling the lists through 0x350500 gives the traits first. Entering an Overlord row applies the same kind of upgrade: its RewardListOnEnterRow rolls OverlordSetup LegendaryUpgrade CommonOrc (twice), EpicOrc , Default EpicTraits PickRemovable , Contract LegendaryTraining MarkerSwap and Overlord ElementalVent Resistances .

- Tribes are Faction/Tribes/Definitions (19): Dark, Feral, Machine, Marauder, Militant, Outlaw, Slaughter, Sorcerous, Terror, Warmonger, Undead, Easterling, Tribeless, the special tribes Bruz, Gondor, Sauron, ShadowWar and NazgulTwins, and DLC TribeDef Sorcerous Poison . A member gets one when he is built (0x1BC6718, reason "Builder") or crosses the level threshold without one. - Roles ( FM+0x318 , 914 Faction/Roles/Definitions ) carry the title; the role setter 0x1BC63F8 writes +0x318 and +0x320 . - Builders. A Faction/FactionMemberBuilder (608 ship) is a recipe: CombatTrees , Roles , Tribe / IncludedTribes , ArmorRowRank , MinLevel (+ MinLevelDelta , PlayerBasedXPLevel ), CalcXPLevelOnAssignToRow , DataLevel , trait markers, desired and excluded trait pickers, RandomTraitPickerLists , personalities, Rewards / RewardLists , SimEventPickers , PlayerFollower , CanSave , RemoveAfterQuest , EnableTraitChanges , EnableRelationships , UniqueBuilderInstance . Captain ( MinLevel 5) and EmergencyOverlord ( MinLevel 30 +/- 5, enters through Builder EnterHierarchy ) are the base ones; families such as FD InvCap , DLC5 Y<n <region C<n , SW Y and Gauntlet serve other game modes. A build request is prepared by 0x1C63920, which stores the builder at request +0x168 , its UniqueBuilderInstance at +0x140 and its flags. The builder build 0x1BBF928 then copies the builder to FM+0x3A0 and the instance to FM+0x350 and sets +0x520 = 2. It writes the seed, a name from the class map and a personality (0x1BDA7AC), forces the intel level to 0 (0x353EC4 with force ), assigns a tribe and the follower and level-cap flags, and then levels him and resolves his traits.

- Followers are marked by bit 27, which events ( SetPlayerFollower , ToggleIsPlayerFollower ) and the follower setter 0x7D52B0 (used by CreateEmergencyPlayerFollower ) set and clear. A betrayal clears it. - Bodyguards. Only the Captain rank has CanBePlayerBodyguard . Bit 29 marks the player's bodyguard (the event BecomeBodyguard is the one with ChangePlayerBodyguard ), and bits 48-50 give the summon slot read by 0x1010790 together with the army's PlayerBodyguardSummonDataSlot0-2 . Overlords and warchiefs have their own bodyguards: their rows' henchmen, made by 0x7DEEE0 when the army fills or a preset with henchmen is built. - Spies and prisoners are event flags ( SetIsSpy , bit 28; SetIsPrisoner ). - Mercenaries. A hire is a transfer, not a new member. The mercenary screen's action 0xDBC910 takes the member from Faction desert mercs DLC4 , prices him (0xFA3AF0: the row's HireCost through the army's HireCostVariable / HireCostOption , scalar 1.0 without discount skills) and pays (0x189353C) in the currency item of the player's skill setup ( PC Mirian for Talion, DLC4 PLBar Coin for Baranor). It then calls TransferMember 0xF6AC90. The afford check 0x18AAD4E and the payment 0xDBD0DF read that setup at [[[base+0x26FFA98]+0x888]+0x2348]+0x738 and count the currency from the inventory records at [obj+0x740 .. +0x748] ( +0x00 item, +0x20 count). A zero price passes the spend check 0x1BCEC24. The mercenary army fills its members as followers and mercenaries (bits 27 and 51) and ships ReinitOnActivate True. It binds the DLC4 pool and belongs to the DLC4 save slot, so the base campaign never fills it.

t: Story and DLC characters in the hierarchy
x: A story character is a Faction/PresetMembers record (203 records, 67 of them belonging to the DLCs). The saves of the base campaign hold the DLC cast too: the mercenary army, the ten Blade of Galadriel twin armies and their presets (the Nazgul sisters DLC3 Nazgul Twin 1 , eight DLC3ToMain specialists, DLC FakeDarkTalion , DLC4 Desert Overlord ). The base game's Nazgul are presets as well (six GP Nazgul ). The build sequence is described in Quests, story and scenes; the seating rule is the creator's: The creator seats any preset by its FactionRow . 0x1C1D378(ctx, preset) allocates (0x1C23C10), builds (0x1BC06C0: +0x190 = the preset, +0x3A0 = 0, +0x520 = 3, flag 25) and registers the member (0x61B5E8). With no row, he is rowless at NoRowXPLevel - 1 (0x1C21448). With a row, he is leveled for it (0x1C1BDA8) and the column is the preset's FactionColumn (0x1C206AC). If that seat is taken (0x4F9014) or the column is negative, the row (0x61AC00) gives a free column (0x1C1BEB4), and the seat call 0x61E13C(flag 1) runs only when a free column exists : in a full row the character is built but unseated. Each preset event is then fired through 0x40C0AC. The creator's callers are army initialization 0xFDAC54 (the definition's PresetMembers ), the henchmen builder 0x1BB7898 ( PresetHenchmen ) and the quest path 0x62666C. Seated this way, a preset takes the row's level and his own tribe (a Blade of Galadriel preset in a Seregost warchief row: level 84, TribeDef NazgulTwins ). DLC FakeDarkTalion ( AI Talion , IsDarkTalion , LockedXPLevel 60) has the build event Debug RecruitFollower , which makes him a follower: seated as an Overlord, he hands the region to the player. An occupied Overlord seat is emptied synchronously by an event with EjectIfOverlord through 0x1B5B610; the engine re-places the ejected Overlord in a captain row shortly afterwards.

FM+0x51A is the intel level and FM+0x510 the intel mask that 0x62136C rebuilds from it with the army's InterrogationSetup ( Default , three DataStages ): level 0 gives 0x2, level 1 0x9B, level 2 0xFB. The setter clamps to DataStages - 1 (0x1163F58), and 37 of the 38 armies have three stages ( Faction None has no setup, and the setter returns), so the engine's top level is 2. The byte is stored only by the constructor (0), the setter (clamped), the member copy 0x1BB95CC and the loaders (0x1BC11F6, 0x1BC2479). The loaders restore a saved value unclamped and then rebuild the mask, which stops at the last stage (0xFB). A level of 3 (65 of 549 members in one campaign, all seated, all above their army's top) therefore comes from outside the engine and lives on in the save. Mask bit 0 means the name is known; UnlockName 0x621208 sets it. A level-0 start is ordinary: the builder build, 0x1BC00C8, 0x1BC02AC, the preset build (twice) and System::HierarchyResetPreSetMemberData 0x1C2373C force it, and the war simulation (0xFCD340, 0xFD0660) forces it whenever its level is lower. Faction island and Faction MtnPass start their members at level 0 ( InitialMemberIntelLevel 0, combat tree shown Orc Unknown ). The unknown model. The Army stage's look chooser 0x2EB2DC (reached from UI CWorldUICharacter 0x627F40) draws the decapitation model when the summary has bits 17 and 21 (0x2EB258 - 0x2EB14C), else the world character record's DefaultModel when 0x170744(summary, flag) is false, else his own model (summary +0x138 ). 0x170744 is true when his member has killed the player ( FM+0x4C4 not 0, so such a captain is always shown). Otherwise, with the flag set, it is true when 0x16FDE0 passes ( is menu presented : the member not found or flag bit 7, else the summary's copy at +0x188 bit 7). Otherwise it is true when the summary's copy of the intel mask ( +0x190 bit 0, written only by the refill 0x169168) says the name is known. The redraw 0x19C395C, the holder path 0x1A2957C, the combat tree 0x170698, the names 0x17EE550 and the replay pass 0x1BFCCC8 pass flag 0; 0x627B74, 0x627E4C and 0x1A1FF24 pass 1. The Faction/World/Character records FactionMember , FactionMember ModelCam , FactionMember GarrisonMember and GraveyardVendor name Character/Models/HierarchyUnknown , FactionMember Portrait names PortraitUnknown , and KilledByDecapitation is Head Stick . Because the chooser reads copies, a change to the member alone shows nothing on an open Army screen until the summaries are refilled. The engine's reveal is 0x19F6C80. It calls UnlockName 0x621208(fm, 0) (the name stage: mask 0x2 - 0x9B, and the quest hooks on the name bit), then 0x1BC6030(fm) (bit 7 through the flag setter), then the intel setter 0x353EC4(fm, 0xFF, 0, 0) (0xFF clamps to the top level: 0x9B - 0xFB). 0x17DE6AC makes the first two calls with the event flag set. The setter also notifies the player (0x7BE290), re-resolves the traits (UpdateTraits reason 6) and, for a body in the world, updates trait visibility (0x355700). The hierarchy treats bit 21 (mock dead) as eliminated: the henchmen link effects 0x18316FC / 0x183191C skip such a member, and the replay layout picker 0x6276F8 picks "Dead".

- What does FM+0x4F8 mean? The seat function tests it; it held 1 on 2 of 555 members in one campaign, both in the InvasionGame pool, and 0 on 527 of 527 in another. - Why is flag bit 16, which the un-death sets, missing from most returned members? - What reads flag bit 35? It has no resolved getter call, and 60 of the getter's 125 calls pass the bit indirectly. - Is the role counter at FS+0xB0 the number of times the role was given? It would then lower the role's weight by WeightReductionPerUse per use, as the scar table does by its use count; the code that reads it is not traced. - Are the pool's ImpC coefficients the importance score used when a full pool recycles a member? - Is the world's resurrection total FS+0x21C saved with the game, and under which key? The faction manager's document keys include Resurrected . - When exactly does the cancel pass 0xF9BA70 run relative to a save and a load? Its caller 0xFA0D30 is reached from two places. One is the faction manager's part of the game document (0x1B5D254, keys TimeStamp , Resurrected , FactionPool , FactionRecord , FactionRole , AmbushMgr , GauntletMgr , MonumentMgr ), which the document routine 0x1C5B4C4 runs together with the quest manager, the game variables and the inventory. The other is the online-fortress setup's finalization (0x1B40CAC - 0x1B5D368, stage SETUP FINALIZE VALIDATE DATA INTEGRITY ). The direction of the document routine (write, read or both) is not traced, and the second caller 0xF665F0 has no direct caller. - Does a queued ambush request's retry count survive a save and reload? - Which loading screens rebuild the army contexts and members? Values changed in the mercenary army's context and records survived two region changes. - Does a head, hair or body carried only in the appearance cells (slots 0-2 and the face record) draw on another player's game? The document carries the cells, but the receiving game makes no gear load request for a cell, only for an item. - What exactly does the quest system's re-evaluation 0x7AF25C do after a seat move or a follower change, and under which conditions inside 0x61E13C is it reached? - Can the quest branch reached on a name change (0x4A87C8 / 0x19F80C8, from the name bit's hooks) start a mission tied to the captain when the engine's reveal 0x19F6C80 runs?

Shadow of War ships an importer, the Nemesis Forge, that rebuilds a player's Shadow of Mordor follower and nemesis as War captains (Mordor is "Firebird" and War "Kraken" in its names; compiled from ...\KRAKEN CODE STREAM\source\Game\Shared\NemesisForgeUtils.cpp , log tag [NEMESISFORGE]: , the logger compiled out of the shipping build). The captains came from the publisher's online service, never from Mordor's files, and enter the game through two story missions; the import itself is an ordinary member build fed by a 13-key payload and a set of conversion tables.

title configuration key nemesis forge (bool) - parser 0x18368B0 - [GM+0x6D48]+0xD1 world entry 0x1E3E78 (its only caller) - check 0x1B3ABFC on the online manager [GM+0x6D30] stop if a captain is already stored (+0x38, +0x80) or Invasion/Settings.HaltNemesisForgeCheckPredicate holds - request 0x1B3AA94: stop unless the switch is on; stop while one is in flight (+0x28) - reply 0x1B3D500: Follower[0].attributes - parser 0x1B3A148 - +0x30 ; Nemesis[0].attributes - +0x78 quest job filler 0x1BD40C4 (a story mission's job setup) - UseNemesisForgeAlly (Rat3 Ally1, "Damaged") takes +0x30 ; UseNemesisForgeNemesis (CapChief HighPIS, "The Arena") takes +0x78 ; no valid payload - the job fills the ordinary way - 0xF636F0(FS, payload, job context) - 0xFD51A0(the region army's context, payload, ...) - 0x1BC05D0 - conversion 0x1C6369C - builder 0x1BBF928 - its Firebird look branch 0x1C04F20 - FM+0x520 = 4 - creation sim event NemesisAlly Levels (a PromoteEmpty event seats him) ; telemetry 0x1B2CC68 (event 42)

The title configuration's boolean nemesis forge is stored at [GM+0x6D48]+0xD1 by the configuration parser 0x18368B0 (at 0x1836A6F, through the bool reader 0x17C6F50; its neighbors are ssc version +0xC8 , garrison size +0xCC , challenges enabled +0xD0 , conquests +0xD2 , purchase system +0xD4 and ps2 epoch +0xD8 ). The same parser reads two keys named for the import's telemetry event, Events NemesisForgeImportEnabled and Events NemesisForgeImportSampled . The check 0x1B3ABFC has one caller, the world-entry routine 0x1E3E78 ( [ENTER WORLD HANG DETECTED] ). It returns while either stored captain is valid, and once the halt predicate holds: Interface/Predicates/GameState::IsPastNemesisForgeUsage , a StructuresUIGameDataPredicates { GameData/Variables::StoryState , GameData/Predicate::StoryState 300+ }, true from StoryState 300, the end of the campaign. Otherwise it tail-jumps to the request 0x1B3AA94, which returns unless the switch is set and no request is in flight. The request carries the player's FirebirdProfileID (when one is known), the platform user id, the platform and the web environment, and registers 0x1B32CD0 as its completion handler. FirebirdProfileID ( [0x2A364F0] ) is a static string initialized empty (0xC2D10, default at 0x1DB10E0) that no code writes (its 3 references are the initializer, its exit cleanup 0x10820B0 and the request), so the request identifies the player by platform user id only. The game therefore asks on every world entry until it holds a captain or the campaign is over. The online manager [GM+0x6D30] (see Saves, the store and the network layer) keeps the forge's state: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x28 u8, a request is in flight (set by 0x1B3AA94, cleared by 0x1B3D500) +0x30 the follower payload (0x48 bytes; valid byte at +0x38 ) +0x78 the nemesis payload (0x48 bytes; valid byte at +0x80 ) +0x468 the Invasion/Settings record ( HaltNemesisForgeCheckPredicate )

On success the handler 0x1B3D500 checks that element 1 of the result is a map (engine value type 6), reads its Follower and Nemesis lists, and passes the attributes map of each list's first object to the parser; on failure it only clears +0x28 . The parser 0x1B3A148 fills a payload object (vt 0x1FCB338, 0x48 bytes) from exactly 13 keys and sets its valid byte last: Payload Key Type Used by the conversion --- --- --- --- +0x08 (valid) u8 = 1 tested by every consumer +0x0C CombatTreeRecord name hash the class template and War's Combat/Tree +0x10 FactionRecord name hash never; the parser stores the tree's value here (0x1B3A1AC reads the tree key's register) +0x14 NameStringIdHash name hash the name, when War's string store has it +0x18 PersonalityRecord name hash FirebirdFactionPersonality (no fallback) +0x1C RoleRecord name hash FirebirdFactionRole , else War's own roles +0x20 RowRecord name hash never +0x24 ScarTypeRecord name hash FirebirdModelScarType +0x28 ISCurrent int never +0x2C MenaceLevel int the level +0x30 RandomSeed u64 the look, and the builder specification's +0x170 +0x38 IsBranded bool the player's follower (specification +0x17D ) +0x39 IsWarchief bool never +0x3C / +0x40 TraitList count, pointer to 32-bit hashes the traits Every record value is the 32-bit name hash of a Shadow of Mordor record. No look, color or memory travels: the look is rebuilt from the seed.

t: The two jobs and the two missions
x: Quest/Jobs/Definition (849 records) has three bools the job filler 0x1BD40C4 tests before filling a job the ordinary way: UseNemesisForgeNemesis (0x1BD3494), UseNemesisForgeAlly (0x1BD344C) and UseOnlineArenaOpponent (0xF729F0 - 0xFA2F60, the online arena). One job carries each forge flag: Job Flag Takes Setup - quest Ordinary builder Notes --- --- --- --- --- --- Rat3 Ally1 Ally the follower Rat3 Captains - Quest/Quests::Ratbag3 , "Damaged" (an allied captain while the player retakes the fortress from Brûz) Rat3 BackupAlly1 (all 5 trees, Captain armor, MinLevel 12, enters through Builder EnterHierarchy Rat3 ) row rank Captain, a living player follower, no ologs; reward Ratbag3 ProtectAgainstForgeAlly , a marker the hierarchy-duel jobs NemesisAlly Other exclude CapChief HighPIS Nemesis the nemesis Gon2 Fighters - Quest/Quests::Gondor2 , "The Arena" (Minas Ithil's arena) CapChief HighPIS (5 trees, Roles who are unimportant , MinLevel 14, reward GP Gondor2 Cap1 ) AlwaysUseBuilderRecord ; the setup awards intel level 2 With a valid payload the filler makes the captain, fm = 0xF636F0([GM+0x6C68], payload, job context) , keys the job to him ( {FM+0x178, FM+0x174} ) and sends the telemetry event 0x1B2CC68( [GM+0x6D18] , fm, is follower). Without one, the job's builder record makes an ordinary captain, so both missions play the same either way, and the forge only ever showed in those two missions, before StoryState 300. The missions' world scripts stage the result (2 classes, 7 of the 2,679 script bodies): - "Damaged" ( worlds\retail\island\sectionsandlayers\narrativequests\ratbag3.scripts , class ratbag3 RA03 SO Script , method Follower1Spawn , prefab followercage.prefab06c ): the ally waits in a cage. The script fires the faction event AddNemesisAlly (one level more and the sim-event tag NemesisAlly , which is never removed; the member is the ambusher). It adds the sim-event picker NemesisAlly EnterHierarchy ( Faction.AddFactionSimEventPicker : the duels DuelIntoHierarchy NemesisAlly and NoFol that bring him into the hierarchy) and gives Item Quirk Fearless , Item InfiniteBleedOut and GP Nemesis PreventDespawnAttacks . - "The Arena" ( worlds\retail\minasithil\sectionsandlayers\narrativequests\gondor2.scripts , class gondor2 Go02 SO Script , method Captain4Spawn , prefab gondor2 gangspot.prefab06c ): the nemesis is the fourth captain. The script uses GP Gon2NemForgeCheck (a saved marker item with no data test of its own) and NemesisStory NemesisForge AuxBanner IT (saved; its UI data NemesisStoryUI NemesisForge , name UI Nemesis Forge = "Nemesis", gives his nemesis story a banner), plus the arena champion items. The forge's own records: - 11 Faction/Events/Events ( AddNemesisAlly , AddNemesisAllyLevels , and the DuelFrom NemesisAlly , PromoteDead NemesisAlly and PromoteEmpty NemesisAlly families); - 5 Faction/Events/SimEvent ( DuelIntoHierarchy NemesisAlly , NoFol , NemesisAlly Levels , PromoteDead NemesisAlly , PromoteEmpty NemesisAlly ); - 3 sim-event participants and 3 quest jobs ( NemesisAlly , NemesisAlly Other , NemesisAlly Other NonFol ); - 2 sim-event pickers ( NemesisAlly EnterHierarchy , NemesisAlly Levels ); - the tag NemesisAlly with its list and tag mod; - 110 NemesisForge Role titles in Faction/Roles/Definitions , the War targets made for Mordor's titles.

- The pool. 0xF636F0(FS, payload, r8) takes the current region's army ( FS+0x1B8 - its context) and tail-jumps to 0xFD51A0(context, payload, r8). That allocates a member in the army's pool (0x1BD2E20; r8 is the job context, 0 from the console), sets FM+0x178 and, when empty, FM+0x180 , and calls 0x1BC05D0; it removes the member again when his name hash is one of five keys reserved for Ratbag. - The conversion 0x1C6369C fills the builder's specification: Input Conversion Specification --- --- --- tree the template (0x1C76C68) and War's Combat/Tree (0x1C76C0C, 0x1C4EDC0), both found with the same hash class seed copied +0x170 personality FirebirdFactionPersonality.KrakenPersonality (0x1C76F10; no row maps to nothing, 0x1C62B24) role FirebirdFactionRole.KrakenRole (0x1C770BC); a hash with no row is searched again in War's Faction/Roles/Definitions by the same hash, so a Mordor title War also has comes through as War's +0x148 level max(MinXPLevel, MenaceLevel + 1) - 1 (0x114FFD0 is an unsigned maximum; every template's MinXPLevel is 14, so never below level 13, shown 14) +0x178 IsBranded copied +0x17D name kept (0x1C62ABC) only when War's string store has the hash (its slot 8, a has-test); otherwise the builder gives him a War name scar type FirebirdModelScarType.KrakenScarType (0x1C77158) +0x158 traits each through FirebirdFactionTrait.KrakenTraitPicker (0x1C774B8; a trait with no row skipped) - 0x1C62AA4, then the template's TraitMarkers ( Marker OrcRarity Legendary , 0x1C4EE48) - The builder 0x1BBF928 then runs as for any builder-made member, and for an import its Firebird look branch 0x1C04F20 (below). - The creation mark FM+0x520 (u8, saved by 0x594788 and loaded by 0x1BC0F2C) records how a member was made: 0x1BC00C8 writes 0, 0x1BC02AC 1, the builder build 0x1BBF928 2, the preset path 0x1BC06C0 3 and the forge's 0x1BC05D0 4, after the builder's 2, so an import reads 4. - The introduction. The template's CreationSimEventPicker NemesisAlly Levels (job NemesisAlly , tag list NemesisAlly ) runs the sim event NemesisAlly Levels : participants NemesisAlly , PromoteEmpty events, the subject always wins, world-UI presentations, nav markers always shown. That event seats him in an empty seat; the payload's RowRecord is never read. How the tables are searched. vt 0x1FBD460::vf3 stores the categories the import uses at 0x26FFEE8 .. 0x26FFF28 (templates [0x26FFEE8] , roles [0x26FFF18] then War's own [0x2701D70] , traits [0x26FFF20] , personalities [0x26FFF28] ). Every lookup is a binary search of the category's record array by hash (0x1C77018: BinarySearch([cat+0x38], hash, [cat+0x28]) ) that ignores the category's "unsorted" byte +0x30 ; all six Firebird tables ship sorted. Rows the engine's gamedb patch merge appends to a category are therefore in the table the import searches, but are found only where their hash sorts. And because one hash picks both the template and the tree, a template can be replaced by name (the merge's override, 0x4BAB60 - 0x17675FC) but not added for a single captain.

The payload has no look; the builder's branch 0x1C04F20 (one caller, at 0x1BBFA6E) rebuilds one by replaying Shadow of Mordor's own generator over the Firebird tables, from RandomSeed : - Scale: t = float32(low32(xorshift64(seed))) 2^-32 (0x1C5B76C - 0x17956D4, shifts 13, 7, 17; the constant 2^-32 at 0x202ED88), Mordor's size rule. - The random stream: 0x1C76F8C(rng, min, max), the engine's 64-bit generator state = state 0x0BB38435 + 0x3619636B , value (state 32) / 4294967295.0 scaled into [min, max], starting at the seed itself. The same constants sit at 136 places in Mordor's executable and 86 in War's. - Picks (0x1C767E0): the weights summed in float32, nothing when the total is under 1e-4, one draw in [0, total], the first entry whose running sum reaches it; at most 32 entries, in record order. - Order, as Mordor draws: body (0x1C76238: the template's Models entries whose RequiredScaleRange , a float-pool pair, holds t and that have a body piece, weighted by the piece's SelectionWeight ), armor (a spent draw), head (0x1C763EC, the entry's heads), helmet (spent), hair (0x1C7632C, only with CanApplyHair : the head's hair pieces), legs (spent), one spent draw per NumAccessories , then nine colors. - Colors (0x1C7686C and its eight siblings - 0x1C7664C): a weighted pick of a Firebird color entry (0x1C76B24) gives a War color setup ( KrakenColorSetup ) and a color id ( ColorId , one of 15: Red, White, Fleshtone, Grey, Black, Blue, Brown, Yellow, Blue Rare, Charcoal, White Rare, Green, Brown Rare, Green Rare, Purple). War's entry of that setup with that FirebirdColorId (94 of War's 542 color entries carry one) is rolled (0x1158AC, HueDeltaRange ) on a copy of the state, and then the Firebird entry's NumRandomCalls draws are spent on the real state to stay in step with Mordor's color roll. Each entry's AppearanceTag is applied (0x2EA128). The palette entry is chosen through 0x2EBB4C before each tint: skin 0, eye 1, clothing 7, tattoo 3, paint 4, hair 2, armor 1 to 5 and armor 2 to 6; the leg-leather roll goes to a local the branch drops, so 8 of Mordor's 9 colors land. - What lands: the template's base model ( orc anim base ) at appearance +0x20 , the head record at +0x170 , the combat tree, the body type at +0x00 , and SetPieceSlot 0x4C62EC for slot 0 (the body's KrakenModelPiece ), slot 1 (the Head of the KrakenHead record), slot 2 (hair), with slot 7 cleared. Armor, helmet, legs and accessories are not carried: their draws only keep the stream aligned. For a Berserker the body is Smp Orc Buff Torso01 for t in [0, 0.5] and Smp Orc Stk Torso01 for [0.5, 1.0]: the Berserker's and the Defender's Slim entries have no body row, so War draws such a captain Buff. Templates without CanApplyHair (Berserker, Defender) never get hair. The entries are full per body: 11 of 11 hold 10 heads, every entry of one body lists the same 10, and Archer and Spearman have one Slim entry; the limit is the 30 head rows (24 War heads). The replay equals Mordor's own roll. Read live from 48 captains of a Mordor campaign army, 28 are "plain generated" (his head record is in the head list of an entry whose body is his body): his own seed draws his head for 23 of 28 and his body for 26 of 28. The control, seeds swapped between captains of the same class, draws the head for 17 of 253 (6.7%) and the body for 180 of 428 (42.1%, mostly the scale band). The other 20 wear heads that have no Firebird row (17 DLC1 , DLC2 and GI heads, GraugRider twice, OrcBuff16 ): Monolith's tables carry the base game's generated heads only. Because the look depends on nothing but the seed and the template, the seed in the payload decides the face an import wears.

The scar types map Wraith to Curse, Sack Head to Sack Head and Eyepatch to EyeGouge; Melee, Burn and Pin Cusion have no War type (3 of 6). What the tables can carry , over 48 captains of a Mordor save: traits 596 of 732 (of the 136 left, 83 are markers, 28 traits Mordor hides and 25 have no War counterpart); body 35 of 48, head 28 of 48, hair 10 of 14; armor pieces, legs and faction helmets none (War ships none of Mordor's armor). The import hands War a trait picker, and of the 34 Mordor traits that have a War trait but no Firebird row, none has a shipped single-trait picker (132 of War's 493 pickers hold one trait).

The two games never exchange data directly: no string in Mordor's executable names War ( Kraken , ShadowOfWar , Shadow of War or War's request: 0 hits, where the same scan finds 13 NemesisForge strings), War never reads Mordor's files, and War's request carries no Mordor profile id (above). Shadow of Mordor reached the publisher's earlier online platform, Agora ( Social/Agora , AgoraUserDataMgr , ProfileAttributeData ), Shadow of War its successor, and the publisher's servers joined the two through the player's account. Mordor's document does not use the payload's 13 key names (it writes CombatTree , Role , XPLevel where the payload has CombatTreeRecord , RoleRecord , MenaceLevel ): the reply was assembled by the service. The addresses in this section and the next are in Mordor's executable. A Conquest mode. In Shadow of Mordor the Nemesis Forge is Conquest/Definition::NemesisForge , one of eight Conquest definitions ( BG Easy , Medium , Hard , Random , SON LordOfTheHunt , Lithariel , BrightLord and NemesisForge ). It names the world WorldInfo::SeaOfNurnen , the game mode GameModes::NemesisForge , the army Orc Faction NemesisForge , the difficulty range Region SeaOfNurnen , the tutorial NemesisForge Intro and the active variable ConquestActive , with UseFactionSerialize true, no loot, no leaderboard, no award and an empty unlock predicate. Its completion counts (warchief and captain kills) and failure limits (time, deaths) are all -1: an endless sandbox with no goal (text Conquest Mode NemesisForge , failed header DLC ChallengeMode Failed ). The game mode (one of 13, with the Conquest modes' 38 fields: default world SeaOfNurnen , inventory type DLC1 , Type 4, UIAreaState 3, CanSave ) turns off, against Conquest, CanGainXP , CanSpendCurrency , AllowRuneSlotPurchases and AllowRuneSlotUnlockPresentation , and turns on EnableNemesisNavMakers , CanScriptRegionFaction , FOWRevealFastTravelMsg and a flag of its own, NemesisForgeQuitConfirm . Talion does not progress there; the army is the point. The army Orc Faction NemesisForge is serialized, tracks 32 members of the five orc classes, uses the event setup OrcFaction NemesisForge (the standard Active events) and has the rows NemesisForge Row warchiefs (5 seats), 2 (8), 3 (7) and 4 (5) at Sea of Nurnen locations. CanPopulateNemesisForge is true on exactly the two campaign armies, Orc Faction BG and Orc Faction SoN (of 12 armies; false on the downloadable and Conquest armies), and NemesisForgeFromThisFaction only on the forge army. Of Mordor's 503 quests, 65 list the forge army among their required factions, all of them Sea of Nurnen side missions (trials 5, duels 10, beast hunts 5, riots 5, executions 5, assassinations 5, recruitment 5, feasts 5, betrayals 8, outcast rescues 12). In this mode the Army screen has two states of its own, NemesisNonBranded and NemesisBranded ( MemberState::NemesisForge requires the game mode): a living member whose Nemesis state is true, split by BrandedTarget false or true. The main-menu entry MM NemesisForge registers four handlers in the main menu's table (0x68C1E0, through 0x5E68B0), by kind: - 0, the enable gate 0x688F30; - 4, the start 0x689F80 (the mode found by the name "NemesisForge"); - 2, the card 0x68C1B0 - 0x68B940 (a save card: an empty-save field, a Nemesis field, DLC NemesisForge Available Desc , the save status, an install-progress check); - 6, a dialog (0x68A400, id 0x7F) when the menu's +0xBFA is set. The restart and continue prompts are 0x689390, and the pause page Pause Skills NemesisForge (0x6A8770) tests the mode by name. The gate reads the active user ( p = [base+0x18F1228]+0x10 , slot = u32 [p] , 6 = none, user = [[[p+8] + slot x 8] + 8] ), takes the object at [user+0x3A0] (getter 0x4E8790) and opens only when its bytes +0x1BB and +0x1BC are both non-zero. In a running Mordor at its main menu both read 0, so the entry is closed; the only instruction in the executable with displacement 0x1BB is the gate's own read (0x1BC has 116), so the code that set them must have written through a wider store, a copy or a table. Debug tools. DebugSpawnAI (0x53AD00) holds a forge-nemesis key at +0x178 and a forge-follower key at +0x188 ( {faction record, index} , tested by 0x868F90) and offers "Spawn NemesisForge - Nemesis / Follower"; the debug command DebugSpawnAI.NemesisForge.FetchNemesis is described as querying the forge nemesis from Agora. A single captain can be saved to and loaded from an .orc file through Profile/Commands::DebugFactionMemberSave , Load and List , enabled only in the debug command sets (menu layers FactionMemberSave , FactionMemberList , FactionMemberLoad , linked from no normal menu).

The captain document, the form a Mordor captain is written in, has 99 keys. Its writer 0x8558C0 writes 54 keys from the member: - FactionRecord ( +0x58 ), FactionID ( +0x54 ), NPCProfileGuid ( +0x2F0 , u64), RowNumber (the index of his row record +0x88 in his army's Rows , or 0xFF), ColumnNumber ( +0x3A0 , u8) and CanSave (always 1); - CombatTree ( +0x60 ), Role ( +0x2B8 ), RandomSeed ( +0x48 ), Personality ( +0x90 ), NameStringIDHash ( +0x50 ), Name (its text), Location ( +0x2C0 ), XPLevel ( +0x340 ), TraitLevel ( +0x344 ) and PlayerKills ( +0x348 ); - twenty bits of the flag dword +0x3A4 ( IsDead 2, KilledByPlayer 3, CanResurrect 4, PresentedToPlayer 5, SpawnConditionComplete 9 and its previous value 10, HasVow 12, IsSevered 17, IsSquealer 18, GangLeader 19, GangLeaderMatchClass 20, HasNemesisTrait 21, IsMockDead 23, RevengeTarget 26, WasEverPreset 27, OnlySpawnWithBoss 29; IsResurrected = bit 0); - one Trait key per trait ( +0x70 ), the interaction scores ( +0x384 / +0x388 ) and one FactionEvent key per history entry ( +0x2A0 , stride 0x10); - OverrideCharacterModel ( +0x98 ), IntelDataLevel ( +0x3AA ), SpawnCondition , PreSetRecord , Purpose , PurposeStringIDHash , PurposeTimeOut , ResurrectionScarType ( +0x2D0 ), AppliedScarType ( +0x2D8 ), LastDeathType , the encounter indices, CanInterrogateAbout , ResurrectionCount ( +0x394 ), LastDeathCharacterType , LastDeathAttack and LastDeathPlayerKiller . Then come two scar keys ( CFactionMemberScars Scar / Brand , from +0x290 / +0x298 ) and the look block's own 43 keys: - 20 records ( SMC BaseModel , BodyModel , BodyModelOriginal , BodyFlairModel , HeadSimpleModel , HeadModel , LegsModel , HelmetModel , FactionMemberHelmetModel , HairModel , ArmorSet , ArmorModel1 to 4 , AccessoryModel1 and 2 , HeadScarModel , BodyScarModel , ScarSetup ); - 9 ARGB colors ( SkinTint , EyeColor , ClothingColor , TattooColor , PaintColor , HairColor , ArmorColor1 and 2 , LegLeatherColor ; alpha 0xFF = shown, as in War); - 12 mesh-group bytes, written as four keys each; - up to 4 appearance tags and up to 8 flairs. Its users are the faction save (0x8EE2B0, FACTIONDATA ), a debug export of one captain to a <name <date .orc file (0x91A800) and the presentation recorder (0x5FBA10, a text file). The number writers differ in sign: 0x5F9BA0 stores type 3, printed "%s = %lu" , and 0x5F9BE0 type 4, printed "%s = %ld" . The document is read back by 0x855F70, which also takes the member's index, army, row, seat and GUID. Mordor's own apply over an existing member is the reader 0x863040 (675 instructions; used by its save load, the .orc load 0x91ACB0 and the presentation load 0x5FB6E0), which reads 44 of the 54 member keys and then the look (0x886830). A missing key resets its cell (every getter defaults to 0), and the trait and event lists are emptied before their keys are read, so an apply is a whole document. Exceptions: IntelDataLevel only ever rises, and CanResurrect , ResurrectionScarType and AppliedScarType are written by the writer and read by no code. The reader never touches the member's index, army, row, seat or GUID. The document is text: lines split on \n , every space, tab and carriage return removed, starts a comment, [Name] opens a section, and keys and values keep 63 characters.

t: War's documents for a whole member
x:
War keeps four doors through which a whole member can be written or read: the binary save (0x594788 / 0x1BC0F2C, see The Nemesis system), the online member document (exporter 0x1BC5044, importer 0x1BC21B4, 57 keys read), and a capitalized member document with a writer 0x1BC45A8 and a reader 0x1BC159C. The last one descends from Mordor's: of the reader's 61 key and node names, 29 are spelled exactly as in Mordor's 54, but War groups them into nodes where Mordor is flat. Two document classes. The SAVE document (constructor 0x18786F0, 0x18 bytes; nodes 0x40, properties 0x60, values 0x70) is built by the writer's API (add child 0x1878CA0 and the setters); the LOAD document (constructor 0x1878608, 0x30 bytes: a parser-state stack, then the top nodes; nodes 0x20, properties 0x20, values 0x108 with a 0x100-byte text) is read by the getters (find child 0x18791F0 / 0x1879358). The only bridge between them is text: - Writing: a named node 0x187A580 writes "
" NAME " = {
" , its properties one tab deeper, then "}
" ; a property 0x187A654 writes "%s = " and its value, or for several values "%s = [
" , one per line, then "]
" ; a value 0x187A824 writes a record as its name ( [rec+0x20] when [rec+1] & 2 , 0x18BDB0, else empty), integers as %llu , %lld , %lu or %ld , booleans as True / False, a string's first 0x7F characters, and a child node in braces. The text save is 0x187A3CC (0x187AAFC - fwrite ). - Reading: the text load 0x1879AC4(path, unused, callback, context) opens the file and the parser 0x1879B48(document, {begin, end}) splits lines on 
 ; 0x187A2F4 strips every space, tab and carriage return and comments; a normalized line index reaching 0x400 is the engine's assert. The reader is a whole-member re-initializer. 0x1BC159C(fm, node) reads these nodes: - Identity ( CombatTree , Role , PreviousRole , BuilderInstance , Tribe , RandomSeed , Personality , NameStringIDHash , CharacterModel , PreSetRecord ); - Flags ( Location , LocationArea , XPLevel ... PlayerFleeCount , 24 flag bits through the bare bit setter 0x1156740, IntelDataLevel (raise only), RevengeType , Purpose , ResurrectionCount , the last-death keys and the scar types); - PIS , Relationships ( BossID ), EventHistory , SMCStorage , HierarchyMenuOverrides , Inventory and Traits . A record is read by name from one category table per key (0x187985C: the name's hash, then a binary search of [table+0x38] over [table+0x28] ; trees [0x2700960] , roles [0x2701D70] , personalities [0x2701A88] , models [0x27018B8] , presets [0x2701D08] , tribes [0x2701D80] ) and stored without a null test; inside a node a missing key writes null, and a missing node is skipped. Between nodes it always destroys his relationship objects, and it frees his appearance object and makes a new one before SMCStorage (0x2EB59C, 0x2EB490, 0x2EB56C at 0x1BC1D19 .. 0x1BC1D42, so [FM+0x2D8] changes). It also destroys and rebuilds his 25 items and re-dresses him (0x61BAD4), and empties his active traits and re-adds his pickers (0x7CD03C; the trait rebuild decides every slot again). A partial document therefore leaves him with an empty look. Its last step, 0x1BC3554 (138 instructions), first acts under flag bit 1: it clears bits 1, 11 and 26 and unlinks his body ( FM+0x28 , the character at [FM+0x48] ) without despawn events. It then destroys the quest handles at FM+0x3B8 , sets FM+0x518 to 0xFFFF, clears bits 23 and 47 (and 6 and 46), and runs the trait rebuild with reason 0, the rarity and the importance; finally it zeroes FM+0x3A8 , +0x388 , +0x470 and +0x380 , sets FM+0x51C to 1 and +0x51F to 0, and applies Faction/Global.ModelFixups . Its callers are the member factory 0xF99FF0, the presentation loader 0x182AFBC, 0x1C619FC and 0x1C69B58; every chain that feeds it a document from outside starts at a console command, the debug member load or the [FS+0x250] request. Monolith's own brackets are 0x61AE80 / 0x7C9DC4 around it (the sync-action debugger's load) and 0x1B5F4B0(FS) after it (the load-member event). The member copy 0x1BB936C is not an apply: it unlinks the body and copies the seat, the army and the whole flag word. The look sub-reader 0x1C0546C(look, node) reads BaseModel , HeadSimpleModel , BodyModel , HeadModel , HairModel , AccessoryModel1 and 2 , BodyFlairModel , BodyScarModel , HelmetModel , HeadAccessory1 , ArmorShoulder , ArmorChest , ArmorArms , ArmorPants , ArmorLegs , LowLOD , HeadScarModel , the colors SkinTint , EyeColor , HairColor , TattooColor , PaintColor , Metal , Leather , Cloth , Bone , TrimColor and their Faction twins. Of these, 11 model keys and 5 color keys are Mordor's names without SMC ; the armor is cut differently (Mordor's set, ArmorModel1 to 4 and legs, against War's five armor slots). Dormant doors. The console command FactionMember.Load (0x1C5B9DC) parses the file, but its callback 0x1C5B4B0 only fetches the current target (0x16A550): the apply step is compiled out. FactionMember.Save (0x1C5BAC4) still writes FACTIONMEMBER SINGLESAVE through 0x1BC45A8 to a text file. The data-driven loader Faction/Events/Setup.LoadMemberEvent - 0x1B5D4BC - 0x1C61AD8(FS, fm, name) runs only while [FS+0x250] is set, and that read 0 in a live campaign. Its path goes through the platform storage interface [0x26FEFD0] slots 7, 15 and 17, wfopen s , a whole-file read and a binary parse, then FACTIONMEMBER - 0x1C619FC: the reader plus the row's DemoImportFactionEvents . The faction system's tick has an asynchronous form of the same request (0x1E2BC4 - 0x1E34FC). The GameDB still holds Profile/Commands::DebugFactionMemberSave (left key, left on the pad) and DebugFactionMemberLoad (right).

- NemesisForge.CreateFollower (0x1C775EC) and NemesisForge.CreateNemesis (0x1C77604) create the stored follower or nemesis at once through 0x1C77514. When the payload is valid, 0xF636F0(FS, payload, 0) makes the captain; then 0x1B5EE34(FS, fm) - 0x1C28018 makes him his army's interrogation subject (the context's +0x160 = his key, cleared instead when he is dead), fires the army's EventSetup.SetInterrogationSubjectEvent and refreshes the old and the new subject. The quest path takes that step for neither captain, and neither path seats him: the quest path leaves the seat to the introduction sim event. The commands are registered by 0xCC460 and torn down by 0x10892D0. - NemesisForge.Override.ClearAll is a console entry referenced only from a command table (0x267DA68). - Telemetry 0x1B2CC68 ( [GM+0x6D18] ) sends event type 42 ( NemesisForgeImport in the event-name table 0x716210) with is follower , npc role , npc type , npc advanced class , npc full name and npc guid , behind the telemetry switches. - Other names: a player-profile property User.OwnsShadowOfMordor (a data table at 0x266EDF8, no code use traced), Interface/Movies::FirebirdFrontEndLoop ( frontendloop.vid ), AI/Count::Firebird and Model/SimpleModelColorSetup::Firebird Orc Eye Color Grey .

- Why some Mordor captains wear a head their own seed did not draw (3 of the 28 plain captains): something in Mordor appears to re-pick heads after generation; reading Mordor's later head writers would settle it. - Whether War's 13 payload keys are a server-side rename of Mordor's document keys ( CombatTree - CombatTreeRecord , Role - RoleRecord , AppliedScarType - ScarTypeRecord , XPLevel - MenaceLevel ), and whether Mordor's Army-screen states NemesisNonBranded / NemesisBranded mark the nemesis and the follower that were handed over (non-branded as the nemesis, branded as the follower with IsBranded ); what sets a member's Nemesis state is not read. - Which code fills Mordor's forge army from the two campaign armies: the readers of CanPopulateNemesisForge sit behind Mordor's cached schema tables (its static schema 0x1974A40 is referenced only by its builder 0xA87AB0 and a data registry slot), and what the mode stored on the online platform, and how, was not found in the client. - The exact success reply: element 0 of the result list and the value types used for the 13 keys (the parser's readers accept any integer tag through 0x7DFBF8). - What removes an imported member that no sim event has seated: of six captains imported through the console route and left unseated, five were gone minutes later and their members reused. Two candidates: the next import's interrogation-subject step, or the pool's recycling of its least important unseated member at the next allocation. - What creates members with creation marks 0 (0x1BC0084 - 0x1BC00C8) and 1 (0x1C1CDAC - 0x1BC02AC). - What NemesisForge.Override.ClearAll clears, whether User.OwnsShadowOfMordor gated anything, and what the two mission scripts do with GP Gon2NemForgeCheck and the banner item (only the names the scripts hold were read, not their lines). - Whether anything besides the member holds the appearance object the member reader frees: a world body draws from its own copy (the bind copy 0x40EF82 - 0x2EBA60).

t: Captain appearance: bodies, armor, color and scars
x: A captain's look is a small appearance object built from his seed and his class, then dressed by the items his class kit, army, tribe, title, personality and scars give him. The same object feeds the Army screen's copies and, through the character's visual, the body in the world; the items, not the object, are what the engine keeps and re-applies.

The appearance object is a separate allocation at [FM+0x2D8] (save key SMCStorage ; see The Nemesis system). It is built by the SimpleModel builder 0x4C5194, written piece by piece by SetPieceSlot 0x4C62EC, and copied field for field by 0x2EBA60, which fixes its layout: Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- +0x00 u32 body type (2 Slim, 3 Buff, 4 Stocky, 5 Olog; Easterlings use 12) +0x08 / +0x10 vector appearance tags, 16-byte entries {tag record, u32 count} +0x20 record the base Model ( Model/SimpleModel.Base : orc anim base , olog anim base ), which carries the skeleton +0x28 record[23] piece slots ( Model/SimpleModelPieces , 1,727 records) +0xE0 record[15] design cells ( Inventory/ArmorData ), indexed by armor slot +0x158 / +0x160 vector material-override records added by the tattoo and paint rolls +0x170 record the head record ( Model/SimpleModelHeads , 335 records): the face +0x178 u32[17] the color palette, ARGB ( 0xAARRGGBB ); alpha 0xFF = set A spawned character's visual carries a structure of the same layout at [visual+0xB8] (see Characters). The object is 0x1C0 bytes. The FactionMember constructor 0x1BB4C1C creates it through 0x2EB490 ( malloc(0x1C0) , constructor 0x2EB4B8) and moves it into FM+0x2D8 (0x2EB56C). The heap block header in front of it reads 0x1CB on 60 of 60 seated captains. Nothing past +0x1C0 belongs to it: the next heap block starts there (an inventory item instance, vt 0x1FDABF8, in 20 of those 60 cases). The head category Model/SimpleModelHeads is held in the category-cache slot 0x26FFDC8 (see GameDB), which 0x1C05970, 0x1C0546C and 0x1C0606C read.

Every design ( Inventory/ArmorData , 1,349 records) names an ArmorSlot . 0x36B700 maps it to a piece slot and 0x4C63F4 maps a piece slot back to its design cell, so the design cell index is the armor slot itself: ArmorSlot Designs Piece slot (offset) Content --- --- --- --- 0 99 7 (+0x60) helmet 1 454 8 (+0x68) shoulders (and the player's cloaks) 2 479 9 (+0x70) chest (and the player's armors) 3 54 10 (+0x78) arms 4 69 11 (+0x80) pants 5 27 12 (+0x88) legs 6 38 3 (+0x40) quiver (and scabbards) 7 50 4 (+0x48) accessory 8 7 13 (+0x90) body LOD 9 10 15 (+0xA0) head extra: metal jaw, gold tooth, masks, hoods, hair 10 9 0 (+0x28) body (no design cell) 11 18 1 (+0x30) head (no design cell) 12 35 none rings The enum EInventoryArmorSlot (0x7D6E9C, 15 values) names them in order: Helmet, Shoulder, Chest, Arms, Pants, Legs, Accessory1, Accessory2, LowLOD, HeadAccessory1, BodyReplacement, HeadReplacement, Ring, Accessory3, Accessory4. ArmorSlots 13 and 14 map to piece slots 16 and 17; no shipped design uses them (the 1,349 designs stop at ArmorSlot 12). The build itself fills slot 2 (hair) and slot 5 (body flair), which no design reaches.

The names are the engine's own. Slots 0-15 take theirs from the stored forms of an appearance, slots 16 and 17 from the slot enum 0x836D18, and the five FX slots from the character node table 0x2A40950. "Built on" names the object on which the model load places the piece: 0x4C71D0 sends slots 1, 14 and 15 to the head object when the character has one, and every other slot to the body model. Slot Offset Name ArmorSlot Design cell Built on In the save --- --- --- --- --- --- --- 0 +0x28 BodyModel 10 none body yes 1 +0x30 HeadModel 11 none head yes 2 +0x38 HairModel none none body yes 3 +0x40 AccessoryModel1 6 6 body yes 4 +0x48 AccessoryModel2 7 7 body yes 5 +0x50 BodyFlairModel none none body yes 6 +0x58 BodyScarModel none none body yes 7 +0x60 HelmetModel 0 0 body yes 8 +0x68 ArmorShoulder 1 1 body yes 9 +0x70 ArmorChest 2 2 body yes 10 +0x78 ArmorArms 3 3 body yes 11 +0x80 ArmorPants 4 4 body yes 12 +0x88 ArmorLegs 5 5 body yes 13 +0x90 LowLOD 8 8 body yes 14 +0x98 HeadScarModel none none head yes 15 +0xA0 HeadAccessory1 9 9 head yes 16 +0xA8 Accessory3 13 13 body no 17 +0xB0 Accessory4 14 14 body no 18-22 +0xB8 to +0xD8 FX1 to FX5 none none not built no The model load 0x4C67B0 builds a fixed list of slots, not a range: 0, 5, 6, 8-13, 3, 4, 16 and 17, and, through 0x103978, slots 1, 14, 7, 2 and 15. 0x36B248 walks all 23 slots but refreshes only pieces that already exist (0x4C6718 returns on an empty model slot). The copy 0x2EBA60, the compare 0x369F60 and the tint writer 0x36B430 also walk all 23, so a value in any slot is carried along whether or not it is ever built.

Eight routines write the piece array. SetPieceSlot, the copy 0x2EBA60 and the three load routines below carry records. The constructor 0x2EB4B8, the reset 0x2EA718 and 0xD587B0 only zero it; 0xD587B0 does so with inlined stores rather than the accessor and then calls the build, which is how a rebuild empties every slot the build does not fill. The executable supports that list in three ways. First, only 6 functions bounds-check a 23-element array: 0x36A018, 0x4C62EC, 0xFC93A0 and 0xFC93C0 on this array, and 0x1A9A068 and 0x1AE9F18 on others. Second, no block fill or block copy has a count of 23 cells or of the whole object, which holds two vectors and so cannot be copied raw. Third, following appearance pointers across 2,984 functions finds no other store to a record slot. That walk reproduces all 48 calls to the write accessor 0xFC93A0, but it does not follow virtual calls. SetPieceSlot is always called with a known slot: Caller Slots --- --- the build 0x4C5194 0-5 and 7 the item application through the ArmorSlot map (0x61BBC4, 0x4C61BC) never 2, 5, 6, 14 or 18-22 0x619C1C, for Inventory/Flair/BodyModelReplace (3 records) BodySlot 0 is slot 1, and 1 is slot 0 0x1C049D4 empties slots 7-13 the Firebird import 0x1C04F20 0, 1, 2 and 7 0x79B700 0, 1 and 2 0x103CB8 1 SetPieceSlot(appearance, slot, piece, design, visual) returns early when the slot already holds that piece. Otherwise it removes the old piece's appearance tags (0x4C64EC), adds the new piece's (0x4C647C), writes the design into its cell and, when a visual is passed, swaps the piece on that visual as well (0x4C6C8C, 0x4C7274).

t: The slots the game barely uses
x: - Slot 5, BodyFlairModel , comes from the BodyFlair of a Model/SimpleModel entry. Of the 207 entries, 4 have one: Zhoja and Zhoja Skirt ( Zhoja Flair ), GraftEltariel Wraith and GraftEltariel DarkWraith ( GraftEltariel Wraith Cloak ). No orc or olog entry does. - Slots 6 and 14, the scar slots, come from Shadow of Mordor, which stored SMC BodyScarModel , SMC HeadScarModel and SMC ScarSetup together and filled them from Model/Scar/Setup (45 records), Model/Scar/Scars (122, such as Orc Head06 Burn and Orc Slim Head04 Eyepatch ) and Model/Scar/Types ( Wraith , Burn , Pin Cusion , Sack Head , Eyepatch , Melee ). No Model/Scar category ships in this game: scars are items under Combat/Scar (see Captain scars and the return from death). The slots remain in the array, the model load and every stored form, but no run-time route fills them, so only a stored value can. The slot enum still lists BodyScar and skips 14. - Slots 16 and 17, Accessory3 and Accessory4 , are the third and fourth accessory slots, which Mordor's table does not have. The engine groups them with slots 3 and 4: on the player's animation commands HIDE ACCESSORIES and SHOW ACCESSORIES (0x4CD070), 0x1BEA070 removes all four pieces from the model and 0x1BEA544 restores them from the appearance.
