No design uses them and no stored form carries them, so shipped content leaves them empty. - Slots 18-22, FX1 to FX5 , also come from Mordor, whose piece table numbers them 13-17 and whose stored fields omit them. No routine fills them or builds a piece there: the model-piece creator 0x4C72B4 is reached only with a known slot up to 17, or with an empty piece from 0x1D641C4. SetPieceSlot with a visual would build one (0x4C6C8C, 0x4C7274), but no caller passes such a slot.

Inventory/ModelHide (7 records) hides slots and weapon slots by count. 0x1C68F08 keeps one counter per slot, 18 of them, and calls 0x1BEA4AC when a slot's visibility changes. Its ModelSlots values use the slot enum 0x836D18, which has 17 names: Body 0, Head 1, Hair 2, Accessory1 3, Accessory2 4, BodyFlair 5, BodyScar 6, Helmet 7, ArmorShoulder 8, ArmorChest 9, ArmorArms 10, ArmorPants 11, ArmorLegs 12, LowLOD 13, HeadAccessory1 15, Accessory3 16, Accessory4 17. Meatshield , Bound Prisoner and FailSpy Balcony hide Accessory1 . Blinded Dissolve lists 15 of the names in alphabetical order, all but Accessory3 and Accessory4 , so those two stay visible through it.

0x47888D0 fills a static table at 0x2A40950: 23 rows of 0x30 bytes, each with a name, readers for the <name Visible and <name AnimatedShape properties, two accessors and the Visible key. The rows run Body, Head, Hair, Accessory1, Accessory2, BodyFlair, BodyScar, Helmet, Shoulder, Chest, Arms, Pants, Legs, LowLOD, Accessory3, Accessory4, HeadScar, HeadAccessory1, FX1 to FX5. 0x1D641C4 and 0x1D67D20 index a model directly by row, so rows 14-17 do not line up with slots 14-17: Accessory3 Visible acts on slot 14 and HeadScar Visible on slot 16. Rows 18-22 are what ties FX1 to FX5 to slots 18-22. In live inspection of a running game, slots 6, 14 and 16-22 were empty on all 527 captains (slots 8 and 9 held a piece on 514) and on 65 spawned characters, and no model of 66 spawned characters had a piece in slots 18-22. None of these slots therefore holds anything in normal play. They are not inert, however: a record written to slot 5, 6, 16 or 17 of a captain's appearance is built on his spawned character alongside slot 4.

An appearance is stored in three forms, and all three stop at slot 15, so slots 16-22 do not survive a save and reload. - The save. The pool serializer 0x59460C writes each member through 0x594788, which hands the appearance to 0x36BA30: +0x20 , +0x170 , slots 0-15, design cells 0-5 and 8, the 17 colors and the material-override list. 0x1C0606C reads the same fields back. Design cells 6, 7 and 9-14 are not stored. - The document form uses keys such as smc body piece record , smc bodyfair piece record , smc bodyscar piece record , smc headscar piece record and smc accessory1 piece record . It is written by 0x1C06810 and read by 0x1C05970. - The property form uses the names in the table above. It is written by 0x1C06444 and read by 0x1C0546C. The member document that the exporter 0x1BC5044 writes for online publishing carries the appearance in the document form under SMCStorage.smc storage (35 keys): BodyType , smc bodymodel record (the base model), smc headModel record (the face), the 16 smc piece record of slots 0-15, color words for palette slots 0-14 and smc storage appearancetags . Its Inventory part lists each item by record hash ( fmi equipment list , with fields such as Item , WeaponData , ArmorData , Affixes and Source ), the color list ( smc flaircolor list ) and the look-record list ( smc nonequipment record list ). The export omits slots 16-22, the design cells, the material overrides, palette slots 15 and 16, and FM+0x180 . The importer 0x1BC21B4 reads SMCStorage into the appearance (0x1C05970), then the inventory (0x1C112F8), and then always re-dresses the captain from the items (0x61BAD4, below), so an armor cell that differs from the item under it never reaches another player's game.

Every member build runs the same sequence: 1. Parameters. 0x577190 clears a parameter block and 0x1BEA190 fills it from the member: +0x00 the seed FM+0x168 , +0x250 a size fraction (below), +0x210 the class model FM+0x278 , +0x228 personality, +0x238 role, +0x240 row (a story character's DisplayFactionRow when he has none), the active traits, and the class kit's appearance-tag setup from the combat tree FM+0x188 (0x576FFC). 2. The SimpleModel. 0x4C5194(appearance, params) takes Character/Models.SimpleModel of the class, adds the class kit's appearance tags (0x6FEA04, 0x1C06064), then rolls body, head, helmet, hair, colors, accessories and flair (below). 3. Items. 0x1C10F00 empties the inventory (0x1C7BF4: every slot, the color list and the look-record list), then 0x1C10AB0 gives, in order, the personality's Items , the role's Item list, the role's ScarType items, the tribe's Item list and the class kit's ItemsFactionMember , then the kit's named list for a follower ( Named PlayerFollowerItems ) or an enemy ( Named SauronFollowerItems ), chosen by flag bit 27. 4. The army outfit. 0x61BA74 adds pieces of the army's outfit by level and rank (below). 5. Apply. 0x61BAD4 writes every item's look into the appearance object. The builder build 0x1BBF928, the preset build 0x1BC06C0 and 0x1BC00C8 run these steps inline (the builder build reaches step 4 when it sets the member's level). RebuildDirect 0x1BC3AA8(fm) runs the whole sequence on an existing member. Its only caller is 0x1C15B0C, which is reached only from the console command Faction.RebuildSMC 0x1C5BDA8; that command rebuilds every member of the current region's army ( [FS+0x1B8] ) and then refreshes that army's Army-screen data.

Every roll of the look derives from the 64-bit seed FM+0x168 : Lcg(s) = s 0xBB38435 + 0x3619636B Unit(s) = (u32)(s 32) / 4294967295.0 The size fraction is Unit(Lcg(seed)) (plus 0.0). 0x4C5194 copies the seed once and passes that copy to the body roll 0x6A9F38, the head pick 0x2EDBB4, the helmet pick 0x701A98, the hair pick 0x6C8BB4, the color roll 0x2E9A2C and the accessory picks 0x6F4CA4 / 0x6F5614, in that order. Every draw advances it. A class whose body table draws a different number of times therefore also changes the face, hair and colors that follow. Item builds start again from the seed: the give path passes FM+0x168 to the item build, which draws from a local copy, so a member draws the same design from the same builder at every build. Color items ( FlairColors ) are rolled from the seed the same way, one stable color per member. The army outfit's choice of slots is the exception: it draws from the engine's global generator (0x1B3C6C). The weighted pick used throughout is the reservoir 0x1B3B90: a weight of zero or less never draws; otherwise s = Lcg(s) , r = Unit(s) (acc + w) , the entry wins when w r , and acc += w .

0x6A9F38 walks Model/SimpleModel.Models ( StructuresModelSimpleModelEntry ). For each entry, the weight is the BodyWeights[j] of the last RequiredScaleRange[j] (a float pair) that contains the size fraction; an entry with no matching range or no Body.Model is skipped. The chosen entry's BodyType goes to +0x00 and its Body to piece slot 0. The orc classes' tables: Class Buff (3) Slim (2) Stocky (4) --- --- --- --- Orc Infantry 1 over 0.3 - 0.7 1 over 0 - 0.33 1 over 0.67 - 1 Orc Defender 0.3 over 0 - 0.6 0 1 over 0 - 1 Orc Berserker 1 over 0 - 1 0 0.15 over 0.6 - 1 Orc Spearman 0.15 over 0.3 - 0.7 1 over 0 - 1 0 Orc Archer 0.15 over 0.3 - 0.7 1 over 0 - 1 0.01 over 0.67 - 1 OlogHai Infantry has one entry (body type 5). A Defender is Buff for about 14% of seeds (0.6 x 0.3 / 1.3); a Spearman or an Archer is mostly Slim. The bodies are Orc Buff Body001 , Orc Slim Body001 and Orc Stk Body001V2 . Changing a member's class therefore re-rolls his body at the next build, and a non-orc class gives a non-orc body and head. The roll reproduces the built body type of 144 of 144 living captains. Whether a class belongs to an orc or an olog is decided by its record, not by its name. AISimulationConfig is OlogHai on every olog class, whatever it is called (for example DLC Thrall , DLC Architect , GP Bruz , CommanderOlog and MachineDestroyerOlog ; all 281 Character/Models records were read). An OrcInfantry or OrcArcher config alone, however, does not make an orc: Gondorians, Easterlings, Serka, Zhoja, Torvin, Celebrimbor and the Family carry one too. ModelRecord is empty on 8 of the 9 DLC classes.

The in-world size uses the same fraction. 0x7F8488(fm) takes the member's birth army ( FM+0x180 , InitialFaction, else FM+0x178 ), the seed and the class, and 0x4E541C returns size = min + (max - min) Unit(Lcg(seed)) + army.ScaleAdditiveModifier where (min, max) is the class's Character/Models.AIScaleRange and the bonus is read from the captain's birth army, FM+0x180 . ScaleAdditiveModifier is 0.1 on all 7 army records read (see Characters, the player and the camera). 0x4E3CF0 stores the size into the character's scale component ( char+0x2738 , at +0x10 and +0x6C ) only when it differs by more than 0.01. Because body and size share the fraction, an Infantry captain is Slim at the small end of his class's size range, Buff in the middle and Stocky at the large end.

0x2EDBB4 picks a Model/SimpleModelHeads record from the chosen entry's DynamicHead list (the entry's Head list when that is empty), weighted per head. When the parameter byte +0x254 is set, it considers only heads whose DynamicBundle is available (0x2EDDFC); member builds leave it clear. The record goes to +0x170 and its Head piece to slot 1. The helmet comes from the record's Helmets (slot 7) and the hair from its Hair (slot 2, only when SimpleModel.CanApplyHair ). Every orc class lists the same heads per body: 24 Buff, 24 Slim and 23 Stocky, in two head families each. Unique heads are the 18 designs of armor slot 11. Given by a title or a scar, such a design replaces the head piece, while the head record (the face) and the hair stay. Smp Empty Set NoHair differs from Smp Empty Set only by the tag Tag I ARE BALD , which hides the hair. Where a head ships. A head's skeleton, mesh and animation file ship in the bundle of its face record: Model/SimpleModelHeads.DynamicBundle - a DynamicResource/BundleDefinition (group NPCHead , type Cha Head C ), for example bundles\modelcharacters\orcs\heads\head03\head03 c06\orc stk head03 c06.bndl . Its materials ship in the head family's shared g bundle ( orcs\heads\head01 to head03 , olog\heads\head01 and head02 hold one each; a tribe-head folder such as npc\heads\head metal holds one per body). The head piece itself links either that shared geometry (114 pieces link Orc Buff Head01 G = orc head01 g.bndl , which is loaded in every region) or nothing (56). Of the 335 face records, 306 name a piece of their own name and 168 carry a bundle. Of the pieces, 7 are named by more than one face (the I1035 Orc cinematic faces share the stock face's bundle). Head02 is linked the same way as head01, but its materials ship in orc head02 g , which is loaded only while one of the game's own head02 captains keeps it. The engine streams a head when its own build picks it: in one army, 18 of 18 natively dressed seated captains held their face bundle. A head's material set has 12 cells ( Model.MaterialSets - StructuresMaterialSet.SolidMaterial ): cell 0 holds the wrinkle material, 1 the base, 2 the distance material, 3 and 4 the gore caps, 5 and 6 the eyes ( eye orc.mat ), 7 the beard, 8 the beard decal, 9 the piercings, and 10 and 11 the ear burn. Up close (LOD0) a head draws cell 0, the wrinkle material on head cin . The next LOD draws the base cell ( head lod1 ), and further out the head draws the distance cell ( head lod1 ), according to a census of 99 orc and 7 olog head materials. Bodies draw body lod0 / body lod1 on scar materials and body noscar on plain ones. Eyes draw with cells 5 / 6 on 42 of 42 Head02 meshes, and beards and beard decals with 7 / 8 at every LOD on 532 of 532 meshes outside the Head03 family. Head01, head02 and head03 all bind head01's tint mask orc head01 m.tex .

0x2E9A2C(appearance, SimpleModel, generator; 361 instructions) rolls palette entries 0-14 from the SimpleModel's color setups, reading each setup live and storing through 0x2EBB4C. A color setup ( Model/SimpleModelColorSetup , 465 records) holds entries of StructuresSimpleModelColorEntry { SelectionWeight , Hue in degrees +- HueDeltaRange , Saturation / Value minimum and maximum 0-255, AppearanceTag }. The chosen entry's tag is added to the appearance. The palette slots roll from these setups: Palette slot Rolled from Slot Rolled from --- --- --- --- 0 skin SkinTint 8 bone ClothingTint2 1 eye EyeTint 9 trim Trim 2 hair HairTint 10 faction metal FactionMetal 3 tattoo TattooTint , if a roll passes TattooChance 11 faction leather FactionLeather 4 war paint PaintTint , if a roll passes PaintChance 12 faction cloth FactionCloth 5 metal ArmorTint1 13 faction bone FactionBone 6 leather ArmorTint2 14 faction trim FactionTrim 7 cloth ClothingTint1 15 faction war paint items only A passed tattoo or paint roll also picks one record of TattooMaterialOverrides / PaintMaterialOverrides into the list at +0x158 . Slot 16 exists in the array but no tint layer reads it. In the shipped orc tables, the skin setup Orc Infantry Skin Color (used by every orc class) is greenish (hue 63), flesh-toned (32) or bluish (187) at weight 1, with charcoal ( Tag DarkSkin ), albino ( Tag WhiteSkin ) and three more at 0.01. The eye setup Eye Color weights red 3 ( Tag RedEyes ), yellow 2 ( Tag YellowEyes ), blue 1 and green 1, and the hair setup weights brown, gray and black at 1 and white at 0.01. TattooChance is 0 on every class, and PaintChance is 0 on every class but the Berserker (0.5). Infantry, Defender and Archer share every setup; the Berserker has its own paint and tattoo, and the Spearman no clothing tint. The beasts' SimpleModels ( Warg , Troll , Fellbeast ) have every tint link empty (with PaintChance 1.0), so their palettes stay unset.

A design's ModelPicker is a list of StructuresInventoryArmorModelPicker { SimpleModelPiece , RequiredBodyType }. 0x61BC24(design, body type) returns the first entry whose RequiredBodyType is the member's body type or 0 (any body). A design with no piece for that body type empties the slot. Which armor fits a captain is decided by the body type at +0x00 , not by the body piece's name. On 162 living captains, 870 of 870 armor pieces in slots 7-12 whose name carries a body family carried the captain's +0x00 family; those captains include 10 Stocky and Olog captains drawn in the any-body Orc Buff Machine Body . Of the 926 armor-named pieces, 847 are put on some body by a shipped design; the rest are Easterling sets and DLC character accessories. Sets are named design families AD <Set <Slot , many with Bling variants (21 Bling designs). A Bling piece is the same model as its plain twin with a different mesh-part table (see Shoulder pads and appearance tags below). The nine tribe sets cover all four bodies, except that Regal has no Olog legs. A piece record carries Model , Tint (its tint layers), MeshIndexPairs , AppearanceTag , BaseWeight and ArmorDataDynamicBundle (its geometry bundle). A design also names its material bundle ( DynamicBundle , a link to a DynamicResource/BundleDefinition , for example Black Base ), its follower and enemy color overrides, and an OutOfMemoryBackups design, used when the piece does not fit the gear budget ( AD Black Shoulders names AD Sauron Shoulders ; see Resource streaming, "The gear budget").

Beyond the SimpleModel's own pieces, a captain wears armor only as items. The member's inventory inv = FM+0x50 is laid out as follows: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 + 8 x slot item instances of the 10 weapon slots (by the look's ItemSlot ; see Items) +0x50 + 8 x slot item instances of the 15 armor slots (by ArmorSlot ; accessor 0xFCA450 asserts slot < 15) +0xC8 / +0xD0 the color list: entries {u8 source, u32 palette slot, u32 ARGB} +0xE0 / +0xE8 the look-record list: Inventory/Items records with a body change or material overrides The give path 0x355474(inv, fm, item, source, appearance), 181 instructions long, works in five steps: 1. It refuses the item (returns false) when the member's combat tree's CharacterType fails the item's RequiredCharacterType / ExcludedCharacterType . 2. For each FlairColors entry ( Inventory/Flair/Color { ColorType < 17, ColorRecord }), it gets or creates the color-list entry of that slot (0x1C10E54) and rolls it in 0x1C11A74: the replace rule below, a weighted entry pick and an HSV roll seeded by FM+0x168 . 3. An item with an ItemBuilder becomes an instance. The build 0x649790 draws one WeaponData look and then one ArmorData design uniformly, sets +0x48 to the design and +0x30 to its ArmorSlot (15 when none), and the source goes to +0x100 . 0x61B868 then places the instance in its slot and adds its item's AppearanceTags . The give returns whether the equip succeeded and stops there. 4. An item without a builder is filed in the look-record list (once, 0x1162D40, de-duplicated by 0x7D9234) when it has a BodyModelChange or any PassiveMaterialOverrides . 5. Only such a builderless item then gives each of its PairedItems the same way, recursively, with the same source. Its own return value is whether it was filed, whatever its pairs did. PassiveFXSequencePicker is not read on this path. The give path has 13 callers, among them the army outfit 0x61BE74, AddScar , the role setter 0x1BC6698, the tribe change 0x1BC6718, the reward paths 0x351AF8 and 0x34FEB4, the build's item givers 0x1C10AB0 / 0x1C10F3C / 0x1C11B08, and itself (for the pairs). Each give reads the item's FlairColors rows and ColorRecord links live: there is no compiled copy on the path. Which item wins a slot. 0x61C238(new source, old source, new item, old item) decides whether an item may replace the one in a slot (and whether a color entry may replace another): Old source Replaced by --- --- 0 (empty) anything 1 / 2 a source of at least 1 / 2 3 a source above 3 4 - 10 a source of 4 or more whose item's FactionMemberItemReplaceValue is at least the old item's 11 and above nothing A new source of 11 never replaces, nor does the same item. The build uses the sources 2 (class kit), 3 (army outfit), 4 (personality), 5 (role), 6 (tribe) and 10 (scar). A trait's items come at 8 (0x355400; see Captain traits) and a reward's ItemsToGive at 9. FactionMemberItemReplaceValue is 0 on 5,003 of 5,618 items; the rest use values from 1 to 100 (10 on 247 items, 5 on 137, 2 on 87 and 20 on 44), and one item uses 9001. What the save keeps of an item. The item reader 0x1BF320C reads three record hashes into +0x38 Item , +0x40 WeaponData and +0x48 ArmorData , and derives +0x30 . 0x1C10FE0 then stores the source byte +0x100 only when it is below 11, so 10 is the strongest source that survives a reload: an 11 comes back as 0 and yields to anything.

0x61BAD4(inv, appearance) writes every armor-slot instance ( FM+0xA0 to +0x118 ) through 0x61BBC4: the design's piece for his body type (0x61BC24 / 0x61BC84) goes into piece slot 0x36B700( inst+0x30 ) with SetPieceSlot and no visual. Then it applies each BodyModelChange ( Inventory/Flair/BodyModelReplace , 3 records: a model picker by body type and a BodySlot , 0x619C1C) from the slot items and the look-record list, and copies each color-list entry ( {+0x04 slot < 17, +0x08 ARGB} ) into the palette. An armor slot with no item is skipped, so a piece written into the appearance under an empty slot stays. A piece written over a slot that holds an item is replaced by the item's design at the next re-dress. It runs far more often than a build (11 call sites and 2 tail calls): When Caller --- --- despawn of the member's body the NPC class's vt 0x1FB3640::vf17 (0x4A1764; it also runs DespawnWhileFleeingEvent ) - 0x355150(fm, character) when [FM+0x48] is empty or that character a reward gives items 0x351AF8 (from ApplyReward 0x3511F4), after ItemsToGive when 0x34FEB4 gave one (source 9) a title change the role setter 0x1BC6698 (tail call) a scar given or removed AddScar 0x7BB8C4, RemoveScar 0x1BC409C domination 0x7D52B0 a level or row change the army outfit 0x61BA74 (tail call), from SetLevel 0x35188C and the row placement 0x61B614 a member build or document load 0x1BBF928, 0x1BC02AC, 0x1BC06C0, 0x1BC159C, 0x1BF659C every online import 0x1BC21B4, right after it reads SMCStorage The local save load 0x1BC0F2C reads the item table (0x1C1115C) and does not call it, so a reloaded captain shows his saved cells until the first of the events above. An armor look therefore lasts only when it lives in the item of its slot, with inst+0x48 a design that puts the piece on his body and a source that holds the slot. A piece written into the appearance cells alone comes off at the next despawn, reward, scar, domination, level or row change, and is never seen online.

Each orc class kit's named lists give a base suit at source 2, the lowest priority. An enemy gets Sauron Chest , Sauron Pants , Sauron Shoulders , Sauron Arms and IT Faction Enemy Tint ; a follower gets Talion Chest , Talion Pants , Talion Shoulders , Talion Arms , FactionPlayerFollower and IT Faction Friendly Tint . An Olog's lists give Sauron Pants and Sauron Helmet , or Talion Pants , and Archers and Spearmen add their quiver. The kit's ItemsFactionMember gives the body LOD ( IT Orc Body LOD - AD Orc Body LOD ).

0x61BA74(fm) decides how many armor pieces a member wears and fills them from an outfit. The count comes from the army's Faction/Definition.ArmorSetup ( Faction/ArmorSetup/Default ). 0x61C940 walks its Entries in order and returns the ArmorPieceCount of the first entry whose MinLevel is at most the shown level ( FM+0x4B8 + 1) and whose RequiredRowRank list is empty or holds the row's rank: Entry MinLevel Rank Pieces --- --- --- --- 0 1 Overlord 6 1 30 any 6 2 22 any 5 3 16 any 4 4 10 any 3 5 5 any 2 6 2 any 1 A level-1 member gets none. The outfit is the tribe's ArmorSetOverride , else the role's ArmorSetOverride (2 of 914 roles), else the class kit's DefaultArmorSet (1 of 93 kits). Each is a Model/SimpleModelArmorSet (17 records) with an item and a weight per slot: Tribe Outfit --- --- Dark Black Base Outfit Feral Beast Base Outfit (no arms item) Machine Industrial Base Outfit Marauder Regal Base Outfit Outlaw Scavenger Base Outfit Slaughter Slaughterhouse Base Outfit Sorcerous (and its DLC poison variant) Mystic Base Outfit Terror Torture Base Outfit Warmonger, Bruz Warmonger Base Outfit (no arms item) Militant Fanatic Base Outfit (every item empty) Easterling, Gondor, Sauron, ShadowWar, Tribeless, Undead and NazgulTwins have none. Every tribe outfit weights chest 5, pants 4, shoulders 3, arms 2, legs 2 and helmet 1. The Feral and Warmonger tribes' own Item lists give Beast Arms / Warmonger Arms directly. 0x61BE74 lists the outfit's six slot items as candidates where the slot is empty or the outfit may replace what is there, judged at the outfit's origin (6 for a tribe outfit, 5 for a role's, 3 for a kit's). Slots held by an item it may not replace count toward the total. It then draws candidates by weight, one per missing piece, and gives each through the give path at source 3, so a drawn piece lands only on an empty slot or over the base layer. Besides the build, 0x61BA74 runs on a level change ( SetLevel 0x35188C) and from 0x61B614, which places a member in a row (it reads the row's Rank and EnableHenchmen ), so captains gain armor as their level and rank rise.

A title ( Faction/Roles/Definitions , 914 records) carries no look of its own: its Item list does. Among the roles, 725 list items, 685 list at least one item with an ItemBuilder (armor or weapon), 374 list an item with a look payload, and 6 carry a ScarType . An item builder's ArmorData list holds 1 to 40 designs. Of 5,618 items, 317 carry a look payload: PassiveMaterialOverrides 210 (decals, glow, hides), FlairColors 123 (palettes, including about 55 full colorways IT Tint ), MaterialSetVariants 71, PassiveFXSequencePicker 21 (auras) and BodyModelChange 3. Of these, 199 have no builder and live in the look-record list. - Role Pretender gives Tower Head ( BodyModelChange Tower HeadReplacement - Orc Buff Tower Head ), Tower Body (its design has a piece for body type 3 only: the four-blade back), Only LeftShoulder , IT empty head NoHair , IT AllBlack Tint , weapons and a quiver. Its predicates admit only a Buff-torso Defender. - Role OfTheSpiders gives Spiders Helmet (with the ears hidden by orc Hide Head Ears ), Spiders Arms , Spiders Accessory (whose effect picker carries the aura), a Mystic chest and a body-animation marker item. - Of the 914 roles, 70 empty armor slots with IT empty items ( Role Machine empties all six). A title change through the role setter 0x1BC6698 dresses the captain at once. 0x1BC63F8 writes FM+0x318 (and the old role to +0x320 ), forces the role's personality when it has one, and applies the role's ScarType through AddScar , its SimEventTagModList and its role event ( FactionEventOnSetRole ). 0x1BC6698 then gives each of the role's items at source 5 and re-applies the look (0x61BAD4). A plain write of FM+0x318 gives no items until the next build, but it is not inert: every reader of the role takes it from that cell live. When Reader What it takes from the role --- --- --- a spawn, without a build 0x4F0938 - 0x355AD8 - the item handler 0x1C0E0C the slotless Item s: material overrides, appearance tags, material-set variants every build 0x1C10AB0 every Item , the ScarType a row change 0x61B614 - 0x61BA74 - 0x61BE74 ArmorSetOverride the Army stage 0x410BC4 - 0x355894, the role from the summary's +0x140 the slotless Item s The title text is a separate read (see The Nemesis system, "Names").

The Machine's armor is its body. Role Machine gives 9 items: Machine Body , Machine Head , Machine BodyLOD and an IT empty item in each of the six armor slots. The rib cage, the riveted shoulder plates and the arm and leg plating are submeshes of Orc Buff Machine Body (piece slot 0), which draws the skin material plus four gear materials ( bodies\body machine\orc machine body , shoulders , legs arms , pants , on gear lod0 / gear alphatest lod0 ) from machine body m . Machine Body has no UIItemData , so the game names no armor for it, only the title. Title bodies. The armor-slot-10 designs name 14 bodies. Besides the standard and scar bodies, they are Orc Buff Machine Body , Orc Buff/Slim/Stk Infested Body , Orc Buff Tower Body , Orc Buff Flint Body , Orc Buff Tinder Body , Olog Buff Glutton Body and Olog Buff Dragonborn Body . The Slim and Stocky Machine bodies ship as pieces with their own geometry bundles that no design names. The elemental orcs' distance bodies Orc Buff Machine/Flint/Tinder BodyLOD are armor-slot-8 designs. A body that comes from an item ( Machine Body - AD Machine Body , armor slot 10) is written back at every re-dress and travels with the save and online. Whole outfits. In all, 20 orc pieces that a design puts whole into a single cell carry no slot word in their names: Sauron FullSet , Sauron faction , Talion FullSet and Talion faction (Buff, Slim, Stocky), Orc Buff Sauron Gondor1 , Black Grunt and Industrial Grunt (all armor slot 4, the pants cell), and Orc Slim Bone Full (armor slot 2). The tribe FULLSET meshes and the story characters' one-piece models (such as Orc Zog , CommanderOlog , Olog Thrall and the Acolytes) are not armor: no design and no SimpleModel names them. Names that disagree with the slot. In 42 orc and olog (piece, design) pairs, the piece's name says one slot and its design another. Underclothes , NazgulArm , the claws and the Blight arms are named chest, pants or arms, but their designs are armor slot 7 (accessory); Orc Buff Defender Shoulders and Orc Buff Backpack are chest designs.

t: Body model, body paint and body look
x: Three separate mechanisms change "the body": - The body model is the mesh in piece slot 0 and its LOD in slot 13. The base model ( +0x20 ) does not change with it; of the 70 body pieces, 16 are built for orc anim base . Body designs are the nine of armor slot 10, among them AD Body Scar , AD Machine Body , AD Glutton Body , AD Infested Body , AD Tinder Body , AD Flint Body , AD Dragonborn Body and AD BodyModel Forced Buff . - A body paint is a tint mask on the same mesh: a builderless item <Name BodyPaint whose MaterialSetVariants swap the body piece's material for one that binds the stock orc body001 d / n / s textures and only a different tTintMaskMap ( body001\uniquetints\orc body001 m <paint .tex , 2048 x 1024). The paint's pattern is the mask's B channel, the war-paint layer of the body tint Skin Cloth Warpaint Tattoo . The item switches that layer on with a PassiveMaterialOverride (such as BodyTintWhitePaint Slave ) that sets k fBTintAmount to 1.0 and a B specular tint, and colors it through FlairColors : Digger Orc Warpaint LightBrown , Black Blade Orc Warpaint Black , Slave Warpaint White , and Gravewalker and Unashamed Warpaint White plus Orc Skin Dark . Model/SimpleModelMaterialSetVariant (58 records) holds six families (Digger, BlackBlade, Gravewalker, Unashamed, Rogue, Slave), each with a variant for Buff and Slim (excluding Tag Olog and Tag Stk ), a Stk variant and a LOD variant; Slave has no Stocky variant. Orc Body Digger exists only as a variant, never as a mesh. Digger BodyPaint excludes Ologs, and <Name HeadPaint repaints only the generic heads ( Orc Head 01G / 02G ). The painted materials are scar twins ( body lod0 / body lod1 with the scar arrays), so decals draw on them. - A body look , such as the curse veins, consists of decals on the body's scar material (see below). Material-set variants stack. The item handler 0x1C0E0C - 0x730C70 keeps a reference-counted list at visual+0xD0 : the same record again raises its entry's count at +0x54 , every entry is re-applied through 0x730DBC, and removal is 0x1BEA358, called from 0x10C290. One item's variant therefore does not remove another's. The body masks, decoded at 512 x 256, cover the following shares of texels (B above 0.5 is war paint; A above 0.03 is the fourth layer, Tattoo): Mask B 0.5 A 0.03 --- --- --- stock orc body001 m 9.8% 8.5% (a knotwork tattoo) orc body001 m digger 2.9% 21.2% (a full-body vein network) blackblade / slave / unashamed 53.0% / 23.1% / 24.1% 100% (layer unused, filled white) gravewalker / rogue 18.6% / 20.2% 0% olog body001 tint m (BC1) - 100% The Tattoo layer is on only when a SimpleModel tattoo roll sets k fATintAmount , and every captain class ships TattooChance 0. The game's own Digger is the one that lights it. His class ( Character/Models DLC Digger - Model/SimpleModel Orc Digger ) uses Orc Buff Body001 , Orc Buff Head01 G , skin Orc Skin Albino , eyes Eyes Red and tattoo Orc Skin DarkPurple at TattooChance 1.0. His body veins are the alpha of orc body001 m digger , and his face's veins are the blue of heads\head01\uniquetints\orc head01 digger m.tex . On an olog the tattoo mask is solid, so that layer covers the whole body.

A worn piece's vertices name bones by the piece skeleton's own numbers. The engine turns them into the wearer's through one table per (rig, piece): the binding object [part+0x80] (vt 0x1DC7220, 0x2F0 bytes, constructor 0x702870, find-or-create 0x1CC280, key at +0x10 = hash(rig) hash(piece) << 32), whose u16 vector sits at +0x38 / +0x40 . Every wearer on that rig shares it, and one piece on two rigs has two objects with the same high half of the key (12 models, 50 parts). Each part's render object ( [part+0x48] , vt 0x1FFE3E8) holds a copy that the draw reads directly: the u16 table at +0x148 , the u8 table at +0x150 and the count at +0x158 , inside a member struct at +0x10 (vt 0x1DAB810, constructor 0x1BE460, which is why its own code addresses them as +0x138 / +0x140 / +0x148 ). The setter 0x1BFBB8 frees the old copy, keeps the u16 table and derives the u8 one from its low bytes. The render object's vf60, 0x4C11A4(render, u16 , count), copies a caller's table and queues 0x1BFBB8 on the render ring 0x272E8D8 (the same ring and commit, 0x251E00, as vf47, the material setter). The callers of vf60 are the part's resource-arrived callback (0x66C714 - 0x1BD968) and vt 0x1FE1A18::vf1 0x1BE1C0, both passing the binding's vector. An empty vector means no table at all (0x6D5CE4). The table comes from walking the piece's bone tree: a bone takes the wearer's number for the same name only when it and every ancestor exist on the wearer, and otherwise keeps its raw number. That rule reproduces the engine's tables on 128 of 128 entries (a by-name rule matches 57, the identity mapping 122). The table is not in the .mesh file. Talion's skeleton runs Null pNull Pelvis and no other rig has pNull , so on any other rig every bone below it keeps its raw number. The arms then bend incorrectly, and raw numbers past the wearer's bone count (32 of a Talion suit's on a 96-bone rig) index past his palette. A piece that finds no bone of its own on the rig, such as Talion's hair, comes out as the identity mapping and gets no table. Havok cloth reads the wearer's bones through the same table (see Cloth).

The piece's skeleton is [[part+0x70]+0x10] , and the wearer's is [[[part+8]+0x1D8]+0x10] (see Animation): Offset Meaning --- --- +0x38 nodes, 0x40 bytes each: byte 0 the parent (0xFF = root), byte 1 its own index, byte 3 the child count +0x40 bone count +0x58 / +0x60 {u32 hash, u32 index} pairs sorted by hash (P919 of the name; pNull = 0xB8AD19F7) +0x70 name pointers in number order Nodes are in level order: a parent comes before its children (3,047 of 3,047). Pairs whose index is at or past the bone count exist and are not bones (435 of 3,482), and a complete skeleton has exactly one in-range pair per bone (27 of 27).

The humanoid piece skeletons share one bind pose. Talion's suits sit within 0.2 cm (median) of orc base.skel over 82 shared bones, with limb rotations of 0.00 degrees; only the shoulder-pad helpers differ, R SPadX by 12 degrees. orc base.skel has 100 bones and player base.skel 128. The three orc body skeletons (Buff, Slim, Stocky) are one bind pose with every bone in the same place: only girth differs between body types. An orc piece skeleton is the whole orc rig, 76 bones in the body's runtime order. A piece whose table maps it therefore follows the wearer, and the difference that remains is surface volume. A Talion suit weights 2.1% of its vertices to bones the orc rig lacks ( Scabbard Joined , Belt 1/2 , loincloth) and has no hand weights. The p90 radius around the shared bind segments is 10.8 / 11.9 cm on a Slim / Buff orc's upper arm against 8.6 - 8.7 cm for the suits, and 18.3 / 22.1 cm on the torso against 26.6 - 27.0 cm. Of 77 non-orc torso pieces, the player's suits (Talion's and Celebrimbor's) fit 32 of 32, with no weight on missing bones and the chest within 1.9 cm. Eltariel's armors fit 0 of 19: 1.6 - 6.1% of the weight sits on bones an orc lacks ( R ShoulderX / L ShoulderX among them), and the chest lies 4.4 - 8.6 cm inside a Buff orc. The Gondorian pieces fit 9 of 10, and the Easterling, Serka, Baranor and Sauron pieces fit. Talion's suits are a single mesh part, so their MeshIndexPairs cannot split them, and their vertex alpha is 255 everywhere, so no sever mask takes their arms off. In player rhovaniont2 armor.mesh , group 0 holds the chest, shoulder plates, forearm guards, legs and boots (17,118 vertices), groups 1 and 2 the shoulder straps and the collar with a cloth proxy, group 3 a 4-vertex placeholder, and group 4 the baldric and belt. Of 32 readable suits, 24 carry no second UV stream at all. A mask is never a separate piece: it is part of a cloak model. Scabbards put all their weight on scabbard back / dagger sheath back , bones an orc lacks. Easterling armor pieces use the orc rig's bone names (on the heavy chest, 71 of 74 bones; only the collar bones are missing). Easterling armor is split like orc gear, but its chest pieces are strap and plate pieces worn over the body, whose mesh carries the torso clothing.

- The orc Druid legs ( orc buff/slim/stk druid legs.mesh ) share one geometry with olog buff druid legs.mesh (same vertex counts, bounds within 0.1 cm), re-exported against the plain orc bind. They measure 183 x 72 x 81 cm against 74 x 52 x 45 for Orc Buff Black Legs , so they skin from an orc's bones at Olog size. The orc Druid pants are the Olog pants with only the waistband lowered (up to 19 cm); the hem is left at the Olog's height, below an Olog's knee and at an orc's ankles. Their material sets are the Olog's. Among 510 orc pieces with an Olog twin by name, these are the only ones on Olog geometry. In the other direction, Olog Buff Apron Chest , the FaceCape chest and Olog Buff Master Helmet Head01 carry orc-sized geometry. - No orc twin by name exists for 22 Olog-only piece meshes: the Thrall set (helmet, shoulders, chest, pants), the Architect (helmet, chest, arms, head), The Beast (chest, arms), the Amputator, MetalBandage and Tailor helmets, the Skirt pants, the Shackles and Stitch accessories, and heads and bodies. AD Thrall Helmet / Shoulders / Chest / Pants list only an Olog piece. Every Thrall piece draws six material cells: the Mystic or Mystic-helmet material, thrall spider , and thrall webs or orc spiders accessory , each as a LOD0 / distance pair. - Where the game ships both, its own Olog-to-orc helmet fit is consistent: 28 helmet designs per body type carry both pieces, scaled about 0.48 - 0.52 across, 0.50 below and 0.61 above the Head joint, 0.45 behind and 0.66 in front. - Orc Buff Tower Body draws its four back blades in the same submeshes as its spiked harness, beside the Orc Buff Body001 skin, the far body and two gore caps. It has 16 submeshes and 34 LOD rows, and its material set holds 7 solids: orc body001 and its distance twin, two gore caps, orc atlas , and orc tower and its distance twin. Its skeleton (74 bones) binds the 20 bones that carry the blades within 0.033 cm of the Buff body.

t: Level of detail and material cells
x: Each mesh part's row in the piece skeleton is {u8, u8, f32 distance, u32, i32 -1} . On every piece read (7), the u32 is the index, in the Model's SolidMaterial list, of the material the part draws at that distance. Shipped orc armor uses cell 0 for LOD0 and cell 1 beyond (main parts [0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0] over 0 / 500 / 800 / 1200 / 2000 / 7500 cm), and the mesh's LOD table sends both of the first two distances to the LOD0 submesh. LOD0 vertices are 64 bytes and carry a second UV set, which gear lod0 draws: every vertex shader of gear lod0.fxo (3) and gear alphatest lod0.fxo (15) takes TEXCOORD1 , and those of gear lod1.fxo (7) do not. Distance vertices are 60 bytes. Orc Buff FaceCape Chest , the Druid legs (60-byte vertices at all four LODs) and the Druid pants keep cell 0 at LOD0 with no second UV set, so they vanish in close-up. A skeleton can list more LOD rows than its mesh has parts (the Thrall shoulders list 28 for 14 parts, some Head03 heads 54 for 24).

A shoulder piece's MeshIndexPairs are ranges of the model's mesh parts. Each is a StructuresSimpleModelMeshIndexPair { MinIndex , MaxIndex , RequiredAppearanceTag[] , ExcludedAppearanceTag[] }; the database holds 4,447 of them. 0x1B37F0 keeps the pairs whose required tags are all present in the appearance and whose excluded tags are absent, and picks one uniformly from a copy of the visual's seed ( +0x98 ). 0x1BD724 packs the chosen (min, max) at piece +0x56 (a min of 1 becomes 0), and the material object's vf38 0x1BD764 queues it on the render ring 0x272E8D8; the render side keeps it at (material+0x10)+0xB8 . On orc gear, the part a vertex belongs to is round(uv1.x x 10) : the rule is exact on the Slaughter parts 1-5 at all four LODs and on 26 of 29 Buff shoulder pieces. The mesh's arenas are LODs, not parts. The tags are Tag ShoulderBoth , Left Shoulder and Right Shoulder , given by items ( Both Shoulders , the Only items, some chests and scars). A Bling piece maps 2-2 to 1-2, 3-3 to 3-4 and 2-3 to 1-4 (parts 1 and 4 are the plates). Of 132 orc and Olog shoulder pieces, 80 have no both-sides layout. Tags are added by SetPieceSlot , by item equip (0x61B868 and 0x6E9174, from an item's AppearanceTags ), by the class kit at the start of a build (0x6FEA04) and by color entries; they are removed per piece on a swap. 0x2EA18C adds a count, and 0x6E90F4 subtracts a count and removes an entry at zero. A build adds the kit's and the colors' tags again without clearing, so counts grow with each build. The vector is saved ( smc storage appearancetags , P919 hashes; the save loader is 0x1C67944). Tags also select weapon models through StructuresInventoryItemModel.OverrideModels (0x3FF344): 0x1BFB1FC picks such a model when the wearer holds every required tag.

A scar is a set of items, not a model slot. AddScar 0x7BB8C4 gives one random variant of a Combat/Scar/Type and its helmet item at source 10, and re-dresses the captain. A variant's parts are decals on the head or the body (scar materials only), hides, and armor items that bare or replace the head, empty the chest or arms, or swap the body for its scar twin. Captain scars and the return from death describes the full system, which parts arrive and which never do, and how a return from death picks its scar.

A piece's Tint is a Model/SimpleModelTint (76 records) that maps the tint mask's R, G, B and A channels to palette slots, where index 16 means unused. The records are named after the slots they read, and 74 of 75 named records agree: for example, Skin Eye Warpaint Hair reads 0, 1, 4, 2 and Metal Leather FactionCloth Trim 5, 6, 12, 9, while Skin Eye Warpaint Metal reads Hair on A. Only skin layouts map a channel to Tattoo: 5 of the 76 (the orc body, the Machine bodies, two Easterling and the Gondorian heads; 14 pieces in all). The writer 0x36B430 walks the visual's 23 pieces. For each piece with a Tint , it finds or creates the tint entry (0x4C3634), and for each channel below 16 (0x2EAD20), 0x2EAF10 - 0x2EAFF4 writes the layer. When the palette entry's alpha is 0xFF, the layer gets amount 1.0 and color (R, G, B) / 255 ( SetParamVector , handle slot 7); otherwise it gets amount 0.0 and no color record. The head gate 0x2EAF10 (59 instructions) gates palette entries 3 and 4 only: on the head (slot 1), it gates the tattoo layer by SimpleModel.TattooApplyToHead and war paint by PaintApplyToHead (true on 182 of 185 SimpleModels). SimpleModelPieces.Tint is read live by 0x36B430, 0x36B5D8 and 0x4C4974, and the layout's channels by 0x2EAD20; nothing copies them. The second writer (0x36B5D8 - 0x4C3F58 - 0x78CD3C) applies a design's PlayerFollowerColorOverrides or SauronFollowerColorOverrides (list fields of Inventory/ArmorData ), rolled in HSV, in an entry keyed by that design, which wins over the palette entry. Most of the 855 designs carrying such lists name human and elf colors ( Ranger , Gondor , Eltariel , Haradrim ). The caragor armor designs AD Warg Armor Chest and AD Warg Rare Armor Chest name orc colors, and this writer is what paints caragor armor: on 5 of 5 armored caragors, layer A holds AA4425 on enemies and 5A8FAA on allies, entry 4 of the lists ( Orc Warpaint Red / Blue ). An orc ally's colors do not come from this writer but from his tint items (see below). The tint owner [visual+0xC0] holds the character's SimpleModel at +0x08 and a vector of 0x18-byte entries at +0x18 / +0x20 : {SimpleModelTint, design (0 = base), handle} . An entry whose design is the slot's design wins over the base entry. Pieces that share a SimpleModelTint share one store, and a piece binds one store for all its materials: the Machine body's skin and its four plating materials read the same Skin FactionWarpaint Metal Tattoo store. The handle class and its setters are described in Rendering. The store (0x28 bytes, constructor 0x4C38B8) holds its records {u32 type << 28 hash, u32 size, data} at +0x00 / +0x08 (type 2 is a float3 k c?TintColor , type 5 a float k f?TintAmount ), a reference count at +0x1C and a change stamp at +0x20 . The render cache. A piece's render node rebuilds its parameters only when one of its stores' stamps is newer than its last build. Values written into a store in place change nothing on screen until the stamp moves ahead of the counter the render thread keeps in its thread-local block (about 7,900 increments per second). The blend. Each layer, in order R, G, B, A, moves the running color toward the tinted diffuse: c = c + mask x amount x (tint x diffuse - c) , always from the original diffuse (as read in full in the three body pixel shaders that blend). Neither the factor nor the albedo is clamped from below (of the skeletal variant's 11 saturates, 8 clamp decal coordinates and 3 a wet / blood factor), so an amount above 1.0 extrapolates and the 8-bit target stores an undershoot as 0. The store holds the palette byte / 255, but on screen a tint behaves as an sRGB-encoded color. A paint color chosen to equal its plate as a linear factor ( 6F5D4A ) drew strokes at 0.40 / 0.34 / 0.30 of the plate (14,172 pixels measured). That is near what decoding the byte as sRGB first predicts, and far from the 1.0 a linear factor would give. Paint colors encoded as sRGB ( B0A393 , BBBFBA ) blend into their plates. The gear shader also interpolates each mask layer's specular sample toward k v?SpecularTint (reflectance, specular occlusion, roughness) by mask x k f?TintAmount x k fSpecularTintToggle x k f?SpecularTintAmount . Gear materials declare the vectors (0.6667, 1, 0.5) with amounts 0, and no captain's tint store carries them.

The class roll fills palette entries 0-14. Entry 15, faction war paint, only ever comes from items, and so do most of an orc's armor colors. A FlairColors row ( Inventory/Flair/Color { ColorType = palette slot, ColorRecord - Model/SimpleModelColorSetup }) is rolled when the item is given (see above), so one repointed ColorRecord reaches every orc the engine dresses or re-dresses after it. - Grunts hold IT Faction <Enemy Friendly TintItem , and captains hold IT <Tribe Tribe Tint or IT <Tribe Tribe Follower Tint (Blackguard, Dark, Feral, Industrial, Marauder, Mystic, Slaughter, Terror, Warmonger, plus IT Bruz ). - Allies use Orc Faction Cloth Blue (slot 12, Clothing Color 01 Blue 5E89A5 ), Orc Faction Paint Blue (15, 5A8FAA ), Orc Cloth Friendly (7, Orc Talion Faction Clothing 5B87A5 ), Orc Metal Friendly and Orc Trim Metal Friendly (5 / 9, C2CCBE ) and Orc Leather Friendly (6). Enemies use the Red / Enemy twins ( Orc Sauron Faction Clothing with red, black, green and purple entries; Orc Metal Enemy A09590 ). - Eighteen records color every orc's armor: for metal, Orc Metal Enemy / Friendly / Copper (Industrial) / Silver (Mystic); for trim, Orc Trim Metal Enemy / Friendly / Orc Trim Gold (Marauder); for leather, Orc Leather Enemy / Friendly / Black / Brown (Feral) / YellowBrown (Slaughter) and Orc FactionLeather GreyFur Range (Warmonger, slot 11); for cloth, Orc Cloth Enemy / Friendly / Black ; and for side cloth, Orc Faction Cloth Red / Blue . The enemy grunts' leather setup Orc Faction Leather Enemy has no entries, so every enemy grunt's leather ships untinted. - Beasts have every tint link of their SimpleModels empty, and no item colors them, so a caragor's palette slot 4 stays unset. Armor whose design carries color overrides ( AD Warg Armor Chest , above) is painted by the second writer; any other shows the white base of its strokes. Graug and drake pieces have no tint mapping at all: their paint is in their textures. War paint on armor is a tint layer over a light neutral base. Under the paint channel the diffuse reads saturation 0.03 - 0.06 and 1.5 - 2.7 times the luminance of the texels around it (13 materials decoded), so an unset entry (amount 0) shows white marks. The paint channel differs by set: A carries faction paint on Beast, Industrial, Scavenger, Warmonger and the Sauron / Talion chests, and B on Commander, Destroyer, Marksman, Thrall, Tank and Feather. On the Metal Leather Cloth Warpaint title pieces and the caragor armor, A carries war paint (slot 4). Faction cloth (12) covers a large share of Black (B 23%) and Mystic (B 26%). The grunt outfit has no faction-cloth layer; its plate paint is baked into faction armor d.tex . A stroke is also present in the specular map, so a painted texel on a metal plate is matte and shows its full albedo: faction armor s.tex reads R 0.72 / G 0.61 / B 0.68 in a stroke's core against 0.92 / 0.92 / 0.43 immediately outside, and R 170 / 255 is a dielectric.

t: Masks: what a layer can reach
x: A layer reaches only where its mask channel is set. - Blank masks. Of 431 character materials on the four gear shader trees, 114 bind a blank mask: 103 bind flatblack alpha.tex (all four channels 0) and 11 bind flatblack.tex (R = G = B = 0 and A = 1). Among them, the big claw, the peg leg and the underclothes carry a tint store that the palette writes, yet still draw untinted. metalplates.mat / metalplateslods.mat are drawn by 18 Models: the four Metal Heads, the MetalJaw, MetalBandage and MetalCap helmets of the three orc bodies, the three olog helmets, and the Shovel and Snare weapons. Both materials use flatblack alpha with every amount declared 0. The Metal Head (a scar's head, AD Metal Head , armor slot 11) is a single material object holding head01's face materials (cells 0-2), gore caps (3-4), eyes (5-6) and plates (7-8), so one store reaches the face and the plates alike. Monolith's own metal head, Orc Machine Head ( Skin Eye Metal FactionWarpaint ), puts its metal on B ( orc machine helmet m sets B on 93.1% of texels). Each plate Model owns its material set (2,995 of 2,995 set primaries have their own instance). Every engine store bind uses index 0 (351 of 351 pairs on 119 pieces). - Plating with no alpha. The Machine plating masks are BC1 (alpha 1) or BC3 with alpha 1.0 on 262,144 of 262,144 texels, so a Tattoo layer at amount 1.0 on the Machine body's store covers the whole plating after Metal. The Machine body's tint is Skin FactionWarpaint Metal Tattoo , with metal on B over 82.8% of the body plating, 91.0% of the shoulders and 86.1% of the pants; the arms and legs are 50.4% metal and 49.6% skin. The Machine head's tint is Skin Eye Metal FactionWarpaint (its helmet mask is 100% B). The Tower body uses Skin Metal Leather Metal , the Dragonborn Skin Metal Leather , and Flint, Tinder, Infested and Glutton the standard Skin Cloth Warpaint Tattoo . - Skin keeps its sores. Inside the skin zone of orc body001 m (R above 0.05, G below 0.3), R is 0.86 at the median and 0.55 / 0.67 / 0.72 at the 1st / 5th / 10th percentile (0.58 / 0.71 / 0.74 on the Machine body's mask). The low-R texels are the scabs, blisters and folds, which keep part of their own color under any skin tint: a black skin at amount 1.0 keeps 15.5% of the texture on average. G is the cloth zone (loincloth and wraps: 14.4% of the standard mask and 15.0% of the Machine's). On the Machine body, G is faction war paint, which reads amount 0.0, so its wraps show the raw texture. - Accessories. In all, 42 orc and olog accessories form 22 families, 10 of them with no Tint . Orc Buff Spiders Accessory has none and therefore no store. Its material ( orc spiders accessory.mat , gear alphatest lod0 ) masks with flatblack.tex , so only the A layer could reach it. Its strands are an effect: thespider spidersbody01.fxp , three PolyString nodes on Head and the forearms, whose color is the effect key's shared StringColor .

A captain's eyes are solid material slots 5 and 6 of his head piece's material object, one material per eye (see Characters for the slots). The eye materials are eye orc , black , bright , serpent , undead , cataracts , cut , metal and crossed , eye cursed and olog eyes , all resident in a loaded world. eye orc spider ships only in a DLC bundle, and its own tint mask is blank (its red comes from its diffuse). No eye mesh ships. The eye shader tints the iris by the G layer (the eye palette entry) and writes an emissive value saturate((mask . k vEmissiveTintChannelMask - range.x) / (range.y - range.x)) x k fEmissiveScale . Orc heads ship range (0, 2) and scale 0.05 (0.35 on bright eyes, 0 on cataracts), so a fully masked pixel glows at half the scale. Olog heads have no eye glow. The emissive class and row go into the G-buffer material alpha as (32 + row) / 255 . Eyeballs always write row 7 (39 / 255, the generic diffuse row, which glows in the eye's own tint), and ordinary pixels 0 or 1. The rows index materials\0dev\engine\emissive lut.texa (16 x 256, R11G11B10 float), whose header names them: 0 blackbody, 1 wraith, 2 balefire, 3 lit interior, 4 nazgul, 5 cursed, 6 zone map, 7 generic diffuse, 8 lava flow, 9 balrog ice, 10 / 11 blackbody, 12 blackbody test, 13 fire decal, 14 fire, 15 balefire. Each row ramps over the strength: it is near black below about 0.4, nazgul reaches (0, 1.06, 0.28) at 0.75 and wraith (0.18, 1.06, 1.59), and rows 12-15 reach values in the hundreds. The head writes its row from k nEmissiveLUTIndex (orc heads ship 7), and the EyeGlowLUT records set rows Fire 0, Wraith 1, Poison 2, Nazgul 4 and Cursed 5. Integer material parameters are stored as floats ( EyeGlowLUT Nazgul puts k nEmissiveLUTIndex in its store as type 5, 4.0). Of 378 override records, only the five EyeGlowLUT set a row. The brand. After its eight color decals, head cin reads one more slice of the scar array: layer k fBrandIndex , position k vBrandPosition , rotation k fBrandRotationCosSin and scale k vBrandScale . Its strength, the slice's alpha x k fBrandBrightness , is written as the emissive strength with row k nBrandLUTIndex (the eyes' encoding). The Olog head01 / head02 materials ship it at brightness 0, layer 15, position (0.33, 0.35), scale 0.909, rotation -5 and row 1 (wraith). The title look "Brand of the Dark Lord" turns on HasBrand , DarkTalionBrand and EyeGlowLUT Nazgul . The body shaders write no emissive: their G-buffer alpha is a subsurface class ( k vSubSurfaceID ), and the body materials' k vEmissiveTintChannelMask is (0, 0, 0, 0) and is read by none of the three body pixel shaders. A title's eye look is an item (58 items, given by 64 titles). Its MaterialSetVariants swap only the eyeball (19 variants, all on the head), its PassiveMaterialOverrides paint the rest, and its FlairColors set skin and eye colors. An undead captain's glowing eyes are not the eye material but the I Am Undead item's PassiveFXSequencePicker : UndeadFX - necro undead ambient effects with "Left Eye Star" / "Right Eye Star" particles on the eye bones, started by the item handler 0x1C0E0C - 0x79BFF4 (see Visual effects). The fire helmet is the same kind of look: Fire Helmet names FireHat - firehat.fxp on Head , whose flame nodes take their color from a slice of the emissive table ( k fFireLUT ). Of 5,618 items, 21 carry an effect picker.

AddMaterialOverride 0x57AF70(visual, record, n) and RemoveMaterialOverride 0x57D530(visual, record, n) put an Inventory/MaterialOverride (378 records) on a drawn character and remove it. Add does nothing unless the visual's byte +0xB2 is set and the visual has a skeleton ( +0x90 ). The list visual+0xC8 holds 0x38-byte entries {+0x00 decal slot, +0x08 record, +0x10 count, +0x18 handle, +0x20 vector} . The same record again only raises the count, and a remove at zero unbinds and frees the entry. A new entry's parameters come from the record. Each StructuresInventoryMaterialParam names either a parameter picker (such as ScarLayer , ScarPosition , ScarRotation or ScarScale , with 16 names each) or a plain name, and ParamValueType sets the value's type: 0 float, 1 a float-pool pair, 4 int. The entry is placed in the lowest decal slot that no entry of the same piece group sharing that picker uses, and is bound at index 0 of the piece's material, behind the stores already there. When two stores bound to one material carry the same key, the first in the material's list wins. With the engine's amount ahead of a second store's, the second store changed nothing; with the order reversed, it took effect. Two overrides on the same piece and key therefore do not combine. The head and body shaders read decal slots 0-7, so an entry filed past slot 7 is not drawn. Body decals need the scar material. Normal bodies draw orc body001(v2).mat / olog body001.mat ( body noscar.fxo , no decal slots). The scar twins ( orc body scar , orc body stk scar , olog body scar and their LODs, body lod0/1.fxo ) use the same textures and meshes plus eight decal slots. A decal store holds k fScarLayerN , k fScarRotationN , k fScarTintN (floats) and k vScarPositionN , k vScarScaleN , k fScarRotationNCosSin (type 11, float2). A decal of scale s covers a UV square of side 1 / (4s), with no tiling. The decal reads the scar array's color, normal and specular slices. k fScarTintN blends its color toward the same decal tinted by the body's layers (0 gives the raw decal, 1 a decal tinted like the skin under it): decal = raw + ScarTint x (raw x layers - raw) , unclamped, so a value above 1 extrapolates. Decals 1-7 composite over one another ( total += (1 - total) x a ) and are normalized by that total before the tint; decal 0 is not. The orc body atlas, shared by Slim, Buff and Stocky, in engine texture coordinates: Region u v --- --- --- right hand / right arm 0.00 - 0.15 / 0.17 - 0.49 0.10 - 0.44 torso (back / front) 0.35 - 0.65 0.02 - 0.25 / 0.30 - 0.54 left arm / left hand 0.51 - 0.83 / 0.85 - 1.00 0.10 - 0.44 thighs right 0.03 - 0.33, left 0.67 - 0.97 0.41 - 0.66 shins right 0.03 - 0.33, left 0.67 - 0.97 0.71 - 0.97 Left and right islands do not overlap. For the olog body, the game's own records give the layout: olog curse body 01 to 08 default to a chest and belly ring (u 0.42 - 0.57, v 0.36 - 0.47) and the left arm (v 0.30; u 0.68 / 0.80 / 0.875 for the upper arm, forearm and wrist). The regional records place LTrapezius at (0.685, 0.215), LShoulder at (0.64, 0.28), LLowerArm at (0.80, 0.25), CLowerBack at (0.50, 0.10) and the abdomen at (0.46 - 0.55, 0.45 - 0.525). For the olog head, its 70 wound records place the eye sockets at v 0.31 (u 0.38 / 0.61), the mouth at v 0.47, the chin and jaw at 0.5 - 0.7, the ears at u 0.12 / 0.88 (v 0.38), the eyeball islands at v 0.75 - 0.9 and the teeth at 0.9 - 1.0. The records store the engine's v unflipped. orc Cursed (the curse) pairs Body Scar BodyReplacement , sets skin Orc Skin White , the curse face (layer 1, ScarTint 1) and black eyes, and four olog curse body vein decals (layer 0) on the torso. Orc Skin White and Orc Skin Undead have HSV saturation 0 and value 255: a white tint that shows the pale diffuse itself. The vein layer is slice 0 of the 40-slice scar array (16,121 of 262,144 pixels covered, purple-gray with specular alpha 1.0), and the shipped curse body decals use ScarTint 0. The undead skin records ( orc undead body / head , LightbleedRange and SubSurfaceID ) write only k fScarRotationNCosSin through AddMaterialOverride and take a decal slot; their other keys are dropped.

Weapons use the armor shaders ( nemesis\gear lod0/1.fxo , gear alphatest lod0/1.fxo ) with the same tint parameters, so a palette color lands on a weapon wherever its mask is set, and almost nowhere is. An Inventory/EquippedWeaponData.Model names an item model { ActiveNode / InactiveNode , Models (- ModelRecord , a Wep Model, MinMeshIndex / MaxMeshIndex ), MaterialOverrides , Tint , ApplySummonedByTribeMaterialOverride }. The engine makes a tint store only where Tint is set, on 20 of 1,903 item models (16 shields, such as Regal Metal Leather Trim and RangerKiller Cloth Leather FactionWarpaint , the throwing spear and the war banner). Of 77 orc weapon and shield materials, 64 bind flatblack alpha.tex (every layer masked off) and 9 their own mask (the Regal and RangerKiller shields, both throwing spears, the quiver and three war banners). Over all weapon materials, 68 of 306 are masked. - Parts are the mesh's own material ids. The id is uv1.x in tenths, one per vertex, on 53 of 87 orc weapon meshes; 11 hold real coordinates there and 23 have no second UV set. The vertex shader passes it on, and the pixel shader picks the detail layer round(id - 1) from characters\modelcharacters\global\detail\detail array 01 .texa , whose header names the slices: 1 leather, 2 metal, 3 cloth, 4 bone, 5 skin, 6 cloth 2, 7 chain, 8 noise. gear lod1 and gear alphatest lod1 do not pass the second UV set. The same channel is the armor pieces' mesh-part number (see Shoulder pads and appearance tags above). - Metal is the specular map's R. It is 170 / 255 on every dielectric and rises toward 255 on metal (63 of 77 materials have both; 6 are all metal). A metal texel's albedo tints only its reflections, so a colored polished blade reads dark with colored glints. k bSpecGAlphaTest , used by 3 of the 11 alpha-tested weapons (the war banners), cuts the alpha by the specular G after the tints. The blood decal's position is seeded from the R and G tint colors ( frac(sum(R) x 8) , frac(sum(G) x 6) ). k fBloodValue (shipped 0), k fBloodAlpha and k cBloodColor drive the decal in gear lod0 modes 0 and 2; meshtype5 does not read them. - A weapon's drawn model is reached through a chain of objects. The visual component ( [char+0x2348] , on an Army copy [stage+0x768] , vt 0x1FD63F0) holds the holder of each slot at [component+0x38 + slot x 0x28] (holder vt 0x1DB1F68, or 0x1DCA710 for a shield carrier's slot 0). The holder keeps its elements at +0x148 / +0x150 (vt 0x1DB4F58, an object reference: +0x08 next, +0x10 previous, +0x18 self, +0x20 target). An element's +0x20 is the built object (vt 0x1F782C0), whose +0x120 is the model (vt 0x1DB4948, empty while not drawn). The model holds the wielder at +0xE0 , the material object at +0x120 and the mesh path at +0x170 (54 of 55 models on 27 Army copies, 16 of 16 world characters). A material object holds one material per LOD ( orc metalshield.mat , orc metalshieldlods.mat ), and an item can pick a variant ( orc metalshieldv4.mat ). A weapon's render node watches the character's own store, which carries only k fDissolve (its handle is at [skel+0x238] in the world). - Two-model looks. A look whose Models list holds two item models draws both. Orc 1HS EliteSwordX2 , for example, uses RightHand / Ber R sheath and LeftHand / Ber L sheath , both drawing Wep Orc 1HS EliteSword with no mirror or offset (18 of 18 two-model looks in hand holders had both built). Every Defender look is a two-model shield look (41 of 41 Orc , Gondorian and Easterling shield looks): model 0 is his weapon ( RightHand / Socket Sheath Def01 ) and model 1 the shield ( Shield L Attach / Socket Sheath Def02 ). In the world his item builds the shield holder, whose vf35 0x6E517C calls the hand holder's 0x3FCF70 (destroy and build every model) and then reads Items.ShieldWeaponData . Over 1,748 looks and 1,909 item models, the active sockets are RightHand 1,053, LeftHand 673, Shield L Attach 85 and RightDagger 16, followed by creature and test sockets. The rest sockets are Sheath Socket 383, Dagger Sheath Socket 380, Socket Sheath Def01 / Def02 79 each, L sheath 51 and Ber R / Ber L sheath 11 each. No right-hand shield socket exists. LeftHand sits on L Weapon , which a Defender's clips never move (200 cm from his L Hand on his stage pose); his clips carry Shield L . - The drawn mesh is the model chain, not the name. The chain runs EquippedWeaponData.Model - StructuresInventoryItemModel.Models - StructuresInventoryModel.ModelRecord - a Model record. Over 1,763 looks (40 with no model), BlackHand Sword , Sauron Mace , BlackHand Bow , BlackHand 2 and BlackCaptain01 Belroth draw the broom prop Wep Orc Misc Broom , and Raptor Body draws a whole caragor. The boss weapons (such as Sauron 1HB FlangedMace , Sauron 1HS ElvenSwordT3 and Nazgul 1HS BlackBlade ) have an empty InactiveNode , so they never sheathe. In all, 1,742 looks reference 1,852 item models, 10 of them shared; 1,111 share one descriptor run (21 fields).

Grunts are not faction members and get no member build. The dresser 0x4F12E0(visual component, is follower) dresses them from the class kit ( [Combat/Tree].InventorySetup , read at every call; accessor 0x4F171C). It skips the player, recognized by the combat object [component+0x440] (vt 0x1F995E0), whose +0x50 is set on the player only. For an unnamed character (0x4F16F0: the owner's +0x2710 pool index is -1), an enemy gets Grunt SauronFollowerItems and loses Grunt PlayerFollowerItems (0x4F163C), and a follower the reverse, so domination re-dresses a grunt. A named character gets the Named lists minus every item with a builder. The dresser's callers include inventory initialization 0x4F0938 and the follower setter 0x102F0C. The shipped grunt armor is one item: Sauron Armor ( Talion Armor for followers) - AD Sauron Armor (armor slot 4) - Orc <body Sauron faction , the strap-and-loincloth outfit, or Olog Buff Skirt Grunt . The tough kits give Sauron Armor FullSet (the same skirt on an Olog), and the Orc Prisoner kit is bare. The give path 0x1C01E0 - 0x1C1224 - 0x11565A4 - 0x649790 draws one design per item build exactly as for a captain, and the equip requests the bundles of what it draws: 128 of 129 distinct rolled pieces were resident. A piece with no ArmorDataDynamicBundle (the AD Industrial Helmet(Bling) pieces, which reuse another model) has nothing to request.

Residency. A piece draws only when its geometry and material bundles are resident. Both are requested by the gear load request of an equipped item (0x61B868 asks the gear budget manager through 0x4B4C7C; see Resource streaming). A piece no design lists has no material bundle to request: AD Machine Body lists only Orc Buff Machine Body (body type 0), so the Slim and Stocky Machine bodies, which have their own geometry bundles, have materials ( machine body m.bndl ) that nothing requests. Easterling pieces' designs list body type 12 only and name no material bundle; their shared easterling outfit.mat ships in easterlings base , easterling buff heavy arms g and flair\grunt\desert grunt m . A head is the same: its face record's bundle and its family's g bundle must both be resident (see Head, hair and helmet above). The appearance object and the body. 0x61BAD4 and the build write only the appearance object ( SetPieceSlot with no visual). A drawn body changes through SetPieceSlot with its visual and through the equip path's load request. 0x62EB14 (often labeled UpdateVisualModel ) is an army refresh, not a character refresh: it takes an army context and that army's summary container ( [ctx+0x30] ), rebuilds the container's summaries (0x62BC44, refilling each from its member through 0x62BF54) and asks the world UI to refresh the army's stage (0x62E30C). All 7 of its 12 call sites that were examined pass an army context: the walk over every army 0x1B5D66C, fort-upgrade removal 0x1B5E39C, 0x1C1B22C, 0x1C1DB10, the promotion events 0x1C1D828 (with a temporary container), the console rebuild, and 0x7A97DC, which first replaces the army's summary container (0x62AFD4) and is called after the faction system initializes and from sim-event generation. A member is not a valid first argument. The rebuild's first instructions ( mov rax,[rdx+0xD8] / mov [rcx+0x9F50],rax ) store the context's +0xD8 in the container's +0x9F50 before anything is tested. Passed a member and his 0x1C0-byte appearance object in place of a context and a container, it therefore writes a pointer 0x9F50 bytes past the appearance object.

The Army screen draws each captain from his army's summary (0x1A8 bytes, one per member, in the summary container), not from the member (see User interface for the stage objects). The refill 0x169168(summary, fm) copies the key {FM+0x178, FM+0x174} ( +0x88 ), the class ( +0x138 ), combat tree ( +0x130 ), role ( +0x140 ), personality ( +0x148 ), tribe ( +0x150 ), rarity ( +0x178 ), level and flags. It rebuilds the trait and marker lists, and copies the appearance into [summary+0x40] with 0x2EBA60 and the inventory into [summary+0x30] . Both copies come from the mock member when FM+0x2E0 is set (0x75D2FC / 0x75D314), so such a captain shows the older look (see The Nemesis system). The per-captain redraw is 0x19C395C(world UI [base+0x26FFB60] , &key). It resolves the army's stage (0x455EDC; armies of one region share one stage object), the summary (0x1B5C0F8) and the stage character (0x1A28FAC), and runs the character's rebuild UI CWorldUICharacter 0x627F40(object, summary, 0, 0). The game calls it after a Training Order (0x1C51630). It draws from the summary as it is, so a summary that was not refilled redraws the old look, and the open screen also keeps its own summary copies per army (0x16FC1C). The screen builds a new character copy, with new tint handles from the palette, each time a captain is shown: one captain received three copies in a row, then one about every 40 seconds while he stayed in view. A tribe or armor change rebuilds the copy too, so a value written into one copy's material does not last.

- Head03 is cut content. The head03 name is carried by 30 pieces and 30 face records: 29 Head03 C heads over the three orc bodies, and Orc Buff Head03 G . The family is never rolled (0 of 557 captains, against 206 head01 and 293 head02), and its family bundle orc head03 g.bndl (12,404,972 bytes, holding the six head03 materials, its textures, and beard and piercing materials) is linked by no record. Its diffuse orc head03 d.tex is a flat orange placeholder with a black "3" in all three copies the engine reads: the bundle's BC1 section, the high-mip .tex0 and the HD .texuhd tier (a texture's header names its sibling tier). The sculpts, normal and specular maps and materials are finished, on the shared head UV template. Of its meshes, 16 (every Stocky one, three Slim, three Buff and the family mesh) are skinned on a 139-bone face skeleton with five extra leaf bones under Head ( L Ear , R Ear , NoseUp , MouthUp , MouthLo ) that no live face skeleton has; the live ones hold 134 bones, in head02's order. Three heads draw their eyes with the wrinkle skin material (cell 0), several LODs carry invalid rows or are skinned to the wrong bones, and three Buff heads ship their head sculpt as a part named Beard mash2 . Head03 carries no MeshIndexPairs and no stubble, piercing or ear burn parts. - Head geometry formats. Head LOD0 / LOD1 index buffers are tessellation patches ( head lod0 is a tessellation shader). A head part's palette is a stack of strictly ascending runs of at most 64 bone indices, and vertex lanes use slots 0-63 of the first run. - Model.Scale is not a piece property: its only copier 0x56E870 fills the creation parameters of objects spawned from a Model record. - No shipped record references the items behind 69 armor pieces (among them the Druid pants and legs, Underclothes, Leather shoulders, the Buff Defender set, and Easterling heavy and plate pieces). No archive ships a mesh for 15 cut pieces (among them the Buff Defender set, two Celebrimbor rings and a cinematic hair). A record count does not see world scripts: Sauron Gondor1 and Vines Accessory are given by mission scripts.

- How does a spawned body pick up a rebuilt appearance object, and does the engine support a body type change on a loaded character? A live comparison of [FM+0x2D8] with the visual's +0xB8 before and after a level-up would settle the first. - Where is a tint color decoded from sRGB to linear? The store holds byte / 255, but the screen behaves as if the byte were sRGB. A frame capture of one known color through the gear shader would settle it. - Does the engine read a skeleton's LOD row u32 as the material cell? The shipped pattern fits it on 7 pieces; a capture of a part's bound material at two distances would settle it. - Does an override that carries a key the tint store also carries ( k fEmissiveScale of an eye-glow record) win, as it appears to, against the first-store rule measured on armor? Reading the head material's store list order with both bound would settle it. - How does the draw compare a vertex's part number ( round(uv1.x x 10) ) with the range that MeshIndexPairs stores at (material+0x10)+0xB8 ? The comparison on the render side is not traced. - A material parameter the shader does not read ( k vEmissiveTintChannelMask on the body, k fBrandRotation ) never reached the constant buffer when added to a store. Does the engine update only the parameters a shader declares? That path is not traced. - How does Rogue BodyTattoo (no material override, so the give path files nothing) apply the Rogue body, and which items carry the LOD painted variants? - How do the body-animation marker items ( Personality UniqueBodyAnim IT , no payload) reach the animation, and how are the ChildItemPicker tint items ( IT Faction Enemy Tint ) resolved, since the give path reads neither? - Cloaks made for Talion's skeleton hang some cloth from bones turned 150-178 degrees from any bone a man has (the Rhovanion cloaks have 15 such anchors each; 43 of 53 cloaks on his skeleton have none). The presumed cause is that Havok's skin operators keep Talion's inverse binds; a posed capture of one such cloak on another rig would settle it.

t: Captain scars and the return from death
x: A scar is not a model: it is a set of items a scar type hands out, each painting decals on the head or the body, hiding part of the body or taking an armor slot. The engine gives scars through AddScar , titles, rewards, events and the return from death, and they live in the captain's item lists like any armor (see Captain appearance).

A combat tree names its setup, and the setup lists the types it may carry: Combat/Tree.ScarSetup - Combat/Scar/Setup (Orc 22 entries, Olog 18) - StructuresCombatScarTypeStruct { Type - Combat/Scar/Type (24 records: WeightPerUse, ExcludedItems) ScarItems the variants HelmetEquipment an item given with every variant } WeightPerUse is the same list on every type, [1000, 10, 1, 0.01, 1e-4], indexed by how often the faction system has given that type (the scar-use table at FS+0x128 , see The Nemesis system). Three types are bookkeeping with no items ( ScarBookmark Role Claw , Machine , Stormbringer ); HeadRemoved Olog gives only the scar body; Resurrected PlayerAbility RaiseDead gives orc Cursed / olog Cursed , the look of Talion's raised dead. A variant is an Inventory/Items record, and a part is one item it hands out: the variant itself when it carries something, and its PairedItems (hash 0xE512B887), recursively. Each part is one region of him. Its PassiveMaterialOverrides are Inventory/MaterialOverride records with a ModelPiece (0 body, 1 head, 13 body LOD) and MaterialParams primaries whose ParamNamePicker names the key: ScarLayer (a slice of scararray d.texa , a float), ScarPosition (a UV, a float-pool pair in ParamValueVector2 ), ScarRotation (degrees), ScarScale (a pair), ScarTint , or SeverMask (a hide: a sever group, no decal). For example the orc burn orc burns WholeBody Right (no builder, no decal of its own) hands out Body Scar BodyReplacement , orc burns body rightArm (3 decals, layer 13), orc burns body rightChest (4 decals on chest and back, and AD empty chest ), orc burns body rightLeg (1 decal) and orc burns head massive 01 (5 face decals and AD empty head ).

AddScar 0x7BB8C4(fm, type), 100 instructions: 1. returns when FM+0x370 already holds the type; 2. refuses when he holds any of the type's ExcludedItems (0xFCB040 over his items; 0x24DF7C on a spawned body); 3. takes the setup from his combat tree's ScarSetup and gives one random entry of the type's ScarItems (0x7BBABC) and its HelmetEquipment (0x7BBAF4), each through the give path 0x355474 at source 10; 4. only if one of those gives returned true: writes FM+0x370 , re-dresses him from his items (0x61BAD4) and counts the use on the faction system (0x7BBA44), which lowers the type's weight for later picks. It removes no older scar's items: scars stack, and FM+0x370 names only the latest. RemoveScar 0x1BC409C removes one random item of the type's list, so it can miss on a type with several. A member build gives only the role's ScarType ; nothing in it reads FM+0x370 , and its item clear removes the earlier scar items, so a rebuild drops a scar given by AddScar .

t: Pairs pass only through slotless items
x: The give path 0x355474 hands out PairedItems only for an item without an ItemBuilder . An item with a builder becomes an instance, is equipped (0x61B868) and the give returns at once (0x355600 - 0x3556EC), never reaching the pair loop at 0x35568D. A builderless item is filed in the look-record list ( FM+0x130 ) when it has a BodyModelChange or any override, then gives each pair recursively with the same source; its return value says whether it was filed, regardless of what its pairs did. The consequences: - Burns never registers. All four variants of each kind are bundles with no builder and no override of their own. They are filed nowhere, and the give returns false although every pair landed, so AddScar writes no FM+0x370 , re-dresses nothing and counts no use. In one save, 0 of 116 scarred captains held Burns as their type, and one carried a Burns part. - A slotted variant's pairs never arrive. This affects Poison ( orc poison head 0x , whose pairs are the scar body, orc poison body rightArm , Tumor Chest and IT empty shoulders ), the orc Mauled heads ( Body Scar BodyReplacement and orc multipleScars body 01 , 7 decals), Sack Head ( HeadReplacement DoNotScarHead ) and Metal Head ( orc metalHead head , the same decals the head carries itself). No Poison holder carried any pair (0 of 3); in the control, 2 of 2 olog Mauled holders, whose heads are slotless, carried olog cuts body leftBody and the scar body. - The olog Burns bundles exclude Trait Olog themselves , so an olog never gets one through AddScar (their parts require Trait Olog ). - No slot-taking part has a slotless twin carrying the same override records (0 of 29).

t: What a part does to his armor
x: Part's design (armor slot) Parts --- --- AD empty head (0) the burnt heads, the Mauled heads, the Poison heads, orc sauron brand AD empty chest (2) the burnt chest-and-back parts, orc multipleScars body 01 AD empty arms (3) the olog burnt arms AD empty shoulders (1), AD Tumor Chest (2, a piece) Poison's pairs (which never arrive) AD MetalBandage Helmet , AD MetalCap Helmet , AD SkullDagger Helmet , AD SkullAxe Helmet (0) helmet pieces AD empty head NoHair (0) IT empty head HighWeight / IT empty head NoHair , the helmet equipment of MetalJaw, Sack Head and Metal Head AD MetalJaw Helmet (9) the face piece AD Sack Head , AD Metal Head (11) head replacements the claw arm, the peg leg (7) accessories AD Body Scar (10) Body Scar BodyReplacement , and orc Cursed / olog Cursed , which dress it with the curse face, black eyes and four body veins Decal-only parts take no slot. The plain body draws no decals; its scar twin does (see Captain appearance, "Material overrides and decals"). Judged by the items the give path actually delivers: - Poison, Branded Slave and Mauled (and the olog Poison) bare the head; - Burns bares the head and takes slots 0, 2 and 10 on an orc, and 0, 2, 3 and 10 on an olog; - Metal Head and Sack Head replace the head; - MetalJaw uses slot 9; - ExposedBrain, DaggerHead and AxeHead are helmets; - cuts, eye wounds, Facepeele and Shamed are decals only; - the claws use the accessory slot, and the curse the body.

Of the 378 Inventory/MaterialOverride records, 296 carry a ScarLayer .
