Each layer is a slice of the scar array, and the game names each as one kind of mark: Layer Mark Layer Mark --- --- --- --- 0 the curse veins (27 records: body and head) 19 swelling 1 the curse face (2 head records) 20 tally marks 3 bruise 21 Sauron brand 4 mauled 22 sores 5 blood 23 soot 6 boils 24 trickster face 7 cuts 25 torn face 8 old cuts, brain drips 26 serpent eye 9 stitched cuts 27 undead / slayer scar 10 gouges 28 exposed brain 11 cataracts 30 / 31 maggots 12 poison 32 / 36 whole-face burns 13 burns (48 records) 33 crossed eye 14 metal eye 34 black eye 15 shame scar 35 cut eye 16 old scars 37 / 38 stitches 17 Black Blade glyph 39 spider eye 18 bullet 29 no record So the game ships one vein pattern as a decal, layer 0. Each record carries a default placement for its decal: orc Serpent Eye L , for example, sits at layer 26, UV (0.437, 0.854), scale 2, and olog spider Head LEye at layer 39, (0.59, 0.83), scale 1.43. orc Hide Head Eye L is a hide instead, k nSeverMask 4 (the left eye). The head and body shaders draw decal slots 0-7 only, filled lowest first; a captain whose own wounds hold those slots draws no further decal (one olog held 12 body decal entries, stitches in slots 0-3 and cuts in 4-11, and anything added landed at 12 and up).

Six designs replace a limb: AD L Arm Claw , AD BigClawL Accessory , AD R Leg Claw , AD NazgulArm , AD Blight Arms (accessory slot 7) and AD Zog Legs (legs slot 5, one Slim piece for every body). Five of them share armor slot 7, so a captain can hold only one of those five limbs as an item. The orc's own limb is hidden by the item's PassiveMaterialOverrides , not by the piece: an Inventory/MaterialOverride names a model piece and a SeverMask over the sever groups: Bit Group Bit Group --- --- --- --- 1 left lower leg 16 left upper arm 2 right lower leg 32 right forearm and hand 4 lower body (below the navel, pants) 64 right upper arm 8 left forearm and hand The 46 shipped Hide records target model pieces 0 (body), 8 (shoulders: upper arms), 10 (arms: lower arms), 11 (pants), 12 (legs: lower legs) and 13 (body LOD); none spans an arm and a leg. On the three orc bodies' LOD0 meshes the groups are the lower legs (1, 2), the lower body below the navel (4), the forearms with the hands (8, 32) and the upper arms (16, 64); the chest (985, 982 and 1,180 vertices) carries no group, so no mask hides the chest. On gear the vertex alpha is the sever side of a limb part: shoulder pieces carry 16 on the left and 64 on the right, inside the masks of orc Hide Armor Armu L / R (24 / 96), and the Easterling plate arms 8 / 32. The claw and peg-leg items hide only the body skin and its LOD. The game ships armor hides that no item uses ( orc Hide Armor Arml L , piece 10 mask 8; orc Hide Armor Legl R , piece 12 mask 2; the olog twins the same), so the limb's armor still draws over a claw. Two overrides on the same piece and key do not combine: only one store's value of a key is used. NazgulArm (orcs only) puts Orc <body NazgulArm in the accessory slot, with three hides ( orc Hide Body Armu R mask 96, orc Hide Armor Arml R 32, orc Hide Armor Armu R ) that cut the orc's own right arm and its armor away. The piece uses orc buff nazgularm.skel and orc nazgularm.mat on gear alphatest lod1 , with its own 512 x 512 atlas: pale skin, dark veins, rot at the hand and metal plates painted into the diffuse; its tint Metal Leather FactionCloth has no skin layer. It comes from Role Accursed , Role Hand and Role StormBringer . The Blight arms (mask 120) come with IT empty arms ( Role Blight , PlagueBringer ) and Blight Shoulders . Replace values: L Arm Claw 20, R Leg Claw 20, BigClawL 10, NazgulArm 0, Blight Arms , IT empty arms , Blight Shoulders and Zog Legs 10. Of the 8 limb items only L Arm Claw ( Trait Berserkers , Trait Defenders ) and NazgulArm ( Trait Olog ) carry an ExcludedCharacterType (the give path's reader 0x36686C skips an empty cell), and none a RequiredCharacterType . No Olog piece of the Nazgul arm or the Blight arms ships.

t: How a return chooses its scar
x: The cheat-death evaluator 0x1BC5D44 (166 instructions; see The Nemesis system, "Cheat death and the return") does, in order: 1. for each sever effect on him, adds Combat/Sever/FX.ResurrectionExtraScarType to the list at FM+0x358 (5 records: a lost forearm gives LeftArm ClawProsthetic , a lost leg RightLeg ClawProsthetic ); 2. picks a scar through 0x1B5AA00(FS, [FM+0x370] , cause, [FM+0x500] ); 3. drops that scar when his spawned body holds one of its ExcludedItems ; 4. with no scar and no extra: "Cannot resurrect - No Available Scars", and nothing changes; 5. otherwise increments FS+0x21C and FM+0x500 , stores the scar at FM+0x348 unless it equals FM+0x370 , and fires the cause's DeathEvent . 0x1B5AA00 (131 instructions) is the only reader of ScarType , SecondScarChance and SecondScarType . With no scar yet ( FM+0x370 empty) it picks one of the cause's ScarType , weighted per type by use (0x1B5C97C). With a scar already, SecondScarChance[min(count, n - 1)] (0x7FD964, an unsigned min; count is FM+0x500 before its increment) decides whether one of SecondScarType (weighted) is picked; otherwise his existing type comes back and nothing new is added. Its compiled-out log line names it: "Selected Scar Type '%s', (was the existing scar type = %s)". The data. Faction/Resurrection has 34 records, 33 of them causes with a scar field. SecondScarChance 0.5 with SecondScarType [ Sack Head , Metal Head ] is on 28 of them. The other five: the lost forearm and the lost leg (chance 1.0, no second type), Beheaded (no ScarType , chance 1.0, no second type), Cut in half ( ScarBookmark Role Machine only) and Beheaded olog ( HeadRemoved Olog only). The first scar by cause: Cause ScarType --- --- fire, wraith fire, explosion Burns caragor, ghul, troll Mauled or CutsHead an orc's arrow EyeGouge or DaggerHead Talion's arrow (and to the head) EyeGouge an orc's slash MetalJaw, CutsHead, ExposedBrain, AxeHead poisoned Poison balefire Burns or Poison flies, torment, curse Curse a lost forearm or leg the claw or the peg leg, plus a role bookmark beheaded (olog) HeadRemoved Olog

- Faction/Rewards/Definitions : 18 rewards with AddScarType , RemoveScarType , Included / ExcludedScarType (the pinnacle scars, the Hook and Claw role changes, Reward KeepSlaveBrand ). - Faction/Events/Events : 18 events (every Captured gives Branded Slave , the three domination shames give Shamed ). - Faction/Roles/Definitions : 6 titles carry a ScarType (GrogBurner Burns, FleshRot and its Nemesis Forge copy Poison, OneEye EyeGouge, Trainer and Grizzled CutsHead), applied through AddScar by the role setter and given again at every build. - Shadow of Mordor's scar types map onto War's through NemesisForge/FirebirdModelScarType.KrakenScarType : Wraith to Curse, Sack Head to Sack Head, Eyepatch to EyeGouge; Melee, Burn and Pin Cusion have no War type (3 of 6 mapped). In Mordor a scar was a model in the appearance's scar slots (see Captain appearance, "The slots the game barely uses").

- What applies the scar a pending return stored at FM+0x348 , and when? In one save 3 of 117 scarred captains held one, none equal to their FM+0x370 ; its consumer is not traced. - How often captains carry the items of more than one scar type in an unmodified campaign: AddScar stacks by code, but the one census taken (19 of 116) was not of an unmodified save. - Which of two hides on the same piece applies when a second limb item replaces the first: whether a replaced item's hide leaves with it is not measured.

Captains are FactionMember objects (see The Nemesis system). Their strengths, weaknesses, class bonus, advanced class, gangs, combat moves and quirks are all traits, held in trait slots and resolved by the engine from data.

FactionMember offset Meaning --- --- +0x1E0 the trait slot vector {begin, end, u32 capacity at +0x10, u8 owned at +0x14} ; a slot is 0x20 bytes (below) +0x198 the active trait set, a vector of 8-byte Faction/Traits/Definitions pointers (it equals the set of slot traits in 528 of 531 captains) +0x1B0 the marker vector ( Marker records) +0x378 a cache: the first active trait with GangLeader (0x1BC3CB4) +0x508 derived bits: 14 any CanBypassRequiredDataLevelToSpawn , 19 any NPC summon / gang, 43 a trait that forbids sim events with a boss, 34 the slot list needs sorting, 38 the engine refuses trait edits (0x114B55C) A slot is +0x00 the Faction/Traits/Picker , +0x08 the trait it resolved to (null = nothing), +0x10 the trait a story mission unlocked for it, +0x18 a u16 flag word, +0x1A an i16 option index (-1 = none). A picker's options are Picker.Traits - StructuresFactionTraitPickerEntry records ( .Trait ); an option entry is a primary record (its header byte +0x01 is 0x00, not 0x0A). There are 493 pickers, for 484 traits. At most 64 active traits. Activation (0x3566B0) ends in 0x355114, which counts the active set and, above 64 (0x40) entries, deactivates traits picked at random from a candidate list (0x1BBA324) until 64 remain.

t: The flag word is the gate list and the re-roll mask
x: When a slot is added, its u16 at +0x18 is copied from the faction system's table FS+0xE0 (indexed by the picker's record index; 18,508 of 18,508 entries match). It serves two purposes at once: - the gate list - 0x1234E0(&slot+0x18, bit) ( bt ) decides which tests the resolver runs: bit 1 minimum level, 2 required row rank, 3 player follower, 4 required other traits, 6 intel level, 7 a campaign predicate, 8 difficulty; - the re-roll mask - the resolver 0x3528C4 first ANDs the rebuild's reason mask with it and, when the result is 0, returns slot+0x08 unchanged (0x352AB8: xor eax,eax; cmp word [rcx],ax; sete al ). A slot is re-decided only by the events whose bit it carries. Every picker carries bit 0 (493 of 493), so reason 0 re-rolls every slot. No live slot has a flag word of 0 (19,713 slots), so a zero word marks a slot that the engine will never re-roll: the resolver returns its trait for every reason. The resolver returns the first option whose flagged gates all pass. Options with MissionUnlock MinXPLevel set additionally require the level to reach the remapped MissionUnlock - 1 (0x352DB8) and the option's trait to equal slot+0x10 (0x3529A3); +0x10 is 0 on every live slot. Its option walk: 0x352BB8(&iterator, picker) over Picker.Traits (a 0x30-byte iterator: +0x28 index, +0x2C count), 0x352B2C the entry at the index, 0x352AC4 the entry's trait, 0x2774A8 "at end".

- UpdateTraits 0x3528A0(fm, reason) runs the rebuild 0xF88230: mask = 1 << reason if FM+0x508 bit 34: sort the slots (comparator 0x7127A8: Picker.SortPriority, higher first, ties by address), clear bit 34 reason 0: active set emptied (FM+0x1A0 = FM+0x198), FM+0x378 = 0, FM+0x508 bits 14 and 19 cleared, byte FM+0x51C = 1 per slot: new = resolver(slot, &mask, &ctx) if new == old and reason != 0: skip mask = bit 4 (a trait changed: later slots' required-trait gates re-run) deactivate old (0x353454), activate new (0x3566B0) - ApplyReward 0x3511F4 - 0x351AF8 and five other callers rebuild with reason 0, so every reward re-rolls every slot. - Add = 0x7CD03C pushes {picker} (constructors 0x7CD150 / 0x7CD184, push 0x7CD0CC, growth 0x1144628), then UpdateTraits. - Remove = find the slot by picker, 0x353454 (drop it from the active set and re-derive only the bits that trait set; unregister its spawner hijack or catalyst; remove its items from a live body), then erase it (0x7A7378). - Activate 0x3566B0: gives the trait's items (0x355400 gives each Item through 0x355474 at source 8), registers a spawner hijack (0x1A32D88) for captains of the current region, and starts a catalyst only when he has a body. The give checks RequiredCharacterType against the type of his combat tree ( FM+0x188 ; 0x30CF30, exclusion 0x36686C) before giving a weapon item (olog flamethrower or harpoon, the power-shot crossbow, grenades). Its first loop also writes the item's flair colors into the list at FM+0x118 ( {u8, u32 channel at +4, ARGB at +8} via 0x1C10E54 / 0x1C11A74, seeded by FM+0x168 ). What an away captain keeps. The give files an item only when it has an ItemBuilder , a BodyModelChange or PassiveMaterialOverrides (see Captain appearance), so a trait's plain items do not reach the record of a captain who is not in the world. Of 22 such captains with the curse weapon, 0 had CursedWeapon in their 25 item slots ( FM+0x50 ) or their look-record list, and of 26 with the fire weapon, 0 had FlamingWeapon . The trait items kept away from the world are weapons, one per loot slot (19 items over 557 captains, source byte 8): crossbows in slot 2, and the Olog harpoon or flamethrower in slot 3. Two traits that want one slot therefore cannot both hold it. Gangs, bombs, mines, mounts and immunities are applied when the captain is built in the world. Exclusive groups. 51 PickerGroup records cover 207 of the 493 pickers ( Picker.ExclusiveGroup ). 0x19F66C collects the groups of every slot a captain has, rolled or not, and 0x7DABFC refuses a picker that shares one. They are of three kinds: - design limits: DLC4 Ultimate (10 pickers), DLC4 Opener (3), BodySlamThroatGrab (2) and Mannerisms Pool (23 audio mannerisms that never appear on the card); - one-of-a-kind features: GangOrPet (13), HasMount (2) and ElementalWeapon (5); - a strength paired with its own opposite: Resist <element (immune or resistant against vulnerable or mortal to one element), every <X Fear Hate , BeastSlayerOrDismount , AggressiveUnAgressive , LastChanceModifiers , RepositionMoveAway , VaultBreaker , BodyguardDefeat , HateBossDefeat , KillOtherCaptain , WeakByHate PinningShot , Alone Fear and Blocks . No rarity picker ( Picker OrcRarity , 3), advanced-class picker ( Picker BaseStrength <advanced class , 10) or class-bonus picker ( Picker BaseStrength <class , 6) carries a group, so the group test never refuses a second one: a member holding two advanced-class slots has both BaseStrength traits active (one such member read live). The first option he qualifies for wins. Picker GangOfDoppelgangers (flags 0x83: level and a campaign gate; group GangOrPet ; excluded markers Marker SpecialButterfly , Marker Deranged ) lists Quirk HasGang Doppelgangers Elite (minimum level 35) before Quirk HasGang Doppelgangers (minimum level 15); both share the card name "Decoys". From level 35 that slot always rolls the Elite trait.

A save keeps only the slots. The FactionMember loader 0x1BC159C (a keyed tree: Identity ... Inventory, Traits, PickerLevelRemap) clears FM+0x1E0 (0x1BB9068), re-adds each saved picker through 0x1BB255C - 0x7CD03C with no trait, then calls UpdateTraits(fm, 0) unconditionally (0x1BC3554). Every load therefore re-rolls every slot: only single-option, level-only slots come back identical, and gated slots are decided again. The re-add copies the table's flag word back, so a slot whose word was cleared is rolled the game's way again. The loader bypasses the exclusive-group test, so a state that breaks a group persists. (0x1C12224 is the serializer of the online "searchable" index, not the save.)

A trait is on the card when its UIGroup is one of the eight card rows' TraitGroups (below) and its CanDisplayInUI is not false (an absent cell is true). Of the 484 Faction/Traits/Definitions , 331 are on the card and 153 never are: - 143 have no UIGroup ; - 3 have a group no row lists ( UIGroup MiscPassives for Quirk Adaptable , UIGroup OrcRarity Epic / Legendary ); - 7 sit on a row's group with CanDisplayInUI false ( Easterling Deadly Rage , Lifesteal , TargetsCaptains and TripleShot on Classes, Easterling Dismount Rider on Bonuses, DEMO ImmuneToCurse on Immunities, Resistant GroundTakedown on the hint row). Who gives them. Of the 153, 150 are an option of some picker (control: 327 of the 331 card traits). Combat moves have small pickers of their own ( Picker BodySlam , Picker BlockCounter with Block Counter 1 / 2 , Picker ThroatGrab , Picker AudioMannerism 01 howl ...). No picker gives Marker Is Archer (named by Faction/Predicates/TraitLists ) or Quirk BloodBrother AttackedByAI / Killed (named by Faction/Traits/Relationships , the blood-brother bond). The 4 card traits no picker gives are the nemesis system's own: Hate Nemesis , Terror Nemesis , Hate SuperiorDamage and Quirk BloodBrother . Rarity is a requirement, not a source: OrcRarity Epic / Legendary sit in the RequiredTraits of the element and weapon pickers ( Picker Curse Weapon , Picker Fire Weapon , Picker FuryAttackCombo ...). What they give. Most moves carry one ability item ( BodySlam - BodySlam , Block Counter 1 - ParentItem CounterBlock1 , Counter Stun - CounterStun ); the five Terror give Item Terror General with OnAppliedItem Fear LowHealth ; Quirk FalseRetreat has only an OnAppliedItem ; the betrayal traits, Prevent Resurrection , Quirk Ambusher and Quirk Sneaky carry no item. By their record names, the 153 are roughly: - 46 combat moves (counters, dodges, jump attacks, body slam, throat grab, whirlwind, grenades at his feet, dismount and their Easterling variants); - 34 behaviors (aggressive or cautious, ambusher, sneaky, false retreat, second wind, terror alone or at low health); - 11 company traits (elite gangs, summoned caragors, bodyguard counts, a DLC mount); - 36 story traits (betrayal, blood brothers, last words, no resurrection, self-raise, a DLC island's items); - 21 voice mannerisms ( Mannerism 01 to 21 ); - 5 system traits ( Marker In Hierarchy , Marker Is Archer , the three OrcRarity ). A trait's row is its record's UIGroup , not its kind: Quirk OlogHarpoon is UIGroup Classes ( StrengthPriority 10, items Olog 2HR Harpoon and Olog Harpoon ; it comes from the Tracker and Beast Master advanced classes), and Quirk OlogFlameThrower is UIGroup Bonuses (36).

The elemental weapons (curse, fire, poison, the necromancer's) are traits the reward system rolls; the game ships frost only for Talion and as captain defense ( Immune Frost , Resistant Frost , Hate Frost ), with no frost-weapon record, picker, reward, hit effect or text. Picker Curse Weapon is held by 28 reward definitions through PickerGroupsToGive ( EpicOrc , LT , KillPlayer ), 22 titles ( Faction/Roles/Definitions.PickerTraits ) and 10 presets. Everything on that path is read live: the reward lists ( Rewards/Lists.Reward ), the weights ( Definitions.WeightBase , the weighted pick 0x3505F4 under 0x350500), PickerGroupsToGive (0x351AF8) and the level table XPLevel.Entries (0x352DC4 <- 0x3513DC <- 0x34F9F0, which also calls 0x350500). - On a level-up the setups Default , Act1 and DLC3 name XPLevel::Default StatusEffect : a chance of 0.1% at levels 5-10, 0.2% at 11-20, 0.9% at 21-35 and 1% at 36-60 to roll the list StatusEffect StatusEffect (count 1, 15 entries, weight total 82), whose weapon entries are Curse 7.5, Necromancer 2.5, Fire 10 and Poison 10. A second table, Default GiveStatusEffect (4 / 6 / 8 / 10% over the same levels), is named by no setup. - Exclusivity is markers. Each element gives Marker StatusEffect <X and excludes MarkerList StatusEffect Not<X , and Marker NoStatusEffect sits in all three lists, so one element bars the others; MarkerList StatusEffect All lists every element. - The level tables also hold level-1 entries of chance 1.0 ( Default OrcRarity , Default Resistances ). Of the 1,239 reward definitions, 43 are held by no record.

Class = FM+0x278 (a Character/Models record) + FM+0x188 (that model's own combat tree) + one class-bonus slot Picker BaseStrength <Infantry Defender Archer Hunter Savage Olog . Six pairs exist (Orc Infantry, Orc Defender, Orc Archer, Orc Spearman, Orc Berserker, OlogHai Infantry, each with its AI <same tree); the spearman's bonus is Hunter and the berserker's Savage (156 of 156 living row captains follow this). Changing the class re-rolls the body at the next build (see Captain appearance); whether a class is an olog's is its record's AISimulationConfig , not its name. Advanced class = one slot Picker BaseStrength <Assassin BeastMaster Berserker CombatMaster Commander Destroyer Marksman Tank Tracker Trickster (155 of 156). All 16 BaseStrength pickers have table flags 1, one option and no exclusive group, so the slot's picker alone decides it, and it survives a save; the traits carry no item. AdvancedClass and OriginDeathTaunt are Faction/Rewards/Types weight records ( InitialValue , OnUseThisReturnToValue , OnUseOtherValueDeltaScale ) that no captain holds. A death-taunt "origin" is the title its reward gives ( Reward GruntDeathTauntOrigin <X : MustHaveAvailableRole RoleCategory <n <X with SetRoleFromFilter , the marker Marker GaveOriginDeathTaunt and one level). The Champion<X rewards ( CommonOrc , EpicOrc , LT , KillPlayer ) are the Legendary promotion: Picker OrcRarity Legendary , the epic Picker ET Champion<X , the BaseStrength slot, the advanced class's kit (for Destroyer Fire : explodes on death, plants mines, explosive shot, grenaded retreat, grenades at his feet, fire weapon), the markers Marker Specialization <X and Marker JustEarnedAdvancedClass , SetRoleFromFilter and XPLevelDeltaMin 1. Personality is the voice. FM+0x270 is a Faction/Personalities record (120 records; their ShortName is the voice set: pr, br, tw, wh, cv for orcs, ws, ze, bs for ologs, ea for Easterlings; empty for nonverbal and undead characters). Base tables live in Faction/PersonalityTable (11 orc, 3 olog, 4 mercenary). The engine's setter 0x1BC60A0(fm, record) (used by the reward SetPersonality 0x3523EB and by role changes that force a personality) removes the old personality's marker traits (0x79A1D4) and writes FM+0x270 . It then re-registers a captain in the world with the new voice (0x73D548: CCharacter+0x2B28 and AudioHooks/List.CharacterSpawns on [char+0x2808] ) and adds the new marker traits (0x7D3EA4), skipping markers while bit 38 is set. 0x7D3EA4 refuses a marker whose exclusive group is already held (every PersonalityMarker is in MarkerGroup Personality ), and the setter removes only the markers of the personality it replaces.

The card's rows are Interface/Menu/MenuTreeNode/TraitGroup records, each listing its UI groups in .TraitGroups (TraitType 0 / 1 = strengths / weaknesses). The rows are Immunities; Hates; Class traits (Classes); Bonuses (Bonuses and Epics); Mortal weaknesses (MortalVulnerabilities and Terrors); Vulnerabilities; "Dazed by" (WeakenedBy and Fears); and a hint row of the resistances. A row shows at most MaxVisTraits traits (7; the hint row 3), a limit read only by the Details layer (4 readers), so it caps the card and not the captain. Miscellaneous passives and rarity are not drawn. The number under each row's icon is the captain's trait count in that row. Icons are Icon strings ( interface\textures\hud\traits\enemy\...\x.tex ); base icons ship in interface\bundles\ingame navmarkers.bndl . A trait's PreviewBundle holds only its preview movie, and the picture behind a card is the trait's own PreviewMovie . GameModes.Bundle gives each game mode one UI texture bundle: the fourth DLC's mode interface\bundles\ingame tex dlc.bndl (129 textures, 7.1 MB, all 42 icons of hud\traits\enemy\dlc4\ ), the third DLC's ingame tex dlc2.bndl (43 assets, no trait icon the campaign lacks), and the other 11 modes ingame tex talion.bndl . The campaign therefore never loads the DLC4 trait art: 41 of those icons (all but easterling caragortamer.tex , which ships in the base set) are resident in no campaign bundle, and the card's request is registered with no data and draws a placeholder. The icons also ship as loose files, but a loose path alone stays absent: only a bundle makes them resident. The card builds from the path, so a reopened card shows art that has arrived since. The 484 traits use 161 distinct icons. Of the traits, 68 have no icon and 54 name pda\orcattributes\placeholder.tex (resident, a real picture); 116 of those 122 have no UIGroup . immunities\immune curse.tex (only DEMO ImmuneToCurse ) ships in no bundle. The four DLC3 light traits share fx\characters\shared\combat\blade light.tex , which the campaign's bundle carries. Monolith shipped identical pixels under several file names ( damageboostenemyhealthlow = defenseboostselfhealthlow , damageboostselfhealthhigh = defenseboostselfhealthhigh ), so the seven Easterling health traits use four images. Text. The localization strings carry the card's markup (counts over the base game's 63,493 strings): - color runs {Color <Alias }text</font (Enemy 593, Player 498, Objective 305, Broken 46, Intel 43, Epic 35, Follower 16, Reward 6, Weakened 5 ...); among trait names only Epic, which wraps 35 names whole ( {Color Epic}Epic Trait: Slayer Counter</font ); 36 of the 484 traits' Summary strings carry markup; - font runs <font face="$INTHUD" ...</font (51), glyph and button tokens ( {Poison} , {CombatPrimary03} , {EpicSkull} ), format arguments ( {1!s} , {2!d} ) and voice cues ( <laugh ). A color alias is a Profile/ActionAlias record ( Color Epic ; GamepadString, KBMString, FontColor) whose FontColor links an Interface/Color record with an ARGB Color . The token pass ReplaceActionsWithDevices 0x2995F8 (named by its own assert) turns each {name} that is an action alias into a <font color run of that color (0xD06CF0), after the game's own formatting. The aliases in use: Enemy 0xFFED5F09, Player 0xFF09D5ED, Objective 0xFFFFC640, Epic 0xFFE24E2C, Intel / Broken / Green 0xFF359737, Follower 0xFF09D5ED, Reward 0xFFED5F09, Weakened 0xFF94BFD6, Red 0xFFA42E06 and Hate 0xFFDF4E2C. Legendary 0xFF4700BF, Yellow 0xFFFFC640, Disabled 0xFF626262, Vulnerable 0xFF5279BD, Terrified 0xFF81294A and Immune 0xFFDC9B50 are defined but used by no string. There are 21 card names that belong to two or three traits each; the record names' family words tell them apart (Easterling / East, D4RES / DLC, DEMO, Elite, Rare, Six, Archer, CMT for Combat Master, Perm, ET): "Decoys" / "Decoys (Elite)" / the DLC's six-decoy version, "Agile" and its Easterling twin, and so on. Looks from traits. Of 334 addable traits, none sets ModelHide , BodyModelChange or AppearanceTags . Only Quirk Undead changes the body and colors: Body Scar BodyReplacement - IB Body Scar - AD Body Scar.ModelPicker (the scarred orc and olog bodies) plus I Am Undead Appearance( OLOG) (flair colors, cataract-eye material overrides, material-set variants and the undead effect).

- What a slot with a zero flag word does across every trait type in play (gang, summon and spawner hijack traits on a captain who is in the world). - Traits gated on a marker (for example Raise Dead , which wants Marker StatusEffect Curse ) and whether they act when forced. - Does only one gang spawn for a captain holding two gang traits? FM+0x378 caches the first gang leader and 0x1BC3CB4's only caller is the deactivation; spawning such a captain and reading his company would settle it. - Which events give the four nemesis card traits ( Hate Nemesis , Terror Nemesis , Hate SuperiorDamage , Quirk BloodBrother ), and which code reads the item-less behavior traits (betrayal, Prevent Resurrection , Quirk Ambusher , Quirk Sneaky ) by name. - Whether promotions run the level-up reward path that hands out elements, and whether the engine's reward filter 0x105AEC(fm, reward) is where the element markers bar a second element: emulated against live memory on 18 captains it refused every element to each captain that already held one, but no rolled promotion has been observed. - How the Army stage draws an elemental weapon's glow for a captain whose trait items are not on his record: a shipped fire weapon draws there, and the route from the trait's buff tag to the stage is not traced.

Campaign progress is data, held in two tables owned by the GameManager ( GM = [base+0x26FFAA8] ). Game variables. GameData/Variables holds 573 records ( VariableType 1 int, 2 bool, 0 float: 45 / 514 / 14, each with a default and a designer's description). The store is [GM+0x6C58] : +0x00 entries (stride 0x18), +0x08 count, +0x10 the category; an entry is +0x00 the record, +0x08 the value. Entries are in record-index order. Scripts use GameData.<Variable :GetValue() / :SetValue(v) ; the method tables are registered by 0x1B46E44, 0x1B46EF4 and 0x1B46FA4 (Set, SetValueByRecord, Get, GetSerializeId, TestPredicate). The getter core is 0x1E154C(store, record) and the bool setter 0x59A1D8(store, record, value). The variable StoryState carries the campaign stage; its own description lists the stages: Value Stage --- --- 5 intro 100 Act 1 105 after the intro of the Shadow of the Past 110 after Gondor 1 198 / 199 Blade 1 200 Act 2 205 / 210 after the Ratbag and Carnan steps 230 after Carnan 3 290 during the finale 300 after the finale Global-variable predicates ( Quest/GlobalVarPredicates , 290 records) gate quests and scenes. In the evaluator 0x1E1118: - with AndTest (the default) every test must pass, otherwise any one; - a bool test (0x1DFF70) passes when the value equals RequiredValue , and an int test (0x1E1470) when Min <= value <= Max (inclusive); - a test without a variable fails; - with no tests, an AND passes and an OR fails. Of the 573 variables, 330 are read by no GameDB record (scripts may still read them). Quests. The quest system is [GM+0x6C60] . Its table at +0x18 : entries of 0x40 bytes, count at +0x08 , category at +0x10 ; an entry is +0x00 the Quest/Quests record, +0x28 the placed quest object (null when its region is not loaded) and the byte +0x34 the completion counter. The completion core 0x1B55008 compares that counter with NumCompletesForPreReq (1 for every quest); a quest with no table entry counts as complete. The script method GetIsComplete (0x19F4064) takes a placed quest object, not a record: it reads [arg+0x258] , the record of the quest object that Quest.Create(scriptId, ...) gives a layer script, and passes that on. Called with a DBQuest.<name record it answers false for every quest: Intro Tower , IntroPart30 , FinalePart40 and Go01 all read false on a StoryState-300 save whose table held 463 complete quests, each with counter 1. 2,256 quests exist. GetIsActive 0x171A20 tests the object's state for 17. The running quests are listed at +0x3D8 of the quest system. The towers' story gate and the seeing-stone store are in Haedirs: towers, seeing stones and fast travel. Quest availability (0x1E00C4) rejects at the first failing gate, in this order: completed / incomplete quest lists ( Quest/QuestLists with RequireAllMatch ), failed last attempt, active / inactive quests, any quest active, triggerable quests, preset member unlocked, day only, the global-variable predicate, and the rest. The rejection messages exist in the executable, but the logging function they are passed to (0x19C83AC) is an empty ret in the shipped build.

A mission marker is a placed quest object (vt 0x1F9DFE0): +0x40 name, +0x58 context, +0x120 its state machine (vt 0x1F9DFB8), +0x180 the trigger and +0x188 the Quest/Quests record; the trigger's +0x198 is its navigation marker. The state is the pending state ( +0x12C ) unless that is -1, otherwise the current state ( +0x128 ); SetState 0x159DE4 parks the current state at -1 during a transition. The dispatcher 0x1162D8 sends five events: 0 CanEnter, 1 CanExit, 2 Enter, 3 Update, 4 Exit. State Meaning --- --- 0 Inactive 1 SimEventEval 2 PreActivate 3 DirectActivate 4 FadeOut 10 TimeOfDay 11-15 Load 16 InstantiateBundles 17 Active (CanEnter = its bundles loaded; Update = the fail-distance check) 19 PostActive 20 / 21 / 22 Completed / Failed / Cancelled 25 Cleanup ActivateBypassTrigger (body 0x19F060C) moves a quest in state 2 or lower to state 3; its handlers run synchronously, so it belongs on the main thread. Tribe missions fail beyond 120 m of their relay (the prefab script sets QR:SetFailObject(QR, 15000) and RequestDistanceToObjectEvents(QR, 12000) ). Teleports are queued. CCharacter.TeleportToObject for the player (0x658C30) pushes 0x659884 onto the queue at [base+0x2A86880] and sets the character's byte +0x2C21 until the engine performs it; the AI version is 0x658B5C. The character vtable's slot 109 ( +0x368 ) is TeleportToObject and slot 110 ( +0x370 ) TeleportToPoint (coordinates in xmm1-xmm3). CCharacter.TeleportToLastKnowNavMeshPos 0x19B7AA0 is the engine's own "unstuck", also queued.

A story character is a Faction/PresetMembers record (203 exist); a built orc carries it at FM+0x190 (FactionMember; see The Nemesis system). Two paths build them: army initialization ( Faction/Definition.PresetMembers , 0xFDAC54) and quests, whose PrefetchPresetFactionMembers are built fresh at the quest's LoadFactionBundles state (0x625D98 - 0x62662C - the army of the current region - 0x62666C). The build sequence: 1. ctx = 0x18DE04(FS+0x98, army) (asserts on a record that is not an army: an army context is a 0x290-byte entry whose +0x18 matches the army category); 2. fm = 0x1C1D378(ctx, preset) ; 3. if 0x1C1C638([ctx+0xD8], preset) (the preset belongs to that army), 0x1BD2300([ctx+0x20], fm) . A character created without a row starts at level NoRowXPLevel - 1 . The build copies GlobalVarToSetOnDeath to FM+0x398 ; SetDead 0x626E38 sets bit 2 of FM+0x508 and sets that campaign variable (for example the Bruz brothers' death variables, which gate the next brother's ambush). After his story ambush the character becomes a captain of the current region (row, tribe, role, rarity) and FM+0x190 is cleared. A built copy is saved. A queued ambush fires only in its own region: the request's +0x18 must equal the current region's faction [FS+0x1B8] (0x6DD92C, "The faction has changed"); otherwise it is retried. A preset ( Faction/PresetMembers ) carries, besides the fields in the table below, the character's standing in the systems around him: CanBeNemesis , CanSetAsTarget , CanEverBeHenchmen , CanEverChangeLocation , CanPlayerAssignToSimEvent , CanPlayerSelectAsOverlord , CanSlotInAssaultGroup , CanVow , DisableSimEvents (with DisableSimEventExceptions ), DisableOrderEvents , LockedXPLevel , NoRowXPLevel , FactionRow / FactionColumn / DisplayFactionRow , PresetHenchmen / UsePresetHenchmen , Morale , IsGoldenPath , IsDarkTalion , SeedHigh / SeedLow / UseSeedValues , UnlockName , UnlockTraits , Events , InvolvedQuests and nav-marker overrides. The script natives around presets are NPC::IsPresetFactionMember (0x19B6B78), System::HierarchyResetPreSetMemberData (0x1C2373C), HierarchyUnlockPreSetMemberData and its tutorial twin (0x1B5CEC0), SetCanInterrogateAboutPresetFactionMember (0x1B5C314), CCharacter::SetLinkToPresetMember and Faction::CreateFactionMemberBuilder (0x1B5B824). The UI predicates Interface/Predicates/FactionMemberPreset::PresetMember Bruz and Ranger name the preset, not the role.

In one late campaign, twelve built copies of seven story characters (found by their name string id at FM+0x170 ) agree with their presets field by field: Preset field Member Notes --- --- --- Name +0x170 a string key ( Bruz CharName , OrcName Unique Forthog , or an ordinary OrcNameGen1st ); the member holds its P919 id OverrideModel +0x278 (class) the model's own CombatTree is the tree the body fights with in the world CombatTree +0x188 (army tree) 12 of 12 copies hold their preset's tree, which can differ from the model's: Zog's model fights with AI Zog while +0x188 holds AI Spearman ; the Ranger's model is GP Ranger , his army tree AI Olog Infantry RoleList - Roles[0] +0x318 the title and the role items (Bruz's mauled head, olog mauled head Bruz , is a role item); the role's Tribes entry names the tribe at +0x328 ( TribeDef Bruz is Bruz's own) the role's ForcedPersonality , else the preset's Personality +0x270 Bruz's three brothers carry personalities of their own ( SpecialButterfly 411 Baz , 412 Gaz , 413 Daz ) PickerTraits the trait slots a preset without EnableTraitChanges gives exactly its list (Bruz 11 of 11, the Ranger 7 of 7, the Shadows of the Past warchiefs 22 on 22 and 24 on 25); with it the member carries more (Zog 36 to 37 on 15, Baz 34 on 2) Rarity and the advanced class are ordinary pickers on the list ( Picker OrcRarity , Picker BaseStrength <advanced class ), or the preset's RewardLists name a Specialization <advanced class reward. A preset whose list names no rarity picker leaves +0x390 null: six of the seven such copies read (Bruz, the Ranger, the Shadows of the Past warchiefs), the seventh, back from death, is Common. Zog's first preset lists Picker OrcRarity Common , and his three copies are Common. Each boss tree these presets use names a DefaultAITemplate ( GP Bruz - GP Bruz , AI Zog - Orc Zog , AI Forthog - Orc Forthog , GP Ranger - OlogHai Infantry ), the template that summoning and member spawns take from the army tree. Their class models are linked only by their presets and their AI templates. The Shadows of the Past missions ( StatueOfThePast <region SC ) each have a warchief preset SotP <region SC with a class model of its own ( SOTP<region Orc <class Warchief ) and two bodyguard presets.

t: Quest jobs pick members by role
x: A Quest/Jobs/Definition takes an existing member through IncludedRole / ExcludedRole (role lists), RequiredPresetFactionMember with CanBePresetFactionMember , IncludedCharacterType , MustBeAlive , RowRank , MustBeAssignedToOutpostPosition and similar tests, or builds one ( FactionMemberBuilder , FactionMemberBuilderChance ); AliasJob names the job whose member it shares. Every role list that names a story character's role, and every record that names those lists, shows three patterns: - The characters' own story jobs require the preset member itself: Rat2 Bruz / Rat2Replay Bruz ( GP Bruz / GPR RB2 Bruz ) and Rat2 Ranger / Rat2Replay Ranger ( GP Ranger / GPR RB2 Ranger ). - Special Butterfly Roles (Bruz and his three brothers) is excluded by 27 jobs (mission subjects and their opponents, side-quest captains, Rat3 Enemy1 to 5 , Rat3 Executioner ), and GP RoleCategory Bruz by four more ( Finale EnemyOlog , Captain Gondor4 , GonSide2 Captain , GonSide3 Captain ): these jobs never draw them. - Two jobs include a unique's role without requiring the preset: GP Bruz Volcano PostRelease (alias PS Subject , Bruz's role category) and PC ShamedCaptain ContextAmbJob ( RoleCategory Shamed Unashamed Daz ). The selection reads the member's role, so any member that holds the role passes that test. Zog and Forthog have no job (only their presets, a dialogue marker predicate and the savior's class maps name them), and the class models of these characters ( GP Bruz , SQ Zog , GP Ranger , Orc Forthog , the Shadows of the Past models) are named only by their presets and AI templates. Forthog Orc-Slayer ( Forthog OrcSlayer , role Role OrcSlayer with a lute) is the game's tribute to Michael Forgey (1973-2016), its own text says; a second preset, Savior ForthogOrcSlayer , shares his role list.

Faction/PresetMembers::GP Nazgul Suladan is a base-game character the player never keeps: model Nazgul ArPharazon and tree AI Nazgul ArPharazon (Ar-Pharazôn was the working name; 114 records carry it), role list GP RoleCategory WitchKing , morale Immune , LockedXPLevel 10, IsGoldenPath ; false CanBeNemesis , CanSetAsTarget , CanEverBeHenchmen , CanEverChangeLocation , CanPlayerAssignToSimEvent and CanPlayerSelectAsOverlord ; true CanVow and CanSlotInAssaultGroup ; DisableSimEvents with the one exception Promote Suladan WC . He is a QuestOnlyPresetMembers entry of Minas Ithil's army and its quest-replay twin. - His name. The five presets GP Nazgul 00 , 01 , Hammerhand , Isildur and Suladan share the name key GP Nazgul ("Ringwraith", 5 of 203 presets) and the title Name Nazgul Generic ("Nazgûl"); their real names exist only as Appendix keys, the Name of Inventory/UIItemData::UI Denizens ( App Name Suladan "Suladân", App Name Isildur , App Name Helm "Helm Hammerhand"), while the Witch-king's own preset takes App Name WitchKing as its name. Every copy of the five is named "Ringwraith". - The fight is Blade15 ("The Tower of Sorcery", layer minasithil/blade15 ): the script spawns him, gives GP B15 Nazgul and No SaviorKill IT and registers AI ArPharazon CurseAOE ; a counter-stun kill plays Blade15 Suladan Domination , whose event finishes with no action, no command set and no script keys, then the script removes him and the quest ends. Nothing in it makes him a follower, and his area attack is meant to kill followers (the script plays BL015 030 Sul KillsFollowers when the player's dominated orcs die to it). - The job that picks him , Quest/Jobs/Definition::GP Suladan ( RequiredPresetFactionMember his preset, CanBePresetFactionMember and MustBeAlive true, builder chance 1.0, alias PS Subject , no follower filter), runs twice on the story's path. Minas Ithil's NazgulTime adds the picker Nazgul Promote Suladan - the sim event Promote Suladan WC ( SubjectAlwaysWins ), and he becomes a Minas Morgul warchief. StartShadowWar adds EjectWarchief for GP Isildur and GP Suladan , which the finale fires right after StoryState is set to 300. So any second living member built from his preset can be taken by either step until then. In a save at StoryState 300 the game's own copy is a "Ringwraith" at level 10, in Minas Ithil, with no row, not a follower.

The shipped data never lets the player's Overlord betray: - all 18 betrayal ambush definitions list Overlord in ExcludedRowRanks (91 of 100 ambush definitions do); - the betrayal job General Betrayal picks only captain and warchief rows; - the betrayal triggered by hitting a follower ( ImmediateBetrayal Predicate : 3 hits in 3 s, then 5 in 6 s) requires IsOverlord Not . No Overlord-specific betrayal voice exists; a forced betrayal plays the Overlord's own personality line. AI BecomeHighestLevelFollower Betrayal takes a provided ambusher ( NeverPickAmbusherWithJob ), and TriggerAmbush is 0x6DDCB8. Region ownership has two planes. - The faction. Faction:GetFactionPlayerOwned (stub 0x7A2800) asks 0x1E484C(FS, faction), which returns the region's Overlord, and its wrappers (0x7D18BC, 0x1E47AC) test bit 27 of his FM+0x508 , nothing else. An Overlord who betrays therefore takes the fortress with him, and a region can be held while its captains stay enemies (Minas Ithil was held with 21 enemy captains in one save). The fort-defense script ( OwnerNamedOnSpawn ) converts any named defender, the Overlord included, to the attackers on a FA FollowerBetraysPlayer event. - The ground. Faction:GetAreaPlayerOwned (0x696FF0) reads a table of 180 areas from 0x6221F0(FS, [FS+0x1B8] ): the object's +0x78 holds {area record, u8 owned at +8} entries of 0x10 bytes, its count u32 at +0x80 (the same object for all six regional armies). It answers false while the online flag [GM+0x6D30]+0x47C is set. The world scripts ask by area: fortress gates and map canvases ( FortControl ), stoplights, tower scenarios and the grunts' side rule (see AI). What moves the area table. Faction::ApplyAreaOwnershipTransform 0xF624E0(FS, record) from scripts, and natively the sim-event result step 0x62258C (the result's AreaOwnershipTransform field; its callers include the event dispatcher 0x62E670 and Quest::SetSimEventResultType 0x19FA100). Faction/AreaOwnershipTransform has 20 records, 10 To Player / To Sauron pairs (the 5 fortresses and the 5 Lithlad outposts; none for Minas Ithil); an entry is {owner enum: 1 player, 2 Sauron; area} , for example Núrnen's pair over IS FortFront and IS FortRear . SetAreaPlayerOwned writes one byte through 0x1B5ECA8; SetAllCurrentWorldAreasPlayerOwned(bool) writes every area brush of the current world (0x1A03E88). Both planes are saved: an Overlord's bit and the areas set in one world survived a world reload and a restart. Outside fortresses and outposts the only area write in the shipped scripts is one mission's Vale Fort . The real conquest. The siege quest's completion ( FA QuestComplete ) applies the fortress's transform, gives the <Region FortOwned item, sets GameData.<Region Fort , adds one to PlayerOwnedForts , sets LastFortConquered and removes the bought war upgrades ( RemoveFortUpgradeList(FortConqueredReset) ). Quest::SetFortAssaultComplete 0x19F9B8C - 0x1B5BB68 - 0x1C1E828(context, on) fires OverlordEjectedEvent , vacates his seat (0x61B274), clears the sim events, flips all spies, ejects the warchiefs (0x1C23B90, WarchiefEjectedEvent ), creates an emergency player follower and sets ctx+0x214 ; it needs a running fortress quest ( Quest/Types.IsFortAssault ). SetAllAreasPlayerOwner is false on all five SC FA quests, so a conquest takes the fortress's areas only. Losing a fortress is the mirror: to Sauron and DisableFortFastTravel (the item off, the bool false). GameData.<Region Fort changes the fortress at once (the fort's FortStatusInit subscribes to its change event and runs FortOwnerIsPlayer ), while the area flag is what placed prefabs read when they initialize.

Faction/Transforms holds four records (AddOlogs, AddBerserkers, AddDefenders, AddSpearmen). The game applies them once, when the Shelob mission in Cirith Ungol completes ( mtnpass/shelob1 QuestComplete), to the Minas Ithil and Cirith Ungol factions. A transform's ClassInjections name a StructuresFactionTransformClass record (OldFactionMemberJob Quest/Jobs/Definition::PlayerKiller Duel Other , a ChanceArray [0,1,2,4,1] , and PossibleSimEvents Transform IntoCaptain <class ); AddOlogs runs the Berserker event, because no Olog event ships. The binding 0x1B755EC leads to the injection 0x1C261A4 - 0x1BD2A54 - the job filler 0x1BD40C4, which builds a new orc only when the job names a FactionMemberBuilder (0x1BD42F1). This job names none, so it picks existing members (0xF9A320, matcher 0xF9BB20: alive, captain rank, no species, faction or identity filter) and seats them. Return packages. The 23 WillResurrect <death events are the package applied to a captain who came back from that kind of death: LevelsToAdd 1, 15 actions, KeepPriority 30, reward lists MaybeNewRole CheatDeath <death , CheatDeath Ambush and Betrayal CheatDeath Ambush , the ambusher flag and the resurrected gear tag. The 31 Contract training orders mostly add a level and the trait, gang or mount, plus Upgrade CommonOrcToEpic and Contract RemoveAnEpicTrait ; the element orders add only the element.

A scripted scene is a presentation. The scripts queue a relay on the player: System:GetPlayer():QueuePresentation(DBPresentationRelay.FortAssault Intro, overlord) . The native call is CPlayerObj::QueuePresentation 0x734C30(player, relay, target) - 0x734C7C(the player's scene component [player+0x2FC0] , relay, target), which builds a message holding the relay's Event , the target handle (0x18D888) and a camera type (message +0x78 ). The chain is relay - event - sequence pool - the first sequence whose predicate passes - elements. Each element sets a camera, a duration or an advance hook, script keys, voice and actions; an action is {source actor, target actor, AnimType or AudioKey} . A sequence plays only if every predicate passes; WarchiefIntro EVT , for example, tries the mounted betrayal, the betrayal, the failed spy chief and finally the default.

- The target actor ( Target ACT , Overlord ACT ) is the relay's target, tested by the AssumedTargetPredicate . - Extra actors (a failed spy chief, a betrayer, a beast) come from ExtraTargetPredicates . The binder 0x4303E4 takes the first character in a candidate list that passes its object predicate and is not already bound. 0x6FD134 picks the list: relay messages (types 14 / 15) use [base+0x27265B0] , every spawned character (it keeps corpses too: about 60 of 120 entries in a battle); other messages use [base+0x2728EE8] , a subset of about 12. - Object predicates bind actors mostly by inventory items , which the scene scripts hand out ( AddInventoryItem ). The sequence evaluator 0x3650B4 is called per pool entry by the start routine 0x43E6B8, and the queued message is its context (subject at ctx+0x88 , source at ctx+0x80 ). It tests, in order: 1. the player predicate; 2. the source predicate: a source, when present, must pass the object predicate and is bound to its actor by 0x43EE28, and a failure fails the branch; 3. the assumed-target predicate (the subject; none fails the branch); 4. the player's-target predicate (0x182B5F0 - 0x523B0C( [player+0x2FA0] ) = the player's own combat object's current target; null while idle, which fails the branch); 5. the AI-spawn predicate last, so a spawn anchored on the target sees a source-bound victim. Field reads go through a per-category slot table ( [base+0x2645720] - static slots at 0x2892A70, 0x48 bytes each). The evaluator does not check that the target is still alive: the target test reaches the held-item test 0x24DF7C( [char+0x2348] , item) through 0x365882 - 0x2F1768 - 0x275BE0, so a character being removed (inventory component already cleared) faults there.

The camera filter 0x4328DC compares each pool entry's CameraType and CameraVariantRequireAny with the active type [ctx+0x38] and variant [ctx+0x40] . The type is decided when the relay is queued (0x734E1C): the relay's own CameraType (at +0x20 in every relay, a link to Presentation/Predicates/Types/Camera ), otherwise, when QuestCameraType is set, the PresentationCameraType of the first running quest. Siege quests carry <Region FortAssault CT , so the fixed fortress shots exist only inside a siege. The variant (A or B, the two sides an assault can start from) comes from the sequence's CameraVariance picker. Fixed frames are absolute world positions in cm ( Presentation/WorldFrame , 694 records with CameraPos and LookAtPos ); their prefixes name the regions: DS Lithlad, IS Nurnen, MP Cirith Ungol, SM Seregost, VC Gorgoroth.

t: The scene clock and slow motion
x: Every element duration is a timer at +0x288 of the running presentation, on the clock [base+0x2702578] (0x37B784 - 0x37BCE4; expiry is bit 1 of pres+0x6C ). The engine keeps five scaled clocks, which slow motion drives as channels (0x5CF888): 0 the world [base+0x2702598] , 1 the player [base+0x2702548] , 2 the combat companion [base+0x2702570] , 3 the world UI [base+0x2702558] and 4 presentations [base+0x2702578] . 0x5CF834 writes a clock's numerator, denominator and scale at [clock+8]+0x28 / +0x2C / +0x30 ; 0x5CEBB4 resets it to 1/1. A slow-motion instance stores channel c as {+0x44 enabled, +0x48 scale} + c 0xC . Period and ramp-up timers run on [base+0x2702550] (UI: [base+0x2702588] ), which slow motion never scales. The slow-motion manager is MainScene+0x7A8 (ticked by the scene tick): requested instances at +0x00 / +0x08 , the running one at +0x38 (the update 0x5CF55C picks the lowest priority at instance+0x80 ; requests go through 0x5D08B8). An instance copies its SlowMo record's scales at Start (0x5CEC10), and the manager re-runs Start whenever its current instance changes. A SlowMo record's enum pair (1, N) means N times slower (332 records; KillCam 13x SM = (1, 13)). Advance hooks ( Presentation/AdvanceHook , 122 records) are {Actor, Hook} with hook 0 FacialEnd, 1 DialogEnd, 2 AttackEnd and 5 AttackStart. They are raised by 0x42DA2C (via 0x42DA18 and the attacker's presentation link [obj+0x100] , from the attack path 0x2E0520) and matched by 0x42FFEC(pres, type, actor) against the element's copied hook ( pres+0x1C0 ). AdvanceOnTargetDeath (0x37B6C4) advances when the target actor's binding returns null; a victim's dead flag and binding drop as the execution starts. Element camera definitions, durations and slow motion are copied when the presentation starts (0x5D0AB4). A presentation can take the camera and hold the player ( CommandSet PresentationDisablePlayer ); 0x17A13AC stops the player's scene component.

t: The screen fader and its locks
x: The screen fader is [[CGameClientShell+0xE38]+0x160] (CGameClientShell [base+0x26FFA98] ). A lock 0x6589E4(fader, reason) sets bit reason of +0xD0 (reasons under 11) or of +0xD4 ; its wrappers are 0x6589D8 (by owner) and 0x6588E8 (with fade parameters). An unlock is 0x657974(owner [CGameClientShell+0xE38] , reason) - 0x657980, wrapper 0x658A44. The screen fades back in only when no lock is held, so a black screen that never ends is a lock that was never released; the fader's state byte +0x08 says what the screen does (2 fading out, 3 out, 1 fading in, 0 clear). Reason Taken by Released by --- --- --- 3 presentation elements with a fade-out (0x5D3170 in the element player 0x5D20C4); a script ScreenFade out (0x1D86F28) a presentation's fade-in (0x5D310D); a script ScreenFade in (0x1D86FB2): the only two 4 quest fades (0x5769A8, 0x19F723C) 0x57407C 5 (lock site not read) its flag is byte +0x188 of the manager at [base+0x2A86880] that manager's tick 0x4C6050, once 0x1DCC20( [GM+0x6D98] ) answers true 6 (lock site not read) byte +0x189 of the same manager: the scripted player-model setup (record +0x180 = StructuresQuest.PlayerModelSetup ) 0x4C5EFC: it waits for the fade to be fully out, applies the model (0x19BB3CC), and unlocks only once the player's build flag [player+0x2D40] is down, [player+0x19A8] is set and every gear request is ready (0x7B86B8) 7 the player's queued teleport (0x658828) the teleport queue's finisher 0x658650 Reason 2 is held at every arrival in a region (its sites are not read). Reason 4 was held for 12 s at a mission start, until the player's build flag fell, and reason 3 for 1 to 2 s while the player scenes EnterZone Player EVT and Resurrect Player EVT ran. Bit 11 of +0xD4 turns on for about a second, many times a minute, in ordinary play. A lock bit alone therefore does not mean a dark screen: the state byte beside it does. A mission start that takes lock 3 and whose fade-up scene never plays leaves the screen black over an Active mission (see Outposts, strongholds and fortress upgrades, "The assault missions").

The animation a sync kill plays comes from a variant table. AnimationData.AnimOverridePicker / AnimOverrides lead to Combat/AttackAnimOverride , whose entry is chosen by the attacker's weapon class (0x2D5430, which checks the source's character type [combat+0x60] and weapon type per entry); the entry holds StructuresCombatAttackAnimOverride variants (Weight, source and target animations, the source's weapon animation, PresentationCameraType, SeverActionTarget and Pred gates). The chooser 0x2D5828 keeps variants with weight 0 that pass every gate, then picks at random by weight (0x1B3B90) among those not played within RecentAttackWindow ; when all are recent it plays the oldest, so one passing variant always plays. Olog entries are selected only by weapon type ( SourceRequiredWeaponType = WeaponTypeList/Olog All ), so an olog holding an orc-typed weapon item draws an orc animation. Combat/Sync sets both characters' scale (0x11498C8) to SourceModelScaleOverride / ModelScaleOverride ; with UseMinimalScaling it keeps only their difference, split half each (0x202E8F8).

A siege is staged by the fortress layers' scripts with presentations and animate tasks. Scene Relay Cameras --- --- --- Warchief walk-out intro ( WarchiefIntro EVT ) WarchiefIntro RL follow the actor Fort defense: the Overlord arrives ( FortDefense OverlordArrival EVT ) FortDefense Overlord follow the actor; the voice line rides the presentation, so any orc delivers it Talion's victory walk-out ( FortOutro TalionBalcony EVT ) FortAssault Outro ( Conquest without the speech) a rig on Talion's clip Keep throne showdown ( Overlord Showdown EVT ) FortAssault OverlordKeep a fixed throne view per fortress, then follow Keep-top intro: the Overlord executes the failed spy chief ( FortAssault Intro Overlord EVT ) none (only the NextEvent of the walk-out) fixed fortress frames The Witch-king makes an Overlord kill himself ( She3 OverlordSuicide EVT ) its relay has no event follow the actor Spy-chief reveal explosion ( SpychiefExplosion 0x EVT ) FA RevealSpy 0x look at the target E3 demo fortress scenes ( DEMO ) FAD E3 rigs (cut content) Of the 860 Presentation/Events , 85 belong to fortress assaults and defenses, with 103 relays. Script keys ( FA Intro UnhideOverlord SK , FD OV Arrive DoorOpen SK ...) do not stop a scene; they are signals the siege layer's scripts listen to. - What the bytes at +0x30..+0x3F of a quest-table entry mean. The table lookup returns the entry's value part at +0x08 , and GetIsComplete reads the completion count as the byte at value +0x2C (entry +0x34 ). In one late campaign (2,256 entries): the word at +0x30 held 1 to 6 (3 on 1,953 entries, 1 on 255, 4 on 31, 6 on 6, 5 on 5, 2 on 4); +0x31 .. +0x33 and +0x35 were 0; +0x34 was 1 on 459; +0x36 .. +0x3E are 0 / 1 flags set on 80 to 1,975 entries each; +0x3F held many different small values. - Whether the warchief intro's lines are personality dialogue (they did not play on a plain grunt). - What the 56 placeholder movies of the third story DLC stand in for at run time (see Audio and video). - Where the traits beyond a preset's list come from when the preset sets EnableTraitChanges : two built copies of Zog at the preset's level 20 carry 36 traits on 15 listed pickers (a third, at level 42, 37), Baz 34 on 2. The build adding them would match Zog's count at his starting level; later events are not ruled out. - Which code reads the Interface/Predicates/FactionMemberPreset predicates ( PresetMember Bruz , PresetMember Ranger ), and so whether a member that holds only the unique's role matches them. - What set Núrnen's fortress areas when its Overlord became a follower without a transform being applied: the best candidate is the sim-event result step 0x62258C; reading the area table before and after a world load around a plain follower change would settle it. - Where the screen fader's reasons 2, 5 and 6 are locked, and which owner toggles bit 11 of +0xD4 .

t: Haedirs: towers, seeing stones and fast travel
x: The campaign has 15 Haedirs, three each in Minas Ithil, Cirith Ungol, Nurnen, Gorgoroth and Seregost. Purifying one at its seeing stone unlocks fast travel to it, lights its flame and counts toward the region's challenge. The engine keeps a purified Haedir as three separate pieces of saved state, and derives one of them from another when the player enters the world.

t: A purified Haedir is three pieces of state
x: Piece Where Read by --- --- --- the seeing stone's owned byte the stone store [GM+0x6D28] the stone at its initialization (its flame), and the item reconcile when the player enters the world the item <Region Tower 0N the player's inventory fast travel, the map marker, region progress, DLC side quests, the tower's own script GameData.<Region Tower 0N the GameData variable store no GameDB record reads it (its 15 predicates have no users) (The Minas Ithil variables are spelled MinasItihlTower in the data.)

[GM+0x6D28] keeps the stones in the same layout as the GameData store ( GM+0x6C58 ) and the quest store ( GM+0x6C60 ): an array of {record, u8 owned} entries of 0x10 bytes at +0x70 , the u32 count at +0x78 , and at +0x80 the category it holds, WorldPuzzle/SeeingStone (16 records: the 15 stones and Base ). Function What it does --- --- get 0x19C90CC(store, record) asserts "Bad record index" unless the record's category is the store's, indexes by RecordIndexOf 0x1898E8, checks that the entry holds the same record, returns the byte != 0 (0x19C91A0: is any stone owned) set 0x19C9BA4(store, stone object) finds the entry for the stone's record ( [stone+0x1B0] ) through 0x19C9014 and writes 1; no event, no other flag; its only caller is the purify load 0x19C94D0(table, stream) a count, then per entry a record (by hash, 0x17A9528) and the byte for that record: the store is part of the save The stone object is a SeeingStone (vt 0x200B5E8). It keeps its record at +0x1B0 and a copy of the owned byte at +0x211 , taken by its initialization (vf16 0x1D60140; the copy is made at 0x1D601D9). The script method SeeingStone:IsPlayerOwned (0x1170DF4) returns that cached byte. The script class has no setter: its members are Cast , Create , GetCanExit , GetEnabled , IsPlayerOwned , Serialize , SetCanExit and SetEnabled . The items follow the store, not the other way around. On entry into the world, the player's handler 0x19BD8F8 calls 0xE857A0 with the store. For every owned stone whose UnlockItem is missing from the inventory, that function adds the item ( AddItemToInventory 0x1C1224); UnlockItem is a WorldPuzzle/SeeingStone field read only by 0xE85340, which only this caller calls. A stone owned in the store therefore restores its fast travel at the next world entry, while an item alone does not light a flame. The store's owner holds more than the stones: - a list of 0x68-byte world-item entries at +0xE8 (0x19CA048, keyed to GameModes.ItemSpawnTransferableToModes ), which 0x19C992C walks for Social/Gifts/Save ; - a list of 0x28-byte entries at +0x00 (0xE85760, called from the player's vf134 0x19BB8BC); - a flag at +0x69 , set on entering any stone's view and cleared at 0x1D5E938; - the data that System::SetItemLocationRevealed reads (0x1A08660). The stone array itself is written through its lookup 0x19C9014 by exactly two functions, the setter and the loader.

In GameDB, 118 cells point at the 22 Tower 0 items. For each campaign tower: - Regions/TravelPoint::<Region 0N.UnlockItem unlocks the fast-travel point, and its NavMarkerSetup[].RequiredItem shows the map marker. - WorldPuzzle/SeeingStone::SeeingStone <Region 0<N+1 .UnlockItem names it: a stone's number is its item's number plus one (15 of 15). - Combat/Predicates/Item::TowerPurify <Region lists the region's three items, used only by Quest/AutoObjectives::TowerPurify <Region .IncludedPlayerAddItemList : the region's progress counts item additions. - The Blade of Galadriel side quests Blade Side02 to 05 require towers ( RequiredInventoryItemAll ), and three demo loadouts in Inventory/ItemLoadouts ( E317 , E317 Ellie , WW Demo ) hand them out. Tut TowerOwned lists all 15 and is used by no record; MinasIthil QuestTowersActive is the tutorial's marker item. The GameData switches. All 15 <Region Tower 0N variables are set by the tutorial, not by climbing: finishing Minas Ithil's tower mission ( PostIntro SR IdentifiedBarrows ) runs the remote script Intro EnableAllTowers ( IMI EnableAllTowers.Script ), which sets every one. A finished save therefore reads all 15 true whether or not the towers were purified. HaedirUnlocked (read by Interface/Predicates/GameState::IsHaedirUnlocked , a menu legend) is not a story gate.

- The tower prefab prefabs\gameplay\travel\watchtower notower.prefab06c (in each region's .scripts ): its SO:Init , after a one-second wait, asks self.player:HasInventoryItem(self.UnlockItem) . With the item held it does nothing more; without it, it waits for the stone's OnGainOwnership , then plays the tower presentation and runs the region's unlock script. Its FXSO:Init starts the blue flame ( Haedir CB ) when SS:IsPlayerOwned() or GameData.DLC DLC3Active holds, else Sauron's ( Haedir Sauron ). Both read their state once, at initialization: a tower that is already loaded keeps its look until its layer loads again. - The purify is the first use of the stone's view, 0x1D5E398: if +0x211 is 0 and the current game mode has GameModes.SaveCurrentWorld , it sets +0x211 to 1, calls the store setter 0x19C9BA4, runs the achievement check and raises the presentation and ownership event; the script side then fires. - The unlock script in each region's travel.worldlayer06c , Watch 0N SR.Script1 , runs System:GetPlayer():AddInventoryItem(DBInventoryItem.<Region Tower 0N, 1) and GameData.<Region Tower 0N:SetValue(true) . - The DLC unlocker prefabs\gameplay\quests\dlc3\dlc3haedirunlock.prefab06c , used when the Blade of Galadriel story starts, gives each missing tower the same item and variable, and lights the flame through DLC DLC3Active rather than through the store. The achievement. Interface/AchievementSetup.SeeingStoneChecks lists the 15 stones. Its accessor 0x17C3DB0 has one caller, 0x17C6EAC, whose one caller is the purify (0x1D5E48E). Only a purify done at a stone evaluates it; nothing that writes the store does. The records involved are Interface/Achievements::PurifiedHaedir (trophy 27, 20 points), Interface/Collectables::PurifiedHaedir and the profile statistics AchievementsPurifiedHaedir / HaedirPurified in Interface/GameProfileData . The region challenge. Quest/DynamicChallenge::TowerPurify <Region has a stage whose ItemAwards is a skill point (5 of 5 regions) and a goal with CompleteProgress 3 and the automatic objective TowerPurify <Region (type 28) counting additions of the region's three tower items. Purifying a region's three Haedirs pays one skill point. The story gate. Quest/Quests::Intro Tower ( GoldenPathQuest NoFade , contributes to progress, cannot be quit, after IntroPart30 ) is the story's first Haedir: it completes when the player identifies the barrows through a purified tower's stone. Lithlad has no campaign Haedirs. Desert Tower 00 to 05 unlock Regions/TravelPoint::Desert 00 to 05 , which neither the campaign's fast-travel legend ( QuestLog Row6 FastTravel : the fort, the landmarks, the zone exit) nor the online modes' LockedTravelPointsOverride lists; no seeing stone or purify objective names them. ( Desert Tower 01 's predicate tests DesertFort 01 , a slip in the data.)

Each tower is a Watch 0N prefab instance. Its objects include the flames FX SS CB World / FX SS Sauron World and their wraith-world versions FX SS CB Wraith / FX SS Sauron Wraith ; the eyes FX Eye CB / FX Eye Sauron (all SpecialFXSeq , vt 0x1DC1530); the transitions FX SS Transition / FX Eye Transition ( SpecialFX ); the stone SSP.SS ; the script objects FXSO and SO ; and the map marker LockedNM . Placed objects are found by name through the update manager's object sets at [base+0x26FF050]+0x3E0+0x18 : 128 sets, one per world context (vt 0x1DB5D58), each with its name table at +0x68 . The tower's script ( fx watchtower.script06a ) starts the flame once at initialization, by SS:IsPlayerOwned() . Its WraithOnCallback (wraith vision or a presentation) starts the eye and the wraith flame of the matching color, by IsPlayerOwned() at that moment, and its WraithOffCallback stops exactly what it started. So the eye exists only in wraith vision, and after a purify both the flame and the eye keep the old color until the layer initializes again: after advancing the time of day ( System.AdvanceTimeOfDay 0x1787D08) or a load. The SpecialFXSeq class provides Start (0x74F0E4), Shutdown (0x74F1A0), QuickStart (0x1B201F0), QuickShutdown (0x1B201A4) and IsPlaying (0x1B1FEF4). Its sequence player sits at +0x138 ; the player's vf1 takes 0 to start, 1 to start quickly and 2 to shut down, and IsPlaying is 0x114ED48(+0x138) != -1 . The effects are haedir cb loop.fxp (a sprite, a light and two sounds), watchtower eye cb loop.fxp (a light, 3 models and 7 particle systems) and haedir cb wraith loop.fxp (a sprite and 2 particle systems). They use their own materials, such as haedir glow.mat , cele eyeball flame.mat and sauron eyeball flame.mat , and textures in color pairs such as cele eyeflame v2.tex / sauron eyeflame v2.tex . None of them has a MaterialController, so their color lives in the textures and the lights (see Visual effects).

- Whether 0x17C6EAC is what updates the HaedirPurified profile statistic, and whether anything but the setter and the loader resets the stone array directly (63 code sites address GM+0x6D28 ; not all are read). - Whether the region challenge counts an item added again after it was taken away (the objective counts additions). - Which material constants the tower effects' shaders read, and the lights' color curves.

Every region has outposts: warchief strongholds whose missions, map zones and signal fires each follow one saved switch. In Lithlad, five outposts are also seats of an army, with a commander and a reward. The engine's data and scripts mostly call them strongholds. The population inside one is shaped by spawn-scenario tables, and a fortress keeps a table of upgrades that its army's tribe and warchiefs choose. The army, its seats and faction events are covered in The Nemesis system; quests and the campaign store in Quests, story and scenes; spawning in AI; and the menus in User interface.

The game's text says "outpost"; most of the spawn data and the world scripts say "stronghold". Across the shipped database, 2,335 record names in 131 categories contain either word. The spawn tables are named almost entirely for strongholds: Category Records named for strongholds / outposts --- --- AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenario 13, including StrongholdBattle , StrongholdDynamic and StrongholdEventLarge AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenarioCategory 28, including Stronghold , StrongholdDaytime , StrongholdDummyArcher , OutpostCaravan , OutpostRanging and OutpostSentry AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenarioSetup 78, including CapCheckStronghold and CapStaticStronghold AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenarioOverrideList 21 of 142, including Stronghold , StrongholdCenter , StrongholdSlaughter , OutpostCoreStrict , OutpostLargeStrict and PlayerControlledSH DLC4 AI/SpawnAmbient/Predicates 15: StrongholdCaptain and Stronghold 40M to Stronghold 150M , with and without line of sight AI/SpawnAmbient/Removal 7: StrongholdCaptain and Stronghold Removal50M to Stronghold Removal150M AI/SpawnAmbient/NodeTags 13, including Stronghold Core , Stronghold Leader , Outpost Guard and Outpost Captain AI/SpawnAmbient/Locations / AlarmAreas 29 / 23, one or more per outpost (for example IS Outpost Harbor and D Outpost East ) The remaining names belong to the game around them: 1,000 or more audio and dialogue names, 174 inventory items (rewards, intel, the outpost boosts), 120 quest variable predicates, 88 sim events with their participants, 73 quest lists, 31 map canvases, 27 interface game-state predicates and 18 remote scripts (such as EnableAllOutposts and DisableAllOutposts ). In the executable, 103 functions carry an outpost or stronghold name in their own strings or field registrations: 8 schema builders, 33 field registrars, 45 field bindings, 11 string users, 2 field accessors and 4 others. Among the others is the one script binding exposed, Faction::GetOutpostCount PlayerFollowerOrEmpty (implementation 0xF647F0).

Each region's warchiefs live at outposts: Lithlad DE Outpost Central / East / North / NorthWest / West , Núrnen I Outpost Harbor / Lighthouse / RiverRuins , Cirith Ungol MP Outpost Arena / LostHearth / Shelob , Seregost SM Outpost ArmyCamp / FrozenLake / Summit , Gorgoroth V Outpost BlackIron / Camp / Ledge , Minas Ithil MIOutpost 01..05 . Each has one boolean in GameData/Variables , true by default and part of the saved state. - Its only writer is the world script method DeactivateOutpost in the regions' spawn-condition layers. A warchief mission's end paths call it (the warchief killed, one of seven domination events, or branded, but never a death threat), and only when the active quest is on that outpost's own list. Nothing in the shipped scripts sets a switch back to true. A count over the script copies the game loads (a later patch archive's copy replaces an earlier one; 1,403 of the 2,679 distinct script bodies) finds 193 bodies that name a switch, with 748 SetValue(false) calls, every one inside DeactivateOutpost (34 bodies, 22 switches each), and 0 SetValue(true) calls. - Its readers are the region's stronghold controller (below), which subscribes to the variable's change event, and 889 GetValue reads, every one of them in a side-activity layer's CheckMapCanvas (caravans, guarded caragors, camps, feasts, war councils, labor, supplies, drills); those run only while the outpost is active. - The zone on the map is Interface/MapCanvasSettings::<R ZoneMap <X (Núrnen 3, Cirith Ungol 3, Seregost 3, Gorgoroth 3, Minas Ithil 6, Lithlad 5). Its game-state predicate is the outpost's own switch ( IS Outpost Harbor = I Outpost Harbor == true ), so a zone is drawn while the outpost is active and dropped once it is cleared. Minas Ithil adds a story stage (100+ or 200+) or IsVendettaMode , and maps Common , Noble , TradeWest , TradeEast and Wild to MIOutpost 01 to 05 ; MI ZoneMap Keep has only the story stage. Lithlad adds NOT DLC4 OPCaptured <X . The zone's QuestPredicates only hide it while the outpost's own quest list runs. The mc map-canvas objects placed at outposts belong to side-activity layers, not to these zones. - Where an outpost is. An outpost lies at the center of its commander spawn points, the AISpawnerAmbientQuestJob objects such as SC Sp <nn .OutpostCmdr in the region's spawnconditions op<n layer. Of the placed objects, 116 carry "Outpost" in their name, every one a quest-job spawner, and the points of one outpost spread over 22 to 91 m. Seregost's Frozen Lake has no commander spawner: the 88 quest-job spawners within 120 m of its zone all belong to nemesis activities. The region's map information, however, names each outpost zone's canvas with a position ( mcOP ArmyCamp , mcOP Summit , mcOP FrozenLake ); their x and z sit within 16 to 32 m of the spawn centers, while their heights are not the ground's. - Setting a switch back to true through the engine's own variable setter (0x59A1D8 on [GM+0x6C58] ) relights the signal fires at once, through the controller's change handler, and the outpost's missions are offered again from a later world turn. Completion blocks nothing (see below), so the switch is the only lock. - In Desolation of Mordor's mode ( DLC DLC4Active ) the same DeactivateOutpost captures instead of clearing: a win sets DLC4 OPCaptured <X true and the outpost's D OP areas player-owned, and leaves DE Outpost <X true. - OutpostsDisabled is not a feature switch: it is the data of the achievement OutpostDisabled , a count of the outposts the player cleared. Quest/Types::Outpost is unused: no quest has it as its type.

t: The warchief missions, end to end
x: The game's own outpost assault is built from data and the nemesis turn engine: 1. Generation at a world turn. AdvanceTurn 0x1B5EE88 - FactionSimEventGenerate 0x597A9C(army context) - the candidate pass 0x597C7C over the seats - per member 0x5924EC (his row FM+0x268 , flag bit 27) - the row's SimEventGenerationSetup entries in order - a weighted pick 0x5926EC (per-type weights in the pass's own context at +0xA8 / +0xB0 ) - 0x5935DC creates the event. The captain rows' setups (such as Island Captain and SnowMtn Captain ) list the region's outpost types first (3 or 5 entries). 2. The outpost type <R Outpost OP<n (Minas Ithil OutpostGeneric OP<n NoAct1 , Gorgoroth VO , Núrnen IS , Cirith Ungol MP , Seregost SM , Lithlad DE ) has the switch as its GlobalVarPredicate (in Lithlad, the switch AND NOT the capture flag; Minas Ithil's also wants StoryState 200 or more). It lists 7 events ( Kill{Archers, Berserkers, Defenders, Ologs, Spearmen} Outpost 0<n , RapidStealth , SustainedAlarm ), the high-priority ReleasePrisoners UB OP<n (for a captain tagged UnfinishedBusiness OP<n ), and weights [999, 0] : one event per outpost per army. Variant predicates such as DE Outpost 01 Berserkers add a class unlock ( BerserkersUnlocked ). 3. The event <Challenge Outpost 0<n names the participant job SC Subject OutpostCommander , whose holder must be of row rank Captain, an enemy and alive, not on an event, not a bodyguard, spy, prisoner or vow holder, not an Easterling, with no revenge within 3 turns, not tagged OP<n UnfinishedBusiness , and not on a DLC outpost seat. The event also carries AddHenchmen , PreventHenchmenSelection , the builder OutpostCommander at chance 1.0, EventOnAssignSubject Outpost Commander Subject (one level more), the results SubjectFled, SubjectKilledByPlayer, SubjectKilled Fallback, SubjectDominated, Shamed, Shunned, PlayerFledWarchief and SubjectSucceeded, Army-screen presentations, a portrait and AlwaysShowMemberNavMarkers . The commander holds the event at [FM+0x4F0] ( +0x48 the sim event, +0x50 the quest record). 4. The quest <R SC OP<n <Challenge (Seregost names its three SM SC W , P and AC ) has the predicates {the event, the switch, NOT OP<n Retry running} and the type SpawnCondition : ActivationType 3, shown on the zone map, shown as new, kept on the HUD, replayable with XP and items on replay, startable in combat, and disabling travel points. Its objectives are {the challenge, SpawnCon KillChief Obj "Defeat {1!s}"}, with an extra objective picker Optional Kills . It asks for player confirmation with the start screen QS SingleParticipant Base WUIP , gives the rewards Outpost <Region 0<n Complete and Outpost XP , has the outpost's zone as its MapCanvas and LimitGroup LG OutpostMission , and uses the markers OutpostAlarm / CharacterOutpost . Each outpost has one quest list (for example DE Outpost 01..05 , IS Outpost 01..03 , MI Outpost 01..05 and SM Outpost 01..03 ), and there are also Outpost Retry and a progress count per outpost. 5. Placement. The event binds a placed quest whose predicates pass (0x597884 - 0x19EFAB4, the map at QS+0x518 ; 0x19EFAB4 prefers the variant with the fewest completions), so a mission is offered only while its region is loaded. A placed quest is in state 2 (quest object +0x128 ), and a running one is Active, state 17. 6. The commander comes out. While the challenge runs, the commander is not in the world. The layer script's OnObjectiveComplete waits for SC ConditionObjectives , then a spawner set brings him and his gang ( SC Sp <nn .OutpostCmdr , SetOnScenarioSpawningComplete ). He walks to a menace node while Player:QueuePresentation(WarchiefIntro RL, him) plays his walk-out. When it finishes, his senses, traits and pathing come on, his henchmen follow him and SpawnCon KillChief Obj is displayed. A spy among his henchmen gets ActiveRevealSpyGuard , and the commander gets Warchief Betrayed IT (the betrayal branch of the same presentation). WarchiefIntro EVT has five sequences. The default, WC Default , asks of its target only that the attack category PC DisallowShowdown is excluded. IsPlayerFollower is empty on every object predicate of all five branches, so the walk-out plays on any captain (as read from Núrnen's spawnconditionsop1 layer; the outpost missions of every region run the same spawnconditions prefab). 7. The end. The mission's scripts run DeactivateOutpost (setting the switch false) on its win paths, and the outcome's job events apply to the commander. Quest/Types::SpawnCondition is replayable ( CanReplay , with XP and item awards on replay), and no predicate tests a completed quest, so completion blocks nothing. Clearing an outpost turns its alarm off ( <R Outpost <n Comp , "You disabled the alarm in ... Outpost") and gives XP and an item. The XP is Combat/XP/EventQuest::Outpost XP = FloatArray::Outpost XP by player level (2,526 at level 1 to 66,306 at 99), times XP LevelDiff . The item, Outpost <Region 0<n Complete ( Faction/Loot/LootItemLists::OutpostProgress , ContributesToProgress , ShadowWarItem ), is the Shadow War progress trophy and gives no stat bonus. The card's text. Every outpost mission's DescriptionPicker is one of 11 Quest/JobStringPickerGroup::Outpost groups, all holding the same two entries on SC Subject OutpostCommander with PassIfNoMember true: IsNameKnown - SC <Challenge Outpost Desc ("Draw out {1!s} by ...") and IsUnknown - ... Desc Unk ("Draw out the Outpost leader by ..."). Both test MemberHasNameUnlocked = 0x1149E60(fm) = [FM+0x510] & 1 . The quest's Description , ShortDescription and StartPointDescription point at one string, and missions of different outposts share pickers, so the text is per challenge, not per outpost. SpawnCon KillChief Obj is shared by 855 quests (outpost 233, vendetta 294, warchief and fort 100, other 228). A quest's text resolver is 0xCF9D90 (see User interface). Outpost names. Each base outpost's AlarmAreas record names its switch in its HUD predicate, and its DisplayName is the key <tag Outpost <n . The mission's SC <tag Outpost <n Name and the capture line's <tag Outpost <n Comp print the same name for the same n (17 of 17).
