The number n is not the outpost's order in its region: Seregost's Frozen Lake is 2 ("Oroshnalkh"), Summit 3 ("Gordumi Orlû") and Army Camp 1 ("Zunakh'mi Khaargh"); Minas Ithil's MIOutpost 01 is 2 ("Taghumi Ghor"), 02 5 ("Taghumi Omakh"), 03 3, 04 4 and 05 1 ("Shulgumi Shaghkam"). Seregost's quests number them OP1 Frozen Lake ( SM SC W ), OP2 Summit ( SM SC P ) and OP3 Army Camp ( SM SC AC ). As a data quirk, SM SC AC RapidStealth names the sim event SustainedAlarm Outpost 03 as its predicate.

The commander is the captain the generator is working on, or nobody. 0x5935DC puts the generating captain in the cast list with the eligibility check on. The evaluation 0x61EF8C places him first (0x61FC88 - 0x622170 - 0x621834, a one-candidate run of the job matcher 0xF9BB20) and drops the whole event when he fails ("Fill Failed - Participant %s not able to assign to Job %s"). The job's builder is read only by the job filler 0x1BD40C4, and only when its seventh argument allows building. The evaluation calls the filler through 0x1BD2A54 with that argument 0, and lets a required slot stay empty when its job has a builder (0x7D7CB4 at 0x61F41B). No outpost commander is therefore ever built by a generation pass: the builder serves the quest side and the participant re-fill 0x5969A4. The generator's own candidate tests. 0x597A9C returns at once while [ctx+0x1F8] is set. Otherwise it collects the seated members of every row (0x597C7C - 0x597D7C) into two lists by FM+0x51D . It skips a follower with flag bits 27 and 28, a member already on an event ( FM+0x4F0 ), a dead member not coming back (bit 2 without bit 4, 0x597E2C), flag bit 21, and a preset whose Faction/PresetMembers.DisableSimEvents is set. Before generating for a candidate, 0x597F28 skips flag bit 29, bit 43 when 0x1B5CFBC(FS, FM+0x2C8 ) says so, and a member whose body is loaded in the world ( [FM+0x48] set with flag bit 1, unless an entry of the [FM+0x158] list, 0x10 bytes each, has its byte +0xE set). A captain standing near the player therefore gets no mission. SimEventGenerationType.ZoneMustBePlayerOwned is 0 (no requirement) on every outpost type and 1 (must be the player's) on NeverEndingShadowWar and DeathThreats OwnZone ; the value 2 (must not) is tested at 0x59365A. Bodyguards are refused. A job's MustBeBodyguard is 0 (no check), 1 (must be) or 2 (must not), tested as FM+0x2D0 != -1 (0xF9F14B; FM+0x2D0 is the pool index of the member he guards, part of the boss key at FM+0x2C8 ). Late in a campaign most captains are a warchief's bodyguard (in one save, Gorgoroth 16 of 19 captain rows, Minas Ithil 16 of 19, Cirith Ungol 13 of 19). Only free enemy captains who guard nobody can command an outpost, so with 15 of 22 switches on, one outpost had its mission. A refused captain falls through to the Location filler ( EvalChanceIfNoOtherExists ). No event releases a warchief's bodyguard: Faction/Events/Events has only RemoveBodyguardToPlayer , its DLC4 twin and the BecomeBodyguard family. Arriving in a region gives every free captain a SimEvent::Location filler (type 2, lifespan 3 turns, weight 5), so missions appear from the turn those fillers expire. A pass without a turn. The script native System.FactionSimEventGenerate (0x1B82860) runs 0x597A9C on the current region's army; no shipped world script calls it. The engine's own [SIMEVENT] and [QUEST JOB] log lines are compiled in behind byte switches (0x2A34DA0, 0x2A34DAF, in the block 0x2A34D98 to 0x2A34DB7), and the retail logger 0x19C83AC is a three-instruction stub, so the lines are produced and dropped. No base-game event sends the player's captain against an outpost. Of 431 sim events, 163 let a required follower face a required enemy. Six of the generated events are attacks ( Duel , CampRaid2 , Raid Caragors , Raid Checkpoint , Raid Supplies , Chase ; a follower's win kills the enemy), and only the Duel moves a seat. No faction event and no sim event clears an outpost mission; only the quest's own DeactivateOutpost clears the switch. All 15 event results with an AreaOwnershipTransform are Lithlad's. None of the 50 outpost events ( Outpost 0<n , UB OP<n ) carries a slot beyond the commander's (an ambush or reinforcement slot exists on 19 and 24 other events), and none of the 30 outpost layers holds a spawner for a second job.

One world-script class, strongholdcontrol , runs both the fortresses and the warchief outposts of the five base regions; its own comment reads "Set to a default value so that outposts don't do fort stuff!". Lithlad uses strongholdcontroldlc . The copy each region loads is the same 926-line body. - Start. A fortress calls FortStatusInit(<Region Fort) once (4 regions). Each outpost's relay object ( srO<X Control , after a 1 s delay) calls OutpostStatusInit(<switch ) , 17 in the base regions. In Lithlad each outpost runs FortStatusInit(DLC4 OPCaptured <X ) and then OutpostStatusInit(DE Outpost <X ) . - What the switch drives. The switch drives only the outpost's AINodeElevateTransientAlarm nodes (its signal fires). The map canvas calls are commented out ("handled entirely in the DB"): the zone follows its own game-state predicate. An outpost also stays dark while StoryState is below minStoryState (a per-placement property, 100 by default), a condition re-checked on every story-state change. - The alarm. Orcs that reach the signal fire raise the area's alarm. Above Low, the controller adds the HighAlarm spawn override list (training dummies, dummy archers and the arena categories off) and the red alarm canvases. At the second and third high waves it fires a fear burst: every tagged enemy flees, or 40% of them when a captain is present. A warchief mission raises the alarm to High when its commander spawns and resets it to Low when the objective ends. - An owner change in a base region swaps only the map style ( Strongholds versus the Friendly canvases) and the gate logic. No spawner, override list or garrison changes there; garrisons that follow the owner exist only in Lithlad. On a loss the script writes the cave style to the main canvas variable ( localMC ) where the cave canvas variable ( localCaveMC ) is meant, in every loaded copy. - All outposts at once. The remote scripts DisableAllOutposts and EnableAllOutposts are fired 160 times in 101 loaded script bodies: story missions, DLC missions, tribe fights and statues silence every outpost when they start and release them at cleanup. The controller's enable path respects each outpost's switch. - Calls into the engine. The outpost scripts call AISpawnManager:AddScenarioOverrideRecord / RemoveScenarioOverrideRecord ; Faction:GetAreaPlayerOwned , SetAreaPlayerOwned , GetOutpostCount PlayerFollowerOrEmpty , VacateLocationList , CreateFactionMemberBuilder , AddFactionSimEventPicker , AddFactionEventJobSourceAndOther , IsEventOnEventList ; System:ActivateRemoteScript , SetAlarmLevel , ElevateAlarmLevel , GetObjectsWithTag , IsDayTime ; and the game-data variables' GetValue , SetValue and change events. - Class unlocks. The mission-variant predicates <R Outpost 0<n <Unit are the outpost's switch AND <Unit Unlocked AND NOT the capture flag. The same <Unit Unlocked booleans gate the AI templates themselves ( BerserkersUnlocked has 98 users, AI/Templates::Orc Berserker among them): they decide which orc classes any garrison can contain.

t: The alarm, the HUD block and captain spots
x: The alarm level. System.SetAlarmLevel (script stub 0x1BA7EA4) is 0x1AA0A80(alarm area, level, flag); its only other caller is a quest's own AlarmLevel (0x4F86E8). It takes an AI/SpawnAmbient/AlarmAreas record and accepts only two levels of the area's TransientAlarmSettings : RequiredDefaultAlarmLevel (meter 0) and ElevatedAlarmLevel (meter = ElevatedAlarmLevelMeterMin , the elevated flag on). Any other level returns without a change. It writes the transient-alarm manager's entry for the area ( [base+0x26FFBF0] : +0x40 level, +0x48 meter) and notifies the alarm system; 0x11FBC8(area) reads it back (the entry's level, else the area's default). All 22 outposts' areas use TransientAlarmSettings::Default : Low and High, meter minimum 300, falling 5 a second, so an elevated alarm falls back by itself in about a minute. The block over the minimap. minimap.gfx 's MM-Combat ( Interface/HUD/Widget::Combat ; the C++ widget vt 0x1F7CF88 at [[UIManager]+0x30]+0x48 ) has two parts: PlayerLevel (the player's own level, [[player+0x26A8]+0x568] + 1 ) and Alarm , the area's name, icon and cooldown. The area is the highest-priority alarm area brush around the player (0x60763C - player+0x26E8 - UIManager+0x1A8 ). The redraw 0x18D1974 runs when the area, the alarm level or its trend changes. With no trend, it asks the record's HUDPredicates (instance +0x10 , through 0x1DDBE0), of which it is the only reader, and hides the alarm part when the predicate is false. The 17 base outposts' predicate is Interface/Predicates/GameState::<switch , true while the enemy holds the outpost (Minas Ithil's also want StoryState 100 or 200); Lithlad's five, the fortresses and the Lumbermill have none. That is why Desolation of Mordor shows the name and alarm of an outpost the player holds, while the base game shows them only for an enemy's outpost. Captain spots. Every base outpost has captain spots ( AI/SpawnAmbient/Locations ), listed by each region's captain rows: <R Outpost<X Tribal in Faction/Rows.Locations and <R Outpost <X in LocationsLowPriority (28 spots for the 17 base outposts; Black Iron and Minas Ithil's have no Tribal one). The location picker 0x78ADB8 is called from the location writer 0xFE3790 (the one writer of FM+0x330 and FM+0x338 ), from the fortress defense 0x1C1F244 and from the army's passes. It filters each spot through 0x592F9C - 0x591D98(spot, the candidate's follower bit, ...): when a spot's MustBePlayerFollower link is set, its Combat/Predicates/Bool.Value must equal the candidate's follower bit, and then PlayerFollowerMustMatchOverlord applies (0 on every outpost spot). All 28 outpost spots name Bool::False , so they take enemy captains only, whoever holds the outpost. The game's own follower spots (the Overlord's and the follower war camps: 28 locations) name Bool::True .

What stands in a stronghold is ambient spawning: spawn scenarios ( AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenario ) grouped into categories ( SpawnScenarioCategory ) and filled through setups ( SpawnScenarioSetup ). An override list ( AI/SpawnAmbient/SpawnScenarioOverrideList : Priority , Overrides , CategoryOverrides ) changes them inside a ScenarioOverrideVolume or for as long as a script holds it ( AISpawnManager:AddScenarioOverrideRecord ). It names no unit types: it switches and caps scenarios and categories through two kinds of entry: Entry ( Structures... ) Fields --- --- SpawnScenarioCategoryOverride CategoryType (a category), ForceEnabledStatus (a Combat/Predicates/Bool : True , False , or none to leave it), MaxConcurrentAI , MaxConcurrentSetup , Priority , MinDistance , AutoCooldownChance (-1 = leave as is) SpawnScenarioOverride ScenarioType (one scenario), disable , MaxConcurrent , MaxConcurrentAI , FrequencyDecay , Priority Three lists, as read from a running game and the shipped data: List Priority Effect --- --- --- Stronghold 4 categories Wilderness and AmbStartGraug off, AmbSentries capped at 3 bodies, AmbColumn at 4, SHOnlyEvent and FortPlayerWelcomeBlocker on; the scenario AIBlockout disabled ( MaxConcurrent 0) HighAlarm 8 StrongholdDummy , StrongholdDummyArcher and Arena off; StrongholdDynamic and StrongholdDynamicArcher listed with every field left as is PlayerControlledSH DLC4 1 Orcs off, StrongholdEasterling on: who guards a held Lithlad outpost The tables never name a unit. A setup ( SpawnScenarioSetup : ScenarioType , ScenarioCategories , RequiredAITypes , Priority , global and instance cooldowns, MaxConcurrent , MaxConcurrentAI , MinDistance , StartDisabled , ForceAISpots , ForceNextScenario , IgnoreMaxConcurrent , AllowFailedSpawn ) belongs to a scenario ( SpawnScenario : ScenarioCategories , Priority , FrequencyDecay , MaxConcurrent , MaxConcurrentAI , StartDisabled ), and a category carries only MaxConcurrentAI . The shipped data has 151 categories, 53 scenarios and 282 setups, 87 of them stronghold or outpost setups. RequiredAITypes points at {AITemplate, NumRequired} entries: all 114 of them in the shipped data have no template and require 0 (a running game agrees). What spawns is decided by the spawners placed in each outpost's layers and the AI types they hold. Categories and override lists only decide which placed scenarios run and how many bodies they may field. The code that applies them is one module of about 200 functions that reads every field of the override lists, both entry kinds and the setups. It is called from the ScenarioOverrideVolume class (vtable 0x1FB4BA0), a placed volume whose +0x120 holds its override list, and from the setup code. How lists compete. 0x5ED360 resolves the overrides per running scenario: the spawn manager keeps its running scenarios in a table ( [mgr] , count [mgr+8] , 0x60-byte entries with the scenario record at +8 ) and the active override lists in a vector at [mgr+0x10130] to [mgr+0x10138] . For each scenario it walks the lists and considers a list only when its Priority is strictly above the best one applied so far, so the highest priority wins and a tie goes to the earlier list. Inside the winning list, the direct Overrides entry for that scenario applies first, then the first CategoryOverrides entry whose category contains the scenario. A scenario no list mentions gets its own values back. The list priority is read in three places (0x5ED1B8, 0x5ED360, 0x5ED50C). The stronghold vocabulary around them includes the distance predicates Stronghold 40M to Stronghold 150M (with and without line of sight), the despawn rules Stronghold Removal50M to Stronghold Removal150M and StrongholdCaptain , and the node tags Stronghold Core , Stronghold Leader , Stronghold Gather , Outpost Guard , Outpost Captain and Outpost Defense .

t: Lithlad's outposts: seats of an army
x: Desolation of Mordor's five Lithlad outposts are records of Faction/Outposts (6 records with DE Fort ; fields Row , Column , UIName , GlobalVarToSet , CreateSimEventOnDie , CreateSimEventOnVacate , PlayerOwnedItemGiverPicker ). They are seats in an army's row table that a captain holds as the outpost's commander. The campaign's Lithlad is the same world ( WorldInfo::desert ), with these systems placed and switched off. - The capture flag. GlobalVarToSet ( DLC4 OPCaptured <X ) is written through the boolean setter 0x59A1D8, which fires the variable's change event. Its faction-side binding 0x100F4C0 has 5 callers: 0xFE2E90 (a seat change: true when the new holder is a player follower, false otherwise; true on vacate, then CreateSimEventOnVacate ), 0xFD4DE0 and 0xFDCAB0 (bulk false), 0xFE0A60 (recompute) and 0x1010750 (a setter wrapper). Scripts write it too: DeactivateOutpost in Desolation's mode and a debug script. - The garrison follows the owner. Each outpost's gameplay layer has a controller (script object outpostcontroldlc ) that runs OutpostStatusInit on the capture flag: with the player as owner it switches on a ScenarioOverrideVolume (vtable 0x1FB4BA0, +0x120 - the override list PlayerControlledSH DLC4 ) and shows the outpost's faction-member props. With Sauron as owner, the volume is off and the props are hidden. Desolation applies the Easterling garrison inside each held outpost only. - Who has outposts. Faction/Definition.Outposts lists the five on 2 of the 38 armies, Faction desert DLC4 and Faction desert mercs DLC4 . Quest/FactionOutpostPredicate::DLC4 AllOutpostsOwned asks for 5 seats held by a player follower, dead or empty (the count Faction::GetOutpostCount PlayerFollowerOrEmpty returns), and DLC4 NotAllOutpostsOwned for 0 to 4. Inventory/FactionIntelGiver::GiveIntel OutpostCommanders unlocks outpost data, and Desolation's game-mode record sets an OutpostValue of 1000. - The spawn areas change hands too. Faction/AreaOwnershipTransform::DLC4 Outpost <X To Player sets the outpost's AI/SpawnAmbient/Areas player-owned (1) and To Sauron sets them back (2): D OP Umbral (West), D OP SorrowSea (North), D OP SouthWatch (North-West), D OP SootGulch (East), D OP Stillwind and D OP Stillwind A (Central). The fortresses use the same mechanism ( <Region FortAreas to Player / to Sauron , 10 records). DLC4 Outpost N To Sauron holds no area entry, so the North outpost's area is never returned through its transform. - Two systems on one spot. The warchief outpost's gate in Lithlad is DE Outpost <X == true AND DLC4 OPCaptured <X == false (OP1 North, OP2 East, OP3 West, OP4 Central, OP5 North-West), and its mission generation uses the same gate: while the player holds the spot, it runs the seat system, and once lost, it runs the warchief system. Desolation's captain generation ( DLC4 Desert Captain ) differs from the campaign's Desert Captain only by the five DLC4 EnemyOutpostCommander <X types and two DLC3 hunting and power-struggle types. - The map. No outpost controller of Lithlad holds a map canvas (of 207 MapCanvas objects in 416 desert layers, none is in the main layer or an outpost gameplay layer). Desolation marks an outpost on the map only through its assault quest ( NavMarkerTypeQuest Quest OutpostAssault , map target OutpostAssault ), and the marker type Quest OutpostAssault Empty is referenced by no record or script. The DE ZoneMap <X zones draw whenever their game-state predicates pass, with or without a mission, in the record's own colors (the enemy red, the values of Stronghold ZoneMap ). - No enemy attacks a held seat. No shipped record has an enemy captain attack a player-held outpost commander: a job's MustBeAssignedToOutpostPosition (0 ignore, 1 must hold a DLC outpost seat, 2 must not) is 2 on 245 of 849 jobs (12 are 1), including every duel, power-struggle, hunting and location job; the job matcher rejects at 0xF9F5BF. Only the 6 Faction/Outposts records exist, all in Lithlad.

Each Lithlad outpost has an assault mission ( D4OA C , E , N , NW , W ; quest type DLC4 OutpostAssault , listed only by GameModes::DLC4 , whose type table 0x598804 rebuilds; predicate DLC4Active ), generated at a world turn while an enemy captain commands the outpost ( DLC4 EnemyOutpostCommander <X ). Starting one runs as follows: 1. The start plays Presentation/Events::QuestScreen Confirm EVT , whose one element Quest Confirm FadeToBlack ELM (camera hold, combat paused, slow motion, HUD cinematic, a fade action) takes the screen fader's lock 3: the screen goes black. 2. The quest goes fade-out (4), loading (11 / 13), Active (17). The mission layer pD4OA <X runs QuestStart : the player is teleported to tpPlayerStart , then SpawnerSetup . 3. SpawnerSetup asks the set pD4OA <X .setOwnCap (scenario setup 0 Missions ) for 1 + N owner captains, N = Faction:GetOutpostCount PlayerFollowerOrEmpty(Faction desert DLC4) (0xF647F0 - 0xFD92F0), at most 4. 4. Only the set's OnScenarioSpawningComplete queues the intro D4OA Intro on the leader; the intro's fade-up releases lock 3, and its end runs StartAssault . The set spawns as one batch (5 bodies within 0.05 s). The owner-captain slots are AISpawnerAmbientQuestJob objects (vt 0x1DC5360, 0x1E0 bytes, the job record at +0x1C0 ): slot 1 is PS Subject (the sim event's subject, the outpost commander), slots 2 to 5 D4OA Own 02 to 05 . Slot 38 of the spawner (0x1AC21B8) takes its member from 0x1AC2288: the active quest (0x43D984; the container at QS+0x3D8 ) +0x1C8 - {begin, end} of 0x38-byte job entries ( +0x08 the job, +0x10 its alias, +0x20 / +0x28 the member key {FM+0x178, FM+0x174} ). 0x1BD5544 matches the job (0x4FBE3C) and skips a member with flag bit 1, or with bit 2 unless the spawner's +0x1D1 allows it. Without a member the spawner does not spawn ("%s unable to spawn - FactionMember not found", compiled out). The setup's JobsToFill are D4OA Own 02 to 05 (the subject comes from the event). The job filler 0x1BD40C4 skips the pool search when AlwaysUseBuilderRecord is 1 (0xF9A320), then rolls FactionMemberBuilderChance (0x1B3C6C; "%s Failed random roll"): a failure leaves the job empty, with no retry. With no member in a slot, the set never completes, no intro plays, and lock 3 stays held over an Active mission (a region change clears it). In the campaign the count reads Faction desert DLC4 , which has no members there, and an empty seat counts as the player's, so every campaign assault asks for 1 + 4 owner captains, whatever the player holds. The outposts' life is in the mission script ( dlc4 outpostassault ). FinalizeResults picks the sim event's result: SubjectDied when the mission is won with the commander dead; SubjectSuccess (his DLC4 Defended Outpost event) when it is lost with him alive; and SubjectKilledButPlayerLost , with a new commander through CreateFactionMemberBuilder(DLC4 OutpostCommander Understudy <X ) , when it is lost with him dead. The script binding Faction:CreateFactionMemberBuilder (0x1B7F544, 31 instructions) calls 0x1B5B824(FS, builder, faction 0, jobs 0): a null faction means the current region's army. IfVictory on a first capture sets DLC4 OPCapturedFirstTime <X and raises DLC4 NumberOfOutpostsLeveledUp , whose change adds all five DLC4 OutpostLeaderLevelUp <X pickers (three levels) to the faction. Their participant needs an empty seat, while their result targets the commander. Understudies are enemies of level 30 or more, seated by DLC4 PromoteUnderstudy <X - DLC4 TakeOutpost . Every dispatched defender gets DLC4 Died DefendingOutpost from the script's OwnerCaptainFactionEvent . The generation types DLC4 FakeOutpostDefense <X and OutpostCommanders are unused even in Desolation: no record links them.

- Retake timing. An empty seat falls 3 turns after it empties, through DLC4 FakeOutpostDefense Empty <X (type 1, lifespan 3 turns, SubjectAlwaysWins ). That event is bound to the cut defend quest D4FD <X , which has no placed object, so nothing shows. The cut defend missions D4FD C/E/N/NW/W and D4FD REF are power-struggle stubs with no job setup, no outpost link, no marker and no placed object. - Retake commanders. Faction/FactionMemberBuilder::DLC4 OutpostTakers has one level field, MinLevel 20: every retaken outpost gets a level-20 commander. - Duels move outposts. A Duel ( DE Duel 00 to 02 , generation PowerStruggle Act2 ) pits PS Subject Cap Duel against PS Other Cap Duel ; its action code 7 kills the loser and 10 swaps their seats. With the two jobs' MustBeAssignedToOutpostPosition opened, a retaken outpost's new enemy commander generated a duel against a follower captain. The follower won and took the outpost seat, DLC4 OPCaptured <X turned true, and enemy captains refilled the row he had left. Desolation's own "Assign Outpost Leader" ( SlotMemberMove DLC4Outpost , success text DLC4 Orders Success DefendOutpost ) takes only an empty, dead or follower-held outpost seat. DLC4 Debug MercDuelIntoOutpost (a merc killing an enemy outpost commander) has one referrer, a sim-event picker of the same name, which nothing references or scripts fire.

PlayerOwnedItemGiverPicker names DLC4 OutpostItems : 16 givers ( Faction/Outposts/ItemGiver::OutpostBoost <X ), each with 3 entries ( StructuresFactionOutpostItem ) selected by the commander's rarity ( RequiredRarity ). An entry has the UIName "<Rarity Mercenary Leader", a description and effects, and Items ( StructuresFactionOutpostItemData : a CombatType filter, the player and / or an Easterling class, and one of 33 OutpostReward items to give). A reward item's PassiveVariableMod ( Combat/Stat/Variable/Modifications ) adds to float variables or sets bools whose numbers live in the formulas that test them. Archetype items gate the Combat Master, Guardian and Quartermaster rewards. Only Lithlad's outposts give boosts: Giver Common Epic Legendary --- --- --- --- CaptureBoost capture rate x1.3 the player and allies take x0.65 damage while capturing +0.035 health regeneration while capturing SummonCooldown the player's FollowerCoolDown x0.65 x0.5 x0.25 MoneyDrop the mercenaries' kills drop coin the player's kills drop coin both Damage mercenaries +0.25 damage the player +0.25 both Defense mercenaries +0.25 defense (clamped 0 to 0.9) the player +0.25 both CommandMight mercenaries' charge meter x1.4 the player's Might x1.3 both CurseDef / FireDef / PoisonDef (mercenaries) resistance immunity healed by it (curse: also no fleeing) BoostArcher / Defender / Infantry that class +0.35 defense +0.5 damage a fire weapon, unless an elemental weapon comes from a trait BoostGrunts all three classes +0.5 defense +1.0 damage both BoostGuardian / Quartermaster / CombatMaster that archetype +0.35 defense +0.5 damage both Coin drops ( DLC4 PLBar Coin Comb Bonus , 12 items gated on the two coin rewards) are worth 10 for an orc, 25 for a stealth kill, 100 for an Olog, 100 for a looted body, 250 for a common captain and 750 for a rare beast; an outpost mission itself gives 1,500 ( DLC4 Coin OutpostMission ).

Presentation/Events::DLC4 Outpost Intro EVT (priority Quest Urgent , blocks fast travel) has one sequence of nine elements: a camera cut that disables the player ( DLC4 Outpost Teleport Hold ELM , which teleports nothing), the outpost's fixed frames, a start camera and its voice, an identify hold, then the enter-zone camera and the return transition DLC4 Outpost Return TR . Its predicate assumes no target ( Target Empty OPR ). The frames are per outpost ( DLC4 Outpost <X WF1 Begin / End / RTP ) and are chosen through the camera pools DLC4 Outpost Begin CP , End CP and RTP CP . The pools' predicates Outpost <X CPR require the assault mission's camera type D4OA <X CT , so the intro frames the right outpost only when it is queued with that camera type. The one relay named for outposts, Presentation/Relays::PS Outpost Intro 00 , has no event and no camera type.

t: Fortress upgrades: one table per army
x: Every army keeps one fort-upgrade set at [armyCtx+0x40] , where armyCtx is an army context (an entry of the faction system's context map at FS+0x98 , plus 8): Offset Type Meaning --- --- --- +0x00 pointer a table of 16-byte rows {UpgradeType record, Definition record} indexed by the UpgradeType's record index (28 rows) +0x08 u32 the row count +0x10 pointer the category of the upgrade-type records (0x107A74 asserts "Bad record index" for a type from another category) +0x18 / +0x20 pointers a vector of the Faction/FortUpgrade/Definitions the army has unlocked The read path is 0x4F6644 (whether an army holds every upgrade of a Faction/FortUpgrade/Group ; the fortress's defense rating adds a warchief's group contribution only when it does) - 0x4F66D8 (the army context for a faction) - 0x10681C - 0x107A74. In a loaded late campaign, 31 of 38 contexts held this table. An enemy fortress fills one Defense row per family: 6 of 6 rows on each of the two enemy-held fortresses, 0 on each of the four whose Overlord served the player, and 2 on Lithlad's invasion army, whose Overlord also served the player. Who chooses. Faction/FortUpgrade/PickerEntry records select a definition by the fort's tribe list ( IncludedTribe - Faction/Tribes/Lists ) or by a warchief's trait marker list. The tribe lists group the tribes: List Tribes Army Beasts Siege beasts Archers Battlefield Structures First assault wave --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- Beast Feral Berserker Caragors Fire Farsight Poison mines Fire spouts Cavalry Black Dark, Nazgul Twins Spearman Graugs Curse Spikes Poison mines Poison spouts Sappers Industrial Machine Defender Gronds Poison Fire Fire mines Iron gates Sappers Mystic Fort Sorcerous, Undead Berserker Graugs Curse Fire Poison mines Fire spouts Ologs Outlaw Outlaw Berserker Graugs Poison Farsight Poison mines Poison spouts Sappers Regal Marauder Spearman Gronds Poison Farsight Fire mines Poison spouts Cavalry Slaughterhouse Slaughter Spearman Gronds Curse Spikes Fire mines Iron gates Sappers Torturer Terror Berserker Caragors Fire Spikes Fire mines Fire spouts Ologs Warmonger Warmonger, Bruz, Nazgul Twins Defender Caragors Fire Spikes Poison mines Iron gates Cavalry The trait markers add their own picks: MarkerList IsBerserker adds the berserker host, IsBeastMaster caragors, IsDestroyer graugs, IsMarksman farsight archers, IsTank the defender host or iron gates, IsTracker the spearman host, StatusEffect Fire / Poison / Curse that element's picks, IsAssassin poison mines or spouts, and IsCommander fire mines. What a pick does. FortAssault/Modifiers keyed on the definition hold a Makeup ( AISetup , Count , Weight , Priority , SpawnOnlyOnce , NeverRemove ), and the FortAssault/AISetup names an AI type: Family Effect during a siege --- --- Army the garrison weighted to that class ( FU Berserker , FU Defender , FU Spearman : count 0, a weight; 9 modifiers each) Siege beasts FU SiegeBeast , 4, spawned once: a graugapult with the element's item Beasts caragors FU Caragor 6 (wargs), gronds FU Drake 2 (the drake), graugs FU Graug 1 Archers, structures, battlefield no modifier: battlement items ( FM Archers Battlements ) and the fortress's own gates, spouts, mines and drums Prices are Faction/FortUpgrade/Group.CurrencyAmount , paid in the player's currency item: Group Price --- --- walls 1,000 / 3,000 / 7,500 structures 750 / 750 / 1,100 army 800 siege beasts 875 beasts 950 archers 1,025 battlefield 1,100 the defense levels Defense Lvl 01 to 06 700 to 1,050 offense 700 to 1,100 A graugapult is a tamed graug and an item list. The AI types Troll Graugapult , Poison and Curse all build the template Troll Tame . What makes the siege beast is GruntPlayerAllyItems / GruntPlayerEnemyItems (the list used depends on the side): Graug A Pult , Wep Graug A Pult , Troll Graugapult Marker , Troll Graugapult Disabled SetRenderID , the four box items and the element ( FM Siege FireBeast on Troll Graugapult , which also carries Attack Structures ; FM Siege CurseBeast on Curse ). The one allied graugapult type is DLC3 GP Troll Ice Graugapult . An AI type's side. Orc types carry it in GruntPlayerFollowerStatus : 0 enemy or wild, 1 a player follower, 2 the area's owner, 3 an invader, 4 and 5 the two sides of a fortress assault. Beasts carry it in GruntBrandStatus instead: the Branded types (such as Warg Brown Branded , Troll Branded and FellBeast Branded ) read follower status 0 and brand status 1. No archer-named orc type is a player follower (enemy 0, owner 2, invader 3, assault 4 / 5), and Summon OrcSapper Poison reads 0.

t: The endless Shadow War: sieges after the ending
x: Faction/Events/SimEventGenerationType::NeverEndingShadowWar (global-variable predicate PostShadowWar , ZoneMustBePlayerOwned 1, high-priority event FortDefense , weight 1) attacks a fortress the player holds. SimEvent::FortDefense sets an enemy Overlord, 5 warchiefs and 6 reinforcement captains against FortDefense PlayerOverlord . It has the quest FD <Region , the scenes FortDefense Intro EVT and FortDefense OverlordArrival EVT , lifespan 0 and SimulateOnQuestTimeout false, so it waits until it is played. In one late campaign, 3 of 38 armies held one: Lithlad's, with FD Desert placed on the map; Seregost's, not placed (another region); and Núrnen's, with no quest bound yet. The siege's own settlement results are SubjectWinsSimulate - OtherKilledBySubject (the other side is FD Overlord : the player's Overlord dies) and OtherWinsSimulate - SubjectKilledByOther . None of the three results carries an AreaOwnershipTransform , and the odds are SimEventChance::FortDefense . An event settles at its expiry turn (a duel with lifespan 3 and SimulateOnQuestTimeout false was seen settling at its expiry), so a siege's deadline is its LifeSpanGenerated alone. Enemy-held fortresses carry FortAssault ( SC FA <R ).

The world map is a model of the region drawn far below the world. Its object is [base+0x26FFAC8] (vtable 0x1F715F8; null while the map is closed): Offset Meaning --- --- +0xAC position (about (0, -24200, 0)) +0xB8 rotation (quaternion) +0x2AC / +0x2B0 the model's size in x and z (512 in every region read) +0x2B4 / +0x2B8 the height range +0x2C0 the region record 0xD11D10 converts a point on the model to the world: the point is taken into the model's local space, u = local.x / sizeX + 0.5 (and the same for z), and world = rect.min + (rect.max - rect.min) u . The rectangles come from a table at [[CGameClientShell+0x8C8]+0x10] (to +0x18 ): 0x110-byte entries {hash, path at +4, info at +0x108} , with the rectangle at info+0x18 : Region Rectangle (min x, min z, max x, max z) --- --- desert -73950.6, -83550.3, 56049.4, 46449.7 island -88000.7, -50000.0, 55000.0, 93000.9 minasithil -55450.1, -53099.7, 43549.9, 45900.3 mtnpass -66001.9, -74401.9, 63200.0, 54800.0 snowmtn -47999.9, -62999.9, 48000.1, 33000.1 volcano -60000.5, -10000.8, 60000.3, 110000.0 The map camera is [[base+0x26FFB08]+0xA8] (vtable 0x1DB1F48), with the position at +0x158 , the rotation at +0x164 , the horizontal and vertical fields of view in radians at +0x174 and +0x178 , and the gameplay camera at +0xD0 . The renderer's per-draw projection agrees with it (P00 1.1309, P11 2.1445 at 3840 x 2025). The cursor is in pixels at [[CGameClientShell+0xE38]+0xEC] / +0xF0 , the viewport at [CGameClientShell+0xC00] . The camera list at [[CGameClientShell+0xE38]+0x220] holds a free camera (vtable 0x22F4E18, unused by default) and the HUD minimap's camera (vtable 0x22F4F20). Each region's 3D map is the section Regions/Region.ZoneMapWorldSection textured with ZoneMapTexture (Lithlad: prefabs\ui\zonemaps\desert\desertzonemap d.tex , BC3 2048 x 2048), captured at MapCaptureHeight (95,000; Lithlad 30,000). The zones are built when the map shows a region. 0x1800EA0(zone map, mode) ("Too many dynamic zone shapes") has two callers, MapMenuActivate 0xEED810 and 0x17E6724 (reached from the map's region switch, 0x18DC74C). It returns at once when the zone map is already the current one ( [base+0x26FFAC8] ) and [zm+0x164] is the mode asked. Otherwise it closes the zone map built before (0x1802900) or tears down its own shapes (0x18028CC: the mesh [zm+0x2F0] destroyed by 0x17FF1D0 and freed, 0x3D0 bytes; the shape list [zm+0x2E0] cleared by 0x17FF510). It then stores itself and the mode (0x1800F30) and builds the shapes from the region's Interface/MapCanvasSettings zones (their gates and colors, 0x4DF148 / 0x4DF294). Each region has its own zone map object (0x18003A0 finds it by +0x2C0 ). A zone's gate that changes while the map is open therefore shows only at the next open or region switch. The icons come from a baked list. 0x18E81A0 builds the map's icons each time it shows a region, from that region's baked map information: 0x188E208(region) - 0x17DDE1C - 0x1794FC0( [CGameClientShell+0x8C8] , region) returns the region's UIWD blob (magic "UIWD", version 4, the rectangle at +0x18 ). The blob holds the icon list at +0x40 , its count at +0x48 (Núrnen 345, repeated at header +0x14 ) and the map-canvas list at +0x30 / +0x38 (117). An entry is 0x40 bytes: +0x00 u8 type, +0x08 name ( char ), +0x10 game-mode name, +0x18 canvas name (ties the icon's height to a zone), +0x20 position (x, y, z in cm), and +0x30 three u32 slot ids and a hash that the builder does not read. Entry type What it names Icon kind Núrnen --- --- --- --- 0 a Quest/Quests record 0, or 2 (the quest's captain, 0x61D0F8) when the quest type's UIDisplayAsQuest is false 186 1 a Regions/TravelPoint 3 7 2 an Inventory/Items record, drawn only while the player holds the item (the Haedir towers, collectibles) 1 133 3 a map canvas positions only 14 4 an Interface/MapMarker 6 5 (the monuments) 5 a Regions/ZoneInfoNode and a game mode 7 A first pass counts what will draw and a second builds it (0x18E6A40(layer, kind, record, &position, target, ...)). Hunting captains come from a separate pass over the region's own army (0x77AB2C). This is how the map shows the icons of regions the player is not in: it never needs their worlds. Every reader of the list tests an entry's type first and copies what it needs. The builder reads every type; the zone build 0x1800EA0 and the Army screen's hierarchy map 0x334E90 read canvases only; and the position lookups 0x17DDE30, 0x17DB9A4 and 0x17DF220 read types 3, 2 and 0. Nothing keeps a pointer into the array, and a name the GameDB lacks draws nothing (0x59A728 returns no rules for a null record). The map finds a MapMarker record by name (0x1B08870, the category's index). MapMarker records ( Interface/MapMarker , 28 shipped, among them 25 <Region 0N Monument , Desert 06 Monument and Test ForgeTower ) have one field, NavMarkerPredicateList - StructuresMapMarkerPredicate entries { AllowedGameModes (0xD03B90 against [UIManager+0x430] ), Predicates [{ Variable , value}] tested against the GameData store [GM+0x6C58] (0x1DFC4C), a NavMarker type}. 0x59A404 returns the type of the first entry whose game mode and every predicate pass (an empty list passes); the monuments read <Region 0N Status . No MapMarker record exists for an outpost. The placed MapMarker objects are the HUD's. The world class "MapMarker" (vt 0x1F74D58, 0x158 bytes) is placed with a property naming its record (read by slot 12, 0x1835E68) and registered in [0x2A25F38 .. 0x2A25F40) (slot 21, 0x1835D9C; rebuilt at new addresses by every world load). It holds its position at +0xAC , the bound world nav marker at +0x128 / +0x148 , its own nav-marker component at +0x120 when none is bound, and the record at +0x150 . Its refresh 0x59A280 takes the type from 0x59A404, then enables and types the marker. The engine re-runs the refresh for each MapMarker whose rules name a variable whenever that variable is set through the GameData setters (0x59A1D8, 0x59B024, 0x1B4747C - 0x59A53C - 0x59A584). A MapMarker can be the current target (type 6, 0x1835F24). A nav marker's map flags are the minimap's. The component vt 0x1DC0708 sits at NavMarker+0x120 . NavMarker::SetType (0x1162DE4) skips an unchanged type (0x3576A4). Its body 0x3576B8 writes the type to +0x38 and its DefaultMapTarget to +0xE0 , re-reads the HUD configuration, sets up the marker's effect (0x357CD4), writes the type into its widget ( [marker+0x60]+0x2C0 ) and sets the rebuild flag ( +0x48 = 1 ). Three condition sets of three u64 masks each (forbidden, need-one, need-one), tested by 0x1CD170 against the HUD state word [0x2725120] , come from the type's HUDStateConfig ( +0x3C8 , giving +0x30 ), from the map target's ( +0x3E0 , giving +0x417 ) and from AltDisplayRangeHUDStateConfig ( +0x3F8 ). 0x1CD0C8 evaluates them and fills the widget: +0x32D = (enabled +0x28 or forced +0x418 ) and +0x30 , and +0x32E = 0x109ECC. The only reader of +0x32E is 0x1C5E08, the placement of the minimap and compass. The HUD state word reads 0x00080000 in play and 0x01080800 with the map open. The 3D map never draws placed nav markers, only its baked list: renaming one list entry to another MapMarker record drew that record's icon, card and prompt at the entry's position, while enabling a monument's world nav marker drew nothing on the map. A held Lithlad outpost has no marker of its own. The orange mark shown there is the commander's CharacterOutpost marker (attached to his torso, icon Outpost NamedIcon = hud\questicons\new\kraken\chief.tex , map target OutpostAlarm ). Both outpost map targets ( OutpostAssault , OutpostAlarm ) are quest markers (bucket GoldenPathQuest , MapTargetType 4), whereas forts have an owner pair of types, Fort / Fort Owned . The open map's layer. While the map is open, its layer ( CUI3DZoneMapLayer , vt 0x1F7E570) is the top of the menu system's layer stack (menu [UIManager+0x50] , layers at +0x520 , up to 8, count u32 at +0x560 ). A layer's +0x6B8 is its menu system and +0x6C0 its MenuLayer record; [UIManager+0xF0] holds the top layer's record, not the layer. 0xDAC2B0(layer) gives the icon under the cursor ( [+0xA78] , else [+0xA70] , else [+0xA80] ), and the card dispatcher 0x18E6358 builds its card by kind (2: the captain card 0x18EACD0). The icon pool is [layer+0xA38 .. +0xA40) , 0x3A80 bytes an icon, refilled at every region shown: +0x00 the kind (u32), +0x08 the list entry's record, +0x3A20 a captain key (army record, pool index at +0x3A28 ; {0, -1} for none), read only through 0x170794, and +0x3A68 the shown region ( [layer+0xA10] ). The hover setter 0x7C1274 reads [FM+0x330] of a set key's member with no null check (0x7C12F3). - A captain icon (0x18E68B4) takes kind 2 and his key, the widget from his marker type's target, and then LoadTarget 0x18EA410, which passes his states (0x18EA334 - 0x10BD90) to the NamedOrc character data. A player follower is drawn blue 0xFF09D5ED, a default member in the enemy orange 0xFFED5F09, and an unknown one gray with no level. - Keys come from Profile/Commands and are dispatched by the layer's slot 12. MenuEnter (Space or Enter, the pad's A) runs 0x18E9AD4, behind the map's quest lock [layer+0xA30] . On an icon whose map target has AllowAsWaypoint off, it returns at once (0x18E9C88 - 0x18EA300); on a captain icon it marks him as the target (0x18928A8; his HierarchyOrc type allows it); on free ground it sets a point waypoint (0x189286C - 0x17A98AC( [GM+0x6C80] , &position, [layer+0xA10] )). MenuAux06 (key 2) runs 0x18E97FC: on any hovered icon that is not a region, it tests only the key at +0x3A20 , and when the key resolves and 0x1149E60 passes, it opens MenuManager.FactionMemberLayer , his captain screen with his 3D model. MenuAux08 (Home) cycles the icons, and Map (M) closes the map. - The clip and the states. The builder 0x18E6A40 and LoadTarget 0x18EA410 both ask whether the icon's marker type (0x18E73B4: for kind 6 the type its MapMarker rule picks; for kind 2 the member's own type, 0x4AA220) has CharacterData , and whether its target (the type's DefaultMapTarget , 0x18E7394) has InheritParentCharacterStates on. If both hold, the clip is the type's IconMovieClip , and LoadTarget runs the states (0xD88020) and puts the picture in the clip's child LoadTarget , or else in Content LoadTarget . Otherwise the clip is the target's Symbol , sent to its normal label (clip slot 112), with the picture only at Content LoadTarget . With no holder, nothing is loaded and the clip's own placeholder shows. The picture is a state's texture override, else the target's ZoneMapTexture , then its IconTexture , then the type's IconTexture . A map icon draws only a resident texture: IconTexture is a bare path that nothing loads, and only a card picture's DescriptionImgBundle loads a bundle. In sphud.gfx , SPH-UserWaypoint , SPH-SimpleMarker and SPH-CharacterMarkerCommon keep LoadTarget at the top with no Content ; minimap.gfx 's MM-LoadTarget (labels normal, new, blink) has Content LoadTarget . Of 30 Interface/NavMarkerCharacterData records, ForgeTower tints its default state 0xFFED5F09 (state 6 SoP Targeted 0xFFFFC640, 15 PlayerFollower 0xFF09D5ED), Collectible 's default does not tint, and NamedOrc (42 types) runs a captain icon's 20 states. Of the 525 shipped Interface/NavMarkerTypes , 21 use Collectible , all on SPH-UserWaypoint with their target's flag on. An icon's states (0x18EA334) always include state 0; kind 6 adds state 6 while the map's current target is this marker, and kind 2 takes the member's own states. The waypoint. The current target lives at [GM+0x6C80] , with its type at +0x20 (7 a point, 1 a tracked target), its position at +0x10 , its region at +0x28 and its marker at +0x90 . 0x17A98AC(targets, &position, region record) sets a point and System::ClearCurrentTarget 0x17A8C5C clears it. The waypoint's marker (vtable 0x1DC0708) holds NavMarkerTypes::UserWaypoint at +0x38 and MapDisplay/Targets::UserWaypoint at +0xE0 . The legend's outpost glyph is Interface/Menu/MenuTreeNode/Legend::Outposts ( interface\textures\hud\glyph\outpost.tex ). The quest lock. [GM+0x6C80] is one cell for a quest's target, the Army screen's Mark Target and the map waypoint, and its setters test nothing (the shared clear-first core 0x17A8F6C and its 9 callers), so each screen asks first. The Army screen (0x321508) refuses when the active quest (0x103508: the first running, Active quest that stays on the HUD) has +0x2B0 set (no target) or requires one (0x624AC4: +0x2A8 not -1 with +0x2B0 clear). The world map (slot 29, 0x18E954C, run as the map opens) sets [layer+0xA30] to 0, and so refuses SPACEBAR, when the tracked quest record [UIManager+0xE0] has TargetForcedToNone or its quest object ( [GM+0x6C60]+0x18 , 0x40 bytes per record index, the quest at +0x28 ; 0x4FA590) requires a target. +0x2B0 alone holds nothing there, since it is copied from the field only when the quest starts (0x57407C). Of all quests, 60 set TargetForcedToNone , and on one of them the game itself answers SPACEBAR with "You cannot change your Target while on this mission". Outposts on the map's own data. The world map lights outposts through material parameters. Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/WorldMap.OutpostStateParameters holds one entry, k vOwned4567 (ownership) and k vSelected4567 (selection), with four outpost slots of which two are bound ( DE Outpost Central , DE Outpost West ). The world map's update applies it (0xF252F0, together with the DLC4AreaMaterial region material) only when 0xD0B350 passes, which compares the current game mode against the name "DLC4": the lighting runs in Desolation of Mordor's own mode and never in the campaign. The zone map plays d4 menu zonemap outpost over when the cursor is over an outpost ( 3DZoneMap.OutpostSFX ) and steps an outpost's widget through stages of 2, 2 and 1 seconds ( Interface/Shared.ZoneMapWidgetOutpostStageDurations ). In that mode, a focused outpost ( [layer+0xA90] , written by 0x18E934C and by 0xD608B0, whose one caller 0xEF2F00 is one of the zone-map material's outpost bindings) gets its own card (0xDAECF0, which sets [layer+0xFAC0] ). Key 2, with nothing hovered, opens MenuManager.MercenaryLayer on that outpost's Faction/Outposts.Row / Column through System::EnterFortAssaultCompleteFlow (0xD64800). Of the 103 map canvases, every outpost zone and the Stronghold ZoneMap , Stronghold Cave and Stronghold Alarm1 to 3 canvases carry the enemy colors (zone fill 0xE6A41606, outline 0xFFA41606); Friendly Strongholds and Friendly Stronghold Cave carry the friendly ones (0xE609D5ED, 0xFF09D5ED); and CP Offense and CP Defense are an orange and the friendly cyan.

The interface keeps a generic two-line banner that any text can fill. The script binding CPlayerObj::DEMO ShowGenericBanner (a press-demo leftover, stub 0x1B80E20, two arguments: the player and a string key) is a jump to 0x1892F34( , key, 0, 0). That function (37 bytes, two callers, first argument unused) takes the banner manager at [[UIManager+0x30]+0xE0] (nothing happens while UIManager+0x30 is null) and calls 0xE604C(manager, key, secondKey, flag). Each key goes through the string lookup 0x471F2C, the same table all game text uses, into a wide-character buffer, and 0xE7A98 (string "GenericAux") shows the banner: the first key's text as the title and, when a second key is given and its text is not empty, that text as the second line. The banner appears beside the minimap.

- Which placed spawners, and so which AI types, do each outpost's layers hold, region by region? - What does a category-override entry with every field left as is do ( HighAlarm lists StrongholdDynamic and StrongholdDynamicArcher that way)? Is it a placeholder, or does it apply the list's own priority to the category? - Which override list does each outpost's sovOutpost volume hold (its +0x120 ), and which remote scripts do the controller's relays listen to? - Do repeated OutpostStatusInit calls stack change handlers on the same variable? - What, if anything, changes a base region's outpost garrison when the region's fortress changes hands? No outpost script does; a candidate is an area-ownership predicate in the spawn data. - Is Gorgoroth's own EnableAllOutposts listener, which ignores the outpost switch, in a layer the retail game loads? - Does the string FactionOutpostChunk (returned by an 8-byte function reached only through a function pointer) name a chunk of the save file, and if so, what does that chunk hold? - Does the world map's material have a k vOwned0123 twin, and what do the unbound slots of k vOwned4567 draw in Desolation of Mordor's mode? - What does the North outpost's missing To Sauron area entry change when Sauron retakes it? - Where does the "Bad record index" assert come from that is met when an assault mission's defender jobs build from D4OD OACaptain ? On that path (filler - 0x1B5B824 - 0x1C1D240 - builder 0x1BBF928), the role pass 0x1BD6A48 met a job-list handle naming an Inventory/MaterialOverride record. - Do the action codes of a duel (7 kills the other, 10 swaps the seats) mean the same in every event? They are read from the 2,039 events' use, not from the code. - Do the outpost missions of every region spawn their commander through the same spawnconditions prefab code read in Núrnen? - Does a campaign map ever reach Desolation's focused-outpost card ( [layer+0xA90] )? Reading it while hovering a Lithlad outpost zone in the campaign would settle it. - Is a siege's LifeSpanGenerated read only when the event is created, so that only sieges generated after a change get the new deadline? - What does the stronghold script's high-wave fear burst do to orcs at an outpost the player holds?

t: User interface: Scaleform, menus and the debug menu
x: The interface is a set of Scaleform GFx movies that the engine drives entirely from code and data: the movies hold artwork and timelines, while the GameDB holds menu layers, element placement, prompts, HUD states, text tokens and cameras. This chapter follows the stack from the UI manager down to a single movie clip and a single line of text, then covers nav markers, the Army screen's 3D stage and its camera, the title and loading screens and the developer debug menu that shipped without its controller. The mission start screen has its own chapter, The mission start screen.

The UI manager is [base+0x26FFB08] (vt 0x1F7A878, a class with three virtual methods; see Engine core). 0x1889674 stores the object in that slot and creates its members; CInterfaceMgr::Init (0x17804C4) later calls 0x188BAE4, which builds the views (below). Offset Meaning --- --- +0x30 the HUD; its +0x108 is the combat widget holding the ammo count ( +0x408 ) and the reticle state (byte +0x414 , written by 0x114C588), its +0xE0 the banner manager (below) +0x50 the menu system (below) +0x58 the UI effects manager that plays 3D effects behind widgets (below) +0x88 the object that owns the debug-menu open byte +0x7AE (below) +0xA8 the world map's camera (see Outposts, strongholds and fortress upgrades) +0xB0 the player's visual component (the same object as [player]+0x2348 ), used by the Skills screen and the currency readers (see Items) +0xF0 / +0xF8 the top menu layer's record and its layer state +0x144 the camera the UI projects nav markers with; +0x17C instead while the byte +0x198 is set (0x16D438) +0x1E8 the UI camera's transform (position and quaternion), with its horizontal and vertical fields of view in radians at +0x204 / +0x208 (0x18B7150) +0x220 the UI viewport as an int32 rectangle {left, top, right, bottom}; view initialization takes its width and height from it +0x240 the current state of the UI state machine (below) +0x248 / +0x250 the pending message-box completion {function, context} ; the box's close callback 0x17DA030 calls function(result, context) +0x2FB byte: setting a target is allowed ( IsInterrogationAllowed , read at 0x1DDC9D; see Mark Target below) +0x318 the Army screen's highlighted member as a key {army record, pool index}, written by the highlight (below); +0x328 is written with it +0x360 the views, one per Interface/Shared.UIViews entry; the first three are cached at +0x378 , +0x380 and +0x388 +0x430 a GameModes record (the HUD builder reads its UseMercenaryWidget ) The top menu layer is what menu predicates test: the evaluator 0x276E74 compares each record of a predicate's IncludedTopMenuLayers / ExcludedTopMenuLayers with [UIManager+0xF0] and each record of IncludedTopMenuLayerStates / ExcludedTopMenuLayerStates with [UIManager+0xF8] . The cell holds the layer's record, not the layer object. There is no UI thread in a running game. The UI manager's constructor also creates a thread object named UIThread (0x1889460 - 0x193856C; vt 0x22F94B8 with the shared thread methods, vf8 the name, vf9 the stub 0x19385BC, vf10 a 0x4000-byte stack), but it is never started. The shared thread start 0x529500 has 30 call sites, and each starts another object: the named threads of Threads and the frame, a Bink worker, a queue worker and two event workers on static objects. The object sits at UIManager+0x08 , and the UI's own console commands live in the source file CUIThread.cpp . The UI's per-frame work is done on the main thread instead. The HUD's CUIMgr::Render (0x1AB28C) runs inside the main scene's render submission. The nav-marker loop 0x1C4AEC runs on the main thread: its frame 0x2A9228 appears in 1.6% of 3,000 main-thread samples and in 0 of 1,938 render-thread samples. The menu selection's prompt rebuild runs from the client update (below), and captured movie frames reach the render thread through the main thread's command ring (below). The UI state machine is vt 0x1F74D30: vf2 is the handler (state, event), and the current state is at UIManager+0x240 . State 12 ( HierarchyTransition , the move into and out of the Army screen) enters at 0x437514, updates at 0x437594 and exits at 0x4375F0. Its update waits on the world-UI owner's busy test 0x19C36A8, but the wait is capped: the duration [0x2671338] is 20.0 seconds, armed by 0x49F9C8 and expired by 0x16CFA4 on the real-time clock (a measured 1,508 ms per 1.5 s).

t: Views: the generic host and the factory
x: A view is a CUIBaseView (vt 0x1F7CD48, 0x60 bytes). The factory 0x1889250( &view , 0, &record , &index ) allocates one and calls the constructor 0x18CAA38(view, record, index). The host is generic: it builds any record of Interface/GFX/UI . View offset Meaning --- --- +0x48 its layer (below) +0x50 u8, set to 1 at construction +0x54 u32 view index +0x58 the Interface/GFX/UI record Interface/GFX/UI has five records; a view record names a flash layer and the bundles it needs: View ActiveFlashLayer RequiredBundle Built --- --- --- --- NavMarkers Structuresuiflash primary 1 ( interface\flash\navmarkers.gfx ) interface\bundles\gfx\ingame.bndl , ingame uifx , ingame navmarkers , pc alternatbuttonstyles yes (index 0) Player primary 2 ( interface\flash\sp.gfx ) the same four, plus five additional bundles (among them worlduidata , ingame tex and store icon ) yes (index 1) MessageBox primary 4 ( interface\flash\messageboxes.gfx ) interface\bundles\gfx\ingame.bndl yes (index 2) PreLoad primary 3 ( interface\flash\preload.gfx , the only layer with BackgroundAlpha 1) none no Debug primary 0 ( interface\flash\widgets\debugmenu.gfx ) interface\bundles\gfx\debug.bndl no 0x188BAF0 walks Interface/Shared.UIViews , which ships as [NavMarkers, Player, MessageBox] , and builds one view per entry into UIManager+0x360 . PreLoad and Debug are never built. Layer setup 0x18CACF4(layer, record, index) reads ActiveFlashLayer and refuses a layer whose Structuresuiflash.File is empty; it stores the index at layer+0x30 and the flash record at layer+0x48 . The view's methods then do the rest: - vf1 0x18CB7DC, initialize. 0x18CBBA4 waits until the required and additional bundles are resident and the movie file ( Structuresuiflash.File , opened through the engine interface's vf13 service) is loaded into a movie definition at layer+0x40 . 0x18CAD78 then creates the movie. The view index becomes a movie mode (0 - 1, 1 - 2, 2 - 4, anything else - 2). The definition's vf4 0x11BBE3C(mode) (vt 0x22C2B00) builds a 0x3938-byte movie wrapper (vt 0x1E6EE80, constructor 0x11BC268), which is stored at layer+0x38 , and the record's EdgeAA , MaxCurvePixelError , StrokeQuality and BackgroundAlpha are applied to it. The method is called until the wrapper exists. It also fills the wrapper's glyph table (see Text below). - vf2 0x2A92A4, advance. The method takes the frame step from the layer's timer ( [layer+0x58]+0x14 ) and calls the wrapper's vf4. The engine advances only the views it owns in UIManager+0x360 ; a view built outside that list draws nothing until its vf2 is called.

t: The movie wrapper and the UI render list
x: The wrapper's +0x18 is the GFx movie and +0x38 its render ID. Its vf4 0x47D78F0 is one UI frame: 1. It calls movie- vf24 Advance(step, 2, 0), then movie- vf25 Capture(1), which returns the captured frame. 2. 0x115226C posts a 0x28-byte command on the main thread's render command ring 0x272E8D8 (see Threads and the frame): {+0x00 thunk 0x65086C, +0x08 the UI render list, +0x10 method 0x650888, +0x18 u32 render ID, +0x20 frame} . On the render thread 0x650888 locks the list and stores the frame into the entry with that ID. 3. It calls 0x251E00(ring, 0); then 0x2AA3A8 runs the wrapper's callback queue at +0x3920 . The UI render list is a static object at 0x272EB20: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x10 / +0x18 vector of 0x18-byte entries, kept sorted by mode +0x28 lock Entry offset Meaning --- --- +0x00 the render target (vt 0x22C6720) +0x08 u32 mode bit +0x0C u32 render ID +0x10 the last captured frame 0x1C8DAF4(list, handle, mode) registers a movie: it takes the next ID from the counter at 0x27966A0, inserts an entry before the first one with a higher mode and returns the ID. Every movie has its own entry, so two movies of the same mode do not collide. In a loaded game the list holds NavMarkers (mode 1), the Player HUD (mode 2), MessageBox (mode 4) and two more movies with modes 8 and 0x10. The last captured frame stays on screen until the next capture. Scaleform draws the list through its own D3D11 renderer (see Rendering).

Interface/MessageBox holds 173 box definitions; each picks one of three elements, Interface/Elements::GenericMessageBox ( LIB-Dialog ), Larger GenericMessageBox ( LIB-Dialog Delete ) or BannerMessageBox ( LIB-Banner ). A request is queued on the message-box manager at [CGameClientShell+0x890] (the request layout is in Saves, the store and the network layer); the caller's completion function goes into UIManager+0x248 / +0x250 and receives the button result. messageboxes.gfx is a shared-library client: it imports one symbol, CompLibrary , from the component library, which exports it as an empty sprite, and places it on its root, which is how Scaleform makes a library's exports attachable there. The dialog widgets animate out 0 .. 9 to off 10 (alpha 0) and in 11 .. 19 to on 20. The generic banner is a two-line text banner beside the minimap, owned by the banner manager [[UIManager+0x30]+0xE0] : 0x1892F34( , key, secondKey, flag) - 0xE604C looks each key up in the string database and shows the title and, when its text is not empty, the second line (details in Outposts, strongholds and fortress upgrades).

The save-select screen's row frames and prompt bar, and the HUD's bars, are not Scaleform art but 3D ClientFX effects drawn beneath the Scaleform views. A menu widget that names an FXList hands its node to the UI effects manager [UIManager+0x58] . The call 0x15747C(node, fxList, 0) - 0x157DF8 fills a 0x190-byte entry { +0x00 node handle, +0x138 FX list, +0x140 state (1 create, 2 running, 3 stop, 4 kill), +0x144 index} and stores the index in the node ( +0xD0 , node vf2 / vf3 0x157FB0); 0x157890(node) retires the entry (state 3). 0x2249E8 (from 0x224430) builds the effect. The save-select screen's prompt bar, for example, is the widget Interface/Menu/MenuWidget/Prompt::DifficultyPrompt (symbol LIB-PromptBanner , attached from the library, FX list Interface/ElementFXList::Difficulty PromptBar ), whose box is StructuresUIFXData {UIFX Client/ClientFXSequence::Store PromptBar = fx\ui\menuitems\store promptbar.fxp , depth 26.5, TrackRotation }. At the title screen the manager held 23 entries, among them the save rows' frames DifficultySelect / DifficultySelect Highlight . A menu widget's state is at +0xDC (0 out, 1 off, 2 in, 3 on), its record at +0xE8 and its clip's output handle at +0x58 . UI Widget d 0x3293D0 attaches the clip (node slot 76, or slot 83 GetMember when the symbol is not taken from the library), and 0x46DC80 hands the node and the FX list to the manager.

The base game's movies are sections of three bundles in UI Assets.arch06 ; a scan of its 2,269 containers finds 19 movies: - interface\bundles\ingame.embb holds 17: the component library, the HUD ( sphud.gfx ), the Army screen ( hierarchy.gfx ), upgrades, skills, swords, progression, minimap, zone map, message boxes, struggle sequence, reveal-and-death, world puzzle, the main menu, the online sign-in movie ( wbid.gfx ), navmarkers.gfx and sp.gfx ; - interface\bundles\debug.embb holds interface\flash\widgets\debugmenu.gfx ; - interface\bundles\font latin.embb holds the font movie interface\fonts\fonts latin.gfx (9,649,751 bytes, a 550 x 400 stage). A running game holds 18 resident movies (see The executable), which matches the 17 of ingame plus the font movie. The patch archives also carry 56 loose copies of eight of them (24 distinct versions). The archive search order (see Archives and file formats) serves these copies: Movie Library symbol Base copy: bytes / SWF version / exports Served copy --- --- --- --- componentlibrary.gfx CompLibrary 183,424 / 8 / 197 Patch DLC4 : 204,515 / 8 / 246 sphud.gfx (none) 177,433 / 14 / 133 Patch DLC4 : 191,900 / 14 / 141 hierarchy.gfx HIELIB 47,651 / 17 / 31 Patch 09 : 60,114 / 15 / 34 upgrades.gfx UPGRADESLIB 96,435 / 17 / 39 Patch DLC5 : 112,457 / 15 / 48 minimap.gfx MM-LIB 25,070 / 17 / 21 Patch DLC4 : 25,505 / 17 / 22 zonemap.gfx MAPLIB 10,747 / 17 / 15 Patch DLC4 : 13,765 / 17 / 15 messageboxes.gfx (none) 11,734 / 8 / 7 Patch 09 : 17,906 / 8 / 10 wbid.gfx WBIDLib 17,176 / 8 / 16 Patch 09 : 17,040 / 8 / 16 skills.gfx , swords.gfx , progression.gfx , strugglesequence.gfx , mainmenu.gfx SKILLSLIB , SWORDSLIB , PROGRESSLIB , StruggleLib , MainMenuLib base only debugmenu.gfx (none) 27,142 / 9 / 33 (12 DBG- symbols, 21 textures) base only All 18 interface movies, and the eight served patch copies, are uncompressed ( GFX ), have a 1280 x 720 stage (25,600 x 14,400 twips) and a single root frame, and run at 60 frames per second (30 for the minimap, the message boxes, navmarkers.gfx and sp.gfx ). Fonts are imported from interface\fonts\gfxfontlib.swf ( $HydraHUD ); the message boxes import the component library, and the zone map imports MM-LIB from the minimap. No movie embeds a picture: all 231 images of the 18 base movies are Scaleform external images ( DefineExternalImage2 ) named by their .tex path and resolved by the engine's texture system. Symbol names carry the movie's prefix: LIB- (component library), SPH- (HUD), HIE- (Army screen), MAP- (zone map), UPG- (upgrades), MM- (minimap), WBID- , DBG- (debug menu).

The movies are ActionScript 2 skins with almost no code. A widget's timeline has the frame labels out , off , in and on ; the off and on frames run stop(); if (this. FrameEventHandler) this. FrameEventHandler( root.EFrameEvents Off) (or On ), and the root defines EFrameEvents None , On , Off , FX and Sound (0 to 4). Code selects a widget with gotoAndPlay("in") and deselects it with gotoAndPlay("out") ; the widget animates itself and reports the end of the animation through the handler. Layout, lists, counts and text all come from code and the GameDB.

t: Driving a movie from code: the node API
x: The engine wraps every Scaleform value it touches in a 0xF8-byte node (vt 0x1DAB888, constructor 0x1C309C): +0x28 the value's object interface, +0x30 the value type ( (type & 0x8F) == 0xA is a display object), +0x38 the object. Callers receive nodes through output handles that the callee constructs in place (0x1C2F80, the node at handle+0x10 ); a handle holds pointers to itself, so it cannot be moved once constructed, and its destructor 0x1C68FC releases the node. Call Address Arguments --- --- --- root wrapper vf42 0x4679C4 (wrapper, out) GetVariable 0x467A20 ( [wrapper+0x18] , value, "path"): resolves root , not clips attached at run time GetMember node vf83 0x1C2EE4 (node, out, "name") GetMember by path node vf84 0x11C063C (node, out, "a.b.c") createEmptyMovieClip node vf80 0x7B1EE4 (node, out, "name"): creates the clip; returns an empty handle when the name exists attachMovie node vf76 0x474434 (node, out, "symbol", "instance"), both char ; refuses an existing instance name (0x47482C) removeMovieClip node vf86 0xEBDAC (node) Invoke without arguments node vf85 0x11C10B4 (node, "method"); the general invoke is 0x4676C0 play / stop node vf121 0xEBDE4 / vf122 0xEBE0C (node) gotoAndPlay / gotoAndStop by label vf110 0x46F30C / vf112 0x471BE8 (node, "label") gotoAndPlay / gotoAndStop by frame vf111 0x7DE75C / vf113 0x16D9B8 (node, frame) setText vf103 0x471BFC ( char ), vf102 0x471C84 ( wchar t ) (node, text) setHTMLText vf106 0x11C156C (node, char ) set the 2D matrix 0x128592C ( [node+0x28] , [node+0x38] , matrix): rows {a, b, 0, tx}, {c, d, 0, ty}, translation in pixels (multiplied by 20.0 into twips) The text setters share 0x710ADC(movie, value, text, html), which sets the member htmlText when the last argument is 1 and text when it is 0: vf103 passes 0, vf106 passes 1. When the string contains { , both first set the plain text TestStr and call vf108 to size the field's picture substitutions before setting the real text (see Text below). Interface elements are found by name through Interface/Elements (0x32A774): an element record names its library symbol ( SymbolName ), an effect list and an Interface/ElementAttribute placement.

An attached clip lives exactly as long as the node attachMovie returned. attachMovie allocates the node, attaches the symbol (0x115BB34), then 0x4744EC sets the owner byte node+0x58 to 1 and registers an onUnload listener at node+0xA0 whose callback is 0x7941C4. The node destructor (vf0 0x1C3158 - 0x1C318C) releases the listener and, while +0x58 is set, invokes removeMovieClip on the clip. If the clip is unloaded some other way (removed, or its parent removed), 0x7941C4 clears +0x58 first, so a clip is never removed twice. Lookup nodes (GetMember vf83 / vf84, root ) never set the owner byte. Releasing an attach handle therefore removes the clip, while a lookup handle for the same clip is a different node whose release leaves the clip alone. Code that keeps attached clips on screen must hold their attach handles (and release children before parents).

All game text is looked up by key in the string database [base+0x2702000] (vt 0x2008F70). The database is a list of loaded string tables (the list at +0x10 ). A table is its list node minus 0x40, with +0x0C the row count, +0x10 the rows, +0x18 the narrow rows and +0x30 the UTF-16 text. A row is {u32 key hash, u32 text offset in UTF-16 units}; the rows are sorted by hash, and the hash is the key's case-insensitive P919 (see GameDB). A table's lookup 0x472104 binary-searches its rows (0x472134). 0x471F2C takes a key string, hashes it and returns the text. The store's vf8 answers whether a hash exists, and vf8 and vf9 take the first table in the list that holds it. Because the key is hashed from its content, a key string can live anywhere in memory. The tables are the shipped per-language files ( database\string\<language \string.strdb , see Archives and file formats). Table-shaped data also lies elsewhere on the heap (one such copy lacked keys that the listed table holds); the game reads the tables reached through the database's own list.

t: Format arguments, color runs and tokens
x: Text carries three kinds of markup, resolved in this order: 1. Format arguments ( {1!s} , {1!d} , {1!.0f} , {1!ls} ) are filled by the game's formatter ( Str WBFormatMessageT ). 2. Action and alias tokens are replaced by ReplaceActionsWithDevices 0x2995F8, named by its own assert string. It is reached through the UI callback 0x299520 that CInterfaceMgr::Init registers, which looks up $KEY strings and runs any text through it. For each {name} : - an input-action name (one of the 377 actions) becomes the button bound to it: {<Device } when that button has a text glyph, otherwise its PCKey string; - a Profile/ActionAlias record becomes its FontColor as a <font color run (0xD06CF0), otherwise its gamepad or keyboard-and-mouse string, which is run through the pass again; - anything else is copied back unchanged. 3. Picture tokens left in the text are drawn by Scaleform's image substitution (below). A letter key has no text glyph ( KeyG has TextFieldGlyphReplacement off and device code 71), so the game prints its string, IDS Key G = {Color Player}[G]</font . The cyan bracketed key is the game's own style for a key in text. The color aliases. An alias's Profile/ActionAlias.FontColor leads to an Interface/Color.COLOR value (ARGB). The table gives each alias's color and its uses in the shipped English strings: Alias Color Uses --- --- --- Enemy 0xFFED5F09 745 Player 0xFF09D5ED 626 Objective 0xFFFFC640 344 Epic 0xFFE24E2C 58 Follower 0xFF09D5ED 18 Reward 0xFFED5F09 6 Intel , Broken , Green 0xFF359737 Weakened 0xFF94BFD6 Red 0xFFA42E06 Hate 0xFFDF4E2C Legendary , Yellow , Disabled , Vulnerable , Terrified , Immune 0xFF4700BF, 0xFFFFC640, 0xFF626262, 0xFF5279BD, 0xFF81294A, 0xFFDC9B50 0

A picture inside a line of text is a Scaleform image substitution, set up per view. - The glyph table. Each owned view's initialize method (vf1 0x18CB7DC) fills its movie wrapper's glyph table: first every Profile/Inputs/PC/Buttons record with TextFieldGlyphReplacement on (27 of 155: the gamepad buttons and the mouse) under the token {<Device } (wrapper vf37 formats {%d} ), then every Interface/GlyphReplacement record (133) under its TokenText . - AddGlyph is wrapper vf38 0x11BCF78(wrapper, token wchar t , texture path char ). It returns at once when the table holds 256 entries ( cmp [rcx+0xA0], 0x100 ). It gets the texture's handle (0x1BEAAC, get-or-create), its data object [[handle+8]] (0x3DF304 - 0x3DF388) and, from [obj+0x10] (0x3DF2B8), the width and height words +0x52 / +0x54 . There is no null check, so a texture that nothing has loaded faults there. It stores width and height in a 0x38-byte entry (entries from +0xA8 , 0x469A5C), makes img://<texture a BitmapData (0x11BED8C, main thread only) and pushes {image, subString, width, height, baseLineY = texture height x 0.8} onto root. GlyphData ( +0x38A8 ). The wrapper's constructor 0x11BC268 publishes root.RegisterGlyphs and GlyphData . The engine has no call that removes an entry. - Sized to each field's font. Setting a text that contains a { (above) calls vf108 - 0x4697D0. Every picture's height is the font's getTextExtent("W").ascent x 1.2, and its width is that height times the entry's aspect; the function then calls setImageSubstitutions(null) and setImageSubstitutions( GlyphData) . A wide picture therefore becomes a strip one text line high. - The tokens. TokenText is a wide string capped at 15 characters, braces included: {BrokenCaptain} fills it, which accounts for the shipped {LegendarySkul} . The record name need not match the token: SocialCurrencyIcon is {Spoils} , CurrencyCoin is {Coin} , CurrencyIcon is {M} , and PremiumCurrencyIcon 's {G} is the Gold icon, not the G key. Counted by TokenText , which is what Scaleform matches, the shipped strings use 95 of the 133 tokens 851 times in 593 strings; 185 of those uses are in strings that also carry format arguments. A record instance holds +0x00 ReplacementTexture , +0x08 PCMousePrimarySwapTexture and +0x10 TokenText . - The glyph textures ship inside UI bundles. A bundle-membership index placed 12 of them in no bundle, but parsing 19,525 bundle manifests of five archives puts 9 of the 9 checked inside patch bundles ( Patch DLC4 's interface\bundles\gfx\ingame.bndl and ingame navmarkers.bndl , Patch 05 's store icon.bndl ). The views' initialization waits for those bundles, so AddGlyph's unchecked read meets a loaded texture.

A quest's card text comes from one resolver, 0xCF9D90( , quest record, out, kind), reached through the thunk 0xD64810 and the wrapper 0xD731E0(quest, out, kind). Kind 0 is Description , kind 3 ShortDescription , and two more kinds go through other accessors. For each kind it reads that kind's picker. When one is set, it asks the picker (0x18A0C4C with the live quest, otherwise 0x4AA370 with the record); the picker walks its entries in order and takes the first whose Predicate holds for the member filling its Jobs , or that has PassIfNoMember with nobody there. The entry's String and StringArgs are used only when an entry passes and its String is not empty (0xCFAAE8 .. 0xCFAB43); otherwise the quest's own field and its Args are used (0xCFABA7). The name's twin, 0x17DEE5C, shows what the argument bits mean: bit 1 the subject's name and title (0x4A9810), bit 2 the second participant, bit 4 SupporterStringPicker , bits 8, 0x10 and 0x20 numbers. - Readers. The two wrappers have 9 callers. Kind 0 is read by the world map's quest card 0x18EB6B4, the captain card with his 3D model 0x190338C (the CharacterPresentation widget) and 0x18DAF8C (an unidentified layer). The mission start screen's text writer 0x18E356C fills its QuestDescription field through the same wrapper. Kind 3 is read by the Army screen's captain line 0x18A36B8 and two others, kind 2 by one. - Pickers are shared. Quest/JobStringPickerGroup has 127 groups. All 11 Outpost groups are the same two entries on the outpost commander's job with PassIfNoMember True: IsNameKnown gives SC <challenge Outpost Desc ("Draw out {1!s} by ..."), IsUnknown gives ... Desc Unk ("Draw out the Outpost leader by ..."). Both predicates are MemberHasNameUnlocked , 0x1149E60(member) = [FM+0x510] & 1 . Emulating 0x4AA370 on live memory picked the entry this rule predicts for 3 of 3 live quests. Text cells are shared too: on SM SC W RapidStealth the Description , ShortDescription and StartPointDescription cells all point at one string, and the objective SpawnCon KillChief Obj ("Defeat {1!s}") is shared by 855 quests (outposts 233, vendettas 294, warchiefs and forts 100, others 228). An empty picker link reads 0. - The world map's quest card honors \n line breaks in the description.

A menu is data: layers, trees of nodes, widgets, elements and their placements, all under Interface/ . - The menu manager record Interface/Menu/MenuManager::Menu (at [[UIManager+0x50]+0x518] ) links the default pause layer ( PauseRoot/PauseLayer ), the title screen root ( FrontEndRoot/FrontEnd ) and one layer per screen, among them the world map, zone map, quest log, appendices, war upgrades, the Army screen ( Hierarchy/HierarchyLayer ), the captain detail ( FactionMember/FactionMember ), upgrades, equipment, gems, store, gold, mercenaries, skins and options. - Layers. Interface/Menu/MenuLayer has 48 layer classes and 74 layer records (one more class, Graveyard , survives only in an old patch). Every layer has the common fields ContentSymbol , LayerFX , the title fields, DirectExitAction , sounds for init / activate / sub-layer push and pop / deactivate / term, a Transition ( Interface/Menu/MenuTransition , 43 records), Components , NavPane , a status header type, AutoWidgets , a HUDState , a default layer state, MenuSelectionPredicates and a telemetry alias; each class adds its own (the Army screen's has 97 fields, most of them actions). The Interface/Menu/MenuLayerList records (32) are stacks of layers pushed together, for example Hierarchy Full and NewGameSetup Full . - Trees, nodes and widgets. Interface/Menu/MenuTreeGroup records group Interface/Menu/MenuTreeBase trees (155). Interface/Menu/MenuTreeNode has 58 node classes, among them skills, gems, traits, quests, skins and game modes. Interface/Menu/MenuWidget holds 271 widgets, and Interface/Menu/MenuComponent holds buttons (78, each with a ContentElement naming a LIB- symbol), checkboxes, cycles, sliders and text entries. The trait card's rows are tree nodes too (see Captain traits); the Skills screen's node state is computed in code (see Items). - Elements and placement. The categories are Interface/Elements (242) and Interface/ElementAttribute (962). An attribute is a screen placement and its animation: AppliedProperties , InterpolationTime , DelayTime , InterpolationType , VisibleOnInterpolateTerm , UseSafeZone , Position (a screen fraction), Offset , Scale , Alpha , Z , ZScale , Rotation , a 3D rotation and Filters ( Interface/ElementFilter : bevel, blur, color matrix, drop shadow, glow). Attributes come in named pairs such as AgeGate Active / AgeGate Inactive , an element's placement with its layer active and inactive. - Predicates. Interface/Predicates/ gate nodes and actions: Menu (66), HierarchyState (115), Hierarchy (28) and 39 more classes. - Selections. Interface/Menu/MenuSelection/Predicate/ and /Action/ tie an input to a prompt and a result action (below). - Text and input. The text and input records are Interface/GFX/Fonts::Main , Interface/GFX/FontMapping ( Console , IntHUD , LatinHUD ), Interface/GFX/KeyMaps ( InGame , Menu ) and 109 Interface/GFX/Text styles for the engine's own debug text. Menus take input through command sets ( Profile/CommandSets ).

[UIManager+0x50] is the menu system: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x500 .. +0x508 vector of every layer built (23 at the title screen) +0x518 the Interface/Menu/MenuManager record +0x520 the layer stack, open layers in push order; its u32 count is at +0x560 , and the top layer is entry count - 1 (0x3245F0 reads it) +0x568 a layer record queued for a push +0x6FD0 the menu selection (below) +0x71E0 a one-shot request that the Army screen's enter method uses and clears +0x728 set: a push happens at once instead of being queued +0x800 the store header (see Saves, the store and the network layer) +0xD38 seven widget callbacks, run by 0xD8E770(menu, 7) The vector and the stack hold each layer's menu-layer part, which sits at +0x48 of the layer object (in the quest-start layer every caller of the layer lookup subtracts 0x48); from that pointer +0x6B8 is the menu and +0x6C0 the layer's Interface/Menu/MenuLayer record. The lookup 0x466758(menu, record) is get-or-create: for a layer that is not open it builds and registers one (the factory 0x7219D0, 0x7C0FC4). 0x18BB000(menu, record) pushes a layer (0x31A034) or queues its record at +0x568 . A layer's action handler is its vtable slot 19. Layer objects are instances of per-class engine types: the mode-select layer is vt 0x1F92AF0 (see Saves, the store and the network layer), the Army screen layer vt 0x1F7B588 (its job vt 0x1F7B748 at +0x9C8 , run 0x189C4F8), the captain detail layer vt 0x1F7CB10 (job vt 0x1F7CC18, run 0x18CA348), the world map's CUI3DZoneMapLayer vt 0x1F7E570, the war-upgrades layer vt 0x1F895C0 and the quest-start layer vt 0x1F7E110 (see The mission start screen).

The pause menu is data. Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/PauseRoot::PauseLayer names its SelectionTree Interface/Menu/MenuTreeGroup::PauseRoot , its audio hooks and its DirectExitAction ; the group holds the trees MenuTreeBase::RootTree (Army, Quests, Character, Inventory), MinorSelection (Market, Online, Guide, Appendices, Options, Quit) and MOTD , the community challenge panel. The panel's text is not in the shipped string tables: it comes from the online service's broadcast feed.

t: Selections, prompts and the prompt bar
x: The menu selection is menu+0x6FD0 ; its first qword points back at the menu. It holds the predicates that are offered, the prompts drawn for them and the Army screen's mode lists.
