Selection offset Meaning --- --- +0x10 active +0x11 byte: when 0, a predicate's keyboard-and-mouse input is preferred (below) +0x18 13 type buckets of 0x20 bytes (0xD8EA20 asserts the type is below 13); each bucket's +0x08 / +0x10 is a vector of predicate sources, and each source's +0x08 / +0x10 a vector of predicate records +0x1E0 the Army screen's mode lists, 0x20 each: +0x00 the list record, +0x08 / +0x10 the Interface/HierarchyMode/Type rules that passed +0x208 1 on the Army screen +0x3E8 .. +0x3F0 the prompt-bar widgets, 0x28 bytes each, the widget at +0x20 +0x418 the rebuild flag A source names its subject at +0x28 . With the world map open, bucket 6 held one source (vtable 0x1DB12B0) whose +0x28 is the 3DZoneMap layer record and which held 7 of that layer's 8 predicates. On the Army screen, bucket 0's sources carry a member key at +0x28 and his position at +0x38 , and the highlight's selection set 0x18BE498 appends one on every call (0x18BB704). Who rebuilds it, and when. The client update 0x1A864C - 0x52440C - 0x1890700 calls 0x163CFC( [UIManager+0x50] ) - 0x163D28( menu+0x6FD0 ) every frame. 0x163D28 rebuilds the prompts only when the selection's byte +0x418 is set, and then clears the byte. 0xD8F220(selection, 0) sets it and is called from 14 sites in the engine. The bar belongs to the main thread. The refill. 0x320B08 (51 call sites) runs each type's sources in TypePriority order. A source's vf2 0x321338 clears its vector and calls vf21 0x322324, which reads the layer record's MenuSelectionPredicates (0x767E2C: the record's own run, then its instance) and keeps each predicate that 0x3223CC passes. The test covers the predicate's CommonPredicates and the running tutorial's DisableMenuSelectionPredicates . The common-predicate check 0x322D9C passes a null link; otherwise it tests the build, store and online-service predicates, then the required, allowed and excluded menu, hierarchy, faction, quest, game-state, player and bodyguard lists. None of the 74 shipped predicates has a null CommonPredicates ; 15 point at a common-predicate record that sets no condition. The build. 0x31EC5C skips each kept predicate that has no Prompt . Otherwise the predicate's input actions ( InputPromptOverride , else InputKBM when +0x11 is 0 and the predicate has one, else Input ) go through 0x31EDF0, which claims each action index for the first predicate that uses it, in a table of 377 entries; an index past the table is an engine assert. A predicate whose actions were all claimed is dropped. The kept ones are sorted (0x76CE58) and handed to each bar widget whose context matches the prompt's Context : 0xDDC940 - 0xE4F570 fills one of the widget's 16 slots of 0x4D8 bytes with the PromptID key, two action IDs, Enabled and the device flags ( KeyboardPrompt 1, GamepadPrompt 2, ClickablePrompt 4). A second loop reads each predicate's Prompt again (0x163F80) and uses it without a null check: a Prompt link that changes between the two reads would reach 0xE4F570 with a null PromptID . The accessors themselves return 0 for a null record (0x73E4CC). Prompt-only predicates. A predicate may name a prompt and no ResultAction : it only draws the prompt, and the layer handles the key itself. The world map's SetWaypoint KBM , Zoom MordorMap , Zoom Army and Player Center are such predicates. Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/ZoneMap::3DZoneMap.MenuSelectionPredicates lists eight predicates ( PushQuestLog , PopToQuestLog , 3DZoneMap PushLegendLayer , Zoom MordorMap , Zoom Army , Player Center , SetWaypoint KBM , Back ); its prompts use the context FortStatusHeader . Only SetWaypoint KBM names ZoneMapHasHighlight (as an exclusion). The input actions are an enum of 377 names ( None 0 .. Search Enter 376; see GameDB for the enum name registry): for example ZoneMapZoomOut 68, MenuAux0 78, CombatKBM11 135, MenuKBM00 145, PhotoMode CameraMode 368. On the PC keyboard the menu actions are bound to Space, 1-7, A, D, Q, E, Z, X, B, Shift, Home and Esc ( Profile/Commands ).

The HUD is the Player view. Interface/ElementSetup::Setup (108 fields) configures it: HUDBase - Interface/HUD/Widget/HUDManager , five event managers (among them center, left and right), the item widget, the mercenary widget, DebugHUDElements - Interface/HUD/Widget/FXTest , the bar effects and fill rates, toast events and minimap thresholds. The HUD builder 0x18C3E80 creates the widgets by name: combat ( CUIHUDCombat ), photo mode, combo, the event managers, the standard, keyboard, quick-time, center and top prompt groups, combat hints, the pausing tutorial, pinned challenge, character and quest-start presentations, quest failure, brand notification, the crosshair ( CUIHUDCrosshair ), skill points, score and timer. Last, it tests GameModes.UseMercenaryWidget on the record at [UIManager+0x430] : when the field is set it builds the mercenary summon bar ( CUIHUDMercenaryWidget , the Desolation of Mordor bodyguard slots), and when it is clear, the item widget. The per-frame loop 0x1C4AEC walks every widget through an intrusive list: the sentinel is base+0x26725F8 , the first node [sentinel+8] , the widget the node minus 0x18 and the next node [node+8] (170 widgets in a loaded world, the walk ending at the sentinel). For each widget 0x1C5140 - 0x1C3EF8 updates it, and 0x1C5140 ends by clearing the flag word [widget+0x48] (0x1C544B), so a raised flag lasts one update (170 of 170 read 0 at rest): Flag at widget+0x48 Tested by --- --- 0x1 rebuild (0x1089E8) 0x2 0x189C6E4 0x8 0x10BA84 0x20000 the nameplate text (below) 0x100000 0x10B828 0x1000000 0x18DB270 0x8000000 0x32AF0C 0x10000000 0xD6D530 Projection. 0x1C4AEC builds a context each frame from the UI manager's camera ( +0x144 , or +0x17C ), its camera transform and lens ( +0x1E8 , +0x204 , +0x208 ), the viewport rectangle +0x220 and the safe-zone factors VP SZ Top / Left / Right . 0x1C3C54 projects a point with a plain centered pinhole: view = 0x2577DC(camera, world), u = 0.5 + 0.5 vx P00 / z and v = 0.5 - 0.5 vy P11 / z, and the point is on screen when both are within [0, 1] and z 0. The card over a hovered captain on the Army screen (name, class line, level shield, prompts, arrow) is not drawn by the Army screen layer. It is a nav marker widget, updated by the same loop as every marker in the world, and it never polls: 0x189B438(clip, &position ) refills its text only when flag 0x20000 is raised or right after the clip loads. Hovering away and back reloads the clip, and highlighting the captain already highlighted does nothing. - The text is read from the live member. 0x188CE30(position) finds the member from widget+0x290 = { +0x00 army, +0x08 u8 row, +0x09 u8 seat}, and 0x4A9810(member, ..) builds the line. A change to his name or title therefore shows at the next refill, without a summary refill. - The engine's raise is 0x17FE784(marker, &position ): it copies 16 bytes to marker+0x3B8 and widget+0x290 and sets flag 0x20000 ( bts [widget+0x48], 0x11 ), with no same-value test. It takes the 0x420-byte marker, not the widget. Its callers build the position from the member (0x60C424) or from a summary's +0x48 (vf74 0x1823448, vt 0x1F77FA8::vf1).

t: The hierarchy movie and the 3D stage
x: The Army screen is a 3D stage in a dedicated menu world with the hierarchy.gfx overlay on top. The movie draws only the 2D panels: its 22 HIE- symbols are the enemy overview, the trait card parts ( HIE-TraitHeader , -TraitGroup , -TraitContent , -TraitDivider ), dialogs (upgrade, target, cancel), quest start and complete panels, assault and defense groups, contract overview and the player icon. No symbol describes rows or seats: the captains, the seats and the fort are world objects. (The instance names Row0 - Row9 belong to the component library's control-bindings screen, and OverlordTree / WarchiefTree to the zone map's fort highlight.) Faction/HierarchyMenu/Setup::Default (114 fields) configures the screen: the stage bundle bundles\hierarchymenu.bndl , the menu world collision prefabs\ui\worlduimenuws collision.bndl , the henchmen, power-struggle and blood-brother link effects, the fidget bundle bundles\animationcharacters\menu\fidget.bndl (at most 20 fidgets at once), one camera state per mode (among them army, mercenary, orders, garrison and contract assignment, store, map and pause), the character model manager and 38 tutorials. Each army's stage is chosen by its Faction/Definition.WorldUIFaction - Faction/World/Faction (10 records): Instance names the stage rig ( prefabs\ui\wuim regionfaction ws.bndl for five regions, wuim minasfaction ws for Minas Ithil, wuim desert dlc4 ws and wuim dlc4merc faction ws for the Desolation of Mordor), FortPicker the fort pieces, and Member / GarrisonMember / VendettaMember the seat grids. The section is requested by the region's stage object in the menu world (vt 0x1FA4008, named Hier.Map.Region ) when that object activates. Its vf16 0x1A34E78 maps the record Region to the region's army through Region GetFaction 0x1E4418, which ends in Regions/Region.GameModeFactionOverrides keyed by the current game mode, then in Region.Faction . It then resolves the world section, requests it into the object's own group (0x4B420C) and links the object into the active-stage list 0x2675860. The activation runs when the menu world is rebuilt during a load, not on a visit to the Army screen. The stage objects sit at their regions' real positions on the map at scale 1.0 (eight active in a loaded game), and vf16 requests each section at its object's own transform.

t: Stage holders and the world-UI owner
x: The world-UI owner [base+0x26FFB60] (vt 0x1F97950; see Engine core) keeps one slot per army at +0x2B8 : 38 slots of 0x50 bytes in army-table order (the key at +0x00 is the Faction/Definition , and 38 of 38 agree), with the count at +0x2C0 . StageFor 0x455EDC(owner, army) returns a slot's +0x48 , the stage holder; +0x28 .. +0x48 is an object handle (vt 0x1DC0488) chained on the region stage object's +0x2A8 , which points at the spawned holder. The armies of one region share one holder (21 of the 38 slots are filled in a loaded game). After a load every slot is empty until the owner's +0x400 goes to 1, around the first visit to the Army screen; +0x400 drops again later, and the slots stay filled. A holder (vt 0x1FA2FB8) has this layout: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x158 the replay event +0x160 the holder's frame {position, rotation}, from which grid seats are placed +0x198 / +0x1A0, +0x1A8 / +0x1B0 the stage characters: arrays of 0x28-byte entries, object at +0x20 +0x1B8 the summary container (its +0x9F50 is the army) +0x1C0 the stage manager +0x1E8 the fort (vt 0x1FA2698); +0x274 requests a fort build +0x275 rebuild every stage character +0x276 rebuild the rows The holder tick 0x16EE24 (called from the owner's per-frame Update, vf18 0x16F4A0) runs the fort reconciler 0x2EC464, which diffs the wanted fort pieces against the built ones. Then, when +0x275 is set, the tick prunes relationships (0x1B5E13C) and rebuilds every stage character from the summaries (0x1D7A918), writing the word +0x275 = 0x100 so that the row rebuild 0x1A284D8 follows on the next pass. The engine sets +0x275 itself when it sets a holder up for an army (0x1A29168, from 0x19C3760 and 0x19C3F60). With the menu closed an army has no stage objects; they are built fresh from the summaries when the screen opens. An army with no stage cannot be shown. When a region's stage object activates before its region maps to an army, it spawns nothing (its +0x2A8 handle points at itself) and the army's slot stays empty. A screen that shows such an army (the Mercenary screen pointed at it) then holds a black loading screen indefinitely, although the UI state machine's own wait expires after 20 seconds (above). A later load in which the region is mapped rebuilds the stage, and the screen then opens normally.

A captain on the stage is a CWorldUIFactionMember (vt 0x1F733C0, 0xB58 bytes, placement constructor 0x1822164), created through the object server by class name. It is built from the army's member summary , not from the FactionMember. Stage character offset Meaning --- --- +0xA0 the pose node +0xAC / +0xB8 / +0xC8 position of the animated root (the hip) on top of the seat, rotation, scale +0x110 the character model (vt 0x1F6F950) +0x1A8, +0xAF8 the cast seat position +0x1CC / +0x1CD / +0x1CE bytes: in the detail view, highlighted, under the cursor +0x668 the mount, for a mounted captain +0x720 the previous look, kept while a new one is set up +0x728 - its private look (0x40 bytes, constructor 0x62DCB4) - a private summary copy +0x738 its selection object (0xD0 bytes, no vtable, linked into a list at [0x2A86858]+0x160 ) +0x740 the preview states ( Faction/HierarchyMenu/PreviewTypeStates ) +0x758 its nav marker +0x760 the model object +0x768 its visual component (vt 0x1FD63F0), holding the weapon holders like a world character's +0x2348 +0xB18 its world-UI type record (for example Faction/World/Character::FactionMember or FactionMember WorldMap ), not the member +0xB3C set when the preview states must be rebuilt Its vtable slots are vf63 (the summary), vf67 / vf70 (highlight on / off), vf68 / vf69 (detail view start / end), vf71 / vf72 (cursor on him / off; 0x1A21664, byte +0x1CE , 0x188EE34) and vf73 (the selection object). A bone of a stage character is placed at world = P + s R(Q) t, where P, Q and s are the character's +0xAC , +0xB8 and +0xC8 and t is the bone's model-space position. A drawn weapon read this way sat 0.3 cm from the R Weapon bone (0.4 cm on an Olog), against 43.6 cm and 130.4 cm without the rotation. A loaded Army screen held 27 stage characters (an orc's rig has 100 bones, an Olog's 89), and the stage's captains draw with render ID 245 (see Characters, the player and the camera). A member summary (vt 0x1DB1070, 0x1A8 bytes) is one member's frozen description: Offset Meaning --- --- +0x30 a copy of the member's inventory (slot items, colors at +0xC8 , overlays at +0xE0 ) +0x40 a copy of the appearance (piece for piece like the live appearance object) +0x48 the faction +0x58 .. +0x60 a copy of the active traits +0x70 a copy of the markers +0x88 the key {u64 FM+0x178 army, u32 FM+0x174 pool index, u32 0} +0x100 location +0x114 the hash of his title (refilled by 0x169168) +0x120 level +0x124 his size (see Characters, the player and the camera) +0x130 combat tree ( FM+0x188 ) +0x138 / +0x140 / +0x148 / +0x150 class, role, personality, tribe +0x168 / +0x178 row, rarity +0x188 the flag word ( FM+0x508 ) +0x190 bit 0: the name is known ( FM+0x510 bit 0) There are three generations of copies. The army context keeps one summary per member ( [ctx+0x30] ; the lookup 0x1B5C0F8(FS, &key ) - 0x16FC5C is a pure read). The open stage draws from its own container of copies ( 0x16FC1C(owner, army) ), none of them shared with the army's. Each stage character draws from a third, private copy behind +0x728 . The engine refills the copies as follows. 0x169168(summary, member) re-reads the whole member into a summary: the appearance from 0x75D2FC, the items from 0x75D314, class, tree, role, personality, tribe, level, flags, the trait list rebuilt from FM+0x198 and the markers from FM+0x1B0 . Its sources are the member's mock-member snapshot when one exists (see The Nemesis system). 0x62BF54 refills a container copy, or appends one for an unseated member. The per-captain redraw is 0x19C395C(owner, &key ), which the engine calls after a Training Order is applied (0x1C51630): holder 0x455EDC - summary 0x1B5C0F8 - stage character 0x1A28FAC(holder, key) - UI CWorldUICharacter 0x627F40(character, summary, 0, 0). Every step returns quietly when the army is not on a stage. 0x627F40 chooses the look (0x2EB2DC, below). 0x62EEE4 then swaps the new look in and rebinds the model; only when the look test 0x170564 reports a change does it tear down the selection and model objects, rebuild them and set +0xB3C . The look test does not compare the death bits (flag bits 2 and 21), so a change of state alone does not rebuild a captain's preview pose. Under modification, a value written into an army summary reaches the open stage only when the screen is entered again, because the stage draws from its own copies. A stage character's private copy is deep (it owns its item instances), so refilling it in place frees items that the model has bound. Every frame while the screen is open, the owner's tick runs the character model manager ( HierarchyCharacterModelMgr , ConfigSwapsPerFrame ) - 0x628BF8 - the stage character's vf63 0x3680B0 (its summary) - 0x30DE28, which walks the summary's trait list for a MountAITemplate .

A fort's composition is data: Faction/World/Faction.FortPicker - Faction/World/Fort/Picker - fort setups - piece entries - pieces {world sections, position, rotation, fixed seats}. A piece entry ( FortPieceEntry ) is { FactionPredicate , HierarchyMenuPredicate , RequiredPredicateValue , Piece }. 0x62B600 builds the piece list from all seven entry lists of a setup and passes every entry through 0x62BB18, which allows the entry when the menu predicate's result (0x276E74) equals RequiredPredicateValue . The shipped data uses that switch only on lighting pieces: 132 of 132 lighting entries carry it, against 0 of 135 keep, 0 of 726 gate and 0 of 33 streamed entries. 0x2EC464 then diffs the list: pieces no longer listed are removed, and new WorldUIFortPiece objects are created. It rebuilds only when the fort's +0x271 is set, which 0x326168 does when called from 0x16E570, 0x455D78 (each tick from the owner's vf18, with regions sorted by distance) and 0x7A126C. 0xE83590 also calls 0x62B600. A normal fort's Foundation piece has no world section and sits on the map's own terrain. The Desolation of Mordor's mercenary camp brings its own ground ( Fort/Piece::Foundation Desert Mercs - prefabs\ui\mordormap\foundation desert mercs.bndl , 91 assets, 49.6 MB), which is why that camp shows on the map as a square of terrain wherever its stage is built. The upper rows (Overlord, inner and outer warchiefs, the first captain row) sit on fixed seats ( WorldUIFixedFactionMemberPos : a row and column, a position and a rotation), which any piece can register (0x629EEC - 0x62A17C). The other rows are a grid ( StructuresWorldUI.FactionMember : RowGap , ColumnGap ) placed from the holder's frame (0x1D79DF0). A seat is dropped onto the stage's collision by a ray, 0x62AA6C(seat, offset, out): on a hit the height becomes the hit point plus the offset, and on a miss the seat keeps its data position. The stage character (its vf11) calls it through 0x62AA48 with a zero offset, so the character's animated root, the hip, is placed on the seat itself. Stage idles are chosen by data and played by clip name. A preview state's HierarchyPreviewTypeAnimData.RootAnimChoice / RootInAnimChoice is a choice group. 0x42E72C takes the first child whose predicates pass (0x42E984 - 0x42EAFC); their inputs are the combat tree's CharacterType , the role, the personality and whether the name is known. 0x42E82C collects the child's Animation records, 0x42F794 picks one at random, and 0x42F1D0 plays it by name (0x4C8A0C - 0x302540, which looks the name's hash up in the skeleton's animation set). A name the character's set lacks plays the bind pose. Fidgets fire only for tags the current choice carries. The detail view plays the effects of Faction/World/Interactable/FX/States::FM Army Detail : its entries choose, by species predicate, an InteractableFXData whose FX names a ClientFX sequence ( Hierarchy Detail , Hierarchy DetailOlag , Hierarchy RiderDetail ). 0x2ECF5C reads the link on every update.

A captain whose name the player does not know is drawn as a generic model. The look chooser 0x2EB2DC tries three sources in order. When the summary's flag word has bits 17 and 21 set, it takes the decapitation picker ( DecapModelPicker , 0x2EB258 - 0x2EB14C). Otherwise, when the stage character's type record has a DefaultModel and 0x170744(summary, flag) is false, it takes that default model (0x2EA718). Otherwise it takes the captain's own model (summary +0x138 ), built by 0x2EBA60 from the appearance copy. 0x170744 returns true when the member (found from the key at summary+0x88 ) has killed the player ( FM+0x4C4 non-zero: such a captain is always shown). Otherwise, with the flag argument set, 0x16FDE0 must pass too. It is true when the member is not found or has flag bit 7; otherwise it takes the summary's copy of that bit ( +0x188 bit 7). With the flag set, a known captain therefore stays unknown until the menu has presented him. Last, it returns summary+0x190 bit 0, the copy of the name-known bit (see The Nemesis system for intel levels). The redraw 0x19C395C, the holder path 0x1A2957C, the combat-tree reader 0x170698, the name reader 0x17EE550 and the replay pass 0x1BFCCC8 call it with the flag clear, and 0x627B74, 0x627E4C and 0x1A1FF24 call it with the flag set. Faction/World/Character DefaultModel KilledByDecapitation --- --- --- FactionMember , Assignment , GarrisonMember , ModelCam , Quest , Stash , WorldMap , WorldMap Character/Models/HierarchyUnknown Head Stick FactionMember Portrait PortraitUnknown Head Stick GraveyardVendor HierarchyUnknown none FactionMember StoreFront , Talion , Mount and the other nine none none The silhouette is decided from the copies: the test reads summary+0x190 , written only by the refill 0x169168, so a change to the member alone shows nothing on the open stage until his summaries are refilled and he is redrawn. The engine's own reveal, 0x19F6C80, runs UnlockName 0x621208(member, 0), then 0x1BC6030(member) (flag bit 7 through the flag setter), then the intel setter 0x353EC4(member, 0xFF, 0, 0), which clamps to the top level.

The Army screen's layer is CUIHierarchyLayer , [base+0x26FFB10] (constructor 0x1896D44, vt 0x1F7B588). "Selected" has two meanings on the Army screen. The highlight is the captain under the cursor; the spotlight, the nameplate and the prompts follow it. The target is the captain that "New Target" announces, set by an action on whoever is highlighted. The highlight's owner is the stage controller ctrl = [[base+0x26FFB60]+0x340] , and [ctrl+0x428] is the highlighted stage character. Everything else is downstream of it: UIManager+0x318 (the member key) and +0x328 , the menu selection and the hierarchy layer's card +0x1580 . A write to any of those moves nothing. SetHighlight 0x1834444(ctrl, character, a, b) is the one place a highlight changes (12 callers, 19 call sites). For the character already highlighted it returns 0. Otherwise, for the old character it clears +0x1CD , calls vf70, wipes UIManager+0x318 and calls 0x188EB3C. It then stores the new one (0x629960( ctrl+0x408 ), whose +0x20 is +0x428 ), and for the new character it sets +0x1CD and calls vf67. a and b reach only 0x1832124, the end of the old character's detail view. vf67 0x1822FEC plays HighlightCharacterSound , writes his key to UIManager+0x318 and calls 0x188ED10( &position ) = 0x188ED1C(UIManager, &position ), which sets the selection and runs each open layer's refresh (the Army screen 0x189A560, the captain detail 0x18C97E0, contract assignment and mercenary). Its camera call 0x327120( ctrl+0x4E0 , state, 7) does nothing here, because Faction/World/Character::FactionMember.CameraStateHighlight is unset (only CameraStateSelect is set). A highlight therefore never moves the camera. Keys and positions. 0x400818(out, member) = { FM+0x178 , FM+0x174 }, with index -1 when empty, is the summary's +0x88 key and what the card holds. 0x1896B3C(out, member) builds a position { +0x00 army, +0x08 u8 row (0x1E4D90), +0x09 u8 seat FM+0x51B , +0x10 the key, +0x20 u8 flag}. 0x1862A40( &key ) finds his stage character ( StageFor 0x455EDC, then 0x1A28FAC). Who highlights. The highlight is set by the mouse (0x17DE2A8, from the UI manager's 0x188FE8C), next and previous (0x17DE1A0 / 0x17DE224), a direction (0x17DE394), a menu entry (0x1830AF8) and the store (0x188EEAC). The four input paths share one branch. When the current character is in the detail view, they call SetHighlight(.., 0, 0) , and then 0x1835574(ctrl, new, 0, 2, 0, 0) carries the detail view over to the new captain; otherwise they call SetHighlight(.., 1, 1) . The mouse path is message-driven: a pick of nothing does not clear the highlight (0x1A21664(current, 0)), and 0x183246C returns the current highlight while the cursor has not moved (0x1834E70). The cursor's verdict , 0xEF3A80(character), is one of four values: 1 (his row is in the army's list, ctx+0x170 .. +0x178 ), 2 (the summary's +0x1A1 ), 3 (his selection object's +0xCC is 0) and 4 (selectable). The mouse and the keyboard both use the list 0x1830D60, which keeps verdict 4. Next and previous also need the summary's +0x1A4 and a known name (0x170744(summary, 0)), so the keyboard skips a silhouette and the mouse does not. On one Minas Ithil stage 19 of 25 characters read 4 and 6 read 3 (the Overlord and the warchiefs). A menu entry (0x1830F2C - 0x1862A40 - SetHighlight ) applies no such filter.

Interface/Menu/MenuSelection/Predicate/FactionMember::SetTarget takes MenuEnter and, as its mouse input, Mouse1 on a highlighted captain, with the result action Interface/Menu/MenuSelection/Action::SetTarget , the mode Target Success Allowed and the positions captain, warchief and Overlord (not empty seats). A left click on a hovered captain is therefore Mark Target. The dispatcher vf19(layer, action) - 0x1898AE0(layer, selection, action) takes the branch ActionSetAsTarget (accessor 0x1897668 on the layer record), which calls 0x18928A8 - 0x17A9AE4( [GM+0x6C80] , member, region, 0) and then 0xD6EC60(layer, member, UI TargetChanged Desc ); it is the only branch that raises that banner. ActionClearAsTarget runs System::ClearCurrentTarget 0x188B0C8. The current target lives at [GM+0x6C80] ( +0x00 its key, +0x20 active; see Outposts, strongholds and fortress upgrades for its other fields). 0x18928A8( , &{army record, u32 pool index} , region, flag) resolves the key (0x170794 - 0x18D93C(FS, &key )) and calls 0x17A9AE4(targets, member, region, flag). The Army screen passes the region of the army it shows (0x188D0CC()), and the game's in-world callers pass the current one: a quest (0x625AD8) passes [FS+0x1B0] , and Faction.SetTarget 0x17C0B58 passes the current faction's. The flag ( targets+0x38 ) is the quest type's UIAllowTargetChangedNotice , not a lock. The verdict is the selection's mode list "Target" (selection +0x1E0 ), computed inside SetHighlight from seven Interface/HierarchyMode/Type rules: Rule Reads --- --- Target Success Allowed , Target Clear Allowed the captain can be marked, or is the target already Target Failure Dead flag bit 2 Target Failure Empty an empty seat Target Failure Disabled [UIManager]+0x2FB is 0 Target Failure PresetBlocked [FM+0x190] is a preset whose CanSetAsTarget is false (default true; 0x18AAFB4) Target Failure TargetLockedByActiveQuest the active quest has +0x2B0 set (no target allowed) or +0x2A8 other than -1 (its own target) The active quest (0x103508) is the first entry of [GM+0x6C60]+0x3D8 (begin / end, 0x28-byte entries, object at +0x20 ) in state 17 ( +0x12C unless -1, else +0x128 ) whose type ( [+0x260].Type ) has RemainOnHUD (default true). Of the 2,256 Quest/Quests , 60 set TargetForcedToNone : Golden Path 31, companion side quests 18, story fort assaults and finales, and one statue replay. In a live read, an ordinary captain read Success Allowed and the current target Clear Allowed . Calls and jumps under 0x18928A8 do not reach the script-context check 0x503EF8 (a walk of 937 functions to depth 6, with 59 indirect calls not followed).

The captain detail layer, CUIFactionMemberLayer (vt 0x1F7CB10), is the panel with a captain's trait rows, the bonuses and weaknesses icons with counts, the trait list and its video. With it open, the menu's layer stack held the pause layer, the Army screen layer and this one, and the Army screen layer's card still held another captain: that card is not what the Details view shows. Built once. The enter method vf29 0x18C9408 initializes each embedded menu widget through its vf2 0x3292DC, which stores three callbacks at widget+0x30 / +0x38 / +0x40 and a user argument at +0xD0 . The base widget +0xB090 (vt 0x1DB1688) gets 0x18C5B4C, which handles the trait group trees, StrengthOverlay / WeaknessOverlay , Video and the CharacterPresentation card at layer +0x14278 (its key {army, index} at +0x14280 ). The additional prompt +0xA10 , the video +0xB438 , the contract highlight +0xB7E0 , the contract results +0xBB88 and photo mode +0xBF30 get their own callbacks. The shared widget state machine vf4 0x46D700 calls [w+0x30](w, [w+0xD0]) when it evaluates a widget. Refreshed only when the highlight moves. The engine evaluates the widgets again through the highlight's layer refresh (above). Highlighting the captain already highlighted returns early, so a change to the highlighted captain's traits leaves the panel as it was. The layer's own refresh is 0x18C97E0(layer), which runs vf4 on +0xB090 , +0x5D50 and +0xA10 , then 0x18CA830 (the selection's prompt flag), then 0xD8E770(menu, 7). It takes no captain argument and makes no same-value test: called on an open panel, it rewrote 137 and then 154 of the layer's 24,576 qwords, while a control second with no call changed none. Other calls are not refreshes. 0x188ED10's selection set 0x18BE498 appends an entry to the selection on every call (0x18BB704). The hierarchy refresh 0x189A560 can play HighlightCurrentTargetSFX . 0x1835574 moves only the stage side (the detail pose and the camera), and the engine's own call passes 0 for the menu. The rows are tree nodes on intrusive lists: the rows tree at layer +0x1D340 , its child sentinel at tree+0x488 , the link at node+0x168 , the row's trait at node+0x258 and the lit row at tree+0x4A0 . The group strip (the eight group icons) is a menu tree group at layer +0x17F58 . Its trees are at [+0x53B0] (0x620 bytes each, u32 count +0x53B8 , the active tree +0x53C0 ), each with a child list (sentinel tree+0x488 , link node+0x168 , the node's TraitGroup record at node+0x28 , the lit node at tree+0x4A0 ). SetActiveTree 0x32D15C(strip, tree, node) lights an icon in either tree, but on its own it leaves the rows on the old group. The rows rebuild 0x18C9EE8(layer) then draws the lit group's rows: read live, switching from weaknesses to bonuses changed the rows from 2 to 4, and from bonuses to class from 4 to 6. TraitGroup.MaxVisTraits ships with the value 7 (3 for hints), and its four readers are all in this layer, so it limits only the card (see Captain traits). The shipped trait tree MenuTreeBase/Traits has no Scrolling pane and a ScrollBarRotation of -90. The same widgets on another screen. 0x18EACD0 / 0x18A30F8 build strengths and weaknesses from the live member (0x1BBA470 / 0x1BBA518) and call the CharacterPresentation setup 0xE9204 (19 callers), but they belong to CUI3DZoneMapLayer (vt 0x1F7E570), the world map's captain tooltip.

The Army screen has two camera branches. - The overview. The army camera state Faction/HierarchyMenu/Cameras/States::CS Army Cursor names a fixed overview, but its UseWorldMapCameraPredicate is Faction/World/Predicates/HierarchyMenu::HierarchyFreeCursor , which passes while the top menu layer is the Army screen, contract assignment or the mercenary layer (and not in replay mode). While it passes, the camera belongs to the world-map layer: Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/WorldMap.HierarchyCameraState - Interface/Camera/CameraStates::HierarchyFreeCam , whose two orbit keys ( StructuresUIOrbitPointParams primaries 340 and 341) are the near and far ends of the zoom, with radii 1025 and 5250 and a vertical field of view of 25 degrees. Two keys are what make a zoom axis. - The captain detail. CS Char Detail has no world-map predicate. Its UICameraSettings is an array of 153 Faction/HierarchyMenu/Cameras/UICameraState entries, each chosen by a predicate on the captain's row, seat and state (for example Orc Row2 L , Orc SlotOverlord Row4 3 , Orc Dead and Talion ) and naming one of 111 distinct camera states. Each of the 111 has exactly one orbit key (radius 250 to 550), so its radius is a fixed distance and the detail view has no zoom. Orbit keys. An orbit key ( StructuresUIOrbitPointParams ) holds fov , OrbitRadius and Roll as plain floats of the key's own instance, so a key's radius belongs to the states that reference that key alone. CameraOffset , CameraOffsetRange and CameraAdjust are shared float-pool pairs (type 7; see GameDB), each shared by every key that holds the same values. CameraOffsetRange is the (yaw, pitch) swing in degrees on either side of CameraOffset (the formula is below). The key unpack clamps both values to [0, 180] (0x526DAB .. 0x526DD5; it wraps CameraOffset into -180 .. 180 with the same 180), and at 180 the two ends of a drag meet behind the subject. The overview's keys 340 and 341 carry (24, 12) at radius 1,025 and (16, 10) at radius 5,250, both with fov 25. The 111 detail keys use eight distinct pairs: (0, 0) on 75 (one more key's pair was not decoded), (90, 20) on 16 (among them the standard captain views base Orc / base Olog ), (45, 15) and (40, 15) on 5 each, (60, 20) on 3, and (90, 25), (80, 15) and (60, 15) on 2 each. The (0, 0) pair is the database's shared unset value (see GameDB): a view on it has no rotation axis at all, and a write to that pair would move every cell in the database that shares it. A key also has a node offset (orbit and focal offsets with position and rotation tracking masks) and a DepthOfField link to Client/DepthOfFieldSettings (near and far in-focus and blurred distances, blur intensities), authored for the shipped radius. Orc Details is sharp from 120 to 325 and fully blurred past 375, so a camera pulled back beyond that band renders the captain as blurred background. WorldMapCameraMode is 4 on every Army camera state except two: CS Store ProductDisplay Cursor (5) and CS Mercenary Cursor (6). The camera object is ctrl = [[CGameClientShell+0xE38]+0x60] : the shell's frame update 0x1A864C passes [shell+0xE38] to 0x52440C, which runs [this+0x60] through 0x524BA0 every frame. The pointer is null when there is no menu camera. Offset Meaning --- --- +0x70 the Interface/Camera/CameraStates record it runs ( HierarchyFreeCam on the Army screen, base Orc L or base Olog C in the detail view) +0x88 / +0x8C / +0x90 the interpolation values, each 0 to 1: the sideways drag, the up-down drag and the blend between keys; seeded from the state's InitialInterpolationValue when it is entered (0.5, 0.5, 0.0 on base Orc L ) +0x1D8 / +0x1E0 begin / end of its private copy of the record's Keys , 0x88 bytes each +0x1F4 .. +0x27C the current parameter block (below); +0x33C .. +0x3C8 the copy handed on +0x290 non-zero while a transition runs (the switch into the detail view takes about 1 s) A key copy, unpacked by 0x527A18, holds +0x00 fov, +0x04 OrbitRadius , +0x08 Roll , +0x0C CameraOffset , +0x14 / +0x18 CameraOffsetRange after the clamp, +0x1C CameraAdjust , +0x24 the node offset, +0x6C the depth-of-field flag, +0x70 / +0x74 / +0x78 far focus, far blur and far intensity, and +0x7C / +0x80 / +0x84 near blur, near focus and near intensity. The copy is re-read every frame. While no transition runs, 0x524BA0 calls 0x524AF0( ctrl+0x1D8 , [ctrl+0x70] , ..), which copies the record's keys again, so a write to a key of the running state shows within a frame. A range written on the open Army screen, and a radius and range written in the open detail view, each reached the camera's copy within 100 ms, and the camera object was never replaced. 0x527A18 is OrbitRadius 's only copier. 0x5B9D24 is the camera's state switch: it compares the request with +0x70 , fires the old state's ExitEventTimeline and seeds +0x88 from InitialInterpolationValue . The drag. +0x88 and +0x8C clamp at exactly 0 and 1, and a drag is added to the stored value; nothing recomputes or eases it, so a value written there is where the next drag starts. The parameter block is filled every frame by 0x524BA0 and validated by 0x525168 ("Invalid Camera params."): Current Handed on Field --- --- --- +0x1F4 +0x33C OrbitRadius +0x1F8 / +0x1FC +0x344 / +0x348 orbit yaw / pitch in degrees = CameraOffset + (drag - 0.5) x 2 x CameraOffsetRange (read live: 12.54 = 0.035 x 360 at a range of 180; -6.40 = -4 + (0.486 - 0.5) x 170 at a range of 85) +0x200 / +0x204 +0x34C / +0x350 CameraAdjust (x, y), degrees +0x208 .. +0x220 +0x3B0 .. +0x3C8 depth of field (far focus, far blur, intensity, near blur, near focus) +0x224 +0x354 the camera: position (cm) and quaternion (x, y, z, w), 0x1C bytes +0x240 +0x370 the focal transform (121 cm above an Olog's root) +0x25C +0x38C the pivot: the captain's position plus the node offset, and his rotation +0x278 / +0x27C +0x3A8 / +0x3AC the lens: horizontal / vertical field of view, radians The renderer draws the detail view's captain through +0x224 : in 42 sampled draws the world-to-view transform put the eye 0.4 cm from it with the quaternion's axes to four decimals. A key's fov is the vertical field of view (the projection's P11 = 1 / tan(fov / 2) on 2 of 2 keys), the projection is centered, and the frame is left-handed (+Z forward, +Y up, +X right). The gameplay camera ( [[player+0x2F90]+0xA8] ) stays behind Talion while a menu is open. CameraAdjust 's only reader is the key unpack (accessor 0x528358; helpers 0x5283C8, 0x5283DC and 0x17FAB8C are called only from it). From there it travels in the parameter block, which the state switch copies (0x5B97xx, 0x5B9Dxx), transitions blend (0x689xxx .. 0x68Axxx) and 0x17F9xxx initializes. In the detail view the game parks the system cursor at the window center.

The Desolation of Mordor's mercenary layer shows an army's stage like the Army screen (see An army with no stage above) and a status header. Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/Mercenary.StatusHeaderType is 8. 0x3289C8 switches on the header's type at +0xE0 : 1 pause, 2 upgrades, 3 equipment, 6 store, 8 mercenary, 9 contract (4, 5 and 7 mount the fort, conquest and arena widgets). It runs at each header change (0x328748, 28 callers; 0x328840) and reads its fields fresh. Type 8 puts MenuStatusHeader::Default.MercenariesCurrency in slot 0: the widget StatusHeaderMercenaryCurrency , symbol UPG-DLC4Coin , whose predicates exclude only IsStoreConfirmPurchase and IsDLC3 . UPG-DLC4Coin (in upgrades.gfx ) is a three-line ledger, not a coin: it has the text fields Value , Desc , CostValue , CostDesc , RemainingValue and RemainingDesc over a backing sprite ( UPG-PlayerCurrency has only Value and Desc ). Its ready callback 0xE46560 - 0xE49A60 writes the balance as %u into Value , the selected member's hire cost ( GetHireCost 0xFA3AF0) as -%u in red into CostValue , and the balance minus the cost as %d into RemainingValue , in green, or in red below 0. The cost lines show only with a member selected. All three Desc fields get the literal token {Coin} (its only three references), whereas the player-currency header's setter 0xE49020 takes the token from the currency item. The balance is the player's currency: the visual component ( [UIManager]+0xB0 , the same object as [player]+0x2348 ) holds the skill setup at +0x738 ( Inventory/Skill/Setup::Player Character , whose CurrencyItem is PC Mirian ) and its inventory records at +0x740 .. +0x748 ( +0x00 item, +0x20 count). The affordability check at 0x18AAD4E and the payment at 0xDBD0DF read the same setup (Baranor's setup pays DLC4 PLBar Coin ). {Coin} is the glyph CurrencyCoin ( hud\questicons\new\kraken\coinicon.tex ), whose only item user is DLC4 PLBar Coin . Mirian's own item chain is PC Mirian - UIItemData::PC MordorBucks - CurrencyIcon ( {M} , kraken\currency.tex ).

t: The title screen, save select and loading screens
The title screen and its message of the day
x: The title screen's root layer is Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/FrontEndRoot::FrontEnd (class CUIFrontEndRootLayer ): content symbol LIB-MenuList , the selection tree FrontEndRoot , a build version widget, the new-game layer list NewGameSetup Full , and a message-of-the-day node Interface/Menu/MenuTreeNode/StoreMOTD/Default (cooldown color, size and a 10-second time). The message's text comes from the online service's broadcast feed, not from the localization tables. Interface/Shared names a front-end world, worlds\reference\frontend\frontend.world06c , which does not ship, and a background bundle with two images cross-faded every 10 seconds. The skin choice is a tree node too: Interface/Menu/MenuTreeNode/Skin::Skin DarkTalion names the character model PlayerSkin DarkTalion Main and stores its unlock, notification and viewed state in Profile/GlobalOptions .

The save-select screen is the mode-select layer Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/GameModeSelect::ModeSelect . Its row state, availability test, the Continue / New Game / Delete actions and the confirmation box are in Saves, the store and the network layer; a new game pushes the SingleOption::Difficulty layer. Its prompt bar is the component library's LIB-PromptBanner , a text field in the font $HydraHUD , with a 3D effect behind it (see Widget effects above).

A loading screen is one of the 27 Interface/LoadingScreen records, which hold Allowed , Platform , a GameData predicate, completed / incomplete quest gates, required game modes and world, a fast-travel state, background slides with cycle and fade times, a bundle, an optional movie (6 of the 27 have one, all base-game Cin movies), portrait settings, valid tips and enter / exit audio hooks. CUILoadingScreen::CUILoadingScreen (0x18D2024) looks up the elements LoadingBG , LoadingBGCaption and LoadingProgressBar . Then, only when the byte 0x2A2637D is set (one reader, no writer in the executable), it finds the element ProductionNotes (symbol LIB-ProdNotes in the component library), gets its child Field and writes Monolith's notes into it: Debug/Shared::Debug.DebugMOTD (a "Project Timeline" header) followed by every DebugMOTDDates entry ( DisplayString plus DateString through the month-name formatter 0x18D2608), separated by <br . The five shipped dates run from the fourth DLC's release to the fifth DLC's bug lockdown (May to June 2018). In the retail game the byte is never set, so the notes never appear.

The controller that built and ran Monolith's developer menu was compiled out; everything around it shipped. Piece Where Content --- --- --- The movie debugmenu.gfx in interface\bundles\debug.embb ( UI Assets ; the bundle also holds the controller glyph textures and interface\textures\debug\debugsheet.tex ) title "Monolith / Debug Menu" in the $Console font; 12 widgets: DBG-MenuRoot , -MenuButton , -ItemsWithDesc , -ConsoleCommands , -CheatEntry , -LevelList , -LevelEntry , -ScriptHookEntry , -ScriptHookPrompt , -ProdNotes , -Prompts , -Loading The view Interface/GFX/UI::Debug the movie and debug.bndl The root Debug/Shared::Debug the command set Profile/CommandSets/DebugMenu , enter / exit sounds, the Production Notes text Console pages Debug/ConvarShortcut 34 pages (among them QA, AAA, HDR, Camera, Combat, Inventory, Presentation, AI info, nav mesh, nodes, markup and world review, game speed and frame stepping), 530 items, each a title and a console macro Cheats Interface/Cheat (14) and Interface/Cheat/Order (9 shown) among them God, Health, Clip, RemoveAI, SafeZone, Invisible, quest unlock / complete / teleport, CrimeRemove, AllAchievements and DSDebugCam Captain actions Debug/FactionMember::Default 20 actions (among them level up / down, decapitate, set as follower / spy / dead / prisoner / revenge target, get intel, swap positions, eject and hire mercenary), each a faction event Script hooks Debug/DebugScript (135), Debug/LevelScriptType (14), Debug/MetadataType (94) names and parent links Layout Interface/ElementAttribute::DebugMenu Root , Active , Inactive , SubLayer , PromptBar ; buttons DebugMenu BaseBtn , LevelListBtn , ConsoleCommand , ShowcaseBtn , ScriptHookEntry ; MenuTransition::Debug header at the top right (1.0, 0.0), the active page at (0.05, 0.12), the prompt bar at (0.5, 0.98); inactive pages turn 60 degrees about Y, so pages flip like cards Levels WorldInfo.InDebugMenu 11 worlds; six debug worlds exist as records The widgets are the self-animating skins described above ( DBG-MenuButton : out 0, off 9, in 10, on 14). DBG-ConsoleCommands is a page list with an 18-row sub-menu and a gray command preview, DBG-ItemsWithDesc is a list with a description panel, and DBG-CheatEntry is a row with a checkbox.

The open / close logic is intact behind the byte 0x2A2636D, which has four readers and no writer: - the console commands UI.OpenDebugMenu (0xD652B0) and UI.CloseDebugMenu (0xD64AD0), registered in CUIThread.cpp ; - SetDebugMenuShown 0x7B5980( [UIManager+0x88] , show), behind the script call System:ShowDebugMenu ; - the Army screen's ActionOpenDebug handler 0x18CC238. All four act on [UIManager+0x88] and do nothing while the byte is clear. SetDebugMenuShown pushes Profile/CommandSets/DebugMenu on the input stack (0x1170D44; DisableAllOtherCommands with 26 menu commands enabled, so gameplay input is blocked), plays EnterMenuSFX and sets the open byte [[UIManager]+0x88]+0x7AE . Hiding pops the set (0x1170D34) and plays ExitMenuSFX . The Army screen action pushes the set and sets the byte without a sound. While the byte is set, IsDebugMenuOpen 0x381EEC makes the renderer 0x382044 call 0x381E68, which draws a full-screen black quad at alpha 0xDD over the world and the HUD, and the gameplay-input test 0x17B91EC fails. The commands the set enables include MenuEnter , MenuEscape , the four menu directions and the MenuAux commands. The input data is live too: Interface/Shared.DebugCommandSet ( DebugMenuActivate Hydra ) is pushed at every game start (0x1780A04), and Profile/Commands binds DebugMenuActivate1-4 (held together: Home or 9, End or 0, Left and Right; on a pad L3, Start and D-pad left and right). The input registration 0x3123CC gives the debug commands their IDs ( DebugMenuActivate1-4 0xC8-0xCB, spectator and God shortcuts 0xCC / 0xCD, AI info next / last 0xCE / 0xCF, debug spawn modes 0xD0-0xDB, captain list / save / load 0xDC-0xDF, the debug camera 0xBC-0xC7).

1. The view is never built : Debug is not in Interface/Shared.UIViews , so debug.bndl and the movie are never loaded. 2. No code names the menu's records : DebugMenu , DBG- , Debug Menu , ScriptHook , ProdNotes and Showcase occur nowhere in the executable as strings, while the controls in the same scan do ( NavMarkers 12, MessageBox 25, HierarchyLayer 4, FrontEndRoot 5). The component, attribute and view records have no inbound RecordLinks. 3. The page data has no reader : the fields ConvarShortcut.Key / Title / String / ShowInDebugMenu / CloseMenuOnCommand , Interface/Cheat.CheatConsoleString , WorldInfo.InDebugMenu , Debug/FactionMember.Actions and DebugScript.Parent have no accessor, while Debug/Shared.DebugMenuCommandSet on the same record does (0x7B5A0C). 4. Nothing opens it from input : the open functions have no caller besides the script binding, the console registry and the Army screen action, and the DebugMenuActivate commands are referenced only by their registrar. 5. Most page commands are not in the retail console : the 530 items expand to 1,711 console commands; 85 name a live command, 18 a handler compiled down to ret 0 , and 1,608 a name registered nowhere. The only shipped script that touches the menu is the Bright Lord finale, which prints "Finale Part 4 Triggered" and calls System:ShowDebugMenu(false) , the call the menu's Script Hook page made after firing a script.

The cheat manager is [GameManager+0x6CA8] : a vector of 0x28-byte entries ( +0x10 id, +0x18 the Interface/Cheat record, +0x20 toggleable, +0x21 on), built by 0x180EF9C, with per-id allowed flags (0x65B0E4). The retail game registers one entry, God. The names table 0x22F55A8 reads GOD , HEALTH , CLIP , REMOVEAI , SLOWMO (ids 0 to 4). - Toggle 0x65ADDC(manager, id) finds the entry by id, checks the allowed flags (0x65B0E4) and the record's CheatActivatedString (0x65AEA8), then calls Apply with the entry's +0x21 state. - Apply 0x65AD7C(manager, id, on, character system) applies one cheat. God stores the byte manager+0x30 and calls CCharacter::SetCanDamage(!on) , then refills health. Health refills through 0x65ADCC on the player's combat object. Clip calls 0x19BFDA0(player, on, 1). RemoveAI calls 0x180EC7C and clears three fields of the client shell's +0xA50 object. SlowMo starts the slow-motion record Debug (0x7CE80C). 0x180F184 re-applies Clip when the player spawns. The Interface/Cheat console strings (for example Cheat God ) are not registered in the retail console. The captain actions are faction events fired by CreateAndProcessFactionEvent 0x1B5B610(FS, event, member, other) on the Army screen's highlighted captain, the member of the stage character at [[[base+0x26FFB60]+0x340]+0x428] (see The highlight above, and The Nemesis system for faction events).

ExecuteCommand is the engine interface's vf29 (0x1180D8C): it hands the line to 0x1182FA4, which looks the name up in the console registry ( Find , see The executable) and runs the command synchronously on the calling thread, splitting ; -separated commands. A name value line whose name is not registered creates a new settings variable (0x1182F10) instead of failing. Of the registered commands, 98 of 449 have handlers compiled down to ret 0 . The console's output goes nowhere. Command output and the engine log both end in the sink 0x6AAC14, which under the lock 0x27C45A0 calls the function pointer [base+0x27C45C8] if set, then writes to a stream if the byte 0x27C45D1 is set. In the retail game the pointer is null (written only by its static initializer 0x585A0 and the exit path 0x1196AF4) and the byte has one reader and no writer. The debug camera these pages drive is described in Characters, the player and the camera.

Tutorials are data. Four families of records drive them: Family Records What a record holds --- --- --- Interface/Tutorial/Pausing 116 a modal pane set that pauses play: HUDState ( Interface/HUD/State.PausingTutorial ), HeaderString , DismissString , Panes (348 StructuresTutorialPausingPaneData structures in all: BodyString , image , or video , an Interface/Movies record), its own Bundle ( interface\bundles\kraken\tutorials\ .bndl ), the input CommandSet that holds play ( Profile/CommandSets.TutorialModal A ), InputLockout (0.5 s), RequireAllPressed , HoldAndPress , InputHoldDuration and enter / exit sounds Interface/Tutorial/Gameplay 120 an in-play hint: DisplayString , duration , sounds Interface/Tutorial/Menu 82 a menu tutorial: a Setup (screen position) and OnEnter , OnExitBegin , OnExit steps (253 StructuresTutorial MenuStep ) Faction/HierarchyTutorial 62 an Army-screen tutorial: a predicate, ExitMenuOnFinished and FirstState , a chain of Faction/HierarchyTutorial/States (84) A menu step applies or removes an input command set (for example HierarchyTutorial A or HierarchyTutorial LStickX ), enables or blocks mouse movement and fast travel, and advances on the common input. It may also change the menu around it through three record kinds. WidgetData (18) shows or hides a widget ( Show / Hide ) such as the fort status header or the hierarchy overview. TreeData (24) restricts a menu tree to some nodes (for example ChallengesRestrict and GemSocketsRestrict ) or clears the restriction. MenuSelectionData (8) lists Interface/Menu/MenuSelection/Predicate records to disable, for example every order on a captain during the Bruz ambush tutorials. Layer data adds per-screen settings ( ShowMemberNavMarker / HideMemberNavMarker on the Army screen, SelectMtnPass on the quest log). An Army-screen state names the menu tutorial to show, an optional map presentation, a preset or job member or the mercenary entry point to select, the view, and a camera transition to wait for (with a command set to apply meanwhile). It also holds PopupDelay (1.0 s in PlayerDiedFirstTime State01 ), DelayNextState and Next , and closing conditions ( CloseOnPositionSelected , CloseOnNewEquipmentHighlighted ). The tutorials' predicates live in Faction/HierarchyTutorial/Preadicates (83 records, 73 fields; the category's name carries the misspelling). TutorialViwed links a Combat/Predicates/Bool record (whether this tutorial has been seen), and AnyTutorialsViwed , AllTutorialsViwed and NotTutorialsViwed test other tutorials. The rest test the Army screen's mode and state (normal, replay, interrogation, commanding, orders or assault setup; overview or details), the selected captain's known state (among them known, location known, full info, presumed dead, branded, decapitated and henchman), the active game mode, inventory and new-item counts, skill points and store counts. From script. TutorialPausingShow / TutorialPausingHide and TutorialGameplayShow / TutorialGameplayHide are methods of the CCharacter script class (0x1BB2108 resolves the Interface/Tutorial/Pausing record and calls the character's vtable slot 99). The player raises OnTutorialPausingDismissed / OnTutorialGameplayDismissed . System:GetHierarchyTutorialViewed (0x1B86BA4) checks a Faction/HierarchyTutorial record against the viewed list reached through the player ( [CGameClientShell]+0x888 , with its byte +0x3880 ; the test is 0x30C46C). The HUD classes are CUIHUDPausingTutorial and CUIHUDGameplayTutorial . The Army-screen tutorials are run by the hierarchy menu's tutorial manager ( HierarchyMenuTutorialMgr.cpp ), and the console names a HierarchyMenu.ResetTutorials command.

- What class is [UIManager+0x88] , the owner of the debug-menu open byte? The UI manager's constructor 0x1889674 only zeroes the slot. In a running game the object starts with a heap pointer rather than a vtable and holds a run of text-style entries that name the font "Anonymous Pro" with sizes 45 and 100; the name is not a literal in the executable, so it comes from data. The open byte sits at +0x7AE , near the object's end. - What was the PreLoad view for, and does its preload.gfx still ship? No archive entry has that name and no interface bundle's manifest names it, but ingame.bndl 's manifest does not name sp.gfx either, and that movie ships inside its container. Which movies hold the UI render list's mode 8 and 0x10 entries? - What consumes the DebugMenuActivate1-4 command IDs (0xC8-0xCB)? Data enables them: both Profile/CommandSets records DebugMenuActivate Hydra (pushed at every game start) and DebugMenuActivate Menu list all four in EnableCommands , next to the AI-info and FactionMember debug commands. No code names them: neither their record links (0x9FD00091 - 0x9FD00094) nor their name hashes occur in the executable. A consumer would test the numeric IDs. - Which code selects the Interface/LoadingScreen record for a given load? Data names few of them. No shipped script names a loading screen (0 of 2,562 script sources), and the fields that can link one are GameModes.InitialLoadingScreen (8 of 13 game modes name Intro1 , one DLC3 FastTravel FromUI ), Presentation/Elements.LoadingScreen (set on 0 of 3,000 elements), Regions/Region.ExitOnlineModeLoadingScreenOverride (0 of 19 regions) and Faction/MoneywallSetup/UI.LoadingScreen . In the shipped database Intro1 is linked 8 times and DLC3 FastTravel FromUI once, while FastTravel DesertLoadScreen is linked by no record at all, so the per-region fast-travel screens are chosen in code. - Where is the viewed-tutorial list stored, and is it saved with the game or with the profile? - What holds the screen black when an army without a stage is shown? The UI state machine's wait expires after 20 s, and in a frozen run only one word of the world-UI owner ( +0x68 ) and none of the stage controller changed between 3 s and 30 s. Nine of the 21 callers of StageFor skip a null result; the other twelve were not read that far. - Does the Army screen's action dispatcher re-test the target rules? Emulating vf19 with the SetTarget action on a dead captain marked him, which suggests that only the prompt (withheld by the mode list) keeps the player from it. - Does verdict 3 of the Army screen's cursor test mean "off camera"? On one stage it marked the Overlord and the warchiefs; it should then change as the camera turns. - Who writes a drag into the menu camera's +0x88 ? None of 13 functions that store there in the camera code is the writer, so it likely stores through a pointer. - What consumes CameraAdjust from the parameter block ( +0x200 / +0x34C )? A displacement scan of the camera code found only copies, blends and initialization. - Does the HierarchyTransition handler 0x1834BB0 refill the stage copies from the members? That would make the state change into the Army screen show member edits. - Is node slot 104 an htmlText getter? Before a nemesis mission starts, the game shows a confirmation screen: a 2D card for one captain, two captains or an Army-screen order, over a 3D stage where the mission's captains walk out and face each other. The screen is one menu layer, CUIQuestStartLayer , driven by the quest's WorldUIConfirmSequence and by the mission's sim event; the same layer confirms the Army screen's orders. Menu layers in general are described in User interface: Scaleform, menus and the debug menu.
