t: Saves, the store and the network layer

x: A save file is <name ShadowOfWar.sav , where <name identifies the owner (on Steam, the account number in hexadecimal). Beside it the game keeps rotating copies <name 1 ShadowOfWar.sav to <name 5 ShadowOfWar.sav : 1 equals the main file (same size, same time) and each higher number holds an older save. The number is not a slot: the three slots live inside the file (below). Where each build keeps the files, and which account value it mixes into the key, is described in Game builds: Steam, GOG and Microsoft Store. header 'SOM3' u32 salt u32 padded length (= file size - 16, a multiple of 16) u32 real length body AES-256-CBC, PKCS 7 padding key 256 bits, derived per file from a constant built into the executable, the header's salt and the owning account's number (SOM2 files leave the account out) iv a constant built into the executable The reader 0x119A2C8 accepts SOM2 and SOM3 ( sub eax,'SOM2'; test eax,0xFEFFFFFF ); the writer is 0x52B4BC. Both use OpenSSL's EVP layer linked into the executable ( EVP aes 256 cbc , the decrypt init / update / final calls and the padding switch). The padding byte equals padded length minus real length, and the plaintext's entropy drops from 8.00 to 5.01 bits per byte. This reference describes the format; it does not publish the key material.

The plaintext opens with SAVE version 2: a header (a u32 profile-section count at +0x18 , 5), the profile sections, a u32 slot count (3), then per slot {u32 6, u32 length, u32 0, payload} . A section is tag, u32 version, u32 size, u32 0, u32 n (= size - 4), n bytes of typed values: Tag Value --- --- 00 a 32-bit name hash (4 bytes) 02 u8 04 u32 05 two u32 (a GUID half, a pair of counters) 08 i32 0A f32 0C bool (1 byte) 0E vec3 (12 bytes; positions in cm) 0F byte string (u8 length + bytes: GUID text, a product id) 10 u32, the byte size of what follows With these ten tags, 27 of 27 sections of a story slot read to their exact end. GameDB records are saved as name hashes, never as strings (a 2.3 MB save holds 421 ASCII tokens, all settings); the hash does not carry a category, so the section's context decides which category it names. Layout. 86 sections: 5 profile sections ( GOXC PERF PICB GPDC GMSC ) and the same 27 in each of the 3 slots. Per slot, in file order: SAVE (the summary, version 31), a u32 giving the byte length of the rest of the slot, IVGD (v3), ENT2 IVSH PPDC PDIC PAIC IEUC IVMG (v43), IVPD (v4), TTRL LTMR , about 1.28 MB with no typed section header, then FAST FOTP ASMC DIFF CBTC GCPT INVA REEL QSTD (v23) PDCC LPDC AUDI IIUC UITC STOR (v159). Most sections open with 04 3, 00 hash(<game mode ) . Section Contents --- --- SAVE (slot) the summary: 10 values (region, a hash, a percentage, play time in minutes , ...) IVGD the 573 game variables, three times: 00 variable hash, 02 VariableType, value . The first copy holds the played values; the other two hold the record defaults PPDC the per-mode level and XP table ( [GM+0x6D20] ): {00 mode, 04 level0, 04 XP} (level0 + 1 is the level shown) IVMG the player's inventory (below) IVPD 584 {00 item, 04 value} pairs for the skill items ( PS , S ) PDIC contains world positions (vec3) GMSC (profile) per game mode {mode, int, sub-object, score record A, score record B, bool} ; a score record is {mode, hash, 5 ints, 4 floats, bool} with the score as its second float IVMG , the inventory , holds, in order: - a header ( 04 3, 00 mode, 0C, 10 size, 05 (...), 00 PlayerSkin00, 04 <one above the highest item id , 04 729, 0C 1 ); - the owned stacks {00 item, 04 count, 04, 04 n, n x 04, 0C} (714 on a finished save; the Mirian currency is a stack too); - 14 bools; - the gear records {04 id, 04 level, 02 0, 00 Inventory/Items, 00 EquippedWeaponData, 00 0, 0C, 0C, 04 n, n x 00 Affix/Definition, 04 0, 05 GUID low, 05 GUID high, 0F source product, 02 0, 0C has-nemesis} , followed, when set, by a nemesis block ( 00 NemesisGear, 00 Description, 00 Role, 04 seed, 04 seed, 0C , then optionally an upgrade tier, art, a Combat/Challenge/Eval challenge with its progress and a weighted Faction/Loot/Tag list) and two closing bools; - 25 per-slot entries {0C, [04 item id]} (one per inventory slot); - reward items and 8 gem sockets {00 SocketType, 0C, 00 SocketType, 00 gem} , and DLC flags. The front-screen card. The card printer 0xDF9370 reads the slot info [CGameClientShell+0xEB8] + 0x1C8 + GameModes.SaveSlot 0x298 : it prints ceilf(+0x24 minutes) as hours and minutes and floorf(+0x20) as the completion percentage. Both come from the slot's save summary: its value 3 is the completion in percent and its value 4 the play time in minutes (a summary holding 100.0 and 14,655 showed on the card as "100 %" and "244h 15m"). For a game mode with GameModes.UseHighScore (the fourth story DLC's mode), it prints the score from the GMSC entry found by 0xFAD1B0( [base+0x2A36278] , mode): the first entry with +0x80 equal to the mode and +0x50 non-zero, score at +0x68 .

t: Saving and starting a new game
x: The save switch. Both world-save paths read GameModes.CanSave of the current game mode ( [base+0x2A36260] ; SinglePlayer in the campaign) and skip the save when it is clear: - the save task (vt 0x1F6CC40 vf3 0x52C70C - 0x52C664, which also refuses on the client shell's state at +0xE38 , flags at +0x189 / +0x194 and +0xA20 ; accessor 0x52C5EC); - the world save 0x5B7B58 ("Attempting to save the game without a world to restore", test at 0x5B7BA8). CanSave is packed bool 13 of the record's first cell. It ships clear on QuestReplay (story mission replays) and Benchmark : the engine is built to run a world that never saves. SaveCurrentWorld (bit 3) is a second gate inside 0x5B7B58. The mode-select screen ( GameModeSelect ; layer class vt 0x1F92AF0, record Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/GameModeSelect/ModeSelect ) lives in the menu system's layer vector ( [[base+0x26FFB08]+0x50] , +0x500 .. +0x508 ). The highlighted row is [layer+0x1348] (node +0x28 the record, +0x230 the GameModes record, +0x238 the world). The profile slot info is [[CGameClientShell+0xEB8] + [CGameClientShell+0xED0] 8] ( +0x38 = 3 when ready); a mode's slot is +0x1C8 + SaveSlot 0x298 , whose +0x08 is non-null when the mode has a save. - 0xD07AA0(mode, 0) is the mode's availability: 0 not ready, 1 / 2 a DLC not owned / not installed, 3 playable. 0xE37610(layer) tests whether the highlighted mode has a save. - OnAction (vf12 0xE39590): action 0x20 (MenuEnter) leads to 0xE39E00, where availability 1 / 2 opens the DLC store, 3 with a save continues (0xCF8ED0), and 3 without a save starts a new game by pushing the Difficulty layer with the mode at instance+0x9C8 . Action 0x54 (the "Delete Saved Game" prompt, key 2 / pad X) opens a confirmation when the mode is playable and has a save. - Delete 0xE3B650 resets every save-data chunk handler (0x184CA5C), the mode's GMSC entry (0xFADDC0) and the slot info, and sets the row's world to GameModes.DefaultWorld . Deleting and then starting is the only native way to restart a mode that has a save. - The confirmation is a 0x1138-byte message-box request: +0x00 the close callback 0x17DA030, +0x20 the Interface/MessageBox record for type 0x3F, +0x28 type, +0x2E title wchar[0x80] , +0x12E text wchar[0x800] ; queued by 0x1784F14( [CGameClientShell+0x890] , request). The callback calls the caller's function with the result; Delete acts only on 0 (Yes). New Game+ was cut by nulling one link. Interface/Shared/Shared still carries the whole New Game+ card: NewGamePlusPresentationItem ( Inventory/Items/Player PresentNewGamePlusDialog ), a bundle path that ships in no archive, an image, an icon, a command set ( Profile/CommandSets/NewGamePlusConfirm ), the title "Congratulations!" and a description key with no string. However, NewGamePlusPresentationEvent is null, and the player-UI tick 0x5218C8 builds nothing without it. No restart logic stands behind the card. The console command UI.NewGamePlusDialog (registered by 0xB2220) only sets a byte at +0x98 of the player's +0x2F98 object, which nothing else in the analyzed code writes; Quest/Quests.ShowNewGameDialogOnComplete has a field binding but no reader. The game's own delete warning lists what a new game keeps: all boosts, unused training orders, undeployed follower orcs and unopened chests ("available in Act 2").

The engine keeps the local player profiles in a vector at CGameClientShell+0xE90 ( +0x28 begin, +0x30 end; one profile on PC) with the active index at +0x40 (u8, 0xFF = none). 0x30B254 returns the active profile when its state +0x38 is 3 (loaded). The profile object (vt 0x1F6CC40, constructor 0x17C32F8) also owns the save task (its slot 3 is 0x52C70C, see Saving and starting a new game) and the slot summaries the front-screen card prints. Offset Content --- --- +0x1C0 u8 bitmask of the slots present +0x1C8 three slot summaries of 0x298 bytes +0xAB0 the option store (the GOXC chunk) +0xB10 pointer to the input binding object +0xB28 the per-mode score chunk ( GMSC ) +0xB30 the command-set manager

Settings live in the save file itself: the five profile sections at the start of every save (see The save file) are the profile's chunk objects, each returning its tag from slot 5 and its name from slot 9. Tag Chunk Version Content --- --- --- --- GOXC GlobalOptionChunk 5 the two difficulty settings, then 118 {00 option name, 02 type, value} ; a record-typed option is 04 hash(category name), 00 hash(record name) ; then 19 {00 DLC/Config record, 0C flag} PERF PerformanceChunk 6 25 {0F console-variable name, 0A value} : ClientFXMgr.DetailLevel , WorldDetail , FSAA , LODTextures , ScreenWidth , ScreenHeight ... PICB ControlRebindings 8 the player's rebinds: {00 button, 04 hash(ActionID), 02 slot, 0C, 0C, 00 model-override type} GPDC GlobalProfileDataChunk 5 profile statistics, one entry per Interface/GameProfileData record (350 of 350): a count and {04 key, 04 value} for the 269 records of DataType 0, then the 3 of DataType 1 with 0A float values, then the 78 of DataType 2 with 0C flags, then three zero integers; the key is the CRC-32 of the record's name GMSC GameModeSessionChunk 5 per-mode scores (see The save file) The statistic keys use the standard CRC-32 (0x505400(buffer, length), table 0x27C54D0, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF; six of its 13 callers read Interface/GameProfileData ), case-sensitive: all 350 keys of one save reproduce. It is a third name hash beside the GameDB's (see GameDB) and the animation keywords' multiply-by-31 hash (see Animation). Each statistic record also carries IsGlobalData , ResetOnNewGame , StorageType , UseOnlineStorage , Association , CollectableList and the platform statistic names ( SteamAgoraName , XONEStatId ). The value of an option changed in the menus is the same in the live store and in the save file.

Profile/GlobalOptions defines 118 options ( EGlobalOptionType : 65 bool, 24 float, 23 integer, 6 record) with their defaults; the prefixes group them: CP controls (25), GP gameplay (25), VP video (14), AP audio (6), Skin skin unlock and notification flags (19), SS save slots, Lang languages. Lang Text and Lang Audio hold the locale as a four-character code ( enUS ), and CP Binding PC names a Profile/Inputs/PC/Bindings record. The store (vt 0x1F6F548): Offset Type Content --- --- --- +0x08 vector difficulty settings (reset from Difficulty/Lists.DefaultDifficultySettings ) +0x18 table {data, u32 count, category} of 0x20-byte entries {+0x00 record, +0x08 value, +0x10 u32 type} , indexed by record index; the value is a bool, f32 or i32 in its low bytes, or a record pointer +0x30 u8 dirty +0x38 table DLC/Config flags, 16-byte entries {record, u8} Options are addressed by name: 0x2784D0 hashes the name and binary-searches the category's sorted name index ( [base+0x27007A8] ), and the getters read the record's entry: GetBool 0x2785A0 (falling back to the record's DefaultBool ), GetRecord 0x438468, SetBool 0x7CF4C8, and a float getter 0x5238A4 (used for CP AnalogDeadzone ). Slot 1 (0x17D5060) resets every option to its default. When the profile loads (0x17C65FC) the engine polls four gamepad ports through the input system [base+0x26FEFC8] (slot 13), clears CP UseGamepad when none answers, and applies the binding named by CP Binding PC .

Profile/Commands (382 records) defines one command per action: ActionID (a string enum; at run time commands are keyed by the enum index), CommandType , Event (289 of 382), IgnoreWaitForOff , and two button slots per platform: PCKeyboard , PCGamepad , XBoxOne and ps4 . CommandType is an ECommandType , named in the executable's enum table: Value Type Commands --- --- --- 0 COM MOVE 119 1 COM INV none 2 COM VIEW 9: yaw, pitch, their accelerations, the debug camera's four and CenterView 3 COM MISC 8: the message-box confirm and deny commands and DebugMenuActivate1 - 4 4 COM WEAP CombatSecondary01 and 02 5 kNumCommandTypes , the count, used as "none" 244 The keyboard binds 226 commands (60 in both slots), the PC gamepad 275, the console pads 270 each. Profile/BindingSets (17) group commands in a CommandList plus CommandCharacterModelOverrides (alternative commands for the Eltariel and Baranor model types); Debug and DebugSyncAction are marked DebugOnly . Profile/Inputs/PC/Bindings holds nine keyboard bindings, one per locale, each listing the same 13 sets; Profile/PCKeyboards adds the AZERTY, QWERTY and QWERTZ layouts with five key overrides. Profile/Inputs/PC/Buttons.Device is one code space for every PC device (155 of 155 records): Codes Device --- --- 8-223 keyboard keys: the Win32 virtual-key code ( KeyBack 8 ... KeyOEM8 223; 117 keys) 1000-1008 mouse: buttons 1-5, the X and Y axes, wheel up and down 2000-2019 gamepad: 2000 + the console pad's own code ( Profile/Inputs/Durango/Buttons , 0-19) 0x438498(binding object, binding record, gamepad) builds the active bindings through 0x5B6D20: for each set of the record (skipping DebugOnly sets), first each model override and then each command, every non-empty slot of PCKeyboard (or PCGamepad ) becomes a 0x18-byte entry: Offset Type Content --- --- --- +0x00 ptr the button record +0x08 ptr the model-override type, or null +0x10 u32 the ActionID enum index +0x14 u8 slot (0, 1; 2 for a copied binding) +0x15 u8 Event +0x16 u8 IgnoreWaitForOff 0x5B6C00 then applies CopyBindings (copies of one command's entries under another command, slot 2). The binding object holds the player's rebinds at +0x00 (from PICB ), the active list at +0x18 and a copy of the record-built list at +0x30 ; 0x438518 overlays the rebinds, replacing the button of the entry with the same ActionID, slot and override type, or appending, and only for keyboard and mouse (it returns at once while CP UseGamepad is set). With KeyboardEnglish the active list holds 363 entries: the 348 the records predict (280 in slot 0, 68 in slot 1, 128 of them model overrides), 13 copied slot-2 entries and 2 rebinds. The binding is rebuilt by the handlers of CP Binding PC , CP UseGamepad and CP Southpaw .

A command set enables or disables commands while some state lasts. Profile/CommandSets has 231: EnableCommands , DisableCommands , DisableAllOtherCommands with DisableAllOtherExclusions , WaitForOff and AllowMenuToGameplay . The profile's manager (vt 0x1F6B510, constructor 0x17B77F4) compiles all 231 once (0x17B7E08 - 0x17B8580) and keeps a stack: Offset Content --- --- +0x08 priority table {data, u32 count, category} , 16-byte entries {record, u32 priority} +0x40 / +0x48 the compiled sets +0x58 the input-system context handle +0x7B u8 dirty +0xD0 / +0xD8 the active stack: set records in ascending priority +0xE8 / +0xF0 the compiled-set index of each stack entry +0x100 / +0x108 sets pushed with the flag argument A compiled set holds the enabled ActionIDs ( +0x00 ), the disabled ActionIDs ( +0x18 ), the DisableAllOtherCommands byte ( +0x30 ), the exclusions ( +0x38 ), the WaitForOff byte ( +0x50 ) and the record ( +0x58 ). The priority (0x17B745C) is the record count minus the set's position in Profile/CommandSetPriority.Shared (217 entries, 213 distinct; the first is the highest, a later duplicate overwrites); an unlisted set has priority 0. Push 0x5B5E40(manager, set, flag) (43 callers) refuses a set already on the stack, inserts it before the first entry of higher priority (or appends it) and marks the stack dirty; pop 0x5B4AEC(manager, set) (55 callers) removes it; 0x17B7D38 clears the stack. The active profile's push and pop are 0x7DFB8C and 0x7DFCF8. Scripts reach them through PlayerInput.ApplyCommandSet / ReleaseCommandSet and Quest::ApplyCommandSet / ReleaseCommandSet ; menus, presentations, photo mode, struggles and interrogation push their own sets. The debug menu pushes the set named in Debug/Shared.DebugMenuCommandSet ( DebugMenu : menu navigation plus two debug shortcuts, with DisableAllOtherCommands and WaitForOff ) on open (0x18CC238, 0x7B5980) and pops it on close. A stack read in free roam held StateSupported (priority 15) below PresentationIdentifySystemic (126).

The pre-2018 Market is the pause menu's GARRISON : Root Store - Interface/Menu/MenuLayer/Store (the label resolves to "GARRISON"; an older patch archive still says "MARKET"). Its sections are Store Garrison (Followers), Store Stash (Unopened Chests), Store Contracts (Training Orders), and Store Vendor and Store Boosts , which build only from visible catalog products. - IsStoreEnabled 0x1B1AE04 = GetBool(current game mode, StoreEnabled) ; SinglePlayer ships true. The gold predicate CommerceCurrency Paid 0x1869F48 returns true when the store is off, so gold-only content is free by design in that case. - GARRISON has seven locks, Root Store.LockedIndicatorPredicates (primaries 1896 to 1902): not connected, Minas Ithil not unlocked, under age, an active quest, the store inaccessible (0x1893780 - 0x1B22AF0 - 0x17F5DC4), the game out of date (the build number the service reports above the client's 8874), and not the main game. - The client commerce object is CUser+0xDB8 (vt 0x1F71020), where CUser = ([base+0x26FFA98]+0xE90).users[0] . It holds +0x49 initialized, +0x4B / +0x4C / +0x4D definitions, inventory and catalog loading ( +0x4E has no writer in the executable) and +0x5D store requested; the wallets at +0x158 (paid Gold), +0x160 (earned) and +0x168 (social: the Spoils of War); and the boost state at +0x100 (XP multiplier), +0x110 (end time) and +0x120 / +0x138 (Spoils), parsed by 0x17F6998. - Bring-up. The commerce tick 0x472D44 waits for the platform user-info request to succeed ( +0x60 , set only at 0x17F79B5 in 0x17F7894); until then it retries forever and +0x49 is never set. Then it calls LoadCatalog (0x472E4D). A catalog failure (0x17F5F68) empties the list, and the catalog is not asked for again. - The 2018 update switched the store off on the client by removing the loop that creates shelf nodes (with 9 store-layer action fields and the purchase handlers); the catalog itself is still requested and parsed. Every consumer survived, including the product-node setter 0x194D118 (still used by the Buy Gold layer 0x1930650) and AddNode 0x195B78C. The console command User.Commerce.LoadCatalog (0x17F4AB4) fetches the catalog on demand. - Opening a chest runs the 2017 pipeline: an unpack job (0x1FE1EC0) and one follower reward (0x1FE1F88) per orc in the reply, building the orcs into Faction Player with row Faction/Rows::player created . A local follower is built by the same chain: a builder instance (0x1C62054, filled by 0xFF2370 from Marketplace/Builders/FactionMember/ type, class, tribe, element, rarity and level) - 0x1B5B7F8(FS, region faction, instance) - 0x7D52B0(fm, 1) (bit 27 of FM+0x508 , player follower) - 0x1B5E254(FS, fm) (hierarchy slot). GARRISON's Followers section is the online garrison (see Online orcs). - WB's binary format (Hydra) encodes booleans as 0x02 = true and 0x03 = false. The integer tags 11 , 13 and 15 are unsigned 1, 2 and 4 bytes, and the service always takes the smallest width that fits (over 831 bodies 13 held nothing below 0x104 and 15 nothing below 0x10000); 16 holds negative values, and 10 appeared twice, on values that read as -25 and -10. Its parsed catalog and inventory objects are freed after parsing. - GARRISON's Gold counter sits in the header embedded at [[base+0x26FFB08]+0x50]+0x800 (vt 0x1F92EC8: +0xE0 header type, +0x538 seven element pointers, Gold = element 2). The 2018 switch-off is only that element's callback ( element+0x30 = 0x1983288), which hides its Value and Desc children on every update; the same callback also completes the header's transition step (0x328748). The header type numbering changed between patches (5 in the older archives, 6 in the final one). Currency icons are glyph tokens, not pictures: the Mirian setter 0xE49020 sets Desc to the item's UIItemData.GlyphReplacement.TokenText (fallback {M} ), and Interface/GlyphReplacement::PremiumCurrencyIcon = {G} draws kraken\gold.tex .

The online modes trade orcs as documents: the exporter 0x1BC5044(fm, map) writes one orc into a Hydra map, and the importer 0x1BC21B4 builds a FactionMember from one. An orc travels as hashes of shipped records, so it can name nothing the receiving game lacks: 0 of 428 distinct orcs in captured traffic named a record the shipped database does not hold.

The exporter writes 71 keys plus SMCStorage.smc storage (35). Identity by record hash ( faction record , combat tree record , character record , role record , tribe record , personality record , preset record , location record ...), random seed , menace level (the level), name string id hash , every flag-word bit by name, trait picker list , trait marker list and trait level , and texts for the service ( name , title , the name keys, rarity string id , specialization string id , status effect string id ). Inventory holds fmi equipment list (per item Item , WeaponData , ArmorData , Affixes , Source , GUID64A / B , iLvl ...), smc flaircolor list and smc nonequipment record list ; smc storage holds BodyType , smc bodymodel record (the rig), smc headModel record , 16 smc piece record (appearance cells 0 to 15), 15 color words (no faction war paint, no default) and smc storage appearancetags . Not exported: FM+0x180 (the birth army, the record the size bonus comes from; see Characters, the player and the camera), appearance cells 16 to 22, the design cells and material overrides. The importer reads 57 keys , each asked for by name (0x507C38, a case-insensitive compare, first match); its only loops run over arrays it fetched by name, so a key it does not know is never read. It does not read name , title , any name , rarity string id , specialization string id , status effect string id , trait base , is warchief or is total : the receiver takes the name from name string id hash and the title from role record . Traits come back as trait picker list re-added through 0x7CD03C and rolled by the game, so a slot forced to another option than its picker's roll does not travel. random seed is stored at FM+0x168 (0x1BC243E): a downloaded captain keeps the uploader's seed. Callers: 0x1BC04E4 (the online arena opponent and Garrison followers), 0x1BD3BD8 (a Conquest or Vendetta fort's member array ) and 0xF58270. The import redraws armor from the items. In 0x1BC21B4 the appearance comes first ( SMCStorage - 0x1C05970(appearance), at 0x1BC2BAA), then the inventory ( Inventory - 0x1C112F8( FM+0x50 ), at 0x1BC2BD5), and then, unconditionally, 0x61BAD4( FM+0x50 , appearance) at 0x1BC2BE5, which puts every armor item's own design back over its cell and the items' flair colors over the palette (see Captain appearance). So an armor cell that differs from the item that holds it never reaches another player.

GARRISON's Followers section is the player's online garrison. At the end of an online match 0x1B36D7C calls 0x1B3BA78(match), the match state being [GM+0x6D30]+0x100 : +0x18 the mode ( Invasion/Modes ), +0x28 the army, +0x140 the dominated captains' handles (0x10 bytes each), +0x188 the imported followers (pushed back by PushFromInvasionToOriginal 0x1BC3870). When the mode's SendDominatedEnemiesToGarrison is set (reader 0xF55D10: true for ranked Conquest and Vendetta, false for friend Conquest), it takes the army's followers (bit 27, 0xFD04E0) and calls AddToGarrison 0xF6B7A0(FS, fm, notification, 0, 0, 0). With a fourth argument of 1 it also pulls the orc out of his army (0x1C25FA8); the stack arguments check capacity and set garrison+0x50 when full; and the army must be among the army contexts. - Garrison::Add 0xFCB3A0 makes no follower, pool or mode test. It refuses an orc whose online id FM+0x3D0 ( <prefix NPC <n , exported as npc profile guid ) is empty or already among the rows. FM+0x476 is the service's object id of an orc that came out of the Garrison. - The garrison [FS+0x50] : +0x00 a vector of new entries (empty at rest), +0xF8 the rows, 0x90 bytes each ( +0x00 the id, +0x30 the service's object id). The capacity [GM+0x6D48]+0xCC is 400 (the caller checks it, 0xF664F0). A new row appears within 20 seconds of an add. - An entry (vt 0x1FDD1E0, 0x108 bytes, constructor 0x1C12224): +0x40 id, +0x70 the service's id, +0x98 army, +0xA0 combat tree, +0xA8 base trait, +0xB0 rarity, +0xB8 role, +0xC0 name id, +0xC8 menace ( FM+0x4B8 + FM+0x470 + 1 ), +0xD0 the Hydra map, +0xD8 the notification (a 34-byte buffer, not a C string). The map holds FactionMember (the exporter's document) and Searchable (the index the Followers list loads). The constructor itself starts the upload through 0x1C13508; no later tick is involved. - Bringing one back, the import 0x1BC04E4 (through 0x1B5B780; the Followers layer 0x187E2D8 builds into Faction Player and seats through 0x1B5E254) reads the document with 0x1BC21B4: the exported army goes to FM+0x180 , the army becomes the destination and the row and seat are cleared. Bit 27 is cleared only for the online arena's opponent ( online arena opponent ), so the stored is player follower decides whose the orc is. One Conquest army mixes owners: a recruit keeps the online id of his first owner (7 prefixes in one army of 22 captains, 24 or more in one garrison of 109 rows). The InvasionGame pool outlives the online match (23 of 23 members still there after the return).

The invasion manager is [GM+0x6D30] . A fort is published by a queue of regions: - Marking. The manager's save-chunk writer (vt 0x1F6E9D8 vf4, 0x6246C0, which calls the save serializers 0x36C94C and 0x36E044) tail-calls 0x624724. That function queues the current region ( FS+0x1B0 ) when mgr+0x47E (set by the fort-upgrade purchase 0x17DEB8C and by 0x17DF750, Interface/Shared.DefaultFortGroup ) or mgr+0x47D is set and mgr+0x47C is clear, provided that region's Overlord has flag bit 27 (or the developer byte 0x2A36438 is set); it then clears both bytes. 0x631B64(mgr) is the engine's own "mark the fort": mgr+0x47D = 1 and, only while mgr+0x47C is set (an online match is running), 0x1B3BEE8 unless 0x17BF3E8( mgr+0x100 ). +0x47D is touched by 0x624724 (read, clear) and 0x631B64 (write) only, and 0x631B64 has one caller, 0x630644. So a marked fort goes up at the game's next save; Vendetta and Garrison uploads carry an orc as he is at the moment they are sent. - The queue is the vector at mgr+0x570 , filled by 0x1B3FCEC (publishable regions only, no duplicates, byte 0x267A314 set); 0x1E3E78 hands its head to the publish pump 0x1B3EC50 once the timer at mgr+0x548 has elapsed. Besides the mark, a region is queued by a registration reset (below) and by a retry inside the pump while an earlier publish is in flight ( mgr+0x1B ). - The registration. Entering the world, 0x1B417F8 sends the registration id at mgr+0xC0 (or none when empty); the service answers with a new id, stored by 0x1B3EAF4. When the reply says a reset was triggered, 0x1B3EAF4 clears mgr+0xE58 and queues every region of Invasion/Settings.PublishableConquestRegions ( snowMtn , MtnPass , island , volcano , desert ). - The pump's gates , in order. A refusal returns 1 and the caller removes the head (0x1B36C04), so a refused region is dropped, not retried: 1. the region is publishable (0x1B36688); 2. 0xCAE850 is true or 0xD0BB40 is false; 3. GameModes.CanPublishConquest (0xF55890); 4. 0x114E008 is false (the enqueue tests it too); 5. Regions/Region.Faction - Faction::GetFactionPlayerOwned 0x1E484C, which despite its name tests no ownership: it returns the army's row 0 seat 0 when that row is IsOverlord (0x1E4C08); 6. that member has flag bit 27 (0x114E020), or the developer byte 0x2A36438 is set; 7. 0x16E0C4 returns the seat's member, 0x17A7A0C is false, his tribe ( +0x328 ) and role ( +0x318 ) are set, and the role is not in ExcludedConquestTargetRoles ( ConquestRestricted Roles : Role Store Vender , GP RangerRoleDef ). Followers elsewhere in an army do not make the fort the player's: only the Overlord's seat counts. - The fort id is minted once by 0x573C68 as "%s FORT %d" into the army context at +0x21E , with the prefix at [rcx+0xA81] and a counter (0x2796674) that restarts each launch; 0x1B2F174 builds "%s NPC %d" from the same prefix. A publish replaces the region's fort in place. The Defense rating 0x4F9360(faction) walks the fort's members: an Overlord (0x4FA75C) adds ( FM+0x470 + 1 + FM+0x4B8 ) x FD OverlordLevelMultiplier (2); a warchief (0x4F91AC, by row rank) adds that level once, plus FD FortUpgradeGroupContribution (15) when 0x4F6644 passes and 0x4F7B8C does not. A lone level-80 Overlord gives exactly the published 160. Two early-outs return stored values ( [mgr+0x2D4] , UIManager+0x13C ). The rating screen draws the service's ranking reply as sent. Its rollup, read on nine accounts, is the combined rating = total assault + total defense, each the sum over island (Núrnen), mtnpass (Cirith Ungol), snowMtn (Seregost) and volcano (Gorgoroth), the screen's four rows; desert (Lithlad) is stored but counted in neither, and minasIthil reads 0. The best assault rating is the maximum over every region. A region's id on the wire is the P919 hash of its name (6 of 6). The result is reported by the client. 0x1B377D8 builds the final-score call: Time is the float at [[GM+0x6D30]+0x20C] , WarchiefTraitExploits , OverloadTraitExploits and OptionalObjectivesMet are literal zeros in the builder, and Failed and Aborted are added only when true.

The engine keeps an older peer-to-peer multiplayer layer. The shipped game builds it and ticks it every frame; nothing hosts or joins. - NetMesh (vt 0x22C1170, secondary vt 0x22C1128; constructor 0x119F92C, called only from the engine interface's slot 18): one instance, at CGameClientShell+0xE60 , with its node id ( +0xB8 , u16) at 0xFFFF. CGameClientShell vf1 0x1A864C calls its slot 3 every frame (send vf4 0x66D8F4, receive vf5 0x66DA68). Slots: 6 HostMesh 0x11A0F5C, 7 JoinMesh 0x11A1218, 10 Drop (host only), 12 DetermineNewHost ("Using matchmaking system NOT IMPLEMENTED"); SendJoinRequest 0x11A1C0C; the node registry checks ids and endpoints at 0x119FDB0. HostMesh and JoinMesh have no callers. - NetStateMachine ( Engine\Runtime\net\ ): the JoinMesh state (factory 0x11A01BC, vt 0x1E6FFE0) and HostVote (console variables Net.NSM.HostVote.Timeout 15000 ms and .PauseInStart ), plus Net.PhysicsPause and Net.MaxFinalizeTime . - UDP transport: socket / bind / getsockname 0x11C57E0 (non-blocking UDP), recvfrom 0x11C5880, sendto 0x11C4760 with a network simulator (drop percentage [base+0x27C5480] , corrupted-byte percentage [base+0x27C547C] , a switch byte [base+0x27C5484] - 0x11C4B0C). Packets are bitstreams (0x1197620, size = (bits + 7) / 8). - No replication layer: the bitstream builder's 19 callers all lie inside the network code (0x117F000-0x11C4000); the client shell reads the player object directly ( +0x888 ), so "client" and "server" share memory. The client shell registers LANOnly , publicserver and NetMeshGamePort (default 1032) and never reads them. Profile/Multiplayer ships the older engine's profile (client port 27888, bandwidth settings, IDS PLAYER NAME ). - Also compiled in: Steam game-server, networking and matchmaking interfaces (lobby keys LobbyName, ServerVersion, ReqPassword, BehindNAT, PubIP, PrivIP, LANOnly at 0x11EF670) and a WebSocket client for the online service's real-time channel. - The online service's channels. The client talks to the service over four channels: a REST API, the real-time WebSocket channel (plain, as the client has no SSL support compiled in for it), telemetry and a file store. The REST timeout is 60 seconds: 0x11F4CC5 calls the setter 0x9FDDF0 with 60,000 ms four times (read back on the live object, vt 0x1E39D18); the constructor's 10 s (0x9FCB70) never reaches a running game. The real-time channel is live during play as a keep-alive: every 30.5 s the server sends one byte 0x0C (12, Ping in the id table at 0x9AC000) and the client answers 0x0A, in a median 31 ms (26 of 26 pairs over 13 minutes of a Conquest). Of the platform's 22 services (named by run-time type information), Lobbies and Clans are near-empty shells; "lobby" appears nowhere in the executable. - The input thread polls four XInput pads (0x11537D8). The input-driven attack node runner 0x30FD80 is reached only from the player tick (0x162560 <- 0x43B8F4): AI combat has no virtual controller. The online modes are asynchronous. GameModes lists ranked and friend Overlord arenas (online fight pits), Vendetta and ranked / friend Conquest. Opponent data comes from the online service; the fight is simulated locally. An online fight pit is the quest <Region ArenaOnline (six regions; Quest/Types::OnlineArena ; setup Quest/Jobs/SetupSimple::ArenaOnline : job 0 the player's Overlord, job 1 ArenaOnlineOther = UseOnlineArenaOpponent , builder ArenaOnline Other ). The ranked menu 0xE24AE0 sends a matchmaking request; its reply parser 0xF74430 reads {Id, Info, Overlord} or an error string. The opponent goes through 0xF548C0, the same orc importer as Vendetta and Conquest (0x1B41894), is level-checked by 0xF58EF0 and stored as online arena opponent . Launching (0xF72D30, quest enter 0xEA7700) sends the current region's Overlord, serialized by 0x1BC5044 (fm, map), the engine's orc exporter (also used for publishing, Vendetta and Conquest; see Online orcs for the 71 keys it writes).

- What the second and third copies of the game variables in IVGD are (checkpoints, restore states). - The 1.28 MB of each slot that carries no typed section header. - Whether the 25 per-slot entries in IVMG are the equipped items per slot. - Where the engine keeps the progress a new game inherits (the profile part or the online store). - Which function evaluates the command-set stack for an incoming command, and so how DisableAllOtherCommands , WaitForOff and AllowMenuToGameplay combine at run time; it is probably behind the input-system interface [base+0x26FEFC8] . - What the two flag bytes of a PICB rebind entry are, and what reads a command's CommandType . - Where the PC build keeps its graphics detail settings: the 25 PERF values read 0.0, and the render.cfg and \USER\render.cfg paths named at 0xC27FE0, 0x10152C0, 0x1172A34 and 0x11798AC have no file beside the game or the saves. - Whether the 13 copied slot-2 bindings (all one ActionID, no button) come from the default PC CopyBindings record, whose two links are empty. - Whether a registration reset is what stops a region's ratings counting until its fort is published again: on one account the rollup read 0 until a fort was republished, and the stored ratings came through every reset unchanged. - What the fort-publish gates 2 and 4 test (0xCAE850, 0xD0BB40, 0x114E008), what 0x630644 is (the one caller of the fort mark 0x631B64), and what 0x4F6644 and 0x4F7B8C decide in the Defense rating. - Whether 0xF58270, which adds a mock FactionMember on the stack filled from a stored document, is a route to an orc with no live member. - Whether a receiving game loads the bundles of a head, hair or body that an orc's document names but no equipped item of his requests (the engine makes a gear load request only for an equipped item).

Shadow of Mordor (2014) is the predecessor engine generation. Its internal project name is Firebird ; Shadow of War's is Kraken . The two games share their archive family, container idea, GameDB format and much of their orc rig, but nearly every asset format moved on by several versions, so no Mordor asset loads in War unchanged.

Shadow of Mordor Shadow of War --- --- --- x64 executable ShadowOfMordor.exe , 27,930,624 bytes ShadowOfWar.exe , 117,732,784 bytes Load address 0x140000000 preferred, relocatable ( DYNAMIC BASE , relocation table present) always 0x140000000 (relocations stripped) Code a conventional .text section of about 20.6 MB .arch (about 30 MB) plus 70 MB of code in .bss a (see The executable) Because Mordor's executable is relocatable, its addresses move with ASLR every run; the Steam build of War, which the War column describes, never moves (War's GOG and Microsoft Store executables are relocatable too; see Game builds).

Both games use LTAR archives. Mordor's are version 3 ( .arch05 ), War's version 4 ( .arch06 , see Archives and file formats). The Mordor install has 66 archives, 45.4 GB . header (0x18 bytes) "LTAR" u32 version (3) u32 names size u32 folder count u32 file count u32 1 names null-separated strings from 0x18; the last string may run past the declared size, and a small block precedes the entry table entry (0x20 bytes) u64 data offset u64 compressed size u64 uncompressed size u32 flag (9) u32 name offset The entry table is found by its signature (the flag 9 at +0x18 of consecutive entries). Parsing all 66 archives gives 28,884 entries, equal to the 28,884 declared in the headers ; every entry's data lies inside its file and the data offsets ascend in all 28,828 consecutive pairs. A name offset may point into the middle of a string, and an entry's name does not reliably describe its payload, so asset paths are taken from the containers' own path tables, as in War. Compression. Mordor stores each entry as a stream of chunks {u32 compressed length, u32 uncompressed length (at most 65,536), data} compressed with zlib ; chunks whose two lengths are equal are stored uncompressed (of 192 sampled chunk headers, 166 began with the zlib marker and 26 were stored). Chunks are padded, so the next chunk header can sit a few bytes after the previous chunk's data. War compresses with Oodle.

Mordor's containers are BNDL version 4 (War: version 6); 8,034 of them hold 67,982 asset paths (66,731 distinct). Mordor's world prefabs are PRFB version 5 and its Scaleform movies GFX version 8 (ActionScript 2). Asset formats are older versions that War's loaders reject: Format Shadow of Mordor Shadow of War --- --- --- mesh ( MMSH ) 9 16-17 skeleton ( SKEL ) 8 (War's loader rejects it) 17 animation ( ANIX ) 42 44 texture ( TEXR ) 3 8 material instance ( LTMI ) 4 7-8 string table ( SKDB ) 9 (10 languages, 32,643 keys each) 9 Mordor's version-9 mesh vertex is 60 bytes: half-precision position (4 halves), 16-bit texture coordinates, 32-bit normal, tangent and bitangent, a color, blend weights in BGRA order and bone indices; strides can differ between a mesh's elements. Every Mordor mesh has one UV set , while War's orc gear shaders read a second one. Mordor's texture coordinates can run to 2.0. Textures use the same DDS-based payload, and War's texture header adds a 23-byte block. Materials are authored differently: Mordor's orcs use about 21 generic shaders, War's use the dedicated nemesis gear, head and body shader trees (see Rendering). For the one weapon compared directly (the Master Pike), Mordor's albedo was about half as bright as War's equivalent (mean 56 / 45 / 39 against 108 / 93 / 82).

Mordor's GameDB is a GADB version 17 file (the same container version as War's; see GameDB) of 23,264,671 bytes inside hotchunk.arch05 's globaldatabase bundle: the entry after the named manifest entry, a BNDL v4 wrapping the database. It holds 115 character models named Cha . The Black Númenórean characters are three unique models: Cha Belroth (the Hammer), Cha Imrakhad (the Tower) and Cha Zainzadan (the Black Hand, whose mesh one of Talion's alternative skins in Mordor is built from). Mordor ships no generic Black Númenórean soldier armor: a census of every container path (66,731 distinct), every self-named texture (12,714, none unreferenced) and every XML manifest (8,071) finds none. The warband downloads ( layer52 to layer56 archives) are 216-byte unlock stubs: the Guardian, Blood Hunter, Crusher and Flesh Burner orcs are GameDB presets assembling base-game pieces with paint, not new assets.

Shadow of Mordor Shadow of War --- --- --- orc body rig 112 bones (the berserker 116) orc base , 100 bones shared bone names 72 72 face rig 33 joints 124 joints The 72 shared bones sit at the same bind positions (median difference 0.07 cm, at most 0.94 cm for the core bones). Their bind rotations fall into three groups: Group Bones Difference --- --- --- alike 36: the spine, legs, head and upper arms within 2 degrees re-posed 34: the hands and fingers the same bone frames in another pose: a finger's child joint sits where Mordor's does in its own bone's frame to 0.01 degrees on 31 of 32 finger segments, and the weapon bone's local rotation agrees to 0.008 degrees, its grip 1.6 cm nearer the wrist re-framed 2: the forearm twist bones turned 81.46 degrees about their own long axis, with the joint unmoved The face rigs share no joint names. Of Mordor's orc pieces, those that use only bones orc base also has are: armor 35 of 40, flair 116 of 131, bodies 15 of 15 and heads 44 of 111. A Mordor version-8 skeleton has the same 37-byte bone records as War's version 17, but each record carries its own name offset. Its part rows are 11 bytes (War's are 14), its bounds are a 24-byte box at 0x44 with no radius, and its strings are padded to 4 bytes; 486 of 486 distinct skeletons read this way. The two games share one coordinate space: a Mordor orc piece holds its Head at (0.0, 72.76, 0.66), and War's orc base at (0.0, 72.76, 0.67). Mordor stores its binds in model space, as quaternions (x, y, z, w). Converted to local rotations, they equal the file's own bind clip on 111 of 111 bones (median 0.005 degrees), and every Mordor animation file carries such a bind clip: the rest pose as its clips see it. Because Mordor's humanoids name their bones as the orc rig does, a file's rig is identified by its bind clip's bone lengths, not by its bone names. War's own orc clips never track the ten twist helpers ( L/R ArmuX , Bicep , Forearm , Wrist , Thigh ; 0 of 4,463 clips in 351 files): the engine places them.

Mordor's animation files are ANIX version 42 (War: 44). Mordor's loader (0xE44F80 in ShadowOfMordor.exe ) reads a 0x1C-byte header (magic, 42, file size, the block chunk's offset and size, the animation chunk's offset and size) and then both chunks. The animation chunk holds a directory offset ( +0x00 ), the clip count ( +0x04 ), the node count ( +0x0C ), the channel count ( +0x10 ), the string table offset ( +0x14 ) and the node hashes ( +0x18 ), followed by the channel hashes (position 0x00CE66FC, rotation 0x27436396, events 0x210C8F5A, the same as War's). Where version 44 keeps a run-length track table, this header is a plain node-by-channel grid. A clip record is version 44's without the u32 pair at +0x74 / +0x78 : its codecs start at +0x74 , then one 3-byte entry per track {u8 channel, u8 node, u8 group} , aligned to 4, then the blockset table of 16-byte {offset, size, t0, t1} entries; version 44 has a byte group array and a u16 remap array instead. The 6,656 files (22,390 clip records) use only codecs War also has: SV01 (6,655 files), SQ03 (6,655), AQ03 (5,392), UATR (482), STRI (436) and AV01 (237), with USBT, USFT and USCO in a few records. Every track entry is in range, and each codec sits on its own kind of channel in 2,076,293 of 2,076,294 entries. Mordor's executable registers ten more codec evaluators (CATR, CART, CSTR, CSRT, USTR, SQ01, AQ02, CACQ, CRS3, Q101) that no file uses. The dialogue clips are face motion: rotations on the face bones (brows, lids, eyes, cheeks, nose, lips, jaw, tongue) with the arms held still. Clip events are the same command language in both games (KeyString hash 0xB9010BE0 in both; for example snd fol cmn attack windup; BPW; STARTFACING; AFACE Angry; ). Of 89,560 commands in 11,326 non-dialogue Mordor clips, 51,646 appear exactly (name and argument) in War's orc clips. Every gameplay command does ( APPLYDAMAGE , AD , BCOL / ECOL , BHITWIN , BCANWIN , BTS / ETS , BPW / EPW , the facing commands, ComplexAnim , STOP ALIGN ), and so do the facial expressions ( AFACE , RFACE , CLFACE ). What War does not carry: Mordor's sound verbs (War's executable has no SND verb at all; see Audio and video), audio keys its database lacks, and the foot markers ( HeelStrike , ToeStrike , HeelLift , ToeLift ). Mordor registers its verbs as strings ( AUDIO HOOK KEY , DIALOG EVENT , SND , SND UI , SND GROUND , SND HAND , the footstep verbs, BODY IMPACT ), where War compares hashes. War ships Monolith's own ports of some Mordor clips. War's bip cmbt attack front 1 ( orcinf cmbt attack.anix ) has the same 56 frames and 1,833 ms as Mordor's Bip Cmbt Attack Front 1 . Retargeted onto War's rig (the hands re-posed as above), Mordor's clip matches the port to a median of 0.27 degrees per body bone; the port adds a weapon grip in the fingers. Mordor keeps that grip apart: animation\shared\orc\orc awareness.anix holds Orc L Hand Weapon and Orc R Hand Weapon , one static pose on 14 finger bones, while its body clips leave the hand open. War keeps the same two layers ( orc awareness misc.anix ) and plays the right one while fighting (41 starts in 250 s of one fight), and its clips carry finger poses as well (99%).

Mordor's FactionMember is 0x3B0 bytes (its pool descriptor at 0x18022E8; War's is 0x528), in a pool array with a stride of 0x3B8. Addresses in this section are RVAs of ShadowOfMordor.exe . Fields, in the order the save writer (0x85BAE0) writes them where it does: Offset Field --- --- +0x48 u64 id +0x50 u32 the name: the string-id hash of an OrcNameGen1st %03d key +0x54 pool index +0x58 faction record +0x60 combat tree, which is his class ( AI Archer , Berserker , Defender , Infantry , Spearman ) +0x68 preset member record +0x70 / +0x78 / +0x80 traits: begin, end, u32 capacity; 8 bytes per entry (21 on one captain); the save writes 32 slots +0x88 row record (0 = not seated) +0x90 personality +0x98 a Character/Models override (the preset's OverrideModel ), read before any derived model +0xA8 purpose +0xB0 / +0xE0 / +0xF0 / +0x100 member keys: his own; his master's (the captain he guards); his nemesis's; the member whose nemesis he is +0x110 the appearance object +0x278 / +0x280 his bodyguards, 0x10 per entry +0x290 / +0x298 the scar record (from his head's scar setup) and the brand scar record; a non-null brand means branded +0x2A0 / +0x2A8 event history, {Faction/Events/Events record, u16 ...} entries of 0x10, at most 32 +0x2B8 / +0x2C0 role / location +0x2D8 scar type ( Model/Scar/Types ), set by 0x84EE60, which also notifies the faction system +0x2F0 NPC profile GUID +0x340 level (the Army screen's power is level + 1, as in War) +0x344 u32 level-up trait watermark: 0x8627F0 rolls the faction's LevelUpTraitSetup when the level passes it, then raises it +0x374 u32 hash of one of his purpose's PurposeText lines (his "thought"), set by 0x856040 (33 of 33 matched) +0x38C / +0x390 the "new information" bits and the time they were set, by the intel reveal 0x85F0F0 +0x398 u16 purpose expiry in faction ticks: FS+0x130 plus a random value from MinPurposeTimeOut (2) to MaxPurposeTimeOut (10) +0x3A0 u8 seat column, 255 = not seated +0x3A4 u32 status bits, default 0x01008000: bit 2 IsDead and bit 23 IsMockDead (the names Mordor's own captain document uses), bit 17 decapitated, bit 11 events pending, bit 7 set when he is shown as known on the Army screen +0x3A8 u8 bodyguard list dirty: set on him and his master by 0x84EEF0, cleared when 0x857C40 recomputes the list +0x3A9 u8 intel categories: bit 0 name known, bit 4 strengths and weaknesses known (stage 1 = 0x4F, stage 2 adds 0x30, 0x7F all) +0x3AA u8 intel level: 2 full, 1 met, 0 unknown, 0xFF never raised; 0 means known to the player

t: Orc content: what carried over to War
x: War moved every asset path ( models\npc\orcs became characters\modelcharacters\orcs ; 1 of 448 Mordor orc model paths exists in War) and renamed its records (0 of 202 preset captains share a name), so names cannot show which Mordor orc meshes War kept. Surface distance can: each of Mordor's 419 orc meshes is compared with War's 1,578 character meshes, using 4,000 area-weighted samples per mesh, the exact point-to-triangle distance in both directions and the 90th percentile in centimeters. A mesh counts as "same" within 0.25 cm both ways, "adapted" within 1.0 and "re-made" within 2.0; "merged" means that a Mordor piece lies inside a bigger War piece. Controls set those limits: different War designs for one slot are at least 3.58 cm apart for helmets, 4.28 for chests and 3.88 for one-hand weapons, while any two orc heads lie within 2 cm of each other, so heads cannot be matched this way. Mordor's Black Hand sword is the exact mesh of War's nazgul blackblade . Only Mordor has the six class armor sets, the Bright Lord outfits, most of the hair and every head, the bodies and legs, the Black Captains' bodies, and 30 weapons, among them the Master Pike, five spears, axes, maces, swords and the orc bow. Mordor's hierarchy screen is a world of its own, worlds\cinematics\wraith visions\hierarchymenu son.bndl ( son.arch05 entry 15, 232,667,989 bytes, 446 assets; near-identical copies in intro.arch05 and outro.arch05 ). It holds a scene, an object database, a world mesh and 10 prefabs (the hierarchy art, the Warchief pedestals, glyphs, orc light posts, a ruin wall, backdrop rocks), and it draws the crowd as card meshes ( fx\ui\hierarchy\models\orcarmy outlinecards.mesh ). The seats are logical rows and columns in StructuresFaction.HierarchyFactionPos (5 Warchiefs and captain rows of 8, 7 and 5: 25 seats), placed in the world as objects Hier.Faction <row <column with a character spot .Chr , a camera .Cam and about 20 points of interest each. The screen's movie is interface\flash\widgets\hierarchy.gfx , which holds no logic.

t: The Mordor importer in Shadow of War
x: Shadow of War ships its own importer for Shadow of Mordor captains, the Nemesis Forge: it rebuilds a player's Mordor follower and nemesis as War captains from data the publisher's online service returns, and brings them in through two story missions. Its switch, payload, conversion tables, the look it replays from Mordor's generator and Mordor's own captain document are described in The Nemesis Forge: imported captains.

- Whether Mordor's engine lays its hand-grip layers ( Orc L Hand Weapon / Orc R Hand Weapon ) over its body clips, as War plays its copy of them while fighting, and how War blends a layer over a clip's own finger keys. - Which of the two death bits of Mordor's FactionMember status word, bit 2 ( IsDead ) or bit 23 ( IsMockDead ), the Army screen shows as dead. - What Mordor's saved FactionMember floats +0x378 - +0x380 and the paired values +0x384 / +0x388 hold (a position and two morale-like stats are the candidates), and whether the 0x3B8 pool stride holds pool data beside each 0x3B0-byte member.
